WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (verified at 1x, at 4x over the whole crown, and at 10x over each individual fruit): a straight, untapered chocolate-brown trunk-stick running from a soft elliptical ground shadow up to about 60% height, with no branching, no flare at the base and no visible junction into the crown. Perhaps 40 lanceolate/elliptic leaves are scattered radially around the rim of that haze, mid-green with a lighter midrib, with a large soft empty green blur occupying the whole centre of the crown. Four fruits sit in the crown at approximately (183,152), (240,113), (272,208) and (222,238).

ON THE FRUITS — the core of the original claim, and it is right on substance but wrong on colour and on what the internal marking is. At 10x each fruit is a completely closed, unbroken sphere about 26px across. It is NOT orange and NOT glowing yellow: it is a matte khaki/tan-gold with a darker ochre rim (a full-image pixel scan returns max R=200 and ZERO pixels that are red-dominant by any margin). MISSED BY THE ORIGINAL JUDGE — the crown also fails its own must-read. The packet asks for a 'dense conical dark crown'; what is drawn is a rounded, wider-than-tall cloud in a hazy MID green with large empty blurred gaps, i.e. it fails on shape (round not conical), on value (mid not dark, and the leaf tone is not the required 'dark glossy green'), and on density. The 'same trunk-and-cloud chassis' characterisation is fair — this is a generic lollipop fruit-tree body with recoloured spheres, and it would read as apricot, loquat or a small pome to any viewer.

FIX DIRECTION: (1) redraw at least two of the four fruits as a split pericarp — two pale-yellow halves hinged apart or one half fallen away — with the interior of the opening filled by a scarlet/vermilion lacy net (branching irregular strands, not a solid red ball) wrapping a dark brown ovoid seed; keep one or two fruits closed for contrast. (2) Re-silhouette the crown to a tall conical/pyramidal dark form, taller than wide, and darken the leaf green to a glossy near-black-green with a hard specular edge. (3) Taper the trunk and give it visible branch stubs entering the crown.

rows.readsAs: a squat rosette of jagged nettle or mint leaves
rows.defect: The leaf blades splay outward almost horizontally in a low flat rosette instead of rising as a tall upright fountain, so the plant's defining posture is inverted. The blades are saw-toothed with spiky jagged margins; turmeric leaves are smooth-edged entire lance blades on long sheathing stalks — the toothed edge alone sends the read to nettle or mint. The cone of pale green-and-pink bracts is absent, replaced by a thin bare wire carrying a small orange bead spike, and there is no knobby orange-fleshed rhizome anywhere.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and must not be fixed as described.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (440x440, measured by decoding the PNG, plus 4x-9x crops of the base, the blade edges and the spike): a single flat fan of about nine lanceolate blades all radiating from ONE point on the ground, over roughly 180 degrees. Green blade mass measures x104-342 by y185-327 = 239 px wide by 142 px tall, i.e. 1.7x WIDER THAN TALL, with the outermost left and right blades lying nearly horizontal and the ground shadow drawn as a flat ellipse under the convergence point. Rising from the same point is a bare dark-green wire stem that clears the foliage by ~90 px and carries an 11 x 46 px column of small yellow-orange beads (331 px total, hue ~30-45) at y93-138. Nothing else is in the frame.

MUST-READ 1 - 'fountain of broad upright ribbed leaves from ground level': FAILS, and the judge is right about the geometry. There is no fountain and no upright rise; it is a low splayed rosette/fan. Two further defects the judge did not name: (a) the blades are NOT on long sheathing stalks - there are no petioles or leaf sheaths at all, every blade springs from one bare point, so the pseudostem that makes a ginger read as a ginger is absent; (b) the venation is a dicot herringbone - one dark midrib with pinnate laterals branching off at ~45 degrees, clearly visible at 9x on every blade - where turmeric blades are 'ribbed', i.e. parallel longitudinal ribs running tip-to-base. Fixing the splay without fixing the venation and the sheathing stalks will not make it read as turmeric.

CORRECTION 1 - 'they are saw-toothed where turmeric blades are smooth-edged' is FALSE. At 9x magnification every individual blade has a perfectly entire, smooth margin - the right-hand outer blade is one long smooth curve from base to tip with no teeth, lobes or crenations anywhere. The saw-tooth appearance is purely a COMPOSITE SILHOUETTE artifact: the stacked lance blades overlap so their exposed tips form a zigzag along the top edge of the fan. Do not go 'de-serrate the leaves' - there is nothing to de-serrate; the fix is to stop the blades from stacking flat and to widen them.

CORRECTION 2 - 'it reads as nettle or mint' is also wrong. Nettle and mint are opposite-paired toothed leaves climbing an erect square stem; nothing here is paired and there is no leafy stem. What is actually on screen reads as a hosta / broadleaf-plantain rosette (or a small fan palm), topped by a Plantago-style bare flower scape. That matters because the wrong diagnosis points a fix at leaf margins instead of at leaf posture and blade width.

MUST-READ 2 - 'cone of pale green-and-pink bracts at the base': ABSENT, confirmed numerically. A full-image hue scan over all pixels with alpha>40, value>90 and saturation>0.2 returns ZERO pixels in the magenta/pink/red band (hue 290-360 and 0-20). The entire palette is 22,497 px at hue 90 (green), ~370 px at hue 105-150 (darker green veins/stem) and ~400 px at hue 30-45 (the bead spike). So there is no pink anywhere in the asset. The judge is correct that a thin wire with an orange bead spike stands in its place, and correct that the spike is not a bract cone - I would add that it is also in the WRONG PLACE: the bracted inflorescence belongs stout and low, nestled at the leaf bases, whereas this spike is lofted ~90 px clear ABOVE the foliage on a naked scape.

MUST-READ 3 - 'orange-fleshed rhizome': ABSENT, judge correct. The only orange in the image is the 331-px bead column at the top of the scape. The 6x crop of the base shows the blades converging to a bare point over a plain dark elliptical ground shadow - no knobby root mass, no cut face, no orange flesh, no soil line.

Two of the three must-reads are entirely absent and the third is inverted (splayed where it must rise, herringbone where it must be ribbed, stalkless where it must sheathe). FAIL stands. (Packet aspect 0.8 also asks for a form taller than wide; the drawn foliage is 1.7x wider than tall.)

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a bottlebrush
rows.defect: The tall unbranched stem and the opposite pinnate ladder are present, but the flat-domed pale pink flower head — the crown identity and the harvest — is a tiny white pill barely wider than the stem, roughly a twentieth of the plant's width, with no dome, no florets and no pink. The leaflet ladder is so mechanically uniform (same blade, same pitch, top to bottom, no size gradient) that the silhouette reads as a single fern frond rather than a flowering herb, and it is the same asset as Yarrow in a different green.

rows.readsAs: the same fern frond as Valerian, one shade greyer
rows.defect: This is Valerian's render with a hue shift — same stem, same shadow, same rung count and pitch, same white apex pill — so a stranger cannot tell the two apart, and neither yarrow must-read survives. The foliage is discrete little oval leaflets in a coarse ladder, not the feather-fine thrice-divided ferny fuzz that is yarrow's signature, and the flat dense PLATE of tiny white florets is reduced to a dot narrower than the leaf spread, when it should be the widest element in the silhouette. The stem is a smooth clean line with no stiff hairiness.

rows.verifyWhy:
I read Yarrow.png at full size, then re-cropped and 6x-upscaled the apex (x150-290, y45-165) and the mid-column (y150-270), and ran a pixel diff against Valerian.png. The FAIL stands, and the judge's structural claim is substantially correct, but two of their details need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A single straight dark-olive stem, 4px wide, running from a flat black base-shadow ellipse (y~350) to a bare apex at y~85. Along y=110-305 the stem carries ~23 opposite rungs at a uniform ~8px pitch (measured peaks: 116,123,132,141,149,156,164,173,181,189,197,204,213,221,230,239,250,259,267,279,291,298,305). Each rung is a straight rachis spur angled up-and-out, bearing roughly 8-9 DISCRETE oval leaflets, colour 152,176,136 (a correct pale grey-green per the spec's leafColour). The leaflets are simple beans -- once-pinnate, with no secondary division into thread segments. At the top of a bare 25px section of stem sits a white cap: measured pure-white pixels span x205-235 (w=31px) by y75-84 (h=10px). It is a shallow CRESCENT/dome sitting on a dark triangular receptacle cone, not a flat plate.

MUST-READS. (1) 'ferny feather-fine foliage' -- NOT MET. Real yarrow is bi-to-tripinnate; the foliage should dissolve into a soft thread-fine plume with no countable units. Here every leaflet is individually countable at native size. The spec also says the leaves 'clasp an upright stem'; these do not clasp -- they are borne on projecting rachis spurs, which is Valerian's arrangement. (2) 'a flat dense plate of tiny white daisy florets' -- NOT MET, and this is the fatal one. The corymb is 31px wide against a foliage spread of 66-68px, i.e. LESS THAN HALF the width of the leaf column and about 7% of image width. Yarrow's corymb is the single most diagnostic thing about the plant and should be the WIDEST element in the silhouette; here it is a token pill on a stick. It also reads as one solid domed lozenge, with zero granulation into individual florets, and it is convex rather than flat-topped. (3) 'stiff hairy upright stems' -- half met: upright and stiff yes, but the stem is a perfectly smooth 4px bar with no hair or bristle texture at all.

VALERIAN COMPARISON -- the judge is right on the substance, wrong in two particulars. Same chassis is confirmed: Valerian has 22 rungs at the same ~8px pitch against Yarrow's 23; both stems are the same 4px olive bar; both base shadows are the same ellipse; both apex caps are the same crescent-on-a-cone at nearly identical size (Yarrow 31x10 at y75-84, Valerian 30x11 at y79-89). So 'same stem, shadow, rung count and white apex pill' is accurate. TWO CORRECTIONS. First, the difference is not hue ALONE: Yarrow's leaflets are visibly smaller and packed denser, so its column edge holds a near-constant width of 65-68px down its whole length, whereas Valerian's rungs pinch between tiers and its width oscillates 45-74px and reads as a more open ladder. Yarrow is therefore the denser, more plume-like of the two -- it is just nowhere near feather-fine. Second, the hue difference is not a defect to be dismissed: Yarrow's 152,176,136 grey-green vs Valerian's 101,136,79 mid-green, and Yarrow's pure-white cap vs Valerian's pink-tinted one, are both exactly what each species' spec asks for. The failure is that correct colour is doing all the differentiating work while the shape does none.

FIX DIRECTION. Two changes, in priority order. (a) Widen the corymb to be the widest element in the silhouette -- a flat-topped plate roughly 90-110px wide (wider than the 66-68px foliage), with a hard flat top edge and a shallow underside, granulated into many tiny white dots rather than one smooth lozenge; it should read as a dinner plate seen at a slight angle, not a pill. (b) Replace the once-pinnate oval leaflets with a bipinnate treatment: subdivide each leaflet into 3-5 thread-thin segments (1px) so no discrete unit is countable, and bring the whole plume tight against the stem so it clasps rather than projects on visible spurs. Fixing (a) alone would already break the Valerian collision, since the corymb becomes the dominant silhouette mass; fixing both is what earns a PASS.

rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. There is no claw holdfast and no rock — the whole plant narrows to a single point on bare ground. The colour is mustard-gold, not olive-brown to dark chocolate. The three flat ellipse blobs pasted on the midline belong to Sargassum's float description and are the wrong feature on the wrong asset.
rows.fix: Rebuild as three elements: a splayed root-like claw gripping a rock at the base, a clear narrow stipe above it, and a single wide dark-brown strap blade split into finger segments that is at least three times wider than the stipe.

rows.readsAs: a furled crimson umbrella or a bundle of red spaghetti stood on end
rows.defect: The colour is right — deep crimson with a purplish sheen. Everything structural is wrong. The identity must-read is fine, repeatedly forking branch structure, and there is not one fork anywhere in the image: the fronds are eight straight parallel rods running the full height without dividing once. The small disc holdfast is absent; the bundle converges to a bare point. The dark tips at the top read as burnt or clipped ends rather than frond apices.
rows.fix: Replace the parallel rods with a repeatedly dichotomous branch tree — each frond forking into two at least three times up the height — and seat it on a small flat crimson disc holdfast.

rows.readsAs: a furled golden umbrella; visually the same object as Kelp with the blobs removed
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is present. There are no round pea-like gas floats on short stalks anywhere — ironically those blobs were drawn onto the Kelp asset instead. There are no toothed narrow leaf-like blades along the branches; there are no branches at all, only the same eight parallel unbranched rods. The mass is neither bushy nor tangled but tight, closed and symmetrical. Only the golden-olive colour is correct, and it is nearly the same value as Kelp's, so the two assets are not tellable apart.
rows.fix: Open the silhouette into a bushy tangle of forking branches and hang clusters of small round stalked berry floats plus narrow toothed blades along them, so the floats are the first thing the eye finds.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon bug / mascot beetle with one big googly eye — nobody says 'leafcutter'
rows.defect: The identity must-read is simply not drawn: there is NO leaf fragment carried overhead anywhere in the frame. The thorax is a plain smooth ovoid with zero backward-pointing spines. There is no pinched narrow waist — head and thorax overlap directly and the gaster hangs off a straight leg-thickness bar instead of a petiole node. The head has no mandibles or cutting jaws at all; instead it carries a single huge vertebrate-style eye with a white highlight, and the antennae sprout out of that eye socket as smooth backswept whiskers with a crook at the tip rather than as elbowed (geniculate) antennae with a long scape. Two of the six legs attach to the head and three to the gaster, so only one leaves the thorax; the gaster is a vertically striped beach-ball.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as an ant rig: put all six legs on the thorax with a visible femur/tibia elbow, cut a true pinched two-node petiole between thorax and gaster, add the backward-pointing propodeal spines on the thorax, replace the single mammal eye with a small compound eye plus a pair of forward cutting mandibles and elbowed antennae — and above all, add the semicircular green leaf fragment held overhead in those jaws, since that silhouette IS the species.

rows.readsAs: a small rust-coloured cartoon spider
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads are present. The body is two fat spheres with a deep waist between them, not a flat unsegmented teardrop wedge - the silhouette is round and tall where a tick is a low flat plate. There are no mouthparts of any kind: the front sphere is a bare ball with no capitulum, no palps and no barbed hypostome spear jutting ahead, so the single feature that IS the tick is absent. The legs are not bunched toward the front - they fan symmetrically fore and aft like a spider's, and they pass behind the spheres so they never visibly attach. A 2x2 cluster of four glossy black eyes is painted on the front ball although the reference calls for hidden eyes, and no deer tick has that. Rendered aspect is roughly 1.3, not the specified 2.2.
rows.fix: Redraw as a single low flat teardrop shield - one unsegmented body, wide at the rear and tapering forward, no waist, no eye dots - and put a short barbed spear (hypostome flanked by two stubby palps) projecting past the front point, with all eight legs crowded into the front third of the body.

rows.readsAs: a pale cream cartoon spider
rows.defect: It is the Deer Tick image recoloured with longer legs - same two spheres, same 2x2 eye dots in the same position on the front ball, same mottled blotching on the rear ball, same stick legs, same shadow. The defining pycnogonid trait is inverted: the body here is the largest, fattest part of the animal instead of being reduced to a thin stick between the legs, so nothing suggests that the gut and gonads have migrated into the limbs. There is no proboscis at all - no long tubular sucking tube at the front, just a bare rounded ball - and no small ocular turret carrying the four eyes; the eyes are flat dots painted on the sphere. The legs, while longer, are still the same two-segment sticks with no joints, no claws and no visible attachment to a segmented trunk.
rows.fix: Shrink the body to a narrow segmented rod barely wider than a leg, hang four pairs of very long jointed legs off visible lateral tubercles along that rod, and add a proboscis at least as long as the trunk projecting forward with a small four-eyed turret on top.

rows.readsAs: a numbat, or a striped short-legged cat
rows.defect: There is no armour anywhere. The bands are flat painted vertical stripes on a soft furry barrel with a fuzzy hair fringe along the topline and belly — no raised overlapping plate edges, no shadowed band gaps, no scapular or pelvic shield, no domed carapace breaking the topline. The topline is a smooth soft arc identical to a generic quadruped. The tail is a thin smooth up-curling cat tail with no rings or taper-plating, and the snout is only mildly pointed with a soft rounded ear rather than the long tube-snout and small tubular ears called for.
rows.fix: Rebuild the mid-back as hard geometry: a domed keratin carapace with a front and rear shield and 6-8 discrete banded plates between them, each band a crisp overlapping arc with a dark shadow line under its trailing edge, the band stack visibly stepping the topline; then run the same plating down the tail as tapering rings and lengthen the snout into a narrow tube.

rows.readsAs: a guinea pig or hamster taped under a dowel
rows.defect: The identity feature is entirely missing — the long hooked scythe claws. Both limbs terminate as blunt flat-topped rectangular straps that butt into the underside of the branch; nothing curls over or grips it, and there is no claw geometry of any kind. Only two limbs exist; the hind pair is absent. The limbs are featureless parallelogram slabs with no shoulder, elbow or wrist, so the body reads as an oval hung on two ribbons rather than a long-armed animal. The face is wrong too: a pointed rodent muzzle with a single bead eye on the side of the head instead of the small flat round forward-facing face with dark eye stripes and a faint smile. The fur is uniform pale cream with no greenish algal cast.
rows.fix: Replace the two straps with four long curved arms whose ends close into two or three big hooked scythe claws visibly wrapping over the top of the branch, and flatten the muzzle into a round forward-facing disc face with dark eye patches.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon mouse with paper wings; 'a bat', but nobody says flying fox
rows.defect: The fox face is not there. The skull is a smooth dome and the muzzle is a short blunt bump with a single dot nose - a mouse/teddy snout, not the long tapering dog muzzle that IS the flying-fox read, and the ears are little round mouse ears rather than the small neat naked ears set low on a long head. The clawed thumb at the wing bend is entirely absent: the leading edge runs unbroken to a bare point. The finger bones are only three straight hairlines fanning from the elbow that fade out before reaching the trailing edge, so the membrane reads as folded card stock, not a stretched hand.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: pull the muzzle out to roughly a third of the head length as a tapering fox snout with a wet dark nose and a visible jaw line, shrink and lower the ears, and hook a distinct clawed thumb up off the top bend of each wing.

rows.readsAs: a Halloween sticker vampire bat - the trope, not the animal
rows.defect: The face has no face. Where the must-read flat pig-like nose pad should sit there is nothing at all: a featureless ball with two dots and no muzzle, so the short conical snout is missing too. What carries the read instead is exactly the thing the note forbids - two long white Dracula canines hanging clear of the jawline, where a real vampire bat shows small chisel incisors inside a stubby snub muzzle. The long thumbs are absent; the wrists are bare points, so the walking/wrist-propping anatomy that makes this species distinctive never appears. Only the tall pointed ears are correct, and they are the sole thing distinguishing this render from the Fruit Bat.
rows.fix: Give it a face: a stubby forward snub muzzle capped by the flat heart-shaped nose pad with two slit nostrils, replace the protruding canines with a small pale incisor pair tucked at the lip, and add a chunky clawed thumb standing up at each wrist.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy tan blob with a spine halo - a porcupine or a hedgehog-boar, not a bear
rows.defect: The pelage is drawn as long straight bristles radiating outward past the body edge, so the silhouette reads as quills rather than fur. The body is a featureless ellipse with the highest point at MID-BACK, so the must-read shoulder hump over the forelegs is absent. The legs are two flat rectangular planks of uniform width that are pasted over the ellipse and simply stop, with no shoulder or haunch mass and no plantigrade paw - just a stub end with white claw dashes. No stub tail visible. Only the head (rounded ear, black nose, dished brow) reads as ursine.
rows.fix: Replace the two rectangular planks with real limbs - a heavy shoulder mass feeding a foreleg that ends in a long flat plantigrade paw resting on its whole sole - and raise the topline's peak forward to sit over the forelegs so the hump becomes the tallest point.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld as FAIL, but THREE of the four stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed against. Corrections first, then the real defects.

WRONG #1 - 'the must-read shoulder hump is absent, the topline peaks at mid-back.' It does not. I traced the silhouette column-by-column: the animal spans x=96..350 in the 440px frame; the topline minimum-y (highest point) is y=130 at x=228-234, and the front leg plank occupies x=225-255. The crest is therefore DIRECTLY over the foreleg station, and it sits ~15px above the mid-back/rump line (y=143 at x=180, y=147-168 at x=120-160). The front of the animal is the tallest point. It is understated - it is the crest of a forward-tilted egg rather than a sculpted muscular mass, and there is a second, LOWER rounded nape blob between it and the skull (top y~136 at x~280) that can be mistaken for the shoulder - but 'hump absent' is false. The fix here is 'deepen/sculpt the existing hump', not 'add a missing one'.

WRONG #2 - 'two legs.' There are four. At each of the two leg stations a near plank and a far, darker-shaded plank are drawn side by side (rear station: dark plank x~131-150 plus light plank x~151-181; front station same arrangement). The near/far pairing is visible at 5x on both stations.

WRONG #3 - 'no plantigrade paw.' Every visible foot terminates in a flat horizontal elliptical ground-contact pad - a genuine plantigrade sole, not a hoof or a point - and each carries a row of four pale claws projecting forward off the toe end. That must-read is drawn. Its problem is execution, not absence: the claws are near-pure white against the mud palette so they read as a strip of teeth/pill beads, and the plank meets the pad at its midpoint instead of at a heel, so the foot looks like a disc pasted under a stick.

CORRECT in their claim: the pelage and the missing tail.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS:
1. LIMB MODEL. The four legs are untapered rectangles of constant width from body to ankle - no elbow, no hock, no knee, no shoulder mass, no thigh, no blend at the top (you can see the plank's straight top edge terminate under the belly ellipse). They are also far too thin and too long for a bear: the body is a fat egg standing on four stilts with a big belly-to-ground gap. A bear's limbs are massive columns continuous with the torso; these are the generic quadruped chassis and read closer to a table or a pony than a bear. Additionally the rear station sits ~40% of body length forward of the rump, so the entire hindquarters overhangs unsupported.
2. PELAGE / SILHOUETTE. The fur is a ring of long, straight, dark bristles set perpendicular to the body outline around the ENTIRE perimeter - standing straight up as a crest along the topline, fanning backward off the rump, hanging as a straight fringe under the belly. At up to ~20px on a 250px-long animal they are ~8% of body length. They do quill-ify the outline; the rump fan plus dorsal crest is exactly the porcupine cue. I would not go as far as 'reads as a porcupine' (the ursine head, rounded ears and clawed flat paws hold the read), but the silhouette is destroyed and the shoulder hump is buried inside the bristle halo, which is a large part of why the previous judge could not see it.
3. NO STUB TAIL. Confirmed at 5x on the rump - the rear of the ellipse is bare outline plus bristles, nothing protruding. Half of must-read #3 is simply not drawn.
4. HEAD IS NOT BROAD OR DISHED. The skull is a plain rounded blob and the muzzle is a smooth CONVEX cone with a small dark oval nose, reading mildly canid/foxy. There is a visible rectangular seam where the lighter muzzle patch is composited over the head. The ears are correct and should be left alone: small, low, rounded, with a near and a far ear both visible as overlapping arcs at the top-rear of the skull. The eye is small in absolute terms but is drawn with a full white sclera ring which reads cartoon rather than the small dark bear eye.

NET: it is recognisably a bear-ish quadruped, so the organism read is not lost the way the previous judge described, but the limbs are a bare chassis with no anatomy, the pelage breaks the outline, the stub tail is absent and the dished face is absent. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a grey Herdwick sheep or a hornless ram
rows.defect: The sheep chassis: level topline, woolly barrel, four stilt legs off the corners, hoof-like nubs for feet. Every must-read misses. The facial profile is not straight - the muzzle is a heavy dark snout that turns down and curls forward like a ram's nose, and it is charcoal, not tan. The rump is NOT higher than the shoulders; the topline is flat and the front is the taller end because of the head mass, which is the brown-bear silhouette the note explicitly warns against. There are no ears at all on the head - the round pale shape by the eye is a face patch, not a tall rounded ear. No claws; the feet are dark cloven nubs.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a bear body - drop the barrel onto plantigrade feet with visible toes and claws, arch the topline so the hindquarters are the high point, and give it a straight tan-muzzled face with two tall rounded ears standing clear of the skull.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but three of the four stated causes are wrong or imprecise and would send a fix at the wrong targets. I read the PNG at 1x and then re-cropped/upscaled the head (5x and 8x), the muzzle, both foot groups and the rump, and measured the silhouette's top edge per column programmatically.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS: a grey woolly Herdwick/Swaledale-type sheep or ram. Deep barrel trunk covered edge-to-edge in fine directional flecked FLEECE texture, four long slim straight evenly-tapering columnar legs with no haunch and no forearm bulk, a dark charcoal head carried high on a short neck, dark hoof-like foot tips. Cross-check: Brown_Bear.png in the same family is the IDENTICAL chassis recoloured tan — same barrel, same fleece flecking, same two dark face ovals, same down-curled snout, same hoof feet. The bear family is one sheep chassis in N colours; fixing this asset means replacing the chassis, not retouching features.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM:

1. 'The rump is NOT higher than the shoulders (topline is flat, front is taller)' — HALF WRONG. Measured on the alpha silhouette (canvas 440x440, body bbox x=92..346, head on the RIGHT so rump is on the LEFT): trunk topline min-y is 167 at x=148-156 (hindquarter) versus 170-172 at x=196-220 (withers/shoulder). So the rump IS technically the highest point of the trunk — by 4 px on a 255-px-long animal, under 2%. The must-read still fails, but because the differential is IMPERCEPTIBLE, not because it is inverted. 'Front is taller' is false for the trunk (the trunk's front is 3-5 px LOWER); what makes the front look taller is the HEAD dome at y=115, carried well above the whole back. Fix = exaggerate the hindquarter rise into a visible arch over the pelvis and drop the head below the shoulder line, not flip the topline.

2. 'There are no ears at all on the head — the pale round shape is a face patch' — WRONG ON BOTH HALVES. (a) The pale round shape is the EYE: at approx x=272 y=157 there is a small cream/tan sclera ring with a black pupil and a white catchlight. It is not a patch. (b) Ears ARE drawn: two dark charcoal rounded ovals sit side by side on the upper face, roughly x=248-268 and x=278-292, y=128-155, the rear one larger and crescent-notched. They fail for two other reasons — they are charcoal-on-charcoal (near-zero luminance separation from the skull, invisible below ~8x zoom), and they sit entirely INSIDE the head mass so the skull silhouette carries zero ear protrusion. At full size they read as a lemur/panda eye-patch pair. The must-read 'tall rounded ears' fails, but the fix is contrast + breaking the ears out above the skull outline, not adding ears from nothing. There is also a lighter grey angular flap notched into the back-left of the skull (approx x=228-245, y=125-175) that reads as a cheek/jaw plate; it is not a readable ear either.

3. 'Feet are cloven nubs with no claws' — HALF WRONG. Each foot does end in a near-black rounded pad, but there IS a claw element: a single pale cream horizontal RECTANGULAR bar projects forward from the toe of the front-most foot of each pair (visible on both the fore and hind groups). It is one flat straight dash, not 'short curved claws' plural, and at full size it reads as a hoof toe-cap highlight rather than claws. The 'cloven' impression comes from two overlapping dark lobes per foot group, which are actually the near-leg and far-leg feet, not a split hoof. The real defect is that the foot is a small rounded hoof-scale terminal with no flat plantigrade sole and no separated digits.

4. 'Facial profile is a down-curled charcoal ram snout rather than straight with a tan muzzle' — CORRECT, and confirmed at 8x. From the brow the profile bulges convex over the nasals then curls downward to a large dark ellipse nose with a highlight; a classic Roman/ram nose. There is no tan muzzle anywhere: the muzzle is mid-grey in the same charcoal family as the skull, with only the faintest warm tint. A thin straight dark line runs from the nose corner back across the cheek as the mouth, reading as a stitched-on stroke rather than a jawline.

DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NAME: (a) COLOUR — this is a BLACK bear rendered in pale-to-mid GREY; nothing on the animal is black except the foot tips, and the fleece flecking actively fights the idea of a bear's flat dense black coat. (b) The tail is a flat dark-grey angular wedge pasted on the rear of the rump (approx x=92-125, y=195-265) that reads as a rump shadow patch or a docked sheep tail, not a bear's stub. (c) Limb geometry is ungulate throughout — straight columns, no elbow/hock articulation, no bear's low-slung heavy-boned stance.

BAND: FAIL upheld. All three must-reads fail (no straight profile and no tan muzzle; rump-over-shoulder differential is 4 px and unreadable; ears carry neither contrast nor silhouette and the claw is a single flat bar). The organism itself reads as the wrong species, which is a FAIL condition independent of the must-read tally.

rows.readsAs: a tan-fleeced ram - the curled muzzle even reads as a horn
rows.defect: Identical sheep chassis, recoloured tan. There is no shoulder hump whatsoever - the topline runs flat and the withers are the same height as the rump, so the diagnostic that the note calls out as THE identity is absent. The face is not dished or broad-browed; it is a dark mask with a heavy blunt snout that rolls forward into a spiral that a stranger reads as the base of a ram's horn. No long pale digging claws - the feet are two tiny dark hoof nubs. The legs are smooth pipes with no elbow, wrist or digits.
rows.fix: Build the muscular hump as an actual mass of shoulder over the forelegs so it is the tallest point of the silhouette, and terminate the forelegs in a broad flat paw with a fan of long pale claws.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, but three of the four stated causes are wrong in detail and must not be fixed as described. Measured silhouette (bg-diff bbox on the 440px PNG): body+head x86-353, y97-328, so w268 x h232, aspect 1.16 against a spec aspect of 1.5. The head occupies x222-353 = 131px of 268 total length (~49%) against headFrac 0.27, and its crown sits at y97 while the back sits at y179 — the head is carried a full 82px ABOVE the topline on an upright neck. That alert, high-carried, oversized head on slim columnar legs is the single biggest reason the asset reads ovine/caprine rather than ursine; no bear carries its skull above its back line. CORRECTION 1 — the shoulder hump is NOT 'completely absent' and the back is NOT 'a flat line with withers level with the rump'. Per-column topline: rump crest y179-180 across x134-158, a shallow saddle y181-183 at x162-186, then a continuous rise to y163-155 at x210-218 (verified in a 6x crop of x150-260,y130-260 — that rise is pale fleece, not head overlap). So the withers ARE the tallest point of the trunk, by roughly 16-24px (~12% of the 173px trunk height). The real defect is that the rise is a gentle unbroken ramp that merges straight into the neck instead of a discrete rounded mass sitting OVER the forelegs, and it is visually annihilated by the head towering 80px above it. Fix = make it a distinct convex boss above the foreleg with a clear dip behind it, and drop the head onto the shoulder line; do not 'add a hump to a flat back' — a rise already exists. CORRECTION 2 — there is NO 'dark mask' and nothing 'spirals'. At 9x (x225-315, y90-170) the two dark shapes on the skull resolve as the TWO EARS: the near one is a raised rounded tan pinna with a dark inset oval, the far one is a second dark oval without the pale rim. They are correctly rounded and bear-like in shape, but they are drawn flush on the skull surface (they never break the silhouette) and are placed far too low and far too forward — the near ear sits immediately behind and above the eye, exactly where a ram's horn boss would be, which is what produced the judge's 'horn base' misread. The face itself is a uniform sand/tan with no mask whatsoever. The judge IS right that the profile is not dished: from brow to nose the outline runs straight-to-slightly-convex over a long blunt rounded muzzle ending in a large dark-brown nose with nostril dots and a thin mouth line — a generic carnivore snout, not the concave brow-to-nose dish with a broad flat forehead the note demands. The skull also narrows toward the crown rather than being broad-browed. CORRECTION 3 — pale claws are PRESENT, not absent, but vestigial. Each foot terminates in a dark chocolate-brown rounded paw ellipse (the near forefoot shows two overlapping dark lobes = two toes) carrying exactly ONE small white dash on its leading edge, roughly 8x3 source pixels, visible only at 12x. That is a single blunt pale nub, not the 'long straight pale digging claws' the mustRead requires, and at any shipped size it disappears. The feet are also not literal hooves as claimed — they are dark rounded paw lobes — but they are small, dark and set on straight untapered cylindrical legs with no visible wrist, hock or flat forward-projecting plantigrade sole, so they still read as hoof nubs, and the dark-on-pale contrast makes them read as cloven at distance. Also noted: no tail stub at all (the rump at 9x is a clean unbroken curve), and the coat is rendered as long streaky lifted hair over a pale cream ground, which reads as fleece rather than dense brown bear pelage. Verdict: of the three mustReads, the dished broad-browed face is genuinely absent, the pale digging claws are present only as an unreadable 8px tick, and the hump exists but is not prominent and does not read; combined with a 49%-of-body head held above the topline and a fleece-textured pale coat, the organism reads as a woolly hoofed animal, not a brown bear.

rows.readsAs: a brown Herdwick sheep, indistinguishable from the Brown Bear asset except for a slightly warmer fleece
rows.defect: Same chassis again. The shoulder hump is missing - the back is a flat horizontal line, so the silhouette does not sit higher at the front and fails the note's own black-bear-opposite test. The facial profile is convex-and-curled, not dished concave. The 'long pale front claws' are two or three white hatch ticks at the hoof nubs, invisible at any normal viewing size. The grizzled fur is a flat tan wash with hair strokes, no silver-tipped guard-hair contrast. Read side by side with Brown Bear it is the same drawing.
rows.fix: Give it a distinct silhouette from Brown Bear by exaggerating the shoulder hump into a pronounced mound and adding real splayed front claws, plus pale-tipped guard hairs over a darker undercoat for the grizzle.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two of the four stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, subject bbox x82-357 y103-323, 276x221 px, rendered aspect 1.25 against a declared 1.8). The organism reads as a fleeced sheep/ram, not a bear. A barrel fleece body with a hard fleece-edge boundary running from the brisket around the flank; a separate head/neck block dropped on top of the shoulder; four slender straight columnar legs of near-equal length front and rear, each ending in a dark oval toe cap that reads as a cloven hoof tip; and NO TAIL AT ALL at the rump (I zoomed the rump at 7x - the hindquarter is a plain fleece curve plus a flat tan haunch plate, no stub, no nub).

SAME-CHASSIS CLAIM: CONFIRMED, and stronger than stated. Cropping the Grizzly head (x235-365) and the Brown Bear head (x220-360) at 5x and putting them side by side, they are the SAME construction part-for-part: identical low crescent saucer flap over the crown with the same small notch bitten out of its lower-rear edge, identical large dark round disc behind the eye, identical dark eye-patch oval with the same small ringed eye at its lower-front, identical stub muzzle with the same kidney-shaped dark nose, identical single thin mouth line. Toplines match too (Grizzly mid-back y=186 -> shoulder y=160; Brown Bear mid-back y=180 -> shoulder y=154). It is one drawing with a coat recolour.

CORRECTION 1 - "No shoulder hump (flat horizontal back)" is WRONG as described. The back is not flat. Column-scanning the top edge: rump y=227 at x=82, rising to y=184-186 across the mid-back x=127-202, then rising again to y=160-164 at x=232-242 where the neck takes over. That is a real ~25px rise, and the front IS the tallest part of the body. The defect is different: it is a smooth gradual RAMP into the neck, not a discrete muscular bulge sitting over the forelegs, and - decisively - it is the identical ramp the Black Bear has (mid-back y=168 -> shoulder y=158) and the Brown Bear has. So the note's black-bear-opposite test does fail, but because all three bears share one topline, not because this one is flat. Fixing a "flat back" would produce no change; what is needed is a distinct convex withers mass whose apex sits AHEAD of the mid-back and clears the neck line, plus a genuinely rump-high Black Bear to contrast against.

CORRECTION 2 - "Fur is a flat wash with no grizzled guard-hair contrast" is WRONG. At 3x the coat is a dense directional hatch of pale blond/cream strokes over a mid-tan ground, with clearly readable light-tip contrast across the whole barrel; it is in fact the MOST grizzled coat of the three brown-bear-type assets, and paler than the Brown Bear's rather than "marginally warmer". The grizzled-fur half of must-read #3 is satisfied. Do not spend a fix pass adding hatch that is already there - the problem is that the hatch is applied to a fleece shape.

CORRECTION 3 - claw count. Not "two white hatch ticks". At 12x each foot carries a row of about five near-white ticks that do overhang the front edge of the dark toe cap, so pale claws are present in principle. They fail on scale and placement: the whole row is roughly 10x3 px on a 276px-long animal (~3.5% of body length, versus a real grizzly's claws at ~10-12% of forefoot length and highly conspicuous), they sit on top of the toe cap rather than emerging from a toe pad, and the identical row is repeated on BOTH HIND FEET, which contradicts the must-read's "front claws" and erases the front/hind claw asymmetry that is a grizzly signature.

MUST-READ VERDICT: (1) muscular hump over the shoulders - NOT READABLE as a hump (present only as an undifferentiated neck ramp shared with the black bear). (2) dished concave facial profile - ABSENT, and the judge is right here: the head zoom shows a domed forehead stepping down onto a muzzle whose upper edge bulges CONVEXLY out to the nose, a ram/roman profile; a dished face requires the nasal bridge to fall below the brow-to-nosetip chord and it plainly does not. (3) long pale front claws AND grizzled fur - split: grizzled fur PASSES, long pale front claws FAIL on size and are wrongly duplicated on the hind feet.

Also worth logging for the fix (not a listed must-read, so not the basis of the verdict): the ear is a large flat crescent flap lying against the crown plus a dark disc, breaking no part of the silhouette. A bear's ear must be small, round and stand PROUD of the skull outline. The limbs are the same slender ungulate columns used across the family and need the short, heavy, bent plantigrade bear limb with a flat foot on the ground.

Two of three must-reads absent or unreadable, the head is a ram's head, the feet are hooves, there is no tail, and the drawing is byte-for-byte the Brown Bear chassis. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a black-and-white sheep - a Jacob or badger-faced ewe wearing a dark blanket

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL stands, but the stated causes are substantially wrong and must not be fixed as written. I decoded the PNG (440x440) and sampled pixels, then re-rendered a tint map classifying every dark-marking pixel red.

CORRECTION 1 (the judge's central claim, and it is FALSE): 'ALL FOUR LEGS ARE WHITE' is wrong. All four legs are filled with the SAME black ink as the eye patches and the shoulder mass -- RGB(21,24,30) sampled at hind leg (115,265) and foreleg (~230,270), identical to eye patch (266,155) and torso patch (230,215). The problem is contrast, not placement: the card background is RGB(6,9,15)-(9,14,20), so the 'black' is only ~15/15/13 above background. Against the dark card the black limbs disappear and only their pale hairline outlines and the mid-grey paw pads survive, which is exactly what produces the 'white stilts / Jacob sheep' illusion. The must-read 'black shoulder band joining black forelegs' IS drawn and IS topologically continuous (the chest mass flows straight into the near foreleg) -- it simply does not READ at delivered tone. Fix is tonal (lift the black ink so it separates from the card, or give limbs a real rim), not a re-placement of black onto white legs.

CORRECTION 2: 'a dark saddle over the shoulder/torso plus a rear-flank wedge' mis-describes the layout. There is NO rear-flank wedge and NO saddle -- the entire hindquarter and rump are white (sampled 242,243,242 at (110,175)), and the topline over the withers is white too. The actual marking is ONE black chest/shoulder mass spanning roughly x 222-290, y 178-265, plus four black legs. Two real defects there: (a) the band stops well below the topline instead of crossing the back over the withers -- at x=220 the back edge is y~154 but black does not begin until y~217; (b) the white torso's front edge is a RULER-STRAIGHT VERTICAL SEAM at x~224 from y~190 to y~250, a hard geometric artifact, not an organic band edge.

CORRECTION 3: 'no black round ears are visible' is half wrong. TWO round ears ARE drawn -- a mid-grey disc RGB(127,126,127) at approx x 250-268, y 138-165 and a light-grey disc RGB(206,203,204) at approx x 266-292 with a mauve inner pinna RGB(131,113,111). They are the wrong COLOUR (grey, not black) and in the wrong PLACE (sitting low on the forehead, overlapping the top edges of both eye patches, never breaking the head's silhouette). Fix = recolour to black and move to the crown so they notch the outline.

CONFIRMED from the judge: eye patches are flat perfect CIRCLES (~30px diameter), not teardrops. Worse than they said -- the single eye (tiny gold ring + pupil, ~(288,152)) sits BETWEEN the two patches on bare white face, inside neither. Also confirmed the leggy stance: torso is ~136x102px (reasonably deep and barrel-like, so 'not round and bulky' is overstated -- the head is in fact a near-perfect round white disc and reads very well), but the legs run ~50px, half the torso height, thin, straight and splayed with the pairs crossing, so the proportion is ovine/pony, not the panda's low stumpy stance. Topline is genuinely flat from x~150 to x~225.

NOT MENTIONED BY THE JUDGE, both in the asset's favour: the packet note's tail IS satisfied -- a small pale wedge tail nub sits at the lower rear of the rump around (95-110, 205-225). And the paws are NOT hooves: at 10x each paw is a mid-grey oval pad with a row of four to five tiny pale CLAWS at the leading tip. The grey pads still hurt (they read as shoes against black legs; panda paws should be black), but do not attribute a hoof.

BAND: FAIL held because at delivered tone the identity collapses -- the black limbs vanish, leaving a white barrel with a detached black shoulder wedge and a panda-ish head, which is the wrong organism at a glance. Ordered fixes: (1) lift the black ink off the card background; (2) carry the band OVER the withers and kill the vertical seam at x~224; (3) eye patches to slanted teardrops with the eye INSIDE each; (4) ears black, on the crown, off the eye patches; (5) legs ~35% shorter, thicker, un-splayed, black paws.

UPHELD. I looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 5x crops of the head and the feet, then rendered Polar_Bear beside Bear, Black_Bear and Sloth_Bear. The organism reads as a white sheep/lamb. All three stated must-reads fail, and the third one (which the original judge did not mention) fails too.

CHASSIS: Polar Bear, Black Bear and Sloth Bear are pixel-for-pixel the SAME body with only hue changed - same barrel with a dead-flat topline, same four thin straight tubular legs, same two-toe grey hoof nubs, same big round masked skull welded to the front of the barrel with a hooked snout and an oversized round nose. Correction to the claim: it is NOT 'every sibling' - Bear (#1) is a different and older chassis (a fluffy oval blob on four column legs with plantigrade white-toed pads), so the sheep chassis is at least the Black/Sloth/Polar cluster, not the whole family. That distinction matters for the fix: the sheep chassis is what has to be replaced, and #1 is not the model to copy either.

MUST-READ 1, 'long neck with a small narrow Roman-nosed head' - FAILS. The head is huge, not small: it spans roughly 120px of a ~303px body, headFrac ~0.40 against a spec of 0.21, nearly double. Its shape is a round dome cranium with a short bulbous muzzle that hooks DOWNWARD to a big round black nose - a ram/sheep curl, the opposite of the long narrow tapering Roman-nosed polar bear skull. Partial correction on the neck: there IS a short angled neck wedge visible behind the jaw and the head does sit raised above and forward of the topline, so it is not literally welded flush - but it is a thick stubby junction, nothing that reads as the long low-slung polar bear neck, so the judge's verdict on this point stands even though 'no neck at all' overstates it. On the mask: the same face-panel geometry as Black/Sloth is there, but because it is white-on-white it survives only as a faint grey seam running from behind the eye down the cheek to the jaw plus a slightly raised crown panel - a fix must not assume a visible dark mask to delete, it is a shape seam.

MUST-READ 2, 'huge furred paws' - FAILS, and this is the loudest defect. These are the smallest feet in the batch. Correction of detail: they are not single 'dark hoof nubs'. Each leg ends in a pale wedge with a grey sole PLUS a separate grey nub set behind it - a two-toe CLOVEN hoof pair, identical to the feet on Black Bear and Sloth Bear. Reading them as cloven is what pushes the whole silhouette over into 'sheep'. Nothing furred, nothing broad, no toes, no claws.

MUST-READ 3, 'sloping shoulders on a long body' - ALSO FAILS (unreported by the first judge). The topline is flat from rump to shoulder with no forward slope, and the whole animal measures roughly 1.5 long-to-tall against the spec aspect of 1.9, so the body is short and boxy rather than long.

TWO further defects not in the original claim: (a) a rigid grey/white ROD protrudes forward out of the mouth past the muzzle tip, reading as a straw or thermometer clenched in the teeth - a lip/mouth element drawn as a hard bar; it is present on Black Bear and Sloth Bear too, so it is a chassis bug not a one-off. (b) The eye area holds a plain grey dot next to a speckled brown/dark smear, so the face carries what looks like a second broken eye. (c) At the rump there is a detached grey rectangular slab where the stub tail should be.

Nothing here rescues the asset: the head, the feet and the proportions are all wrong in the same direction, and the direction is 'sheep'.

rows.readsAs: a scruffy grey sheep with a matted belly fleece
rows.defect: The long hanging belly hair is the one thing that lands, but it hangs from the sheep barrel and reads as an unshorn fleece rather than a shaggy coat, and there is no shoulder mane - the neck and withers are the smoothest part of the animal. The pale U or Y-shaped chest blaze is entirely absent; the chest is uniform grey. The muzzle is the family's short dark down-curled snout, not the long pale grey mobile snout the note says is unlike any other bear's. rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD as FAIL, but two of the stated causes are wrong and the real defects are worse than described.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, zoomed 5-8x on head, withers, chest, feet). The organism reads as a grey woolly SHEEP or RAM, not a bear: a rounded barrel torso covered edge-to-edge in pale grey-beige fleece strokes, a smooth rim-lit topline, four slim pale legs, and a small dark face carried at the front on a short neck. Silhouette, proportion and coat all say ovine.

COAT COLOUR (defect the original claim did not name at all): the must-read calls for a shaggy unkempt BLACK coat. The coat here is pale grey-beige/oatmeal over the whole body, lighter than the head. It is genuinely shaggy - long directional fur strokes plus sparse thin hair spikes that cross the topline and a fringe of hanging hairs under the belly and between the legs - so 'unshorn belly fleece' is a fair description, but the value is inverted from the reference. A pale fleece is the single largest contributor to the sheep read.

SHOULDER MANE - claim CORRECT in substance, slightly wrong in detail. There is no mane. At the withers the topline is a smooth continuous arc finished with a bright white rim-light stroke. It is not literally 'the smoothest area': a handful of thin hair spikes do protrude above the topline there, but at exactly the same sparse density as along the mid-back, so nothing reads as a raised shoulder mass. The highest point of the back is mid-body, not the withers.

CHEST BLAZE - claim CORRECT, with one correction. There is no pale U or Y. The chest and throat are the same pale fleece as the rest of the body. The chest is NOT quite 'uniform grey' however: there is a distinct DARKER grey angular wedge over the shoulder/upper foreleg (and a matching one on the rump). That wedge is the family's shared limb-attachment plate, not a marking - it is darker than the coat, so it cannot be mistaken for the blaze, and it actively occupies the place the blaze should be.

MUZZLE - claim WRONG as stated. It is not 'the family's short dark down-curled snout'. The head narrows into a clearly projecting broad muzzle roughly a third of the head's length, aimed forward and only very slightly downward, ending in a large dark rounded nose pad, with a thin straight mouth line running back from it. So it is neither short nor curled. It still fails the must-read on two counts: it is the SAME mid grey-brown as the rest of the head rather than pale/contrasting, and it is a blunt heavy wedge-and-blob rather than the long slender flexible protrusible tube the note calls for. Fix the muzzle's colour and taper, not its length.

HEAD MARKINGS: the dark face carries a thick dark crescent/arc low on the rear of the skull plus a separate dark oval above and behind the small ringed eye. Read together the crescent reads as a curled ram horn, which reinforces the sheep identity rather than any bear cue.

CLAWS - claim CORRECT and understated. Each foot terminates in TWO dark rounded ovals that read unmistakably as a cloven hoof, with a single tiny straight white horizontal dash at the front toe as the only claw. There is no plantigrade paw, no paw pad, and nothing curved or long. The hooves are a second major driver of the wrong-organism read.

FAMILY CONTEXT: I rendered Sun Bear at the same crop for comparison. It is the identical chassis - same barrel, same shoulder/rump plates, same slim legs, same two-oval hoof with the white dash, same skull and muzzle - differing only in fur texture density and head-marking placement. This asset is not an individually weak bear; it is one shared ovine chassis recoloured, and no per-species retouch of markings will rescue it. All three must-reads (black shaggy coat with shoulder mane / pale U-Y chest blaze / long pale mobile snout with huge curved claws) are absent or inverted.

rows.readsAs: a straw-coloured Herdwick sheep with a dark face
rows.defect: Sheep chassis with a dark head mask. The coat is not shaggy blackish - it is a pale straw-grey fleece, lighter than the head, so the value relationship is inverted from the reference. The pale eye ring does exist but it is the same generic round eye patch that appears on Black Bear, Brown Bear and Grizzly Bear, so it does not read as a species marking. The face is not short and rounded with a heavy muzzle; it is the family's forward-curling ram snout. Feet are hoof nubs, legs are jointless pipes, no tail.
rows.fix: Darken the coat to blackish-brown so the cream spectacles and chest drip read as the lightest values on the animal, and shorten the muzzle into a heavy blunt block instead of the curled snout.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the asset is worse than the claim states. I read the full 440px PNG, then 5x-8x nearest-neighbour crops of the head, the feet and the whole body, then built a 6-up comparison strip of Black/Brown/Grizzly/Sun/Sloth/Spectacled.

WHAT I SAW. Body: a barrel-shaped fleece torso in pale straw-putty (#b9ac9c-ish) covered in fine vertical hair striations with long loose wisps hanging off the belly line and standing up along the topline. High withers, level short back, tucked-up rear flank, slender straight legs of even thickness. Head is a darker warm grey-brown (#6f6055-ish) mounted high on a short neck, turned three-quarters toward the viewer, with a long wedge muzzle that tapers forward and DOWN to a rounded dark nose pad at the tip and a thin curving mouth line running back from it. Darker patches also sit on the shoulder and the hip. Total read: a Herdwick/Swaledale sheep. The claim's headline is right.

THE DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED, AND IT IS THE BIGGEST ONE. The feet are CLOVEN HOOVES. At 4x the front and hind feet are glossy dark two-toed hooves with a visible split down the middle and a tiny pale keratin sliver at the front edge, sitting on slender ungulate pasterns. There is no plantigrade paw anywhere on this animal - no broad flat sole, no furred toe pads, no claws. A bear that stands on hooves cannot be repaired by recolouring; the foot has to be rebuilt. Every one of the nine bears in this batch has the same hoof.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM.
(a) 'Coat is pale straw-grey, LIGHTER than the head' - CONFIRMED exactly. The body is markedly paler than the skull, which is the inverse of the required blackish coat with (at most) a pale face marking. But the claim implies shagginess is absent; it is not. The coat DOES carry long hanging shag strands off the belly and the flank. The shagginess is present and is the one must-read fragment that survives - it just reads as a fleece rather than bear fur because of the pale straw value and the sheep silhouette carrying it. The fix is the VALUE and the body form, not the addition of texture.
(b) 'The pale eye ring is the same generic patch that also appears on Black, Brown and Grizzly Bear' - RIGHT THAT IT IS GENERIC, WRONG ABOUT WHAT IT IS. What is actually shared across all six heads is a pair of DARK ovals sitting side by side across the brow/eye zone - goggles that are DARKER than the surrounding face, not pale. The only pale element on the head is a ~2px cream sclera outline around the single visible eyeball, which is the family-wide eye glyph and appears identically on Black, Brown, Grizzly, Sun and Sloth. So the required marking is not merely non-diagnostic here, its POLARITY IS INVERTED: the packet asks for pale cream rings on a blackish face, and the art delivers dark blobs on a mid-tone face. A fix that recolours the existing eye ring will not work; the face must be made dark and the cream spectacles drawn on top of it.
(c) 'Face is the shared forward-curling ram snout, not a short rounded face with a heavy muzzle' - CONFIRMED, and it is pixel-identical in shape across all six bears I strip-compared. No short rounded face, no heavy bear muzzle.

EARS (small feature, checked deliberately): there IS an ear - a small notched triangular flap at the rear-upper edge of the skull, plus a paler angular flap just forward of it. Present but non-diagnostic; not a reason to soften the band.

FAMILY CHASSIS FINDING. The 6-up strip is unambiguous: Black, Brown, Grizzly, Sun, Sloth and Spectacled Bear are ONE SHEEP BODY recoloured. Identical fleece torso outline, identical high-withers topline, identical slender legs, identical cloven hooves, identical darker skull with paired dark eye-ovals and the same forward-tapering ram muzzle. Brown and Grizzly are the same asset in two golden-tan tints. Spectacled Bear is that sheep in straw-grey. Zero of the three must-reads (pale cream eye rings / shaggy BLACKISH coat / short rounded face with heavy muzzle) are readable, and the organism itself is the wrong order - an ungulate, not a carnivoran. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a grey sheep - and one of the LARGEST-looking animals in a batch where it should read smallest

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD as FAIL on the identity must-reads, but ONE OF THE JUDGE'S THREE STATED CAUSES IS FACTUALLY WRONG and must not be fixed against.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 PNG, read at 1x then re-cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled 4x/6x/8x on head, chest, rump and feet).

ORGANISM READ - CONFIRMED WRONG. The animal is a barrel-shaped fleece body in pale-to-mid neutral grey, covered edge to edge in short vertical/diagonal hair flicks that render as carded wool, with a crisp pale rim-light along the topline. Set on four straight column legs that end in dark rounded nubs. The head is a separate near-black blocky mass carried face-on-to-three-quarter, with a flat trapezoid saucer ear notched at the back of the skull, TWO large dark ovals across the upper face (the ear pair drawn face-on), one tiny pale ring-highlight eye, and a short rounded muzzle boss with a single glossy nostril. Grey fleece body + dark face + ring eye + hoof nubs = a dark-faced sheep (Suffolk/Hampshire read), not a bear. The judge's 'grey sheep' is correct and if anything understated: the black head over a pale fleece makes the sheep read MORE specific, not less.

CHASSIS. I composited Brown Bear / Grizzly Bear / Sun Bear / Sloth Bear side by side. All four are ONE CHASSIS in four colours - identical fleece barrel with the same vertical flick texture, identical blocky face-on skull with the same trapezoid ear, the same paired dark ovals, the same ring eye, the same nostril boss, the same column legs and the same two-lobe hoof nub with a white tick. Only hue and scale change. This is the same single-chassis defect the packet header warns about.

MUST-READ 1 - 'golden-cream crescent patch on the chest': ABSENT. CONFIRMED at 8x on the chest/brisket. There is no cream, no gold, no crescent, no blaze of any kind anywhere on the animal. The only tonal event forward of the ribs is a flat mid-grey quadrilateral shoulder/foreleg wedge and the dark neck bib bleeding down from the head - both neutral grey-brown, neither crescent-shaped. The species' namesake mark is entirely missing. Judge correct.

MUST-READ 2 - 'short sleek jet-black coat': FAILS on BOTH axes. Colour: the trunk samples as pale/mid neutral grey, not black; only the head and a small throat bib approach black, so the value is inverted relative to a real sun bear (black body, PALE tan muzzle) - here the body is pale and the muzzle is dark. Texture: long shaggy striated fleece, the opposite of short and sleek. Judge correct.

MUST-READ 3 - 'very long curved climbing claws and blunt short muzzle': SPLIT. Claws FAIL - at 6x each foot is a dark rounded two-lobe nub with a tiny white hatch cluster sitting on top of the toe line; no length, no curve, no digit separation, reads as a cloven hoof with a highlight. Judge's description here is accurate. BUT the 'blunt short muzzle' half IS PRESENT and readable - a short rounded muzzle boss with a glossy nose, not an elongated snout. Do not report the whole must-read as absent.

JUDGE'S SIZE CLAIM - WRONG, DO NOT FIX AGAINST IT. The judge says it sits 'at proportions identical to Brown and Grizzly Bear' and 'looks like one of the largest animals in a batch where it should read smallest'. Measured subject bounding boxes on the source PNGs (hue-aware background rejection): Sun Bear 209x161, Sloth Bear 239x181, Panda 252x180, Black Bear 250x192, Bear 260x178, Brown Bear 268x231, Grizzly Bear 275x219, Polar Bear 299x211. Sun Bear has the SMALLEST footprint of all nine bears in the batch - roughly 78% of Brown Bear's width, 70% of its height, ~55% of its area - and this is obvious by eye in a side-by-side strip. The packet note 'the smallest bear' is HONOURED. The shared chassis SHAPE is real; the claim that it is drawn at the same scale, or reads as one of the largest, is not.

BAND. FAIL stands: the organism reads as the wrong animal (sheep), and the single defining namesake must-read (golden-cream chest crescent) is completely absent, with the coat inverted in both value and texture. Fixes should target coat colour/texture, the chest crescent, the claws, and the shared sheep chassis - NOT the overall scale, which is already correct.

One stray artefact worth noting for the fix pass: a short isolated black diagonal stroke sits on the outside of the near hind leg just above the pastern, unattached to any form - visible at 6x, reads as a rendering slip rather than a marking.

rows.readsAs: a dark brown gnat or small housefly

The body is not fat or bulky either; it is the same slim three-bead chassis as the other two, and the wings are LARGE and long (they cover the entire abdomen and extend past the tail), the exact opposite of the 'wings small relative to the bulky body' must-read. rows.readsAs: a bee-ish amber insect, or an amber hoverfly

rows.readsAs: a green housefly - the Honeybee asset recoloured green

rows.readsAs: a dark grey ladybug
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is present. The elytra are a flat uniform dark grey-brown with zero orange blotching — the black-and-orange banded pattern IS the identity of a burying beetle and it is entirely absent. rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld after direct inspection (read the 440x440 PNG, then re-read 4x and 2x gamma-lifted crops of the head and whole body, plus a pixel dump). WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a near-circular top-down beetle. Elytra bounding box measures x146-292 by y154-304 = 147 x 151 px, ratio 1.03 - essentially a circle. One vertical midline seam splits the wing cases; one crescent specular highlight sits on the LEFT elytron only; a thin rim-light arc runs down each outer edge; the surface carries a few barely-visible darker speckles. Head is a rounded dark blob (RGB ~14,13,16) sitting on a wider trapezoidal pronotum, with two tiny white eye dots. Six hairline legs, 3 per side, plus an elliptical ground shadow. CLAIM 1 - no orange - CONFIRMED and stronger than stated: a full-image scan finds ZERO warm pixels (r>g>=b with chroma>18) and a maximum chroma of 21/255 across the entire 440x440 canvas. The elytra sample at (36,32,35): neutral dark grey with a faint violet cast, not brown, not banded, not blotched. The black-and-orange transverse banding that IS the burying beetle is completely absent. CLAIM 2 - no clubbed knobbed antennae - CONFIRMED and understated: there are NO antennae of ANY kind. The head silhouette is a clean unbroken dome; nothing projects from it except the two white eye pixels. Not a thread, not a stub, not a club. CLAIM 3 - abdomen fully enclosed - CONFIRMED: the elytra terminate in a smooth rounded apex at y=304 with no exposed abdominal segments, no truncate elytral margin, no protruding tip. All three mustReads are absent. CORRECTIONS / ADDITIONS to the judging claim: (a) The judge described this only as a colour failure; the SHAPE is wrong too and is arguably the larger defect. The row specifies aspect 2 (elongate, twice as long as wide) and 'flat oval elytra'. The drawn body is 1.03 - the ROUNDEST body in the batch, rounder even than the Dung Beetle (1.21) - and the heavy crescent specular reads as a strongly convex dome, which is the ladybug/dung silhouette, the opposite of the flat parallel-sided carrion-beetle read. (b) 'Visually indistinguishable from the Dung Beetle' is true but too narrow. I rendered Dung Beetle and Ladybug side by side: all three are ONE CHASSIS - identical rounded head blob on a trapezoidal pronotum with two white eye dots, identical single midline seam, identical single left-side crescent specular, identical 3+3 hairline legs, identical rim-light arcs, identical ground shadow ellipse. rows.readsAs: an olive-green ladybug

SCORE: 0 of 3 identity must-reads readable. The organism a viewer names from this image is 'green ladybug'. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a black ladybug

MUST-READ 2, 'flat spade-shaped head used as a rake': ABSENT. The judge said 'the shared rounded ladybug lobe' - correct, but imprecise about the anatomy, and the fix depends on the precision. The head is TWO stacked primitives, not one: a small circular head lobe ON TOP OF a wide flared elliptical pronotum collar. The spade/clypeus would have to replace the leading edge of the head lobe with a flat, forward-projecting, straight-edged plate wider than it is deep. At 6x with 6x gain the leading edge is a clean uninterrupted circular arc - there is no flat facet, no straight chord, no forward projection anywhere on it.

Worse than 'the same as the others': the FORELEG (top station) is the SHORTEST and shallowest arc of the three pairs, which is the exact inverse of a digger's proportion, where the fore-tibia is the heaviest, broadest, most toothed limb on the animal. Whoever fixes this must not just add teeth; the foreleg pair has to become the dominant limb.

This is the ladybug spot layer surviving at low opacity in a black recolour, and it must be removed outright, not just darkened.

Nothing in the judge's claim is factually wrong. The corrections are that the head is a two-part lobe+collar stack rather than a single lobe, that the foreleg is the shortest limb rather than merely an equal one, and that two further packet requirements (no horn, untextured elytra) also fail and were not mentioned. rows.readsAs: a spotted goat kid or appaloosa pony foal
rows.defect: Hoof-blocks instead of paws, a long horse muzzle with a side-set eye, and a small ear pinned flat and far back. rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but the stated causes are partly wrong and the worst defect went unnamed. WHAT I SAW (440x440; subject bbox x125-314, y139-294; verified by 6x-8x nearest-neighbour crops of head/rump/feet plus a per-pixel luminance map and direct GetPixel probes).

GESTALT: a barrel-chested, square-standing quadruped with a dead-level topline, a deep short ribcage and straight columnar legs with a hock notch on the hind. It reads as a goat kid / young ungulate on the shared family pony chassis. Confirmed appaloosa-goat colouring: cream-to-tan ground carrying large irregular high-contrast BLACK blotches (1,844 sub-140-sum dark pixels inside the torso box x140-290 / y180-235). A bobcat is rufous-brown with fine, low-contrast dark flecking; this is the wrong colour logic entirely, not just the wrong spot shape.

TAIL - JUDGE CORRECT, and this is the hardest failure. The rump terminates in a clean rounded dome. I probed the entire 26x90 zone behind it (x100-126, y175-265) and found 19 foreground pixels total, all of them edge antialiasing on the haunch curve. There is no tail, no bob stub, no nub, no dark tip. The pale wedge at the back of the rump is the far-side hind thigh, not a tail. The mustRead 'very short bobbed tail' and the note about a 3-4-head-width stub are both unmet at 100%.

CHEEK RUFF - JUDGE CORRECT. The jawline is smooth and unbroken from ear to chin. There are two tiny dark whisker dots on the muzzle side, but no ruff, no flared side whiskers, no widened cheek mass. Absent.

EAR TUFTS - JUDGE WRONG, CORRECT THIS. Tufts are NOT absent. At 6x the ear apex sprouts a fan of five or six thin dark hair strands rising and splaying above the skull (source region approx x272-300, y139-160). The real defect is structural, not missing-feature: there is only ONE ear, drawn as a large brown face-on triangular plate / tent shape sitting flat on the crown, and the strands rise from its apex as a single central crest that reads as a mohawk or a tuft of head-hair rather than as paired black tips on two upright ear cones. Any fix should keep the strands and rebuild the ear as two side-set upright cones so the tufts land at the tips.

MUZZLE - JUDGE SUBSTANTIALLY CORRECT. The snout is a long tapering wedge with a big dark nose button at the tip and a long mouth line running back toward the eye - canid/caprine, not the short broad felid face. HOWEVER 'side-set eye' understates what is actually there: the eye is a large amber iris with a clear VERTICAL SLIT PUPIL, which is correct felid iconography and the only cat-reading feature in the whole asset. It is not the eye that is wrong, it is that a correct cat eye is mounted on an ungulate snout. Do not delete the eye when fixing the head.

FEET - JUDGE PARTLY WRONG. They are not solid hooves. Each foot is a flat olive-brown oval pad, distinctly wider than the leg shaft, sitting flush on the ground, and carrying two or three short vertical grooves on its upper face that are meant to read as toes. So a paw was attempted. The effect is still hoof-like because the pad is a ground-flush splayed slab with no knuckle relief, no digitigrade arch and no visible claw, so 'hoof-block' is right about the read but wrong about the geometry.

DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED: aspect. The subject bbox is 190 x 156 px = 1.22, against a required aspect of 1.9. The animal is roughly 35% too short and deep for its height. This is why it reads as a stocky goat regardless of markings, and it is the single change that would move the silhouette furthest toward a cat. Fix order: (1) stretch body to ~1.9 aspect and drop the chest depth; (2) add the bobbed tail stub with a dark tip; (3) rebuild the single crown plate into two side-set ear cones, carrying the existing dark strands to the tips; (4) shorten the muzzle to a blunt felid mask and add a cheek ruff, keeping the slit-pupil eye; (5) re-tune the coat from cream + big black blobs to rufous + fine flecking.

rows.readsAs: a plain tan goat or pony
rows.defect: The identity of a caracal is the long black ear tassels, and they are completely absent — the ear is a small brown triangle folded flat to the skull. The hind legs are not longer or more powerful than the fore; the tail is a thin donkey hook. Feet are hooves. Nothing in the silhouette is felid.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but the stated cause is substantially wrong and a fix written against it would delete the one correct feature on the asset. I read the 440x440 PNG whole, then re-cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled the head (6x), the ear tip (14x), a hoof (16x) and the tail (6x).

WHAT THE JUDGE GOT WRONG — THE EAR TASSELS ARE PRESENT, NOT ABSENT. At 14x the ear tip carries a fan of roughly seven near-black bristle strands radiating upward from the apex, each about as long as the upper half of the ear triangle. They are the single darkest, highest-contrast element in the entire image and are plainly visible even at 1x. The ear itself is not 'a small triangle folded flat' either: it is a two-plane erect pinna (a mid-brown outer plane plus a darker inner-conch triangle behind it) standing upright off the top of the skull. The only legitimate criticism of the tassels is their SHAPE: they splay outward as a symmetric fan, so they read as a crest/topknot sprouting from the crown rather than as one long tassel trailing off a single ear tip. Do not remove them — narrow the spray, lengthen it, and anchor it to the tip so it trails back rather than fanning.

THE TAIL CLAIM IS ALSO WRONG. Measured, the tail is ~12-13px thick against ~14px legs, i.e. limb-thickness, not 'thin'. And it is SHORT, which is what the mustRead actually asks for ('short tail'). The real tail defect is different: it is a bare, perfectly smooth, uniformly flat-tan tube with no fur texture, no terminal marking, and it is set high on the rump and hooks up-then-down like a pig or donkey tail rather than emerging low off a feline sacrum.

WHAT THE JUDGE GOT RIGHT. Feet: confirmed at 16x. Each foot is an oval dark-olive plate wider than the leg, flat-bottomed, crossed by three or four short dark vertical division lines — a cloven hoof cap, not a padded paw. No toes, no claws, no digitigrade metacarpal. Hind legs: confirmed absent. Fore and hind limbs are the same straight cannon-bone sticks; there is no deep feline thigh mass, no pronounced hock angle, and the topline is essentially level (shoulder marginally HIGHER than hip) when the caracal's identity requires the hindquarters to sit above the withers. Two of the three mustReads fail.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. The chassis is an artiodactyl, not a felid: deep barrel torso with a flat sagging topline, four straight stick limbs on hooves, and a long tapering muzzle ending in a large round dark nose, carried high on a short thick erect neck. The coat is unmarked but it is straw-yellow rather than reddish-tan and is overlaid with heavy pale woolly striations that read as fleece, further pushing it toward sheep/goat. One genuinely feline detail survives — a vertical-slit amber eye — and it is not enough to redeem the silhouette. As drawn this is a tan goat or hornless calf wearing correct caracal ear tufts. FAIL stands on chassis, feet and hindquarters; the ear-tuft charge must be struck from the record.

rows.readsAs: a spotted fawn or long-legged goat
rows.defect: No tear stripes anywhere on the face. The head is large and horse-muzzled rather than small and round, and the chest is a deep pony barrel with no whippet waist. Feet are hoof wedges. The one thing that works — solid round spots — cannot carry it when the tear stripe, the small head and the paw are all missing.
