rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two of the four stated causes are wrong and one is overstated — fix against this description, not theirs.

WHAT I DID: read the 440x440 PNG whole, then decoded it and re-read four zoom crops (head at 7x and 12x, face at 18x, feet at 5x, torso at 2.5x) plus a numeric silhouette profile (column top/bottom scan).

MUST-READ 1 — BLACK TEAR STRIPES EYE TO MOUTH: ABSENT. Confirmed at 18x. The face carries exactly ONE dark facial line: a thin black tapered wedge that leaves the lower-front rim of the eye and runs FORWARD and slightly down along the length of the muzzle, terminating at the lip under the nose. It is the mouth/lip line — it is the only mouth indication on the head, its axis is nearly parallel to the muzzle, and there is no second stroke. A cheetah's tear stripe is a broad dark band crossing the muzzle roughly PERPENDICULAR to that line (inner eye corner straight down the side of the muzzle to the lip). Nothing crosses the muzzle anywhere. The defining identity feature is missing. The judge is right on this one and it alone carries the FAIL.

MUST-READ 2 — SOLID ROUND SPOTS, NOT ROSETTES: PRESENT AND GOOD. ~90 solid black round spots, dense on the flank, shoulder and haunch, thinning on the belly, with a few clustered into 2-3 spot blobs. No rings, no hollow centres. This must-read passes cleanly and should not be touched by the fix.

MUST-READ 3 — SMALL HEAD ON A DEEP NARROW CHEST WITH A LONG THIN TAIL: SPLIT. Tail passes (long, thin, smoothly tapering, sweeping down and forward past the hock; plain tan, no rings/black tip, but rings are not a must-read). Head SIZE passes — measured skull-back-to-nose is 58px against a 278px bbox width, headFrac ≈ 0.21 against the 0.20 target, and it reads visually small. Chest/proportion FAILS: measured torso underline depth runs 72px at the chest (x≈266), 51px at the loin (x≈226), 60px at the haunch — so the greyhound tuck IS there, but it is only ~29% and the topline is dead level with no withers rise, so the deep-chest/narrow-waist contrast does not read. Worse, the whole animal is far too short-bodied: nose-to-rump ≈ 200px over a shoulder height of ≈154px (ratio 1.30) and an overall bbox aspect of 1.44, against the card's aspect 2.0. Legs are straight vertical columns and the neck rises almost vertically from the shoulder with the head carried high — llama/deer carriage, not the low horizontal head carriage of a cat.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM:
• "Feet are hoof wedges" — WRONG. At 5x each foot is a flattened brown OVAL PAD with three faint toe grooves scored across it. They are low-detail disc paws, not hooves. Do not spend the fix on the feet; they read as paws already (they could stand a knuckle/toe bulge, but that is polish).
• "Head is large" — WRONG. It is on spec at headFrac ≈ 0.21 and reads small. The head defect is SHAPE, not size: a long blunt tapering wedge with no forehead stop, the forehead sloping continuously into the muzzle, and a big dark oval nose set on the SIDE of the muzzle mid-length rather than at the tip (reads as an equine nostril). The ears are two flat brown caps lying on the skull rather than the cheetah's small rounded upright ears. "Horse-muzzled" is the correct half of that claim.
• "No whippet waist" — OVERSTATED. There is a real but shallow tuck (72→51→60px). The failure is that the chest is not deep enough and the back is too level for the contrast to register, plus the body is far too short for its height.
• "Reads as a spotted fawn" — CORRECT and the right summary: tall, short-backed, level-topline, pillar-legged, upright-necked, small long-muzzled head, cream coat with scattered black spots. Only the yellow slit-pupil eye argues for cat.

CHASSIS NOTE for the family audit: the straight-column limbs, small oval foot pads, dead-level topline and vertical neck carriage here are the generic quadruped chassis, not a cheetah-specific build.

FIX PRIORITY: (1) add the tear stripe — a bold dark band from the inner eye corner down across the muzzle to the lip corner, and give the mouth its own separate shorter line; (2) shorten the muzzle, add a forehead stop, move the nose to the muzzle tip; (3) lengthen the body / drop the leg column so the aspect reaches ~2.0, deepen the chest and cut the loin harder.

rows.readsAs: a pony stamped with dark paw prints
rows.defect: The markings are small dark paw-print-shaped clusters — the identical stamp used on Jaguar, Leopard and Ocelot — not the large dark-edged cloud blotches that name this animal. The tail is a short thin hook maybe a fifth of head-body length instead of equalling it. Legs are pony posts on hooves.
rows.fix: Replace the paw-print stamps with a few large irregular cloud blotches carrying dark trailing edges, and extend the tail to full head-plus-body length as a thick tube.
rows.verifyWhy:
I zoomed the 440x440 PNG at 7-14x on the coat, head, rump, tail and feet, and side-by-side against Cougar.png from the same batch. The FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes need correcting and a third must-read failure was missed entirely.

CHASSIS (confirmed, and it is the root cause). Silhouette bbox is x95-345, y142-280. Overlaid on Cougar the outline is the SAME PATH: identical dorsal topline with the same shallow saddle dip and the same high croup, the same neck-to-shoulder junction, the same long tapering muzzle ending in a big round dark nose disc, the same pair of small rounded ears on top of the skull, the same four straight untapered pillar legs with no elbow, stifle or hock articulation, the same flat rounded pad-blobs for feet with two vertical grooves scored in them, and the same short flat-tan hook tail. Only the coat texture and the stamped markings differ. So 'reads as a pony stamped with paw prints' is fair; more precisely the chassis reads as a hornless calf/goat - an ungulate head and ungulate legs - not a felid. One thing the judge did NOT credit: the eye IS a correct gold felid eye with a vertical slit pupil, the only genuinely cat-like feature on the asset. It is not enough to carry the identity.

MUST-READ 1 - 'large cloud-shaped dark-edged blotches': ABSENT, judge correct. Every marking is the shared paw-print stamp: a round central pad with four small toe dots arranged around it. I counted roughly 20 of them across flank, shoulder, haunch and neck. CORRECTION to the judge's wording: they are not uniformly 'small'. Along the topline from about x=160 to x=205 the stamps are scaled up ~2.5x and overlap each other into an irregular dark saddle band; at thumbnail size that band is the only thing approaching a large blotch. Zoomed, it resolves unambiguously into merged paw prints - pad + toes still legible - not a cloud. There is no dark-edged, pale-centred rosette anywhere on the animal, and no marking is filled with anything but flat near-black. The coat is uniformly pale tan with hair-stroke texture and no dark edging at all.

MUST-READ 2 - 'tail as long as head and body combined': FAILS, but the judge's number is wrong. Head-body is ~217px (nose tip x=345 to rump rear edge x~128). The tail root is at ~(146,201); it arcs up over the croup to an apex at ~(122,193), sweeps left-down to ~(97,222) and hooks to a tip at ~(103,247). Traced along its centreline that is ~90px, i.e. ~0.41 of head-body, not 'a fifth' (0.2). Straight root-to-tip span is ~64px (0.30). So the tail is roughly two-fifths of the required length, not one-fifth - still less than half of the must-read, so the must-read fails, but a fix brief built on '5x too short' would overshoot. TWO DEFECTS THE JUDGE MISSED ON THE TAIL, and they matter as much as the length: (a) it is drawn in flat solid mid-tan with NO fur texture and NO markings whatsoever, while the clouded leopard's tail is the most heavily blotched part of the animal; (b) its form is a thin upward hook curled over the rump like a pig's or a spitz dog's, tapering to a rounded point, where the species has a thick, uniformly heavy, low-carried tail.

MUST-READ 3 - 'very short stout legs': FAILS, and the judge did not mention it at all. Belly line sits at y~223 at mid-body, ground contact at y~280, so free leg is ~57px against a chest depth of ~51px (top y~172 to belly y~223). The legs are ~112% of body depth and about 52% of standing height - long, straight and evenly thick top to bottom. The species reads by having a low-slung barrel on stubby legs; this reads leggy. Aspect is also off: body-only length/height is 217/139 = 1.56 against the required 2.3, so the torso is far too short and deep for the frame.

Net: two of three must-reads absent (cloud blotches, long tail), the third (short stout legs) also failed, and the underlying body is the shared big-cat/canid chassis rather than a cat. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a plain tan goat or donkey

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, inspected at 6x and 12x nearest-neighbour crops of head, hindquarter and feet):
The organism is a barrel-chested quadruped with a dead-level topline, a long smooth neck, four long straight columnar legs ending in small pads, and NO TAIL WHATSOEVER (the haunch simply terminates in a rounded rump; there is not even a bobbed nub). Coat is cream/bone with dense irregular black blotches concentrated on the flank and shoulder, thinning to speckles on the throat. At thumbnail size this reads as a spotted goat kid / appaloosa foal. The judge's organism call is correct.

CORRECTION 1 - 'No black ear tufts' is WRONG. The ear tufts ARE drawn and ARE black. The single viewer-side ear is a tall dark-brown filled triangle on the crown, and from its apex rise five thin near-black bristle strokes fanning up and back, roughly 40% of the ear's own height. They are legible at 6x and unmistakable at 12x; they are merely thin (1px strokes at native size) so they wash out in a thumbnail. The real defect is different and worse: the identical tuft cluster is present on the Bobcat AND on the Caracal in this same batch, so the tuft is a family-wide default decoration, not a Lynx identifier. It carries zero discriminating power. Fix = make the Lynx tuft long, thick and unmistakable, and make sure the Bobcat's is the short one.

CORRECTION 2 - 'the feet are the smallest hoof blocks in the batch' is imprecise on both counts. They are not hoof blocks: at 6x each foot is a flattened oval pad with three or four vertical toe-division lines scribed into it - a small splayed paw, not a cloven hoof. And they are not the smallest in the batch; they are pixel-for-pixel the SAME foot as the Bobcat's and the same size class as the Caracal's (the Caracal's actually read more hoof-like, being darker and two-lobed). The true finding: the Lynx is using the shared default paw at default scale, when its whole identity requires a paw that is conspicuously oversized - a snowshoe disc wider than the cannon bone above it. Nothing about this foot is enlarged at all.

CONFIRMED AS STATED:
- Flared facial ruff: genuinely absent. The jaw line runs straight back into an unbroken cylindrical neck; the silhouette edge from chin to chest has no flare, no cheek whisker fan, no muttonchop mass. There is a pale diagonal band crossing the neck below the jaw, but it is a shading seam (the same seam appears on the Bobcat and Caracal) and it does not break the outline, so it cannot be counted as a ruff.
- Long hind legs: absent. Rump top and withers top sit level; the hind limb has more angulation (a visible stifle/hock bend swept rearward) than the foreleg but is not longer, and the hindquarters do not stand higher than the shoulders.
- Identical to the Bobcat: fully confirmed and it is the most damning finding. Rendering Lynx.png and Bobcat.png at the same crop and scale gives two images that differ ONLY in spot density and a slight coat-tone shift. Same skull, same long tapering wedge muzzle with the nose oval set back from the tip, same yellow slit-pupil eye, same triangular tufted ear, same neck, same level topline, same barrel, same four legs, same feet, same missing tail, same shadow ellipse. HEAD DETAIL FOR THE FIX: the skull is the batch's generic chassis head and is not feline at all - a long tapered snout with a downturned rounded tip, a large dark nose oval sitting on TOP of the muzzle well back from the end, and a long straight mouth line running past the eye. It reads lizard/canid. The only feline cue anywhere on the animal is the vertical-slit yellow eye. A lynx needs the opposite: a very short blunt muzzle, a wide flat-topped skull, and cheek mass wider than the braincase.

I zoomed the 440x440 PNG at 6-12x on the head, ear, flank, feet and tail before deciding. The FAIL stands, and the organism failure is WORSE than stated — it is not merely a spotted pony, it is a spotted HOOFSTOCK. Corrections and additions to the original claim, feature by feature:

MUST-READ 1, chain-like rosettes running in streaks along the flank — ABSENT, judge correct, but their description of the marks is partly wrong. The marks are not uniformly 'paw-print stamps'; at 8x the flank carries ~14 discrete clusters of 4-7 small round dots, and several of them (mid-flank, over the hip, on the shoulder) are genuine broken-ring rosettes with a hollow tan centre. So the rosette PRIMITIVE is there. What is absent is the ocelot's actual signature: the rosettes never coalesce, never elongate, and never align. They are scattered at random angles with no directional field, so nothing forms the oblique chains/continuous streak-bands that run shoulder-to-haunch on a real ocelot. A few marks on the neck and shoulder DO read as literal paw-print stamps (a large blob with 3-4 toe dots above it) — the generic mammal stamp — but that is the minority case, not the whole coat. The fix is directional, not new shapes: elongate and chain the rosettes already present into 4-6 continuous oblique streaks, and clear the belly/lower flank so the streaks read.

MUST-READ 2, two black stripes on each cheek — ABSENT, judge fully correct. At 12x the cheek is completely flat unmarked tan from the eye back to the jaw hinge. Zero facial marking of any kind. One thing the judge missed and should be preserved by the fix: the eye IS feline — a yellow/amber iris with a hard VERTICAL SLIT PUPIL, correctly drawn. That slit pupil is the only cat cue on the entire asset.

MUST-READ 3, housecat-sized build with a shortish tail — ABSENT, judge correct but understated. The chassis is the shared pony/ungulate chassis: barrel ribcage, straight topline with a dip behind the withers, short thick neck carried level, and — decisively — the FEET ARE HOOVES. Each of the four legs terminates in a dark-brown splayed cleat block wider than the leg column, with no toe separation, no digital pads and no claws. Hind legs are straight columns with an ungulate hock, not a feline crouch. The tail is a flat, solid-fill, uniform-width tan hook curving up and back, with no taper, no banding, no dark tip and no fur shading — it reads as a pasted-on shape, not a tail. It is shortish, so the 'shortish' half of the must-read is technically satisfied by accident, but nothing else about it reads as cat.

HEAD (the judge did not examine this and it is the single biggest defect). At 12x the skull is a long, tubular, slightly downturned equine/canid muzzle roughly 1.6x the length of the braincase, with a dark oval nose set on the SIDE of the muzzle tip and a long horizontal mouth line running most of the muzzle length. A cat skull is short, round and blunt with the nose on the front plane — none of that is present. The ears are two small ROUNDED BROWN LOBES on the crown (a larger flap set back, a smaller lobe forward beside the eye); neither is a triangular feline ear. There is no cheek ruff, no whisker pad, no brow.

VERDICT: three of three must-reads fail on their defining half, and the underlying organism reads as a small hoofed ungulate with cat eyes. This is a chassis-level rebuild (feline skull, digitigrade toed paws, low crouched topline, long tapering banded tail), not a markings pass. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a spotted goat kid or fawn

FAIL stands, but BOTH stated causes are factually wrong and must not be worked from. I decoded the PNG and measured every row, and I cropped the head, ear, face, feet and legs at 6-12x.

CORRECTION 1 - THE LEGS ARE NOT INVERTED AND ARE NOT 'the same short pony posts as the rest of the batch'. Serval has the LONGEST legs in the family in absolute pixels and the second-highest leg-to-body-depth ratio of all 13. Measuring belly-line to ground vs topline-to-belly across the whole batch: Serval 82px leg / 59px depth = 1.39; Cheetah 1.45; Lynx 1.14; Caracal 1.15; Bobcat 1.09; Cougar 1.09; Ocelot 1.03; Clouded Leopard 1.00; Leopard 0.98; Tiger 0.88; Jaguar 0.81; Snow Leopard 0.70; Lion 0.55. Family median is ~1.03. Legs are 43% of total figure height, the highest in the batch. There is a genuinely airy open gap under the belly. Whoever fixes this must NOT lengthen the legs - that axis is already correct and differentiated. Nor is the barrel 'deep': body runs x142-x305 (163px) by 59px deep, aspect 2.76, which is slender, not a barrel.

CORRECTION 2 - THE EARS DO NOT LIE FLAT ON THE SKULL. The near ear is a large oval pinna with a tan rim and a fully rendered dark-brown inner bowl, ~32px wide x 34px tall, standing clear above the skull line (skull top ~y140, ear tip y116) and roughly as tall as the entire visible skull. Its inner bowl is a clear elongated ellipse, not a disc. The real defect is that it is CANTED BACK ~25-30 degrees instead of standing vertical, and that it is accompanied by TWO spurious extra lobes - a shapeless brown blob at lower-left (nominally the far ear, but it has no rim, no bowl, no shape) and a stray triangular point poking up at x285-292 that belongs to no ear at all. Three ear-ish masses, one of which is correct.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS - it is organism-level, not serval-level. All three must-reads are technically present (long legs: yes, measured; large oval ear on a small head: the near ear, yes; short tail and bold spots: yes, tail is ~1/3 body and the flank carries big coalescing black blotches). The asset fails because the underlying chassis is not a felid at all:
(a) THE MUZZLE. The face is a long smooth taper with the nose drawn as a dark oval on the SIDE of the snout rather than a nose-pad at the tip, plus a long thin mouth line running back to the jaw. No muzzle pad, no whisker-pad bulge, no short cat face. This is a canid/ungulate snout and it is the single loudest wrong signal in the image.
(b) THE FEET. Each foot is a broad flat elliptical PLATE with 3-4 vertical toe grooves, splaying far wider than the leg column, with the leg landing on it like a post on a saucer. Reads as a hoof-pedestal, not a paw.
(c) THE LIMB MODEL. Both legs are straight undifferentiated columns - the hind leg runs as one unbroken post from hip to foot with no hock and no stifle, the fore leg has only a token bend. This IS the shared chassis the packet warns about; it is shared in FORM even though it is not shared in LENGTH.
(d) HEAD CARRIAGE. Head hangs low and forward on a thick neck (browsing posture), not the cat's level alert carriage.
(e) TAIL. Short is correct, but it is a fat uniform-width tan tube with a blunt round end, no taper, and crucially NO rings and NO black tip - a serval tail is barred with a black tip. The 'barred' half of must-read 3 is absent here.
(f) THE LEGS ARE COMPLETELY UNSPOTTED. Bold blotches cover the flank and belly but stop dead at the shoulder and hip; both legs are plain cream from top to foot. A serval is spotted right down onto the feet. This is a cheap, high-value fix and it also stops the long legs reading as bare posts.
Net gestalt: a long-snouted, plate-footed, straight-posted spotted quadruped with a low head. The prior judge's 'spotted goat kid' impression is a defensible read of the result, but they reached it by blaming the two things this asset actually got right.

rows.defect: Pixel-identical to Clam except the fill is teal. The heavy fluted shell with wavy zigzag meeting lips is entirely absent - the top rim is a smooth clean arc with no zigzag, no flutes, no scalloped meeting edge. There is no gape at all, therefore no iridescent patterned mantle bulging between the valves, which is the single feature that makes a giant clam recognisable. Reads as a colour variant, not a species.
rows.fix: Open a wide gape along the top with a deep zigzag interlocking margin on both lips, and fill it with a thick mottled blue-green mantle lobe that bulges visibly above the shell line.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the underlying defect is worse than stated. I read Giant_Clam.png at full size and again at ~4x zoom on the shell (crop 125,110 190x160), and I diffed it numerically against its family siblings.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: one single fan-ribbed valve seen face-on, hinge-DOWN. A wide, rounded, roughly hemispherical teal body; ~14 straight dark radial rib lines converging to a point at the bottom-centre; a thin pale specular highlight running along the top edge; two short dark hairline diagonal strokes flicking outward at the upper-left and upper-right corners (they read as tiny hinge ears / stray tentacles); and two flat teal triangular wedges splayed at the base under the convergence point. Flat single-hue teal with a soft top-lit gradient, on the standard dark card with the standard drop-shadow ellipse. That silhouette reads as a SCALLOP valve, not a clam and certainly not a Tridacna.

THE JUDGE'S CLAIM IS CORRECT AND I CAN QUANTIFY IT. Clam.png, Giant_Clam.png and Scallop.png are all 440x440 and are the SAME DRAWING. Clam vs Giant Clam differ in RGB on only 22,933 of 193,600 pixels (11.8%) -- i.e. 88.2% of the canvas, including the entire background gradient, the drop shadow and every anti-aliased silhouette edge, is byte-for-byte identical; the only pixels that differ are the shell body itself, and they differ purely in hue. The alpha channel is identical everywhere. Bounding boxes are identical. So the judge's 'pixel-identical to Clam recoloured teal' is literally true -- and I extend it: it is THREE species on one chassis, not two. Clam = cream, Giant Clam = teal, Scallop = peach/salmon, same ribs, same ears, same base wedges, same everything. The packet's aspect directive (Giant Clam 1.5 vs Clam 1.3) is not honoured either, since the silhouette is bit-identical.

MUST-READ 1 -- 'heavy fluted shell with wavy zigzag meeting lips': ABSENT. The judge's description is accurate: the top rim is a smooth convex arc with a clean pale highlight line, no scalloping, no wave, no interdigitation. I want to sharpen the cause, though. It is not merely that the zigzag was omitted from a rim -- there is no second valve anywhere in the image, no hinge line, no valve-to-valve seam. The pair is not represented at all, so there is no 'meeting lip' for a zigzag to live on. The ribs are also flat dark strokes painted on a smooth surface, not fluting: there is no ridge-and-trough relief, no lit crest / shadowed valley pairing, so even the ribbing does not read as the heavy corrugated Tridacna shell.

MUST-READ 2 -- 'iridescent patterned fleshy mantle bulging between the valves': ABSENT, exactly as claimed. There is no gape, so no mantle. I looked hard for it drawn small or in an unexpected place -- along the top rim, in the base wedges, in the rib convergence -- and found nothing. The only non-shell marks are the two corner hairlines and the two base triangles, and neither carries any mantle cue. There is also zero iridescence anywhere: the body is a single teal hue with one lightness gradient, no colour shift, no spotting, no blue/green mottling. That is the single feature that makes a giant clam recognisable and it is not present in any form.

Nothing else in the asset carries giant-clam identity either: no sense of massive scale, no thick wall section, no reef substrate. Blind, this asset reads 'scallop shell, teal'. Both must-reads are missing, the organism reads as the wrong bivalve, and the drawing is a recolour of two siblings in the same packet. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs a new drawing, not a touch-up. Draw two heavy valves meeting along a horizontal-ish seam with the seam itself cut into 4-6 deep interlocking wavy teeth; give the ribs real relief (lit crest, shadowed trough) so the shell reads as corrugated stone; and open the gape to expose a fleshy mantle lobe bulging proud of the lips, painted with a mottled iridescent blue-green-gold pattern distinct in hue from the shell. And it must not share a silhouette with Clam or Scallop.

rows.readsAs: a dark slate-blue bowl or fan - the Clam asset in navy
rows.defect: The silhouette is the family's round symmetric bowl, not a wedge. A mussel is identified by an asymmetric teardrop wedge that tapers to a narrow pointed hinge at one end and swells to a broad rounded margin at the other; here both ends are equally round and the widest point is dead centre. No byssal beard threads anywhere. The radial ribs are wrong - a mussel shell carries fine concentric growth lines, not a fan. Only the dark blue-black colour lands, and it is so dark against the near-black plate that the form barely separates from the background.
rows.fix: Replace the bowl outline with an asymmetric wedge pointed at one end, drop the radial fan for fine concentric growth lines, add a specular gloss band, and trail a tuft of byssal threads out of the narrow end.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but two of the three stated causes are described wrong and the fix notes need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE PLATE (measured on the 440x440 PNG, plus 4x and 16x brightened crops): a bilaterally symmetric FAN/BOWL shell standing upright. The top is a straight, gently up-arched hinge line running x=140..299 at y~128, capped by the asset's only specular highlight (peak pixel RGB 111,119,135 at 210,126). From that hinge the flanks bulge outward to the widest point of 165px at y=180, then sweep down and inward, converging to a narrow rounded base/point at y~255 where about eleven straight RADIAL rays meet. Shell body is RGB ~(41,40,51) dark navy-slate; the rays are a slightly warmer tan-brown (38,37,47 at mid, 35,35,44 at the convergence). Two grey triangular wedges sit under the base as a shadow/mount, plus a soft elliptical cast shadow lower down.

CORRECTION 1 - the shape description. It is NOT a 'round symmetric bowl with both ends equally rounded and the widest point dead centre'. The symmetry is LEFT-RIGHT (mirror), not end-to-end: the top end is a flat straight hinge, the bottom end tapers to a narrow point where the rays converge. The widest row is at y=180 out of a shell span of y=128..258, i.e. ~40% down, upper-middle, not dead centre. The organism this actually reads as is a SCALLOP (Pectinidae) or cockle - fan outline, straight hinge, radial ribs from a basal umbo - which is the worst possible error here because it collides with a sibling on the same family card. The judge is right that the mussel identity is absent; the shape they described is not the shape that is drawn, so a fix aimed at 'make the bowl less round' will miss.

CORRECTION 2 - the beard. The claim 'no byssal beard' is right in effect but wrong in detail: there ARE six thin thread-like strokes visible above the shell, three at the top-left corner and three at the top-right, poking out past the hinge line into the plate. At 16x they are exactly the same tan-brown as the interior rays and exactly COLLINEAR with them - they are the radial rib strokes overshooting the shell clip boundary, not a beard. So this is two defects, not one: (a) no byssal beard anywhere, and (b) an unclipped-stroke rendering bug leaking ribs outside the silhouette, symmetric on both sides. Anyone fixing this must not mistake the corner threads for an existing beard attempt.

CORRECTION 3 - contrast. 'Only the dark navy colour lands, and it is nearly invisible against the plate' overstates it. Plate immediately beside the shell is RGB (8,12,17); shell body is (41,40,51) rising to (111,119,135) on the hinge highlight - roughly a 3-4x luminance step plus a hard specular line. The silhouette is plainly legible at 1x; it is low-key and undersaturated but not invisible. Do not 'fix' this by brightening the shell.

MUST-READ SCORECARD (aspect 1.8, headFrac 0, eyes hidden, sessile): (1) 'wedge-shaped hinged shell narrow at the hinge end' - ABSENT and inverted. Drawn aspect is 165w x ~130h = 1.27, far rounder than the required 1.8, and the shell is WIDEST at the hinge end and narrowest at the opposite end, which is the exact reverse of a mussel's umbo-narrow / posterior-broad wedge. (2) 'dark blue-black glossy shell with growth lines' - HALF. Colour and gloss land (navy-slate body, specular hinge, soft sheen gradient). Growth lines FAIL: the surface carries straight radial rays fanning from a basal point, where a mussel needs concentric arcs running parallel to the shell margin, and a mussel shell is smooth - it must have no radial ribbing at all. (3) 'byssal beard threads anchoring it' - ABSENT (see correction 2).

One of three must-reads half-lands on colour alone; the defining wedge silhouette is not merely weak but reversed, and the asset resolves as a different bivalve on the same card. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a bone-grey paper fan or bowl - the Clam asset desaturated
rows.defect: Same chassis again. The outline is smooth, symmetric and clean, which is the direct contradiction of the must-read: an oyster is identified by an IRREGULAR, ruffled, rough-layered shell with lumpy asymmetric edges. There are no layered growth flanges, no ragged margin. The two valves are neither visible nor unequal - there is one solid form, so no cupped-versus-flat contrast. No pearly interior because the shell never opens.
rows.fix: Break the outline into an irregular lumpy blob with stacked ruffled layer flanges around the rim, split it into an obviously deep cupped lower valve and a thinner flat lid tilted open, and show a smooth nacre-pale interior in the gap.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the true cause is worse than stated. At 440x440 the asset is a single closed bowl/dome: a smooth convex arc across the top margin, smooth unbroken curved flanks, and a flat-cut bottom edge where the form narrows. Across that face are ELEVEN straight dark radiating rib strokes fanning from a dark umbo notch at the bottom centre up to the top margin. Additional elements the FAIL judge did not mention: three short dark hair-like strokes project outward beyond the shell at EACH upper corner (six total), and two mid-grey hard-edged triangular/trapezoid slabs sit under the flat base as props, plus a detached elliptical ground shadow.

WHAT IS CORRECT IN THE CLAIM: the outline is genuinely smooth and perfectly bilaterally symmetric; there is not one stacked layer flange, foliated lamina, or ragged/frilled margin anywhere on the silhouette or the interior; the form is one solid closed body with no gape, no hinge line, no valve-separation seam, so there is indeed no unequal cupped-vs-flat valve pair and no exposed pearly interior. All three of the packet must-reads (irregular ruffled rough-layered shell; two unequal valves one cupped one flat; pearly smooth interior when open) are absent. Zero of three.

WHAT THE CLAIM GETS WRONG OR MISSES: (1) It frames the body as merely blank/featureless. It is not blank — it is positively wearing ANOTHER species' diagnostic. Radiating fan ribbing converging on an umbo is the Scallop's own must-read in this very packet ('fan-ribbed shell'), and the oyster is drawn with it. This is misidentification, not just omission, and it is the fix that matters: the ribs must be REMOVED and replaced with irregular concentric foliated layers, not merely supplemented. (2) There IS a thin bright specular rim line along the top margin, which could be mistaken for nacre in a fast read — it is an exterior edge highlight on a closed shell, not a pearly interior; no interior surface is visible at any point. (3) The six corner hairs and the two grey triangular base props are undescribed and are not oyster anatomy; if they are meant as byssal threads / substrate they belong on Mussel, and an oyster is cemented flat to its substrate, not propped on two legs.

FAMILY-LEVEL FINDING (the decisive one). I rendered all six bivalves side by side. Clam, Giant Clam, Mussel, Oyster and Scallop are ONE CHASSIS: identical smooth fan-ribbed bowl silhouette, identical convergent bottom umbo notch, identical rim highlight, identical six corner hairs, identical pair of grey triangular props. They differ ONLY in fill colour (cream / cyan / navy / beige / orange) and a small aspect stretch. Oyster and Clam are near-indistinguishable even in hue. Only Razor Clam breaks the mould, and it is merely the same ribbed body squashed into a tilted ellipse rather than a straight parallel-edged blade. So the Oyster does not read as an oyster; it reads as a generic ribbed scallop/cockle shell in beige, and the family reads as one shell in five colours. Rebuilding the oyster requires an asymmetric outline with an irregular wavy margin, stacked overlapping growth laminae, a visibly deeper cupped left valve against a flatter right valve with an offset meeting seam, and a chalk-grey/mud exterior against a faint iridescent nacre band if any interior is shown.

rows.readsAs: an olive leaf, or a squashed almond floating in the air
rows.defect: The same fan primitive squashed flat - the rib lines and the corner whiskers survive the squash and are visible. The result is a pointed lens tapering to a sharp tip at BOTH ends, which is a leaf, not a razor shell: a razor clam has PARALLEL straight long edges with squared-off ends, like a cut-throat razor. No digging foot protrudes from either end, no hinge, no periostracum banding. The render is also broken in placement - the body floats tilted about 20 degrees up and to the left while its ground shadow sits low and to the right, so the organism is detached from its own footing and reads as airborne.
rows.fix: Draw a straight-sided elongated rectangle with rounded square ends and a hinge line running the full length, seat it flat on its shadow instead of tilting it, and extend a pale muscular digging foot out of the lower end.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then at 3x/4x/9x crops of the body and both ends, and measured the pixels. VERDICT UPHELD (FAIL) but THREE parts of the stated cause are wrong and must not be fixed against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a single olive-brown (approx R122 G112 B70) lens/pod, oriented -18.4 deg, body bbox x119-317 y147-222. A bright near-white specular rim runs along the whole UPPER-LEFT edge only (the lower edge has no rim) — that highlight plus the olive body colour DOES satisfy the 'glossy olive-brown periostracum' must-read. About ten evenly spaced dark rib strokes cross the short axis. That is the whole render: one plate, no second valve, no hinge line, no umbo, no axial seam anywhere, no siphon, and NO DIGGING FOOT at either end — both ends just stop. So two of the three must-reads (parallel-edged razor blade; digging foot from one end) are absent, and it reads as a generic seed-pod / leaf, not a Ensis blade.

CORRECTION 1 — 'squashed flat' is WRONG. The oriented (PCA) extent is length 208.7 px by width 40.8 px, ASPECT 5.12, against the packet's aspect: 6. The elongation is very nearly on spec; do NOT stretch it. The defect is the EDGE PROFILE, not the length. Half-width sampled along the axis: 40.8 at centre, 40.5 at +/-20, 36.4 at +/-50, 30.7 at +/-70, 22.1 at +/-90, 15.8 at +/-100 — a smooth cosine falloff with no flat run anywhere. A razor clam needs thickness held constant (parallel edges) across roughly the middle 80% of the length, then a squared/obliquely-cut end. That flat section is what is missing.

CORRECTION 2 — 'tapers to a sharp point at BOTH ends' is WRONG. At 9x both ends are BLUNT ROUNDED caps, still about 16 px thick at +/-100 along the axis, with the white rim curving smoothly around the right tip. It is a lens/pod outline, not a pointed leaf. Fixing this as 'de-point the tips' would miss the actual problem (see correction 1).

CORRECTION 3 — the shadow offset claim is WRONG. Shadow centroid x = 219.0; body centroid x = 218.7. The ground shadow is horizontally CENTRED under the body to within 0.3 px, and its x-span (132-306, 174 px) sensibly matches the body's (119-317, 198 px). There is no 'up-left body / low-right shadow' lateral mismatch. The detachment is purely VERTICAL: body bottom edge y=222, shadow top edge y=277 — a 55 px empty gap on a 440 px canvas, so the shell reads as hovering. Fix by raising the shadow, not by sliding it sideways.

CONFIRMED FROM THE CLAIM: the chassis ribs and stray whiskers are real. The ~10 rib strokes are the generic fan-rib chassis, and at least four of them OVERSHOOT the shell mask and hang in bare background at the two tapered ends — visible stubs at roughly (132,188) and (150,227) off the lower-left tip and (293,135) and (302,172) off the upper-right tip. Also confirmed: no hinge and no foot.

BAND: FAIL. One of three must-reads present (glossy olive periostracum); the two that carry the identity — the straight parallel-edged cut-throat-razor blade and the protruding digging foot — are both absent, and the leftover fan-rib strokes leak outside the silhouette. Nothing here is a small feature I could have missed; I checked both ends at 9x specifically for a foot stub and there is none.

rows.readsAs: a scallop shell, but upside down - a salmon-pink fan standing on its point
rows.defect: The one asset the shared chassis nearly fits, since a radial rib fan IS the scallop read - which is itself the family's problem. But it is inverted: the ribs converge at the bottom and the straight hinge edge is drawn across the TOP, so the shell stands on its umbo with the fan opening upward. The flat wing-like ears are not at the hinge - the only triangles present sit at the bottom, opposite the straight edge, and read as feet. Both flesh must-reads are entirely missing: there is no row of tiny bright blue eyes along the mantle edge (the packet flags eyes as prominent) and no fringe of sensory tentacles between the valves. The two hair-thin whiskers at the upper corners are too faint to register as anything.
rows.fix: Flip the shell so the straight hinge and its two triangular ears sit at the top with the ribs spreading down to a wide scalloped bottom margin, then line the gape with a row of bright blue dot eyes and a fringe of short tentacles.

rows.readsAs: a generic anglerfish or piranha — a fat scaled egg with a glowing bulb on a stalk
rows.defect: The must-read that IS the monkfish is missing: there is no enormous flattened head wider than the body. The silhouette is a plain symmetric egg with no head/body boundary, no widening at the front, no taper at the back — the body actually narrows toward the head rather than the reverse. The mouth is a small notch of straight vertical teeth on the front edge, not a huge upturned gape ringed with inward-slanting teeth. No frilly skin flaps anywhere along the jaw or flanks. No pectoral fins at all, so nothing sprawls; the sprawling posture is unreadable. The only monkfish cue present is the lure, and a lure alone reads as deep-sea anglerfish, not Lophius. Rendered aspect is roughly 1.5, well under the specified 1.9.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as a wide top-down-ish wedge: a broad flattened head disc occupying the front half at 2x the body width, with a crescent upturned jaw across its whole leading edge, inward-raked fangs, a fringe of skin tassels along the jawline and body margin, and the body tapering sharply to a thin tail behind it.

rows.readsAs: a small generic minnow or perch — a scaled leaf shape with a spiky dorsal comb
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are absent. There are no pectoral fins whatsoever — the huge fan-like pectorals that prop a sculpin on the bottom, which are the single most recognisable thing about the animal, are not drawn, so nothing props and nothing fans. The head is not oversized, broad or flattened: it is the narrow pointed right-hand tip of a symmetric lens, visibly narrower than the mid-body, the opposite of the reference. The body is not a scaleless tapering tadpole — it is a fore-aft symmetric almond covered in an explicit crosshatch scale mesh. The eye is a tiny dot, not prominent. The zigzag dorsal comb is the only added feature and it reads as a generic spiny-rayed panfish fin.
rows.fix: Draw a pair of enormous rounded fan pectorals with visible rays splayed downward and outward from just behind the head, planted on the substrate, and swell the front third of the body into a broad blunt flattened skull with big high-set bulging eyes while tapering the rear to a thin smooth scaleless tail.

rows.readsAs: A fern frond, or a rowan/ash sprig — some viewers will say an ear of wheat
rows.defect: The must-read that IS fennel — the cloud of thread-fine feathery foliage — is absent. The leaves are discrete, opaque, hard-edged oval leaflets pinned in a strict herringbone along five horizontal ribs, and the whole mass is boxed into a mechanical rectangle with flat vertical sides. That is a pinnate compound leaf, the opposite of fennel's hair-like dissection. The umbel is a small solid yellow crescent lid rather than a flat-topped spray of spoke-like rays carrying florets, the stem is a plain flat olive pole with no ribbing and no blue tint, and there is no swollen white bulb base at the soil.
rows.fix: Replace the leaflet stamp with hundreds of 1px hair-thread strokes fanning from each rib tip so the foliage reads as a soft translucent haze with a broken outer edge, and rebuild the crown as visible radiating rays each ending in a small yellow floret cluster.

rows.readsAs: A spider plant or a young agave — a generic grass clump with a pin stuck in the middle
rows.defect: The bulb is entirely absent. Zoomed on the base, the blades converge to a sharp pinched point that disappears straight into the ground shadow: no swelling, no papery white skin, no clove divisions, no root fringe. That papery cloved bulb IS garlic. The scape is also wrong — it is a rigid straight stalk, not the signature curling loop — and its head is the same flat crescent lid used on Fennel and Onion rather than a bulbil cluster in a beaked spathe. The blades themselves are plain tapering grass straps with a single highlight line; the flat FOLDED keel that distinguishes garlic from onion is not visible, so the asset cannot be told apart from the Onion card beside it.
rows.fix: Draw a fat white papery bulb sitting on the soil with three or four vertical clove seams and a fringe of wiry roots, then bend the scape into its characteristic single loop before the head.

rows.readsAs: A clump of ornamental grass or a small green flax — not a vegetable at all
rows.defect: Same missing identity: there is no swollen papery bulb and no fringe of wiry roots. The leaf fan tapers to a point and enters the black ground ellipse with no base swelling whatsoever, so the harvest organ named in the reference simply does not exist in the picture. The leaves are also flat sword blades with a pale midrib, not the hollow ROUND tubes the must-read calls for — no cylindrical shading, no blunt hollow tips, and several blades flop over sideways the way a grass does rather than arching stiffly. The crown is the same recoloured crescent lid as Fennel and Garlic instead of a spherical allium head of tiny star florets. Placed next to Garlic this is visibly the identical drawing with the fan opened slightly and the grey warmed to green.
rows.fix: Add a large papery-skinned bulb with concentric skin lines and a root fringe at the soil line, and re-shade the leaves as cylinders — dark edge, bright centre stripe, blunt rounded tip — so they read as hollow tubes.

rows.readsAs: a llama or a shaggy long-necked sandy ungulate; 'camel' only on a second look
rows.defect: Of the three must-reads only the long curved neck is clearly delivered. The single hump does not exist as a separate form — the entire torso is one round egg with a woolly lighter oval painted over it, so the topline is a continuous dome from croup to withers and there is no lean back for a hump to rise out of. The legs are short (belly sits low, legs are roughly a third of standing height, not the stilty camel proportion), they have no knobbly knee pads anywhere, and the feet at 4x zoom are tiny dark CLOVEN HOOF stubs — the opposite of the broad splayed padded camel foot the reference names. Only two legs are drawn; the far-side pair is absent entirely, so the quadruped posture reads as a two-legged side cutout. The tail is also wrong scale: a thick rope leaving the rump high and hanging nearly to the ground with a black tassel, longer than the hind leg.
rows.fix: Rebuild the torso as a shallow lean barrel and sit ONE distinct hump on top of it as a separate mass that breaks the topline (a clear notch in front of it at the withers and behind it at the loin), then swap the hoof stubs for wide two-toed padded footpads that flare wider than the leg, add the knobbly knee callus on the foreleg, lengthen the legs so the belly clears the ground by more than the leg is thick, and shorten the tail to a stub with a tassel.

rows.readsAs: a llama - specifically, the exact same llama that ships as the Llama asset, with a few extra stray hairs
rows.defect: Side by side with Llama.png this is the same drawing: same outline, same skull, same eye, same muzzle, same neck arc, same hip flap, same feet. All three must-reads are missing. The face is LONG and tapering like the llama's, not blunt and short. There is no topknot fringe at all - the crown is bare and smooth. The ears are the flat grey teardrop lying inside the skull outline, so no short spear ear exists in silhouette. The fleece is not dense wool: it is a patch of stringy straw-coloured streaks on the mid-torso plus scraggly grey spikes poking off the neck and belly edge, while the neck, legs and rump are smooth bare shapes. At the shoulder and rump the fleece patch ends in a hard straight cutout edge that reads as a pasted-on sticker seam.
rows.fix: Rebuild the alpaca head separately from the llama head - shorten the muzzle to a stub about half its current length, dome the cranium, plant two SHORT straight ears that clear the skull outline, and pile a shaggy topknot forelock over the brow; then run the crimped fleece over the neck and haunches too so the wool ends in a fuzzy edge instead of a straight seam.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy straw-coloured sheep, or a woolly tapir - nobody names a Bactrian camel
rows.defect: The two-hump identity is not legible. At full size the back is ONE broad flat-topped dome; zooming 3x shows a shallow V notch pressed into it, but the two lobes are wide, low and nearly merged, so the dip is a few pixels on a back over a third of the image wide and vanishes at any real display size. There are not two separate humps, there is one lumpy back. The neck is short and thick, not long and curved, and it is completely smooth - no shaggy hanging hair on the neck or chest, and no hair crowning either hump. The legs are short stubs, roughly a third of standing height, with the belly hanging almost to the hocks. A flat un-shaded tan slab sits over the hip and the tasselled tail sprouts from it like a separate pasted object.
rows.fix: Raise TWO distinct humps with real sky between them - each a tall narrow peak with a deep U valley cutting down to the spine line - then lengthen the neck and legs so the belly rides high, and hang shaggy fringe off the throat, chest and both hump crowns.

rows.readsAs: a camel - a stumpy, overfed one, or at a glance a bison with a long neck
rows.defect: The single hump and the raised curving neck do land, so the animal is namable. But the third must-read fails outright: the legs are short stubs at roughly a third of total height, nowhere near the half the reference calls for, with no knobbly knees or hocks - and the barrel is so deep that the belly hangs down to meet them, killing the leggy dromedary stance. The hump is also not read as a hump so much as the whole torso being one round dome, because the back and the barrel are the same continuous circle with no shoulder or rump line to sit between. The head is the shared chassis skull - a big round eye ringed in white with no split camel lip, no nostril slit and no ear breaking the outline.
rows.fix: Roughly double the leg length and lift the belly line well clear of the knees, then narrow the barrel and set the hump as a distinct peak above a visible withers-to-rump back line rather than letting body and hump be one circle.

rows.readsAs: a llama - the long neck, small head, flat hump-free back and slim legs do carry it
rows.defect: The headline must-read is absent: there are no long banana-curved ears. What sits on the head is a flat grey teardrop painted INSIDE the skull outline, so the silhouette is completely earless and the profile reads slightly reptilian. The neck is one plain forward arc, not an upright S-curve - it leans out over the chest rather than rising vertically then tucking the head back. The flat back is correct. The body has the same hard straight cutout seam at the shoulder and a wedge notch at the rump where the paler wool patch ends against the body, reading as a pasted panel. And because the Alpaca asset is this same drawing, the two species are visually undifferentiated.
rows.fix: Grow two long banana-curved ears that clear the top of the skull by about a head height and curve inward at the tips, and re-carriage the neck into an upright S - vertical out of the withers, then a tuck back at the throat.

rows.readsAs: a sandy Shetland pony / hoofed foal with a bushy tail
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads are absent and the third is contradicted. The frame is not lean or wolfish — it is a deep barrel torso with no flank tuck, four straight posts and dark HOOVES at the ground (visible as split dark caps at 4x). The white feet are missing entirely: the feet are the darkest part of the animal and the only white on the model is a blob on the tail tip. The ears are not erect pointed triangles — they are one dark triangular hood laid flat on top of the skull. The tail is bushy but hooks down and forward, not straight.
rows.fix: Rebuild the chassis below the barrel: cut torso depth ~30%, add a rising flank tuck ahead of the hind leg, replace the four posts with a digitigrade canid limb (angled scapula, elbow at the chest line, a real hock bend on the hind) and terminate every leg in a four-toed white paw instead of a hoof cap.

rows.readsAs: a cream pony / donkey foal, not a dog of any breed
rows.defect: Identical silhouette to the Dingo with a paler fill — same barrel, same four hoofed posts, same hooded head. The plumed tail carried above the back is absent: the tail is set low and swings DOWN and forward past the hocks. The ears are not erect or folded dog ears, they are the shared dark triangular hood on the skull crown. The only must-read that lands is the dark nose blob at the end of the snout, and that snout is a tapered anteater wedge with no jaw or lip line.

rows.readsAs: a white shaggy pony or a long-nosed goat

rows.readsAs: a generic gold aquarium fish — a stranger would say 'goldfish' or 'bream', not 'carp'

The long single dorsal fin running most of the back is also absent: the back carries one tiny rounded nub the same size as the ventral nub, covering maybe 12% of the topline. Side by side with Goldfish.png it is the identical silhouette in a different colour.

rows.readsAs: an orange fish — 'goldfish' is a reasonable guess, but only because of the colour

rows.readsAs: a small slim silvery baitfish — the right ballpark, though it could equally be a sardine or a smelt

rows.readsAs: a fleecy tan goat or young sheep with lyre horns

There is no white band above the muzzle; the face is uniform dark brown. The horns are two small pale crescents perched on a dark cap with no bald forehead plate joining them.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy capybara or a hairy tapir — nothing on it says bison

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and one is understated; fix against THIS description, not theirs. I read the 440x440 PNG whole, then re-cropped and upscaled the skull (8x), the throat/chin (8x), the topline (6x), the tail (6x) and the feet (4x), and measured the silhouette column-by-column. Animal faces RIGHT.

CONFIRMED — NO HORNS. At 8x the crown of the skull is a smooth unbroken dome from the brow to the poll. There is no horn, no nub, no boss, no keratin curve anywhere. The only feature on the upper skull is a small dark soft-edged almond OVAL lying flat against the side of the cranium, tilted up-and-back — that is an ear, not a horn stub; do not mistake it for one when fixing. Every bison carries horns in both sexes; a hornless bovid cannot read as Bison.

CONFIRMED — NO BEARD, but the reason is finer than stated. The throat is not bare: along the jaw/throat leading edge there are roughly eight to ten thin dark hair wisps, each about 6-10px long. They are the SAME generic edge-fur strokes that appear along the topline, the belly and the flank — a rim-fur pass, not a beard. There is no hanging chin mass, no throat curtain, no dark bib. Below the jaw the brisket is a large SMOOTH flat dark-brown wedge with no hair strokes on it at all. So the fix is not 'add hair to a bare chin' — it is 'replace the rim-wisp pass under the jaw with an actual bearded mass'.

CONFIRMED — HEAD CARRIED HIGH, and I can quantify it. Crown of the head sits at y=95. The highest point of the body topline is y=149 (at the withers, x=248). The head is therefore 54px ABOVE the shoulder line, on a short thick level neck. That is the exact inversion of the bison silhouette, in which the head hangs BELOW the hump line. This is the single most damaging defect and it survives independently of the hump.

CONFIRMED — HEAD IS NOT MASSIVE AND IS THE WRONG SHAPE. headFrac 0.27 is roughly met by area, but the mass is in the wrong place: it is a rounded cranium drawn out into a LONG TAPERING WEDGE SNOUT ending in a slightly bulbous down-turned nose pad with a small hooked nostril and a thin straight mouth line. Bison needs a broad, blunt, boxy skull that is nearly as wide as it is long. The eye is also wrong for the row: it is a large rimmed eyeball with a pale sclera ring and a specular highlight — that reads prominent, and the reference row asks for eyes: small.

CORRECTION 1 — THE HUMP IS NOT SIMPLY 'ABSENT' AND THE TOPLINE IS NOT THE FAMILY'S PLAIN ARC. There IS a modest front-heavy topline here. Measured tops: rump x=136 y=180, mid-back x=176-200 y=170-173, withers x=248 y=149. So the back does rise ~31px front-to-rear, and at 6x there is a visible small rounded withers bump with a shallow SADDLE DIP in front of the mid-back arc, plus a short row of standing bristle hairs (a nascent mane) along that dip. The defect is magnitude and placement, not total absence: a ~20-30px rise on a ~227px-tall figure is a bump, not the 'huge muscular' hump the row demands, and it is nullified because the head then rises 54px above it — the eye reads the head as the highest point, so the whole silhouette parses as level-backed. Fix by growing the withers mass so its crest is the tallest thing in the frame and dropping the head under it.

CORRECTION 2 — 'THE HINDQUARTERS ARE AS DEEP AS THE CHEST' IS FALSE. The chest/brisket column is measurably deeper: at x=250 the body runs y=149-278 (~129px); the mid/rear barrel at x=190 runs y=172-265 (~93px). The front is ~35% deeper than the rear and the rump top is 31px lower than the withers. Partial credit is genuinely due on 'narrow tapering hindquarters' — a taper exists — it is just far too gentle, and the haunch is still drawn as a full rounded thigh mass.

OTHER DEFECTS NOT IN THE ORIGINAL CLAIM:
- COAT DISTRIBUTION IS INVERTED. The shaggy hair strokes and the dangling belly fringe cover the mid and REAR barrel, while the forequarters (neck, shoulder patch, brisket) are large SMOOTH flat dark-brown panels with no hair strokes. Bison is the reverse: a long shaggy chocolate cape over head, hump and forelegs, short hair behind. Move the shag forward.
- LEGS ARE TOO LONG AND TOO PALE. They are slim cream/bone-coloured columns; ground is ~y=325 and the belly bottom ~y=264, leaving ~61px of daylight under a 93px-deep barrel. Bison is low-slung on short dark stumpy legs. Feet themselves are FINE and should be kept — at 4x each foot is a correct small dark two-toed cloven hoof.
- TAIL IS WRONG. It is a long, thick, uniform-width smooth tube arcing stiffly out and down from y~195 to y~325 (nearly to the hooves), ending in a straight-cut fan of straw strands. Bison's tail is short with a small terminal tuft. This is a family-chassis donkey/lion tail.

CORRECTION 3 — WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS. 'Capybara' is ruled out by the correct cloven hooves and the long tufted tail, and it is not a tapir either — there is no proboscis, the snout is a plain tapered wedge. The high-carried small head on a short neck, the long tapering muzzle, the shaggy pale barrel, the long slim legs and the fan-tufted tail read closest to a shaggy LLAMA/ALPACA, or a generic long-nosed sheep. Naming it correctly matters because the fix direction differs: it does not need de-rodenting, it needs the head dropped, broadened and bearded, the withers massed up, and the shag moved onto the forequarters.

SCORE: zero of the three must-reads read. No hump, no low-slung massive bearded head, and only a token hindquarter taper — plus no horns at all. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a grey cow or a yak

rows.readsAs: a pale cream goat or a generic antelope

But there is no tall muscular ridge along the shoulders — the topline behind the neck actually DIPS before the barrel rises, the opposite of the gaur's dorsal ridge. rows.readsAs: a pale cream goat — and it is visibly the same picture as Antelope and Impala

The horns are smooth, not ringed. The legs are thick fleecy tubes, not fine and delicate, and the neck is the family's short thick one rather than long. The specified prominent eye is the same size as every other asset's.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan antelope, the same one as Antelope and Impala
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The face is the family's short rounded wedge with a stubby muzzle — nothing about it is extremely long or narrow, despite the 0.32 headFrac. The back does not slope to the hindquarters: it is the same smooth convex arc, and the rump is actually the HIGHEST point of the body rather than the lowest. The horns are the standard lyre pair set flat on the skull with no bony pedestal and no bracket shape.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x and at 4x/6x/8x crops of the head, horn bases, topline and hindquarters, plus a per-column silhouette profile (luminance>70 against the navy plate) and the same profile run on Antelope and Impala for comparison. Verdict FAIL stands, but the stated causes are only one-third correct and one of them is FLATLY INVERTED — fix against this description, not theirs.

MUST-READ 2 (back sloping steeply down to the hindquarters) IS PRESENT, and the claim that 'the rump is the highest point, the opposite of the reference' is WRONG. The animal faces right. Measured top-of-silhouette by column: over the front legs / withers (x=250-270) the topline sits at y=142-156; over the hind legs / rump (x=158-190) it sits at y=186-196. The topline climbs monotonically front-ward from x=202 (y=186) to x=266 (y=142) with no rump hump anywhere. That is ~38-40px of drop across a ~110px torso, roughly 20 degrees of downward slope from withers to rump — the correct hartebeest direction. Do NOT 'fix' this; touching it will destroy the one identity cue the asset has. The comparison species confirm it is a real differentiator: Antelope's torso topline is 176 at 20% of torso length and 178 at 80% (dead level), Impala the same. So 'reads as the same generic tan antelope as Antelope and Impala' is also wrong — this asset has a visibly heavier, taller forequarter, a sloping back, a thicker neck and a fringed tail those two do not have; it is distinguishable from them at thumbnail size. The only fair complaint about the slope is that it could be steeper (~20 deg vs the ~28-30 deg of a real kongoni), which is POLISH, not FAIL.

MUST-READ 1 (extremely long narrow elongated face) IS GENUINELY ABSENT — this is the real reason it fails. The head is a rounded, deep cranial blob with a short blunt tapering muzzle ending in a rounded pinkish-tan nose pad and a drawn mouth line. Measured: eye center ~x=302,y=119; nose tip x=347, so eye-to-nose is only ~45px, while head depth at the eye (skull top y=105 to jaw/cheek bottom ~y=160) is ~55px. The muzzle is SHORTER than the head is deep; a hartebeest needs roughly 2x the opposite. Head length nose-to-poll (~62px) over body length nose-to-rump (~229px) is 0.27, i.e. the declared headFrac 0.32 is not even being spent, and what is spent goes into cranial bulk rather than length. Relative to the family this head is no longer than Antelope's (0.29) — it reads as a cow/bull head, not a hartebeest face. The judge's phrase 'short rounded wedge' is accurate.

MUST-READ 3 (bracket horns on a bony pedestal) IS ABSENT, but the description needs correcting. The horns are not a flat lyre: each is a pale cream tube that leaves the skull at EYE LEVEL (bases at y~120, x~291 and x~312, i.e. BELOW the top of the skull at y~105 — anatomically the horns are pinned to the sides of the face, not the crown), rises, and carries a shallow S-kink in its upper third with the tip turning up-and-outward; the two peak at y=72 about 40px apart. So there is a faint kink, but no common pedicel and no bracket/Z profile: the pair splays into a wide U from two widely separated eye-level roots. What might be mistaken for a pedestal is NOT one — the dark-brown mass at the horn bases resolves at 8x into two EARS: a brown crescent ear laid back on the left/rear of the skull and a small brown triangular ear tucked between the horn bases. The fix is a single raised bony pedicel on the crown with both horns leaving it together, then out, then sharply back.

Other details actually seen (none of which change the band): the tail is a thick tan arc springing from the rump ending in a dark brown fringed tuft (right idea, should be black and thinner); hooves are dark and cloven with a visible pastern; the hind leg is a straight column with essentially no hock angulation (the shared quadruped chassis showing through); there is a pale grey-white arc over the shoulder and a flat mid-brown quad on the upper foreleg that read as unresolved patch shapes rather than the hartebeest's dark thigh/shoulder blazes.

Summary of the fix list, in priority order: (1) elongate the face — pull the muzzle to ~2x head depth and narrow the cranium; (2) rebuild the horn root as one tall pedicel on the crown and re-profile the horns to the bracket; (3) leave the sloping topline alone (optionally steepen slightly); (4) blacken and thin the tail tuft.

rows.readsAs: a tan fleecy goat — the third copy of the Antelope drawing in this batch
rows.defect: No vertical black stripes on the rump; the hindquarters are plain tan and there is no white rump for them to sit on. No black tuft above the hind hoof. The legs are thick woolly tubes rather than extremely fine, and the horns are smooth putty crescents with no rings and no out-then-up lyre sweep.
rows.fix: Add the white rump with two black vertical bars flanking the tail and a black tuft at each hind fetlock, and slim the legs to half their current width.

rows.readsAs: a broken decal — a striped animal with a black slab stuck on its side
rows.defect: The flank markings have collapsed into a solid dark rectangular bar spanning nearly the whole barrel with comb-like tines hanging off its lower edge; it reads as a rendering artifact pasted over the body, not as stripes, and its hard rectangular top and bottom edges cut straight across the topline shading. rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and the real defect is different in kind. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (inspected at 1x, then 3x/6x/10x/12x crops of head, flank, topline, feet, tail, muzzle).

CORRECTION 1 - NOT a 'solid dark rectangular slab'. At 6x the flank carries ~14 DISCRETE dark-brown stripes, each a tapered wedge that radiates down and slightly forward from the topline, with clearly visible pale cream gaps between them. They are individually legible as stripes. What makes them collapse into a slab at 1x is a separate object: a single SOLID HORIZONTAL RULED BAR, ~4-5px thick and ~110px long (src coords roughly x=155..268 at y=232 in the 440x440 canvas), with blunt SQUARE ends that both float in open flank - the left end stops mid-barrel, the right end stops mid-ribcage. Every vertical stripe terminates on this bar, so the assembly literally draws a comb: a straight machined spine with tines hanging off it. THE BAR IS THE ARTIFACT, not the stripes. Removing the bar and thinning the tine count would fix most of the 1x read.

CORRECTION 2 - the stripes do NOT cut across the topline. At 9x the topline is clean: the stripes are correctly clipped to the body silhouette, and there is even a pale rim highlight running along the back that they respect. No marking anywhere overruns the outline - I also checked the muzzle bar at 12x and it stops at the jaw/nose, it does not overshoot into empty space. The 'hard straight edges' the judge saw are the interior ruled bars, not silhouette breaks.

CORRECTION 3 - the ears are NOT small nubs. Behind and left of the horn bases there is a substantial ear cluster: a rounded tan lobe roughly 19x34px on a head ~82px long (i.e. ~40% of head length), plus a dark-brown angular wedge overlapping it, plus a smaller pale triangular flap below. Comparison with Impala.png from the same batch confirms this is a deliberate enlarged-ear parameter, not generic head geometry - Impala's head is a bare wedge with nothing there.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. (a) Must-read 'thin WHITE vertical stripes' is inverted and over-counted: what is drawn is ~14 DARK brown bars on a pale tan coat, where a kudu is thin pale stripes on a darker grey-brown coat. The single most diagnostic kudu marking is delivered in reverse polarity. (b) The comb bar above is a non-anatomical rendering artifact welded across the barrel, and it is not alone - there are three more ruled horizontal bars with blunt square ends on the neck and cheek, one of which crosses the neck striping to form an unmistakable '+' at the shoulder. (c) The ear cluster, while large, is a muddle of three overlapping shapes half-buried behind the horn base and jaw; it does not resolve as the required 'enormous rounded satellite dish'. (d) The face carries 4-5 zebra-like dark bars across the muzzle; a kudu has a plain face with a single white nose chevron.

WHAT IS GOOD AND SHOULD NOT BE TOUCHED: the horns read correctly - two cream, tapering, double-S helical shafts with faint ridge lines, rising ~27% of total figure height above the head, clearly distinct from Impala's lyre. Legs are fine and correctly cloven (two-toe hooves at 6x). Tail is a thick tan rope with a proper fringed brush tuft. Silhouette, stance and proportions read as a large antelope.

FAMILY NOTE: Bongo.png in the same directory is the identical chassis with the identical comb artifact and the identical inverted dark striping, differing only in coat hue. This is one shared stripe-generator defect, not two per-species defects - fix it once at the generator.

FIX ORDER: (1) delete the horizontal ruled bar(s) that the stripes anchor to; (2) invert stripe polarity to pale-on-darker-coat; (3) cut the count from ~14 to 6-10 and make them near-vertical rather than a converging fan; (4) resolve the ear cluster into one broad rounded paddle clear of the horn base; (5) drop the muzzle barring in favour of a single nose chevron.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy ox with one broken tusk

WHAT I DID: read the 440x440 PNG whole, then decoded it and re-rendered 5 magnified crops (head at 6-8x, horn cluster at 8x, topline at 5x, lower legs at 5x, rump/tail at 7x). Subject bbox is x87-352, y91-331 = 266w x 241h, aspect 1.10 against the packet's aspect: 1.5 — the figure is far too tall/square, and the reason is the high head carriage (see below).

What the first judge read as asymmetry is the near/far pair rendered as a stacked double-crescent. Do NOT "add the missing second horn" — it is already there and adding a third will make this worse.

Both horns are rooted at the TOP-REAR of the skull and sweep UP AND BACKWARD over the neck, tapering to points that end in open background above and behind the crown. That is a yak / Highland-cattle horn set. The must-read asks for horns meeting in a helmet-like BOSS across the forehead, then hooking DOWN AND OUT. There is no boss: the forehead between the horn bases is covered by a dark-brown elliptical cap (same dark shading tone as the cheek mass), not a pale keratin plate, and the pale horn material never spreads across the frontal bone. There is no downward hook anywhere — the horn tips are the highest points on the whole animal. So: two horns present, boss absent, hook absent. Fix = re-root both horns low on the forehead, fuse their bases into one pale cream boss plate spanning the frontal, and re-curve them down past the eye line before flaring out.

CORRECTION 2 - THE COAT. The claim "the curtain of hair is missing entirely" is an overstatement. The coat IS long and shaggy: the whole flank is painted with long vertical streaky guard-hair strokes, there are stray hair spikes breaking the dorsal silhouette from rump to withers, a hair fringe along the throat/brisket, and a handful of genuine hanging strands that drop past the belly line at the mid-barrel and at the rear flank. The defect is LENGTH, not absence. The hem sits at the ordinary belly line (real y ~276-284) with wisps to ~y292; hooves are at y~328. So roughly 45-50px of bare pale leg is exposed on all four legs — about 20% of the standing height. The must-read wants that skirt down to just above the hooves, i.e. the bare leg reduced to the cannon/pastern only. Fix = extend the existing hair strands ~35-40px further down and close the hem into a continuous skirt; the texture engine already produces the right strand look, it just stops too high.

CONFIRMED - POSTURE. The claim is right. The neck rises steeply off the shoulder and the head is carried level-to-HIGH: the muzzle tip sits at about the same height as the withers and the crown sits ~180px above the back line, which is what inflates the aspect to 1.10. There is only a very slight withers rise; the back is essentially a flat-to-gently-domed line from rump to shoulder with no musk-ox hump. The head must drop so the poll sits below the shoulder, and the shoulder must gain a real hump.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS: eyes are correctly small — two small dark ovals set high and wide on a 3/4-front face, the near one carrying a white crescent highlight. All four legs terminate in properly drawn dark cloven hooves. No tail is visible at the rump, which is acceptable for this species. Head shape is a long horse-like bovine muzzle, too narrow and too long for a musk ox's short blunt face.

BAND: FAIL stands. All three of the packet's must-reads fail on form (curtain too short, no boss and no down-out hook, head high and shoulders unhumped) and the asset currently reads as a shaggy yak / Highland bull rather than a musk ox. This is not a polish-level gap.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size and then at 4-5x crops of the head, the feet and the tail. UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and one credit is missing.

HORNS (mustRead 1: 'enormous swept-back crescent horns') — GENUINELY ABSENT, the claim is right. There is exactly ONE horn: a pale ivory/bone tapering rod that roots on the top of the skull just above and behind the eye, crosses the crown right-to-left and curves up to a blunt upturned tip that clears the head by about a head-width. No second horn anywhere — not mirrored, not foreshortened, not tucked behind the ear. I cropped Wildebeest.png and Yak.png at the same magnification to test the 'reused element' part of the claim and it is CONFIRMED: both carry the identical single ivory hooked rod in the identical crown position, just shorter and more strongly hooked. Three bovids, one horn part. NOTE one refinement: the rod IS swept backwards (base forward at the brow, tip trailing back over the neck), so 'swept-back' is not the missing property — what is missing is (a) the PAIR and (b) the mass/breadth of a crescent. The fix is a mirrored pair of thick, flattened, broad-based crescents leaving the skull sideways at the brow and sweeping back-and-up over the shoulders, not a longer version of the shared rod.

MUZZLE (mustRead 3: 'broad flat wet muzzle held low') — FAILS, but NOT for the stated reason. The claim that it is 'a small rounded goat nose' is WRONG. The muzzle is large: a long, deep, rounded snout occupying roughly the front third of the head, ending in a big blunt dome, with a thin dark lipline running its whole length and a small hooked nostril tick set high on the front face. The actual defect is that it is a smooth tapered sheep/tapir snout with no broad flat nose PLATE — no dark wet rhinarium pad, no wide paired nostrils, no squared-off front. Head carriage part of the claim is CORRECT: the skull sits clearly above the topline on an upward-angled neck and juts forward; nothing is carried low and there is no shoulder boss or forward-of-the-chest neck drop.

BODY — mustRead 2 ('heavy low-slung body with a straight back') is the one that partly reads: the topline is genuinely straight and the barrel is deep. But the pelt is drawn as fine streaky pale-grey fleece strokes over a light grey ground, the neck is slim, and the ears are small (a dark rounded lobe behind the eye plus a dark pointed lobe forward of it, with a dark brown mask ring around a large glossy eye). Combined with the single ivory rod, it reads closer to a grey woolly SHEEP/RAM than to the 'generic grey woolly ox' the claim names — it is not ox-massive.

CREDIT THE JUDGE DID NOT GIVE: the feet are correct — all four end in two small dark cloven hoof-toes, cleanly separated. The tail is also correct — long, thin, with a broad bushy dark terminal tuft. Neither needs work; the failure is entirely the horn pair and the muzzle plate.

rows.readsAs: a striped grey pony or a badly drawn zebra
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are wrong on screen. The head is not a heavy boxy cow-like skull -- it is a flat pale oval disc held out horizontally from the neck, painted with dark bars, reading as a mask or shield plate rather than a head, and its horns are the same single pale tusk borrowed from the buffalo and yak instead of paired hooks curving out sideways. There is no shaggy chin beard and no neck mane; the dark bars over the neck and barrel read as zebra striping. The topline is level, so the high withers sloping down to a low rump is absent too, and a large pale plume disc hangs off the rump. A stranger names this a striped pony.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1:1, at 3x, and at 5-9x crops of the head, throat, rump/tail and feet; also measured the silhouette's top edge column-by-column from the decoded pixels. The FAIL stands, but one of the three stated causes is factually wrong and the single worst defect went unmentioned.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS: a pale bone-grey pony/quagga. The dominant signal is bold dark-brown VERTICAL BARS painted across the whole barrel, over the shoulder, up the neck AND across the face. A real wildebeest is a plain dark slate animal with at most faint brindle on the forequarters; this is zebra livery applied head-to-tail. Body is a smooth equine barrel on four thick pale columnar legs.

MUST-READ 1 - 'heavy boxy cow-like head with sideways-curving horns': FAILS, and the judge described it correctly in substance. The head is a flat pale ELLIPSE, wider than tall, with a second larger translucent grey ghost-ellipse stacked behind/under it so the head reads as a doubled disc roughly as deep as the neck is long. Two corrections: (a) it is NOT held horizontally - it is tilted about 25-30 degrees nose-down toward the lower right, muzzle end at approx (350,175) in a 440px frame, cranium end at approx (265,120); (b) there IS a feature the judge missed sitting on the skull - a solid mid-brown ellipse at roughly (285,95) reading as an ear or horn boss, the only non-striped element up there. Horn: exactly ONE cream/bone tusk, base at approx (275,105), sweeping up and curving back to the LEFT and terminating at approx (248,80). It reads as a warthog/boar tusk or a small mammoth tusk, not as a pair of cow horns sweeping out sideways and hooking up. No second horn anywhere, no lateral spread, no dark horn boss across the brow.

MUST-READ 2 - 'shaggy chin beard and neck mane': FAILS, absent. At 7x the entire leading edge of the neck from jaw to chest is one clean unbroken smooth curve - no fringe, no dangling hair, no silhouette break at the throat. The top of the neck is likewise smooth; the only thing along it is a thin pale highlight seam over the shoulder, which is a shading arc, not a crest. Nothing on this animal is shaggy.

MUST-READ 3 - 'high shoulders sloping to a slight rump': THE JUDGE IS WRONG HERE. The topline is not level. Measuring the topmost non-background pixel per column: croup at x=136 is y=198, and the back rises monotonically to the withers at x=248, y=154. Ground line is y~330, so withers stand ~176px above ground versus ~132px at the croup - a 1.33 ratio and a ~25%-of-body-height rise. The forequarter-high sloping topline is genuinely present and readable. This must-read should be scored as MET; do not spend a fix on it.

OTHER DEFECTS THE JUDGE DID NOT REPORT:
- TAIL (worst unlisted problem): a huge grey radiating FAN, a disc about 90px across with ~20 spiky bristles fanning off its left edge, held out horizontally from the rump at approx (60-135, 190-260). It is larger than the head. A wildebeest tail is a long thin black horse-like switch hanging to the hocks; this is a peacock/turkey fan and it dominates the rear silhouette.
- FEET: partial credit against the 'pony' read - each of the four legs ends in a tiny paired dark-brown CLOVEN toe cap (two distinct blobs per foot, ~6px each), so the hooves are correctly artiodactyl. They are just far too small to register at thumbnail size against the equine leg columns above them.
- A wide dark brown horizontal band runs the full length of the flank at belly height (y~215) like a saddle girth strap, adding to the harnessed-pony impression.

VERDICT: two of three must-reads (boxy horned cow head; beard and mane) are absent, the identity-carrying head is a striped mask disc with a single boar tusk, and the coat is zebra-striped. It reads as the wrong organism. FAIL upheld.

FIX TARGETS, in order: (1) replace the single tusk with a PAIR of dark horns emerging low and wide from a heavy brow boss, sweeping out sideways then hooking up; (2) rebuild the head as a deep boxy squared-off skull carried LOW on a level or downward neck, kill the ghost underlay disc; (3) add a shaggy fringe on the throat/chin and a coarse crest along the neck top; (4) replace the fan tail with a thin long dark switch; (5) strip the stripes back to a few faint brindle marks on the forequarter only and darken the base coat to slate. Do NOT touch the topline - it is already right.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy brown highland cow or yak
