There is exactly ONE ear form: a mid-brown disc ~30px across centred at ~(305,140) with a tilted dark-brown inner ellipse (concha) sitting directly above and behind the eye. Its outline IS the cranium's top-and-rear outline — the ear is fused into the skull dome and projects nothing above the head line. A faint darker crescent along its far (left) rim hints at a second ear but does not read as one. So the judge's 'single brown disc sitting on the skull like an earmuff rather than a pair of tall rounded paddles' is CONFIRMED verbatim. Worse, the dark concha ellipse reads as a facial mask patch, not an ear opening. (2) 'irregular patchwork blotches' — PRESENT and the strongest read: irregular amoeboid patches scattered over flank, shoulder and rump. Caveat the judge missed: they are chocolate BROWN, never black, and there is NO white anywhere in the coat, so the tricolour patchwork is really two-tone brown-on-tan. (3) 'white brush tail tip' — PRESENT and clean: a bright white round tip at ~(120,237) on a fringed plume. (4) 'lean long-legged frame' — FAILS, but NOT for the reason given. CORRECTIONS: (a) 'hoof-blocks' is FALSE. At 5x both the front foot (~x264-288,y296-306) and the hind foot (~x172-196) are clearly TOED PAWS — 3-4 toe divisions with darker brown pad shading. The feet are the one anatomically correct part of the limb; do not touch them. (b) 'tail attaches mid-back' is FALSE. The tail base is at the rear of the croup at ~(165,205), i.e. the top-rear of the hindquarters, which is the correct attachment. What the judge saw is the PLUME arcing up and forward so its mass overlaps the flank at back height; the fix is the arc and the plume shape (currently a short fan with a hard geometric facet, not a long cylindrical brush), not the attachment point. (c) 'no lean long-legged frame' misdiagnoses LENGTH. Measured: mid-torso topline y=169, belly y=220, ground y=304 — so belly-to-ground is 84px against a torso depth of only 51px. The legs are already LONGER than the body is deep; lengthening them would be the wrong fix. The real defect is THICKNESS and ARTICULATION: shank widths measured 23-29px at y=255-295, i.e. roughly half the torso depth, giving four plush unarticulated tapering columns with no hock break on the hind, no stifle, no elbow or pastern on the fore. Also the far limb pair is drawn almost coincident with the near pair (only two silhouette runs at every scanline y=255-295), so the stance has no depth. THE CHASSIS IS CONFIRMED WRONG: deep barrel torso with only a shallow tuck (belly y=235 at the chest rising to y=220 at mid-body, ~15px of tuck on a 51px-deep body — a wild dog needs a pronounced waist), a thick crested neck with a pale mane band along its top, and a small head on top of it. Two more defects neither judge named: the muzzle is a long, thin, down-curved tube with a separated lower-jaw line that reads nearly beak-like, where an AWD has a short blunt broad muzzle; and there is no black facial mask and no dark forehead stripe, the whole face being plain tan with a dark nose blob. Net: only the blotches and the white tail tip land. Ears, frame and head all fail. FAIL stands.

UPHELD, but roughly half the stated causes are wrong and would send a fixer to the wrong shapes. What I actually saw at 4x-20x zoom (crops of head, crown, muzzle, tail, rump, feet; body bbox 99,141-340,282):

EARS - the judge's 'tiny nub' is wrong; there are TWO ears, and the real defect is worse than a nub. At 20x on the crown (orig x282-327, y133-163) the skull outline is a PERFECTLY SMOOTH DOME with nothing breaking it at all. The ears are two flat-shaded TRIANGLES painted entirely INSIDE that dome - a mid-grey far ear and a smaller pink-grey near ear, apexes pointing up, both stopping ~6px short of the crown edge. They are ear-inner-surfaces with no ear behind them. Direct A/B against Fox.png in the same batch: the red fox's two triangular ears DO rise clear above the crown and break the silhouette. So the Arctic Fox was made by shrinking the fox's ear until it sank below the skull line. Result: the head reads as bald/earless in silhouette, and what pigment is there is POINTED, so 'short ROUNDED ears' fails twice over - wrong shape and no silhouette presence.

MUZZLE - judge is right that it fails and right that it is the family-wide part, but the direction is backwards and worth stating precisely. It is a long tapering wedge running from the eye to a rounded tip carrying a big dark oval nose, plus a SEPARATE flat grey slab beneath it for the lower jaw (the 'generic bar' - the same detached horizontal slab Fox and Coyote carry). Measured skull-back-to-nose-tip: Arctic Fox 59px (x281 to x340) vs Fox 53px (x286 to x339). The arctic muzzle is LONGER than the red fox's in the same batch, which is the exact inverse of the reference note 'everything is shortened and rounded compared to a red fox'. 'Blunt short muzzle' is absent.

TAIL - the judge's description is substantially WRONG and must not be fixed against. It is NOT thin, NOT grey-and-white striped, and NOT non-white. At 7x-10x the tail is a FAT WHITE ROUNDED CLUB - the brightest white in the whole piece, roughly as thick as the thigh, ~1/3 body length - ending in a soft rounded off-white cap. The grey-and-white 'stripes' the judge saw are a one-sided COMB OF INDIVIDUAL HAIR STRANDS fringing only its upper-outer edge against the black background; they are not the tail body. Nor is it 'held horizontally out of mid-back': it attaches at the croup/rump (correct place) and angles DOWN-LEFT about 35 degrees below horizontal. The one grain of truth is the tip - there is a visible elliptical seam where the bright cap meets the shaft, which can read as the cut mouth of a tube. The genuine defect here is different from the one claimed: the tail is white and roundish but reads as a SMOOTH HARD BATON (three quarters of its outline is a clean hard curve, fur strokes on one edge only), so 'dense fluffy' does not land even though 'white' and 'round' partly do. This must-read is the closest to passing of the three.

FEET - correcting a plausible mis-read: these are NOT hooves. At 8x each foot is a flat grey oval pad split into 3-4 toe blocks. They are paws, just grey (which does chip at the all-white coat) and splayed like platters.

COAT - 'thick fluffy all-white coat' half-lands: the body is genuinely all-white with short white fur flicks over it, but the silhouette edge is smooth and hard everywhere, so it reads as white paint on a smooth body rather than winter pelage. No cheek ruff, no neck ruff.

CHASSIS / WHOLE-ORGANISM READ - the judge's headline is right and I can put a number on it. Colour-mask silhouette IoU against its batch-mates: Fox 0.874, African Wild Dog 0.766, Coyote 0.760, Jackal 0.745 (Fennec, which has real ears, 0.350). This is the Fox rig recoloured white. Column profiles confirm it: mid-barrel body depth y174-222 (~48px) with the ground at y282, i.e. belly-to-ground ~60px - the legs are LONGER than the body is deep, and Fox measures the same within 2px. A real arctic fox is the inverse: short legs buried in a deep fluffy body. Deep smooth barrel + long straight stockinged legs + small smooth head + high-carried tail reads as a small white pony or a white lurcher, not a fox. FAIL stands: two of three must-reads (short rounded ears, blunt short muzzle) are outright absent, the third only half-present, and the organism is a recolour of its own batch-mate.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, subject bbox x95-344 y125-299, 250x175, measured aspect 1.43 against the packet's 1.9 -- the animal is markedly stubbier and deeper than the reference asks, and the note 'slighter and leggier than a wolf' is contradicted).

EARS -- THE JUDGE IS WRONG. It is NOT 'one small triangle laid back'. At 12x there are TWO ERECT TRIANGULAR EARS, both pointing straight up, apex at y~124 and base at y~143 (~19px tall on a 175px animal, head length ~65px). The real defect is that they are FUSED into a single tent/pyramid: a shared vertical centre ridge with one dark triangular face flaring left (far ear) and one flaring right (near ear), no gap between them, no ear cup or inner-fold shading, and the far ear's outer corner is squared off flat instead of coming to a point. The result reads as an origami paper hat / a dorsal crest sitting on the crown, not as two independent upright cones rising off the top of the skull. They also sit too far back and too flat on the crown. So: erect and triangular yes, paired yes, but not separated and only moderately large -- a coyote's ears should be conspicuously oversized relative to the skull.

TAIL -- THE JUDGE IS WRONG. It is NOT 'carried level out of the middle of the back'. It leaves the croup at approximately (152,193) and drops down-and-back at roughly 40-45 degrees to a tip at (111,240) -- i.e. it ends near hip level, clearly BELOW the topline (back sits at y~165). It also does carry fringe: there is a comb of dark hair strokes along its whole upper/outer edge. The genuine tail defects are (a) the mass is a smooth tapered banana/tube, fringed on one side only, so it reads as a haired rod rather than a cylindrical brush with volume all round, and (b) it terminates in a HARD FLAT DARK ELLIPTICAL CAP -- the end face of a cut cylinder, the same disc shape used for the feet -- instead of a soft black-tipped brush. The dock is also set high off the croup rather than low off the rump.

MUZZLE -- fully present and the one clean must-read: a long narrow tapering muzzle with a distinct dark rounded nose leather at the tip. Minor defect: a hard straight dark bar for the mouth line running x~306-332 at y~158, which reads as a machined seam and slightly breaks the lower jaw silhouette rather than as a lip.

FEET -- the judge said 'dark hooves'. Close but imprecise: each foot is a WIDE DARK FLAT OVAL PAD, wider than the leg it sits on, with only very faint vertical striations hinting at toes and a small rear lobe. It is not a cloven hoof and it is not a canid paw -- it is a dark blob shoe. There are no separated digits, no visible claws, no metatarsal pad.

WHY IT STILL FAILS -- the chassis, which the judge is right about. Topline is dead level y~163-168 from x175 to x271, then ramps steeply up from x279 (y149) to x295 (y129): a withers hump into an arched, cresty neck carrying the head ~37px ABOVE the back, which is horse/llama head carriage, not the low level-with-the-shoulder carriage of a coyote. Barrel is deep and round (back y165 to belly y224, 59px) with no chest-to-flank tuck. All four limbs are smooth tapering columns with no carpal break in front and effectively no hock angle behind -- no digitigrade rise from the ground to the hock, so the hind leg is a straight post rather than the Z of a canid. Combined with the oval hoof-pads this is the shared equine chassis, and at full size the silhouette reads as a stocky pony with a pointed head. Fixing this is not polish: the limb model, barrel depth, neck set and foot terminators all need replacing, so FAIL stands.

rows.verifyWhy:
REFUTED on the central claim. I decoded the PNG and measured it (creature bbox x143-296, y155-267, i.e. 154x113 px inside a 440x440 canvas) and re-read it at 5x, 7x and 9x zoom on head, rump/tail junction and feet.

EARS - the judge is measurably wrong. There is ONE dominant ear, not 'two small spiky triangles about a third of head length'. Column profiling gives the ear apex at (x252, y156); the skull crown sits at y~170 and the ear base meets the head at y~188, so the ear triangle is ~32 px tall. Nose tip is at x296 and the back of the skull at x~258, so head length is ~38 px. Ear / head = 0.84 - i.e. NEARLY AS LONG AS THE HEAD, exactly the packet must-read. Standing height (ear tip y156 to feet y267) is 111 px, so the ear alone is 32/111 = 29% of standing height, matching the packet note that 'the ears alone can be a third of the standing height'. The ear is also drawn properly, as a pale outer triangle with a concentric darker brown INNER-EAR triangle inside it. The specific failure mode the packet warns about ('undersized ears turn it into an ordinary fox') is NOT present here.

What the judge probably reacted to, and where they are partly right: the ear is surrounded by 3 SPURIOUS TRIANGULAR SPIKES that turn the cluster into a starburst - one small point above-right of the ear apex (~x272,y159), one wedge pointing BACKWARD/down-left off the nape (~x246-252, y173-195), and one point jutting right over the brow (~x276,y168). Only one of the four triangles reads as an ear; the far ear is not resolved as a second ear, just as another spike. So 'splayed like a paper crown' describes the clutter fairly, but 'nowhere near head-length' is false and is the wrong thing to fix. The fix is to DELETE the three stray spikes and mirror a second ear, not to enlarge the ears.

TAIL - the judge's geometry is wrong on attachment, right on the end cap. The tail is NOT detached and NOT floating beside the rump: at 7x the tail mass is contiguous with and overlaps the rump/croup along a shared edge from about (x200,y196) down to (x205,y235); there is no gap. It hangs low and behind, which is correct for a fox. What IS broken is the terminus: the black tip is painted as a hard-edged filled dark-brown CIRCLE (~14 px diameter, centred ~x167,y240) with no taper, no fur strokes crossing it and no shading, so it reads as the open flat end of a tube rather than a furred black tip. The bushy fringe exists but only on the upper-left rim (a comb of ~12 dark hair strokes); the rest of the tail is a smooth untextured paddle, which is what sells the 'drum' impression. A hard-edged tan TRIANGLE (the near hind thigh) also slices diagonally across the tail from ~(x195,y212) to ~(x185,y250), an unshaded flat wedge that compounds the mechanical look.

FEET - the judge is wrong. These are not hooves. Each foot terminates in a cluster of 3-4 small rounded darker-tan TOE LOBES (clearest on both left legs around y258-266); they are generic and undersized but they are paws, not hoof capsules. Do not 'de-hoof' this asset.

BODY - the judge is right here. The torso is the shared heavy quadruped barrel: deep chest with a shaggy ventral ruff, wide croup, thick straight columnar legs with no visible hock or elbow angulation. The packet asks for a 'tiny slender body' and this is neither tiny nor slender - it is the same chassis as the other canids in this family batch. The coat colour IS correct (cream/ivory pale), the muzzle IS narrow and pointed with a dark nose, and the eye is present and amber.

BAND - POLISH, not FAIL. Two of three must-reads are genuinely readable (gigantic near-head-length ear; pale coat with pointed muzzle; black-tipped low-carried bushy tail present though crudely capped). The organism reads as a big-eared desert fox, not as the wrong animal, so the FAIL does not stand. Real work remaining, in priority order: (1) remove the 3 stray triangular spikes around the ear and resolve a proper second ear; (2) replace the flat black circle at the tail tip with a tapered, fur-stroked dark tip and carry the fringe around the whole tail silhouette; (3) slim the barrel and legs toward the 'tiny slender' spec and blend the flat tan thigh wedge into the tail/haunch.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and one is flatly false. What I actually saw at 3x-12x zoom plus pixel sampling (image 440x440, creature bbox x102-338, y141-283, so 237 wide x 143 tall, aspect 1.66 against the packet's 2.3):

CHASSIS (the real defect, and the judge is right about it): this is the shared pony/foal chassis. Deep round barrel (back at y~176, belly at y~225, so ~49px of body depth) sitting on four straight columnar legs of only ~58px, a short thick neck rising steeply off high withers, a high rounded rump, and a horse-style tail dock. The packet's note 'body is far lower and lighter than a dog's' is inverted here - it is taller and heavier. That, plus the hoof-like feet, is what makes it read equine.

TAIL - claim PARTLY WRONG. It is NOT a 'short level cylinder capped by a dark disc'. It is a tapered plume that leaves the dock and angles DOWNWARD to the left, and it does carry a genuine fringe of dark hair strands radiating off the tip, so there is real bushiness in the render. What is true: it is far too short and it is not white-tipped. Tail spans x102 to the dock at x~157 = ~57px, against a nose-to-rump body of ~188px (x150 to x338), i.e. ~30% of body length where the packet demands 'nearly body-length'. On white: I counted pixels in the tail box (x100-165, y180-250) with min(r,g,b)>170 - ZERO. The tail body is saturated orange (250/128/53), the brightest pixel anywhere in the tail is 217/149/96, and the tip fringe is dark brown (~100/55/30). So the tip is dark, not white. Fix = lengthen the brush to near body length and put a genuine white/cream terminal third on it; the hair-fringe rendering already there is worth keeping.

EARS - claim FALSE. There is not 'one small triangle'. There are TWO erect sharp triangular ears forming a clear V above the crown: a near ear in bright orange with a dark inner-face triangle, and a darker far ear behind it. Both are pointed and erect. The real problem is scale and seating, not count: total ear height is only ~17px against a ~53px head (x285-338), roughly 32% of head length where a red fox reads 45-50%, and the bases are sunk into the skull dome so only ~10px actually protrudes above the crown line (ear apex y=141 vs crown y~150). Do NOT 'add an ear' - grow the existing pair and lift them clear of the skull.

STOCKINGS - claim CORRECT, with one nuance. Sampling the foreleg down x=290 gives 209/132/81 continuously from shoulder to y~269, identical to torso midtone 205/124/72; the hindleg at x=178 is the same. Dark colour (91/45/19) appears only in the last ~14px. So there are no black stockings, exactly as claimed. The nuance: the foot is not a bare hoof - at 4x there are three toe grooves cut into the dark block - but at display size it still reads as a hoof cap because it is a squat wedge with no digit relief in silhouette.

NET: the head alone (pointed muzzle, dark nose button, paired erect triangles) is vulpine and salvageable. Two of the three must-reads - huge bushy white-tipped tail, low slender body on black stockings - are genuinely absent, and the chassis is equine, so the FAIL stands.

UPHELD as FAIL, but three of the four stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (looked at 440x440 render, then at 7x-16x nearest-neighbour crops of head, ear, tail, hind foot):

1. SHARED-CHASSIS CLAIM: CONFIRMED, and now quantified. A silhouette IoU of Jackal.png against Coyote.png (background-keyed at threshold 24) gives both=16597 px, Jackal-only=829, Coyote-only=2214, IoU 84.5%. The diff map shows the entire non-overlap is a 1-2px halo tracing the outline - Coyote is uniformly a hair larger. There is no differing feature anywhere: same barrel, same arched topline crest, same neck, same four columns, same foot pucks, same head wedge, same ear pair, same tail. The two species differ ONLY in hue (Jackal warmer/tan, Coyote greyer/cream). This is the family defect the packet's warning box asks about, and it is real.

2. WHAT THE CHASSIS READS AS: a foal / stocky pony with a canid head pasted on. Deep round barrel with a horse-like arched back, short thick neck rising near-vertically to a small head carried HIGH above the withers (canids carry the head low and forward, level with or below the topline), and four straight columnar limbs with zero angulation - no hock, no stifle, no elbow, no carpus - front and hind legs are the same column mirrored.

3. FEET - claim is roughly right but described wrong. At 16x each foot is a wide flat dark-brown ELLIPSE/plinth clearly wider than the leg column, with a thin light rim under it. There ARE three faint vertical toe hatch-marks painted on its front face, so it is not literally a bare hoof - but they are interior shading only, they do not break the silhouette, and at full size the foot reads as a hoof puck. Fix must add real toes/paw pads that change the OUTLINE, not more hatching.

4. EARS - the claim "one small triangle rather than large pointed erect ears" is WRONG. At 14x there are clearly TWO erect triangular ears sharing a vertical apex ridge: a near ear (dark inner face, apex to the right) and a far ear behind it (apex to the left), each with a lit outer rim. Measured: ear height ~18px against a head length (occiput to nose tip) of ~62px, i.e. ~29% of head length. So the must-read "large pointed erect ears" IS present and readable - it is undersized for a jackal (should be ~35-45% of head length) and sits too far FORWARD, planted directly above the eye at the top-centre of the skull with a large pale rounded mass behind it that swallows the occiput, so it reads as a crest/forelock peak rather than ears set at the back of the skull. This ear geometry is pixel-for-pixel the same construction as Coyote's - so the claim that Jackal has ears where Coyote does not is false on both ends.

5. MUZZLE - must-read "slender fox-like muzzle" is PRESENT. Long tapering snout with a distinct dark nose pad and a drawn mouth line. It is a touch deep and hooks/droops at the tip, but it reads as a canid muzzle. This is the one part of the asset doing its job.

6. TAIL - claim is wrong twice. It is NOT level: the tail root sits at orig (155,190), just under the topline at the REARMOST point of the rump, and the dark tip sits at orig (118,238), so it runs down-and-back at roughly 50 degrees below horizontal, ending at belly level. "Carried low" is arguably satisfied. It is also NOT a mid-back tail - the root is at the croup, correctly placed; what makes it read oddly is that the proximal cylinder is fat and overlaps forward across the hip. The dark tip is NOT a "flat cut-off cap": it is a rounded dark-brown ELLIPSE stuck on the end like a ferrule. The real tail defect is different: the tail is a smooth tapering CYLINDER with a hair fringe on the upper edge only and a smooth bare underside, so it reads as a horse's dock-with-hair rather than a bushy canid brush; and the dark tip is a pasted-on disc that stops dead at the cylinder edge instead of carrying into the fringe hairs, so the "black tip" does not look like fur.

VERDICT REASONING: all three must-reads are technically findable (ears present but small and mis-sited, muzzle good, tail dark-tipped and low-ish but not bushy). The FAIL stands anyway on two independent grounds the per-feature checklist cannot see: (a) the organism reads as a hoofed pony, and hooves plus unangulated columnar limbs plus a high vertical neck on a canid is a wrong-organism failure regardless of head detail; (b) at 84.5% silhouette IoU with a uniform-halo-only difference, Jackal is not a distinct asset from Coyote - it is Coyote recoloured, so the species has no identity of its own within its own family.

FIX PRIORITY: canid limb model (angulated hock/stifle, digitigrade paws that change the silhouette) > lower the head and lengthen/lighten the body off the pony barrel > rebuild the tail as a true brush with the black tip carried through the fur > enlarge the ears ~1.4x and move them back onto the occiput. Do NOT 'add ears' or 'un-level the tail' - both already exist.

rows.readsAs: a deer fawn on long legs

There is no dark mane on the neck or shoulders at all; the neck and withers are the same orange as the barrel. There are no black stockings; the legs are uniform orange ending in dark hoof-blocks, which together with the arched hunched back makes it read as a fawn, not a canid. The ears are one small triangle, not 'very large erect'. The tail is again a mid-back cylinder with a white flat cap.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 4-5x crops of head, neck/shoulder, tail and feet. VERDICT UPHELD - two of the three must-reads are genuinely absent and the piece reads as a fawn/foal - but three parts of the original claim are wrong and would send the fix to the wrong places.

WHAT LANDS: leg length. Standing height runs y~85 (ear tip) to y~330 (ground); the leg column from elbow/stifle (~y185) to the ground is ~145px, so legs are roughly 55-60% of standing height. That is the one must-read that reads correctly, and the stilt proportion is genuinely striking.

MANE - JUDGE RIGHT, DESCRIPTION SLIGHTLY OFF. There is no dark mane on the neck or the shoulders. But the field is not 'all uniform orange': there ARE two deeper-orange blotches, one on the near shoulder (~x290-310, y185-215) and one on the rear flank (~x175-200, y155-175), plus fine cream fur-streak strokes over the whole barrel. They read as random dapple, not a mane. Worse, the dorsal line itself - crest of the neck from occiput to withers - is painted PALER cream than the flank, i.e. the exact inverse of the mark it needs. So the fix is not 'add value to a flat field'; it is (a) run a genuinely dark, near-black erect ridge along the nape-to-withers dorsal line, (b) suppress the pale dorsal-rim highlight that is currently painting over that same band, and (c) delete the two floating flank blotches that are eating the contrast budget.

STOCKINGS - JUDGE RIGHT. Both drawn legs are one uniform orange from body to ground with only a slight tonal step at the hock/pastern joint. The dark exists only in the last ~8px: a small brown block at the ground line on each leg, with two faint toe notches in it. At this size the notches vanish and it reads as a cloven hoof. Nothing that could be called a stocking - the black needs to start at the hock/carpus and cover the bottom ~35-40% of each leg.

EARS - JUDGE WRONG ON COUNT AND SHAPE. There is not 'one small triangle'. At 5x the head shows TWO ear forms: a large near-side erect triangle (base ~y110, apex ~y85, so ~25px tall) carrying a distinct darker inner-ear wedge inside it, plus a second narrower spike (the far ear) rising behind and left of it. So the ear is structurally right - erect, pointed, with inner ear, correctly paired. The real defect is SCALE and READ: ear height ~25px against a head length of ~74px (muzzle tip x~328 back to skull x~254) is about a third of head length, where a maned wolf needs half or more; and the dark inner wedge sitting on top of a pale cream cheek panel makes the whole assembly read as a mask or a horn base rather than as an ear. Fix is 'enlarge and simplify', not 'add a second ear'.

TAIL - JUDGE LARGELY WRONG, AND IT IS NOT A MUST-READ. The tail root is at the top of the rump (~x167, y172), directly above the hind-leg attachment, not mid-back. It is not a bare cylinder either: the upper/rear edge carries a dense fringe of fur strokes. The white tip is species-CORRECT - maned wolves do have a white tail tip - it is just rendered as a hard-edged opaque white circle that reads as a golf ball stuck on the end. Polish item, not an identity failure, and the packet's mustRead row for this species does not mention the tail at all.

UNMENTIONED AND LOAD-BEARING: only TWO legs are drawn - near fore and near hind. The far-side pair is entirely missing, so the animal stands on two posts and the silhouette flattens. The 'deer fawn' read is driven as much by this, by the hoof-blocks, and by the very large round eye with white sclera set high on a tapering muzzle, as by the missing markings. Head geometry itself is otherwise canid-plausible: long thin tapering muzzle with a dark nose button and a drawn mouth line.

Band stays FAIL: of three must-reads, one lands (leg length), one is present but undersized and misreading (ears), and one - the mark the species is named for - is absent, with the mane band actively painted the wrong value.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, plus 5x-9x crops of head, tail, legs, torso). Standing left-facing quadruped in pale grey/white. Level topline from withers to croup, uniform-depth barrel, thin neck, small head, four long straight tapering leg columns with a shallow hock bend, each ending in a dark grey rounded cap with only two faint vertical toe notches. Silhouette reads as a grey pony/donkey. The FAIL verdict stands.

SHARED CHASSIS (the real, dominant defect - not stated by the first judge). I rendered Coyote.png and Red_Fox.png beside it. All three are ONE body with the palette swapped: identical topline and croup, identical barrel outline, identical four leg columns and dark hoof-like foot caps, identical banded-cylinder tail with a bristle comb on the upper edge and a flat disc tip, identical box-cranium head with one large erect triangular ear and a thin muzzle bar ending in a dark nose blob. Wolf = grey, Coyote = tan, Red Fox = orange with a white tail tip. Nothing wolf-specific was built; fixing Wolf in isolation will not fix this.

CORRECTION 1 - EARS. Their claim of 'one small triangular ear' is WRONG, and this is the one must-read that IS satisfied. At 9x there are TWO erect triangular ears: the near ear is large (its base spans most of the skull roof, apex well above the cranium) drawn as a dark-grey triangle with a mauve/brown inner-ear triangle inset; the far ear is the paler grey narrow peak overlapping it at the upper left. 'Erect triangular ears' reads correctly. Do not touch the ears.

CORRECTION 2 - HEAD. 'Narrow wedge' is imprecise. The cranium is actually a squarish rounded box, not a fox wedge. What fails is that it is not BROAD or BLOCKY in the wolf sense and is indistinguishable from Coyote's: the muzzle is a thin flat bar that tapers DOWNWARD off the box, with a separate thin lower-jaw bar under it leaving a visible slot (reads as an open pipe or a beak), and it terminates in an oversized dark-brown oval nose blob pasted on the front. There is no depth to the muzzle, no stop, no mass of jaw. The amber/yellow iris with a black pupil is correct for a wolf and the judge did not mention it - keep it.

CORRECTION 3 - TAIL CARRIAGE. 'Held level from mid-back' is WRONG. The tail attaches at the rump/croup (not mid-back) and angles DOWN-and-back at roughly 30-40 degrees below horizontal. The reference permits 'carried level or low', so the carriage angle is acceptable and is NOT the defect. The tail defects are texture and tip: it is a smooth pale cylinder with three or four darker grey banding blocks across it (their 'striped' is correct), a thin one-sided comb of short spiky bristles fringing only the upper/outer edge instead of a full brush, and the tip is a flat dark-brown ELLIPSE that reads exactly as the open end of a cut pipe (their strongest observation, and correct). It also is not straight - it bows. 'Straight bushy tail' fails on bushiness and on the cut-pipe end, not on angle.

CORRECTION 4 - CHEST. Their 'wide round barrel, not narrow and deep' is right in effect. In profile the barrel is the same depth from shoulder to hip with a high, nearly straight belly line and only a token tuck; the brisket never drops toward elbow level, so there is no deep chest and no tucked loin. Legs ARE long - arguably too long, they read as pony pasterns - so 'long legs' passes and only the 'narrow deep chest' half of that must-read fails.

MUST-READ TALLY: erect triangular ears PRESENT; broad blocky head ABSENT; long legs PRESENT; narrow deep chest ABSENT; straight bushy tail ABSENT (banded cylinder with a flat cut-pipe tip); carriage acceptable. Two of three must-reads fail on their defining half and the organism reads as an equid, so FAIL is correct.

rows.verifyWhy: Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then decoded it and re-rendered four crops (whole animal 6x, head 14x and 20x, muzzle 32x, feet 8x, rump 18x) and measured the silhouette column-by-column. The FAIL verdict stands: this is a lamb, not a hyrax. MEASURED GEOMETRY (bright-pixel scan, background is near-black so the creature separates cleanly): creature bbox x148-292, y164-259 = 145w x 96h, aspect 1.51 against a spec aspect of 2.0. Torso topline is flat at y=176 and the belly line is flat at y=227-228 across the whole barrel (x192-x216 all read [176,228]); the ground/foot line is y=259. That is a 31 px void of pure background between belly and ground -- 32 percent of the animal's total height -- and the fore and hind legs are separated by a wide open triangle of daylight (the leg crop shows background all the way from the brisket back to the hind thigh). Torso alone is ~96 x 52 = 1.85 aspect, so even the barrel is not the long low tube the row asks for. MUST-READ 3, 'stubby legs', is therefore not merely weak, it is inverted: the legs are long, slender, tapered and clearly articulated, and the animal stands well clear of the ground. MUST-READ 1, 'tailless rounded guinea-pig-like body', is only half present -- the rump crop at 18x confirms a clean rounded tailless hindquarter with no tail nub at all (credit where due), but the body is a fleece: the coat is filled with short pale hair-flicks over cream/oatmeal, which is a woolly texture, and it is carried high, so it reads as a lamb's barrel and not as a ground-hugging rodent loaf. MUST-READ 2 splits: the muzzle IS short and blunt -- at 32x it is a small rounded snout projecting forward and slightly down off the front of the skull with one small dark nostril dot and a single mouth crease -- but there are ZERO whiskers anywhere, no vibrissae strokes, no dots, nothing. CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (three of its stated causes are wrong even though the verdict is right): (a) 'dark face mask' is inaccurate -- there is no mask pattern; the entire head AND neck are painted a uniform darker grey-taupe than the cream body, so the defect is a wholesale two-tone head/body split, not a facial marking; (b) 'four long slender legs with dark points' is wrong about the points -- the legs are the same cream as the body for their whole length with no stockings or dark points at all; the only dark marking is at the FEET, where each foot ends in two rounded dark toe-caps that read unmistakably as a cloven hoof (this is arguably the single most damaging wrong-organism cue in the piece and the original judge did not name it -- a hyrax has rounded rubbery pads, never a split hoof); (c) the claim is silent on the ears, and 'small rounded ears' is actually the one head must-read that IS present -- at 20x there is a small dark rounded oval sitting on the upper-left skull plus a small nub breaking the rear skull silhouette. It is painted flat onto the dome rather than modelled as a raised ear, so it is weak, but it is not absent and a fix pass should not go looking for a missing ear. ALSO NOT IN THE CLAIM: the eye is far too large and too cartoon -- a big dark pupil ringed by a bright white sclera crescent occupying roughly a third of the skull height -- where the row specifies eyes: normal; this inflates the lamb/plush read. FIX DIRECTION: drop the belly to within ~10 percent of the ground, shorten the legs to stubby columns that barely clear it, stretch the barrel toward aspect 2.0, replace the cloven toe-caps with blunt rounded pads, kill the fleece hair-flicks for a short dense pelt, unify head tone with the body, shrink the eye, and add long whiskers off the blunt muzzle.

rows.readsAs: A needlefish / garfish — or a decorated knife blade or seed pod. Nobody says 'eel'.
rows.defect: The two must-reads that ARE the identity are absent. (2) 'Continuous fin fringe running along back, tail and belly': the only thing present is a faint translucent grey rim hugging the dorsal and ventral edges, so low in contrast against the dark field that at 1x it reads as anti-aliasing or a glow, not as a fin. Worse, that rim STOPS before the tail — the tail is a small separate yellow dart-spike with three stray dark whisker strands trailing off it, so the fringe never wraps the tail as the reference requires. Secondary problems: the belly lobe sitting under the pectoral fan reads as a paired ventral fin, undercutting 'no pelvic fins'; the skin is covered in an even ruled grid of dark dots and dashes that reads as woven cloth or a corn cob rather than wet unscaled eel skin; and the eye is an oversized white cartoon ring.

rows.readsAs: a pale tan plush quadruped -- most people would guess llama or a cartoon donkey before horse, and nobody would say Przewalski's

What is missing is the colour logic — every mark is a lighter green on a mid green, one hue, low contrast. There is no black barring and no yellow flecking anywhere on the body, so the moss-camouflage read never lands and the bird flattens to a single lime tone.

CHASSIS — unchanged from the Emu, which is the underlying cause of both misses. Same egg body, same circular scribble-textured wing disc parked mid-flank, same rounded tail nub at the lower right, same yellow three-toes-forward-plus-hind-spur feet (not the zygodactyl 2+2 a parrot has, though the packet does not demand it). Only the neck differs usefully: it is short and thick so the head sits almost on the shoulders, which is correct for the heavy squat parrot body of must-read 3, and that one does read.

BAND. Must-read 1 partial (green and mottled, but wrong palette, no black/yellow), must-read 2 absent outright, must-read 3 present. The absent one is the defining one — kakapo is the owl parrot and the face is why. As drawn it resolves to a generic plump green parrot, not a kakapo, so FAIL stands. FIX ORDER: (1) build the facial disc — a flat pale-olive saucer around each eye with radiating fine feather rays and a soft rim, plus a fan of dark whisker bristles projecting forward from the bill base over the mandible; (2) repaint the body pattern in black transverse bars with yellow-ochre flecking over moss green instead of green-on-green; (3) shrink the oversized cream eye blob to a small dark eye so the disc, not the highlight, owns the face. DO NOT touch the bill — it is already right.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi, immediately and unprompted
rows.defect: All three must-reads land: the long slender down-curved probing bill is roughly a third of the body, the body is a round tailless mound of genuine hair-like strokes with loose strands breaking the outline, and the legs sit well back under the rear of the body. Only two soft notes: the plumage is olive-green rather than kiwi brown, and the legs are spindly where a kiwi's are stout and heavy-boned.
rows.fix: Thicken the legs and tarsi to stout heavy props and warm the plumage toward brown-grey; leave the silhouette alone.

rows.readsAs: a dark turkey or a peahen — the stiff barred fan tail dominates and names the bird wrongly
rows.defect: The neck is not remotely ostrich-long: it reads about a fifth of total height where an ostrich neck is roughly half, and it ends in the family's round skull with the standard yellow triangle beak, not a tiny flat head on a bare pink-grey column. The 'fluffy plume wings and tail bustle' is rendered as a hard-edged fan of separated pointed barred feathers spread stiffly to the right — that is a turkey's or peacock's fan, not a soft bustle of loose plumes. The legs are thin yellow sticks with three splayed toes, so the two-toed powerful leg is absent too. The shared blob wing and belly medallion are still visible beneath the fan.
rows.fix: Double the neck length and strip it bare to a thin pink-grey column topped by a small flat head, and replace the stiff barred fan with a soft loose bustle of drooping white-tipped plumes.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but several stated causes are wrong and the real proportion defect is worse than reported. Measured from a per-row alpha scan of the 440x440 PNG (bg 5,6,12; threshold 40): creature occupies y=19..409, total height ~390px. HEAD+BEAK y=19..78 (~15% of height, spec headFrac 0.12 - acceptable). FREE-STANDING BARE NECK y=82..122, a constant 16-17px-wide column: only ~40px = ~10% of total height, NOT 'about a fifth' as claimed. An ostrich neck is ~40-45% of standing height, so this is off by 4x, not 2x. BODY y=124..355 = 231px = 59% of total height - the egg-shaped body is the single dominant mass and is the root cause of every proportion failure. LEGS y=358..409 = ~51px = ~13% of height (should be ~45%). So the correct fix statement is: the neck must go from 10% to ~40% and the legs from 13% to ~45%, both stolen from a body that must shrink from 59% to ~30%.

HEAD (4x crop): a plain round ball, ~50px diameter, with a chunky wedge-shaped yellow-orange triangular beak that comes to a sharp point - not the ostrich's short broad blunt flat bill on a tiny flat skull. Judge is correct here. They MISSED an extra defect: a stray pale-grey hairline crescent arcs around the top-back of the skull (roughly x=140..160, y=25..75), a leftover generic rim/ear ring shape that does not belong on any bird head. Eye is a small white oval with a black pupil at the beak base - reads only marginally 'prominent'.

NECK: the column plunges into the body and is then drawn ON TOP of the breast as a thick dark-brown strap that crosses the upper body and terminates in a blunt rounded stub around y=200. It reads as a belt laid across the bird, not as a neck entering a shoulder. The neck is also the same brown as the head and body, so 'bare' does not read at all.

TAIL (3x crop): confirmed a stiff, hard-edged fan of ~7 discrete lozenge-shaped blades radiating from the rump out to x=369, each a flat solid fill with rounded tip and hard dark negative-space gaps between them - a turkey/peafowl display fan, not a soft plume bustle. CORRECTION: the blades are NOT 'barred'. They carry no internal pattern whatsoever; the barring/scallop texture the judge saw is on the BODY, in horizontal rows of chevron feather scallops. Cite the correct defect: solid hard-edged separated blades with visible gaps, where the ostrich needs a soft-edged mass of drooping filamentous plumes with no gaps and no individual feather outlines.

FEET (7x crop): CLAIM IS WRONG. These are NOT three-toed. Each foot is a simple two-prong T-bar - one long toe pointing forward and one short stub pointing backward (a hallux). So toe count is coincidentally near ostrich (2), but the arrangement is wrong: an ostrich has BOTH toes forward, the inner one huge with a hoof-like nail, and NO rear hallux. The real leg defect is not toe count but mass: both legs are uniform pencil-thin yellow sticks of constant ~8px width emerging straight from the bottom of the egg with zero thigh, zero drumstick, zero taper - the word 'powerful' in the must-read has no representation at all.

SHARED CHASSIS PARTS (confirmed, but mislocated by the judge): the belly medallion is NOT hidden under the fan. It is a ~90px circular bolted-on porthole - a raised ring with a cross-hatched disc inside - sitting dead centre of the flank at roughly x=155..245, y=205..295, about a quarter of the body width, completely unmissable. The wing is a flat speckled panel occupying the left/front third of the egg, edged by a pale hairline arc and dotted with pale ovoid speckles; it has no plume structure and does not read as a wing at all.

IDENTITY VERDICT: all three must-reads fail. 'extremely long bare neck with a tiny flat head' - absent (10% neck, round head, pointed beak). 'fluffy plume wings and tail bustle' - absent (flat speckled panel, hard-edged blade fan). 'long two-toed powerful legs' - absent (13%-of-height pencil sticks, forward toe + hallux). Dark speckled body plus a stiff fanned tail plus short thin legs reads as a turkey or guineafowl; the judge's 'dark turkey or peahen' read is correct. Nothing here refutes the FAIL.

rows.readsAs: a penguin
rows.defect: Posture, countershading and short rear-set yellow feet all read. But the stiff flipper wings held flat at the sides are missing — the near side has no flipper at all, and the far side shows only the family's grey rounded wing blob poking out at the lower right, identical to the one on the emu and rhea. The black back also still carries the shared scalloped scale texture, which gives a reptilian shingled look no penguin has, and the belly is a floating white oval rather than a countershading boundary that meets the flanks.
rows.fix: Draw a long narrow flat flipper hanging down the near flank from shoulder to hip and delete the round wing blob, then flatten the back texture to smooth packed plumage.

rows.readsAs: a pale generic ratite, indistinguishable from the Emu in this same batch
rows.defect: The long bare legs and three toes are correct and the tail is absent as it should be. But the head has a narrow pointed yellow beak where a rhea needs a small flat head with a broad blunt duck-like bill, the neck is feathered and too short for a bird whose height is supposed to be dominated by neck and legs, and the 'shaggy drooping wings' are just the shared small grey blob at the rear. Body proportion is the family egg, so it is taller-than-long only marginally.
rows.fix: Swap the pointed wedge for a broad blunt flattened bill and lengthen the neck so neck plus legs carry most of the height, then hang large shaggy drooping wing plumes over the flanks.

rows.readsAs: a flying fish - the three huge translucent wing planes are unmistakable and a stranger names it on sight
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads miss. (1) The tail is NOT unevenly forked: at 7x the caudal fork is essentially symmetric - upper lobe tip and lower lobe tip reach the same posterior x and sit about the same distance above and below the peduncle midline, so the signature long lower lobe is absent. (2) The body is not blunt-nosed: the head tapers to a knife point, and the white ring eye is parked right at the apex sitting half off the outline with almost no snout in front of it - in isolation that profile reads needlefish or halfbeak, not the rounded bullet head of a flying fish. The eye also reads as a floating hoop rather than a seated eyeball.
rows.fix: Round the snout off ahead of the eye so the head ends in a blunt bullet and the eye sits fully inside the head, and rebuild the caudal as an uneven fork with the lower lobe about 1.6x the length of the upper.

rows.readsAs: a mudskipper - a yellow goby on a mudflat with periscope eyes; the identity does land
rows.defect: The eyes are right (two clean domed turrets riding on top of the skull) but the other two must-reads and the posture note do not. The body lies FLAT: the belly line is level on the mud and the front of the animal is not lifted at all, so nothing is propped. The single visible pectoral fin has a good arm-like muscular base and rayed fan blade, but it dangles below the ventral line into the shadow instead of planting on the ground and carrying weight - it looks hung on the fish, not standing on it. The two dorsals are present in count but wrong in form: they are short rounded humps barely clearing the back, not raised sails, and each has four grey spine sticks that overshoot the membrane and float free in the dark air beside and below the fin, reading as loose picket sticks or antennae rather than rays inside a fin.
rows.fix: Lift the front third of the body clear of the mud on a planted pectoral (fin tip on the ground line, belly visibly raised above it) and redraw the two dorsals as tall separate membrane sails, at least head-height, with the rays contained inside the membrane instead of overshooting it.

rows.readsAs: a bat
rows.defect: Reads as a bat unprompted - big paired ears on a small furry body, and the wing membranes do carry visible dark finger struts fanning to the leading edge, so two of three must-reads land. The third is absent: at 9x the torso simply ends in a rounded rump with a tiny notch. There are no hind legs and no uropatagium - no membrane spanning the hind limbs and tail, so the lower half of the animal is a blank capsule. The wing panels also read more as two creased umbrella/kite facets than as a hand: the struts are few and stop short of the trailing edge, so the fingers never fan all the way out.
rows.fix: Add the tail membrane: draw two short hind legs kicking back from the rump and stretch a triangular uropatagium between them and a visible tail spur, then extend the existing finger struts all the way to the trailing edge so each wing terminates in four distinct fingertips.

rows.readsAs: a spotted lamb or a piebald calf standing in a field
rows.defect: This is the wrong organism. There is no gliding membrane anywhere on it - not neck to wrist, not between the limbs, not enclosing the tail - and the patagium IS the colugo. It stands broadside on four separate columnar legs with clear air between them and a ground shadow under its feet, which is the exact opposite of the required flying posture, so it does not even read as a glider caught mid-glide. The eye is a single small side-mounted bead on a long tapering muzzle, not the huge round forward-facing eyes called for. The bare tail hangs down free of any membrane. Only the mottled fur must-read is present, and on this body it reads as cow or sheep piebalding rather than lichen camouflage.
rows.fix: Rebuild it off the quadruped chassis entirely: pose it spread-eagled and flattened toward the viewer, then fill every gap between the neck, the splayed fore and hind limbs and the tail tip with one continuous stretched membrane so the silhouette is a single kite with a head on it, and enlarge the eyes to huge forward-facing discs.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon smiley frog / plush toad — no stranger would say 'bullfrog'
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is visible. There is no large circular eardrum disc behind the eye — only a vague soft olive blotch on each cheek that reads as a dirt smudge, not a tympanum, and certainly not bigger than the eye. The mouth is a small curled smile spanning under half the head width, not a very wide flat mouth line. The hind legs are thin leaf-shaped paddles running straight out sideways from the mid-flank to flat hand-like feet with separated pointed fingers — no muscular folded thigh, no webbing membrane between digits.
rows.fix: Draw a hard-edged circular tympanum disc behind and below each eye, sized larger than the eye with its own rim and a slightly different value from the cheek, then fold the hind limb into a Z (knee peaking above the body topline, ankle high) and fill the toes with a continuous webbing membrane instead of separate fingers.

rows.readsAs: the Bullfrog drawing recoloured pale mint — a mouldy cartoon frog, not a glass frog
rows.defect: The identity of this animal is absent: the body is fully OPAQUE. No translucency anywhere, no heart, no gut, no visible bone or organ silhouette through the underside, and the belly is not even differentiated from the back. The eyes are the same black-pupil, white-sclera domes as every other frog in the batch, set on top of the head pointing up and out, not forward-facing and not pale gold. The grey-green blotches scattered over the body actively read as mould or warts, the opposite of a smooth translucent glass frog. Silhouette, limb geometry, foot shape, mouth curve and shadow are identical to Bullfrog.png.
rows.fix: Rebuild the underside as a genuinely see-through pane — a lighter, desaturated belly field with a red heart shape and a coiled dark gut visibly rendered inside it — drop the grey blotching entirely, and turn the eyes into forward-facing pale gold discs with fine dark reticulation instead of the shared cartoon eyeball.

rows.readsAs: a red ladybird beetle or a shiny red jelly blob — it does not read as a frog at all
rows.defect: The render is broken. The whole face assembly has slid off-centre to the upper right of the body mass: one eye is a plain black disc with no sclera and no highlight while the other has a white ring, they sit crammed against the right edge of the silhouette, and the mouth is not a line but a chaotic dark smear with two black wedges spilling over the right cheek. The limbs are gone — reduced to four small flat red nubs at the base of the blob with no legs, no joints and no feet. The large round black spots on a glossy red dome read straight as ladybird elytra. There is also no bold striping and no readable frog snout.
rows.fix: Re-centre the head assembly on the body axis, give both eyes the same jet-black domed treatment with matching highlights, replace the smeared mouth with a single clean wide mouth line, and restore actual limbs — a slim foreleg and a compact folded hind leg — on a small smooth blunt-snouted body with crisp bold stripes rather than scattered round spots.

rows.readsAs: the Bullfrog drawing in brighter green — 'a frog', never 'a tree frog'
rows.defect: The feature the packet itself names as diagnostic is absent: there are NO adhesive toe discs. Every digit on all four feet ends in a thin point, on the forefeet and on the splayed hind feet alike — not one round pad anywhere. The hind legs are also wrong: instead of long limbs folded into tight Z-shapes they stretch out flat and straight sideways from the mid-flank, running off toward the frame edges like arms. Only 'bulging eyes set high on the head' is present, and those are the identical eye domes reused from the other three frogs. Body, topline, mouth curve, foot shape and shadow are the same asset as Bullfrog.png with the hue pushed to lime.
rows.fix: Terminate every toe in a distinctly oversized round adhesive disc, clearly wider than the toe itself, and rebuild the hind limb as a long tight Z — thigh up and back, knee breaking above the topline, shank forward, foot tucked under the flank — so the tree frog stops sharing the bullfrog's splayed sit.

rows.readsAs: a pale white cartoon frog / a ghost bath toy
rows.defect: The depigmented pallor is genuinely present and is the strongest read in the batch, but the must-read folded hind legs are not there — the haunches splay straight out sideways as flat horizontal wedges with no knee rising above the back, so nothing about it says crouched. There is also no wide flat head as broad as the body because there is no head at all: the cranium and torso are one undifferentiated egg.
rows.fix: Rebuild the hind limb as a folded Z — thigh angled up and back so the knee peaks above the dorsal line, shank folding forward, foot planted beside the body — instead of a horizontal wedge leaving the flank at 3 and 9 o'clock.

rows.readsAs: a green cartoon frog
rows.defect: A stranger does name 'frog', and the bulging eyes plus wide mouth line plus tailless body are present. But the must-read folded haunches with long hind legs are absent: the rear limbs are short flat wedges sticking straight out to either side at mid-flank, with no thigh volume and no raised knee, so the animal reads as splayed flat rather than coiled. The eyes also sit on the front face rather than on top of the skull.
rows.fix: Give the hind leg an actual folded haunch — a bulky thigh mass sitting against the flank with the knee apex above the topline — and raise the eye domes so they break the upper silhouette rather than sitting on the face.

rows.readsAs: the green Frog recoloured brown — a frog, not a toad
rows.defect: Every must-read that separates a toad from a frog is missing. The skin is not warty: it is the same smooth glossy gradient blob as the Frog with the same soft out-of-focus blotches, no bumps, no stippled dry texture. There is no swollen parotoid gland behind either eye — the head is clean. It is not squatter or shorter-legged: the hind limbs are the identical length and identical splay angle as the Frog's, the head is not broader or flatter, and the body is in fact rendered slightly SMALLER than the Frog rather than wider. Zero of the three must-reads survive, and the note's stated differentiation from a frog is entirely absent.
rows.fix: Give it a genuinely different body — widen and lower the mass into a hunched wedge, shorten the hind limbs to half the Frog's, add a hard-edged bumpy wart field across the dorsum, and paint a distinct raised kidney-shaped parotoid gland behind each eye.

rows.readsAs: the same cartoon frog in orange — no species identity at all
rows.defect: The black robber's mask through the eye — the one marking that IS a wood frog — is completely absent; the face is a uniform orange-brown with no dark band behind the eye whatsoever. The pale dorsolateral ridges are also absent: the back carries only the same generic blurred blotches as the other three, with no paired longitudinal lines. The long folded jumping legs are the shared splayed lateral wedges, not folded. All three must-reads are missing, leaving a hue swap of the Frog asset.
rows.fix: Paint the diagnostic dark mask as a hard-edged band running from the snout through the eye to behind the tympanum, and add two crisp pale ridges running the length of the back on either side of the spine.

rows.readsAs: a rosehip or wild-cherry bush - round red berries on bare twiggy stems
rows.defect: The harvest is five perfectly ROUND glossy red spheres with a small dark stalk nub on top. A chili's identity is a smooth tapering elongated pod hanging or pointing up from a green calyx cap, and none of that is present - no taper, no point, no calyx. The must-read white star flower with the purple-black anther ring is entirely absent; there is not a single flower in the render. The leaves are thin sliver lancets scattered sparsely along bare stems rather than smooth pointed OVALS, and the stems read as bare brown twigs rather than a many-branched bushy leafy habit, so the plant looks defoliated.
rows.fix: Replace the spheres with tapered pods - a wide shouldered top narrowing to a curved point over about three times their width - cap each with a small green five-lobed calyx and a short green stalk, and add two or three small white star flowers with a dark purple anther ring at leaf axils.

rows.readsAs: a watermelon or small gourd vine - or, from the leaf shape alone, a hemp plant
rows.defect: The single fruit is a small ROUND green sphere with pale vertical striping - it reads unmistakably as a watermelon, not a cucumber. The must-read warted ELONGATED fruit is absent: there is no length, no ridging and no warty bumps, just the same smooth specular ball used on the chili in a different hue. The yellow star flowers are entirely missing. The leaves are smooth-edged deeply cut STAR-LOBED palmate blades with clean glossy fills, not bristly heart-triangular lobed leaves, so they read as cannabis rather than cucurbit. The tendrils are the one must-read that lands. The vine also does not fill its 2:1 aspect - it sits as a narrow diagonal S with large empty margins on both sides.
rows.fix: Swap the sphere for a cylindrical fruit roughly four times longer than it is wide, hanging under a leaf, with lengthwise ridges and stippled dark warts, and add two or three five-petal yellow star flowers at the nodes; broaden the leaf to a heart-triangular blade with shallow lobes and a bristly stippled edge.

rows.readsAs: a plump golden chick with a spiky topknot
rows.defect: The comb reads as a 3-spike punk tuft sitting on the crown rather than a fleshy red serrated comb, and there are no wattles at all under the bill; the comb/wattle pair is the same tan as the body so nothing reads as bare red skin. The tail fan hangs level-to-drooping behind the bird instead of the short upswept fan called for. The wing is an abstract dark spiral that reads as a hole punched in the flank, not a folded wing.
rows.fix: Make the comb a red fleshy serrated blade fused to the top of the skull and hang two red wattle lobes under the bill, then rotate the tail fan up ~35 degrees so its base lifts above the topline.

rows.readsAs: a generic brown barnyard gamebird — indistinguishable from the Turkey card
rows.defect: The bill is a long straight yellow cone, the opposite of the short rounded gamebird bill in the must-reads. The legs are bare bright-yellow rods with no feathering whatsoever. The tail fan is flat untextured brown with no barring, and it droops below the body line rather than fanning. Side by side with Turkey.png this is essentially the same image at a slightly different tone.
rows.fix: Shorten and round the bill to a stubby dark curve and clothe the tarsi in shaggy feather lobes down to the toes, then band the tail fan with dark cross-bars.

rows.readsAs: a dark grey chick with a few white dots — a speckled pigeon
rows.defect: The identity feature is entirely absent: there is no bare skin anywhere, no bony helmet casque, no blue-and-red face, no red horn wattles. The head is the same fully feathered grey chick skull with the standard yellow bill used on every other card, and it is normal-sized rather than comically small. The neck is not thin or naked — head sits straight on the shoulder like the rest of the family. The white spotting is a sparse rim of dots outlining the wing, not the dense allover pearling that makes a guineafowl.
rows.fix: Replace the head with a tiny bare blue-and-red skull carrying a hard bony casque on the crown and red drop wattles, set it on a thin naked neck, and scatter dense even white pearl-dots across the whole body instead of only along the wing edge.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 8x crops of the head, 4x of the whole body, and 8x of the tail and feet. UPHELD, and the other judge's description of the head is accurate, but their account of the spotting is understated and needs correcting.

HEAD (mustRead 1: 'tiny bare blue-and-red head with a bony helmet casque') — ABSENT, completely. The head is a plain circular ball of the SAME slate-grey (#4a5060-ish) as the body, with a soft spherical shade and a thin cool rim-light along the upper-left arc. The crown is a perfectly smooth dome: no casque, no horn, no bump, no comb, no crest of any kind at the top or back of the skull. There is no bare skin anywhere: no red, no blue, no white cheek patch, no wattle, no pale cere at the bill base. The single hue break on the entire head is the bill, a flat yellow/amber triangle (#e0aa38) with a straight top edge, identical in shape and colour to the generic yellow bill used elsewhere in the gamebird family. The eye is a large glossy black disc with one white catchlight sitting well forward on the cheek. Nothing in the head says guineafowl; it reads as a duckling/chick head.

NECK (mustRead 3: 'thin naked neck on a heavy body') — ABSENT. There IS a visible neck column between head and body, but at 8x it measures roughly 22px against a 37px head diameter — about 0.6 head-widths, i.e. thick, not thin — and it is filled with the same feathered grey as the body and head with continuous shading across the join. No bare skin, no colour change, no narrowing toward the shoulders. So the 'naked' half of the must-read fails and the 'thin' half fails too.

HEAD SIZE — I confirm the other judge: NOT comically small. Measured, the head disc is ~38-40px against a ~190px bill-tip-to-tail-tip length, so headFrac lands near 0.20-0.21, slightly ABOVE the packet's 0.18 spec and far above the 'comically small' note. It is a normal-proportioned family head.

SPOTTING (mustRead 2: 'round hunched body densely speckled with white dots') — PARTIAL, and here the other judge's cause is wrong in detail. It is not 'only a sparse rim of dots outlining the wing'. There are roughly 40-50 white dots arranged in TWO nested contour arcs plus a partial row: (a) an arc that runs the full outer silhouette of the breast/belly, from just below the throat around the front of the chest and along the underside to the tail base; (b) a second arc riding the upper margin of the folded-wing oval along the back; and (c) a short diagonal row across the shoulder between them. So dots appear on the breast and flank as well as the wing edge. The defect is real but it is a CONTOUR-TRACING pattern, not an allover one: the entire interior of the folded-wing oval and the entire interior of the flank are bare grey scale-texture with zero dots, so the bird reads as outlined with beads rather than pearled all over. The dots are also uniform, evenly spaced and large-ish, more polka-dot than the fine graded pearling of the real bird.

WHAT DOES WORK: the body is genuinely round and hunched, the mass sits low and heavy over short legs, and the tail — a long straight dark spike leaving the rump and angling DOWNWARD to the lower right, with a small fringe of thin black filaments at its base — does satisfy the packet note 'the tail droops downward'. Feet are two flat yellow legs, three forward toes and a rear toe, unscaled and untextured but adequate.

NET: only the round hunched body and the drooping tail land. The entire identity cluster — casque, bare blue-and-red face, thin naked neck — is missing, and what remains is the shared family chick chassis (round ball head, yellow triangle bill, ovoid body, plain yellow stick legs) in grey with beads applied along its edges. It reads as a spotted duckling, not a guineafowl. FAIL stands.

FIX ORDER: (1) build the casque — a vertical bony horn rising from the crown, plus recolour the whole head/face to bare skin: pale blue cheeks and throat with red on the wattles and bill base, no grey feathering above the neck line; (2) thin the neck to roughly a third of head width and give it the same bare skin so the head reads as a knob on a wire; (3) shrink the head toward headFrac 0.14-0.16 so it is comically small against the mass; (4) fill the wing and flank INTERIORS with dense graded pearling instead of leaving contour arcs on an empty field.

rows.readsAs: a dumpy tan chick — the Quail card without its topknot
rows.defect: The dumpy body and low short tail are there, but the bill is a straight pointed cone rather than the short curved gamebird bill, and the head/face carries no marking of any kind, so nothing separates this from the Quail, Chicken and Ptarmigan bodies except hue. The same dark spiral 'wing' artefact sits on the flank and reads as a gouge rather than a folded wing.
rows.fix: Give it a short down-curved grey bill plus a partridge face mark (dark eye-stripe and rufous throat patch) so the head is not the shared blank chick skull.

rows.readsAs: a teal chicken with gold dots on its tail
rows.defect: The train — the entire identity of a peacock — is not there. The tail is the SAME short drooping 5-lobe fan used on the Chicken and Turkey cards, no longer than the body, with a single flat gold disc stuck on each lobe tip; those are dots, not ocelli (no blue-black centre, no bronze-green surround). The bird's overall aspect is a round ball, nowhere near the requested 2.2 elongation. The neck and breast are not differentiated from the body — the whole bird is one flat teal, so there is no iridescent neck reading against a duller body. The crest is present but is the same 3-spike tuft the Chicken and Rooster wear, without wire stems or racket tips.
rows.fix: Draw a train that trails two-to-three body-lengths behind and below the bird, made of long overlapping barbs carrying multi-ring eyespots (blue-black pupil, bronze iris, green rim), and reserve the saturated iridescent blue for the neck and breast against a duller brown-green back.

rows.readsAs: a brown chick that has been handed a plank
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. The head is the plain tan feathered chick skull — no red bare facial wattle around the eye, no iridescent green-black hood, no white neck ring. The tail is not an extremely long pointed barred tail; it is a short blunt-ended flat brown plank about a third of the body length with a couple of faint bars, and it is stuck on at mid-flank so it reads as a detached board rather than as tail feathers growing from the rump.
rows.fix: Replace the tail with a long tapering pointed spike two body-lengths long, boldly cross-barred, rooted at the rump; then repaint the head bottle-green-black with a scarlet bare-skin mask around the eye and a crisp white collar at the base of the neck.

rows.readsAs: a white chick or a small white dove
rows.defect: The white winter plumage is present and correct, but the other two must-reads are absent: the feet are the family's bare bright-yellow scaly rods with no feathering at all, which is exactly backwards for the one gamebird defined by snowshoe-feathered toes, and there is no red comb above the eye — no red pigment appears anywhere on the card.
rows.fix: Bury the legs and toes in shaggy white feather boots so no bare scale shows, and add a small scarlet fleshy comb arc directly above the eye.

rows.readsAs: a quail
rows.defect: Reads correctly — round feathered-ball body, very short wedge tail, short legs, small head tucked to the shoulder, and the topknot helps. The only weakness is that this is the family's default chassis, so it passes partly because the chassis happens to be quail-shaped.
rows.fix: Curve the topknot plume forward over the bill instead of splaying it into three straight spikes, so it reads as a quail plume rather than the generic tuft shared with Chicken and Rooster.

rows.readsAs: a rust-red robin or a generic brown songbird
rows.defect: Nothing that makes a rooster is present. The comb is the same small 3-spike tuft as the Chicken and Quail, not a tall red blade; there are no wattles hanging from the chin. The tail is two straight flat planks angled backwards and DOWN — the exact opposite of arching sickle plumes, and the same part used on the Pheasant card. The posture is the family's horizontal ovoid, not an upright puffed chest, and there is no hackle cape at all — the neck-to-shoulder transition is the same smooth featureless join as every other card. Requested aspect 1.0 (upright/square) is ignored.

rows.readsAs: a brown grouse — literally the Grouse card in a slightly darker tone
rows.defect: The head is a small fully-feathered brown chick skull with the standard yellow cone bill: no bare blue-and-red warty skin, no snood, no dangling wattle.
