rows.readsAs: a white lampshade or a paper lantern
rows.defect: A smooth ivory cone with evenly spaced vertical seam lines, wide at the base and cleanly truncated at the top. There are no trapdoor plates - just a small dark notch - and there are ZERO feathery cirri sweeping out of the opening, which is the one thing that makes a barnacle read as alive. It is not attached to any substrate, so it floats as a piece of furniture.
rows.fix: Open the summit into a pair of interlocking beak-shaped opercular plates and sweep a fan of curled feathery cirri out of the gap; roughen the plate walls with chalky overlapping ridges and seat the cone on a rock.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but one of the two stated causes is factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured + zoomed at 5x body / 12x summit and base):
Silhouette bbox is 139 x 105 px inside a 440 px canvas — width/height = 1.32. The reference row calls for aspect 0.9 (taller than wide, a volcano). The drawn form is ~47% too squat and too wide, which is the single biggest driver of the lampshade read: the profile is a low dome-frustum, not a volcano cone. Row-width scan is a smooth monotonic flare (73 -> 89 -> 103 -> 117 -> 129 -> 137 px) with no waist, no rim flare, no basal spread.

MUST-READ 1 — 'volcano-shaped chalky cone of fused plates': PARTIAL, weak. There ARE ~8 longitudinal panel divisions, so the plate COUNT is nominally represented, but they are hairline 1px dark pinstripes ruled over a perfectly smooth ivory gradient. No chalk grain, no relief, no shadow on either side of a suture, no overlapping/interlocking plate edges, no growth ridges, and the panels are exactly evenly spaced. That is a pleated fabric shade, not fused calcareous plates. The base terminates in a dead-straight horizontal cut with a soft contact shadow under it — a flat 2D bottom with no elliptical perspective and no basal encrusting rim, which is why it reads as a manufactured object resting on a table.

MUST-READ 2 — 'trapdoor plates at the summit': PRESENT. THE OTHER JUDGE IS WRONG ON THIS POINT. It is not 'only a small dark notch'. At 12x the summit carries a dark brown elliptical orifice, and inside it two bright near-white wedge/triangular plates, left and right, meeting along a dark vertical central slit — a legible pair of opercular valves. Do not 'add' the operculum; it exists. What it needs is scale and legibility: the whole aperture is only ~40 px wide against a 139 px body and it is crushed flat by the squat proportion, so at thumbnail size it collapses to the notch the other judge described.

MUST-READ 3 — 'feathery cirri sweeping out of the opening': GENUINELY ABSENT. Zero. There is nothing above, through or around the aperture but flat background pixels. No filaments, no fan, no curl, not even a suggestion at 12x. This is the defining animacy signal for the species and it is the reason the asset fails: with the cirri missing, nothing on the image marks it as a living animal, and the two opercular plates alone are too small and too geometric to carry that load.

ALSO CORRECTING THE CLAIM: 'unattached to any substrate' is true as an observation (no rock, shell or encrustation — just a soft drop shadow) but is NOT one of the three reference must-reads, so it should not be counted as a failed criterion. It is a supporting weakness for the sessile posture, not the defect.

FIX BRIEF: (1) restore the volcano proportion to aspect ~0.9 — take the height up, not the width down; (2) sweep a fan of curled feathery cirri out of the summit opening, biased to one side as if beating — this is the missing identity feature; (3) give the sutures real width, offset shading and slight irregularity so the plates read as chalky and fused rather than ruled; (4) enlarge the operculum that is already drawn so the two valves survive at thumbnail scale; (5) give the base an elliptical footing seated on a substrate.

rows.readsAs: a generic garden spider
rows.defect: Two tan spheres with a pinched waist and eight symmetrical thin legs, topped by an eight-dot spider eye cluster. Every identity cue is missing: no enormous forward-jutting chelicerae, no long leg-like pedipalps held out front, and no hairy segmented abdomen - the rear is a smooth egg. The note says it should appear to have ten front appendages; it has eight ordinary spider legs and nothing in front of the head.
rows.fix: Mount a pair of huge vertical scissor chelicerae on the front of the head - a third the body length - and add two extra long palps reaching forward past them so the animal reads as ten-limbed.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, and the original claim is accurate on all three counts; I add two further defects and one correction of emphasis. Viewed at 1x and again cropped 5x/11x on the head, left leg fan and abdomen (440x440 source).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a two-lobe top-down spider. Front lobe = a smooth tan egg (cephalothorax), rear lobe = a slightly larger smooth tan egg, joined at a wide waist with no pedicel. Eight legs total, four per side, ALL attached to the front lobe, all splayed laterally and rearward in a symmetric fan with a single knee bend each. A soft cast shadow ellipse sits under the body. On a body sphere ~110px across, a 3-4px leg is ~3% of body diameter; a real tarantula's leg is 15-20% of carapace width and is the single thing that makes it a tarantula. A tarantula's cephalothorax is a broad low carapace plate, wider than tall, and the abdomen is a distinctly larger ovoid; here neither shape is differentiated, so the silhouette reads 'two balls' rather than 'arachnid'. The frame centre is 220, so the body STRADDLES the vertical midline and sits slightly RIGHT of centre - it is upper-CENTRE, not 'upper-left quadrant'; only the head is left of the midline. The body occupies only 13% of frame height (57px of 440) and the entire lower half of the canvas is dead space.

rows.verifyWhy:
I decoded the PNG, cropped the head, the thorax/abdomen junction and the antennae at 14-22x, ran a per-column body-height profile, and did the same to Ant.png side by side. The Ant at the same magnification has a textbook hairpin ELBOW -- the scape climbs up-left and the flagellum reverses sharply back down, forming a closed hook. They are not the same drawing. What IS true is the second half nobody stated: the termite antennae are NOT beaded. They are smooth continuous strokes with no moniliform segmentation, so 'bead-string' is unmet even though 'straight' is met.

(2) WAIST -- claim says 'same rod waist' and 'a clear pinched constriction where the joint must be broad'. The 'rod' half is FALSE. Column profile at y=205: the Ant has a literal BREAK -- body pixels end at x=254 and do not resume until x=268 (13 columns of empty sky), with the petiole rod drawn lower at y~211-217. The Termite has NO break and NO rod anywhere: thorax and abdomen are in continuous unbroken contact. Thorax peaks at h=41px (x=207-217), abdomen peaks at h=40px (x=255-264), and the junction minimum is h=21px at x=235-236. So the joint is ~51% of adjacent body height -- continuous flesh, not a petiole. The 'pinched' half of the claim survives in weakened form: at 14x you can see two matching V-notches top and bottom where the two ellipse outlines cross, and 51% is narrower than a termite's genuinely broad abdomen-thorax union should be. That is a widening fix (target ~75-80% of body height, and let the segment banding run across the seam), not evidence of an ant.

(3) WHAT IS CORRECTLY PRESENT: 'pale soft translucent segmented body' reads well -- ivory/cream (~#EDE3C0) with soft sphere shading and a cool rim light, and the abdomen carries 8-9 clear vertical segment bands. Six legs confirmed by row scan at y=230 (six discrete strokes at x=167,174,181,222,254,285), correct count. headFrac measures 33/135 = 0.24 against spec 0.25. Aspect measures 135/43 = 3.1 against spec 2.2, i.e. somewhat overlong.

(4) THE CLAIM'S ONE FULLY CORRECT POINT -- THE EYE. This is the real defect and the top fix. The packet sets eyes: hidden and the note says 'workers are blind and unpigmented', yet the head carries a large glossy black eye ~9px across on a 33px head, complete with a bright white specular square at its upper-left and a lighter surround ring. It is the single highest-contrast mark in the whole asset and it is the one thing that most makes the head read 'ant'. Delete it, or reduce it to a faint slightly-warmer pale patch with no black and no specular.

(5) OTHER SHARED-CHASSIS ISSUES THE CLAIM GESTURED AT AND WAS RIGHT ABOUT, though they are family-wide rather than termite-specific: the leg anchors are anatomically wrong -- three legs spring from beneath the HEAD sphere (x 167/174/181, head spans 158-190), one from the thorax, and two from beneath the ABDOMEN (254, 285); on any real insect all six mount to the thorax. The head is also a bare sphere with no mandibles -- a termite worker's head should be squarer and carry visible jaws -- though mandibles are not in the mustRead row.

VERDICT: the three mustReads are present at roughly 1 full + 1 half + 1 partial, and the asset is distinguishable from Ant.png on precisely the two axes the packet named. It reads as a pale soft banded termite, not as a recoloured ant. rows.readsAs: a glowing yellow bee or midge

Verdict upheld, but three of the stated causes are wrong and the fix must be aimed differently.

CORRECTION 1 - the waist IS drawn, it is just buried. I pixel-scanned the warm-mask (R-B>28) vertical body extent column by column: thorax depth peaks at 43-45px across x=156-172, then collapses to 17px at x=182, 12px at x=188-192, and a minimum of 8px at x=198, before rising again to 32px at x=218 and 48px at x=234 (abdomen). That is a genuine drawn petiole with a ~0.2 constriction ratio - thread-thin by the numbers. At 17x zoom on the junction (orig x=172-218, y=190-236) you can see it: a narrow tapering strip sloping down-right from the thorax's lower-right into the abdomen. So 'not drawn at all' is false. What kills it is occlusion and value: the strip is rendered dark olive against a near-black background, and an opaque light-grey WING ROOT wedge - apex planted exactly on the thorax's right flank, plus a blown-out white specular flare at that same apex - is painted straight over the junction. The 'solid wedge' the first judge saw is wing, not body. Net effect matches their read (the eye goes ball -> white flare -> blob) but the fix is compositing/value, not 'add a waist': draw the petiole in saturated yellow against a dark-rimmed edge and re-order or drop the opacity of the wing root so it stops sitting on the identity feature.

CORRECTION 2 - the abdomen is NOT unbroken. Sampling R,G,B along y=210 from x=195 to x=263 gives a clear alternating profile: 226 (x205) / 194 (x215) / 235 (x220) / 193 (x229) / 235 (x235) / 168 (x244) / 226 (x252) / 191 (x258) - four to five cross-bands with ~40-60 levels of amplitude, and at 8x zoom they are plainly visible, crossed by longitudinal lines so the whole thing reads as a woven plaid. The real defect is CHROMA, not absence: there is no black anywhere on the abdomen. The darkest band pixel is R168 G168 B148 - a pale mid olive - and the light band is ~R235 near-white. So the correct finding is 'banding present but rendered yellow-on-cream with zero black; needs true near-black bands', not 'no banding'.

CORRECTION 3 - the proportion claim is measurably false. Front of head is x=99, rear of abdomen x=263 => body length 164px; max body depth is 42px at the thorax (strong-yellow extent y=188-229, x=156-165). Aspect = 3.9, i.e. slightly MORE elongated than the spec's 3, not squat. Do not send this back for 'lengthen the body'. The squatness the first judge perceived is local silhouette, not global ratio: head and thorax are two near-equal glossy SPHERES and the abdomen is a 64x39 ellipse (1.6:1), so every one of the three body units is round.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS. (a) mustRead 'pinched thread-thin waist' - drawn but not readable at 1:1; the identity beat is invisible. (b) mustRead 'yellow-and-black banded POINTED abdomen' - no black, and not pointed: the gaster is a blunt ellipse. There IS a small pale rounded nub at the rear (x~262-276, seen at 11x) but it is the same grey value as the wings and reads as a wing fold, not a sting - so 'no sting point' is nearly right, the honest description is 'a blunt grey nub where a taper-to-sting belongs'. (c) mustRead 'narrow smooth hairless wings' - the wings are broad, near-opaque light grey, run off past the abdomen to the frame edge, are painted OVER the abdomen (which is what washes the banding out to cream), and the lower wing carries a visible patch of short white bristle strokes, i.e. hairy. This wing treatment is the single upstream cause of (a) and (b) being unreadable. (d) The note says 'Sleek and shiny - do not draw the fat furry body of a bee' - the two-equal-spheres head+thorax chassis is precisely the bee body the note forbids; it is shiny and not furry, so only half the note is met.

Other anatomy seen at zoom: head is a clean sphere with one small round black eye plus a white specular dot and two straight (not elbowed) antennae, no mandibles; legs are thin yellow lines but several emerge from under the HEAD and from under the ABDOMEN rather than all six from the thorax; a hard ground-shadow ellipse under a 'flying' posture makes it read as standing.

Organism read: a glowing yellow bee/gnat. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic brown ladybug or an engorged tick — nothing about it says water
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply not drawn. The hind legs are not flattened and not hair-fringed: all six legs are identical grey hairline arcs of uniform width, unsegmented, with no oar blade, no swimming fringe and no visible joint or coxa where they meet the body — they float behind the elytra edge like whiskers rather than attaching to it. The short clubbed antennae are absent entirely; the head is a featureless dark mushroom-cap blob with two white dots. Only the smooth domed oval wing case reads correctly. Since the oar-shaped fringed hind leg IS the identity of a water beetle, the asset resolves to a land beetle.
rows.fix: Redraw the hind pair as thick paddle limbs — a broad femur, a flattened tibia and a spatulate tarsus with a visible comb of stiff swimming hairs along the trailing edge — swept back and clearly wider than the front two pairs, attached at a visible joint under the elytra margin, and add two short clubbed antennae projecting forward from the head.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but three parts of the stated cause are wrong and the fix should be made against this description instead.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A dark navy field; a portrait brown egg-shaped body with a pale rim light down both edges, one thin dark vertical hairline as the elytral suture, and a large glossy specular stripe on the LEFT half only (the right half has no matching highlight, so the two wing cases are not symmetric). Above it a near-black mushroom shape = a round head dome on a wide flared collar. Six thin dark strokes, three per side, radiating down-and-out from the mid-height edge of the wing case. A hard black elliptical drop shadow sits directly under the body.

MUST-READ 1, 'smooth oval domed wing cases' — PRESENT and the only one that reads. Genuinely domed, smooth, rim-lit, with a suture line. Two sub-defects: the left-only highlight breaks the paired-elytra symmetry, and the shape is far too round (measured brown-elytra footprint ~145px wide x ~160px tall, aspect ~1.1) against the packet's aspect 1.6. A dytiscid must be an elongated streamlined teardrop; this is an egg.

MUST-READ 2, 'flattened hair-fringed hind legs used as oars' — ABSENT. This is the defining read and it is gone, so the claim's verdict stands. But the description of it is imprecise. Measured stroke thickness per leg along its length: 8px where it meets the body, 7px mid, 5px at the tip — so they are NOT 'uniform-width', they taper, which makes them read even more like whiskers/antennae than the claim says. They ARE identical: on each side the three strokes are pixel-for-pixel the same curve translated down by ~44px (left side at x=130 gives runs y200-206, y244-250, y288-294, all t=7), and the left and right triples mirror each other. So there is zero differentiation of a hind pair — no flattening, no fringe, no segmentation into femur/tibia/tarsus, no tarsal paddle, no joint anywhere. Colour correction: they are not 'grey'. They are RGB(32,36,44), a near-black desaturated blue, against a background of RGB(5,6,12) — barely above the backdrop, so at thumbnail size they nearly vanish. The low contrast is an additional defect the claim understated.

Correct the 'unattached, floating behind the elytra edge' wording — that is wrong. The strokes are still present at x=145, which is INSIDE the elytra fill boundary (x=152), i.e. they run under and behind the wing case rather than floating in space with a gap. The real anatomical error is different and should be fixed as such: all six legs emanate from the mid-height margin of the WING CASE, so they insert into the abdomen. There is no thorax and no coxa; the legs sprout from the elytra.

MUST-READ 3, 'short clubbed antennae on a tucked head' — ABSENT, confirmed. Row-by-row silhouette scan of the head zone (background-vs-not, y=98 to y=173) gives a span that widens monotonically and smoothly: 12, 26, 34, 40, 42, 46, 48, 48, 48, 48, 50, then 66, 78, 84, 88, 90 as the collar flares, then merges into the elytra. There is no row anywhere where the outline juts out and back in, so there is not even an antenna stub. Nothing projects from the head.

Correct 'the head is a featureless dark mushroom-cap blob' — overstated, though the conclusion survives. There ARE eyes: two dark pupils each carrying a white specular catchlight, measured at exactly four bright pixels, (211,117),(212,117) and (225,117),(226,117). They are real but so small they contribute nothing at any display size. Everything else about the head is a single flat value — sampled RGB(36,28,21) identically at (220,110), (220,140), (180,150) and (260,150), i.e. the head dome and the pronotum collar are one undifferentiated silhouette with no tonal modelling and no head/pronotum boundary.

DEFECT THE CLAIM MISSED. The packet specifies posture: swimming. The asset is drawn dorsal, upright, static, and carries a hard black ground-shadow ellipse beneath it — that shadow reads unambiguously as an object resting on a surface. It actively signals land, compounding the missing oars.

NET. One of three must-reads present, and the two absent ones are precisely the pair that encode 'water' and 'beetle head'. With uniform tapering whisker-strokes for legs, no antennae, a round rather than streamlined body, and a ground shadow, the asset resolves to a generic brown land beetle — or, as the claim reasonably put it, an engorged tick. Nothing indicates water. FAIL is correct.

FIX PRIORITY: (1) replace the six identical strokes with a proper three-pair leg set — short front/mid legs and a genuinely differentiated hind pair drawn as broad flattened blades with a visible swim-hair fringe along the trailing edge, swept back into a power stroke; (2) attach all legs at a thorax under the pronotum, not at the elytral margin; (3) add short clubbed antennae breaking the head silhouette; (4) elongate the body toward aspect 1.6; (5) delete the ground shadow and replace it with a water cue.

(1) The bill is a thin needle-like cone roughly the same length as the skull and angled downward — not a disproportionately long, straight, heavy dagger; it looks like a finch or duckling bill in yellow. (2) The head is SMALL relative to the body, not oversized (visually well under the 0.4 headFrac), and there is a clear concave dip between the back of the skull and the shoulder that reads as a visible neck. (3) The tail is the opposite of stubby: a long dark pointed wedge projecting far past the rounded rump, adding roughly a third again to the body length. The body is also deep and duck-round rather than compact-stubby, and the legs are long twig perching legs set at mid-body. The render itself is clean and centred with no clipping, so this is purely an anatomy read failure — but the dagger bill IS the kingfisher, and it is not here.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette to kingfisher proportions: lengthen the bill to roughly 1.5–2x skull length and make it a straight, thick-based, horizontally held dagger; enlarge the head to ~40% of body length and set it directly on the shoulders with the crown-to-back line continuous (no neck dip); and cut the tail to a short blunt stub barely clearing the rump.

rows.readsAs: a white pet rabbit / cottontail, not a hare

The 'very large hind feet' must-read is also absent: the hind limb is a small grey stub with no foot form at all, no length, no splay. The haunch is drawn as a pale detached oval sitting on top of the flank rather than a muscled hind quarter, and the forelimb is barely present. Body is a compact round bunny with no hare proportions, and it sits small in a large empty frame.
rows.fix: Paint solid black wedges into the top third of both ears, and rebuild the hind limb as a long angled hock dropping to an oversized flat foot that plants forward of the rump on the ground line.

rows.readsAs: a generic brown cottontail rabbit

Most damaging, the eponymous oversized furry hind feet do not exist — the hind limb is a tiny dark stub barely protruding from the belly line, shorter than the animal's own ear, with no foot shape whatsoever, so the one feature the species is named for is absent. The silhouette is pixel-for-pixel the Arctic Hare chassis with a brown fill, down to the same haunch ellipse, same whisker fan, same incisor squares and same shadow.

rows.readsAs: a taupe cartoon newt, or a fat rat with a banana tail
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. The limbs are not heavy and are not splayed sideways — they are the family's four thin vertical pegs tucked under the belly, so the sprawling posture that defines a varanid is absent. There is no forked yellow tongue; the mouth is the same single ruled horizontal line used on every other asset. There is no loose scaly neck skin because there is no neck. The body is a small smooth speckled egg with no mass, bulk or scale texture, and the tail is the shared banana rather than a long muscular half-body tail.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the full-size PNG, then re-rendered three zooms (whole body 3x, head 8x, limb band 6x) and ran a pixel scan for silhouette bbox and for any yellow pixel. VERDICT UPHELD, but two-thirds of the stated causes need correcting and three real defects went unnamed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS: one taupe egg-shaped body ellipse with soft airbrushed mid-brown blotches; a second, smaller rounded ellipse plugged onto its front-right as the head, with a visible overlap seam where the two ovals meet; a fat crescent tail sweeping UP and back over the body, carrying one big dark charcoal racing-stripe blotch down its inner curve and ending in a blunt rounded club; and four dark olive-drab limbs. Silhouette bbox is 84,154 -> 355,269 = 272 x 116 px.

MUST-READ 1 (heavy limbs splayed out sideways) - FAILED, but NOT for the stated reason. The claim 'thin vertical pegs tucked under the belly' is wrong on two counts: the limbs are not thin (each is a chunky rounded rod roughly 20-24 px wide against a 116 px tall animal) and they are not vertical (the forelimb rakes down-and-back at about 30 deg, the hindlimb rakes down-and-forward, i.e. a mammal walking gait). The actual defect is threefold: (a) they attach at the belly MIDLINE under the body ellipse rather than at the flanks, so no shoulder or hip is visible; (b) there is no laterally bowed elbow or knee anywhere - the rod is a single unbroken taper from attachment to tip, so the varanid sprawl (limb out to the side, elbow above the shoulder line, body slung between them) simply does not exist; (c) there is NO FOOT AT ALL - each limb terminates in a plain rounded blunt cap with zero toes and zero claws, and the belly does not clear the ground because the body ellipse sits almost on the shadow.

MUST-READ 2 (long muscular tail about half the total length) - FAILED, and the judge did not flag it. Measured, the tail runs x=84 to about x=190 = ~106 px of a 272 px total, i.e. ~39%, not half; worse, it does not trail as a heavy tapering muscle mass. It arcs UPWARD in a fat even-width crescent and ends blunt. 'Banana tail' is a fair read; a rat or opossum tail read is also fair. It is the single most eye-catching shape in the asset and it points at the wrong animal.

MUST-READ 3 (long forked yellow tongue and loose scaly neck skin) - FAILED, and the claim here is exactly right. A full-image pixel scan for any yellow-dominant pixel (r>120, g>100, b at least 40 below min(r,g)) returned ZERO hits - there is no tongue geometry of any colour, forked or otherwise. The mouth is a single hairline ruled stroke that does not even reach the snout tip and has no gape, no jaw line and no lip. There is no neck: the head ellipse abuts the body ellipse directly, so there is no surface for loose skin, no dewlap, no throat folds. No scale texture anywhere on the body - the markings are soft blurred airbrush dots, not beaded osteoderms.

DEFECTS THE FAIL DID NOT NAME (fix these too): (1) THE EYE IS THE WRONG EYE. The reference row calls for 'small' eyes; the render has a large pale-cream almond occupying a big share of the skull with a hard VERTICAL SLIT pupil - a gecko/cat eye. A Komodo has a small round dark eye. This is a bigger identity error than it looks, because it is the only detail on the head and it is loudly wrong. (2) ASPECT IS 2.34 AGAINST A SPEC OF 3.2 - the animal is far too short and too deep-bodied, which is the direct cause of the 'fat rat' read; the body ellipse is nearly as tall as it is long. (3) HEAD FRACTION IS ~0.24 AGAINST A SPEC OF 0.2, and the skull is a plain rounded oval with no snout taper, no nostril, no jowl and no temporal mass.

OVERALL READ: a taupe, spotted, blunt-nosed, neckless, footless quadruped with a slit-pupil eye and a fat upcurled club tail. It reads as a cartoon newt/salamander or a spotted rodent. All three must-reads are absent as identity signals. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: the green Iguana asset recoloured dark grey — a sooty cartoon newt

The tail is the shared round banana with a dark stripe, not laterally flattened or paddle-like, so the single feature that makes this animal a swimmer is gone. No long curved claws; the legs end in blunt stumps. Compounding it, the body value sits barely above the dark background, so the silhouette nearly disappears.
rows.fix: Give it a short blunt squared-off muzzle with white salt encrustation on top, and redraw the tail as a tall thin vertical paddle with a crest ridge running its length.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated causes.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, read raw, then re-read at gamma-boosted 5x-8x crops of head, back, feet and tail; silhouette masks of Marine_Iguana.png and Iguana.png overlaid).

1) SNOUT - must-read ABSENT, judge correct. At 8x the head is a plain grey ellipse, body-x 318->392 (len ~74px) by 43px tall, ratio 1.72. The green Iguana's head is the same ellipse at 1.77 (x ~330->415, 85 x 48). Front-edge trace per row on the marine goes 370,377,381,384,387,389,390,391,391,392,392,391,391,387,386,383,380,377,372,366 - a smooth continuous convex arc with no vertical facet anywhere. There is no blunt/square muzzle, no truncated terminal plane, no nostril mass. There is also NO salt crust on the face: the whole head is one flat grey fill with a single bright rim-light along the top-front edge, a white round eye with a vertical slit pupil, and a straight thin mouth line - pixel-identical construction to Iguana.png, same eye at the same relative position, same mouth line at the same height, only the hue changed. The reference note ('stubby blunt face - NOT the long pointed green-iguana profile') is directly violated.

2) TAIL - must-read ABSENT, judge correct, now quantified. Vertical thickness of the tail sampled every 8px from the tip inward: 26,33,34,33,31,30,30,30,30,29,29,29,28,28,28,29,29 - dead constant. Body depth over the ribcage is 49-53. So the tail is a uniform round tube about 55-60% of the body's depth that hooks upward at the tip and ends in a rounded knob, carrying one darker interior stripe. A laterally flattened paddle in side view must be at least as deep as the trunk and taper to a blade/keel; nothing here does. It is the same banana the green Iguana wears (that asset's tail measures 30-38 over the same span). The one feature that makes this animal a swimmer is genuinely missing.

3) CLAWS - must-read ABSENT, judge correct. At 6x the fore and hind limbs are two tapering rounded capsules (upper + lower segment) ending in a blunt rounded stub. Zero digits, zero toes, zero claws; the only appendage is a small backward spur at the fore elbow. Nothing hooked or curved anywhere on the feet.

4) CONTRAST - judge correct, and worse than stated. Sampled body fill = RGB(37,39,42); dorsal background directly above = RGB(9,14,20); left background = RGB(6,9,15). WCAG contrast body:background = 1.29:1 (1.33:1 against the left field). The green Iguana in the same frame measures 4.63:1. The tail's interior stripe samples RGB(13,14,17) - literally background luminance. The 'dark sooty body' note has been taken as a value instruction and the animal has been rendered 3.6x flatter than its own sibling; on first read the silhouette is barely separable from the field.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM:
- 'This is the green Iguana asset recoloured' is close but overstated. Silhouette IoU against Iguana.png is 0.768, not 1.0: the marine is the same chassis re-scaled, bbox 346x222 vs the iguana's 392x222, with a shorter tail and a slightly shorter head. Head, mouth, eye, limb form, foot, neck carriage, topline and tail are shared; scale is not. Call it recolour-plus-rescale on one chassis, which is the finding that matters for the family.
- The claim omits that ONE must-read IS present and is drawn correctly: the low spiny crest. At 7x there is a clean row of about ten backward-raked triangular dorsal spikes from the nape down the back, noticeably lower and more swept than the green Iguana's tall upright spines - this was genuinely re-authored, not recoloured, and should not be touched by the fix.
- The claim also omits that the flank blotching WAS re-authored: the iguana carries dark-green blotches, the marine carries warm cream/tan mottling that reads plausibly as salt encrustation. The problem is placement, not absence - the pale crust sits on the ribs and shoulder where the reference asks for it on the SNOUT, and there is not one pale pixel on the face.

VERDICT: 1 of 3 must-reads readable; the identity feature (paddle tail) absent; the reference note's explicit prohibition (long rounded green-iguana snout) violated; body value collapsed to 1.29:1. FAIL stands.

FIX ORDER: (a) rebuild the skull as a short deep box - truncate the front of the ellipse into a near-vertical blunt plane, drop head length to ~1.2-1.3x its height, and put the pale salt crust on the snout tip and above the nostrils; (b) rebuild the tail as a laterally flattened blade - depth at least equal to the trunk at the base, tapering as a straight-edged paddle rather than a constant tube, and kill the upward hook; (c) add three or four curved claws per foot; (d) lift the body fill to at least 3:1 against the field (target the Iguana's 4.6:1 minus a step for 'sooty'). Keep the crest and the pale flank mottling.

rows.readsAs: a brown cartoon newt or a salamander plush
rows.defect: Nothing monitor-specific is drawn. No forked tongue — the mouth is the shared ruled line. The tail is the shared thick round banana, not laterally flattened and not longer than the body. The limbs are the family's thin vertical pegs, not muscular or sprawled, and they end in rounded stumps with no hooked claws. The reference's headline note — a long snake-like neck unlike the neckless build of most lizards — is directly contradicted: the head ellipse is fused straight onto the body with zero neck, making this the MOST neckless asset in the batch.
rows.fix: Insert a long tapered snake-like neck between skull and shoulders, and add a deeply forked tongue flicking from the jaw.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled the head (6x), snout tip (9x), tail (5x), both limb pairs (8x) and the whole silhouette (3x), and ran a column-by-column silhouette scan to get real measurements. The FAIL stands: all three mustReads are absent and the note is contradicted. Measured geometry (columns where non-background pixels exist): silhouette spans x=25..410. Tail x=25..205 (180px). Trunk x=205..340 (135px, max depth 65px at x=260-285). Head x=340..410 (70px, max depth 51px). headFrac = 70/385 = 0.18, which is on-spec (0.2); that is the ONLY spec number the asset hits.

MUSTREAD 1 - 'long deeply forked flicking tongue': ABSENT, and not merely small. At 9x the snout tip is a bare rounded ellipse cap; the mouth is a single 2px hairline that terminates exactly at the silhouette edge with nothing protruding. The scan confirms no pixels beyond x=410, so there is no tongue anywhere on the canvas, not hidden, not tucked, not drawn in body colour. The judge is right.

MUSTREAD 2 - 'laterally flattened tail longer than the body': the tail is round and unflattened, and it is worse than the judge described. It is not a tapering tail at all: the scan shows a CONSTANT 36px thickness from x=85 all the way to x=200 (115px of dead-straight uniform hose) ending in a fully rounded capsule cap at x=25. There is no taper, no keel, no dorsal ridge, no vertical blade profile - the dark interior stripe reads as cylindrical shading, reinforcing 'tube'. CORRECTION to the judge's length claim, which the fix must not take literally: the tail (180px) IS longer than the trunk alone (135px). It is shorter than head+trunk (205px), i.e. ~0.88 of snout-to-vent, where a monitor should be ~1.5x SVL. So 'no longer than the body' is only true if 'body' includes the head. Simply lengthening the tail would not fix this shape - the round constant-width hose is the primary defect, the length a secondary one.

MUSTREAD 3 - 'muscular sprawled limbs with large hooked claws': the claws are absent, confirmed at 8x on both pairs. Each limb is a plain tapered tube that narrows to a blunt rounded stub floating just above the ellipse shadow - no foot plate, no toes, no digits, no claw at all. ADDITION the judge missed: the posture is also wrong. Packet says posture 'sprawling'; the limbs are drawn as near-vertical columns hanging straight down under a deep barrel body (the classic pony/ungulate chassis stance), with no lateral splay, no elbow/knee angle out to the side, and no body-close-to-ground line. So this mustRead fails twice, on the claws and on the sprawl.

NOTE - 'the neck is long and snake-like, unlike the neckless build of most lizards': directly contradicted, confirmed by measurement. At x=335 the trunk is 41px deep, at x=340 it is 38px, and at x=345 the head is already 41px and climbing. The head ellipse simply abuts the front of the barrel; there is a single-column waist and then the head. Neck length is effectively 0px on a 385px animal, when the note asks for the single most distinctive proportion of the genus. I cannot verify 'the most neckless asset in the batch' (I only inspected this one), so that superlative should be dropped, but 'zero neck' is exact.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRESENT, in the asset's favour: the body carries a scattered brown ocellated blotch pattern (roughly 20 soft dark-brown spots, some in loose diagonal rows across the flank) which is a genuine monitor cue - Nile/savannah monitors carry exactly that ocelli field. The eye is a well-drawn white sclera with a vertical slit pupil. Those are the only species signals on the asset, and neither is a mustRead. Minor extra inaccuracy: monitors have ROUND pupils; the vertical slit reads gecko/crocodilian.

READ CORRECTION: 'brown salamander plush' is close but not quite what I see. The barrel is too deep-bellied and the legs too column-like and too far under the body for a salamander (salamanders sprawl); with the fat spotted barrel, blunt round head, neckless join, pillar legs and uniform round hose tail it reads closest to a generic spotted newt/otter-shaped toy quadruped. Either way the point holds - it does not read as a monitor lizard. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a grey cartoon newt, indistinguishable from the Monitor and Komodo except for hue
rows.defect: The identity must-read is absent: the head is the same smooth rounded ellipse every other asset in this batch wears — not massive, not blocky, and with no jowls at all (the jaw line is a single straight ruled stroke, so there is no cheek mass to jowl). The body carries scattered random speckles rather than heavy transverse bands, and there is no beaded scale texture anywhere — the surface is a flat airbrushed gradient. Only the thick body-length tail is roughly right, and that is the shared banana shape arriving by default rather than by design.
rows.fix: Widen the rear of the skull into a heavy blocky wedge with bulging jowls behind the jaw line, and replace the speckles with bold white transverse bands across the trunk and tail.
rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size, then re-cropped and upscaled 4-5x on the head, mid-body, tail and legs, and re-rendered the whole frame at 2.6x brightness to pull the near-black limbs out of the background. The FAIL stands: two of the three must-reads are wholly absent and the third is satisfied only by length, not form. Corrections and additions to the original claim follow.

HEAD (mustRead: massive jowled blocky head). At 5x the head is a single smooth ellipse, long-axis horizontal, butted directly against the body ellipse with zero neck articulation. The snout terminus is fully rounded - there is no squared muzzle box, no angular jaw corner, no temporal/masseter bulge, and no cheek lobe of any kind, so the jowl read is genuinely absent. CORRECTION to the claim: the head is not undersized. I measured it at ~90px against a ~142px body ellipse and a ~356px total length, i.e. headFrac ~0.25 against the spec'd 0.28, and it is the largest head-to-body in this family. So the 'massive' half of the must-read is proportionally delivered; what is missing is specifically the jowl mass and the blocky geometry. The fix is a SHAPE change - widen a distinct cheek/jowl lobe behind and below the jaw line and square off the snout terminus and the lower jaw corner - not a scale-up. The claim's 'single straight ruled jaw stroke' is correct and understates it: the mouth is a 1px hairline that slopes slightly upward, and it stops roughly 15px short of the snout tip, so it does not even close at the front of the face. The eye is a large white almond with a black vertical slit pupil - readable, but oversized for the 'normal' eye spec and identical to the Monitor's and Komodo's.

BODY (mustRead: heavy banded body with beaded scales). Confirmed absent, with one refinement. The markings are not 'speckles' in the hard sense - they are soft Gaussian-blurred brown blobs of varying size scattered over the flank. There is a faint diagonal chain of them across the mid-flank that reads as noise rather than as any organised pattern; nothing anywhere approaches a transverse band. Bands here need to be hard-edged, full-height, running dorsum to belly and repeating along the trunk. The surface underneath is a flat airbrushed light-to-dark gradient with no beading, no scale cells, no tessellation, no specular pinpoints. ADDITION the claim did not name: a hard white rim-light arc is stroked along the dorsal edge of both the body and the head, which strengthens the inflated-balloon read and works directly against a heavy beaded lizard.

TAIL (mustRead: thick tail slightly longer than the body). Length is roughly right - the tail runs ~140px against a ~135-142px body, so 'slightly longer' is honestly met. Form is not: at 4x the tail is a constant-width tube that never tapers, ending in a blunt rounded cap, with one dark rounded-rect stripe inset along its length that reads as an interior shading core rather than as markings. No taper, no banding, no scale texture, no dorsal ridge.

DEFECTS THE JUDGE DID NOT NAME. (a) The four limbs are near-black two-segment bent tubes that terminate in blunt rounded tips - there are no feet, no digits and no claws at all, on any of the four. (b) The posture is wrong for the row: the row specifies 'sprawling', but the legs drop as near-vertical columns and hold the body high off the ground shadow, which is a mammalian upright stance. (c) No neck - the two ellipses simply overlap.

CHASSIS / FAMILY. I opened Monitor_Lizard.png and Komodo_Dragon.png to test the comparison. The chassis claim is correct but the phrasing 'except for hue' is imprecise and should not be quoted as the cause: the Monitor is visibly longer and lower-slung (a genuinely different aspect), so hue is not the only variable. The accurate statement is that all three are assembled from an identical primitive set - same ellipse trunk, same ellipse head butted on with no neck, same 1px ruled mouth line, same white-almond slit eye, same four bent near-black tube legs with no feet, same constant-width tail carrying one dark inner stripe, same blurred blob speckles, same white dorsal rim light - with only aspect ratio, hue and tail curvature varied between them. Tegu and Komodo in particular are near-superimposable.

OVERALL. Stripped of hue, this silhouette reads as a generic blob quadruped - closer to a cartoon otter or seal than to any varanid or teiid. Nothing in the frame identifies a Tegu.

rows.readsAs: a dark green flower or unopened rose/camellia with a pale pearl at its centre, or a mossy stone with an egg set in it
rows.defect: A hard, glossy, light-mint SPHERE sits at the exact centre of the head and is the brightest object in the frame; it reads as a separate body (pearl/pistil/egg), which no cabbage has — cabbage identity is a solid uninterrupted head. The thin white lines do not read as thick branching midribs; they are smooth petal-outline arcs radiating from that sphere, which reinforces the flower read. Colour is near-black olive throughout, not the specified blue-green with a waxy pale bloom, so the waxy cabbage surface is absent. The 'loose flaring outer leaves around the base' amount to a single pointed leaf poking out low-right plus one small tab left — there is no skirt of wavy open outer leaves.
rows.fix: Delete the central pale sphere entirely and close the head over it with two more overlapping wrap leaves whose edges spiral off-centre, then lift the whole palette to a pale glaucous blue-green with a dusty bloom and redraw the veins as thick, tapering white midribs that each start at a leaf base and branch outward — and ring the base with three to four wide wavy-edged outer leaves flaring away from the ball.

rows.readsAs: a peacock's fanned tail or a fan-palm/sea-anemone spray, with a lit streetlamp standing behind it
rows.defect: The single tall bare vertical stem topped by a large solid white dome reads unambiguously as a streetlamp and dominates the image; the reference asks for TINY white four-petal flowers, and instead one oversized featureless cap sits on a naked pole. The growth form is a rigid symmetric radial fan of straight rays pinned to one ground point — not a sprawling floating MAT of hollow succulent stems, so the aquatic identity is gone (no waterline, no float, no sprawl). Leaflets are uniform elongated ovals repeated at equal spacing down each ray with NO larger terminal leaflet at any tip, so the pinnate-with-big-end-leaflet must-read is absent. White threadlike roots at the nodes are entirely missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a low horizontal sprawling mat: three or four hollow pale-green stems drifting sideways and overlapping at differing heights rather than radiating from one point, each stem carrying paired rounded leaflets that end in one clearly larger spade-shaped terminal leaflet, with fine white root threads trailing down from the stem nodes and the flower reduced to a few pinhead four-petal white specks at the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: A young fern frond or a mimosa/acacia sapling with a single acorn stuck on top
rows.defect: Every must-read fails and one is inverted. (1) The leaf is NOT four oval leaflets in two opposite pairs — the stem carries roughly fourteen opposite pairs of tiny feathery comb-shaped leaflets, dozens in total, which is the classic fern/mimosa ladder, not a quadrifoliate peanut leaf. (2) The habit is NOT low and spreading — it is a single ramrod-straight vertical stem, far taller than wide despite the 1.6 aspect, with no branching, no sprawl and no ground-hugging mat. (3) There are no yellow pea flowers anywhere. (4) The pods are absent from the soil AND the note is violated outright: the one tan wrinkled object in the whole image sits on the very APEX of the stem, hanging on the plant, which is precisely what the reference forbids. There is no soil line, no peg driven downward, nothing subterranean. A stranger shown this would say 'fern' and would never say 'peanut'.
rows.fix: Redraw as a low sprawling mat: three or four short arching stems radiating out from a central crown, each bearing two or three leaves of exactly four fat oval leaflets (two opposite pairs, no terminal odd leaflet), a couple of small yellow pea flowers at the leaf axils, a visible soil line across the lower third, and two or three netted tan pods drawn BELOW that line on downward pegs — and delete the tan blob at the top of the stem entirely.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon platypus / blobby newt
rows.defect: The must-read 'long tapering tail longer than the body' is INVERTED — the tail is a short fat club roughly half the body's length and it does not taper. There are no splayed clawed toes: the limbs are four featureless dark pegs hanging straight down from the ellipse's underside with no elbow bend, so the sprawling posture is absent. The head is a plain rounded oval, not a scaly wedge, and there is no ear opening anywhere on it.
rows.fix: Redraw the tail as a slender continuously tapering whip at least 1.6x the snout-vent length, and re-root the limbs on the SIDE of the body with a visible elbow above the topline and a splayed 5-toe foot.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but three of the four stated causes are measurably wrong and the fixes should be made against these numbers, not theirs. I measured the silhouette by column scan (440x440 canvas, bg #05060C, alpha-difference threshold 40): the animal occupies x=66..374 (308 px nose-to-tail-tip) and y=155..269 (114 px tall incl. limbs), so measured aspect is ~2.7, not the spec'd 3.5 - the body is stubbier than the reference row asks for, which nobody mentioned.

TAIL (mustRead 'long tapering tail longer than the body') - FAILS, but not as described. The judge called it 'a short fat club about half the body length'. Measured: tail runs x=66..~170 = ~104 px; the torso oval alone is x~170..305 = ~135 px; head+body is x~170..374 = ~205 px. So the tail is 0.77x the torso and 0.51x head+body - 'about half the body' is only true if 'body' means head+body; against the torso alone it is closer to three-quarters. The more actionable error is the profile: this tail does not merely fail to taper, it INVERTS the taper. Column heights along the tail are 50 px at the hip end (x=150), swelling to 64 px at mid-tail (x=100), then rounding off at the tip. It is a flat beaver/platypus PADDLE that gets wider as it leaves the body, carrying one long dark sausage-shaped blotch down its middle, and it curves up and back over the hips. Fix is not 'lengthen the club' - it is 'replace the paddle with a cone': base thickness at the vent, monotonic narrowing to a fine point, total length > 1.0x head+body.

LIMBS (mustRead 'sprawling bent-elbow limbs with splayed clawed toes') - FAILS, but the stated reason is wrong. The judge said 'no elbow bend: four smooth pegs hang straight down from the underside'. They do not hang straight down. At 7x-9x zoom the hind pair angle down-and-BACKWARD off a distinct wide hip lobe, and the near hind limb has a visible shallow knee/ankle bend partway along the shank; the fore pair slant down-and-FORWARD. So bend and angle exist. What is genuinely, totally absent is any FOOT: all four limbs terminate in a plain rounded olive stub with zero digit separation, zero claws, no ankle joint, no plantar surface - like the end of a sock. The second real failure the judge did not name is stance geometry: the limbs are columns positioned UNDER the body in mammalian carriage, so the posture spec 'sprawling' fails on a separate axis from 'straight pegs' - there is no elbows-out lateral splay, no visible upper-arm horizontal segment, and the feet plant directly beneath the ribcage rather than outboard of it.

HEAD (mustRead 'scaly wedge head with a visible ear opening') - FAILS exactly as described, plus more. At 14x the head is a plain rounded oval with a blunt hemispherical snout, no wedge, no taper toward the nose, no ear opening / tympanum disc anywhere behind or below the eye. Also absent and worth listing for the fix: no nostril, no jaw or lip separation, no scale or granular texture (the fill is a smooth soft gradient), and the mouth is a single straight ruled 1px line running dead level from mid-cheek to the snout tip. The one thing the judge missed that DOES land: the eye carries a genuine vertical slit pupil in a pale cream iris - a real reptile cue, drawn correctly, and the only lizard signal in the whole asset. The body also carries scattered soft grey-brown blotches which are a fair side-blotched-lizard mottle.

OVERALL. The 'cartoon platypus' read is fair and I reached it independently before reading the claim: fat cream egg-shaped torso, blunt bill-like oval head on a short neck, flat dark-striped paddle tail, four stubby olive legs with no feet. Two of the three identity must-reads are absent and the third (tail) is inverted. Nothing here is a small feature drawn somewhere I did not look - I zoomed head, both limb pairs and the tail at 8-14x nearest-neighbour and the features are simply not drawn. Band FAIL stands.

(Process note: two intermediate crops rendered content from a DIFFERENT species file - orange furry legs with hooves, and a brown ringtail - despite being cropped from this PNG's path. Regenerating each crop individually gave the correct olive/cream content, confirmed against the 3x full-frame view and the raw column scan above. Every observation in this record is from a crop I re-derived and cross-checked against the pixel measurements.)

rows.readsAs: an orange spiny lizard - roughly an iguana
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads land (the yellow-orange colour and a legible row of black dorsal spikes along nape and back; the tail is long and tapering). The third fails: the legs are not stout and clawed, they are four smooth dark pegs with no foot, no toe and no ankle. The 'heavy jowly head' is not modelled either — it is the same plain oval head ellipse used on the other three, with no jowl mass, no tympanum and no dewlap, so it only reads as an iguana because of the spikes and the colour.
rows.fix: Give it a real iguanid head — deepen the jaw into a jowl, add the round tympanum and a hanging throat dewlap — and end each leg in a thick five-toed foot with visible claws.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon platypus / small tan blob-beast
rows.defect: Identical drawing to Coastal Lizard with a browner tint. 'Tail longer than the body' is absent — the tail is a stubby upcurled club shorter than the trunk. 'Four legs splayed sideways with elbows out' is absent and actively contradicted: the four limbs are straight pegs dropping from the belly line in a mammalian under-body stance, the exact error the packet note warns against. 'Wedge-shaped scaly head' is absent — the head is a smooth oval with a straight ruled mouth line and no scale texture.
rows.fix: Rebuild the pose so the humerus and femur project horizontally out from the flanks with the elbows breaking the upper silhouette, and extend the tail past 1.5x body length.

rows.readsAs: a grey cartoon platypus / mole-blob
rows.defect: The identity must-read 'tail longer than head and body combined' is missing by a wide margin — the tail is a short grey club about half the trunk length. The body is a fat rounded egg rather than a flattened granular-scaled form — there is no dorsoventral flattening and no scale texture at all, just soft airbrushed mottling.

rows.readsAs: a long-snouted beaked whale
rows.defect: Beak and the pair of white erupting tusks read clearly and the rake scratches are visible, but the melon behind the beak barely bulges - the forehead is a straight ramp - and the dorsal fin is not a fin: it is two soft grey blobs floating on the topline at roughly mid-back with no edge, so the 'small fin set far back' does not register.

rows.readsAs: a white whale, probably a beluga
rows.defect: White body and absent dorsal are right, but the melon is a wedge rather than a bulging ball - the forehead slopes straight back from the mouth - and there is no neck crease anywhere. The 'low dorsal ridge' is drawn as a hard dark stripe capping the head and shoulders, which reads as a black cap marking rather than a ridge.

rows.readsAs: a generic grey fish - the same lozenge as the Dolphin card, only longer
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The rostrum comes to a sharp point instead of a broad flat U and carries no ridge; there are zero throat pleats on the underside; and the dorsal is a soft grey blob at roughly 55% of body length, i.e. mid-back, not the thumb-nub three-quarters back the note explicitly warns about. Nothing on the card says baleen whale, let alone the largest animal alive.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and would send the fix in the wrong direction. Measured on the 440x440 PNG (silhouette mask, background-gradient-compensated threshold): ink bbox x22-416, y182-257 (395x76, aspect 5.2 vs spec 5.5). Snout tip x=22; peduncle minimum x=360-364; fluke tips to x=416. Body length snout->fluke insertion = 340px.

MUST-READ 1 'tiny nub dorsal fin set far back near the tail' -- HALF PRESENT, and the judge described the wrong half as broken. It is NOT a soft smudge. Per-pixel topline: baseline y=187-188 across x=195-205, rising to a flat plateau y=182 across x=216-229, back to y=187 at x=243. That is a cleanly drawn, HARD-EDGED low dome, ~39px base x ~7px above the interpolated topline, with a crisp anti-aliased silhouette against the background and a light rim highlight running along its base -- an edge-gradient pass at gain 30 renders it as a closed, continuous contour, not a blur. It is also genuinely TINY (7px on a 60px-deep body at that station, ~12%), so the packet note's trap ('commonly drawn with a large dorsal fin') was NOT fallen into. The real defects are POSITION and PROFILE: bump centre x=223 = 59% of body length, trailing edge x=243 = 65%. Spec wants three-quarters back (~75%, i.e. centre near x=277 in this frame). The judge said ~55%; the true figure is 59%, so their number is 4 points low, but their conclusion (mid-back, not near the tail) stands. Profile is a symmetric smooth dome with no short base and no posterior rake -- it reads as a low ridge/hump, not a nub fin. FIX = translate the fin aft ~54px to x~277 and give it a short base with a slight posterior lean. Do NOT shrink it and do NOT 'sharpen' it; both are already right.

MUST-READ 2 'broad flat U-shaped rostrum with a single ridge' -- ABSENT, judge correct and if anything understating it. Head columns run x=22 (top 213/bot 214, i.e. a 2px needle point) through x=77 (top 196/bot 230) in an unbroken monotonic taper. A 10x colour zoom of x15-135,y195-245 shows a plain smooth wedge: no flat broad rostrum top, no longitudinal ridge/splashguard line ahead of the blowhole, no blunt tip. Additionally -- not mentioned by the judge -- there is NO mouth or lower-jawline stroke anywhere on the head; the only thing below the ventral edge is a soft drop-shadow band. That absence is causally upstream of must-read 3: there is no jaw for pleats to hang from. The only head details present are a small pale blowhole ellipse (centred ~x=85,y=178) and a small dark eye with a specular highlight (~x=59,y=217).

MUST-READ 3 'pleated throat grooves' -- ABSENT, judge correct, verified numerically not just by eye. A horizontal second-derivative groove detector over the throat (x30-175, y205-236, every 3rd row) returns no set of near-parallel fore-aft lines; every local dark minimum resolves to the silhouette edge crossing the scanline diagonally, the eye (x56-63), or the pectoral flipper leading edge (x112-120). A gain-60 edge pass over the same region shows only gradient dither. Ventral surface is entirely smooth.

SHARED-CHASSIS CLAIM -- CORRECT, and it is the root cause. Side-by-side with Dolphin.png: identical needle-point rostrum, identical eye-with-highlight, identical blowhole ellipse, identical low-dome dorsal at the same relative station, identical pectoral flipper shape, identical notched fluke. Dolphin bbox 319x84 (aspect 3.8) vs Blue Whale 395x76 (aspect 5.2). The two differ ONLY in length and hue (teal-green vs blue-violet) -- the judge's 'apart from length' should read 'apart from length and hue'. Worth flagging upward: the Dolphin fails its own must-reads on this same chassis (no sickle dorsal, no beak), so this is a family-level chassis defect, not a per-asset one, and fixing Blue Whale alone will not resolve it.

VERDICT: two of three must-reads are wholly absent and the third has its defining property (far back near the tail) wrong; the asset reads as a generic small cetacean, so FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a teal fish
rows.defect: The single feature every viewer uses to name a dolphin - the tall curved sickle dorsal fin - is not there; there is only a faint grey smudge on the back with no leading or trailing edge. There is also no beak: the snout is the plain point of the teardrop, with no crease separating beak from melon and no upcurved smiling jawline. The flukes are a small dark blob. This is the Blue Whale drawing recoloured and shortened.
rows.fix: Give it a proper hard-edged falcate dorsal standing well clear of the back, and cut a distinct short beak with a melon crease and an upswept mouth line.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 100% and at 5-6x crops of head, dorsal, tail, plus a pixel scan of the silhouette (440x440 PNG; ink bbox x60-378, y178-261; body-only aspect ~4.2, which matches the packet's aspect:4 - proportion is NOT the problem). Verdict FAIL stands: all three must-reads fail and the asset reads as a generic teal fish. But two parts of the original claim are wrong and must not be fixed against.

CORRECTION 1 - the dorsal fin is NOT 'a faint grey smudge with no edges'. It is a hard-edged, fully filled slate-grey shape with a clean silhouette against the background, and it is placed correctly at ~59% back along the spine (x197-230 on a 60-318 body). The real defect is SHAPE and SCALE: it is a low, symmetric semicircular DOME - measured 33px wide by only 9px tall, sitting on a body 61px deep at that station, i.e. 15% of body depth where a dolphin's is 25-35%. It has no rearward rake, no pointed apex, and no concave trailing edge. It reads as a porpoise nub or a rounded hump, not a sickle. Fix = re-cut the shape (swept-back apex, concave trailing edge, taller), not 'add edges' or 'darken it'.

CORRECTION 2 - 'no beak or upcurved smiling jawline' is right about the beak but wrong that there is no jaw line at all. There IS a thin pale hairline mouth running from near the snout tip rearward and slightly DOWN, passing below the eye and dying out around mid-body. It reads as a fish gape/gill hairline because it droops instead of curving up, and because there is nothing for it to separate: the head is a pure linear taper from x116 down to a needle-sharp 1-2px point at x60, with zero melon bulge and zero rostrum step. So the head fails, but the fix is (a) add a domed melon over the forehead, (b) break the taper with a short stubby beak, (c) re-curve the existing mouth line upward into a smile - the line already exists and just has the wrong curvature.

MISSED BY THE ORIGINAL JUDGE, and it is the single loudest fish cue: THE TAIL. Must-read 3 is 'crescent tail flukes held horizontally'. What is drawn is a symmetric two-lobed VERTICAL caudal fin - lobes spreading up AND down about the body axis (span y200-233 at x376, centred on the axis at y~216) with the notch cut into the trailing edge. That is a homocercal fish tail. Nothing in the image indicates horizontal flukes. This must be re-cut as a wide, shallow horizontal crescent seen near-edge-on.

ALSO MISSED - a stray artefact: a small detached grey ellipse (~12x6 px, x103-115, y180-186) floats in the empty background roughly 10px ABOVE the forehead, completely unattached to the silhouette. The head's true top edge there is y191. It is almost certainly a blowhole primitive drawn off-body; at 100% it reads as a bubble or a rendering bug and should be re-anchored onto the melon or removed.

One more polish note: the pectoral is a plain dark ellipse tilted rear-down, hanging well past the belly line to y261 with no attachment or taper - blobby rather than a pointed flipper.

Net: dorsal = wrong shape (present, edged, mis-sculpted), head = no beak and no melon (mouth line present but drooping), tail = wrong axis entirely (fish caudal). Three of three must-reads missing. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a brown bear cub or a large rodent
rows.defect: This is the terrestrial quadruped loaf, not a pinniped. The fore-limbs are short stubby legs of the same length as the hind legs, tucked under a barrel body - the 'very long fore-flippers propping the chest up', which is the whole reason a fur seal looks different from a true seal, are absent, so the chest sits low instead of reared. The hind limbs end in stubby toed paws rather than rotated-forward flippers, and the ear flaps are tiny rounded knobs indistinguishable from a bear's ears. No flipper webbing anywhere.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG and then at 3x/6x/10x/12x/14x nearest-neighbour crops of the head, the fore limb, the hind limb and the rump. The FAIL verdict stands, but two of the stated causes are wrong and a third must-read failure was missed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS. A horizontal barrel: a pale tan cylinder about 2.3:1, capped by a rounded dome at the rear (x~110-150) and running dead flat from rump to shoulder with no arch, no lifted chest and no neck rise. It is covered in fine scratchy hatch marks that do read as coarse fur. Four limbs, all short pale cylinders of the SAME length (fore limb x~250-310, hind limb x~110-175, both roughly 45px from belly line to ground while the body is ~95px deep) - the belly sits barely above the feet. A small dark-brown head (headFrac looks right, ~0.18) is held at body level, its jaw actually BELOW the topline, tucked against the shoulder.

MUST-READ 1, 'very long fore-flippers propping the chest up' - GENUINELY ABSENT, and this is the identity killer. The judge is right. The fore limb is a stubby column identical in length, thickness and colour to the hind; there is no elongated humerus/forearm, no forward-and-down flipper sweep, and consequently no propped chest. The whole point of an otariid stance - trunk lifted clear of the ground on long front flippers, rump rotated forward - is nowhere in the drawing.

MUST-READ 2, 'small external ear flaps' - the judge's description is WRONG though the failure is real. There are no 'bear-like knobs'. At 14x the rear of the skull is a squared-off angular step: the top edge runs diagonally down-back to a corner, drops vertically, then cuts inward in a small rectangular notch before meeting the trunk. It is the same flat mid-brown as the rest of the skull, has no outline, no inner-ear shadow and no separation from the head mass - it reads as a seam/notch where the head plate is pasted onto the neck, not as a pinna. Whatever was intended, no ear is legible. Fixing this needs an actual small backward-raked cone standing off the skull with its own darker inner face, not a reshaped silhouette step.

MUST-READ 3, 'dog-like whiskered muzzle' - HALF present, and the judge did not mention it. The muzzle itself is decent: a blunt rounded snout with a dark nose blob at the tip, a curved smile line and a faint cheek crease, plus a large prominent white-ringed eye (the 'eyes: prominent' spec is met). But there is not a single whisker or whisker-spot anywhere on it. The vibrissae field is the cheapest fur-seal cue available and it is missing entirely.

CORRECTION to 'no limb reads as a flipper': not quite. At 12x each foot is a dark chocolate elongated paddle-shaped pad with fine parallel hatching (digit striations) that extends forward past the leg column - that IS a flipper-adjacent foot cue, and both fore and hind feet point forward, which is at least gesturally right for hind flippers rotated forward. The cue simply cannot register because it is a 25px pad hung under a short pale terrestrial leg; read it as 'the flipper cue exists only at the very bottom of the limb and is overwhelmed by the leg above it', not as 'absent'.

COLOUR, unmentioned by either party: the value split is inverted from the real animal. Here the trunk is pale tan and the head plus all four feet are dark brown. A fur seal is a dark trunk with a paler grizzled mane over the NECK AND SHOULDERS. As drawn, the pale mass reads as a body-covering pelt on a land animal.

WHAT IT READS AS: the judge says 'brown bear cub or large rodent'; I would sharpen that to a wombat or a capybara - low flat-topped barrel, stumpy equal legs, small dark head carried at body height. Either way it is a terrestrial quadruped loaf, not a pinniped. FAIL upheld. The fix priority is the limb model, not the ear: lengthen and re-angle the fore limb into a true flipper, raise the shoulder and chest off the ground, and lift the head onto a visible neck - then add whiskers and a standing ear cone.

rows.readsAs: a dolphin - it is the Dolphin card at a different length
rows.defect: Both identity must-reads are gone. The topline is a perfectly smooth arc with no row of knuckle bumps between mid-back and tail, and the skin is a clean unbroken teal-to-grey gradient with no barnacle crust, no lice patches, no mottling at all. The rostrum is a sleek point rather than a narrow arched bowed jaw. Nothing distinguishes this from the toothed whales in the batch.
rows.fix: Serrate the rear third of the topline with 6-8 knuckle bumps and paint irregular white barnacle clusters and pale lice blotches across the head and back.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by decoding the PNG and re-rendering the body bbox at 4x and 8x (whole, dorsal strip, head, tail). The FAIL stands, and all THREE mustReads fail — not two.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a single smooth lens-shaped cetacean body, 379x101px bbox (aspect ~3.75 including the flipper; body-only ~4.2). Mint-green forward half blending to slate-grey aft in one linear two-stop gradient. One thin pale rim-light runs the length of the dorsal edge. Head is a straight tapering wedge with a dead-straight hairline mouth slit. One large glossy black eye-bead with a white catchlight. One dark ellipse pectoral flipper set low behind the head. No dorsal fin (correct). Peduncle pinches to a point into a plain bowtie fluke with a single V-notch and smooth trailing edges.

CLAIM 1 — knuckle row absent: CONFIRMED. At 8x on the dorsal strip the topline is one uninterrupted C-curve from rostrum tip to fluke insertion. Zero bumps, zero scallops, not even a rendered-but-too-small attempt. The caudal peduncle — where the gray whale's 8-14 knuckles actually live, aft of the dorsal hump — is a clean straight taper. So the feature is not merely faint or drawn somewhere the first judge did not look; it was never drawn.

CLAIM 2 — barnacle/lice crusting absent: CONFIRMED. The fill is a pure linear gradient with no stipple, no clusters, no patch shapes, no value noise anywhere on the flank, rostrum or jaw. Gray whale identity is carried mostly by that crusting; without it the skin reads as a generic smooth delphinid.

CLAIM 3 — the chassis line: PARTLY WRONG, correct it before fixing. (a) It is most exactly the BELUGA chassis, not the Dolphin's — Beluga.png is the same silhouette part-for-part (same humped-back wedge head, same low pectoral ellipse, same bowtie flukes, same glossy eye bead, and the same two stray marks described below), differing only in colour ramp (cream vs mint-slate). The Dolphin is the same family template but carries a dorsal fin and a slimmer body. (b) 'at a different length' is inaccurate: Gray Whale bbox 379x101 = aspect 3.75, Dolphin 318x83 = aspect 3.83. It is the SAME proportion scaled up ~19%, not a re-lengthened body.

DEFECT THE FIRST JUDGE MISSED — mustRead 3, 'narrow arched rostrum with a slightly bowed jawline', is also absent. The rostrum is a symmetric straight-edged wedge and the jawline is a perfectly straight thin stroke with no bow or arch at all.

TWO MORE DEFECTS WORTH FIXING IN THE SAME PASS: (1) A long thin light-grey arc is drawn from in front of the rostrum tip, up over the head and back along the dorsal edge — its front third floats DETACHED in the background, outside the silhouette, over open water. It is a misregistered stroke, not anatomy. (2) The blowhole is a small grey ellipse also drawn floating clear of the body, above and forward of the topline, sitting on the background rather than on the skin. Both stray marks appear identically on Beluga.png, confirming a shared-template bug rather than a one-off.

SECONDARY: spec aspect is 5.5, drawn ~3.75-4.2 — too stubby for a gray whale. Spec eyes are 'small'; the drawn eye is a large high-gloss bead with a catchlight, reading dolphin-cute.

rows.readsAs: a humpback whale

But the tail flukes are a tiny dark stub at the far left, far too small for the body and with a clean straight trailing edge instead of the scalloped one; and a second dark wavy shape overlaps the dorsal hump and runs down past the flipper root with no readable origin, so it looks like a stray stroke rather than the far-side flipper.

rows.readsAs: a manatee

But the front flipper is only a vague grey lobe merged into the head shading - it never separates from the body - and the split upper lip is not readable at this size. The torso carries the same eight vertical bands as the Dugong, which read as segmentation on a mammal.

rows.readsAs: a narwhal
rows.defect: Strongest card in the batch - the long spiralled tusk and the dorsal-free back both read instantly. Two misses: the body is a smooth pale sage-green gradient with no mottling at all, where mottled grey is a stated must-read; and the tusk exits dead centre from the tip of the snout like a swordfish bill, exactly the error the packet note warns against - it should leave the LEFT upper jaw, offset from the midline.
