rows.readsAs: a black leaf or a lens-shaped blob
rows.defect: The render is broken. The body is a dark crescent that tapers to a hairline at the right and simply stops - there are NO tail flukes at all. The tall triangular dorsal fin, the single most recognisable silhouette in the ocean, is a 10px dark triangle barely clearing the back. The eye patch is a huge white oval sitting where an eyeball would be, so it reads as one enormous cartoon eye rather than a patch above and behind the real eye; the saddle is a soft grey ellipse in the wrong place; and the white underside is a thin sliver rather than a crisp bounded belly field. No pectoral paddles are visible.
rows.fix: Rebuild it: give the body a proper caudal peduncle ending in large horizontal flukes, raise the dorsal to a hard-edged triangle roughly a quarter of body length tall, and re-place the white eye patch as a small oval ABOVE and behind the eye with a crisp hard border against the black.
rows.verifyWhy:
VERDICT UPHELD, BUT THE STATED CAUSE IS WRONG IN THREE OF FOUR PARTICULARS AND THE REAL DEFECT IS A SINGLE FILL COLOUR, NOT MISSING GEOMETRY. What the delivered PNG shows to the naked eye matches the other judge: a black lens/leaf, a big white oval up front, a grey oval mid-back, a white ventral crescent, a faint dark bump on the spine, and a hairline running off to the right that ends in nothing. But I pulled the actual pixel values and re-mapped the 8-16 luminance band, and every 'missing' feature is DRAWN AND CORRECTLY SHAPED -- it is just painted in RGB(9,12,16) on a card background of RGB(6-8,9-11,15-17), i.e. a contrast ratio of roughly 1.1-1.3:1, which is sub-perceptual.

CORRECTION 1 -- 'NO tail flukes at all' is FALSE. Flukes are present and are a good silhouette: a broad blade spanning x=330-393, y=209-245 (63px wide, 36px tall) with a clean concave notch cut into the trailing edge. Fill RGB(9,12,16); background immediately above at (365,190) is RGB(7,11,17) and below at (365,265) is RGB(8,11,17). Luminance 11.5 vs 10.5 -- a one-level difference. They are invisible, not absent. Do NOT 'add flukes'; that would double them.

CORRECTION 2 -- 'the tall triangular dorsal is a ~10px stub' is FALSE. The dorsal is a full fin: apex at approx (217,154), base from x=198 to x=240 on the back line at y~190. That is ~36px tall against a body depth of ~55px at that station, and ~42px wide at the base -- proportionally a proper cetacean dorsal. Same RGB(9,12,16) fill. The ONLY reason any of it is perceptible is that it is very slightly DARKER than the radial glow behind the creature (11.5 vs 13.8-14.2 at (190,160)/(245,160)), so it shows as a shadowy notch in the glow -- and the glow only reaches the fin's lower third, which is why it looked like a 10px stub. The one shape criticism that does survive: the apex is ROUNDED and hump-like, not the crisp backswept triangle the mustRead asks for -- it reads closer to a dolphin's falcate fin than an orca's blade.

CORRECTION 3 -- 'the body tapers to a hairline and simply ends'. The hairline is real but it is not the body. It is the dorsal-ridge RIM-LIGHT stroke (1-2px, lum ~41 at (320,220)) which correctly runs along the top edge to the tail stock and terminates at x~335 exactly where the flukes begin. The body silhouette itself does not taper away -- it carries full depth through the peduncle into the flukes; it merely drops below visibility once the fill hits RGB(9,12,16) around x>250 (body is lum 33 at x=120, 32 at x=160, 28 at x=200, 20 at x=240, then 11.5). So there is also a value RAMP running head-to-tail that fades the animal out, on top of the flat-black appendage fill.

CORRECTION 4 -- the eye patch claim is HALF wrong. There is a white ellipse ~48x40px centred near (88,210), and there IS a separately drawn eye: a small dark pupil with a white catchlight at approx (72,232), below and forward of the patch, plus a third small pale dot at ~(90,178) above it (blowhole). So the patch is not 'sitting where an eyeball would be' -- the eyeball is drawn elsewhere. The judge's READ is nonetheless fair: the patch is roughly twice the size it should be, too circular (a real orca patch is a slanted oval about half this size set behind and above the eye), and because it is an empty white blob with the real eye a full patch-width away, it does dominate as a cartoon eye.

ALSO MISSED BY BOTH OF US: (a) the large rounded paddle pectoral IS drawn -- a paddle ~54x26px hanging below the belly from x=118-172, y=259-285 -- in the same invisible RGB(9,12,16). (b) The rostrum comes to a SHARP POINT at x~42; an orca head is a blunt conical melon with no beak, and the pointed tip is a large part of why the silhouette reads as a leaf/fish rather than a whale.

BAND: FAIL stands. Judged as delivered, two of three mustReads (tall triangular dorsal fin; large rounded paddle pectoral fins) are not readable at all and the tail is not readable, so the asset reads as a finless, tailless black leaf. Only the third mustRead partly lands, and weakly: the saddle is a mid-grey oval (lum 86) rather than the crisp white it should be, and the eye patch is oversized. THE FIX IS NOT MODELLING WORK -- the geometry is already correct and complete. Raise the appendage/limb fill from RGB(9,12,16) to at least the body value (RGB ~26,34,39) or brighter, kill the head-to-tail value ramp that fades the rear half into the background, sharpen the dorsal apex to a backswept point, blunt the rostrum, shrink the eye patch to a slanted oval sitting just behind and above the (already-drawn) eye, and brighten the saddle toward white.

rows.readsAs: an unlit dark blob whale - no species readable
rows.defect: The identity feature is absent: instead of the long low swept-back dorsal set well forward on the back there is a single tiny dark step on the topline about 45% along, with no length, no sweep and no visible edge. The pale anchor patch on the throat is nowhere on the card. The bulbous melon does not overhang the mouth - the forehead runs straight into the snout. On top of that the near-black body sits on a near-black field so the silhouette barely separates from the background at all.
rows.fix: Draw the dorsal as a long low fin whose base spans a fifth of the back at 35% body length, swept back to a rounded tip, and add the pale anchor-shaped throat patch; lift the body value a step so it separates from the field.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two of the three stated causes are described wrong and the real defects are elsewhere. I read the 440x440 PNG at native size, then at 2x/6x/8x nearest-neighbour zooms on the head, dorsal region and throat, and I sampled raw pixel values.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A short, fat, tadpole-shaped cetacean facing left. Big rounded dome head with an eye (dark dot + white catchlight) low and forward, a thin curved mouth line, one white ellipse high on the melon (blowhole/specular), a single short blunt oval pectoral at the shoulder, a tapering body, and a small weakly-notched fluke pair. A bright white rim-light stroke runs the whole dorsal edge from the melon to the peduncle.

CORRECTION 1 - THE DORSAL FIN IS NOT 'a single tiny step with no length or sweep'. Geometry is present and is roughly the right SHAPE: at 8x there is a distinct low broad triangular fin, base spanning source x=196..236 (~40px) and rising ~15px above the topline, i.e. about 2.5:1 length-to-height, apex forward of mid-base with a long shallow swept-back trailing edge. That is a credible long-low-swept-back fin. The reason it reads as only a notch is COLOUR, not form: the fin is filled RGB(13,15,20) while the sky immediately above it is RGB(10,16,22). Luminance delta is under 1/255 - the fin is literally invisible. All a viewer perceives is the abrupt step where the rim-light topline breaks and resumes lower/right. So the fix is fill value and a rim-light carried up the fin's leading edge, NOT redrawing the fin's outline.

CORRECTION 2 - PLACEMENT IS WRONG IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, and the judge did not catch it. The mustRead says 'set well forward on the back'. Nose is at x~50, fluke notch at x~330; the fin's centre is x~216, i.e. ~59-61% of body length - mid-to-AFT, not forward. A pilot whale's dorsal sits near 1/3. So even if it were made visible it would still be in the wrong place.

CORRECTION 3 - 'near-black body on a near-black field barely separates' is too strong for the BODY and understated for the APPENDAGES. Body mass samples 30-42 luminance against a 5-16 background and carries a strong white rim light along the entire back; at true exposure the animal's mass reads perfectly well. What vanishes is every appendage that carries identity: dorsal fin (13,15,20), flukes (13,15,20), pectoral (~20). Those are painted at background value. Restate the defect as 'appendages are painted at background value', not 'the whole asset is too dark'.

CONFIRMED - ANCHOR THROAT PATCH ABSENT. Throat/chin samples (36,38,46) are indistinguishable from flank/belly (32,34,42); the slight brightness there is the diffuse lighting gradient, not a marking. There is no discrete pale shape anywhere on the ventral surface. The only light-valued marks on the whole asset are the eye catchlight and the blowhole ellipse. Correct call.

MOSTLY CONFIRMED - MELON. There IS a faint overhang the judge overlooked: the mouth line's anterior end sits a few pixels behind the forward-most point of the head and the lower jaw recedes below it. But it is a few pixels on a smooth continuous convex arc, with no distinct bulging melon boss and no undercut; it reads as a generic blunt whale/fish head. The must-read does not land.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT NEITHER JUDGE NAMED - ASPECT. Spec says aspect 4.5. Measured bounding box of everything above background luminance is 275x122 = 2.25; including the near-invisible flukes it is ~340x142 = ~2.4. The animal is roughly HALF as long as it should be, which is why the overall silhouette reads as a stubby porpoise/tadpole rather than a long-bodied blackfish. Also the pectoral is a short blunt oval where a pilot whale's is long, sickle-shaped and sharply pointed.

BAND. Two of three must-reads do not read at all (dorsal fin invisible AND mis-sited aft; anchor patch absent), the third is marginal, and the aspect is off by 2x. This does not read as a pilot whale. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a small dark fish or a young dolphin
rows.defect: The blunt beakless head and the stocky short body are genuinely there, so the porpoise-vs-dolphin call is half won. The other half is not: the small low triangular dorsal fin is a faint grey nub with no triangle to it, indistinguishable from the smudge used on the Dolphin and Blue Whale cards, so the fin shape that separates porpoise from dolphin carries no information.
rows.fix: Replace the smudge with a small hard-edged equilateral triangle sitting low on the mid-back, wide at the base and blunt at the tip.

rows.readsAs: a plain grey whale-shaped lozenge, same chassis as Gray Whale and Porpoise
rows.defect: The enormously arched jawline that should occupy a third of the body is completely absent - there is no mouth line drawn anywhere, just a smoothly rounded nose, so the defining bow-shaped jaw never appears. The crusty white callosity patches on the head are also missing; the only white on the card is the single blowhole speck shared with every other cetacean here. The dorsal-free broad back is correct but it is the only must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Cut a deep strongly arched mouth line running a third of the body length with the lower lip bowing up over it, and stipple rough white callosity patches on the rostrum, above the eye and along the lower jaw.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but TWO of the three stated causes are factually wrong and would send a fixer to the wrong place. Measured on the 440x440 PNG (opaque bg 5,6,12; ink bbox x62-376, y107-323).

CORRECTION 1 - 'No mouth line is drawn at all' is FALSE. A mouth line IS drawn. Traced by local-minimum scan it runs from x=74,y=242 (snout tip, just under and forward of the eye) back to x=132,y=257, where it disappears behind the flipper ellipse; a faint continuation is visible as a darker band inside the flipper at x=136-172, y=253-257. It is a ~3px hairline at luminance ~56-59 against body ~80-82 - only a 23-level dip, which is why it vanishes at thumbnail scale and why the previous judge missed it. So the defect is NOT absence. The defect is (a) CONTRAST - the line is too faint to read; (b) LENGTH - visible span 74->132 = 58px against a body length of ~247px (snout x=68 to peduncle pinch x=315), i.e. ~23%, short of the required third; and above all (c) SHAPE - it is essentially STRAIGHT. Sampled y at x=76/100/128 is 242/249/255: a monotonic ~15px droop over a 56px run with zero curvature. There is no bow, no rising rictus, no plunging front corner. It reads as a generic dolphin/manatee mouth slit. The must-read 'enormously arched jawline' is therefore genuinely absent as an ARCH even though a line exists. Fix = re-curve and thicken this existing stroke, do not add a new one.

CORRECTION 2 - 'the white callosity patches are missing' is HALF wrong. Exactly one white callosity IS drawn: an 8x5px light blob at x107-115, y159-163 (the only >125-luminance cluster on the whole asset apart from the 4px eye specular at x88-91,y222-224 and the 1px-wide back rim-light run at x184-219). The bug is that it is drawn OFF THE ANIMAL. At y=160 the body silhouette does not begin until x=120; the blob occupies x=108-114, i.e. it sits entirely in the background with a ~6px gap of pure bg between it and the whale.

NEW DEFECT the previous judge did not name, and the likely root cause of Correction 2: there is a DETACHED FLOATING STROKE arcing over the head. A ~4px light-grey stroke (RGB ~100,108,119) runs from about (65,215) up over the crown to ~(175,145), where it finally merges with the back's rim-light. Over its whole front half it is separated from the silhouette by clean background: row y=185 stroke at x82-85, bg at 86-91, body from 92; row y=200 stroke at x72-75, bg at 76-80, body from 81; row y=210 stroke at x66-69, bg at 70-75, body from 76. So the head's dorsal-ridge/callosity stroke has been laid on a curve offset ~5-6px outside the body path, carrying the sole callosity blob with it. At full size it reads as a stray wire or hair hovering over the whale's head. This is the single highest-value fix: snap that ridge path to the silhouette and it both removes the artefact and puts the bonnet callosity back on the rostrum.

WHAT ACTUALLY LANDS: must-read 3 is fully correct - the back is smooth and completely dorsal-fin-free, with a clean unbroken dorsal profile peaking around x=157 and tapering to a narrow peduncle (column height only 6px at x=312) into a small forked fluke (x322-376). The eye is small, dark, low and set forward just above the mouth corner, which is right for the species. So the judge's 'only the dorsal-free back lands' is a fair summary of the outcome even though the reasoning is wrong.

OTHER PROPORTION MISS: packet asks aspect 3. Measured body is ~247 long by ~127 deep excluding the flipper (~142 including it) = roughly 1.75-1.95:1. The animal is nearly twice as deep as specified - a fat lozenge rather than a long rotund whale. headFrac is closer: the implied head (snout to flipper/mouth end, 68->132) is ~26% against the specified 0.28.

BAND: FAIL stands. Of three must-reads only the dorsal-free back is readable. The identity-defining feature - the enormous bowed jawline over a third of the body - is present only as a faint straight scratch, and the callosity that would confirm the species is rendered in the background rather than on the head. Nothing in the image says Right Whale; a viewer would read it as a generic blunt-headed cetacean.

rows.readsAs: a tan dachshund or a stubby otter standing on four short dog legs
rows.defect: There are no flippers anywhere. The fore-limbs are short cylindrical dog legs ending in small rounded paw pads planted flat on the ground, not long paddle fore-flippers lifting the chest clear; the hind limbs are matching dog legs, not rotated-forward hind flippers. The body is a shallow level sausage with a nub tail. The one thing that could carry the identity, the small external ear flap, is drawn as an ambiguous angular wedge behind the cheek that is identical to the shape on the true Seal, so it separates nothing. Muzzle and eye are generic cartoon-dog. Nothing in the silhouette says marine.
rows.fix: Replace all four legs with pinniped flippers: broad flat elongated fore-flippers angled back from a high shoulder and propping the chest and neck up off the ground at a steep angle, and short rotated-forward hind flippers with visible splayed digit tips under the rear — then give the head a small but clearly separate pointed ear cone standing off the skull.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4-6x zoom on head, limbs and full silhouette, and side-by-side against Seal.png from the same packet. The FAIL stands, but one of the stated causes is factually wrong and must not be fixed as described.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A long tan cylinder body (fur-textured with dry shaggy stroke marks, not sleek wet hide) on four SHORT limbs of equal length. Darker brown blunt muzzle with a dark oval nose, a big cartoon eye with a white ring, and a smiling mouth line. Behind the skull sits an angular wedge with two sawtooth step-notches on its rear edge. A blunt darker cap closes the rump at the far left; no tail.

CORRECTION 1 — 'rounded paw pads planted flat' is WRONG. Each of the four limbs ends in an ELONGATED dark-brown flattened oval carrying faint parallel digit striations, angled forward and downward, i.e. a small webbed/flipper-ish pad, not a round dog paw. The rear pair's pad even points forward under the body, which is a partial hit on the note's 'hind flippers rotated forward'. The defect is scale and the limb above the pad, not the pad shape: the pad is roughly one-eighth the limb length and sits on the end of a short cylindrical dog leg with a hock bend, so the flipper reading is destroyed by everything above it. A fix that replaces the pads with rounder shapes would make this worse.

CORRECTION 2 — the wedge is not literally identical to the Seal's, but the judge's conclusion is right and if anything understated. Sea Lion's wedge has two step-notches; Seal.png's has one deeper single notch. Same part, same place on the skull, same size, same colour on both. Since the Seal's own mustRead is 'no external ear flaps', this wedge is not merely non-discriminating, it is actively wrong on the sibling asset — and it does not read as a pinna in either case; it reads as a crest or a chunk of jagged ruff at the back of the head.

MUST-READS. (a) 'small external ear flaps' — MISS as an identity cue, per above. (b) 'long fore-flippers lifting the chest clear of the ground' — MISS outright. The forelimb is the same short length as the hind, there is no broad flipper blade, and the belly hangs at the same height as the tops of the legs, so the chest is not lifted at all; the topline is flat and low. This is the defining sea-lion cue and it is absent. (c) 'blunt dog-like whiskered muzzle' — HALF. The blunt dog muzzle is genuinely present and readable; whiskers are entirely absent (no vibrissae strokes, no whisker dots on the muzzle).

SHARED CHASSIS. Confirmed against Seal.png: identical body cylinder, identical head-and-wedge assembly, identical four short legs with the same striated oval pads, differing only in hue (tan vs grey) and a slightly lower crouch. The two assets that most need to be told apart are one chassis in two colours.

The judge's 'tan dachshund' summary is a fair read of the silhouette; add that the shaggy dry fur texture pushes it further from a pinniped, which should be smooth and wet-looking.

Band: FAIL. Two of three must-reads absent, the identity-defining one (chest lifted clear on long fore-flippers) entirely so, and the asset is not separable from its sibling Seal.

rows.readsAs: a grey dachshund or a grey otter-dog on four legs
rows.defect: It is the Sea Lion asset recoloured grey — identical topline, identical body depth, identical four stumpy legs at identical attachment points, identical paw pads, identical skull and nose. A true seal cannot stand on four limbs at all, yet this one is propped up on four of them with the belly clear of the ground, which is precisely the error the reference note calls out. The hind limbs point down and are planted as feet instead of trailing straight back as a joined flipper pair, there is no smooth torpedo taper, and the same angular flap sits behind the cheek where a true seal must show a bare earless head.
rows.fix: Redraw it belly-down on the ground with the whole body a smooth torpedo taper, the hind flippers fused and trailing straight back off the tail end as one splayed paddle, the fore-flippers as short paddles tucked low against the ribs, and delete the ear flap entirely so the skull is a clean round earless dome.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and I tried hard to break it. I read the PNG at full size, then cropped and 6-14x upscaled the head, muzzle, occiput, forelimb and rear end, and ran a pixel silhouette diff of Seal.png against Sea_Lion.png.

WHAT THE ASSET ACTUALLY IS: a grey, long parallel-sided furred loaf standing on FOUR separate planted limbs, two under the shoulder and two under the hip, each ending in a small grey paddle-shaped foot with digit striations pressed flat on the ground. There is a clear elliptical cast shadow and an unambiguous air gap between the belly and the ground along the whole trunk. Posture spec says 'sprawling'; what is drawn is a standing quadruped. This is precisely the failure mode the note names: 'drawing it propped up on rotated hind flippers makes it a sea lion.'

SILHOUETTE DIFF (hard evidence for the 'recoloured Sea Lion' charge): thresholded masks of the two PNGs overlap 21,038 px of Seal's 24,091 lit px (87%), and the diff image is nothing but a thin outline halo. Same trunk, same topline, same four limb positions, same limb form, same foot, same head shape, same face-on eye with white sclera ring, same nose blob, same mouth crease. Seal is ~4% larger with a marginally larger head. The judge's core claim is confirmed: this is the Sea Lion chassis in grey. Note also that the packet gives Sea Lion aspect 2.4 and Seal aspect 3, yet the two render at effectively the same proportions, so the aspect spec is not differentiating them either.

MUST-READ BY MUST-READ:
1. 'smooth torpedo body with no external ear flaps' - FAILS twice. The trunk is a constant-width loaf, blunt-capped at BOTH ends, with zero taper toward either the head or the tail. And on the back of the skull, above and BEHIND the eye, there is a hard flat-topped wedge that sweeps back to a sharp point and then has a small square notch cut into its trailing edge - a distinct protruding appendage that juts outside the head's rounded outline. It is pixel-for-pixel the same shape carried by Sea_Lion.png, where it is the ear flap. CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM: the judge called it a 'cheek flap'; it is not on the cheek, it is the occiput/crown region, high and rearward. The substance stands - an earless head has a protruding pointed flap on it.
2. 'hind flippers trailing straight back, unable to fold under the body' - FAILS. The hind limbs are rotated forward and downward under the hip and are planted. Nothing trails back. CORRECTION/ADDITION: the judge said only that there is no fused rear paddle. True, but what IS drawn at the rear is worse than nothing - a short truncated grey CYLINDER stub projects backward from the upper rear of the body, capped with a flat elliptical cut face, reading as a docked/amputated tail. That stub is the thing occupying the space the fused hind-flipper paddle should own, and any fix must delete it, not just add flippers.
3. 'round dog-like head with large dark eyes and whiskers' - PARTIAL, mostly fails. The large dark eye with a bright catchlight and white ring is present and readable (the one must-read element that lands). But the skull is not round: it is a hard-edged pentagon/wedge with a straight sloping occipital facet. And whiskers are ABSENT - at 14x the muzzle shows only a dark oval nose, one curved mouth line, and a short dark jaw crease bar running back from under the nose. No whisker array, no whisker spots.

NOTHING in the judge's verdict is refutable. Zero of three must-reads read correctly; the organism reads as a stubby grey quadruped mammal on planted paddle feet, i.e. the Sea Lion, which is the exact confusion the reference row exists to prevent. FIX ORDER: (a) drop the belly to the ground and delete the two hind standing limbs; (b) delete the rear cylinder tail stub and replace it with a fused rearward paddle; (c) taper the trunk toward both ends; (d) delete the occipital wedge and round the skull; (e) add whiskers; (f) the front limbs should become long fore-flippers laid alongside the chest, not columns.

rows.readsAs: a generic small whale — a pilot whale or a dugong
rows.defect: The head is a soft rounded nose cone occupying maybe a sixth of the body and blending seamlessly into the back; the enormous square blunt head that IS the sperm whale, taking a third of the length and ending in a flat vertical wall, is absent. There is no narrow underslung toothed lower jaw — the mouth is a thin faint smiling line right at the nose tip with no separate slender jaw beneath the head mass. There is no knuckled dorsal hump; the back carries one soft low bump in the middle that reads as a rounded dorsal fin. No blowhole is visible at the front-left of the head. What remains is a smooth grey-green torpedo with one small pectoral and a fluke, i.e. the default cetacean shape.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front third as a tall flat-fronted rectangular block that is deeper than the trunk and ends in a vertical wall, hang a thin pencil-like lower jaw well below and behind that block so the jaw is obviously narrower than the head, replace the mid-back bump with a low triangular hump followed by three or four smaller knuckles running to the tail, and put a single blowhole notch at the top-left front corner of the block.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and would send a fixer to the wrong places. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured off the pixels, body bbox x=23..415, y=159..280; flukes start ~x=352, so the trunk is ~328x122 = aspect 2.7, 3.22 including flukes, against a target aspect of 4 — it is too stubby): a smooth generic cetacean chassis, side-on, swimming right-to-left with the head at the left. HEAD (must-read 1) — genuinely FAILS, but NOT because it is 'a sixth of the body'. The mouth line runs from the snout tip at x=23 back to roughly x=140, i.e. about a third of the trunk, so the head MASS fraction is close to the required 0.33. The defect is purely SHAPE: the leading edge is a single smooth convex arc (tip y=220 at x=23, rising to the dorsal crest y=159 by x=103) — a rounded nose cone / melon. There is no flat vertical front face, no squared box, no straight-cut brow. Fix the profile, not the length. LOWER JAW (must-read 2) — FAILS, and it is not merely 'a faint smile line at the nose tip': there IS a long scribed mouth line running the full length of the head from the tip back to the pectoral flipper. What is missing is the geometry — the ventral silhouette below that line is the full body wall, not a separate slender rod-like jaw hanging under an overhanging head, and there are no teeth. It reads as a mouth drawn on, not a jaw built. DORSAL (must-read 3) — FAILS, and the judge's description is factually wrong. There is NO bump and NO dorsal fin anywhere. The top profile is strictly monotonic: flat crest at y=159 from x=103 to x=131 (rel 0.20-0.28, i.e. directly over the head/shoulder), then an unbroken descent to the tail (x=171 y=167, x=219 y=184, x=267 y=195, x=315 y=206). No knuckles, no triangular nub, nothing at the two-thirds mark where a sperm whale's hump belongs. (For contrast, the sibling Pilot_Whale.png DOES carry a small dorsal nub at ~x=200 — the sperm whale does not, so 'reads as a pilot whale' is true for the body but the judge imported the pilot whale's fin into this description.) BLOWHOLE — partially wrong to call it absent: there IS a small pale ellipse, ~9x8 px, RGB ~(177,189,183), centred near x=88 y=179, sitting high on the melon at rel 0.20 of body length. It may be intended as a blowhole, but it reads as a specular highlight, not a vent: it is near-white rather than a dark slit, it sits behind the melon rather than at the extreme front-left of the head, and the identical pale dot appears on Pilot_Whale.png and other cetaceans in this set, so it is a chassis default, not a sperm-whale feature. DECISIVE EVIDENCE — this is a SHARED CETACEAN CHASSIS, not a sperm whale. Sperm_Whale.png and Beluga.png occupy the identical vertical band (y=159..280, height 122 px to the pixel) and share the same rounded snout, same pale melon dot, same eye dot with catchlight, same low ovoid pectoral flipper at x=119..170, same notched fluke. Only colour and trunk width differ. Every one of the three must-reads that constitute sperm-whale identity is absent as drawn form. FIX ORDER: (1) rebuild the front third as a rectangular block with a near-vertical flat front face and a level flat top from the very tip; (2) hang a narrow underslung lower jaw as separate geometry beneath the overhanging head, with the head mass clearly wider/deeper than the jaw; (3) replace the smooth crest with a low triangular hump at ~0.6-0.7 of body length followed by three or four knuckles down the caudal peduncle; (4) move the blowhole to the extreme front-left top of the snout and render it dark; (5) stretch the trunk toward aspect 4.

rows.readsAs: a walrus — but only because of the tusks; the body alone is a pink dachshund
rows.defect: The tusks read and carry the name, so a stranger will say walrus. Everything else is the shared pinniped chassis recoloured pink: the same level topline, the same shallow sausage torso with no blubber mass, no wrinkling and no rolls, and the same four short cylindrical dog legs on rounded paw pads rather than short broad flippers. The dense bristle moustache is not there — only a couple of thin hairline strokes at the muzzle, so the squared muzzle reads as a dog nose with two teeth stuck on it. The tusks also emerge from the side of the cheek rather than descending from under a heavy overhanging upper lip.
rows.fix: Swap the four dog legs for short broad flippers and inflate the torso into a heavy sagging blubber mass with visible neck and shoulder wrinkle folds, then thicken the muzzle into a bulbous overhanging bristle pad — a dense stippled block of whiskers — with the tusks dropping from beneath it.

rows.readsAs: a kangaroo
rows.defect: The upright macropod silhouette, ears and muzzle land, but two of the three must-reads are not visible: the tiny forearms are absent entirely — the chest is an unbroken slab with no arm shape held against it — and the hind leg is one soft undifferentiated blob with no deep-folded thigh-over-shank, so the 'massive muscular hind leg' never reads. The long foot is a flat dark plank projecting to the right that does not visibly attach to the leg above it and reads as a board the animal is standing on.
rows.fix: Build the hind limb as a visible zig-zag — heavy pear thigh, narrow shank folded back, then a long foot hinged off the shank's base — and add two short forearms with paws tucked against the upper chest.

rows.readsAs: a koala
rows.defect: Ears and the big black spoon nose are present and the trunk is there, but the koala has no limbs at all — it is a fur ball pasted in FRONT of the log with nothing gripping it; the two pale smudges on the chest do not resolve into arms and no hands or feet wrap the trunk's edges, so 'gripping a vertical trunk' fails. The coat is rendered as a halo of straight white spikes that reads as thistle or frost rather than plush fur, and the eyes are large white googly discs rather than the specified small beady ones.
rows.fix: Draw two forelimbs crossing the trunk with visible clawed hands hooked over its near edge and one hind foot braced below, and shorten the fur spikes into a soft dense fringe.

rows.readsAs: a lamb or a small sheep
rows.defect: Wrong organism. It is the shared barrel-bodied lamb chassis: fleecy off-white body, four long straight columnar legs ending in dark cloven-looking hooves, a small rounded head with tiny round ears and a soft muzzle. Every must-read is missing or inverted — the tail is a short, thin, FURRED grey hook, not a long naked scaly prehensile rat tail; there is no pointed white face and no pink nose (the face is dark grey and blunt); and the coat is smooth fleece, not grizzled shaggy guard hair, with no thin bare ears.
rows.fix: Replace the whole chassis with a low crouching short-legged body and draw the identity feature first — a long bare pink-grey scaly tail as long as the body — then a sharply pointed white face with a pink nose tip and thin naked black ears.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and would send the fix in the wrong direction. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, zoomed 4x-14x on head, ear, tail, feet): a lamb. Deep cream/white barrel torso filled with short painterly wool flicks, level topline, tall straight column legs (front pair and rear pair both near-vertical, no crouch, no arch), standing on four dark grey blunt end-pads each split by two faint vertical toe lines. CORRECTION 1 - the tail is NOT 'furred'. It is a completely flat, untextured, uniform-width grey-tan tube (solid fill, visibly different rendering from the flick-textured body), arcing up off the rump then down with a blunt rounded tip - a pig/dog curl. It has neither fur strokes NOR scale rings. It measures roughly 55px of arc against ~180px of body length, i.e. ~30% of head+body where the Virginia opossum's is ~100%, and it does not taper at all from base to tip. The fix is therefore not 'de-fur it': it needs to be 2-3x longer, strongly tapered base-to-tip, trailing/drooping rather than curled up, pale pink-grey, and carrying the ringed scale texture. Score against the packet's three must-reads: naked scaly rat-like prehensile tail = ABSENT; pointed white face with pink nose = ABSENT; grizzled grey shaggy coat and thin bare ears = ABSENT on both halves. rows.readsAs: a small white lamb standing on the ground

MUST-READ 2, huge black eyes with dark facial stripe to the nose: THE JUDGE IS PARTLY WRONG HERE - do not fix what is already present. There IS a large dark eye mass on the cheek, and it is disproportionately big for the skull. The animal is: one curved tail capsule with a dark inner stripe (x=71..185), one fat spotted trunk ellipse (x=185..290, top ~y=175, underside ~y=250), a row of ~8 solid triangular spikes bolted along the mid-back topline (x=195..300, peaks up to y=149), a separate head ellipse butted straight onto the front of the trunk with no neck (x=290..368, max depth ~58px), and four plain capsule limbs.

Its only features are one hairline straight mouth slit running the lower third and a round white eye with a black vertical slit pupil. Column scan across the head (x=326..366) shows top edge 177,177,178,178,180,181,184,189,195 and bottom edge 235,234,234,232,230,228,224,219,212 — it tapers SYMMETRICALLY toward the snout, which is the signature of an ellipse, not a wedge. CORRECTION 1 — 'small' is WRONG. The head is 77px long on a 297px animal, headFrac approx 0.26 against the spec's 0.30, and 58px deep against a 75px trunk depth. It is the second-largest mass in the render and is close to spec scale. The defect is purely GEOMETRY (round ellipse instead of blunt wedge), not size. Do not fix this by enlarging the head — enlarging a smooth oval makes it read more chibi, not more agama.

CORRECTION 2 — 'a belly that sits on the shadow' is WRONG, and this is the one half of must-read 3 the render actually satisfies. Measured: the trunk underside bottoms out at y approx 250; the lowest foot tips reach y=276 (columns x=181..186 and x=311..321). That is a 26px air gap, about 35% of the trunk's 75px depth, and the cast shadow ellipse sits below the limb tips, not against the belly. The belly IS held clear of the ground. What fails in must-read 3 is the SPRAWL and the feet, not the clearance.

CORRECTION 3 — 'two cones' undercounts. There are FOUR limbs: a near foreleg (x approx 300-325), a near hindleg (x approx 155-200), a paler far-side foreleg tucked behind the head/trunk junction at upper right, and a darker far-side hindleg plate at x approx 148-190. 'Toeless' is exactly right — every one of them terminates in a plain rounded cap with zero foot, ankle or digits. 'Jointless' is right for the foreleg (a single straight tapered capsule, verified at 12x) but slightly overstated for the hindleg, which is two overlapping capsules with a faint angle break; it still reads as a bent peg rather than an articulated knee and ankle, and because there is no foot plate the limb never turns out laterally, so the sprawl does not read — the render says 'four pegs under a body', not 'elbows and knees out to the sides'.

CONFIRMED — the shared-chassis charge. Opened Skink.png side by side: same head ellipse, same hairline mouth slit, same white-ring vertical-slit eye at the same place, same tail capsule with the same dark internal stripe, same capsule limbs, same spot scatter. Agama differs only by hue (blue vs brown), a somewhat deeper/rounder trunk, marginally longer limbs, and the bolt-on spike row. One chassis, two paint jobs.

Also worth recording for the fix: the spike row sits on the MID-BACK topline, not on the nape, so it does not do an agama nuchal crest's job either — combined with the round dark-slit eye and the featureless oval snout the whole thing reads as a generic chibi dragon, which matches the original claim.

MUST-READ 2 (tail about as long as the body) PASSES and the original judge did not credit it: tail runs x=71 to the hip at x approx 185 along a curve, versus a trunk of x=185..290 — roughly equal, arguably a touch longer once the curve is counted. That is the only clean must-read.

SCORE: 1 of 3 must-reads present, 1 (the primary identity feature) wholly absent, 1 half-present (clearance yes, sprawl and feet no). FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: rebuild the head as a broad blunt wedge — widest at a defined jaw hinge, tapering to a squared-off (not rounded) snout, with a visible jawline, a short thick neck separating it from the trunk, and a tympanum spot behind the eye. Give every limb a foot plate with three to five splayed toes, and break each limb at elbow/knee so the upper segment goes OUT laterally before the lower segment drops to the ground — the 26px belly clearance is already correct and should be preserved, not changed. Move the crest forward onto the nape if it is kept at all, and shrink the spikes so they read as scale keels rather than dragon horns.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (440x440 canvas; silhouette spans x=43..396, measured by alpha profile, then re-read at 5x-11x crops of head, jaw, feet and tail):

1. DEWLAP — PRESENT AND CORRECTLY PLACED. The judge's claim that the red teardrop hangs 'off the CORNER OF THE MOUTH' and reads 'unmistakably as a lolling tongue' is factually wrong about geometry. At 11x the red mass is a crescent / half-disc whose FLAT TOP EDGE follows the ventral outline of the jaw from x=325 to x=374, bulging down to y=249, with a curved fold crease drawn inside it. The mouth is a thin dark seam at y=209 running x=330..391; it is CLOSED, continuous, and unbroken, and there is a solid ~16px band of face-green (the lower jaw/chin) between the mouth seam and the top of the red. The red never touches the mouth line and does not taper to a tip out in front of the snout. It is a gular fan hanging under the throat — anatomically where an anole dewlap belongs. It is crude (a plain half-moon, no pointed ventral apex, no gular rod, and it sits under the mid-jaw rather than reaching back toward the chest), and at thumbnail size the wide horizontal mouth seam plus the red lobe below gives the face an accidental Kermit-smile read, which is probably what the first judge saw. But the must-read 'extendable coloured throat fan' IS carried. Fixing this feature means refining it, not relocating it.

2. TAIL — GENUINELY FAILS, and the judge's description is accurate. Boundaries from the height profile: tail tip x=43, tail/trunk junction ~x=172 (where the hind-limb mass appears and the trunk ovoid with the dark spots begins), neck constriction / head start ~x=318 (column height dips to 61-62 at x=295..300), snout tip x=396. So tail = 129px, trunk ovoid = 146px, head = 78px, head+body = 224px. Tail/(head+body) = 0.58. The must-read wants >1.0, i.e. the tail should be roughly 1.7-2x what is drawn. Worse, it is not tail-SHAPED: it holds ~39-41px of thickness from x=100 all the way to x=165 (over half the trunk's 70px depth) and only tapers in the final ~40px, so it reads as a fat club stuck on the back, not an anole whip.

3. TOE PADS — GENUINELY ABSENT, judge correct. At 8x the limbs are plain dark-green capsules that terminate in blunt rounded ends. There are no digits, no splay, no lamellae, no pad discs, nothing. Two near-side limbs are drawn (a single-capsule forelimb at x~330 and a two-segment zigzag hind limb at x~180-200) with a faint far-side hind limb behind it. Beyond having no toes, the limbs also fail the 'long slender' half of the must-read: the forelimb is a stubby ~30px capsule on a 354px animal and is as thick as it is proportionate to the trunk.

ALSO (not in the judge's claim, but the reference note is violated): the packet note asks for a 'pointed wedge head longer and narrower than a gecko's'. The head drawn is a fat, blunt, rounded ovoid with a rounded snout tip and no wedge taper at all — head depth stays near-maximal right up to x=375.

FAMILY CONTEXT: this is the same generic chassis the rest of the batch is on — rounded ovoid trunk with scattered blur-dots, capsule limbs, tapering tube tail, blunt ovoid skull. Nothing in the silhouette distinguishes it as an anole except the dewlap.

VERDICT: 1 of 3 must-reads readable, 2 absent — one of them (adhesive toe pads on long slender limbs) has literally no anatomy present to carry it. FAIL stands.

The broad splayed lamellae toes are absent entirely - the limbs are the standard toeless cones. The skin is drawn as the same smooth gradient with the same generic dark blobs as every sibling, so the granular bumpy texture never reads either.
rows.fix: Blow the eye up to fill most of the side of the head - a domed globe bulging past the skull silhouette, gold iris with a hard black vertical slit pupil and no eyelid - and fan the front foot into broad flat pads with visible lamellae ridges.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at Gecko.png at 1x, then at 3x full-body, 7x on the head and 12x on two leg tips, and measured the white-sclera bounding box on all six batch members programmatically. VERDICT UPHELD, but TWO PARTS OF THE STATED CAUSE ARE WRONG and must not be 'fixed'.

CORRECTION 1 (the claim is flatly wrong here): the eye is NOT 'a bare black dot with no iris, no vertical slit'. At 7x the eye is a clean pale near-white iris/sclera oval carrying a crisp, unmistakable VERTICAL black slit pupil, taller than it is wide, sitting mid-head. The vertical-pupil half of the must-read is DRAWN AND CORRECT. Do not touch it; any fix that 'adds a vertical pupil' would be re-doing work that is already right.

CORRECTION 2: 'the SMALLEST eye in the batch' is not quite true. Measured white-sclera bboxes across the batch: Wall Lizard 13x13 (78 px), Skink 13x12 (62 px), Agama 12x11 (61 px), Anole 11x10 (53 px), Gecko 10x9 (38 px), Whiptail 10x8 (32 px). The Gecko is second-smallest, marginally above Whiptail. The INVERSION CLAIM NONETHELESS STANDS AND IS THE CORE DEFECT: the only species in the batch spec'd eyes:prominent carries an eye smaller than FOUR of its five ordinary-eyed siblings, roughly half the sclera area of the Wall Lizard's. Relative to its own head the eye is ~10 px in a ~67 px head ellipse (~15% of head length); a gecko's eye is ~30-35% of head length. The judge's 'no bulge past the skull line' IS correct: the head is a perfectly smooth ellipse and the eye sits flush inside it with no orbital dome, no brow ridge, and no break in the dorsal outline. The head is also mostly empty — a large blank cream ellipse with one small eye and a single pencil-thin mouth line, which is what makes the eye read as under-scaled.

CONFIRMED AND STRONGER THAN STATED: splayed lamellae toes are not merely 'absent' — there are NO FEET AT ALL. At 12x, the front limb is a plain olive-grey capsule that terminates in a blunt rounded cap; the hind limb is a thigh blob ending in a rounded knob. Zero digits, zero pads, zero ankle, on all four limbs. Anole and Skink in the same batch at least carry a small angled foot form at the leg tip, so the Gecko is BELOW its siblings on the one foot feature it is supposed to lead the batch on.

CONFIRMED: skin is a flat smooth radial gradient with the identical blurred dark blob-spots the Anole and Skink carry in the same positions and sizes — no granulation, no tubercles, no surface break of any kind. It is the batch's shared spot vocabulary in a cream palette.

OMITTED BY THE ORIGINAL JUDGE (add to the fix list): (a) the tail. It IS plump, so the third must-read is half-satisfied — but it is drawn as a short thick hook that CURLS UP AND FORWARD OVER THE BACK, ending above the hips like a chameleon's or a possum's prehensile tail. No gecko carries its tail that way; it should extend rearward. (b) Silhouette proportion: measured body bbox is 242x110 = aspect 2.20 against the spec'd 3.0, because the curled tail eats the length. This is the squattest silhouette in the batch (Agama 2.35, Wall Lizard 3.01, Anole 3.34, Skink 3.41, Whiptail 4.04) despite the Gecko being spec'd longer than the Agama. (c) CHASSIS: this is the same body as its five siblings — one fat egg-shaped torso, four tapered stub limbs with no feet, one round head ellipse butted onto the torso with no neck and a single pencil mouth line, one tapered tail with a darker inner streak, the same blurred blobs. Gecko differs from Skink and Anole only in palette, tail length and tail curl.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS: a plump cream ovoid quadruped with a curled tail — closest to a fat newt/salamander or a shell-less tortoise. Nothing about the silhouette, the head, the feet or the surface says gecko; only the vertical pupil does, and it is too small to carry the identity alone. Two of three must-reads fail outright and the third is inverted, so FAIL is the correct band.

rows.readsAs: a small brown lizard-ish creature, though closer to a newt than a skink
rows.defect: This is the row the shared chassis accidentally suits best - elongate, short-legged, tapering tail - so it survives, but the must-reads are still not visible. The smooth glossy OVERLAPPING polished scales are absent: the surface is a flat matte gradient wearing the same generic dark speckles as the other five, with no scale rows and no specular sheen. The body is an egg with a wide fat waist rather than a near-uniform cylinder. The legs are the family cones with no foot, so the almost-limbless polished look never arrives.
rows.fix: Give the body a hard wet specular highlight running the length of the topline plus fine overlapping scale rows, and slim the trunk to an even cylinder from shoulder to hip.

rows.readsAs: an olive-drab newt, indistinguishable from the Skink render except for hue
rows.defect: Every one of the three must-reads is missing. The tail should be roughly TWICE the body length; on this render the tail is about the same length as the body ovoid, so the defining proportion of a lacertid is simply not there. The flattened slender body pressed to the surface is instead the family's deep fat egg, taller than it is thin, held up off the ground on stumps. The long splayed toes are absent - the two limbs are the standard featureless cones with no feet at all. Nothing in the silhouette separates it from the Skink beside it.
rows.fix: Double the tail length and whip-taper it to a hair point, flatten the trunk into a low wide slab hugging the ground plane, and add four sprawled feet with long spidery toes gripping outward.
rows.verifyWhy:
Measured the 440x440 PNG pixel-by-pixel (column silhouette profile) and inspected 6x/12x crops of both feet, the head and the tail. All three must-reads are absent; the FAIL stands, with two corrections to the stated causes.

WHAT IS THERE: the creature spans x=56..380 (325 px, drawn noticeably smaller in frame than the Skink's 393 px). Tail tip x=56; the tail/body junction is at x~194 (column height jumps 41 -> 48 there); the body oval runs x=194..313 (119 px long, 76 px deep at its maximum, x=246..258); the head oval runs x=313..380 (67 px long, 56 px deep). Four limbs hang below the body, and a cast ellipse shadow sits on the ground BELOW the belly with a clear gap.

1) TAIL PROPORTION - must-read 'tail roughly twice the body length' is FAILED, and the judge's description is close but slightly generous. Tail = 138 px horizontal (~145 px along its arc, it curls upward). Body oval = 119 px. So tail/body = 1.16x, not 2x. Measured the way lacertid proportion is normally quoted (tail vs snout-vent = head+body = 186 px) it is 0.74x - i.e. the tail is SHORTER than the animal in front of it. Even on the most generous reading of 'body' it needs to be ~238 px and it is 138. IMPORTANT ADDITIONAL FINDING the judge missed: I profiled the Skink in the same packet the same way - Skink tail 189 px vs body 124 px = 1.52x. So the Wall Lizard's tail is proportionally SHORTER than the Skink's, whose own must-read is only 'tail as long as the body'. The two species' tail proportions are inverted relative to their reference rows. A fix must roughly double this tail (target ~2x snout-vent, i.e. ~370 px at this scale) and taper it to a fine whip point; currently it is a thick near-uniform tube (41-43 px tall across x=110..192) that only pinches in the last ~25 px, and it carries the identical dark dorsal blotch-stripe the Skink's tail carries.

2) BODY FORM - must-read 'flattened slender body pressed to the surface' is FAILED exactly as claimed. The trunk is a deep egg: 76 px deep on a 119 px length, depth/length = 0.64. It is not flattened dorsoventrally and it is not slender. It is also held CLEAR of the ground - the shadow ellipse is a separate mass under the belly with visible dark gap between belly and shadow, so the animal reads as propped up on stumps, the opposite of a wall lizard plastered flat against stone. Extra defect the judge did not name: the tail emerges from the UPPER half of the body (tail base spans y~185..227 while the belly bottom is y=241), so the tail is attached above the hip line rather than continuing the ventral line - part of why the body reads as a detached egg with a tube stuck on it.

3) TOES - must-read 'long splayed toes' is FAILED. At 12x zoom on both the left hind limb and the right fore limb, each limb terminates in a plain rounded capsule end. There are no digits, no foot plate, no claws, no splay - zero toe geometry of any kind. CORRECTION to the claim's wording: the limbs are not all 'standard featureless cones'. The hind limb is actually a two-segment limb with a visible knee bend (thigh wedge + shank), the fore limb is a single tapered cylinder; both are featureless at the distal end, so the verdict is right but 'cones' understates that a limb articulation model IS present and only the foot/digits are missing. The fix is a foot, not a whole limb rebuild.

4) CHASSIS - the judge's 'nothing separates it from the Skink' is essentially correct and I confirmed it by measurement, not just by eye. Wall Lizard vs Skink: body 119x76 vs 124x75; head 67x56 vs 79x59; same blunt egg head with no neck taper and no pointed snout; same hairline horizontal mouth slit; same white sclera with vertical slit pupil (wrong for a diurnal round-pupilled lacertid, and identical to the Skink's); same soft brown speckle field over the flank; same thick curved tail with the same dark dorsal stripe; same four limbs at the same angles. The only silhouette differences are overall scale (325 vs 393 px), hue (olive-green vs brown), and a tail that is shorter - so the one silhouette distinction that does exist points the wrong way. This is one lizard chassis in two colours.

Nothing redeeming was found hiding at small scale. Band FAIL, upheld.

rows.readsAs: a long-tailed brown lizard, but not identifiably a whiptail
rows.defect: The long tail partly lands - it is the longest in the batch - but it is only about one and a half times the body rather than two to three times, and it is thick and club-like at the base with the same upward curl and internal dark stripe as every sibling, so it never reads as a thin whip. The slender pointed snout is absent; the head is the family rounded blob with a straight slit mouth. Most damaging, the pale longitudinal back stripes that are the whole diagnostic marking of a whiptail are missing and have been replaced by the same scattered dark spots the other five wear.
rows.fix: Paint four or five crisp pale stripes running unbroken from the neck to the hip in place of the spots, and redraw the tail as a thin straight whip two and a half times the body, needle-tapered and not curled.

rows.readsAs: a winged ant, or a small bee with an oversized head
rows.defect: The identity must-read is not merely missing, it is inverted: instead of a strongly humped thorax over a bowed head, the render is two grey spheres of near-equal size sitting level on the same centreline, and the HEAD sphere is the LARGER and no lower than the thorax. There is no bowed head, no shoulder hump, no dorsal arch at all. There is also no abdomen — the second sphere is followed immediately by the wing blob, so the 'stubby compact dark body' reads as two beads on a stick. Wings are a rayed white puff rather than short broad clear paddles. Worse, a long angular bracket of two straight thin lines meets at a vertex far off the right side of the animal, disconnected from any visible body part, plus a comb of short vertical black bars sits under the wing base — both read as stray wireframe fragments stranded outside the silhouette.
rows.fix: Rebuild the body as three parts, not two: shrink the head to roughly half the thorax and tuck it DOWN and forward so it is bowed under a thorax raised into a pronounced dorsal hump, then add a short stout abdomen behind the thorax so the wings mount on the thorax rather than terminating the body; and reattach or delete the stray angular line and the vertical bar comb.

rows.readsAs: a mosquito — the plumose antenna and long narrow wings carry it
rows.defect: The organism is nameable, but three of its must-reads are weak or absent. The proboscis is a short thin rod barely one head-diameter long and it is out-lengthed by the feathery antenna above it, so it does not read as a long forward-jutting needle. The six legs are short straight jointless stubs hanging only about one body-length down, not 'very long dangling legs', and the hind pair is not kicked up — the insect stands level and flat-footed above a shadow instead of hanging at an angle. Most damaging, the long tapered abdomen is entirely absent: the taupe body stops at the thorax ellipse and the wing fan takes over, so the mosquito has no slender tail to angle. Several straight vein lines also overshoot past the wing membrane into empty space on the right.
rows.fix: Add a long slender tapered abdomen behind the thorax, tilt the whole body nose-down about 25 degrees with the hind legs raised, and extend the proboscis to roughly twice the head length so it clearly outreaches the antennae.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon tadpole or a fat smiling grub/slug with two little peg legs — most strangers would say tadpole or caterpillar before amphibian.
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail, and the identity one is the worst. (1) The paddle tail is absent: instead of a tapering laterally flattened vertical blade, the tail is a thick blunt club that is wider than the trunk at its midpoint and ends in a rounded stump; behind it sits a semi-transparent brown lobe that does not connect to the tail outline and reads as ghosted/stray geometry, not as a fin. (2) Four small splayed limbs are not present: only two peg-stubs are legible, both crowded into the FRONT half (one under the head, one at mid-belly), so the rear third of the trunk and the entire tail base are limbless — no hind-limb pair at the pelvis at all. The pegs are featureless dark spikes with no splayed toes or foot pads. (3) The skin is a smooth glossy gradient with two soft airbrush highlights — no granular, warty or moist-bumped texture anywhere. Compounding it, the head is a separate oval visibly seamed onto the trunk with a constriction, giving a bowling-pin silhouette, and the single large cartoon eye plus curved smile push it further toward mascot than organism.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as the identity feature: from a tail base no wider than the trunk, taper to a point over a length equal to the body, and give it a tall vertical blade — a dorsal and ventral fin fringe rendered as a distinct laterally-compressed silhouette, with the ghost lobe deleted — then move the hind-limb pair back to the pelvis at the tail base and give all four limbs four splayed toes exiting the flank, not the belly.

rows.readsAs: a long silver pike or gar
rows.defect: The long straight body and the tooth row are there -- the teeth read as a row of white triangles along the lower jaw, which is the one genuinely species-specific mark in the batch -- but the two widely separated dorsal fins are rendered as two soft grey ghost-blobs that look like blur/shadow artefacts sitting BEHIND the body, not like fins; the jaw is not visibly underslung (upper and lower jaw meet in the same symmetrical point as every other fish here), and the tail is the shared triangular fan.
rows.fix: Draw the two dorsals as hard-edged opaque triangles on the topline with a clear gap between them, and step the lower jaw forward past the upper so the underbite is visible in silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a blue billfish, indistinguishable from the Sailfish and Swordfish in this same batch
rows.defect: The round spear bill is present and legible. The rigid pointed sickle dorsal is NOT -- what is on the back is a soft rounded dark-blue hump with no point and no hard edge, reading as a shadow. There are no cobalt vertical bars anywhere on the flank; the flank carries only the shared crosshatch scale patch. The tail is the shared soft triangular fan, not a stiff keeled crescent.
rows.fix: Replace the rounded hump with a hard-edged forward-peaked sickle whose tip rises above the topline, and paint 12-15 pale cobalt vertical bars down the flank.

rows.readsAs: a marlin -- the sail, which is the entire identity of the animal, is not there
rows.defect: The must-read is 'enormous sail dorsal taller than the body is deep, running most of the back'. What is rendered is a low rounded-triangular bump over roughly the front third of the back, perhaps a third of the body's depth in height, soft-edged and the same blurry blob used for every other fin in this batch. A sailfish without the sail is a marlin, and this image is a marlin. The thread-like pelvic fins are also absent -- nothing hangs below the belly.
rows.fix: Build the sail as a real hard-edged membrane running from just behind the head to near the tail, at least 1.3x the body depth in height, with visible ray struts; add two long thread pelvics trailing back from the belly.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as written. Measured on the 440x440 png with a per-column luminance segmentation (background lum 13, dorsal-fin membrane a flat plateau at lum 35, bright body lum 55-110). Fish faces RIGHT; bright body runs x=117 (caudal peduncle) to x=315 (snout), 198px long; max body depth 63px at x=192-213; bill x=315-367 (52px, 3-7px thick).

CORRECTION 1 - the sail is NOT absent. A dorsal fin IS drawn: a dark navy translucent dome sitting above the dorsal line from x=176 to x=287, peaking at y=154 where the body top is y=178. That is 111px of coverage on a 198px body = 56 percent of the back, and it is centred over the middle of the back, NOT 'the front third' as claimed. It also carries roughly eight vertical fin-ray strokes inside the membrane (visible at 6x on the dorsal crop), which the Marlin's dome does not have.

CORRECTION 2 - 'about a third of body depth' is close but slightly understated: the peak rise is 24px above the dorsal line against a 63px maximum body depth = 0.38x (0.41x of the local depth at that station). The mustRead demands a sail TALLER than the body is deep, i.e. >=63px and realistically 1.2-1.5x. The drawn fin is ~2.6x too short. THIS is the real defect, and it is a scale defect, not an omission: the fin needs its height multiplied roughly 3x and its leading edge pushed forward to start just behind the skull (x~300) so it runs the full back, and it needs a squared/high-shouldered membrane top with long rays rather than the current low elliptical arc.

CORRECT - the profile is a soft-edged rounded dome. The inkTop trace descends and re-ascends symmetrically (177,174,172,169,167,165,163,161,160,158,157,156,155,155,154,154,155,156,158,160,163,165,169,172,177,183,190,194) with no shoulder, no straight leading edge, and a heavy blur on the outer boundary. There is no crisp membrane outline anywhere.

CORRECT - thread-like pelvic fins are absent. Ink below the belly line maxes at 7px and only between x=175-205, which is a soft anal-fin bump; an extra-boosted 8x crop of the belly under the head and pectoral region (x=230-340, y=205-265) is completely empty. The dark ellipse at y~285 is the scene cast shadow, not a fin.

CORRECT - chassis-identical to the Marlin. Same measurement run on Marlin.png: dorsal dome x=171-291 (58 percent of a 207px body), peak rise 21px above a 58px body = 0.36x, peak at x=219-231. Sailfish: 24/63 = 0.38x, peak at x=222-228. The two arcs are the same curve within a few pixels. Both share the identical lens-shaped body outline, the same pale keel stroke around the silhouette, the same lateral-line stroke, the same triangular pectoral fan drawn flat on the flank, the same gill arc behind the eye, and the same low ventral bump. The only separators are the Sailfish's diamond scale texture and its dorsal ray strokes; the Marlin also lacks its own mustRead cobalt vertical bars, so neither the shared dome nor the shared body distinguishes them.

WHAT PASSES: the long thin spear bill is genuinely present and readable (52px on a 292px total length, ~18 percent, tapering, clearly separated from the head), so only one of the three mustReads is met. The identity feature - the sail - is drawn at roughly a third of the specified height on a fin silhouette shared with the Marlin, so the asset does not read as a Sailfish. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a mauve-purple marlin
rows.defect: The bill is the exact same thin round spike used on the Marlin -- the packet's own note says it must be flat and blade-like, not round -- and it is roughly a fifth of the total length, not a third. The tall stiff crescent dorsal is absent; the back carries the same soft dark lump as the marlin and sailfish. The body is also the shared crosshatched scale patch, which contradicts 'smooth scaleless body'. The mauve/purple colour reads as an alien fish rather than a swordfish's dark bronze-and-silver.
rows.fix: Widen and flatten the bill into a visible blade with parallel edges and lengthen it to a third of the total length, and drop the crosshatch scale texture so the body reads smooth.

rows.readsAs: a generic deep-bodied blue fish
rows.defect: The body is acceptably deep and spindle-like, but the two marks that make a tuna a tuna are both missing. There is no stiff crescent-moon tail on a narrow keeled stalk -- the tail is the same soft notched triangular fan the barracuda and wahoo get. There is no row of small yellow finlets between the second dorsal and the tail; the dorsal region is instead two vague dark humps of the same blurred blob type. Nothing on the fish is yellow.

rows.readsAs: a blue barracuda
rows.defect: This is the best of the six: the body is genuinely elongate and there ARE faint blue vertical bars on the flank, and the snout is drawn to a point. But the bars are so low in contrast against the blue body that they nearly vanish, the beak-like jaws are the same symmetrical taper as every other fish rather than a distinct long beak, there is no row of finlets running to the tail, and the head region is cluttered by two soft dark blobs (the dorsal and pectoral) that read as smudges rather than fins.
rows.fix: Raise the contrast of the vertical bars to clearly dark navy on a lighter flank and add the finlet row to a stiff forked tail.

rows.readsAs: a generic brown crested songbird or a small partridge
rows.defect: The two features that ARE a hoatzin's face are simply not drawn: there is no bare blue facial skin and no staring red eye — the face is the same plain brown as the body and the eye is the same tiny black bead used on the other three birds. The crest is present but is a small, thin, body-coloured fan of spikes rather than a tall shaggy rufous punk crest, and it reads as an incidental tuft. The 'heavy chest over a slim neck' is impossible to see because the chassis has no neck at all — the skull sits directly on the shoulder. The tail is a flat striped plank of slats, not a broad rounded feathered fan.
rows.fix: Paint a bare cobalt-blue mask over the whole face from bill base past the eye, drop a large red iris with a black pupil into it, and rebuild the crest as a tall ragged rufous spray twice the head's height.

rows.readsAs: a generic kingfisher-ish bird with an oversized yellow bill
rows.defect: The huge dagger bill is genuinely present and the body is correctly stocky and short-tailed, so the silhouette is in the right neighbourhood — but the head is uniformly dark grey-brown with no whitish crown and no dark brown eye stripe, so the single most recognisable head pattern is missing entirely. The bill is also seated too low on the face, hanging off the jawline rather than continuing the line of the forehead, which reads as a stuck-on beak. The head is not visibly oversized relative to the body; it is the same small round skull the other three birds use.
rows.fix: Repaint the head whitish-cream and lay a broad dark chocolate stripe from the bill base through the eye to the nape, then raise the bill so its upper edge continues the forehead line.

rows.readsAs: a green quail
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive. The tail is a short horizontal plank of green slats roughly the same length as the body and pointing straight back — nowhere near 'two streaming plumes far longer than the body', and nothing about it streams or hangs. The belly is the same green as the rest of the bird, so the crimson underside that gives the quetzal its contrast is completely absent. The crest is a tiny spiky green tuft, not a round bristly helmet. What is left is the identical partridge egg-body from the other three assets recoloured green, with the same beady eye, the same mid-belly straw legs and the same flank wing-lens.
rows.fix: Replace the tail plank with two ribbon-thin emerald streamers that trail two to three body-lengths down and behind, and paint the entire belly and undertail crimson.

rows.readsAs: a grey-brown quail or guineafowl chick
rows.defect: The forehead horn — the one feature the horned screamer is named for and the only thing separating it from any other dumpy grey bird — is entirely absent; the crown is bare and smoothly rounded. The bony wing spurs are also absent: the wing is the same dark-outlined feather lens used on the other three birds with nothing at the bend. The body is not goose-like or bulky, it is the family's standard small egg with a short dark wedge tail, and although the posture is called biped the legs are the same thin mid-belly straws as the flying birds, so there is no heavy standing waterfowl stance.
rows.fix: Add a long thin pale horn curving forward and up off the forehead, and put a visible sharp spur at the leading bend of the wing.

rows.readsAs: a quail or partridge chick
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The body is not carried high on long bare legs — the legs are two short yellow stubs barely clearing the belly, with the whole bird squatting on the ground shadow. There is no thick upright neck; the round head is welded directly onto the shoulder. The head is not flat-crowned and the bill is not short and stout — it is a domed skull with a thin pointed yellow dagger. Nothing in the silhouette says 'large terrestrial bird'.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette off the chassis: stilt the legs to roughly half total height as bare pale columns, lift the body into a horizontal barrel above them, and insert a thick vertical neck column between shoulder and a flat-crowned head with a short conical bill.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then re-read it at 3x (whole bird), 7x (head) and 8x (head/shoulder junction), and measured the silhouette in pixels. VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and the fix should be made against these measurements, not against their wording.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS. Ink bbox (shadow excluded) x99-335, y118-310: 236 wide x 192 tall. A near-spherical cream body ball (x~120-285, y~142-266 = 165w x 124h) with speckled/scalloped plumage and a big scapular wing arc drawn as a closed ellipse on the flank. A long grey pointed tail wedge sweeps back and DOWN to x335 at y238, with a fringe of fine black filament hatching under it. A round cream head ball (diameter ~52px) sits at the front-top. Two thin yellow legs and a shadow ellipse under the feet.

1. LEGS - claim is CORRECT in verdict, WRONG in description. They are not "short yellow stubs." They are anatomically complete bird legs: a bare yellow tibia leaving the belly, a clean backward-bending hock/ankle, a straight tarsus, and a flat foot with forward toes plus a long backward-pointing hind toe on the near foot. The defect is purely LENGTH. Yellow leg pixels run y267-309 = 42px of leg, against a body depth of 124px and a total figure height of 192px. So belly-to-ground is 34% of body depth and 22% of the whole animal - the body ball hangs a third of a body-depth off the floor. A bustard's must-read is the opposite: the tarsus alone should be near body-depth so the barrel rides high and clear, with a long open gap of daylight under it. Here the belly nearly grazes the shadow. Also worth noting the hind toe: bustards have three stout toes and no hallux, and one is drawn here.

2. NECK - claim is CORRECT and the 8x crop confirms it rather than refuting it. I specifically hunted for a neck that the first judge might have missed. There IS a neck, but it is a collar, not a column: a pale vertical band about 23px wide (roughly half a head-diameter, so the THICKNESS is right) and only about 7-10px of exposed height between the underside of the head ball and the shoulder line. Row scans show the silhouette is still head-only and 52px wide at y136, then jumps to 129px wide at y142 - i.e. the head merges into the body within ~24px of the crown, so the skull is half-sunk into the shoulder. Head-welded-to-shoulder is a fair summary. The missing must-read is neck LENGTH/CARRIAGE: a bustard needs a long thick upright column lifting the head well clear of the back line, giving the standing S-profile. Nothing here lifts the head; it rides on the shoulder.

3. SKULL AND BILL - half right, half wrong. The skull claim is CORRECT: the cranium is a mathematically clean circle with a fully domed crown and no flat table at all, which is the single loudest wrong signal in the image. The BILL claim is WRONG. It is not a "thin dagger." Measured, the yellow bill is x102-131 by y132-155 = 29px long by 23px deep, i.e. nearly as deep at the base as it is long, and only ~0.56 of head diameter - that is genuinely a short stout wedge and is close to the must-read already. It only reads sharp because it is a flat untextured triangle with a straight gape line running to a needle point; give it a blunter tip and a slight culmen curve and this element passes. Do not "shorten the dagger" - it is already short.

4. BODY MASS - not in the claim but it is the other half of why this fails. The must-read asks for a HEAVY HORIZONTAL body. What is drawn is a ball: 165w x 124h excluding the tail, and visually it reads as round because the widest rows (y196-238) are centered under the head rather than extending behind it. The horizontal reading in the aspect number comes from the tail wedge, not from the torso.

WHAT IT READS AS. Round ball body + head sunk on the shoulder + domed crown + short bare legs = a quail, partridge or gamebird chick. The first judge's "quail chick" is accurate. All three of the packet's must-reads (heavy horizontal body carried high on long bare legs; thick upright neck; flat-crowned head with short stout bill) are missing or unreadable except for the bill's stoutness, so FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a small crested diving waterbird — roughly right
rows.defect: The thin sharply pointed bill and the puffy rounded tailless rear both read correctly, and the crest is a nice touch. rows.readsAs: the Grebe asset recoloured black
rows.defect: The identity must-read — the checkerboard black-and-white back — is completely absent; the back is a flat unmarked dark grey with the generic wing-scallop arc on it. The dagger bill is not held level, it tilts noticeably upward, which is the grebe/anhinga cue and the opposite of a loon's carriage. The body is a short round egg sitting high rather than a long body riding low. Side by side with the Grebe it is visibly the same drawing with the brown swapped for black and the crest deleted.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, measured, not eyeballed): a dark charcoal sphere head at x148-195 carrying a small bright eye dot, a straight yellow dagger bill spanning x91-148, a smooth S-curved charcoal neck dropping to a rounded egg body at x195-355 / y182-272, two pale-blue water rings and a blue shadow ellipse under it. No feet and no tail are drawn, which is correct for posture=swimming and for the packet note about rear-set legs.

CORRECTION 1 - 'the mantle is flat unmarked grey' is FALSE. The mantle is NOT unmarked. Zoomed 6x on x195-360/y175-275 there is a real fleck texture: loose diagonal rows of small pale dashes across the upper mantle, a second field of pale dots on the lower flank, and a broad near-black diagonal band crossing the body that reads as a folded wing. The defect is not absence, it is that this is the WRONG marking at far too little contrast. Luminance over the mantle box (210,190)-(300,235): median 38.6/255, p95 63.8/255, max 114.6. The 'white' of the supposed checkerboard peaks at a mid-dark grey around 64/255 against a ground of 38 - roughly 25 levels of separation. A loon's identity mark is high-contrast WHITE squares in ordered rows on a BLACK back; what is here is unordered low-contrast grey speckle. The same box on Grebe.png returns median 67.8 / p95 124.7 - the identical texture, only brighter. So the fix is: replace the generic speckle with ordered square checks and drive fleck luminance to near-white (200+), not 'add markings to a blank back'.

CORRECTION 2 - 'the dagger bill tilts upward instead of level' is FALSE. I measured every yellow column of the bill. Centerline y = 147.0 at the tip (x=91) and 146.5 at the base (x=145); top edge 147->142, bottom edge 147->151, a symmetric even taper. The bill is dead level within half a pixel over its whole 58px length, straight, and evenly tapered. This is the ONE must-read the asset actually satisfies and it should be left alone.

CONFIRMED 3 - 'short high-riding egg, not a long low hull' is CORRECT. Full creature bbox 272 x 149 = aspect 1.83 against a spec aspect of 3.0. Body alone 161 x 91 = 1.77. The waterline rings cross at about y=258 while the body runs y182-272, so roughly 80 percent of the body height sits above the surface. It reads as a duck-shaped float, not a low submarine hull.

CONFIRMED 4 - 'it is visibly the Grebe asset with the brown swapped for black and the crest deleted' is CORRECT and now quantified. Thresholded non-background masks of Loon.png and Grebe.png over the full 440x440 frame give IoU = 0.918 (39,870 shared pixels, 1,350 loon-only, 2,192 grebe-only). Identical head sphere, identical neck S-curve, identical egg body, identical two-ring water and shadow ellipse, identical fleck texture generator. The whole delta is hue plus the Grebe's head tuft. Two of six members of this family are one chassis.

BAND: FAIL stands. Of three must-reads, the level dagger bill passes; the checkerboard black-and-white back is unreadable (present as grey speckle at ~10 percent of required contrast); the long low body is absent (1.83 vs 3.0, riding high). With the head also a plain sphere carrying no white collar or neck striping, nothing on this asset says loon - it reads as a generic dark waterfowl and, side by side with its own family batch, as a recolored Grebe.

rows.readsAs: a pale quail or a chunky dove

But the long pointed pin tail is only a short flat wedge that barely clears the rump, nowhere near the needle that defines the bird, and the legs are drawn as bare yellow scaly stubs rather than feathered down to the toes.

rows.readsAs: a crested quail

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and one is flatly incorrect.
