MUST-READ 1 - 'spray of erect bristly feathers at the base of the bill': PRESENT, and the judge's description of it is WRONG. It is not a 'small tidy tuft'. At 5x it is a fan of about six separate, splayed, spiky filaments with visible gaps between them, sweeping up and forward - i.e. genuinely a ragged bristle spray, and it is not small: roughly 30px tall x 35px wide against a skull only ~45px across. The real defect is ANCHOR POINT, not shape or size. The spray roots on the top of the crown at approx (150,138), which is up and slightly BEHIND the eye (eye centre approx (145,152)) and about 15px back from the bill base (approx (136,155)) - about a third of the skull length rearward. It reads as a cockatoo/quail crown crest. Seriema bristles spring from the forehead immediately at/above the cere, ahead of the eye. FIX = move the spray root forward to the bill base and lean it forward over the bill; do not redraw the filaments, they are correct.

MUST-READ 2 - 'very long red legs': ABSENT. Judge is right. Measured yellow-leg pixel span Seriema y266..317 = 51px against a 204px total silhouette height (25%); Bustard y267..309 = 42px of 192px (22%). So the Seriema legs are ~20% longer in absolute pixels than the Bustard's - a difference the judge missed - but that is nowhere near the required proportion; a seriema's bare tarsi are roughly half the standing height and the bird should look stilty and long-shanked. Colour sampled on the tarsus is ochre/mustard (approx R152 G124 B64 in shade, same ramp as the bill) - there is no red anywhere on the legs. The leg drawing is also the identical chassis part: same two-segment zigzag, same knee kink at the same relative height, same three-toe splayed foot with the same rearward spur, same fill colour as the Bustard.

MUST-READ 3 - 'long trailing tail': ABSENT. Judge is right and precise. The tail is the same short dark wedge as the Bustard's - a solid triangle projecting only ~40px past the rump with the same fan of thin dark undertail hatch-lines beneath it. Overlaid, the two tails are the same shape at the same angle. Nothing trails; a seriema's tail should be long, broad and carried down/behind, adding real length to the silhouette.

CORRECTION to 'remove the tuft and this is the Bustard image': not literally true. Two other head parts do differ. The Seriema's bill is a short, deep, downcurved wedge with a hooked feel (correct for a seriema), where the Bustard's is a long straight yellow dagger. The Seriema eye is noticeably larger with a bright white catchlight, matching its 'prominent' eye spec against the Bustard's 'normal'. Everything BELOW the neck, however, is one chassis: identical egg body, identical scapular/wing oval with the same dark outline sweep, identical topline, identical rump, identical tail wedge, identical legs and feet, identical ground shadow ellipse. So the family-chassis charge stands for the body, and the head is the only place any species differentiation happened.

Net: 1 of 3 must-reads readable (and mispositioned), 2 of 3 - the two that carry the seriema's whole stilty, long-tailed gestalt - missing. The asset reads as a crested bustard/quail. FAIL.

rows.readsAs: a white pigeon standing on the ground

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 5-6x nearest-neighbour crops of the head (55,120,130x100), the tail (200,200,240x120) and the feet (120,240,140x80). The FAIL stands, and the two identity must-reads really are absent, but several of the stated causes need correcting.

POSTURE (claim correct): spec says posture: flying. The asset is a standing biped. The feet crop shows two amber-yellow legs dropping vertically from the belly onto a hard horizontal plane, each ending in a splayed three-toe foot with the toes drawn flat and side-on as if gripping ground, and a large dark elliptical drop-shadow pooled under the body. The judge said 'one broad half-length tail wedge'; the finer truth is that there are TWO overlapping flat planes back there, not one - a white slab with five dark barb/quill hatch marks ruled across it, and a plain mid-grey wedge sitting behind and slightly above it that terminates earlier. Neither is a ribbon: both are wide flat blades roughly 12-14 px thick at the base tapering to a blunt square-cut tip, i.e. wing/tail-fan geometry, not filaments. Measured on the source image the body runs about x=105 to x=270 (~165 px) and the tail tip reaches about x=390, so the tail is ~120 px, roughly 0.7x body length - short of even 1x, and nowhere near the 2x the row demands. The bill is the right colour (saturated amber-yellow) but the wrong form: a very long, very thin needle/dagger roughly 55 px long and only ~10 px deep at the base, tapering to a hair point. That is a tern/sandpiper bill, not the short deep stout bill the row asks for.

CORRECTION to 'folded wings' and to 'reads as a white pigeon': the wing is not cleanly folded - what is drawn on the flank is an open mid-grey ARC/HOOP, a crescent ring that floats over the body outline and does not close into a wing shape, plus a separate white scallop-textured shoulder plate above it. And with the long thin needle bill the animal does NOT read as a pigeon (pigeons have short stubby bills); it reads as a generic white gull/tern/shorebird chick standing on sand. FIX DIRECTION: rebuild in flight posture (wings spread, no ground plane, no drop shadow, no standing legs - feet tucked or trailing), add the pair of hair-thin ribbon streamers issuing from the tail centre and running at least the full body length again beyond the current tail, add the black wedge stripe sweeping back through and behind the eye, shorten and deepen the bill into a stout coral-red/yellow dagger, and delete the grey flank hoop and the loose hatch marks.

rows.readsAs: A starfish
rows.defect: It is the Starfish asset in pink: five THICK tapering arms with rounded tips radiating from a broad central disc, arms only about two disc-widths long. The must-read snaky whip arms — thin, flexible, many times longer than the disc and clearly set off from it — are entirely absent; the reference note names this exact failure ('not the thick tapering arms of a starfish') and the render is that.

rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and the real defect is worse than described. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN (440x440 canvas; I decoded the PNG, cropped and upscaled the body 3x and the hub 8x, and pixel-measured every row): a single flat five-pointed star in coppery salmon, body bbox 208x170 (it fills only ~47% of the frame), one arm pointing straight up, two lateral arms out and slightly up, two arms angled down; a soft cast-shadow ellipse under it; a pale rim-light tracing the entire silhouette; scattered soft round pale spots over the surface with one larger pale blob just up-left of centre (reads as starfish tubercles/papulae plus a madreporite). CORRECTION 1 - 'thick tapering arms' is wrong. The arms are moderately SLIM and near-PARALLEL-SIDED over their outer half: the top arm holds a constant 12px width from y=147 to y=183 before flaring to 24px at the base; the left arm at 8x zoom is a straight constant-width finger with a fully hemispherical blunt tip. Arm width is only ~0.2-0.3 of the hub width. So the arm CROSS-SECTION is not the failure; whoever fixes this must not merely thin the arms, that part is already close. CORRECTION 2 - 'broad central disc' is wrong, and the truth is more damning: THERE IS NO CENTRAL DISC AT ALL. At 8x the hub is a plain pentagon formed by the five arm bases merging into one another with concave interradial curves; there is no disc outline, no rim, no boundary line, no change of value or texture where arm meets body. The mustRead demands a tiny disc with the arms 'clearly set off from it' - the asset has zero demarcation, which is the absence of the part, not a mis-sized part. CORRECTION 3 - 'arms only two disc-widths long' is generous. Measured, the hub spans ~60-85px (rows y=225-249 give 85, 64, 58, 56, 60) while arm length from base to tip is ~72px (top), ~75-90px (lateral), ~54px (lower). That is roughly ONE hub-width per arm, not two. Against a mustRead of 'many times longer than the disc is wide' the asset is off by something like 5-8x. ALSO ABSENT, and unmentioned by the first judge: no arm segmentation or annulation (brittle-star arms are visibly jointed rings), no lateral spine fringe, and no snaky posture - all five arms are straight rigid rays in near-perfect radial symmetry, whereas the whole point of Ophiuroidea is flexible arms that curl and lash. Nothing readable as brittle-star identity is present anywhere in the image, small or hidden. FIX DIRECTION: shrink the hub to a small distinctly-outlined pentagonal/round disc, break the join so each arm springs off the disc edge as a separate part, and extend the arms to at least 4-6 disc-widths with segment banding and a couple of arms curled rather than straight.

rows.readsAs: A grub or slug sitting in a shallow dish

rows.readsAs: A jellyfish with rainbow stripes painted on it

rows.readsAs: An earthworm
rows.defect: The ringed segmented tube is right, but the swollen clitellum saddle is nowhere on the body — the tube is a uniform diameter end to end, so the front-third band that identifies an earthworm is missing. Against that, there is a black eye dot on the snout, which the reference explicitly forbids ('no limbs, eyes or head features'), and it is the same eye dot reused on the Flatworm and Leech.

rows.readsAs: An earthworm in grey
rows.defect: This is the Earthworm asset recoloured — the identical S-curve, identical ring count, identical lifted head with one black eye dot. Every must-read is contradicted: the body is a ROUND SEGMENTED tube where a planarian must be paper-flat and unsegmented; there is no arrowhead triangular head, no pair of cross-eyed spots, and no auricle lobes at the head corners.
rows.fix: Throw out the worm tube and draw a flat ribbon seen from above — a triangular arrowhead front with a pointed auricle lobe at each corner, two dark cross-eyed spots set inboard on the head, and smooth unsegmented flanks tapering to a blunt tail.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by rendering the PNG, then re-cropping the body at 4x and the head at 6x, and by pixel-diffing against Earthworm.png from the same batch. UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a fully ROUND, cylindrically shaded tube in charcoal grey, laid in the same three-crest S-wave as the Earthworm (nose low-left, arch up over centre, dip, second arch, tail curling down-right), sitting on the same soft elliptical drop shadow. The tube is covered end to end in overlapping annular rings with a bright specular rib running along the top of each — the classic earthworm annulus routine. Scanline groove counts confirm the same generator: ring pitch is 6-8 px on BOTH assets and per-scanline groove counts land within 1-3 of each other. The head is a smooth EGG-SHAPED BULB, wider than the neck, terminating in a continuous convex curve with no taper and no apex. It carries ONE glossy black eye dot with a white specular highlight, set high on the left cheek — a vertebrate-style eye, not a pigment cup.

CORRECTION 1 — it is NOT a pure recolour. Silhouette IoU against Earthworm is ~0.75, not ~1.0. The Flatworm's head bulb is markedly LARGER and rounder (the packet's headFrac 0.16 vs Earthworm's 0.03 was in fact honoured), the body tube is a touch thicker, and the whole figure is a few px bigger (bbox x106-333/y171-263 vs Earthworm x112-327/y175-262). So the sculpt was parameterised, not copy-pasted — but every parameter that was moved is the WRONG one. The chassis, the pose, the ring routine, the shading model and the eye are shared verbatim, so the judge's substantive point stands: this reads as an earthworm, and specifically as a big-headed grey earthworm.

CORRECTION 2 — 'same ring count' is approximate, not exact; the Flatworm's rings are marginally broader and there are 1-3 fewer across a given scanline. Do not chase that number in a fix; it is not the defect.

MUST-READS, checked one by one at zoom:
1. 'arrowhead triangular head with two cross-eyed spots' — ABSENT on both halves. I looked specifically for a small second spot or a faint paired pigment cup at 6x: there is exactly one eye, it is glossy black with a highlight, and the head outline is a rounded ovoid with zero triangular taper. Not present-but-small; genuinely not drawn.
2. 'ribbon-flat unsegmented body' — ABSENT and actively contradicted. The body is round in section (top specular rib, dark underside rolloff) and is the single most heavily SEGMENTED surface in the whole asset. This is the loudest failure: a planarian's defining read is an unbroken, matte, paper-flat sheet.
3. 'ear-like auricle lobes at the head corners' — ABSENT. The head-bulb edge at 6x is one continuous convex curve; there is not even a bump where the auricles belong.

Zero of three must-reads read. The organism on screen is an annelid. FAIL is correct.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs a different silhouette generator, not a retint. Flat ribbon body with a parallel-sided outline and a soft rounded tail, matte unshaded top surface with NO annular rings and no specular rib; head widened into a triangular arrowhead with two pointed auricle lobes at the rear corners; two small matte black crescent eyespots set close together and angled inward (cross-eyed) on the dorsal surface, not one glossy sphere on the cheek. Keep aspect ~4 but read it as a flat gliding ribbon, not a coiled tube.

rows.readsAs: A white sea anemone
rows.defect: It is the Sea Anemone asset with the colour drained out: same squat truncated cone, same rimmed mouth opening, same crown of blunt finger tentacles splaying sideways. The identity must-read — the BLOOD-RED feathery plume — is absent; the plume is the same bone-white as the tube, so there is no red anywhere in the image. The tube is also a short wide cone rather than a tall white chitin tube, and there is no cluster: one column stands alone.
rows.fix: Make the tube tall and narrow (3-4x taller than wide) with two or three shorter tubes behind it, and paint the plume deep blood-red with fine feathery barbs so it contrasts hard against the white tube.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, and the judge's core reading is literally correct — I could not refute any of it. What I saw at full size, then at 4x/8x crops of the crown, rim and base, then under a gamma-0.32 lift to hunt for anything faint: a single squat vase-shaped cone with a bright elliptical rim, from which ~14-16 smooth, cylindrical, blunt-tipped, UNBRANCHED tentacles splay up and outward, several curling over at the tips. The column flares slightly at the rim and again at a flat pedal-disc bottom that sits on a cast-shadow ellipse. This is an anemone, unambiguously.

CORROBORATION THE JUDGE DID NOT CITE, which makes the 'Sea Anemone chassis' phrasing exact rather than rhetorical: Sea_Anemone.png in the same folder is the SAME artwork — same silhouette, same pose, same tentacle count and splay, same rim, same flared cone, same shadow — only recoloured. Sea_Anemone measures 86.61% strongly-red pixels; Giant_Tube_Worm measures 0.00%. The asset is the anemone chassis with the hue removed. The red the tube worm needs is sitting on the anemone.

MUST-READ 1 — 'tall white chitin tube standing upright in a cluster': FAILS on both counts. Silhouette bbox is 180 x 165 px, aspect w/h = 1.09, against packet aspect 0.25 (should be ~4x taller than wide) — off by ~4.4x. The tube column proper is only ~110 px tall by 55-75 px wide, and it is a flared cone (widest at rim and at base, narrowest mid-column), not a straight chitin cylinder. Horizontal scanlines through every row of the column return exactly ONE filled run, and the gamma lift revealed no second tube anywhere in the frame — so 'standing alone' is confirmed; there is no cluster, not even a faint background one. (The only other mark is one dim pale lump low on the column's left, which reads as painterly mottling, not a neighbouring tube.)

MUST-READ 2 — 'blood-red feathery plume protruding from the tube top': ABSENT, and absent in FORM as well as colour, which the judge understated. Colour: zero pixels in the entire image satisfy r>g+30 and r>b+30; mean foreground is 167,167,162 (neutral grey-white); only 3.5% of pixels are even mildly warm. Form: not one tentacle is pinnate, branched, barbed or filamentous — they are smooth tapering fingers. Even recoloured red this crown would still not read as a feathery branchial plume.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM (a): 'the plume is the same bone-white as the tube' is very slightly imprecise. The crown is a warm cream/ivory (dominant buckets 216,216,192 and 216,192,192) against a cooler grey-green tube (dominant 216,216,216 / 192,192,192 / 144,144,144). There IS a faint warm/cool separation between crown and tube — it is just nowhere near red, and far too subtle to register at thumbnail size. The judge's conclusion stands; the fix must add saturated red, not merely raise contrast between the two parts.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM (b): 'rimmed mouth' is the one piece I would restate. There is no painted mouth aperture. At 8x the rim is a bright specular ellipse and the disc inside it is the SAME pale value as the tube; the two dark slots the judge read as a mouth are background showing through the gaps BETWEEN tentacle bases, not a drawn opening. It still fails must-read 3 ('no mouth, gut or eyes at all') because the rim-plus-dark-slots reads as an open oral disc at a glance — but a fix that paints out a 'mouth' will find nothing there to paint out; what has to go is the flared anemone oral-disc rim itself.

WHAT THE FIX NEEDS: not a recolour of this chassis. It needs a new form — a tall narrow near-parallel-sided chitin tube (aspect ~0.25) with 2-3 shorter companion tubes behind it to make the cluster, capped by a compact BLOOD-RED plume of fine branched/pinnate filaments emerging from the tube mouth, with the tube lip drawn as a thin chitin edge rather than a flared oral disc.

rows.readsAs: A jellyfish
rows.defect: Reads immediately and correctly — domed bell, a long curtain of trailing tentacles dominating the height, and short pale frilled oral arms under the bell centre. Minor: the bell is fairly opaque grey rather than truly translucent, and the oral arms are short enough to be easy to miss.

rows.readsAs: An earthworm in olive-green
rows.defect: The Earthworm chassis again, third recolour: same S-curve, same ring count, same blunt lifted head. The body is a round tube, not a flattened ribbon, and there is no inchworm looping arch; it lies in the same flat serpentine as the other two worms.

FAIL upheld, and the chassis charge is confirmed by direct comparison — but one part of the stated cause is wrong and must not be fixed as written.

Same lazy horizontal S-curve (head low at left, dip, hump right-of-centre, descend to a tail at far right), same ~22 coarse overlapping annular rings, same bulbous ovoid head cap at the left, same soft ellipse ground shadow, same footprint: subject bounding boxes are Leech [117,180 -> 326,254], Earthworm [114,176 -> 326,260], Flatworm [111,172 -> 331,258] — agreeing within ~5px on all four edges in a 440px frame. The ONLY per-species differentiation across the three is hue (olive / pink / grey) plus the presence of a small black eye dot on Earthworm and Flatworm, which Leech omits. It reads as 'earthworm, olive', not as a leech.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Facing right. A near-spherical trunk with a second, smaller sphere fused to its front as the head, no neck. Two upright ears. One eye. Four straight whisker strands. Two ivory rectangular incisors. Two dark stub limbs. One thick smooth hooked tail arcing up over the back to the left. The only muzzle cue is a ~5px grey wedge nose pad appliqued at the tip of that arc where the whiskers attach. Measured from the eye, the face carries roughly 12-14 px of forward extension on a ~65 px head ball, i.e. essentially none. A tree shrew's defining feature is a long, narrow, forward-projecting pointed rostrum, longer and finer than a squirrel's; there is no rostrum here at all.

1. "blunt flat face" is wrong in shape. The face is not flat — it is a rounded convex dome that tapers slightly forward to the nose pad. The defect is that the taper is a ball's own curvature rather than an added snout, not that the face is a flat plane. A fix that only 'unflattens' the face will not produce a snout.
2. "big rounded ears" is wrong. The ears are two TALL, NARROW, UPRIGHT TRIANGULAR ears with pointed tips and pink-tan inner surfaces, rising well clear of the skull like a rabbit's or a chinchilla's. They are the single loudest wrong-organism signal in the drawing and they push the read toward lagomorph/chinchilla, not away from it. A real tree shrew has small, low, thin, rounded, close-set ears. Any fix must SHRINK and ROUND these ears, which is the opposite of what "big rounded ears" would suggest to someone reading only the claim.
3. "feet are invisible stubs" overstates invisibility. Two dark-brown limbs ARE plainly visible against the navy background below the belly: a hind limb at roughly x=180-215 ending in a rounded paddle/flipper foot pointing forward, and a much smaller forelimb peg at roughly x=245 that ends in nothing at all. The real defects are (a) zero digits, zero toe separation, zero claws on either; (b) only one limb per pair reads — the far side pair is entirely absent; (c) the forelimb is set too far back under the mid-belly and is half the size of the hind, so the animal has no shoulder; (d) both limbs are so dark they nearly merge with the ground shadow ellipse.

CLAIMS I CONFIRMED AS STATED. The buck teeth are real and are exactly as described: two ivory rectangular slabs with a vertical split, hanging below and in front of the nose. This is a rodent incisor appliqué; tree shrews are not rodents and have no such visible incisors, so this feature actively asserts the wrong clade. The body is a sphere: I measured the full silhouette bounding box at 217 x 150 px (aspect 1.45 including the tail), and the trunk alone at roughly 110 x 105 px — a circle — against the required 2.2 slim low form. Head fraction measures ~0.37 of body length against the specified 0.28, so the head is oversized as well. The tail is a smooth-edged thick club with a soft rounded tip and a lighter interior lozenge highlight; its outline has no fur strands, no serration, no silhouette break-up whatsoever. One partial credit the claim did not give it: the tail's arc length (~165 px) is roughly body-length, so "as long as the body" is approximately met — it is only the "bushy" half of that must-read that fails.

NET READ. Ball body + ball head + tall pointed ears + buck incisors + smooth clubbed tail + toeless stubs = a generic chunky rodent. Chinchilla is the closest single match, as the original judge said; a fat cartoon squirrel is equally close. Guinea pig is the weakest of their guesses since guinea pigs are tailless. Nothing in the silhouette would let a viewer arrive at tree shrew. FAIL is correct.

FIX PRIORITY. (1) Build an actual rostrum: a narrow tapering cone projecting forward from the skull, roughly 35-40% of head length, with the nose pad at its tip and the eye set back behind it. (2) Delete the rodent incisors entirely. (3) Shrink the ears to small low rounded flaps set close to the skull. (4) Stretch the trunk to the 2.2 aspect and drop the belly line so the body is long and low, not spherical. (5) Give four limbs with separated digits and visible claws, forelimb under the shoulder. (6) Break the tail outline with fur strands along its whole length.

I cropped and 6x-upscaled the head, belly/legs and rump of Wild_Sheep.png and did the identical crops on Tahr.png (same batch, row 1) to test the hue-swap allegation directly. The ring is of near-uniform slender width (~8px against a ~90px skull), it never tapers, it sits ON TOP of the skull as a hoop rather than sweeping down and around BESIDE the head, and it does not spiral (a spiral advances outward and downward across turns; this is a single flat closed loop that returns to its own start). 'Massive spiralling horns curling beside the head' therefore fails, but it fails as 'wrong horn architecture', not as 'no horn'.

Critically, the Tahr's horn is ALSO the ribbed ring, same radius, same anchor point, same annuli. My initial hope that the ribbing differentiated the sheep was wrong. The two assets differ only in hue (Tahr warm brown, Sheep cream) and nothing else. Same body, same leg placement, same hoof, same shadow ellipse. This is one chassis painted twice.

COAT — THE JUDGE DESCRIBED THIS INCORRECTLY. It is NOT 'a fluffy cream fleece'. There are no curls, no crimp, no woolly clumping anywhere. What is drawn is the TAHR'S LONG SHAGGY-HAIR OVERLAY, recolored cream and extended across the whole trunk: long diagonal straggling strands over the flank, a fringe of long hanging locks dangling clear of the belly line, and a spiky bristle fringe along the dorsal and rump silhouette. The fix is to strip/shorten the long-strand overlay to a short close-lying coarse pelt; there is no fleece to remove.

BODY — JUDGE CORRECT. Shallow barrel, flat topline, no chest depth, no shoulder mass, no brisket, on four straight thin near-columnar legs with a wide open gap under the belly. 'Muscular blocky body on sturdy legs' fails.

(2) The haunch shows a hard-edged flat quadrilateral plate with a visible straight seam cutting across the hip — raw chassis polygon showing through the paint, a construction artifact, also present on the Tahr. That detail is real and should be preserved through any rebuild.

NET: all three must-reads fail, the organism reads as a pale goat/domestic-sheep and is pixel-for-pixel the Tahr chassis in a different hue. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a cabbage — and it is Alpine Sorrel's cabbage in a different hue

On its own terms it also misses everything: the clump of LONG-STALKED oblong, arrow-based basal leaves is drawn as six giant stalkless round discs, the stem is olive-green not reddish, and the dense rose-pink papery seed spire is a thin orange bead column narrower than the stem it sits on.
rows.fix: Redraw from scratch as a loose clump of long red petioles each carrying a narrow oblong blade with an arrow-shaped base, and fatten the seed spire into a dense rose-pink column of overlapping papery discs.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and the fix should be made against this description instead.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440). A single fused dome of ~7 overlapping round discs, symmetrical about a centre notch: four discs fanning back-to-front down the left lobe, three on the right with the frontmost carrying a midrib plus a pinnate side-vein rake. The discs are khaki-olive (leaf-body mean RGB 118,130,83) with a pale specular highlight top-left of each. One dark olive stem, ~4 px wide, runs from the notch straight up through the dome and emerges above it carrying a column of ~7 discrete round coral/brick beads (x 211-220, y 62-110). Leaf mass bbox x57-377, y62-377.

MUST-READS. (1) 'clump of long-stalked basal leaves' - ABSENT. There are zero petioles. The blades meet in a bare V notch directly at the ground (verified in a 2x crop of the base); there is no stalk, no clump, no stout rootstock. Nothing separates the blades into countable leaves - they read as one head. (2) 'reddish stems' - ABSENT, hard-verified: I scanned every pixel below y=130 for r>g+25 AND r>b+25 AND r>70 and got a count of exactly 0. The stem is uniformly olive-green over its whole length. (3) 'bright pink-red papery seed spire' - the only must-read that is present, and only weakly: it is 48 px tall and 9 px wide on a 440 px canvas, rendered as ~7 discrete round beads (a caterpillar/bead necklace) rather than a dense spire of overlapping papery discs, and its colour is brick-salmon (~182,79,64) rather than bright rose-pink.

Also missed and not named by the first judge: the spec leaf is 'long-stalked oblong to arrow-based' - these are round orbicular discs, i.e. Alpine Sorrel's reniform spec, not Arctic's; leafColour is spec'd 'fresh mid green' and is drawn khaki-olive; and aspect 0.7 (taller than wide) is violated - the mound is ~320 px wide by ~215 px tall, markedly wider than tall.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM. (a) 'Identical silhouette' is FALSE as stated. Pixel comparison against Alpine_Sorrel.png: silhouette IoU 0.873, symmetric difference 7,807 px, Arctic leaf area 54,325 px vs Alpine 60,422 px (Arctic ~10% smaller), right edge x377 vs x383, top y62 vs y60. It is the SAME generator re-rolled with slightly different disc radii, not a pixel copy. Disc count, overlap order, vein-rake placement, stem path and bead-column geometry ARE identical, so the 'one chassis, two hues' diagnosis stands - just not 'identical'. (b) 'The seed spire is thinner than the stem' is FALSE. The bead column measures 8-9 px across on every row sampled (y=70,80,90,100,108); the stem measures 4 px at y=125. The spire is roughly TWICE the stem width. The real spire defect is scale and texture, not width: it is far too short, it is a string of separate beads rather than a papery-disc spire, and it floats as an isolated stick above a cabbage head because there is no clump for it to rise out of. (c) 'Olive instead of mint' is CORRECT (Arctic 118,130,83 vs Alpine 124,154,142). (d) 'Reads as a cabbage' is CORRECT - it reads as a cabbage or hosta rosette head, not a sorrel clump.

BAND. Two of three must-reads are flatly absent and the third is present only as a token, so the organism does not read. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: an upright willow sapling or an olive shrub
rows.defect: The reference note says in as many words: never draw it as an upright tree — and this is an upright vase of tan trunks standing tall on a bare base, the exact forbidden reading. The prostrate ground-hugging mat, which is the whole point of an arctic willow, is absent. The leaves are narrow grey-green lances rather than small glossy rounded ovals, and the catkins are pale cream rather than red-tinged, so they read as seed heads on a reed.
rows.fix: Lay the stems flat along the ground into a low creeping mat only a few leaf-widths tall, put small round glossy leaves on them, and stand short red fuzzy catkins upright out of the mat.
rows.verifyWhy:
Measured the render (440x440). Non-background bounding box is x144-294, y103-323 = 151 wide x 221 tall, aspect 0.68. The reference row asks for aspect 2.8 and a 'prostrate mat creeping over the ground, only a few centimetres tall'. The drawing is four times wrong, in the wrong direction: it is a tall upright plant, exactly what the note forbids ('A true willow but ground-hugging; never draw it as an upright tree'). FAIL is correct.

CORRECTIONS to the original claim. (1) It is NOT 'an upright vase of tan trunks'. Zooming the base (crop y250-360) shows a SINGLE fused tapering bole: the silhouette narrows monotonically to 13 px wide at ground level (row widths 47px@y270, 30@280, 23@290, 19@300, 17@310, 13@320), flares upward, and only splits into five or six upright stems at roughly 40% of the plant's height, with short incised gouges marking the split. That is a standard/small-tree chassis with one root collar, which is a worse read than a multi-stem vase clump would be, and it is the specific defect to fix. Trunk colour is mid chocolate brown rgb(104,72,40), not tan. There is a wide dark ellipse under the plant but it is the standard cast drop-shadow, not a ground mat.

(2) Leaves: the claim is right and I can sharpen it. They are long narrow lances roughly 5:1 length-to-width, sage/grey-green rgb(120-152,136-168,104-136) with a pale silvery core highlight, arranged in near-opposite paired fans that cross into an X-lattice up the stems. The reference wants 'small rounded oval leaves, glossy above' and 'small glossy round leaves' in mustRead. Nothing in the render is round or oval; the leaf reads as weeping-willow/olive foliage. Must-read absent.

(3) Catkins: present and, on their own, the one must-read genuinely delivered. Six upright fuzzy bumpy cylindrical spikes stand at the stem tips, correctly rendered as beaded/hairy rather than smooth. The judge is right that they are cream rgb(216,200,152), with no red pixels anywhere in the image. But this is the mildest of the three faults and their description overstates it: the harvest line explicitly permits 'red or yellow', so cream/straw is a washed-out yellow, a near-miss on an allowed variant, not a contradiction. Only the mustRead's stricter 'red-tinged' is missed. Do not spend the fix budget here.

Band rationale: two of three must-reads (prostrate creeping mat; small glossy round leaves) are flatly absent, the explicit never-do note is violated, and the aspect is off by 4x. The catkins, correct in form, sit above a tree canopy instead of above a mat, so even the passing feature is staged wrong. FAIL upheld. The fix is a re-draw, not a tint: creeping horizontal stems radiating low across the ground plane, wider than tall, small round glossy leaves along them, catkins as short red-blushed uprights poking a little way above the mat.

rows.readsAs: a ghost-white agave with a sunflower sticker on a wire
rows.defect: Reuses African Ginger's stiff radial sword-blade fan, so the basal rosette of plain OVAL untoothed leaves is drawn as a spray of sharp pointed spikes, and the colour is a bleached cream-white instead of mid green — the plant does not read as living foliage. The 1-2 opposite stem leaves never appear. The flower is present but tiny and mechanical: a neat symmetric gear-toothed yellow disc, where the must-read is ragged ray petals that visibly droop.
rows.fix: Swap the spiky fan for a flat rosette of six soft mid-green oval leaves, add one opposite pair partway up the stem, and enlarge the head with long uneven drooping ray petals.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 8x nearest-neighbour crops of the flower head (src 180,50 80x80) and the rosette (src 60,170 320x190), and side-by-side against African_Ginger.png and Agave.png in the same folder.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Lower ~55% of the canvas is a symmetric fan rosette of about 11 blades springing from one point at ground level, arcing outward and up, tips reaching roughly canvas mid-height. Each blade is a broad-based pointed lanceolate blade with a drawn midrib and 6-10 pinnate lateral veins in translucent grey; the outermost pair on each side sweep nearly horizontal. Fill is bleached cream-white / bone (roughly #E6E9DC to #F2F3E9) with faint warm-grey shading, over a dark navy plate with a soft elliptical ground shadow. A single bare olive-green stem rises from the rosette centre, straight, unbranched, no leaves on it at all, terminating at ~y=95 in one small yellow flower head: a disc ~40px across with about 12 short blunt triangular ray teeth radiating stiffly and a distinct darker olive-brown central disc.

THE CHASSIS-REUSE CLAIM IS CORRECT IN SUBSTANCE. African Ginger, Agave and Arnica are unmistakably one generative rosette plus one bare central stalk carrying a terminal organ. African Ginger is the same fan in mid green with narrower spikes and a yellow bead spadix on the stalk; Agave is the same fan in pale grey-green; Arnica is the same fan bleached whiter than the actual Agave asset, with the yellow bead spike swapped for a yellow gear disc. So the identity of the plant below the flower is entirely borrowed.

CORRECTIONS TO THE STATED CAUSE. (a) The blades are not "sharp spikes" in the agave sense - they are broad-based leaf blades with full pinnate venation drawn in, aspect roughly 4:1, wider than either African Ginger's or Agave's. Because of that the thing reads less like an agave and more like a bleached white water-lily / lotus rosette or a giant white chrysanthemum leaf-fan. That does not rescue it: the must-read wants SMALL PLAIN OVAL leaves and these are large pointed lances, so the leaf shape is still wrong, just wrong in a different direction than stated. (b) The daisy is not merely "a gear-toothed disc" - it does have a properly differentiated darker central disc and ~12 rays, so it reads as a daisy head and the must-read "one yellow daisy head per stem" is genuinely satisfied. What is missing is exactly what the judge said next: the rays are short, stiff, blunt, evenly spaced and swept slightly UP, with zero raggedness and zero droop, and the head is small (~9% of canvas width) where arnica's head is conspicuously large relative to the plant.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. Two of three must-reads are not met and the failure is in the most legible property of the image. leafColour is specified as mid green, slightly hairy; the rendered foliage is cream-white and occupies ~55% of the canvas, so the dominant read of the asset is a white-foliaged rosette succulent, not a green herb. "Basal rosette of plain oval leaves" gets the arrangement right and the blade shape and colour wrong. "Ray petals slightly ragged and drooping" is absent outright. The packet's "plus 1-2 opposite pairs on the stem" is also absent - the stem is completely bare.

FIX TARGETS, in order: (1) recolour the foliage to mid green with a slight grey-hairy bloom, not bone-white; (2) replace the pointed lanceolate fan blades with short broad blunt-tipped ovals lying low and outward, 4-6 of them, so the rosette is squat rather than a tall fan; (3) enlarge the flower head and rebuild the rays as ~12-15 long narrow strap petals of uneven length with notched/tattered tips, angled downward below horizontal; (4) add one opposite pair of small oval leaves partway up the stem.

rows.readsAs: a cabbage — the same cabbage as both Sorrels, in green
rows.defect: The unmistakable arrowhead leaf silhouette is the entire identity of this species and there is not one arrow-shaped leaf in the picture: it is the Sorrel disc-pile chassis recoloured green, six huge rounded stalkless blades with no backward-pointing basal lobes and no long spongy triangular stalks. Nothing indicates water — no waterline, no emergent stance, the leaves sit on the same dry ground ellipse as the terrestrial herbs. The whorled three-petal flowers are reduced to a single white star at the very tip.
rows.fix: Cut deep twin backward lobes into every blade to make true arrowhead leaves, raise them on long straight triangular stalks from a waterline, and run three or four whorls of white three-petal flowers up the bare stem.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and would send a fix in the wrong direction. What I actually saw at 440x440, plus 2x and 5x crops of the crown, the basal notch and the flower: a mound of roughly six to seven large ROUNDED-OVATE blades, all stalkless, all radiating from a single point at bottom-centre and overlapping like a shingled fan. Each blade carries a straight midrib with pinnate side veins (clearest on the lower-right blade, which shows about eight herringbone veins). Confirmed absent at every zoom: not one blade has backward-pointing basal lobes, not one has a sagittate/arrow outline, and there are no long triangular spongy petioles anywhere - the blades attach directly at the crown. The only V-notch in the whole image is the incidental gap where the two lowest discs meet at centre-bottom, which reads as a heart/hosta clump, not an arrowhead. So must-read 1 (unmistakable arrowhead leaf silhouette) is entirely missing, and the asset reads as a hosta or wild-ginger clump rather than Sagittaria. CORRECTION 1 - the chassis attribution is wrong. This is NOT 'the Sorrel disc-pile chassis recoloured green'. I opened Sorrel.png: Sorrel is a spiky rosette of NARROW POINTED LANCE leaves with sharp tips and a red beaded flower spike - a completely different primitive. Arrowhead is on a rounded-disc shingled-rosette chassis. Anyone told to fix 'the Sorrel chassis' will edit the wrong generator. CORRECTION 2 - the flower is misdescribed. It is one terminal white star, correct, but it has SIX petals and a pale YELLOW/cream centre, not three petals and not the dark-purple centre the packet requires. It is the same generic six-point white star primitive that Water_Lily.png uses, so it is a shared default, not an Arrowhead-specific bloom. Must-read 3 (whorls of three-petalled white flowers with a dark purple centre, spaced up a bare stem) fails on petal count, on centre colour, and on whorl count - there is exactly one bloom at the very tip of a thin dark-green stem that runs unbroken from the crown to the top. CONFIRMED as claimed: no waterline and no emergent stance. The plant floats on plain void with the leaf mound hanging below the crown. This is a specific engine gap worth flagging - Arrowhead's packet form is 'aquatic' and Water_Lily.png DOES get a painted water ellipse with a horizon rim, so the water primitive exists in the engine and simply is not being applied here. Must-read 2 (leaves rising straight out of shallow water) fails. Score: zero of three must-reads readable. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a fountain of pampas or fountain grass, or a spray of wheat
rows.defect: The culms arch outward and droop like a fountain grass instead of standing as tall straight hollow culms; the nodes are drawn as bare cross-ticks on naked stems with no leafy sprays anywhere; and the harvest itself — the fat brown-sheathed pointed shoot at the base of the clump — is completely absent, so the thing named on the card does not exist in the picture.
rows.fix: Stand the culms vertical and straight with visible ringed nodes and leaf sprays only in the top third, and plant two or three fat brown scale-sheathed cones pushing up at the base of the clump.
rows.verifyWhy:
I read the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-cropped the base (x140-310, y220-330) at 5x, the mid-clump at 4x, and the whole subject at 2x, and ran a pixel scan for ink bbox and hue histogram. The FAIL is correct on every point it makes, and the asset is worse than the claim states.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a low, wide, symmetrical fan of roughly 14 smooth strands radiating from ONE point at ground level, over a flat dark elliptical shadow. Every strand tapers continuously from base to a bare blunt tip. Two alternating tones are used (pale straw for the front strands, darker olive for the back ones) to fake depth. The only surface detail anywhere is a scatter of thin flat horizontal light-yellow bars laid across the strands.

CLAIM POINT 1 - ARCHING/DROOPING: CONFIRMED. At 2x the outermost strands on both sides sweep past horizontal and their last third hangs tip-down; the second rank curls over at roughly 45 degrees. Exactly one near-central strand is genuinely straight and vertical. The silhouette is a fountain/pampas grass or a firework burst, not a stand of canes. It also is not a 'clump' in the bamboo sense - real culms emerge as separate parallel verticals from a spreading rhizome mass, whereas here all 14 strands converge to a single sub-pixel point, which reads as a tussock/grass crown.

CLAIM POINT 2 - BARE CROSS-TICKS FOR NODES: CONFIRMED, with a precision correction. The bars are not merely 'bare', they are the wrong geometry: each is a flat horizontal light bar that overhangs the strand it crosses by 2-3x the strand's own width on BOTH sides, so it reads as a tick mark or a plus sign painted on top rather than as a swollen ringed node in the strand's own silhouette. The strand edge never bulges or steps at a bar - the outline passes straight through. Several bars in the upper centre also sit at spacings and angles that do not track their strand, so at a glance a few read as detached floating dashes. Additionally nothing in the drawing reads as HOLLOW or as a rigid cane: the strands taper the whole way like grass blades instead of holding near-constant diameter between joints, so the mustRead 'tall hollow jointed culms with clear ringed nodes' is only weakly gestured at, not delivered.

CLAIM POINT 3 - NO LEAFY SPRAYS: CONFIRMED, and total. There is not a single leaf blade anywhere in the image. At 4x the tips of every strand terminate bare and rounded with nothing attached. The mustRead 'leafy sprays only near the top' and the leaf spec 'narrow lance leaves in sprays on the upper branches only' have zero pixels.

CLAIM POINT 4 - THE HARVEST IS ABSENT: CONFIRMED, and this is the decisive failure. The 5x base crop shows the 14 strands funnelling to one point directly on the shadow ellipse with clear empty background either side. There is no cone, no fat pointed shoot, no sheath, no scale texture, nothing pushing up from the ground. The hue histogram over all lit pixels returns ONLY hues 45-105 (yellow through yellow-green); there is not one brown, red-brown or tan pixel in the whole 440x440 canvas. The named item - 'a fat pointed cone-shaped shoot pushing up from the ground, sheathed in brown hairy scales' - is entirely unrepresented, and the packet note is explicit that this ground-level cone, not the tall culm, IS the harvest. The species is named Bamboo SHOOTS and the shoots do not exist.

TWO FURTHER DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT REPORT (fix these too):
(a) ASPECT IS INVERTED. Reference aspect is 0.5, i.e. twice as tall as wide. Measured ink bounding box is x 47-392, y 118-310 = 345 wide by 192 tall, a w/h of 1.8 - about 3.6x too wide for spec. The subject also floats: it occupies only the middle vertical third of the canvas and its top is 118px down from the frame edge, so there is no sense of height at all. Bamboo's single strongest silhouette cue is verticality and this asset spends its budget on horizontal spread.
(b) COLOUR IS WRONG. leafColour is specified 'mid green'. Every lit pixel measures hue 45-75 (straw yellow to yellow-olive) with a handful up to 105; there is no green in the image. The palette reads as dried/dead ornamental grass, which compounds the fountain-grass misread rather than correcting it.

VERDICT: two of the three mustReads (leafy sprays near the top; brown-sheathed shoots at the base) have literally zero pixels, the third (jointed culms with ringed nodes) is served only by overhanging cross-ticks on tapering non-vertical grass blades, and the harvest item the species is named for is missing. The asset reads as ornamental fountain/pampas grass. FAIL upheld.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS: straighten the strands into near-parallel vertical canes of constant diameter with the aspect flipped to about 0.5 (tall, narrow, top of the clump near the frame top); build the node as a slight bulge and a ring band contained WITHIN the cane silhouette rather than a bar overhanging it; add narrow lance-leaf sprays branching off the upper third only; recolour the canes to mid green; and add two or three fat pointed brown-sheathed cones at ground level, overlapping the cane bases, big enough to read at thumbnail size, since those cones are the harvest.

rows.readsAs: a palm or a cycad
rows.defect: It is drawn with a woody brown FORKED trunk and a radial crown of stiff feathery pinnate fronds — exactly the two things the note forbids. There is no smooth green false trunk of rolled sheaths, no torn paddle blades, no hanging bunch and no purple-red terminal bud; the only fruit cue is a small yellow floret cluster sitting up in the crown instead of a bunch hanging below an arching stalk.
rows.fix: Replace the brown fork with a single smooth green sheath-column, swap the fronds for a few huge paddle blades torn into ribs, and hang a downward bunch of yellow-green fingers tipped with a purple bud.
rows.verifyWhy: Verified at full size, at a 3x crop of the crown and a 4x crop of the trunk, plus a programmatic colour scan of all 193,600 pixels. The FAIL stands: all three must-reads are absent and the note's two explicit prohibitions ('no woody trunk, no branches') are both violated. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: (1) TRUNK — a single flat mid-brown stem (sampled ~#604830 / RGB 96,72,48, the 4th most common colour in the image at ~1,100 sampled px) rising from a dark ground ellipse, bare and unmarked for its whole lower two-thirds, then splitting into a clean Y: two short upright branches with rounded cap ends diverging left and right just under the crown. Woody colour AND branching, both forbidden. There is no green false trunk, no overlapping rolled leaf-sheath edges, no sheath lines or vertical striation of any kind — the stem has zero internal detail. (2) CROWN — a radial semicircular fan of roughly 13 fronds all springing from one point at the top of the trunk. Each frond is a narrow solid green strip (~12px wide at source) with a darker midrib line, flanked on BOTH sides by fine needle-like teeth that extend well PAST the blade outline, with gaps wider than the teeth. That is pinnate leaflets — a palm/cycad frond — not a torn paddle. I looked specifically for the charitable reading (a banana paddle tears into ribs along the midrib, which could be drawn as slits) and it does not hold: a torn paddle keeps a broad ovate outline with slits cutting INWARD, whereas here the blade is narrow and the teeth project OUTWARD past the silhouette, and there are 13 narrow fronds in a fan rather than 5-8 huge blades spiralling up a false stem. Silhouette overall = bare pole + hemispherical feather fan = palm. (3) HARVEST — I corrected one part of the judge's description. What sits in the crown is not a 'small yellow floret'; it is a tight roughly spherical knot of about 14 rounded pale cream-yellow beads (~30x28px at source, ~244 yellow-ish pixels total), wedged into the CROTCH of the trunk fork, held UPRIGHT and tucked under the fronds. It reads as a coconut/date/palm drupe cluster or a berry knot, not as a hand of fingers. There is no arching stalk, nothing hangs downward anywhere in the image, and no elongated finger shapes. (4) BUD — I scanned every pixel for any purple/magenta/red-violet value (R>70, B>60, R>G+25, B>G+10): the count is exactly 0. There is no purple-red bud, not even a small or dark one. NET: an unbriefed viewer would name this a palm or a cycad. Zero of the three must-reads (green false trunk of rolled sheaths / torn paddle leaves / hanging bunch tipped with a purple-red bud) are present. FIX DIRECTION: replace the woody forked stem with a single unbranched smooth GREEN pseudostem showing overlapping sheath edges; replace the pinnate fan with 5-7 very large green paddle blades spiralling out from the pseudostem top, each blade broad and ovate with slits cutting inward to the midrib but the outline staying paddle-shaped; and add a single stalk arching out and DOWN from the crown carrying tiers of upcurved yellow-green fingers, terminating in a pendant purple-red teardrop bud below the bunch.

rows.readsAs: a saguaro or an organ-pipe column cactus with a sunflower stuck on it
rows.defect: The body is a tall narrow tapering spire roughly four times taller than wide — the fat squat accordion-ribbed BARREL that is the whole identity is absent. The crown is a point, not a flat top ringed with fruit; the harvest ring of scaly yellow barrel fruits is reduced to one tiny beige cluster tucked to one side; and the spines are sparse straight white sticks with none of the long flattened hooked central spines.
rows.fix: Squash the body to a wide squat ribbed barrel with a flat top, ring that flat crown with scaly yellow fruits, and give each rib crest stout red-brown hooked spines.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated causes.

MEASURED SILHOUETTE (440x440 canvas, green-body pixels): bbox x198-241, y112-342 = 44 px wide x 231 px tall. Width/height = 0.19 against the packet's aspect: 0.9. Sampled widths: row 120 = 8 px, row 160 = 24, row 200 = 34, row 240 = 40, row 300 = 44 (max, at the very base), row 335 = 43. So the body is a 5.3:1 straight-sided column that swells slightly from the base upward for the first third and then tapers continuously to a needle apex. It reads as a saguaro / organ-pipe spike. The judge is right: the fat squat barrel that IS this species is absent, and the aspect miss is ~4.7x, not a nudge.

CORRECTION 1 - THE RIBS EXIST, THE CHASSIS DOES NOT. The claim implies accordion ribbing is missing. It is not. Zoomed 4x on the trunk I count roughly 10-12 fine vertical flutes running the full length of the column, shaded in alternating light/dark green bands with a specular file down the centre-left. The rib renderer is working. What is wrong is only the body it is wrapped around. Do NOT re-derive ribbing; re-derive the form: a squat barrel roughly as wide as tall (aspect ~0.9-1.0), widest at mid-height or slightly above, with a rounded shoulder, and the ribs should read as 12-18 CHUNKY vertical accordion pleats with visible depth, not 10+ hairline flutes.

CORRECTION 2 - THE CROWN IS NOT JUST 'POINTED', IT IS CROWNED BY A LARGE DAISY THE JUDGE DID NOT MENTION. The single most dominant element in the top third is a ~35 px yellow composite flower with about 12 sharply pointed petals and a dark brown central disc, sitting directly on the apex like a sunflower on a stalk. This is the main reason the asset reads as 'generic flowering desert plant' rather than cactus, and it is a bigger defect than the fruit. Barrel cactus blooms are short cup-shaped funnels borne in a RING around a flat, woolly, slightly depressed apex - many small cups, never one big rayed daisy on a point. Fix: kill the composite daisy entirely, flatten the crown to a wide woolly disc, and ring it.

CORRECTION 3 - THE FRUIT IS NOT BEIGE. The claim calls it 'one tiny beige clump'. Zoomed 6x it is a cluster of about 6 distinctly golden/amber round berries, each ~7 px, each carrying a pale grey-white specular highlight - it reads as a small grape-like berry bunch, roughly 20x14 px overall. What IS right in the claim is the placement and the count: the cluster hangs to the RIGHT of the stem, below the flower, entirely off-axis, so there is no ring and no crown-crowding. The must-read wants a ring of scaly, barrel/torpedo-shaped yellow fruits crowded shoulder-to-shoulder AROUND the flat apex, each with visible overlapping scales - not smooth spheres, not a side bunch.

SPINES - CLAIM CORRECT, SHARPENED. About 20 straight cream/bone-white dashes, 8-14 px long, angled down-and-out, arranged in two loose vertical files on the left and right margins. Critically, most of them are drawn 2-8 px DETACHED from the silhouette edge, floating in the background void with no contact point, and several are doubled into little parallel pairs. There are no areoles, no attachment to any rib crest, no hook, no flattening, and no red-brown colour (packet: 'red-brown spines'). They must become dense clusters seated ON each rib crest, tinted red-brown, with a long flattened downward-hooked central spine per areole.

COLOUR - unstated by the judge but off: the body is a mid grass/olive green with a fairly saturated highlight, where the packet asks for grey-green.

Band FAIL stands: the organism is the wrong shape at the silhouette level, and two of three must-reads (fat ribbed barrel; flat-topped crown ringed with yellow fruit) fail outright while the third (long flattened hooked central spines) is present only as detached white sticks.

rows.readsAs: a sparse bare cane shrub or a dying willow whip with pom-pom seedheads
rows.defect: Drawn on the shared cane-vase chassis: mostly naked brown sticks, airy and see-through, when the must-read is a DENSE CONICAL EVERGREEN. The leaves are tiny thin mid-green slivers, not thick leathery very-dark glossy lances with a rippled margin, and there are so few of them the plant reads as leafless. The cream flowers are white pom-pom balls stuck on the cane tips rather than small clusters tucked into the leaf axils.
rows.fix: Fill the silhouette into a solid dark conical evergreen mass of large leathery wavy-edged near-black-green leaves, and move the cream flower clusters down into the leaf joints.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the full 440px render and at a 4x nearest-neighbour zoom of the crown (crop 130,70 180x180). Replace the composite head with a Monarda inflorescence: a flattened dome of many long thin lavender tubes bursting outward and downward at irregular angles from a knobbly centre, ragged in silhouette; ring the base of that head with a whorl of small leafy pink-tinged bracts; give the stem visible square facets (two darker edge lines / a flat-sided silhouette); and widen the leaves to true lance blades with coarse teeth, cutting the node count to roughly four or five opposite pairs so the head dominates the plant instead of being a 13% ornament. rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG and then at a 4x nearest-neighbour zoom of the plant (x140-310, y80-340). The FAIL stands, but two parts of the stated cause are described wrong and the fixer needs the accurate reading.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a vase-fan clump of five or six straight tan-brown canes rising from one narrow trunk-like base plug on a dark ground ellipse. Each cane is terminated by ONE flower head. The heads are NOT 'pink pompoms' - at 4x they resolve as flat, face-on radial RINGS: a dark maroon-plum disc with a ring of 10-14 small pale cream-white beads set around its rim and one or two ochre specks at the centre. They read as flat-topped umbels / pincushion discs seen from the front, roughly as wide as they are tall (about 20x16 px each at full size), held UPRIGHT and clear of the foliage. There is nothing pendulous, nothing elongated, no axis. Confirmed: the long drooping cylindrical bottlebrush raceme that is the identity must-read is entirely absent, in both its white-flower phase and its cherry phase.

FRUIT: confirmed absent. No cherry, no berry, no hanging cylinder anywhere on the plant. The only dark red-black pigment in the piece is the maroon receptacle disc behind each floret ring - it is a backing plate, not fruit, and does not rescue the harvest read.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM (1): the judge said the heads are 'exactly the loose-bunch arrangement the reference rules out'. That undersells it. The reference rules out loose BUNCHES of fruit; what is drawn is not a loose bunch of anything - it is the wrong inflorescence architecture entirely (a solitary terminal flat umbel per cane, apiaceae/valerian-like). A fixer told 'tighten the bunch into a cylinder' would be working from the wrong starting geometry; the head has to be replaced with a pendent 8-12 cm axis bearing 20+ stalked units.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM (2): 'thin willow lances rather than broad glossy sharply-toothed ovals' is right on shape but incomplete. The leaves are narrow lanceolate blades about 5:1, mid dull green, and their margins are perfectly SMOOTH - not a single tooth is drawn anywhere on any leaf. There is also no specular gloss on the upper surface and no paler underside; the reference asks for 'dark glossy green above, paler beneath'. So three separate leaf attributes fail, not one. Leaves are set in near-opposite pairs sprigged along the canes rather than alternate.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT NEITHER JUDGE NAMED: proportion. The reference aspect is 0.9 (near square). The drawn plant measures roughly 126 px wide by 228 px tall, an aspect near 0.55 - a tall narrow clump, not a broad shrub crown. The growth habit also reads herbaceous (bare straight canes off a single base) rather than a woody branching shrub.

Net: correct organism family cannot be recovered from this image. It reads as a generic flowering perennial, not a chokecherry. FAIL upheld.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at full size and at 3x/6x crops of the crown, mid-column and base. VERDICT UPHELD, but the first judge got the berry badly wrong and that error would misdirect the fix.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A single dark-olive stem runs the full height of a 440x440 frame. From roughly y=100 to y=310 it carries a dense, perfectly regular ladder of paired leaflets - about 20 tiers, ~40 leaflets total - each leaflet a narrow pointed ellipse/lanceolate blade angled downward and outward, all identical in size and shape, packed tip-to-base so the column edge is a continuous sawtooth. Below y=310 the stem is bare for ~60px down to a soft elliptical ground shadow; above y=100 a short bare stem tip pokes out of the crown. The rendered silhouette is a tall narrow bottlebrush/horsetail/pinnate-frond spike roughly 3:1 tall-to-wide, against a spec aspect of 0.9 (near-square, short herb). The colour is a flat pale sage-green with soft internal leaflet embossing; no deep venation.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM - THE BERRY IS NOT 'a tiny orange knot'. At 6x the crown resolves as a genuinely well-drawn aggregate berry: a solitary golden-amber/orange raspberry-like cluster of about 10-12 distinct rounded drupelets, each with its own specular highlight, nested in the topmost leaf whorl and hanging slightly left of the stem tip. It spans roughly 30x22px in the 440px frame - small relative to the leaf column, but crisply modelled and unmistakably a cloudberry-type compound drupe in the correct amber-orange (not red, not darkened). The must-read 'a solitary golden-amber berry' is PRESENT and readable. Any fix must preserve this berry as-is; it is the one correct element and the only thing distinguishing the plate from a fern.

WHAT GENUINELY FAILS (two of three must-reads).
1. 'a short single stem with a couple of crumpled lobed leaves' - ABSENT. The spec asks for one or two rounded five-lobed wrinkled leaves per stem. Delivered: ~40 identical unlobed pointed leaflets in a pinnate ladder. There is not a single rounded, lobed or crumpled blade anywhere in the frame, and the leaf count is off by a factor of ~20. This alone makes it read as the wrong organism.
2. 'one white five-petalled flower' - ABSENT. I searched the crown crop, the whole-plant crop and the base crop at 6x. There is no white, cream or pale pixel cluster anywhere; the only non-green element in the entire plate is the amber berry.
3. Aspect - the plate is ~3:1 tall where the row specifies 0.9. The herb form is not honoured.

MINOR CORRECTIONS TO THE FIRST JUDGE'S WORDING: 'thirty-plus identical pointed leaves stacked in a ladder' is close but undercounts slightly (~40 leaflets in ~20 opposite pairs, not a single-file stack); the berry is buried in the top whorl but is a properly rendered drupelet cluster, not a knot.

FIX DIRECTION: keep the berry render and its palette; replace the pinnate leaflet ladder with 1-2 large rounded palmate five-lobed crumpled blades with deep radial venation on a short stem, add one white five-petalled flower with a pale centre, and compress the plate to ~0.9 aspect.

rows.readsAs: a pink sea pen, a bundle of soft noodles, or a feather duster worm

rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, with corrections to the count and to the stated cause. What is actually on the canvas (440x440, subject occupies roughly x=180-265, y=88-330): a single tight bundle of long, perfectly smooth, unbranched tapered strands that all radiate from ONE point at the bottom and splay outward as they rise, each ending in a blunt rounded finger tip. The judge said six tubes; at 9x zoom on the crown I count nine to ten strands, not six — about six lit rose-pink ones (#D7A6AF) in front, with three or four more rendered entirely in the mauve-brown shadow tone (#59454E) behind and between them. Beyond the miscount the claim holds and all three must-reads are absent.

(1) 'stony brittle pink texture, not soft or floppy' — ABSENT. Each strand is a flat two-tone cylinder: one broad lit face, one dark side, a soft antialiased outline, and zero surface incident. No chalk grain, no matte pitting, no crisp fracture edges, no highlight breakup — the shading language is exactly the smooth soft-body ramp used for tentacles and stems. One refinement to the judge's wording: the strands are not floppy in PATH — they run essentially straight and stiff from base to tip with only a gentle outward bow, so the failure is TEXTURE and EDGE (smooth, rubbery, uniformly rounded in cross-section), not slack curvature. A fix must attack the surface treatment and silhouette edge, not the pose.

(2) 'jointed bead-like segments in the branching form' — ABSENT twice over. There is not a single constriction, node, bead, ring or tonal break anywhere along any strand; each one is a continuous unbroken tube from base to tip. And the branching is missing too, which the judge did not call out: every strand runs from the common basal point to a free tip without a single fork, so there is no branching architecture at all, let alone a segmented one. This is a radiating tuft, not a branched thallus.

(3) 'hard pink crust plating the rock' — ABSENT. There is no rock, no substrate, no crust, no encrusting plate of any kind. The only thing below the subject is a flat dark elliptical drop-shadow on the ground plane (y~315-335). Worse: at 9x the converged base does NOT meet that ground — the bundle terminates in a rounded blunt cap around y=328 with the shadow ellipse sitting under and behind it, so the whole plant reads as floating/unanchored with no holdfast.

Colour is the one correct element and the judge is right about that: lit #D7A6AF and shadow #59454E sit in the chalky-pink-to-lilac-mauve band the reference asks for. Read-as: a pink sea pen or sea-anemone tuft / a bundle of stiff pink drinking straws. Nothing in the silhouette or surface says calcified alga. Every identity must-read is missing, so FAIL stands — this needs a rebuild of the form (short forked segmented branchlets with visible bead constrictions, hard-edged chalky surface, and an encrusting plate over a rock base), not a polish.

rows.readsAs: a pussy-willow stem or a florist's snowball twig

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, with two corrections to the stated cause.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 canvas; I zoomed the boll cluster 4x and 7x with nearest-neighbour, and ran a pixel histogram). The subject's ink bounding box is x139-238, y107-322 — roughly 100px wide in a 440px frame, about 2.9% pixel coverage. A single olive-green stem (RGB ~ (72,80,45)) rises from a dark ground ellipse at y~305-322, runs straight up to about mid-canvas, then forks into three thin branches that all lean up and to the LEFT. Nothing else exists on the canvas. Histogram totals: ~2,400 white pixels, ~1,770 olive-green pixels (all of it stem), ~73 brown pixels (the crescents described below). There is no second green mass anywhere, so the leaflessness claim is verified, not merely eyeballed.

LEAVES — the judge is right and it is total. Zero leaves, zero leaflets, zero stipules, zero bract. The reference wants form=shrub, 'broad palmate leaves with 3-5 pointed lobes, alternate on a branching stem', mid-green with reddish veins, and mustRead 'three-to-five lobed leaves on a bushy plant'. The render is a bare three-pronged stick. The 'bushy' silhouette does not exist either — this is one thin vertical wand, not a shrub.

FLOWER — the judge is right. No hibiscus-like cream-yellow flower with a dark centre anywhere. No petal shape, no yellow pixels at all in the histogram.

BOLLS — the judge's DESCRIPTION IS PARTLY WRONG, though the verdict still stands. They are not 'four plain white spheres with no capsule or split'. At 7x zoom each of the four white puffs is a soft mound with faint concentric lobing across its crown (a hint of separate fibre locks), and each carries a single thin BROWN CRESCENT ARC (~2px, warm tan ~ (110,88,50)) painted across its lower-front face. So a brown husk element IS present — the judge missed it. But it fails anyway, because that arc is a hairline smile-line sitting ON the white, not a split capsule: there are no husk valves, no splayed four/five-part calyx, no brown shell that the fibre bulges OUT of, and no tonal separation between husk and fibre. The read at native size is four marshmallows with smiley faces on a stick — I agree the pussy-willow/dried-florist-stem reading is fair, but the specific reason is 'decorative arc instead of a splayed husk', not 'no brown at all'.

ADDITIONAL DEFECTS THE JUDGE DID NOT MENTION, which a fix pass needs:
1. Only THREE branches reach the cluster but there are FOUR puffs; two puffs float with no stem attaching, resting on their neighbours. Every boll needs its own pedicel.
2. The four puffs overlap into one continuous lumpy horizontal sausage leaning up-right, all crowded into the upper-LEFT of the plant. Bolls should sit at separated branch tips distributed around a bushy crown.
3. Framing: the plant fills under a quarter of the frame width and its mass is off-centre to the left; scale it up and centre it.

FIX DIRECTION: rebuild as a bushy branching shrub — main stem with several alternate side branches, each carrying a broad 3-5 lobed palmate leaf in mid-green with reddish petiole/vein accents; add at least one cream-yellow five-petal hibiscus-form flower with a dark maroon throat; and re-model each boll as a brown four-valve husk splayed open with white fibre bulging out between the valves, so brown husk and white fibre are distinct shapes rather than a tan line drawn on a white ball.

rows.readsAs: an upright twiggy shrub with grey seed heads
rows.defect: The identity must-read is a flat creeping heather-like carpet, and the render is its exact opposite: a tall upright vase of straight brown canes, distinctly taller than wide, despite the reference aspect of 2.2 asking for a wide low mat. rows.verifyWhy: Measured the render: ink bbox x129-310, y88-338 = 182 wide x 251 tall, aspect w/h = 0.73. The packet asks for aspect 2.2, and the convention in this batch is width/height (Date palm = 0.6, Curry Leaf 'slender open shrub' = 0.7, Creosote 'open airy shrub' = 1.0). So the reference wants a mat 2.2x wider than tall and the render is 0.73x — off by a factor of ~3, and it is the widest-mandated entry in the whole batch drawn as one of the most upright things on the page. Must-read 1 ('a flat creeping heather-like carpet') is ABSENT: at 3x magnification the base is a single fused solid brown trunk ~20px wide that flares into 7-8 straight, unbranched canes fanning upward in a vase/broom silhouette. Crowberry is prostrate and rooting-as-it-spreads with no trunk at all; this silhouette reads as a young broom/bamboo whip clump. Must-read 2 ('short needle leaves packed on wiry stems') is ABSENT: the green marks are long straight single-width blades roughly 20-40px long (each one ~15% of total plant height), scattered at random angles, sparse, and many of them float free in empty space unattached to any cane. They read as pine straw or grass blades strewn across the canes, not as tiny rolled needles crowded along a stem; there is no packed heather texture anywhere. Must-read 3 ('glossy black berries nestled tight against the foliage') FAILS, but I must CORRECT the other judge's stated cause: the berries are NOT solid pale grey-white pompoms. At 5x magnification each of the 6 terminal clusters is 5-6 discrete spheres with genuinely dark near-black bodies and dark rims; the problem is that the specular highlight on each sphere is blown out to near-white (sampled mean of the pale pixels is RGB 132,130,131, neutral grey) and covers roughly 40% of the sphere face, so at 1:1 the highlight swamps the dark body and the cluster reads as a grey pompom. Fix the highlight size/value, do not repaint the berry body. The judge IS right on placement: all 254 pale pixels lie in y93-139, i.e. the top 18% of the plant, and every cluster sits on the bare terminal 10-15px of a cane with clear background around it, well above where any green mark ends -- terminal pompoms on bare tips, never nestled among foliage. Net: all three must-reads fail and the organism reads as the wrong plant. FAIL upheld. Rebuild as a low spreading mat (target w/h ~2.2, no trunk, prostrate wiry stems radiating sideways from a low centre), replace the long blades with very short dense needle ticks packed along the whole length of every stem, and set the berries down inside the needle mass with a small tight highlight.

rows.readsAs: a generic feathery-leaved twig shrub

rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size, then decoded it pixel-by-pixel (bounding box and an ASCII luminance map at 1px horizontal / 2px vertical resolution over x=175..260, y=90..340) specifically hunting for a small pod, hook, or flower the first judge might have missed. There is nothing else on the canvas. Ink bbox is x 187-247, y 99-327 = 60px wide x 228px tall, an aspect of about 0.26 against the packet's aspect: 2 (i.e. the asset is roughly 8x too tall-and-narrow for the specified sprawling habit).

What is actually drawn: one straight vertical green stem (a 4px-wide column running unbroken from y~100 to y~327, with a bare naked tip from y~100 to y~128 above the topmost leaves), carrying exactly 7 pairs of opposite leaves at y~130, 155, 180, 205, 230, 255, 280. Every leaf is an identical lanceolate/pointed almond blade angled ~30 degrees upward, ~35px long, in a pale khaki-olive with a lighter highlight streak along its upper edge. Below the stem base sits the standard flat elliptical ground shadow. A full colour histogram of every pixel above luminance 25 returns ONLY greens, olives and khaki-greys (peak buckets rgb 144,144,120 / 72,72,48 / 144,168,120). There is not one pink, purple, magenta, brown, tan or woody-grey pixel anywhere in the image.

Every part of the first judge's claim checks out and I can confirm each independently:
1. The woody seed pod splitting into two long recurved grappling hooks -- the named feature and the mustRead's first item -- is ABSENT. Not small, not tucked at the base, not behind foliage. Nothing hook-shaped, curved, or woody-coloured exists at any point on the silhouette; the stem terminates as a plain bare taper at the top and a plain taper into the shadow at the bottom.
2. The trumpet flower (pinkish-purple, spotted throat) is ABSENT -- confirmed by the histogram having zero non-green hue.
3. The sprawling flat-to-the-ground habit is ABSENT; the plant is rigidly upright and vertical, the exact opposite of the required trailing mat.
4. The leaf model is wrong: the packet calls for LARGE ROUNDED LOBED opposite leaves on sticky trailing stems. The drawn leaves are small, narrow, smooth-edged and pointed -- no lobing, no rounding, no clamminess cue.

But CORRECT THE DESCRIPTION: the one mark present is not a 'circle', it is a genuine spiral -- 14 line segments at 0.6 rad each = ~1.34 turns of steadily decreasing radius, ending in a short inward tail, which is why at this size it reads as a ring with a nick out of it. Its problem is scale, contrast and placement, not shape. The real framing defect is horizontal and the opposite axis: side margins are only 31px left / 30px right, and the silhouette is 1.70:1 WIDE against a spec aspect of 0.9. The fronds fan out flat into a squat shuttlecock rather than standing up into a vase ring, and yes, one frond does spear off to the right and break the ring -- that half of the claim is correct.

WHAT IT READS AS: a sago palm / cycad rosette. Stiff perpendicular needle pinnae, uniform length, no taper of the rachis, no unfurling tips, no vertical lift.

ROOT CAUSE, so the fix has an address: packages/art/src/floraoverrides2.ts, the spec.habit === 'fern' branch (~lines 564-580). It draws nf = 6 fronds at -PI/2 +/- 1.05*spread -- the wide spread is what flattens the vase into a fan -- then a comment that reads 'one small fiddlehead tucked low at the crown, not floating over them' followed by ONE spiral at radius S*0.020, lineWidth S*0.008, positioned at (cx + S*0.02, base - S*0.10). That is the entire crozier budget for every fern species in the game. There is no brown-scale code anywhere in the branch. The fix needs a cluster of 3-5 croziers at several times that radius, standing near the crown centre on visible upright stipes, drawn with a dark outline or a brown scale wrap so they separate from the green behind them, plus a tighter spread so the fronds ring rather than fan.

Against the reference row (form: moss, aspect 1.4; leaf: flat overlapping leathery lobes in a rosette on rock, or fine antler-like branching tufts; mustRead: flat crusty rosette clinging to rock or bark / lobed edges with a paler chalky margin / small raised cup discs on the surface; note: not a plant, no stems or roots, drawn as a crust or antler-tuft on a substrate, never as foliage) — all three must-reads are absent, none of them merely small or hidden:

A full-image color census shows the entire body is ONE flat fill, RGB 174,191,175, covering 11,160 px; every other color in the body is a 1-2 step antialias variant of it. There is zero internal shading, zero mottling, no white/sulphur-yellow/rust patch, no rim value change anywhere. Antler-tuft (fruticose) lichen means repeated dichotomous forking: each branch splits into two, then two again, giving a tangled coral mass with no single origin. Here every ray is a straight, unbranched, uniform-width capsule emanating from ONE point, which is exactly the stem-and-frond / radiating-fan reading the note forbids. rows.readsAs: a stiff green fern or feather-frond with a small lilac tip
