The pinnate arrangement is drawn as a mechanically regular double comb of tiny identical leaflets stacked in eleven perfect tiers, which reads as a fern frond or a bottle brush rather than a locust-like legume leaf. The pale blue-lilac spike is present but is a small pixel-scale bead chain crammed at the very top, easy to miss at icon size.
rows.fix: Pull a long straight ropey yellow root with side runners out below the soil line so it occupies the lower third of the frame, and break the leaflet rows into larger irregular oval leaflets with visible gaps.

rows.readsAs: an upright garden shrub with red berry clusters — a coffee or cotoneaster bush
rows.defect: The habit is wrong in the direction that matters: this is a tall upright twig-fan standing on a trunk, when the must-read is a low creeping evergreen mat barely a hand high. Leaves are pointed lance blades spread along the stems, not small thick box-like leathery ovals. The berry clusters sit as flat upward-facing rosettes on the tips rather than nodding under their own weight. It is the identical stem-fan chassis as Labrador Tea with red triplets substituted for white discs.
rows.fix: Flatten the whole plant into a wide low mat with creeping horizontal stems and a squat aspect, shorten the leaves into small rounded leathery ovals, and hang the berry clusters nodding beneath the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: a water lily floating on a pond
rows.defect: The harvest that names the asset is absent. The render is three flat green pads lying ON the water surface inside a dark pool ellipse with one small pink star flower — no sausage-chain rhizome, no cut cross-section showing the ring of holes, no mud, nothing pulled up at all, despite the reference note explicitly demanding the root chain. The leaves also lie flat like Nymphaea pads instead of being held high above the water on stalks with upturned bowl edges, so even the plant above the waterline reads as the wrong genus.
rows.fix: Put a fat pale sausage-linked rhizome chain in the foreground lifted clear of the mud with one segment cut to show the ring of holes, and raise the round leaves onto tall central stalks with upturned rims.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1:1, at 6x crop zoom on both halves, and at 3x brightness boost over the whole 440x440 frame (to rule out a rhizome hidden in the near-black underwater area). The FAIL stands, and the underwater sweep confirms nothing is hidden: the entire painted content is (a) one flat navy-blue ellipse spanning x~45-390, y~205-250, with a thin pale rim highlight and a soft dark drop-shadow beneath it -- a pond/puddle disc, not mud; (b) three overlapping pale mint-green ellipses (pads) sitting ON that disc, each ~110x60px; (c) one 6-petal pale-pink/white flower with a small yellow center, ~35px, resting on the middle pad's upper edge. That is the whole asset. Nothing else is drawn anywhere in the frame.

Against the packet row (harvest: 'a chain of fat sausage-linked pale rhizomes, pierced with round holes in cross-section'; mustRead: 'round dish-shaped leaf on a central stalk . sausage-chain rhizome . the ring of holes in the cut root'; note: 'here the harvest is the rhizome, so show the root chain pulled from the mud'): must-reads 2 and 3 -- the two that separate Lotus Root from Lotus -- are 100% absent. There is no pale tan/cream tuber, no sausage-link chain, no cut face, no ring of holes, no root hairs, no mud clod. The named harvest, which is the entire reason this species exists as a separate entry from 'Lotus', was never drawn.

TWO CORRECTIONS to their stated cause, both of which change what the fix should touch:
1. They say the pads have no central stalk at all. Not quite -- each pad carries a short dark-green dash near its center (the front-center pad carries two, at roughly (240,215) and (285,205); the left and right pads one each). These are clearly an attempted petiole/peltate-notch mark, but they are drawn flat ON the pad's top surface, horizontally, ~30px long, so they read as a vein or a split, not as a stalk. So must-read 1 is not absent so much as drawn wrong: the geometry exists but is coplanar with the pad. Don't add a stalk from nothing -- rotate/extend the existing mark into a vertical petiole that pierces the water line.
2. 'lie flat on the water instead of being held high on stalks with upturned rims' is correct on both counts, and the rim half is the more damaging one: the pads are pure flat ellipses with a top-down gradient, zero bowl, and their edges intersect the water ellipse rather than floating above it, which is exactly the water-lily silhouette. The packet's leafColour ('blue-grey green, water-repellent') is also missed -- what is painted is a bright mint/spring green.

One defect the original judge did not report: framing. The packet aspect is 0.8 (portrait-ish), but the composition is strongly landscape and tiny -- the subject occupies ~78% of frame width and only ~20% of frame height (y~170 to y~262 of 440), leaving the top 38% and bottom 40% of the canvas empty. Even before the rhizome is added, the asset does not fill its own frame. The fix that resolves all of this at once is the packet's own note: pull the sausage-chain rhizome out of a mud bank as the dominant foreground mass (with one link cut to show the ring of holes), and demote the dish leaves on their prickly stalks to the upper background -- that fills the portrait frame and restores the identity in the same pass. As it stands the asset is indistinguishable from a water lily and would be misread by any player.

rows.readsAs: a lollipop tree carrying plums or damsons
rows.defect: The four-lobed green calyx cap — the single feature that separates a mangosteen from any purple stone fruit — is not on any of the four fruits; they are plain unbroken purple spheres. The crown is a soft round fog-blob, not a dense narrow conical crown, and the leaves are small pointed slivers scattered on the blob's rim rather than large thick leathery blades in opposite pairs. The trunk is the same untapered brown pole used for Mangrove, Maple and Marula.
rows.fix: Cap every fruit with a clearly readable four-lobed green star calyx and rebuild the crown as a narrow upright cone of large paired leathery leaves.

rows.readsAs: a generic green shade tree — the batch's default tree with the fruit deleted
rows.defect: The arching stilt roots that ARE the mangrove are entirely absent: the trunk is a single straight brown pole that plunges into flat ground with an ellipse shadow, no water and no root arch anywhere. The propagules are reduced to three or four thin dark slivers hidden inside the crown where they read as shadow gaps rather than long hanging cigar-shaped seedlings, and the leaves are not bunched at branch ends because there are no branches. Strip the fruit off Mangosteen and this is the same picture.
rows.fix: Lift the trunk clear of a water line on a cage of arching stilt roots and hang half a dozen long pale-green pencil propagules below the outer foliage where they break the crown's silhouette.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated causes.

WHAT I DID: read the 440x440 PNG at full size, then re-cropped it in four passes (base 130,250 180x180 @4x; crown 90,40 260x260 @3x; three 7x zooms at 130,95 / 240,150 / 165,215) and ran a colour mask isolating all brown (r>70, r>g>b) pixels to map the trunk geometry exactly.

MUST-READ 1 — 'arching stilt roots lifting the trunk clear of the water': ABSENT, total. The brown mask returns ONE connected blob: a perfectly straight vertical bar, constant width (~20px), from y~285 to y~372, capped by a rounded lozenge bottom. Zero branching, zero basal flare, zero aerial/prop roots, no arch, no root-to-ground contact points. It is a lollipop stick. Nor is there water: the background is a single flat dark-navy vignette with no horizon line, no water plane, no reflection, no waterline on the trunk. The only ground cue is the stock flat dark ellipse shadow (spanning roughly x 150-290, y 345-380) that the trunk's rounded end sinks into. The judge's description of this is accurate.

MUST-READ 3 — 'long hanging cigar-shaped seedling propagules': DRAWN BUT UNREADABLE, and the judge mis-described them twice. (a) There are FOUR, not three: orig approx (200-225, 120-133), (142-172, 143-160), (268-296, 168-188), and (192-220, 238-256). (b) They are NOT mere 'shadow gaps' — at 7x they are deliberately drawn lens/cigar solids, pointed at both ends, and two of them (the upper-left pair) carry faint internal segment lobes reading as pod nodes. So the propagule element EXISTS in the render. It fails for different reasons than stated: they are painted near-black olive (sampled 25,45,25 and 18,28,14) against a mid-green crown (sampled 80,155,96), i.e. DARKER than the foliage instead of the spec'd pale green; they are laid nearly horizontal / diagonal at the same angle family as the leaves instead of hanging vertically; they are short (~30px, no longer than a leaf) instead of 'long'; and all four sit buried inside the crown mass rather than dangling BELOW branch tips. Net effect at 1x is exactly what the judge reported — dark holes in the canopy — but the fix is re-colour + re-orient + lengthen + move outside the crown silhouette, NOT 'add propagules'.

MUST-READ 2 — 'thick glossy paired leaves bunched at branch ends': HALF PRESENT. Leaf SHAPE is correct and readable: elliptic, blunt-tipped, with a drawn midrib and faint lateral veining, glossy highlight on the upper face. Arrangement is wrong: no branches are drawn at all, so nothing is 'bunched at branch ends'; ~30 leaves are scattered singly around the rim of a soft airbrushed green blob, at random rotations, not in opposite pairs. Two near-pairs at bottom-right are coincidental. No flowers of any kind (the harvest line also calls for small pale yellow flowers) — nothing yellow exists in the image outside the trunk brown.

CHASSIS CLAIM — CONFIRMED. I opened Mangosteen.png alongside. Identical construction: same straight brown pole, same width, same rounded bottom, same ellipse shadow, same airbrushed green ball crown with elliptic leaves ringing the rim. The only delta is harvest tokens (purple spheres vs dark slivers) and slightly larger leaves / broader crown on the Mangrove. Neither tree honours its own crown must-read (Mangosteen's spec asks for a narrow CONICAL crown and also gets a ball). The judge is right that this is one shared tree chassis with the harvest swapped.

BAND: FAIL stands. The one feature that makes a mangrove a mangrove — the stilt-root scaffold standing in water — is entirely missing, and the propagules are present only as dark voids. Stripped of both, this render is generic broadleaf tree #2 and cannot be told from Mangosteen. This is not a polish-level gap; the silhouette has to be rebuilt from the roots up (arching prop roots meeting a water plane, trunk lifted clear) before leaf/propagule tuning is worth doing.

rows.readsAs: a broadleaf tree with ragged star-shaped leaves
rows.defect: The harvest is missing: there is no spile and no bucket anywhere on the trunk, so nothing on the render says sap. rows.readsAs: a woody rosemary or heather bush with pink buds
rows.defect: This is drawn as the rosemary the reference note explicitly warns it is not. The render is a woody twig-fan with short grey-green needle leaves along the rods and small pink tulip-shaped buds capping the tips — no flat basal rosette of spoon-shaped leaves, no bare wiry branched stems fanning out level on top, and no dense mist of tiny papery blue-violet florets. The flower colour is pink, not blue-violet, and the whole silhouette is the Labrador Tea / Lingonberry shrub chassis again.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as sea lavender: a flat ground rosette of leathery spoon leaves with bare wiry stems branching up into a level flat-topped spray of a hundred tiny papery blue-violet florets.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, and the original claim is accurate in nearly every particular; I tried hard to find the must-reads hiding somewhere small and they are not in the file. What is actually drawn (440x440, ~9,600 ink px on the dark plate): a single woody brown trunk, rgb(107,74,46), rising from a bare dark ground ellipse at y~300-320 and running unbroken from y=341 up to y=98, splitting at about y=290 into 6-7 upward-fanning woody twigs in a vase/V spread. Along those twigs sit ~30 short straight blade/needle dashes in grey-green, rgb(120,136,120) with a darker rgb(102,119,106) shading pass, all of them stem-borne between y=99 and y=290. At the twig tips are ~14 discrete little closed tulip/teardrop buds in pale pink-mauve, rgb(208,168,192), occupying only 539 px and confined to y=86-156 at staggered heights, each a solid ~6x9 px shape with a lighter facet - individually countable ornaments, not a mist. CORRECTIONS/CONFIRMATIONS TO THE CLAIM: (1) 'small PINK tulip buds' is exactly right - the measured mean is rgb(208,168,192), R>B>G, a rose-mauve. There is no blue-violet pixel anywhere in the image; the harvest colour is simply the wrong hue family, not merely desaturated. (2) 'the Labrador Tea shrub chassis recoloured' is CONFIRMED, not rhetoric: I opened earth-flora/Labrador_Tea.png side by side and it is the same construction - same single brown trunk on the same shadow ellipse, same multi-stem woody twig-fan at the same spread and height, same stem-borne blade leaves, differing only in leaf density and in what is stuck on the tips (white domed clusters there, pink buds here). (3) The three must-reads: FLAT BASAL ROSETTE OF SPOON LEAVES - absent entirely. I cropped and 3x-upscaled the bottom 200 rows specifically to look for a small rosette tucked at the soil line; below y=290 there is nothing but bare trunk and the shadow ellipse. No leaf-coloured pixel exists below y=290 at all, and no leaf in the image is spoon-shaped or stalked - every one is a straight parallel-sided dash. BARE BRANCHED WIRY FLOWER STEMS FANNING OUT LEVEL ON TOP - absent. The stems are thick tapered WOODY twigs, not wiry; they are clothed in leaves rather than bare; and the tips are at markedly staggered heights (buds spread over y=86 to y=156, a 70px vertical scatter across a 250px-tall plant), so there is no level flat-topped corymb silhouette. DENSE MIST OF TINY PAPERY BLUE-VIOLET FLORETS - absent; ~14 large countable pink buds instead. The one thing that survives is the branching-spray gesture in the abstract, which is not enough. Since the packet note states outright that the flower sprays, not the leaves, carry the identity, and the flower sprays are the element that is most wrong, this reads as a generic bog shrub / a rosemary-family lookalike and not as sea lavender (Limonium). FAIL stands. Fix direction: throw the woody chassis away - this needs a ground-hugging rosette of dark bronze-green spoon blades tapering to long stalks, and from its centre a naked thin much-branched stem system whose branchlets terminate at one common height, dusted with a haze of many tiny blue-violet papery florets.

rows.readsAs: a lollipop tree hung with oranges or apricots
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are absent: the bark is a flat untextured brown pole with no mottled grey flaking, and there is no fallen fruit on the ground — all four yellow fruits are pinned inside the canopy, which is the one place the reference does not put them. The crown is the shared soft round blob rather than a broad spreading crown, though the feathery pinnate leaf sprays are at least a distinct leaf glyph for this family.
rows.fix: Mottle the trunk with grey flaking bark patches and scatter a heap of fallen yellow fruit on the ground under the canopy so the harvest reads from the base of the frame.

rows.readsAs: a squash or gourd vine with one small ribbed fruit
rows.defect: The fruit is far too small and sits up on the vine mid-frame rather than resting heavy on the ground, and its skin is drawn with vertical pumpkin ribs and no netting, so it reads as a mini gourd rather than a netted melon. The leaves are sharply cut star-shaped blades with pointed fingers rather than the rounded shallowly lobed rough leaf of a cucurbit, and they carry no grey hairy texture. Tendrils are present as small dark coils, which is the one must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Enlarge the fruit to sit heavy on the ground at the base of the frame with a tan netted rind, and round off the leaf lobes into broad shallow scallops with a grey hairy surface.

rows.readsAs: a generic ladder-leaf weed stem with a pink speck on top
rows.defect: The warty pod bursting with white silk — the feature everyone knows milkweed by — is not on the render at all. The flower is reduced to one tiny flat pink half-disc perched on the very tip, far too small to read as a drooping domed umbel and not drooping at all. The leaves are paired, but they are small neat identical ovals stacked in a rigid mechanical ladder of nine tiers with no visible pale midrib, so they read as fern or vetch rather than large thick oblong milkweed leaves. Same stem-ladder chassis as Licorice Root.
rows.fix: Add a split warty pod spilling a plume of white silk on the upper stem and enlarge the flower into a nodding dusty-pink ball umbel; widen the leaves and draw a pale midrib down each.

rows.readsAs: a generic leafy stalk with one daisy on top - a wheat ear, or a young sunflower
rows.defect: The circular perfoliate leaf that the stem passes through - the entire identity of this plant - is completely absent. What is drawn is chassis A: a ladder of eleven identical pale-green oval blades up a straight stem, with a single white daisy floating above the top pair. There is no saucer, no basal spade leaves on long stalks, and the flowers are one showy daisy rather than a tiny spray rising out of a disc.
rows.fix: Draw one large flat round disc leaf seen near face-on with the stem visibly piercing its centre, and put a small spray of pinhead white flowers standing up out of that disc; drop the leaf ladder entirely.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but the other judge's shape description needs correcting in two places. What is actually on the canvas (440x440, measured plant bbox x177-257, y72-353): a single perfectly straight vertical olive stem carrying SEVEN TIERS OF OPPOSITE PAIRED ELLIPTICAL LEAVES — 14 leaves total, each a plain pale-green ovate blob with a faint V-shaped vein scribble, all identical in size and all angled ~30 degrees upward, stacked at even intervals like the rungs of a ladder. On top of the bare upper stem sits ONE large white composite daisy: ~12 blunt white ray petals around a solid brown-gold disc centre. At the base the stem meets a plain black cast-shadow ellipse with nothing else — no basal rosette, no long-stalked spade leaves.

The packet's two mustReads are: (1) a circular leaf pierced by the stem like a saucer, (2) tiny white flowers standing up out of that saucer. NEITHER is present. I zoomed 5x on the top of the plant and 3x on the whole stem specifically hunting for a small or partially-occluded perfoliate disc — there is none anywhere. Every leaf is a lateral ellipse attached at its narrow end to the side of the stem; not one leaf is a round plate with the stem emerging through its middle, which is the ENTIRE reason Claytonia perfoliata is recognisable. The reference leaf note (round disc + long-stalked basal spade leaves) and the harvest note (a small SPRAY of tiny white flowers rising from the middle of the disc) are both unrepresented.

CORRECTIONS to the original claim:
- 'reads as a wheat ear' is wrong. Wheat has no broad leaves and no terminal daisy. The leaf arrangement here is OPPOSITE PINNATE — the silhouette reads as a vetch / locust / young ash frond, or a generic pinnate-leaved herb, with a lawn daisy pasted on the tip. 'Young sunflower' is closer but still off, since a sunflower has large alternate cordate leaves, not 14 identical opposite ellipses.
- The flower is not merely 'a single white daisy' loosely described: it is a full composite capitulum with a brown disc floret centre, i.e. an Asteraceae head. Miner's Lettuce is a Montiaceae with 5-petalled tiny white flowers in a loose cyme. So the harvest is drawn as the wrong FLOWER FAMILY, not just the wrong count.
- ADDITIONAL DEFECT the original judge did not report: the aspect is badly off. Packet calls for aspect 1.1 (roughly as wide as tall). The drawn plant measures 80 wide x 281 tall = aspect 0.28, roughly 4x too narrow. Miner's Lettuce is a low spreading clump of disc leaves, not a tall thin wand.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs a bespoke silhouette, not a tweak. Draw a low spreading clump (aspect ~1.1): several long bare petioles fanning up from the base, each terminating in a ROUND FLAT PLATE seen at a slight three-quarter tilt with the petiole visibly continuing through the plate's centre and a short flower stalk rising from that pierce point, topped by a loose spray of 4-8 tiny 5-petalled white flowers (no brown disc, no ray-petal daisy). Add a few long-stalked spade-shaped basal leaves at ground level. Retire the shared 7-tier opposite-leaf ladder chassis entirely for this species.

rows.readsAs: a dark green bottlebrush or a small conifer with a purple bud at the tip
rows.defect: The hooded flower spike, which is the whole reason this plant has its name, is reduced to three or four tiny flat purple lozenges peeking above the foliage - no helmet, no hood, no spike. The leaves are not deeply palmately cut with narrow toothed segments; they are the standard chassis A blades, blunt and undivided, packed into a dense grey-green column that swallows the stem. Nothing about this says Aconitum.
rows.fix: Make the flower spike the dominant top third of the silhouette - a stiff vertical raceme of six to ten clearly separated blue-purple flowers, each with a rounded helmet hood arching over the lower petals - and cut the leaves into narrow finger-like segments.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 6x and 12x magnification on the crops. VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and the fix brief must not be written against them.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. The asset is a tall narrow green column (~130px wide x ~340px tall in a 440px frame, aspect ~0.38, so the 0.35 aspect target is met). The column is built from about TWELVE identical full-circle leaf whorls stacked one on top of the next, each whorl a radial fan of 11-13 narrow lance-shaped pointed segments radiating from a single central node. Below the column is a bare dark-green stem to the ground shadow. Above the column, poking clear of the topmost whorl, is a short green stemlet carrying FOUR purple blossoms.

CORRECTION 1 - FLOWER COUNT AND SHAPE. There are FOUR flowers, not three, and they are not 'lozenges'. Each is a flat-topped, straight-sided, round-bottomed shield/bell about 12x16px, alternating left-right up the stemlet. The judge's count and shape word are both wrong.

CORRECTION 2 - THE LEAVES ARE NOT UNDIVIDED LADDER BLADES. This is the judge's biggest error. Zoomed in, every whorl is unmistakably a PALMATE FAN of narrow, sharply pointed, individually shaded segments radiating from one point, each with a visible midrib crease. 'Finely divided leaves' is arguably the ONE must-read this asset satisfies. Do not send this back to be re-divided; it is already divided.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. (a) THE HOOD IS GENUINELY ABSENT - this is the defining identity and the reason for the name. Each blossom is a single uniform flat fill (roughly #5B4FA8) with zero internal modelling: no helmet arching over anything, no lower petals or sepals for a hood to cover, no shading break, no highlight, no stamens. There is nothing 'over the rest' because there is no rest. mustRead 'each flower with a helmet-like hood over the rest' = not readable at any zoom. (b) THE SPIKE IS VESTIGIAL - four blossoms spanning ~40px of a ~340px plant, i.e. under 12% of height, sitting on top of a foliage mass that occupies ~65% of it. Aconitum reads as a tall dense flower spike standing well clear of the foliage; here the flowers read as three or four stray buds. mustRead 'stiff upright flower spike' is technically present (it is upright and on a stem) but is so under-scaled it does not carry the read. (c) LEAF COLOUR AND ARRANGEMENT ARE OFF-SPEC - the foliage is a pale grey-sage green, not the specified dark glossy green, and a dozen identical stacked radial whorls is a bottlebrush/lupine/horsetail arrangement, not the few open alternate palmate leaves of a monkshood stem.

SO the judge's headline read is right for the wrong reason: it does read as a dark bottlebrush or narrow conifer, but the culprit is the WHORL-STACK ARRANGEMENT plus the pale colour, not undivided leaves. FIX BRIEF: keep the palmate segment fans, thin them to 4-6 alternate leaves on an open visible stem, darken to glossy deep green, and rebuild the top third as a real dense spike of 10-14 modelled flowers, each with a distinct arching helmet sepal shaded darker on its underside and overhanging two smaller lower petals.

rows.readsAs: a twiggy brown berry bush - a hawthorn or a barberry
rows.defect: The must-read is an upright broom of BARE GREEN jointed stems with no foliage at all. What is rendered is the opposite: the main structure is chocolate-brown woody twigs, the green appears only as small scattered leaf slivers pinned along them, and the harvest is drawn as five clusters of glossy RED berries. Papery cones and the swollen nodes with their paper collar of scales are nowhere on the image.
rows.fix: Recolour every stem to yellow-green and make the stems themselves the whole plant - long straight leafless rods with a visible dark banded joint every so often - and replace the red berry pom-poms with small papery tan cones sitting at those joints.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4x zoom on the upper canopy and the base. The FAIL stands, and the judge's description is substantially correct, but two parts need correcting and one credit is missing.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A single solid chocolate-brown trunk (~14px wide) rises from the ground shadow and splits at about 30% height into roughly seven brown woody stems that fan upward and outward. Every load-bearing stem is the same saturated mid-brown (approx #8a5a35) from base to tip — there is not one green stem in the render. Across the whole plant are roughly thirty short, straight, uniform-width olive/pale-yellow-green line segments (approx #b9c47e) set at random angles. Five clusters of glossy spherical red berries (approx #b8302c with white specular dots, 5-7 spheres per cluster) sit on brown pedicels: one top-left, one mid-left, one dead centre, one upper-right, one far-right at the silhouette edge.

MUST-READS, ONE BY ONE. (1) 'Upright broom of bare green jointed stems' — HALF present, and the judge gave no credit for the half that works. The broom ARCHITECTURE is correct: many near-parallel stems rising from one basal trunk, aspect ~1, an upright besom silhouette. What fails is everything about the stems themselves — they are brown not green, and they carry zero segmentation: no joints, no rings, no colour breaks, no diameter changes anywhere along their length. (2) 'Swollen nodes with a paper collar of scales' — COMPLETELY ABSENT. I looked along every stem at 4x; there is not a single node mark, band, bump or collar on the plant. This is the defining Ephedra read and it is not attempted. (3) 'No foliage at all' — VIOLATED. The green slivers read unambiguously as needles/leaf blades, so the plant is foliated when its identity depends on being leafless. (4) Harvest 'small papery cones at the joints' — WRONG ORGAN. Glossy red spheres with specular highlights are berries; nothing papery, tan, or scale-textured appears anywhere.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM. (a) The judge wrote 'woody twigs CARRYING scattered leaf slivers'. They are largely not carried — most green segments do not touch a stem at all. At least six float in open canvas with no attachment (clearest: the segment at the far right of the canopy, and three to the right of the trunk near the base, all suspended in empty space). The green marks are free-floating strokes stamped over the plant, not leaves attached to twigs; whatever generates them is not anchored to the branch geometry. That is a distinct defect from 'wrong leaves' and needs fixing separately. (b) 'Reads as a hawthorn or barberry' is fair but slightly narrow — with five red berry clusters on bare brown wood and thin needle-like green marks it reads as a generic red-berried woody shrub (hawthorn / barberry / redcurrant); nobody would name Ephedra.

WHAT THE FIX MUST DO, given the broom form is already right and does not need re-deriving: recolour every stem yellow-green to olive along its full length; delete the free-floating green slivers entirely (the plant must be leafless); break each stem into visible segments with a slightly swollen node and a small brown/tan papery scale collar at each joint; and replace the five red berry clusters with small tan papery cones sitting AT the nodes rather than on terminal pedicels.

rows.readsAs: a blueberry bush - the right call, if a slightly generic one

rows.readsAs: the same bush as Mountain Blueberry, with the berries repainted red

The leaves are long soft lance blades, not small thick leathery ovals with rolled-under edges and a notched tip, and the berry clusters sit as upright pom-poms rather than nodding at the shoot ends.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the chassis charge is verified rather than merely asserted. WHAT I SAW (440x440, then a 3x nearest-neighbour crop of x140-310/y80-350): one thick tapered brown trunk sitting on the ground shadow, its crown split into four or five short 'finger' notches from which five slender brown canes fan upward in a vase/broom. Along each cane, narrow lanceolate leaves roughly 4x longer than wide, pale sage-green with a lighter midrib stripe, alternating and angling up at ~45deg. At the tip of each cane, a tight rosette of five to six small scarlet spheres, each with a white specular dot, held ERECT on top of the tip. Silhouette is unmistakably taller than wide.

MEASURED (non-background bbox, thresholded on green/red/brown): Mountain_Cranberry 141w x 234h = aspect 0.60. The reference row demands aspect 1.5. That is not a near-miss; it is 2.5x wrong and on the wrong side of 1.0. The headline mustRead 'low evergreen creeping mat' is ABSENT — there is no mat, no ground-hugging spread, no runner; there is a woody standing trunk, which lingonberry/Vaccinium vitis-idaea does not have.

MUSTREAD 2 'small leathery glossy leaves notched at the tip' — ABSENT. The leaf stamp is a narrow pointed lance, acute at the apex with no notch, no rolled-under margin, no dark dotting beneath, and it is matte sage rather than dark glossy. It is also far too elongate: cranberry leaves are small obovate paddles about 1.5x long, these are ~4x.

MUSTREAD 3 'tight nodding clusters of red berries at the stem ends' — PARTIALLY present, and this is where the claim needs correcting. The judge implied the berries alone were changed; in fact the berry clusters ARE at the shoot tips and ARE tight and red, so a third of the identity does read. Two caveats gut it: (a) the clusters stand erect ON TOP of the tips, not nodding/pendent beneath them; (b) this is not cranberry-specific drawing at all — Mountain Blueberry in the same batch gets the IDENTICAL five-to-six-sphere rosette with the same specular dots, even though ITS row demands 'berries carried singly with a pale bloom'. The cluster is a generic harvest stamp, not evidence of cranberry identity.

CHASSIS CHARGE — CONFIRMED. I cropped Mountain_Blueberry.png at the exact same rect and compared. Same tapered trunk with the same fingered crown notch, same five-cane upward fan, same lanceolate sage leaf with lighter midrib at the same scale and the same ~45deg alternation, same tip rosette. Bounding boxes are nearly interchangeable: cranberry 141x234, blueberry 138x211. CORRECTION to the wording though: it is not a pure pixel-identical recolor. Cane angles, leaf count and overall density differ (blueberry is slightly bushier and shorter), so it is the SAME PARAMETRIC GENERATOR with jittered seed plus a berry-hue swap — which is the same defect, but a fix must change the generator's habit/leaf primitives, not just re-tint. Note also that blueberry is itself off-aspect (0.65 measured vs 1.0 required), so the shared chassis is dragging the whole Vaccinium pair toward one upright vase shrub.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO: kill the standing trunk entirely; lay a wide low mat wider than tall (target w/h ~1.5) of prostrate wiry stems creeping laterally with only short 2-4cm ascending shoots; replace the lance leaf with a small dark-glossy obovate paddle, ~1.5x long, notched or blunt at the apex with a visibly rolled-under margin; and hang the red clusters NODDING off the ends of the short upright shoots. Only after the habit and leaf primitives diverge does the berry colour carry any identity.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a palm leaf with a caterpillar on it
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The flowers are a vertical string of white beads running up above the foliage instead of a flat domed corymb - a flat-topped cluster is the diagnostic shape of this plant and there is no flat top anywhere. There is no square branching stem: it is one unbranched central rachis, chassis A again. The pale silvery bracts under the flower heads are absent, and the leaves are wide flat lance blades rather than narrow opposite leaves on a squared stem.
rows.fix: Replace the vertical bead spike with two or three wide flat-topped domes of pinhead white flowers held level at the top of branching stems, and blanch the leaves immediately under each dome to near-white.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size and again at 4-6x nearest-neighbour zoom on (a) the apex, (b) a mid-stem node block, plus pixel sampling. The FAIL stands, and the core of the claim is accurate, but two details of it need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: one perfectly straight, unbranched, round-tapered green stem running from a bare basal segment (~x=222, no basal leaves, no rooting mat) to the apex. Along it are ELEVEN pairs of sessile, narrow lance leaflets, and the mid-node crop shows both leaflets of a pair springing from the SAME node band on opposite sides — so the pairing is genuinely opposite, not alternate; the judge did not claim otherwise but it is the one leaf spec that is met. Every leaflet sweeps outward and DOWN-curving with a pale central highlight stripe, and the pairs are evenly spaced and evenly graded in length (longest low, shortest at the top), which is exactly the rachis-and-pinnae read of a palm/cycad frond. Correction to the judge's wording: it is not a FERN frond (no pinnules, no subdivision, no crozier); it reads as a single pinnate palm/ash-type frond. The gestalt conclusion is right, the organism named is slightly off.

MUST-READ 1 - square branching stems: ABSENT, exactly as claimed. The stem is a single smooth round taper of uniform width with faint darker node bands; zero side branches, zero axillary shoots, no angular/quadrangular facet or edge-highlight anywhere. Nothing about the stem says Lamiaceae.

MUST-READ 2 - flat domed clusters of tiny white flowers: ABSENT. Measured the near-white pixels: bounding box x219-228, y89-133 - a 10px wide by 45px tall column (4.5:1 TALL), 241 white pixels total (~1.2% of the subject). It is roughly eight to nine white lumps stacked vertically on the naked stem tip, the topmost slightly hooked over. So the judge's 'vertical string of white beads' is literally correct and geometrically confirmed - it is the inverse of a flat-topped corymb, which would have to be WIDE and SHORT and sit as a plate over the foliage. At thumbnail size it reads as a grub/caterpillar or a cattail spikelet clinging to the frond tip. Additionally: the flowers are pure blue-white (sampled 224,224,240 / 201,201,216) with NO purple speckling at all, so the packet harvest line 'speckled purple' is also unmet - the judge did not mention this.

MUST-READ 3 - pale silvery bracts under each flower head: ABSENT, as claimed. There is no bract collar, no whitened involucre, nothing beneath the white column but bare green stem. Worse, the packet's 'whitish dusting on the upper leaves' is inverted: sampling an upper leaf (200,140 = 91,108,90) against a lower leaf (200,290 = 130,157,124) shows the UPPER foliage is DARKER and duller than the lower, the opposite of the frosted-top-leaves cue that makes Pycnanthemum identifiable in the field.

VERDICT: three of three must-reads are missing, the flower - the single diagnostic organ - is drawn as the wrong shape class (erect spike instead of flat dome), and the habit is a frond rather than a branching square-stemmed herb. Nothing is 'present but small' or hidden anywhere in the frame. FAIL upheld.

FIX DIRECTION: replace the apical bead column with two or three WIDE, SHORT flat-topped domes (each ~3-4x wider than tall) held at the tips of a stem that FORKS at least twice into opposite pairs near the top; render the stem with a visible angular edge highlight so the square section reads; ring each dome with a collar of pale silver-white bracts; dust the top two or three leaf pairs pale/frosted so they are lighter than the lower leaves; and add fine purple speckling into the white florets.

rows.readsAs: a cycad or a young palm carrying one gourd
rows.defect: The crown is a rosette of stiff feather-pinnate fronds - exactly a cycad - where papaya needs deeply lobed palmate hands on long stalks. Only ONE fruit is drawn where the row asks for a cluster of small five-angled fruits hugging the stem, and it is a smooth round-shouldered gourd with faint ribs rather than sharply five-angled. rows.readsAs: a low rosette of round leaves with a red seed spike - a wild ginger or a sorrel, roughly right
rows.defect: The basal mound of rounded fleshy leaves reads well and is one of the few silhouettes in this batch that is not a shared template. The leaves are also plain round rather than kidney-shaped with a notch at the base.

rows.readsAs: five pink daisies on bare wires - a sparse aster sprig, not a herb mat
rows.defect: The plant has no foliage. The must-read calls for very small paired leaves crowded along creeping wiry stems, and what is drawn is a bare skeletal fan of straight yellow-green lines radiating from a central point with nothing on them - the crowded leaf mat that IS a thyme is absent. The flowers are also wrong in kind: five widely spaced ray daisies with pale pink petals and a dark eye, rather than dense rounded heads of tiny lipped rose-purple flowers. The low wide aspect is the only must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Crowd every stem with pairs of tiny dark grey-green oval leaves until the mat reads as dense foliage, and replace the daisies with tight rounded pompom heads of small purple-pink flowers at the shoot tips.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5x-20x crops of the 440x440 canvas. The verdict stands, but the stated cause is partly wrong and the correction matters for the fix.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a single ground contact point at ~(220,270) from which ~10-12 straight tapered dark-olive spokes radiate upward-outward in a symmetric V/chevron fan, ~230px wide x ~115px tall (so the aspect:2 'wider than tall' requirement IS met numerically). Five pale-lilac flowers sit on five of those spoke tips (far left, left, centre-top, right, far right). The remaining ~6 spokes terminate bare in empty background, so mustRead 3's 'flower heads at EVERY shoot tip' also fails on count, not just on form.

CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE'S CLAIM — 'no foliage at all' is not literally true. There IS a leaf layer and it is placed correctly: short PALE SAGE-GREEN straight bars, ~6-14px long and 1-2px thick, sit on the stems, and at several nodes near the base two of them radiate OPPOSITE from the same point (a proper opposite-pair node — visible around x=195-250, y=225-250 and x=145-175, y=235-250). So the opposite-paired arrangement the packet asks for is already encoded in the geometry. The defect is that each leaf is STROKED AS A BARE ZERO-WIDTH LINE with no blade: no oval outline, no width, no midrib, no taper. At 1x they read as crossing wires, and because they cross the spokes at shallow angles the whole base resolves as a chain-link / lattice mesh rather than a leafy mat. Value is also inverted: the leaves are LIGHTER (pale sage, ~#b9c49a) than the stems (dark olive, ~#5b6b2e), where the packet calls for dark grey-green leaves — so the foliage reads as highlight lines on twigs. Density is also far too low: roughly 2-4 leaf sticks per spoke with long bare runs between them, versus the 'crowded along creeping wiry stems' the packet requires.

FLOWERS — the judge is correct here. Each of the five heads is a 12-rayed daisy: separate pointed pale-lilac (#dcc0e2) ray petals radiating from a large filled gold-brown disc (~#7a6410, about 40% of the head diameter). That is an Asteraceae capitulum (aster / erigeron / echinacea), NOT a thyme head. The packet wants 'dense rounded heads of tiny rose-purple lipped flowers' — a compact pompom with no disc and no individual visible rays. The big brown disc is the single loudest wrong signal: it is what makes the plant read as a daisy. Colour of the rays is acceptably in the rose-purple family; hue is not the problem, form is. Heads are also isolated singletons spaced ~55px apart with black gaps between, so there is no massing.

SILHOUETTE — not a creeping mat. It is a radial spray from one point (a hand-fan / whisk), with an unbroken pointed apex at the ground and no horizontal creeping runners, no ground-hugging mass, no overlapping foliage volume. A viewer reads 'small daisy plant', not 'thyme'.

BAND: FAIL upheld. Two of three must-reads are absent as readable identity (paired leaves present as geometry but unreadable as foliage; flower heads are the wrong organ type), and the third (low creeping mat) is satisfied only by bounding-box ratio, not by form. FIX ORDER: (1) replace the flower primitive - kill the brown disc, replace the 12 separate rays with a dense clustered pompom of tiny lipped florets; (2) give the existing leaf sticks a filled oval blade 3-5px wide in dark grey-green and darken them below the stem value; (3) triple leaf density along each stem; (4) flatten and spread the fan into a creeping mat with horizontal runners instead of a single-point radial spray, and put a head on every spoke tip. The limb/branch skeleton itself is already the right topology - do not re-derive it.

rows.readsAs: a frost-killed or albino bottlebrush - a dead white plant
rows.defect: The entire plant is rendered chalk-white. The tall reddish-purple grooved stem is invisible under the foliage column, and the leaves are chassis A blades with sawtooth edges rather than deeply pinnately cut leaves with pointed lobes. It is Monkshood's silhouette with the saturation removed.
rows.fix: Paint the leaf upper surfaces dark green and show white only on the reversed, upturned leaflets, and expose a tall reddish-purple grooved stem running the full height.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, with two corrections to the stated cause. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS: a single erect axis, plant bbox x184-259 / y93-332 (76 x 240 px, w/h ~0.32 against the packet's aspect 0.5 -- slightly too narrow). Along that axis sit about seven stacked radial WHORLS of entire, undissected lanceolate blades, each whorl a full 360-degree rosette pinned at a node, so the silhouette is a symmetric bottlebrush / dwarf-conifer column, not a leafy herb. At the apex (y93-135) there IS a narrow beaded ivory-khaki spike with no petals -- that third must-read ('narrow drab flower spires with no showy petals') is genuinely PRESENT and the first judge did not mention it; it is the one thing the asset gets right, though it is cream-khaki (~174,175,145) rather than dull greenish-grey and it is the same value as the foliage so it barely separates as a distinct organ. COLOUR MEASURED over all lit plant pixels (n=11,216): 51.4% desaturated white, 42.3% pale grey, 6.2% green, 0.0% red/purple. So 93.7% of the plant is chalk white. CORRECTION 1 to the claim: it is NOT true that 'the whole plant is painted chalk white' -- there is a stem, and it is visible. A thin olive-green stem (~(71,84,45), 4-5 px wide) runs from the ground shadow up to the lowest whorl at y~300, and thin olive slivers show between whorls higher up. CORRECTION 2: that stem is smooth and untextured -- no groove, rib or flute is drawn -- and it is olive-green, not reddish-purple; the red-channel count of 0 confirms the judge's 'no reddish grooved stem' verdict even though they wrongly implied no stem exists at all. WHY IT STILL FAILS: the headline identity is the BICOLOUR leaf -- dark green above, white-felted beneath, so the plant flickers silver. Here there is no dark green surface anywhere on any blade, so there is nothing for the white to contrast against; the 'silver flicker' read is destroyed not by the white being present but by the green being absent. And the blades are entire -- no pinnate cutting, no pointed lobes, no rachis -- so must-read 1 ('silver-white undersides on CUT leaves') fails on both halves. Must-read 2 fails outright. Two of three defining must-reads absent, and the organism reads as a frosted bottlebrush / white conifer sprig rather than a tall cut-leaved herb. FIX DIRECTION: paint blade upper faces dark grey-green and reserve the chalk white for the reversed/undersides and blade edges only; recut each blade into 5-9 pointed pinnate lobes off a central rachis; re-arrange the leaves ALTERNATE up the axis rather than in radial whorls; recolour the stem reddish-purple and add vertical groove striations; keep the apex spike as drawn but shift it toward dull greenish-grey so it separates from the foliage.

rows.readsAs: a tropical tree with feathery leaves and small yellow fruit - close enough to a neem

The leaflets are straight and blunt rather than sickle-curved and toothed, and the loose sprays of small white flowers named in the must-read are entirely absent - only three yellow-green fruits appear. The trunk is a flat brown bar with no taper or bark.

rows.readsAs: a corn cob, or a green succulent column - certainly not a nettle
rows.defect: The leaves are featureless smooth green ovals overlapping so tightly that they fuse into one solid vertical cylinder with no gaps and no visible stem. Every diagnostic is gone: no heart-shaped base, no coarse teeth, no bristles anywhere, no tiered spacing between leaf pairs, and the drooping stringy green flower tassels in the leaf axils are replaced by a single cream bead spike sticking out of the top. A stranger would not name a plant at all, they would name a vegetable.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the full 440px render plus 6x/14x/18x crops of the crown, the base and the left silhouette edge. VERDICT UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and the fix brief must not be written against them.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a single vertical column of leaves running from y~110 to y~318, ~80px wide, dead straight sides. About nine OPPOSITE PAIRS of leaves are stacked with almost no vertical gap, each pair attached at a shared node on a visible dark-green central axis that runs the full height of the column. Below the foliage a bare, straight, flat mid-green stalk ~10px wide runs from y~318 down to the ground shadow at y~355. On top, a single erect cream/ivory knobbly spike ~10px wide x 45px tall stands straight up out of the leaf mass.

CORRECTION 1 - "no stem" is FALSE. There IS a stem: a clean bare green petiole/stalk stub below the leaf mass, plus a continuous darker-green midrib/rachis line threading every leaf node up the whole column. The real defect is not absence, it is that the stalk is a featureless smooth round-section green stick - not square in section, not grooved, and carrying zero bristles - and that it is completely buried by leaf overlap for the entire 200px of foliage, so the must-read "upright square bristly stem" never becomes readable anywhere on the plant.

CORRECTION 2 - "featureless" leaves is FALSE. Each leaf carries a broad pale specular highlight and faint diagonal lateral-vein hatching converging on its own midvein; the paint is not blank. And the must-read "opposite ... leaves in tiers" IS actually satisfied - the pairing and the tiering are the clearest thing in the image. The judge under-credited this.

WHAT GENUINELY FAILS: (a) LEAF SHAPE. Every leaf is an elongate lance-ovate blade ~40px x 16px with a tapered-rounded base and a blunt tip. Zero cordate/heart bases, zero basal lobes. The 14x edge crop shows the silhouette as one smooth continuous soft curve, scalloped only by leaf tips - not a single serration, tooth, or projecting hair anywhere on the outline. So "coarsely toothed heart-shaped bristled" is absent in all three of its terms. (b) HARVEST. The packet demands drooping stringy green catkin-like flower tassels hanging from the LEAF AXILS. What is drawn is one erect, rigid, cream-white beaded column standing TERMINALLY on the apex - wrong colour (cream vs green), wrong count (one vs many), wrong attachment (terminal vs axillary), wrong direction (erect vs drooping). Nothing hangs anywhere in the image. (c) The leaf packing is so tight (pairs touching, no internode showing) that the whole thing resolves as one solid green capsule.

GESTALT: the judge's "corn cob" is fair - a straight green cylinder of tight overlapping opposite leaflets on a central rachis with a pale spike on top reads either as a corn ear or as a single pinnate frond (sumac/fern). It does not read as a herb. Two of three must-reads are absent; the surviving one (opposite tiers) is present but degenerate. FAIL stands.

FIX BRIEF: open the internodes so the square bristly stem shows between tiers; give each leaf a cordate base with two basal lobes flanking the petiole, a serrated margin, and stubble bristles breaking the silhouette; and replace the terminal cream spike with several drooping grey-green stringy tassels hanging from the leaf axils partway down the stem.

rows.readsAs: the exact same palm tree as Mountain Papaya, with a grey fruit instead of a yellow one
rows.defect: The single defining fact about nipa - NO VISIBLE TRUNK, fronds erupting straight out of the water and mud, with the cannonball fruit head sitting at ground level - is contradicted on every point. The render gives it a tall thick brown trunk that occupies the lower two thirds of the frame, and parks a small grey fruit ball high in the crown notch. Worse, the trunk is identical to Mountain Papaya's down to the same amputated right-hand stub branch, and the frond crown is the same stamp; only the fruit colour differs. There is also no water or mud.

rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld. Packet mustRead: (1) no visible trunk, fronds erupting directly from water and mud; (2) huge upright feather fronds fanning from a single point; (3) spiky brown cannonball fruit cluster at the BASE. Aspect 0.7, form palm.

What is actually on the 440x440 canvas: a tall solid mid-brown trunk running from y~390 up to y~185 — roughly 47% of the frame height and the single most dominant shape in the image. At y~200 it forks; the right limb is a thick brown branch angling up-right that ENDS in a blunt rounded cut, poking clear of the fronds on the right side. I cropped and 4x-upscaled the fork region to confirm this: it is unmistakably an amputated stub branch, not a leaf petiole or a frond base. A crop of the bottom region (3x) shows the trunk simply terminating in a rounded capsule end sitting on a flat elliptical drop shadow — bare dark background all around it. There is no water line, no mud, no basal rosette, no clump of frond bases at ground level, and no fruit anywhere near the bottom of the frame. Must-read #1 is not merely weak, it is inverted: the asset's loudest feature is the exact thing the species is defined by NOT having.

The crown is a fan of pinnate fronds with fine regular leaflets, mid-to-dark green, radiating from the fork at y~190 and spanning x~120-320. This is the ONE must-read that partly lands — the fronds are correct in leaflet character and they do radiate from a single point — but they radiate from the top of a trunk rather than erupting from the ground, and they arch outward and downward like a coconut/cycad crown instead of standing as huge stiff upright feathers, so even #2 reads only halfway.

Corrections to the original claim, which is right in verdict but imprecise on the fruit: the judge said the fruit is 'parked high in the crown'. The fruit IS elevated and wrong, but it is not up in the frond canopy — it is a small cluster nestled in the crotch of the trunk fork at about y~180-205 (roughly 42% down from the top, i.e. mid-frame, well above ground but below the frond mass). More importantly the judge did not note that the fruit is also the wrong COLOUR, TEXTURE and SIZE: at 4x it is a bunch of ~12 smooth pale cream/beige-to-tan ovoid pebbles, reading like a small bunch of grapes or a clutch of eggs, about 30px across. The packet calls for a LARGE round woody head of tightly packed BROWN ANGULAR fruits — a spiky dark-brown cannonball. So the harvest fails on position, scale, hue and surface, not position alone.

The cross-reference to Mountain Papaya is accurate and I verified it by opening that PNG: same trunk width and taper, same fork at the same height, same up-right amputated stub branch with the same blunt rounded terminus, same radiating pinnate crown. The only differences are that Nipa's crown sits slightly lower and is a warmer/greener hue where Papaya's is paler sea-green, and the fruit swaps Papaya's single yellow ribbed ovoid for Nipa's pale cream cluster. So 'identical down to the same amputated stub branch' is fair — it is one shared chassis with a recoloured crown and a swapped fruit token, not a palm-specific build.

Band FAIL, not POLISH: the defining identity of Nipa is a trunkless mangrove palm whose fronds burst straight out of the mud with a woody cannonball head sitting in the water at their feet. This asset reads as a generic trunked tree-palm with a small pale berry bunch, so 2 of 3 must-reads are absent and the primary one is actively contradicted. Fix requires deleting the trunk and stub branch entirely, planting the frond bases at a mud/water line low in the frame, and replacing the pale pebble bunch with a large dark-brown faceted spiky sphere resting at ground level between the frond bases.

rows.readsAs: a thin fern sprig or a single sparse leaf - an almost empty frame
rows.defect: The pods are missing. This asset is named for its pods and the must-read leads with clusters of long bean-like green pods hanging from the stem; not one pod is drawn. There are no waxy flowers either, no aerial roots gripping anything, and no bark or host to climb - the plant floats free on a wire stem. The leaves are small flat dark slivers in a herringbone ladder, the opposite of thick fleshy waxy oblong leaves alternating up a vining stem. It is also the emptiest render in the batch, mostly background.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but ONE part of the claim is factually wrong and would send a fixer after the wrong thing.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THE FRAME. 440x440 canvas. The entire subject sits inside a bounding box of x 192-244, y 98-328 -- 53px wide by 231px tall, i.e. 12% of the frame width and an aspect of ~4.4:1 against the packet's specified 1.2. Nothing exists outside that box except a flat dark ground ellipse. Content: one dead-straight rigid vertical stem (mid-green, ~(44,81,33)) running the full height, carrying ~11 OPPOSITE pairs of narrow lanceolate leaflets swept up at ~30 degrees, all the same size, terminating in a bare lower third of stem that plunges into the shadow ellipse. That is a pinnate fern frond / horsetail sprig, full stop.

CORRECTION 1 -- 'Not one pod is drawn' is WRONG as stated. There IS a pod-ish element, and the judge missed it. At approximately x 202-232, y 108-126 (immediately above the topmost leaf pair, crossing the stem) there is a diagonal chain of THREE round lobed blobs running upper-left to lower-right, each with a darker core. Only visible under magnification with brightness boost -- at native size it reads as a smudge or a dead pixel cluster. Measured RGB inside it: (9,11,10), (15,14,10), (26,38,16) against a background of (5,6,12). That is a delta of 3-30 -- functionally invisible. And even when you CAN see it, it is wrong on every axis the packet asks for: dark khaki-brown/near-black instead of green; three short round lobes instead of long slender beans; one single object stuck on the stem instead of a hand-like hanging cluster; and it does not hang -- it lies diagonally across the stem, reading more like an insect or a fungal blight on the plant than a vanilla pod. So the practical conclusion ('the pods do not read') stands, but the fix is NOT 'add pods from nothing' -- it is 'the pod geometry exists and must be rebuilt as 4-6 long slender green beans hanging DOWNWARD in a splayed hand from a node, at 2-3x the current length, in a green light enough to separate from the background.'

CORRECTION 2 -- 'thin DARK herringbone slivers' gets the colour backwards. The leaflets are a fairly LIGHT sage green, measured (76,115,80) and (87,128,92) at blade centres -- lighter and more desaturated than the packet's 'flat mid-green, thick and waxy', not darker. They are the brightest thing in the frame after the stem. Darkening them would make the asset worse. A pixel scan of all 18,943 opaque non-background pixels finds NOT ONE where g exceeds r — the leaf mass is uniformly salmon/terracotta (~rgb 152,80,64 to 168,88,72), the branchlets are olive-brown where r>=g. The reference row demands leafColour 'mid green with red veins and stalks'. This is a total colour-channel inversion across the whole organism, not merely an omitted harvest, and it is why the bush reads as an ornamental pink foliage plant rather than a crop.

FIX DIRECTION: recolour the entire canopy to mid green with red veins and red petioles; make the stems upright, multiple and red; replace the 12-ray magenta daisies with clusters of fat waxy crimson calyces pressed against the upper stem — swollen ribbed cups with 5 pointed sepal tips, sized clearly larger than a flower head; if any bloom is shown at all it should be a small cream funnel with a dark eye, subordinate to the calyces.

The render is a SINGLE upright object occupying roughly x=195-250, y=110-315 of a 440x440 frame: a sealed, smoothly tapering spindle that narrows to one sharp apex point, surfaced with about eight flat vertical facet stripes (alternating lighter/darker sage bands) that read as ribs or folded husk. There is no branching anywhere on the silhouette edge - I traced both edges from apex to ground and they are two continuous unbroken curves with zero side shoots, zero notches, zero lobes. Against the packet row (mustRead: stout succulent finger-lobed leaves / flat-topped greenish-yellow umbel / low bushy clump on rock; note: interpreted as rock samphire, Crithmum maritimum), all three must-reads are absent, so the FAIL stands and the other judge's three-part absence claim is accurate.

Corrections and additions to their description, since the fix will be made against this text:
(1) Their read of 'closed flower bud or husked corn cob' is close but slightly off - the facets are flat vertical planes of uniform width running the full height with no cross-banding, kernel rows, or overlapping bract tips, so it does not read as a corn cob. What it actually reads as is a single upright agave/aloe leaf tip, a cypress cone, or a plain obelisk/bullet. That distinction matters: the defect is not 'the bud never opened', it is 'only one organ was drawn at all'.
(2) The judge did not mention the base, which is a second independent defect. The spindle does not resolve into a base - at y approx 313 it is cut off by a hard, perfectly flat, horizontal edge with visible square corners, i.e. the geometry is clipped by a rectangle rather than terminating in a stem, root, crown, or rock. Below that cut there is only an empty dark elliptical ground shadow. So the 'low clump wedged into rock' must-read is not merely omitted; the plant has no basal structure whatsoever.
(3) Colour is also off-spec: leafColour calls for glaucous blue-grey green, waxy and succulent; the render is a flat mid sage/eucalyptus green with no blue cast, no waxy specular, and no salt/glaucous bloom. Nothing in the surface treatment reads as succulent - the facets are matte and hard-edged, more like a folded leaf or carved wood than a fat fleshy segment.
(4) The harvest state is entirely unrepresented - no umbel, no umbel stalk, no rays, no seed heads, and no yellow-green hue appears anywhere in the image.

Rebuild required, not polish: needs a low bushy clump of several stems rising from a rock, each stem carrying thick blunt cylindrical finger-like segments (fat, rounded tips - explicitly NOT fennel's hair-fine threads), in glaucous blue-green, topped by at least one flat-topped greenish-yellow umbrella flower head so the silhouette breaks horizontally at the top instead of coming to a single point.

Top blob (~x218-250, y150-168) is TWO overlapping horizontal capsules with a bright specular highlight, reading as one fat horizontal lozenge lying ACROSS the straps. The straps have parallel sides, uniform width, and rounded blade tips -- this is exactly the blade/strap morphology the reference explicitly forbids. Caulerpa lentillifera has slender wiry upright axes so densely covered in stalked spherules that the axis is barely visible; here the axis IS the whole drawing and the spherules are three stickers.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM'S READING: 'spring onions' is not quite right, because there is no swollen white bulb and the base narrows to a point rather than widening. It reads as a clump of eelgrass / a tuft of chives / a leek silhouette. That does not change the verdict.

STRAY DEFECT NEITHER JUDGE FLAGGED: at the upper right of the crown (~x252-262, y82-105) a thin DARK, near-black diagonal line projects up and right beyond the green mass, above one strap tip. It is unlit, thinner than every other element, and reads as a rendering stray or an unpainted stem rather than part of the plant. Worth removing whatever the redraw does.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS: replace the wide blades with 4-7 thin wiry upright axes (2-3px), crowd each with 15-30 small translucent bright-emerald spheres on short visible stalks so the sphere mass dominates the axis, and run a horizontal creeping stolon along the ground from which two or three separate shoot clusters rise. FAIL is correct.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are mis-measured and one real defect was missed. What is actually on the 440x440 canvas (measured, and inspected at 3x/6x/8x crops):

LEAF MASS — bbox x62-377, y150-353 = 316 x 204 px. Eleven to twelve blades radiating from one basal point in a flat, near-bilaterally-mirrored fan (the left set is close to a mirror of the right set about the stem). Each blade is LANCEOLATE, roughly 3:1 length:width with an acuminate point, carrying a drawn midrib plus a herringbone of pinnate side veins. The judge's word 'narrow spear' overstates it — these are broader than agave spears — and because of the pale top-lit gradient the mass reads less like an agave/aloe rosette than like a white water-lily / chrysanthemum bloom. That correction does not rescue the asset: the identity leaf is a CABBAGE-SIZED OVATE blade, and nothing here is ovate.

MARGINS — CONFIRMED at 6x on the left-hand leaves: every edge is a clean straight-then-arc geometric contour. Zero crinkle, zero undulation, zero lobing, zero serration, not even a wobble in the antialiasing. The single defining must-read, 'huge thick wavy-crinkled ovate leaves with lobed undulating edges', is wholly absent. This is the reason the asset fails and it is where the fix must go: the blade OUTLINE needs deep undulating lobes and a rippled margin, and the blade must be re-proportioned to broad ovate (roughly 1.3:1), not lanceolate.

FLOWER — the judge's '~18px dome cap' is wrong in size and in form. The white element is x200-230, y80-90 = 31 x 11 px, and it is a hollow CRESCENT ARC (a rim), not a filled dome, sitting on a dark slate-grey triangular wedge (rgb 8,11,17 at its centre) that reads as a receptacle. Together they read as a tiny parasol or a pin head. It has no granularity, no individual florets, no branching. At 31 px it is 9.8% of the 316 px leaf-mass width, so 'dome of tiny four-petalled white flowers held in a broad FROTH above the leaves' fails: the fix is a wide, granular, many-floret cloud spanning most of the leaf-mass width, not a bigger cap.

STEM — not a hairline; it is 4-5 px wide (green pixels at x215-220). MISSED BY THE JUDGE: this stem is painted IN FRONT of the whole leaf mass, running unbroken from the flower head at y~90 all the way down to y~353 at the base, so it visually bisects the rosette into two mirror halves. That is an occlusion-order defect independent of the shape problem — the peduncle should emerge from behind/among the leaves, not overlay them.

COLOUR — the judge did not raise it, and it should NOT be changed. Body samples are ~rgb(140,168,168) to rgb(151,181,180), a cool desaturated glaucous grey-green that is roughly on-brief; it only reads white-ish because of the strong top-lit gradient across the upper blades.

MUST-READ TALLY: 'cabbage-sized crinkled blue-grey leaves' FAIL (no crinkle, wrong blade shape; colour ok). 'low spreading dome shape' PARTIAL — the mass is genuinely wider than tall (316 x 204) but its outline is a spiky star, not a dome. 'white flower cloud on top' FAIL (31 px pin). Two of three defining must-reads absent, so the asset does not read as Sea Kale.

The leaflets are pale silvery-white/light grey with dark outlines and a dark midrib, NOT the 'dark green, slightly leathery' the packet specifies. MUST-READ 3 — 'leathery rosette pressed to the mud': ABSENT. At 4x the base is bare: the stem runs straight into a flat dark elliptical cast shadow with no foliage at all. The lowest leaf pair sits ~45px ABOVE the ground line, so nothing is pressed to the mud. The claim is correct here.

rows.readsAs: a single opaque olive leaf blade, or a paper bag

Both long margins are perfectly straight lines and the top edge is a dead-flat horizontal cut that runs to the frame, so the sheet reads as clipped rather than terminated. The colour is a dull opaque olive-yellow with no translucency or glow, so the 'vivid translucent grass-green' read is gone too; only the tiny disc holdfast is correct.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim need correcting and one must-read the judge ignored is actually present.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a single tall goblet/funnel-shaped opaque blade on the dark canvas. It rises from a narrow stipe at the base (~x210-235) and flares smoothly outward to a maximum width of ~123px at the very top, where it is terminated by a dead-flat horizontal cut. Three to four pale hairline strokes run the length of the blade and converge at the base, reading unmistakably as a midrib plus lateral veins. A large dark cast-shadow ellipse sits on the ground plane, and inside it a small pale-green ellipse (~x200-250, y~345-356) sits where the stipe meets the ground.

MUST-READ 1 - paper-thin translucent green sheets: ABSENT. Sampled fill is fully opaque (alpha 255 everywhere) and runs rgb(144,155,85) at the top of the blade, (133,144,79) mid, (91,98,54) at y=240, (48,52,30) at y=340. That is a dull yellow-olive/khaki with R approximately equal to G, darkening to near-black toward the base under a heavy vertical shading ramp. The reference calls for 'vivid translucent grass-green, almost glowing'. The strong opaque top-lit-to-dark-bottom gradient is exactly what makes it read as a thick solid object rather than a membrane. Judge is CORRECT here.

MUST-READ 2 - ruffled lettuce-like frilled margins: ABSENT, and I verified this by measurement rather than by eye. Scanning left/right silhouette extents every 6px from y=78 to y=258 gives a perfectly monotonic profile with zero oscillation: L goes 158,159,160,162,163,163,163,163,163,163,163,163,163,163,164,165,167,168,170,172,175,178,181,184,187,190,193,196,199,201,204 and R mirrors it. A frilled margin would show sawtooth swings of 5-15px; this shows +/-1px of anti-aliasing noise in the straight section and then a smooth continuous taper. There is not a single crenulation, lobe or wave anywhere on either edge. Judge is CORRECT that the ruffle is absent.

CORRECTION 1 to the claim - 'both margins are dead-straight lines' is only half true. The margins are near-vertical and straight ONLY in the upper region (y=96 to y=156, where L holds at 163 and R at 277). Below y~160 both margins curve smoothly and continuously inward in a long concave taper down to the stipe. The correct description of the defect is 'perfectly smooth, unbroken vector-like edges with zero high-frequency detail', not 'straight lines'. A fix that merely bends the outline will not help; the edge needs a high-frequency wavy/lobed margin.

CORRECTION 2 to the claim - the judge said nothing about the veins, but the 3-4 pale converging hairlines are an independent identity-breaking defect and arguably the biggest one after the missing ruffle. The reference explicitly says 'no true leaves'; sea lettuce is a two-cell-thick membrane with NO midrib and NO venation. Drawing a midrib and laterals is what actively converts this into 'a single leaf blade'. Those strokes must be deleted, not just recoloured.

CORRECTION 3 to the claim - MUST-READ 3, the tiny disc holdfast at the base, IS PRESENT and readable. Zooming the base at 6x shows a distinct small pale-green ellipse seated under the stipe, clearly separate from the dark ground shadow. The judge's write-up implies nothing of the identity survives; one third of it does, and a fix pass should keep it.

CONFIRMED - the top is genuinely a flat horizontal clip. The blade first appears at y=77-78 spanning x=158 to x=281 with squared corners and no taper into it; at 5x it is a razor-straight horizontal terminus. It reads as the render being cut off by a bounding box, not as an organic apex.

BAND: FAIL stands. Two of three must-reads are absent, the single missing one (the frilled margin) is the entire visual identity of the organism, the palette is olive rather than glowing grass-green, and added false venation pushes the silhouette further toward a generic leaf. Fix priority: (1) rebuild both margins with deep irregular lettuce frills and let a few lobes fold/overlap, (2) delete the midrib/vein strokes, (3) reprofile to a vivid light grass-green with a much shallower value ramp and lighter overlap tinting to sell translucency, (4) terminate the top with ruffled lobes instead of a straight cut, (5) keep the existing base holdfast disc.

rows.readsAs: a broken render — a succulent rosette with a flower floating detached in the sky above it
rows.defect: The pink star flower is stranded in empty space roughly 80px above the plant with no stem, pedicel or contact of any kind between them; it reads as a stray sprite, not a flower in a leaf axil. Beneath it the plant is an upright bouquet of five fat rounded pale paddles, not a low mat sprawling flat and rooting at the nodes; there are no opposite pairs, no visible red-purple stems, and no narrow leaves.
rows.fix: Attach the flower to the plant — tuck it into an actual leaf axil against a stem — and rebuild the body as a horizontal sprawling mat of reddish stems running out sideways with plump narrow leaves in opposite pairs along them.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, and the floating-flower claim is confirmed at the pixel level rather than merely by eye. Measured on the 440x440 PNG: the pink flower occupies bbox x[206,234] y[97,120] (a 28x24px 6-petal star, mid-pink petals rgb 216,144,184 around a pale yellow disc rgb 243,230,168 — on its own it is the one genuinely well-drawn element). The green body occupies bbox x[128,312] y[189,310]. I ran a per-row median-subtracted scan of the intervening band (x150-290, y118-192) specifically to hunt for a faint stem the other judge might have missed: from y=122 through y=188 the maximum deviation from each row's own median is 3-5/255, i.e. pure vignette noise. There is NO stem, thread, hair, or connector of any kind. CORRECTION to their figure: the empty gap is 68px, not ~80px — the substance of the claim is right, the number is slightly overstated.

The body is confirmed as five broad ovate paddles radiating up-and-outward from a single point that tapers to a wedge and terminates at y=310 (rows 298-310 narrow 112px -> 22px, then nothing). That is a basal rosette / fan, i.e. a lotus- or aloe-like crown, not a mat. PARTIAL CORRECTION to their wording: they call it 'upright', but the overall silhouette is actually wider than tall — 185w x 122h, ratio 1.52. It is the individual blades that point upward. That still misses the packet's aspect: 2.4 is mandated (a low, wide, sprawling mat) and 1.52 is far too tall and compact.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE OTHER JUDGE UNDERSTATED: they wrote 'reddish nodes' as if only the nodes were missing. I ran a red-channel census over every non-background pixel (r > g+18 and r > 60): 291 such pixels exist and their bounding box is x[206,234] y[97,120] — exactly and only the flower. There is not one red-purple pixel anywhere else in the image. The packet's leafColour is 'mid green with red-purple stems', and no stem of ANY colour is drawn at all — the paddles simply fuse into each other at the base. So the failure is not just missing nodes, it is a total absence of the stem structure the species is built on. The leaf colour itself is also off: a pale desaturated sage/mint (sampled rgb 153,190,175 / 159,197,181 / 144,180,166) rather than mid green.

Must-read scoring: (1) 'low mat sprawling flat and rooting at the nodes' — ABSENT; upright fan converging to one basal point, zero nodes, zero roots, zero sprawl. (2) 'plump narrow succulent leaves' — HALF PRESENT; the blades read fleshy and thick, but they are broad ovate paddles roughly 2:1 length-to-width where sea purslane needs narrow oblong fingers nearer 4-5:1, and they are not in opposite pairs. (3) 'pink star flower tucked against the stem' — the star flower is drawn and legible, which is real credit, but it cannot be 'tucked against the stem' when no stem exists and it sits 68px away in open void.

One further flaw neither of us should let through: each paddle carries sharp straight-line angular vein strokes (visible as L- and V-shaped segments in the 3x crop) that read as cracks or fractures in the blade. Venation of that kind is wrong for a fleshy succulent leaf regardless of the other issues.

Two of three must-reads are absent and the asset reads as a generic succulent rosette with a detached flower decal, not as Sea Purslane. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond with one mauve daisy stuck on the end
rows.defect: This is the Sea Lavender image with a daisy swapped for the dome. Every must-read fails: the stem is ramrod-straight and unbranched, not sprawling and zigzag; the leaves are smooth pointed lances with entire margins, not thick pinnately lobed fleshy leaves with rounded lobes; there is one radial many-rayed daisy where the reference needs four-petalled cross-shaped flowers; and the fat two-jointed corky seed pods, which are half the identity, are nowhere in the image.

rows.verifyWhy: I looked at the full 440px render and then re-cropped and 5-6x upscaled the flower head, the mid-stem leaf zone, and the stem base, and I measured the plant bbox numerically. The FAIL stands: all three mustReads (fleshy lobed leaves / sprawling zigzag branching over sand / lilac cross-shaped flowers with jointed pods) are absent. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS: one perfectly vertical, unbranched olive stem running from a dark ground-shadow ellipse to the apex; roughly 11 OPPOSITE PAIRS of entire-margined, blunt-tipped elliptic blades in pale sage-grey-green, each with a drawn pinnate midrib-plus-side-vein pattern and faint pale speckling; and a single terminal flower head. Bare stem for ~60px between the shadow and the lowest leaf pair; nothing else anywhere in frame.
