rows.fix: Draw one flat upright sword-shaped scape and hang a short fat green finger off its side at about 60% height, angled 40 degrees out, then crimp the blade edges with a shallow wave.
rows.verifyWhy:
I tried to refute this and could not. Zoomed 7x-8x on the apex, the fan and the base, and ran a colour scan over the whole 440x440 canvas.

SPADIX — claim CONFIRMED, and it is worse than stated. A pixel scan for pale khaki/cream (the only non-green hue present) returns exactly ONE mass in the entire image: 7px wide x 38px tall, bbox x236-242 / y122-159. That is a single perfectly vertical column, aspect 1:5.4, sitting at the dead apex of the tallest stem and TERMINATING it. At 7x it resolves as ~8 stacked pale-tan bead lobes with visibly scalloped left/right edges — a plantain / timothy-grass / bottlebrush catkin. Reference demands 'a stubby green finger (spadix) angled out sideways from the flat stem' and the note explicitly says 'not from the tip.' Every one of the four properties is inverted: it is thin not stubby, tan-cream not green, vertical not angled, and apical not partway up. There is no second spadix hidden lower in the tuft — the colour scan proves it, and the base crop confirms it.

STEM — claim CONFIRMED. The stalk under the spike is a uniform-width round green rod ~5-6px, drawn identically to the leaf blades. There is no flattened scape, no leaf-like spathe continuing past the spadix (the stem simply ends in the beads), and therefore nothing for a lateral spadix to jut FROM. This is the structural root cause: the generator built a grass culm topped by an inflorescence, which is the wrong architecture entirely.

CRIMPED MARGIN — claim is directionally right but the stated cause is WRONG and this matters for the fix. The judge says 'no crimped leaf margin.' In fact a crimp WAS attempted, just in the wrong geometry: short bright-green rectangles are stamped across the blades. They are strictly axis-aligned HORIZONTAL bars regardless of blade angle, so on the diagonal and arching blades they cross at the wrong angle and overhang both edges — they read as ladder rungs / bamboo nodes, not as an undulating edge. Worse, several of these dashes float completely detached in empty background (clearly visible above and left of the tuft in the fan crop) — stray marks with no leaf under them. So the fix is not 'add crimping'; it is 'stop stamping perpendicular bars and displace the blade OUTLINE into a wave, and clip the marks to the blade.'

LEAF FORM — an additional must-read failure the judge did not name. 'Fan of upright sword leaves' is not met. The blades are constant-width tubes with ROUNDED blunt tips, no taper to a point, no midrib (reference asks for an off-centre midrib), and they arch outward and downward almost to horizontal like a spider plant or fountain grass. Non-background bbox is 256w x 185h, aspect 1.38 wide — the packet specifies aspect 0.4, i.e. tall and narrow. The silhouette is a low spreading fountain, not an upright emergent iris stand. All blades converge to a single point at the ground with no rhizome, no swollen fan base, and no planar (two-ranked) arrangement.

The judge's summary 'reads as a generic grass tuft' is fair but slightly imprecise: it reads specifically as an arching ornamental grass or spider plant topped by a timothy/plantain seed head. Nothing in the drawing says Acorus. Identity absent on three of three must-reads plus the aspect. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of dead brown sticks with pink beads glued on - a besom broom

Crossing them are roughly 45 pale rods of a single flat blue-grey (#808E97) — every one a perfectly straight line segment of uniform width with flat butt caps at BOTH ends, no taper, no curve, no scale texture, no sub-branching, no clustering. CORRECTION TO THEIR CLAIM (matters for the fix): the pins are NOT all 'stuck into bare brown poles'. A large fraction float completely detached in the background - the long rod at upper right crosses no stem at all, several at far left and lower left begin and end in empty space, and there are multiple free-floating X crossings of two pins with no wood at the junction. MUST-READ 3 'slender arching wind-blown branches' - ABSENT, and this is the most complete miss. There is not one curved path in the entire asset. ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE JUDGE DID NOT NAME: the drawn bounding box is 137 x 283 px = aspect 0.48, against a reference aspect of 1.1 (this packet uses width/height - Sweet Flag's narrow upright fan is 0.4). OVERALL READ: a bundle of dead sticks with pipe-cleaner tips - closest to a besom broom or a vase of dried pussy-willow. It does not read as a tamarisk and does not read as a living tree. FAIL upheld.

FIX DIRECTION: replace the straight pin layer with tapered, curved, scale-textured sprays parented to and following each branch; bow the branches into arcs with the tips falling away; expand the crown to aspect ~1.1; and rebuild the pink as many small soft-edged tapering plumes massed at and beyond the twig tips rather than five hard beaded rods.

rows.readsAs: the Tamarisk drawing recoloured, topped with the Tea flower sprite
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The trunk is a plain smooth brown cone with no papery white bark and no peeling sheets. The foliage is the same straight pale pin-twigs as Tamarisk, hard and spiky, not fine soft needles that read feathery in mass. The flowers are the identical white disc-daisies used on Tea, where tea tree's signature is a fluffy creamy bottlebrush spike wrapped around the twig.
rows.fix: Give it a white papery trunk with dark peel-curls, mass the twigs with fine soft needle foliage, and replace every daisy with a cylindrical fluffy white bottlebrush spike encircling a twig.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld. I zoomed the 440x440 PNG at 4x on both the crown (x130-310, y80-200) and the base (x160-290, y200-340) and compared it side by side against Tamarisk.png and Tea.png from the same family. All three packet must-reads are absent, and the shared-chassis diagnosis is correct with one correction to how it was stated.

MUST-READ 1 - 'papery white bark peeling in loose sheets': ABSENT and not merely faint. The trunk is a single flat mid-brown tapering column (a warm ~#8a5636 brown, darkening slightly toward the ground) that splits upward into six brown stems. At 4x the only internal detail is the set of vertical seams where the six stems converge into the bole - straight, parallel, hairline, dark-on-brown. There is no white or cream anywhere on the trunk, no lighter patch, no torn/curled sheet edge, no ragged silhouette. The bark reads as smooth plain wood. The judge described this correctly.

MUST-READ 2 - 'fine soft needle foliage': ABSENT, and the judge's description of the substitute is accurate. The foliage is roughly 40 discrete straight line segments in pale grey-sage (~#c2cbb4), each a rigid stick of uniform width with squared-off ends, laid across the stems in an X crosshatch at two repeating angles. They are not attached in tufts, they do not taper, they do not cluster, and they are the same width from end to end - they read as scattered pin-twigs or dropped matchsticks, not as needles and certainly not as a soft feathery mass. Colour is wrong too: the packet asks for 'bright fresh green, soft and feathery in mass' and the pixels are a cool desaturated grey-green. There is no massed canopy at all - the silhouette is open sticks against the background, so from thumbnail distance the plant reads as a dead or leafless winter twig-bundle.

MUST-READ 3 - 'creamy white fluffy bottlebrush flower spikes': ABSENT. There are exactly five flower heads, all at the tips of upper stems, and every one is a flat radial daisy: 14-16 pointed white petals radiating from a solid dark olive-brown centre disc. That is the identical sprite used on Tea.png two rows earlier in the same batch. A bottlebrush is a cylindrical brush of filaments sleeved AROUND a length of twig with the twig continuing past it; nothing here is cylindrical, nothing wraps a twig, and the flowers sit as terminal buttons. The woody seed capsules clustered around the twigs from the packet's harvest line are also nowhere on the image.

CORRECTION to the claim: 'It is the Tamarisk drawing recoloured' understates and slightly mis-states it. The geometry is not merely similar - it is the same shape program. Overlaying my Tamarisk base crop on the Tea Tree base crop, the trunk taper, the six-stem splay, the convergence seams and the pin-twig crosshatch occupy the same positions at the same angles. What actually differs is (a) a very slight palette shift - Tamarisk's twigs are a cooler blue-grey and its trunk a touch more saturated orange, Tea Tree's twigs are pushed a few points greener - and (b) the tip decoration, where Tamarisk's pink bead-spikes have been swapped for Tea's white daisy heads. So it is better described as the Tamarisk chassis reused near-unchanged with Tea's flower sprite pasted on, rather than a recolour: the recolour is the smallest part of what was done. Three species in this one batch (Tamarisk, Tea, Tea Tree) are the same drawing with different tip sprites.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS: (1) a white-to-cream trunk and stems with irregular pale sheets peeling off the edges so the silhouette is ragged, not a smooth brown column - this is the single loudest identity cue for Melaleuca and it is the one currently furthest from the target; (2) replace the crosshatched straight sticks with dense short fine needles crowded along the whippy twigs in bright fresh green, massed thickly enough to make a soft closed canopy rather than open sticks; (3) replace the five daisies with creamy-white cylindrical bottlebrush spikes sleeved along the upper twigs, with the twig visibly continuing past the spike, plus small woody capsules clustered on older wood below.

rows.readsAs: a tobacco plant - big leaves stepping up a stout stalk under a head of pink trumpets
rows.defect: All three must-reads are visibly present: huge ovate leaves clasping and stepping up one thick unbranched stem and shrinking toward the top, a terminal cluster of long pink trumpet flowers with flared mouths, and fine hair spikes bristling from the stem and leaf edges for the sticky texture. The only real miss is colour - the leaves are dark forest green where the reference calls for a pale matt yellow-green, which costs some of the sticky, sun-faded tobacco look.

rows.readsAs: a sago palm or cycad rosette sitting flat on the ground
rows.defect: The tree is missing from the tree fern. There is no fibrous brown trunk of matted old frond bases - the crown springs straight out of the soil, which is the one structure that separates a tree fern from bracken. The fronds are only once-divided with coarse triangular saw-tooth pinnae, so they read stiff and cycad-like rather than huge and lacy, and the crozier is a single tiny spiral tucked at the crown edge where it should be the readable harvest. The whole crown is also slumped left, leaving the right half of the frame empty.
rows.fix: Stand the crown on a tall shaggy brown fibrous trunk, split the pinnae a second time so the fronds read lacy, and enlarge the coiled croziers into two or three obvious brown-scaled spirals at the centre of the crown.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at full size and at 3-10x crops of the base, crown and two fronds; also measured the pixels. FAIL upheld, but two parts of the original claim need correcting.

MUST-READ 1 - 'fibrous brown trunk of matted old frond bases': GENUINELY ABSENT, and this alone is the failure. Below the crown there is only a small dark wedge-shaped nub, roughly 40px wide by 30px tall (x~200-240, y~290-320 in the 440px frame), sitting directly on a flat cast-shadow ellipse. I sampled it: RGB ~[46,61,36] at (218,300) and [75,98,54] at (210,295) - that is dark olive GREEN (r<g), the same shade used for the shadowed frond undersides, not brown, and it carries no fibre striation, no scale texture, no matted frond-base pattern. Everything below y=329 is bare background. So the judge is right that the crown springs straight off the soil and the 'tree' is gone.

MUST-READ 2 - 'umbrella of huge lacy fronds': FAILS on division, and the judge is right that they are only once-divided. Correction on the description: the pinnae are not 'coarse saw-tooth' notches cut into a blade - each frond is a genuine rachis (a broad tapering mid-blade with a darker shadow stripe) carrying separate, simple, undivided narrow-lanceolate pinnae set at ~35-45 degrees, shortening toward a blunt tip. They only read as saw-teeth at thumbnail scale. Nowhere is there a second order of division (no pinnules on the pinnae), so nothing reads lacy - it reads as cycad/sago or a young palm rosette, which is the judge's correct conclusion. Also note the arrangement is a ground-level hemispherical fan/rosette, not an umbrella crown: fronds radiate sideways and downward from one point on the soil.

MUST-READ 3 - 'coiled croziers at the centre of the crown': PARTIALLY PRESENT, and better than the judge implies but still short. There is exactly ONE crozier at ~(225,272), just right of the crown centre: a 2-3px light-green stroked spiral about 14px across (~3% of frame width), coiled ~1.5 turns on a short curving stalk that rises out of the crown. It is legibly a fiddlehead when zoomed and is even visible at full size, so it is not missing - but it is singular where the packet asks for croziers plural, it is bare mid-green with none of the specified brown scale wrapping, and at 14px it is far too small to carry the harvest identity of a species literally named 'Shoots'.

COMPOSITION - the judge's claim here is WRONG and should not be actioned as stated. The plant bbox is x=23-417 of 440, i.e. nearly edge to edge; left/right pixel mass about the frame centre is 24389/17136 (59/41) and the centroid is x=200 against a centre of 220. That is a mild left bias, not a slumped crown, and the right half is well populated - long fronds sweep out to x=417. What is actually empty is the UPPER-RIGHT quadrant, plus a large dead band across the entire top (y<110) and bottom (y>329): the plant occupies only the middle half of the frame vertically. That vacant lower band is precisely the space the missing fibrous trunk should have filled, and the vacant top is the space an arching crown lifted on that trunk would have filled.

FIX DIRECTION: add a tall fibrous brown trunk (matted old frond bases, vertical fibre striation, warm brown) occupying roughly y=200-400 so the crown is lifted into the top half; re-cut the fronds to at least twice-divided (pinnae bearing pinnules) so the mass reads lacy rather than palm-like; and add 2-3 croziers at 2-3x the current spiral size with brown scale wrapping at the crown centre.

rows.readsAs: a generic lollipop cherry tree
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive. The trunk is a tall straight bare pole running half the image height with no branching into thick limbs - the reference calls for a short brittle trunk splitting low into a few heavy limbs. The canopy is a ball of small round blobs, not big soft heart-shaped leaves. The fruit are tiny clustered red spheres tucked inside the foliage, where tamarillo fruit are large smooth egg-shaped red-orange bodies hanging clear on long stalks below the leaves.

rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld on the verdict; one of the three stated causes is described wrongly and must not be fixed as stated. I read the 440x440 PNG whole, then cropped and upscaled four regions (canopy 4x, trunk 4x, canopy/trunk junction 6x, a fruit cluster 11x) to be sure.

TRUNK - claim CONFIRMED and if anything understated. The trunk is a flat mid-brown capsule: perfectly parallel sides ~28px wide running from y~200 to y~390, zero taper, zero bark texture, a single flat fill with only a faint vertical gradient, and a ROUNDED PILL CAP at the bottom that floats above an elliptical drop shadow with no root flare and no soil contact. It is bare for its whole length - roughly 45% of the plant's height is naked pole. At the 6x junction crop the trunk does widen slightly into a short brown wedge as it enters the canopy, but it NEVER FORKS: there is no bifurcation, no limb, no crotch. The only linear elements above the fork point are 2-3 hairline dark-green twigs/petioles (visible upper-left and beside the right-hand fruit cluster) about 2px wide carrying single leaves. mustRead 'short brittle trunk branching into a few thick limbs' is absent in both halves - the trunk is neither short nor branched.

FRUIT - claim CONFIRMED. Four fruit clusters (upper-centre pair, left edge at y~165, lower-right at y~190). At 11x each cluster is 5-7 PERFECT SPHERES about 7px across, saturated pure red, each with a large round white specular dot, packed into a tight flat rosette that sits ON TOP of the canopy surface / on the upper face of a leaf. There is NO stalk of any kind - not a pedicel, not a peduncle - the spheres touch the foliage directly. Nothing hangs: the clusters are oriented upward and outward, never pendant below a branch. No ovoid/egg profile, no long axis, no orange in the ramp, no persistent calyx. mustRead 'long-stalked pendant egg-shaped fruit' fails on all three of its terms. This is the single most identity-destroying defect: red spheres in tight upward rosettes read as rowan/holly/coffee berries, which is why the whole asset resolves as a berry lollipop.

LEAVES - claim is WRONG as worded, though the must-read still only half-lands. They are NOT 'small round blobs'. There are ~30 leaves, each roughly 40-55px across on a 440px canvas (so each leaf is ~1/5 the canopy width - substantial, not small), and each is properly drawn: a broad ovate/obovate blade with a darker central midrib and 3-4 pairs of lateral veins branching off it, a soft painterly gradient light on the upper-left, and a slightly darker rim. So 'big soft leaves' is arguably satisfied. What actually fails is the SHAPE: every blade is a blunt, near-symmetric rounded oval - no cordate notch at the base, no basal lobes, no drawn-out acuminate tip, no asymmetric insertion. Tree tomato leaves must have a deep heart-shaped base and a pointed tip; these have neither. Do not 'enlarge the leaves' in response to the original note - they are already big enough; re-cut the outline to a cordate base plus a pointed apex, and give them the felted pale underside the packet calls for (currently both faces are the same mid green).

OTHER: the canopy interior is a soft blurred green mass with the leaves stuck around its perimeter, so the crown reads as a stuffed ball rather than as foliage hanging off limbs - this compounds the missing-limbs defect. Overall the judge's summary sentence ('generic lollipop cherry tree') is a fair description of what the asset reads as.

rows.readsAs: a dried ornamental grass tuft
rows.defect: The fountain of arching blades is there and reads correctly, but two of the three must-reads are missing. There is no dense pedestal mound of old dead thatch at the base - the blades converge to a bare narrow point on the soil. And there are no seed panicles at all, which is the harvest: nothing stands clear above the leaf fountain. rows.readsAs: a jasmine or star-flower vine twining on nothing
rows.defect: This is the Water Spinach drawing with a different flower sprite. The stem is a thin wiry green line freestanding in space - not a thick green rope-like succulent stem, and there is not a single aerial root, nothing gripping bark, no host at all. The leaves are small narrow lance blades, not the thick flat fleshy oblongs that make vanilla recognisable. The flowers are symmetrical six-point cream stars with no lip and no orchid asymmetry, and the hanging cluster of long slender green pods - the entire harvest - is absent.
rows.fix: Thicken the stem into a fleshy green rope running up a bark-textured trunk with white aerial roots clasping it, fatten the leaves into broad flat oblongs, and hang a bundle of long slender green pods from one node.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 3x-10x crops and again with a gamma-boosted full frame (nothing is hidden in the dark). What is actually drawn on the 440px canvas: a single freestanding sinuous S-curve stem, smooth flat mid-green, roughly 6-7px wide, rising from a bare ground-shadow ellipse; eight narrow lanceolate leaves with a pale midrib highlight, ~4-5:1 length-to-width, pointed tips, alternating left and right at the nodes; eight tiny dark-green appendages, one per node; and three cream-white radial star flowers with a pale yellow eye. That is the whole asset.

All three must-reads fail, so the FAIL stands. (1) 'thick green rope-like stem with aerial roots gripping bark' - the stem is a slender uniform smooth curve with no rope texture, no thickness taper, and there is no bark, trunk, post or host of any kind anywhere in the frame; the plant is planted in empty ground. (2) 'flat fleshy leaves alternating left and right' - only half met: the alternation is correct and clean, but the blades are narrow willow/jasmine lances, not the thick flat blunt oblongs (~2:1, matt succulent) the packet calls for. (3) 'pale greenish-yellow orchid flower' - the blooms are radially symmetric stars with no labellum, no lip, no column, no trumpet throat, no bilateral symmetry at all, and they are cream-white rather than pale greenish-yellow. The harvest state - a hanging cluster of long slender green pods - is completely absent; there is not a single pod on the plant.

Corrections to the original claim, which a fix brief needs:
- 'no aerial roots' is OVERSTATED. There ARE eight node appendages, but they are drawn as flat coiled SPIRAL TENDRIL CURLS (pea/cucumber style loops), rendered in a very dark green that is nearly invisible against the near-black background, and they curl into empty air gripping nothing. So the geometry hook exists at every node - the fix is to REPLACE those spirals with straight, thick, pale grey-green aerial roots that reach out and clasp a bark surface, not to add root geometry from scratch.
- 'six-point cream stars' is miscounted: the flowers have SEVEN narrow petals each, with a pale yellow center disc.
- 'narrow lance leaves instead of thick flat fleshy oblongs' is correct, but note the alternating left/right arrangement is already right - only the blade silhouette (too narrow, too pointed, too thin) needs changing.
- 'thin wiry freestanding stem' is correct in substance; add that it is smooth and untextured and reads as a herbaceous twiner, and that the missing host support is as much of the defect as the stem width.
- 'reads as a jasmine vine' is fair - star jasmine / a willow-leaved climber is exactly what it reads as. Nothing in the image says orchid or vanilla.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of celery or leeks standing upright
rows.defect: There is no blade anywhere in the image. It is the same splayed vase of straight tapering stalks used for Tamarisk and Tea Tree, recoloured olive - narrow tubular stems pinched at the base and fanning upward. The real failure is not width or midrib, it is that the blades carry no cylindrical read at all AND they have the wrong posture and taper: ~30 blades in a single symmetric radial fountain-fan, each tapering continuously from base to a fine whip tip and arching far out and downward past the horizontal. What is drawn is the agave / dracaena / spider-plant rosette silhouette — so the judge's summary read ('agave tuft with a daisy') is fair even though the stated cause is off.

BASE — must-read 3 FAILS, and the judge did not mention it. At 10x the entire fan converges to ONE narrow point about 10 px wide at the soil line, a fused solid wedge, sitting on a plain elliptical ground shadow. There are no bulbs, no bulb necks, no papery scales, and critically no CLUMPING: no second or third shoot, no offsets, one rosette from one point. 'Clumping tuft from clustered bulbs' — the third must-read and the second listed harvest — is entirely absent.

VERDICT. Two of three must-reads are outright absent (spherical lilac pompom; clumping tuft from clustered bulbs) and the third (hollow tubes round in section) is not readable. The asset reads as an agave/dracaena rosette with a daisy on a wire. FAIL upheld.

FIX DIRECTION: (1) replace the daisy entirely with a dense sphere of ~40-60 tiny six-pointed lilac starlets on short radiating pedicels from a common point, silhouette a slightly loose ball, not a disc; (2) cut blade count to ~10-16, make them near-parallel-sided cylinders that stand erect for most of their length and only nod at the tip, and give each a narrow specular stripe with dark rolled edges both sides; (3) split the base into 3-5 separate shoots emerging from a cluster of small pale bulbs with visible necks, not one fused wedge point.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon plum tree

The three dark purple figs sit in the leaf canopy at the crown edge, which is precisely where the note says they must NOT be: figs must stud the bark of the trunk and limbs.

rows.verifyWhy: Verified at 1x, at 3x nearest-neighbour on the whole 440x440 frame, at 5x on the trunk column (x170-300, y200-400) and at 3x brightness-boosted on the entire lower half to hunt for anything drawn in near-black. All three mustReads are absent, so the FAIL stands. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS: (1) TRUNK — one perfectly straight capsule of flat mid-brown, roughly 23px wide on a 440px canvas, EXACTLY the same width at the crown as at the base, shaded only by a soft left-to-right vertical gradient. It has a ROUNDED, PILL-SHAPED bottom cap that simply stops inside the shadow ellipse: no root flare, no taper, no buttress fins, no fused root lattice, no bark texture of any kind, and not a single fig on it. The brightness-boosted pass is decisive — at 3x gain the background reveals only the dither noise of the backdrop and the shadow ellipse; there is no faint aerial root, no secondary prop stem, no drop-root curtain anywhere in the frame. The trunk is also PALE-less: reference calls for a pale trunk and it is drawn a saturated cocoa brown. (2) CANOPY — a single soft elliptical green gradient blob sitting on top of the stick, with sprigs of foliage tufted around its rim and one small tuft where the trunk enters it. THERE IS NO BRANCH ARCHITECTURE AT ALL: not one limb, bough or fork is drawn: the trunk goes stick-straight into the blob, so there is no 'trunk and limb bark' for figs to stud even if they had been placed there. (3) FRUIT — exactly three fruits, all clustered on the LOWER FRONT EDGE of the leaf mass at roughly the same height, drawn as glossy dark purple-black spheres with a hard white specular highlight, each carrying a short brown PEDICEL at its top. CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM: (a) 'no buttressing, no fused root lattice, no aerial roots' — CONFIRMED, and stronger than stated: the trunk is not merely un-buttressed, it is a constant-width capsule with a rounded end, which reads as a lollipop stick rather than any kind of tree base. (b) 'a small blob crown' — IMPRECISE. The crown is not small in absolute terms; it spans roughly half the canvas width (x105-x330) and is wider than tall. The real defect is that it is a featureless lollipop mass carried HIGH on a long bare stick, with no horizontal spreading boughs and no layered limb tiers, whereas a strangler fig must read as a massive low dome resting on a mass of wood. Fixing this by enlarging the blob would not fix the read: the missing thing is limb structure, not crown area. (c) 'figs hung in the leaf canopy rather than studding trunk and limb bark' — CONFIRMED and understated: each fruit has a visible drawn stalk, i.e. the art asserts stalked twig-tip fruit, the precise OPPOSITE of the cauliflory the note demands (figs sitting directly on the wood). The colour is also wrong: harvest calls for green-to-red figs, these are damson purple-black with a plum-like specular. (d) ONE DEFECT THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NAME — the foliage is wrong too. The reference asks for alternate leathery OVAL leaves with a short drip tip in dark glossy green; what is drawn is light-to-mid green sprigs of deeply serrated, many-pointed lanceolate leaflets radiating in fans, closer to a hemp or sumac frond than to any fig leaf. So the 'cartoon plum tree' read the judge reported is right, but the leaf shape contributes to it as much as the fruit does. FIX ORDER: give the trunk a flared buttressed base of several fused vertical root ribs meeting the ground; hang at least a few thin aerial roots from the outer limbs to the soil; draw 3-5 spreading horizontal boughs out of the trunk top so a canopy has something to sit on; move the figs OFF the leaves and onto the trunk and bough bark as stalkless green-to-red knobs in tight clusters; and replace the serrated fan sprigs with entire dark glossy oval leaves ending in a short drip tip.

rows.readsAs: a clump of ornamental grass with a small white pill floating above it

rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, with two corrections to the stated cause. CORRECTION 1 - the flower head is described wrongly. It is not a 'smooth featureless white pill'. At 8x it is a thin white CRESCENT / mushroom-cap arc: a solid pure-white dome with a hard flat lower edge, sitting on top of a darker green cone-shaped wedge, the whole assembly about 28 px wide and ~12 px tall. The differences are only parametric - Onion's blades are shorter, stiffer and spread less, and its head carries a faint lilac tint where Garlic's is pure white. VERDICT: two of the three identity signals (broad lily blades; starburst of individual white star flowers) are absent, and the leaf shape is the one the reference explicitly forbids. rows.readsAs: a hosta or cabbage rosette with a small pink flower spike

rows.readsAs: a small berry bush with glowing pale-green fruit — not a tree at all
rows.defect: The form is specified as a tree and every must-read is bark- or leaf-specific, yet this is drawn on the same broom-shrub chassis as Wild Blueberry and Wild Chili: a fused brown wedge base, straight unbranched canes, tiny paired slivers for leaves. There is therefore no trunk to carry the smooth mottled flaking copper-and-grey bark. The leaves show no quilted impressed parallel veining, and the fruits are plain glowing spheres with no dried calyx crown at the tip.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at native 440px and again at 2x/7x/9x/10x crops of the base, the leaf mass and the fruit row, plus a five-way side-by-side strip against Wild_Blueberry, Wild_Chili, Wild_Mango and Wild_Fig. FAIL UPHELD, but two of the judge's four stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as written.

CONFIRMED — WRONG CHASSIS, and this is the whole defect. The strip is decisive: Wild_Blueberry, Wild_Chili and Wild_Guava are pixel-for-pixel the same construction — a short conical stub base, a splayed fan of 4-5 straight vertical brown wands, small lance leaves ranked along each wand, and exactly one fruit ball impaled on the tip of each wand, with the tips stepping down left-to-right to make a shallow V-shaped top. Only fruit hue (blue / red / yellow-green) and leaf density differ. Meanwhile Wild_Mango and Wild_Fig — which carry the SAME `form: tree` as Guava — are on the real tree chassis: a tall bare trunk with a wide rounded canopy sitting on top of it. So Guava is the only one of the three specified trees rendered as a berry shrub. Footprint is roughly 145 wide x 230 tall (aspect ~1.6 tall), not the aspect 1 the packet asks for; Mango and Fig are correctly wide and round. At thumbnail scale this asset is a blueberry bush recoloured yellow.

CORRECTION 1 — "there is no trunk" is FALSE. A trunk IS drawn: a tapering tan/clay stub about 14px wide by 45px tall sitting between the ground shadow and the point where the wands splay, and the wands themselves are broad brown stems visible through the whole foliage mass. There is plenty of woody surface. What is absent is any TEXTURE on it — the stub is one flat uniform mid-tan fill with a soft vertical gradient and three darker fissure streaks near the top where the wands separate; no mottling, no flaking patches, no patch-work of copper against grey, no colour variation at all. So the must-read "smooth mottled flaking copper-and-grey bark" genuinely fails, but the fix is to paint bark onto an existing surface (and to make that surface a real single trunk with a crown), not to add a trunk that is missing.

CORRECTION 2 — "leaves show no quilted parallel veining" is FALSE. At 9x every leaf blade carries 4-6 darker oblique strokes running from the midrib out to the margin, roughly parallel to one another, plus a paler midline — this is precisely the impressed parallel side-vein treatment the packet asks for, and it is the one must-read component that IS present and readable. Do not spend the fix budget re-adding it. What the leaves actually get wrong is elsewhere: they are narrow willow-lance blades set ALTERNATE/spiralled along each wand rather than the broad OPPOSITE oblong pairs specified, and the colour is a washed pale sage-grey rather than matt mid-green (the pale downy underside tone has been applied to the whole blade).

CORRECTION 3 — "plain glowing spheres" undersells them; the calyx point stands. The five fruits are correctly round, correctly pale yellow-green, correctly sized, and each carries a soft specular highlight on the upper-left — colour and form read as guava. The real fault is the apex: each fruit has a straight brown stalk stub emerging from the TOP and pointing upward, which is the wand tip continuing through the fruit, i.e. the berry-finial rule of the shrub chassis. There is no dried 4-5 lobed calyx crown anywhere, and the geometry is backwards — a guava hangs from its stalk with the persistent calyx remnant at the free apex, whereas these sit skewered on upright sticks. All five fruits also sit in a single row at the outermost tips with none borne inside the foliage.

NET: 1 of 3 must-reads present (parallel veining), 2 absent (mottled flaking bark, dried calyx crown), and the organism reads as the wrong growth form entirely — a berry shrub, indistinguishable in silhouette from its Blueberry and Chili siblings. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: an orange tree

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but TWO parts of the stated cause are factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

CORRECTION 1 - the stalk is NOT absent. At 9x zoom every one of the four fruits carries a short reddish-brown pedicel stub rising from its top, angled ~15-25 degrees off vertical, roughly 7px long on a 25px fruit (about 28% of fruit diameter). It is invisible at 1x, which is presumably why the first judge called it 'no stalk visible'. The defect is not a missing stalk, it is a stalk that is a SHORT STUB instead of the long pendulous peduncle the mustRead demands. A fix that merely 'adds a stalk' would be re-adding something already there.

CORRECTION 2 - the fruit is not 'bright orange'. Measured native pixel values (unboosted) give an average fruit colour of rgb(161,124,48) with the brightest specular at rgb(185,159,89) - a muted amber/ochre gold, hue about 40deg. It reads gold-apricot rather than traffic-cone orange. It is still wrong: the row asks for green-yellow fruit, and there is no trace of green or of the pale yellow-green ripening tone anywhere in the fruit body. Each fruit is also a perfect geometric sphere with a blown-out white specular hotspot, which reads plastic/bauble rather than the row's 'smaller rounder green-yellow fruit with fibrous flesh'.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS (both mustReads):

MustRead 1, 'tall dense dark crown' - ABSENT. Measured green-crown bounding box is 230 wide x 191 high, ratio 1.20, i.e. the crown is WIDER THAN TALL - a squat oblate cloud blob, the opposite of tall. It is also not dark and not dense: the interior is a washed-out pale mint-green highlight patch occupying the upper-centre third, lighter than the rim, so the mass reads hollow and soft-focus rather than a dense dark canopy. The row also asks for dark green with bronze flushes; there is zero bronze anywhere in the foliage.

MustRead 2, 'fruit dangling on long stalks' - ABSENT. The fruit bounding box is y=108..193 while the crown spans y=64..254, so all four fruits sit wholly INSIDE the foliage mass with substantial leaf above and below them. Nothing hangs clear of the canopy, nothing hangs below it, and with only a 28%-diameter stub there is no dangle read at all. Mango's single most diagnostic silhouette cue - fruit swinging on long cords well clear of the leaves - is simply not drawn.

SECONDARY, not in the claim but relevant to any fix: the leaf glyph is actually the ONE thing partly working - the blades are genuinely narrow lanceolate/willow shapes, so the shape vocabulary is right. But they are SHORT and they RADIATE outward and upward from the blob rim like a spiky halo. The row asks for long leathery lance leaves drooping in whorls; nothing droops, and there is no whorl grouping. Lengthen them and turn them downward and this becomes the cheapest identity win available.

Trunk: measured width is 22-23px at y=270, 300, 330 and 360 - literally parallel-sided over 90px, no taper, no root flare, no bark texture, no branching into the crown, rounded popsicle-stick ends. Flat single-tone tan.

CHASSIS CLAIM VERIFIED: I opened Fig.png and it is the same asset with two swaps - identical parallel-sided tan stick trunk, identical pale-centred green cloud-blob crown of the same squat proportion, four fruit spheres pinned into the upper crown in the same scatter. Only the leaf glyph (lobed fig vs lance) and the fruit colour (purple vs amber) differ. So 'same flat stick trunk and pale blob crown as Cherry and Fig' is correct as stated.

NET: what a viewer sees is a generic cartoon fruit tree that would serve equally well as apricot, orange, or plum. Neither mustRead is present, and the organism is not identifiable as a Mangifera. This is a wrong-organism read, not a polish gap, so FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: lavender, or a generic herb spike

rows.readsAs: a spiky green column — a cactus, a bottlebrush, or a cannabis cola

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 render, then re-cropped and upscaled three bands (top/mid/base) at 5-6x. The FAIL stands; the mechanism is slightly different from how it was described.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a single vertical column, bbox x191-248 / y104-321 (58 x 218 px, measured aspect 0.27 against a packet aspect of 0.7 - it is drawn roughly 2.5x too narrow for its height). The column is one unbroken slab of overlapping triangular leaflets, left-right mirror-symmetric, tiled in ~14 identical rows from top to base with no size or shape gradient. BELOW: at y~300-321 the leaflets stop and a single bare olive stalk runs down to the ground shadow. So there IS a bare stem - just only at the very bottom, below all foliage, contributing nothing to the identity.

THE TOP: correcting the other judge - it is not a 'yellow smear'. It is a discrete, cleanly-edged saturated-yellow crescent/dome cap about 30 px wide and 10 px tall, sitting on its own short bare olive pedicel that lifts it ~15 px clear of a whorl of green points. Structurally it reads as a mushroom cap or a bun on a stick, or at best a composite (dandelion/hawkweed) capitulum. 2. 'slender pods held out from the stem with a pointed beak' - ABSENT. Nothing anywhere on the plant projects at an angle away from the axis as a slim linear body; every projecting element is a short broad triangle in the leaf tiling, and none has a beak, a stalk, or a two-valved pod body.
3. 'flowers at the tip with pods forming below' - ABSENT as a progression. There is a tip/below split (yellow cap above, green mass below), so the other judge's phrasing 'no flower-above-pods-below progression' is half wrong: the vertical arrangement exists, but the 'below' element is undifferentiated foliage, not pods, so the diagnostic reading is not available.

ALSO MISSING from the reference row: no lower lobed leaves with a big terminal lobe, no contrast between broad lower and narrow toothed upper leaves - every leaf on the plant is the same triangular point.

FIX DIRECTION: strip the leaf column down to a slim visible stem with widely spaced leaves so there is background between elements; replace the single yellow cap with a loose cluster of small four-petalled crosses (petals separated by visible gaps) at the growing tip; and add 6-10 slim beaked pods angling upward-outward off the stem below the flower cluster, each with a narrow body and a pointed tip. Also widen the overall silhouette toward aspect 0.7.

rows.readsAs: a clump of ornamental grass with a white pill above it — indistinguishable from this batch's Wild Garlic

The ball of tiny flowers is ABSENT. CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM: it is not a 'flat disc' and not a 'lozenge'. It is a CRESCENT - a shallow arc, thickest at the crown, tapering to two down-curved points at left and right, like a tiny opened parasol or a mushroom cap - sitting over a separate dark-olive DOWNWARD-POINTING CHEVRON/WEDGE (sampled RGB 20,32,27) whose apex meets the stalk. A horizontal pixel scan across the crescent at y=122 returns the identical value RGB(208,192,224) for 18 consecutive pixels with only 2px of antialias at each end: it is one flat fill with no gradient, no beading, no radiating pedicels, no floret separations, no globe shading. rows.readsAs: a floating sprig of pea or bean vine
rows.defect: The two things that make a yam - heart-shaped leaves with strongly arcing veins, and the big knobbly brown tuber at the base - are both missing. The leaves are plain round blobs with a single straight midrib and no basal notch, and there is no tuber, no soil, nothing at the base at all. Verified at 2x and 4-6x magnification with the background brightened, plus a full-image hue histogram. Packet mustRead: (1) thin twining stem spiralling up a support, (2) heart-shaped leaves with arcing veins, (3) a big knobbly brown tuber at the base. Form=vine, aspect 1.4, leafColour mid green.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS: a single mid-green stem describing a shallow reversed-S from about (300,105) down-left then down-right to about (250,315) in the 440px frame, bearing NINE leaves in loose alternating pairs, and a soft dark elliptical contact shadow at y~320. Nothing else. A hue scan of every non-background pixel (11,057 px) returns ZERO warm/brown pixels — the entire subject is hue 90-180 (green). So the tuber must-read is not merely 'not readable', it is literally not drawn: no tuber, no root, no soil mound, no dug earth, no brown of any kind anywhere in the image. The lowest element is a leaf whose petiole terminates in mid-air above the shadow; the stem never even meets the ground plane. Must-read 3: ABSENT. Confirmed exactly as claimed.

LEAF SHAPE — the other judge's wording needs correcting on two points, though their verdict on this must-read stands. The leaves are NOT 'plain round blobs'. Each leaf is BILOBED: two fused circular lobes with a straight seam running between them, giving a butterfly / Bauhinia-like outline with a shallow notch at BOTH ends of the seam. Critically the lobes sit either side of the midrib along the leaf's length, and the distal end is ROUND, not pointed — a heart needs paired lobes at the PETIOLE end converging to an acute tip, and neither the basal sinus nor the apex point exists here. The petiole attaches to the flank of one lobe, not into a notch. So 'no heart shape' is correct, but the reason is 'bilobed round leaf with no apex and no basal sinus', not 'featureless round blob' — a fix that only rounds the blob into a circle would not help.

VENATION — the claim 'one straight midrib, no arcing veins' is partly wrong. There IS internal venation: a faint low-contrast fan of short secondary strokes spreading from the seam into each lobe, visible on every leaf at 4x. But it is (a) subordinate to the hard straight seam that dominates the leaf and (b) a straight radiating hatch, not the yam's signature 3-7 strong veins arcing from the leaf base out to the tip. So secondaries exist and need re-shaping into curved base-to-tip arcs; they do not need adding from nothing.

VINE HABIT — the claim 'nothing to twine around, so even the vine habit fails' overstates it and misses real geometry. There are EIGHT small dark-green TENDRIL CURLS drawn at the nodes — flat lens/spiral loops about 12-18px across, one at nearly every leaf axil, clearly rendered and clearly intended as tendrils. That is a genuine vine cue the other judge did not see. What is true is that there is no support (no pole, stalk, twig or neighbouring stem), the stem is a free-floating open S-curve rather than a helix wrapping anything, and the curls sit beside the stem rather than gripping. So must-read 1 is PARTIAL, not absent: thin stem yes, tendrils yes, spiralling-up-a-support no.

VERDICT: two of three identity must-reads fail — the defining brown tuber is entirely absent (zero brown pixels) and the heart leaf is replaced by a bilobed round leaf — with the third only half-delivered. With no tuber, no soil and no cordate leaf, nothing distinguishes this from a generic bilobed-leaf creeper; the other judge's 'reads as a sprig of pea vine' is a fair characterisation of the result. FAIL upheld.

FIX ORDER: (1) add the knobbly brown tuber half-buried in a soil mound at the base and run the stem down into it — this single omission is the largest identity loss; (2) reshape the leaf to a true cordate outline: basal sinus at the petiole, broad shoulders, drawn-out acute tip; (3) re-curve the existing secondary veins into 5-7 arcs sweeping from the leaf base to the tip and demote the straight seam; (4) give the stem something to twine on and make it wrap in a helix, keeping the tendril curls which are already good.

Each blade is individually rendered — it has its own outline, its own soft light-to-dark gradient, and its own scatter of short dark vein ticks — so the mass is NOT undivided; it is divided the wrong way. Blade tips are sharp acute points, which is what produces the sawtooth silhouette; the sawtooth is the stack of pointed tips, not marginal teeth cut into one blade. Colour is a bright lime/yellow-green.

CORRECTION 1 TO THE CLAIM: 'one solid undivided fan of sharp saw-toothed lobes' is imprecise. The fan IS segmented, into ~15 discrete overlapping lance blades. The defect is segment COUNT (15 vs 3), segment SHAPE (acute-tipped lance vs heart with a notched apex), and segment ATTACHMENT (all fused at a single point, zero visible petioles) — not an absence of segmentation. A fix that merely 'adds separation' to the existing fan will still fail; the blade primitive and the count both have to change.

CORRECTION 2: 'pixel-for-pixel Wild Rhubarb's chassis' is right in substance, wrong in literalness. I opened Wild_Rhubarb.png and Clover.png side by side. So it is the same chassis reparameterised, not a pixel copy. Note that Clover — the species the packet's own note tells us Wood Sorrel must be distinguished FROM — is drawn on this identical chassis too, so the engine currently has no trifoliate leaf model at all. That is the real root cause and it is a family-level defect, not a one-asset defect.

MUST-READ 1, 'low carpet of three heart-shaped leaflets on thin stalks' — ABSENT on every clause. There are no three leaflets. There is no heart shape and no notched apex anywhere in the silhouette; every tip is a point. There are no thin stalks — no petiole is drawn at all, the blades meet the ground point directly. At 6x zoom the flower is a flat face-on star of SEVEN (not five) narrow pointed cream petals, held bolt upright at the top of a rigid vertical stem. It is small and delicate, and its pale cream colour is defensible against 'white or pink'. But it does not nod, it is not cupped, it has no purple veining, and the petal count is wrong. rows.fix: Add dark saddle crossbands over a warm ground, roughen the dorsum with keeled scale texture, and expose a visibly tapering tail tip outside the coil.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated causes. Packet row 8 (other-snakes/batch-001.md): aspect 9, headFrac 0.05, eyes normal, posture coiled, mustRead = 'keeled banded body / narrow head with eyes set high / slender tapering tail'. I read the 440x440 PNG at 1:1, then cropped and 3-8x upscaled the head, the outer coil and the inner-coil terminus, and pixel-scanned the file.

WHAT IS THERE: a flat-lying spiral coil, bbox x72-370 y126-281 (298x155), one full outer loop plus an inner loop, head exiting bottom-right with a bright red forked tongue. The body is a stout rounded tube with genuine painterly volume - a real light-to-dark roll from the top of the tube to the shaded flank, a soft cast shadow under the coil, and scattered pale cream specular dots. Head: a narrow pointed lozenge, clearly a distinct head shape, with a big pale sclera and a black VERTICAL-SLIT pupil.

MUST-READ 1 'keeled banded body' - ABSENT, BOTH HALVES, confirmed by pixel scan. A horizontal scan across the top of the coil (row y=150) returns base 106,83,65 on the smooth stretch and then a tight repeating oscillation 43,35,29 <-> 106,83,65. Every one of those samples is the SAME HUE (r:g:b ratio constant); the only variation is luminance. So there is literally zero colour banding - no saddles, no crossbands, no dorsolateral stripe, nothing. And the texture that IS drawn is TRANSVERSE - dense evenly-spaced rings wrapping the tube perpendicular to its long axis, running unbroken from behind the head all the way round the coil. That is the wrong AXIS for a keel: a keel is a longitudinal ridge down each dorsal scale and should read as lengthwise grain/matte roughness. What is drawn is closer to a ventral-scute treatment applied over the entire circumference, and at the density used (~4px pitch on a ~30px tube) it reads as annelid annulation. This is the fatal defect: the organism reads as a giant earthworm or a caecilian, not a snake.

MUST-READ 2 'narrow head with eyes set high' - HALF PRESENT. The judge said 'eyes mid-side, not set high'; I measured it and they are right, in fact more exactly than they claimed. Sclera pixels occupy x317-325, y211-218 (centre y=214.5). The head silhouette at x=320 spans y199-231, midline y=215. The eye centre is 0.5px off the head's exact vertical midline - a dead-centre lateral eye, zero dorsal bias. A Nerodia-type water snake wants the eye pushed up onto the top third so the animal can lie at the surface with only eyes clear. CORRECTION to the judge, in the animal's favour: the head itself IS narrow and distinct - a tapering lozenge with a visible snout point, not a blunt worm end - so the 'narrow head' half of this must-read passes. ADDITIONAL DEFECT the judge missed: the pupil is a vertical slit. Natricine water snakes have ROUND pupils; a vertical slit reads viper/nocturnal-ambusher and actively fights the identity.

MUST-READ 3 'slender tapering tail' - CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE'S WORDING. They said 'the tapering tail is invisible inside the coil', implying nothing was drawn. Something IS drawn: at 8x the inner loop does narrow, and around full-image x150-190, y172-180 it thins to a 1-2px sliver and fades out. So a taper exists in the geometry. The defect is ROUTING and TERMINATION, not absence - the taper has been sent into the black interior of the coil where it sits against a near-black background (bg 5,6,12) and is completely unreadable at 1:1, and the very tip dissolves into shadow rather than resolving to a clean point. The fix is to bring the tail terminus out over the lit outer coil or lay it across the front of the body, not to 'add a taper'.

OTHER CORRECTION: 'flat uniform brown tube' is right about PATTERN but wrong about rendering - the tube is not flatly filled, it has correct cylindrical shading and specular highlights. The flatness is entirely a pattern/marking failure, so a fix must add colour banding on top of the existing shading rather than re-lighting the form.

ONE MORE, unmentioned by the judge: the tongue is a thick pure-red (~#E01030) Y, the only saturated colour in the piece, drawn as a flat vector stroke about a third of the head's length. It clashes with the painterly treatment everywhere else and should be a thinner, darker, desaturated fork.

BAND: FAIL stands. Two of three must-reads are missing outright (banding absent, keel drawn on the wrong axis, eye placement dead-centre), and the transverse-ring texture makes the asset read as the wrong PHYLUM, which is a FAIL condition independent of the checklist. The single highest-value fix is to delete the transverse annulation entirely and replace it with dark dorsal crossbands/saddles over a lighter ground plus a longitudinal keel grain.

rows.readsAs: a khaki coiled tube; the least whip-like shape available

rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size and then at 4x-14x crops of the coil interior, the inner-arc terminus and the head, and I measured the silhouette in pixels. The FAIL stands, but two parts of the stated cause need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A closed, fat doughnut/torus of olive body lying flat, head emerging at the right with a red forked tongue. Silhouette bbox (body only, tongue excluded) is x 87-354, y 130-258. Measured body gauge across the left limb at the vertical midline is 46 px. Estimated centreline length of the torus is only ~400 px, so the drawn length:gauge ratio is roughly 8:1 on an organism whose whole identity is 'extremely thin whip-like'. For scale reference the eye alone is ~14 px across on a 46 px body. This is a rope, not a whip.

CLAIM PART 1 - 'drawn at full family gauge' - CONFIRMED, and it is worse than stated. This is not merely the same gauge, it is the same MESH. Silhouette IoU against family siblings: Tree Snake 0.843, Vine Snake 0.794, Garter Snake 0.738. Measured left-limb gauge at midline: Whip 46 px, Vine 55 px, Tree 36 px, Garter 45 px. Vine Snake (packet aspect 12, note: 'Extraordinarily thin - roughly pencil-width along its whole length') is the SAME fat torus in green and is actually THICKER than the Whip Snake. Tree Snake (note: 'startlingly thin - pencil-width even at a metre long') is the same torus in a different olive. The family's three whip-thin species are indistinguishable from its heavy-bodied ones; only hue and speckle pattern change. So the packet's aspect field is having no effect on the renderer at all for this family - that is the root defect, and fixing Whip Snake alone will not fix it.

CLAIM PART 2 - 'the tail is not visible anywhere' - PARTLY WRONG, correct this in the fix brief. The tail terminus IS present and I located it: trace the head at the right, follow the neck down-left along the outer bottom limb, around the left side, up and over the top, then the body dives inward and runs left-to-right along the inner floor of the coil, ending in a blunt wedge at approximately x 215-235, y 172-185 (the notch/step in the top edge of the dark inner hole; visible at 14x). So it is not missing - it is TERMINATED AT FULL GAUGE with no taper whatsoever, cut off square against the shaded inner wall of the doughnut where the low-contrast inner shading hides it. The judge's conclusion (the defining proportion cannot be read) is right; the reason is 'blunt untapered stump hidden in shadow', not 'absent'. A fix that merely un-buries the tail without tapering it will still fail.

THIRD MUST-READ, not mentioned by the judge - PARTIAL. 'Narrow head with a large round eye': the eye is genuinely large and prominent, a white globe with a clean dark VERTICAL SLIT pupil, well rendered. But the head is a rounded lozenge only marginally narrower than the body, so 'narrow head' reads weakly, and the vertical slit is wrong for a diurnal whip snake, which has a round pupil. Also note the packet specifies posture 'crawling' and the asset is coiled into a closed ring - the coil posture is itself part of why no length proportion can be read.

BAND. Two of three must-reads fail outright (whip-thin body; long tapering tail at half total length), the third only half-reads. The asset reads as a generic fat colubrid coil - the same coil the whole family shares. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a white duckling or fluffy chick — a cartoon baby waterfowl, not a raptor of any kind
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are flatly absent and the third is contradicted. (1) The eyes are BLACK beads with white specular dots — there is no yellow iris anywhere in the face. Brilliant yellow eyes in a white face IS the snowy owl's identity and it is missing. (2) The feet are bare yellow scaled chicken toes with visible segment lines; 'heavily feathered feet' is not merely weak, it is the opposite of what is drawn. (3) The head is round and untufted, which is correct, but it is small and grafted low onto the FRONT of the body rather than sitting on top, and there is no facial disc or rim at all. The note explicitly asks for a rounded column taller than wide; the render is a horizontal egg clearly wider than tall, with the long axis running left-to-right and a grey pointed tail spike stabbing off the right side. Nothing about the silhouette, the eye colour or the foot says owl.
rows.fix: Give it the yellow eye first — large forward-facing discs with a saturated yellow iris ringed in black, set into a dished white facial disc — then stand the body up into a vertical column taller than wide and bury the legs in white feathered trousers so only stubby dark talons show below.

rows.readsAs: a white dove or a white pigeon with a stray tuft
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply absent. The bill is a small smooth yellow cone with NO hook and no dark heavy mass - a dove's bill, not a cockatoo's black hooked bill. The feet are three-forward-one-back perching feet, not zygodactyl. The crest is a thin four-strand wire spray sitting on top of the skull rather than a raised fan of feathers rising out of the crown, and it is small enough to read as damage. Body is the shared plump pigeon oval with a long grey pointed pigeon tail; posture is horizontal despite the packet asking for upright.
rows.fix: Replace the yellow cone with a heavy dark down-curved hooked bill with a visible cere, and rebuild the crest as a broad layered fan of 6-8 overlapping recurved feathers sweeping back off the crown, tall enough to read at thumbnail size.

rows.readsAs: a red pigeon, or a cardinal that has lost its crest
rows.defect: The identity must-read - a tail streamer far longer than the body - is absent. The tail is a short striped slat roughly a third of the body length, leaving horizontally from mid-body, and it is the SAME tail shape as the Parrot's, only red. The packet specifies aspect 0.5 (much taller than wide, tail hanging vertically); the render is visibly WIDER than tall. There is no bare white facial patch traced with feather lines - just a small white eye smudge. The beak is pale and slightly hooked, which is the only must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Redraw with the bird perched upright and the tail a single long tapering streamer hanging vertically to at least twice body length, so the silhouette becomes tall and narrow, and add the bare white cheek patch with fine feather striations around the eye.

rows.readsAs: a green bird - a parakeet at best, a green pigeon at worst
rows.defect: The hooked yellow beak is present and is the only thing carrying the read. The zygodactyl foot is missing - both feet show three toes forward, one back, ordinary perching feet. The tail is not short and squared; it is the shared long horizontal striped slat also used on the Macaw. The posture is horizontal on the pigeon chassis rather than the biped upright the packet calls for, and the stocky compact body is the family's generic plump oval rather than a parrot's upright barrel. No fleshy cere is visible at the beak base.
rows.fix: Draw the zygodactyl foot explicitly - two toes forward, two back, wrapping a visible perch - and shorten the tail to a short squared fan while tipping the body to an upright stance.

rows.readsAs: a white cartoon duckling / bath-toy duck
rows.defect: The identity must-read — vividly coloured blue or red webbed feet — is entirely absent: the feet are the same thin orange-yellow three-toed chicken sticks used on Gannet and Pelican, with no webbing at all. The eye is one round black dot set on the side of a spherical head, so there is no forward-set binocular stare, and the bill is a short blunt yellow cone with a clear forehead step rather than a long tapered dagger running straight into the skull. Visually it is the same asset as Gannet.
rows.fix: Repaint the feet as large fully-webbed triangular paddles in saturated cobalt blue extending forward of the body, and lengthen the bill to at least head-length with the culmen running unbroken into the crown.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but one third of the stated cause is wrong and must not be fixed as stated.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, zoomed 5-11x on head and feet, plus a pixel diff against Gannet).

FEET - judge is RIGHT, and this alone fails the asset. At 9x the feet are two thin ochre sticks dropping from the belly, each ending in a simple bent V: one forward prong, one rear prong. Sampled dominant foot colour is RGB(201,162,79) - a dull tan/gold, the same amber family as the bill. There is no blue anywhere on the legs, no red, and no membrane: the prongs are separate strokes with dark background visible between them, no webbing polygon, no lobes, no paddle. Correction to the judge's wording: it reads as TWO prongs per foot, not three, and the hue is dull ochre rather than saturated orange. The single most identity-bearing must-read for a booby - 'vividly coloured blue or red webbed feet' - is absent in both of its parts (colour and web).

BILL - judge is WRONG on the description, half right on the defect. It is NOT a short blunt cone. It is a long, finely tapered dagger: it runs roughly 1.2x the head diameter forward from the skull and narrows from a wide base to a needle point, sharper than most of this family. The length-and-taper half of must-read 2 is genuinely satisfied and should NOT be 'fixed' by lengthening the bill. What fails is the second clause, 'running straight into the forehead': the bill is a flat amber wedge pasted onto the side of a perfectly spherical white cranium, so the dorsal line breaks at a hard step where the ball bulges up and back over the bill base. There is no continuous skull-to-bill ramp. That is the real bill defect - a culmen/forehead junction problem, not a bill-length problem.

EYES - judge is right. One eye only, lateral: a round black disc with a single white specular highlight, sitting immediately behind and just above the bill base. Its placement is actually reasonably forward (it touches the bill's rear edge), so 'side-set' overstates it slightly, but there is no second eye, no forward-facing pair flanking the culmen, and no binocular stare. Must-read 3 is not delivered. No dark facial mask, no bare facial skin, no throat stripe.

SAME BIRD AS GANNET - judge is right, and I confirmed it numerically. I diffed Booby.png against Gannet.png pixel-for-pixel and rendered the delta map: the result is nothing but thin edge lines and interior stipple noise. Head sphere, bill wedge, eye, the white teardrop body, the grey wing wrap arcing over the flank, the grey wedge tail spike and both legs/feet land at IDENTICAL coordinates. Only 5.87% of sampled pixels exceed a visible threshold and every one of those is procedural feather-texture jitter or a marginally larger eye - zero shape displacement. These are one chassis with a re-rolled noise seed, not two species.

FIX ORDER: (1) blue (or red) webbed feet with a visible interdigital membrane spanning three forward toes - this is the whole species; (2) ramp the cranium into the bill base so the culmen is one unbroken line, and drop the spherical ball head; (3) rotate the head toward 3/4 so both forward-set eyes read; (4) differentiate the body from Gannet - booby wants a slimmer, longer-tailed, more pointed rear than the gannet's bulk.

rows.readsAs: a black duck or coot floating on a pond
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is on screen. The wings are not open — there is no heraldic drying pose at all, just the family's folded grey flank crescent, and that pose IS the cormorant. The bill is a small straight yellow triangle with no hook. The body is the family egg half-sunk in a water ellipse with no low-slung waterline profile and no stiff wedge tail. The neck is a short thick grey tube, not long or snaky.
rows.fix: Redraw it perched and upright with both wings spread wide and half-cocked in the drying pose, add a hooked nail to the bill tip, and extend the neck to roughly body-length with an S-kink.
rows.verifyWhy: Verified at full size and at 6x/14x zoom on head, bill tip and rear of body, plus a pixel bbox/row-span scan. The FAIL stands: all three mustReads (hook-tipped bill on a long snaky neck / wings held open to dry in a heraldic pose / low-slung body with a stiff wedge tail) are absent, and the asset reads as a black coot or duckling floating on a pond. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a near-circular dark body (137px wide, ~120px tall) sunk to its waterline in a blue pond disc with two concentric ripple ellipses; a big round head (58px across, headFrac far above the specified 0.2); a plain black bead eye with a single specular dot; a short vertical neck stub; a yellow bill; a faint dark crescent on the flank standing in for a FOLDED wing. WING: there is a wing indicated, but it is a closed folded-wing arc drawn as a shading crescent across the body flank, not an open shape. Nothing is spread, raised or held away from the body; the heraldic drying pose, which is the entire identity of this bird, is nowhere on the canvas. TAIL: the judge said 'no stiff wedge tail'; it is stronger than that. There is NO tail of any kind. The 6x crop of the rump shows the body terminating in a smooth unbroken circular dome edge with zero projection past the rump; the silhouette right edge is a clean arc from y182 to the waterline. BODY: not low-slung and not elongated. Row spans give a body 137 wide x ~120 tall, i.e. essentially round; the packet asks for aspect 2.8 and posture 'upright' and the drawing delivers neither - the whole creature bbox (excluding the water rings) is about 165 wide x 185 tall, and it is drawn SWIMMING, not standing upright. NECK - the judge's wording is right but for a reason worth stating precisely: measured, the neck is 14px wide and only ~24px of visible length between the skull base (y158) and the shoulder flare (y182), so it is SHORTER than the head is tall (36px) - a stubby ~2:1 column. It is also perfectly straight and vertical with no S-kink or forward reach, so 'snaky' fails on curvature as well as on length. It is slender relative to the oversized head, so 'thick' is the one word to discard; 'short, straight, stubby' is the accurate description. BILL - one correction to the claim. It is not 'small' and not quite 'straight'. It is a yellow quadrilateral roughly 40px long (about 0.7 head-widths), with a slightly convex culmen and a concave underside, and its tip is canted DOWNWARD into a small point that drops below the gape line. So a shallow droop is present. What is missing is the hook proper: there is no overhanging nail, no separation between an over-curling upper mandible and a shorter lower one - it is one solid yellow wedge, and at full size the droop reads as a blunt duck/coot bill, not as a cormorant's hooked tip. Colour is also wrong-signalling: an all-over saturated yellow bill on a black body is the coot/moorhen frontal-shield read, which is exactly why the whole thing lands on 'black duck'. FIX ORDER: (1) open the wings into the heraldic drying spread - that alone converts the read; (2) add the stiff wedge tail projecting behind the rump and stretch the body into a low horizontal cigar so the silhouette stops being a circle; (3) triple the neck length and put an S-kink in it; (4) put a real overhanging hook on the bill tip and desaturate the yellow to a horn/grey-yellow with only a small yellow gular patch at the base.

rows.readsAs: a dark pigeon or grouse standing on the ground
rows.defect: The asset is not flying — it sits on the family egg body over a cast ground shadow with the two yellow chicken feet visible underneath. The deeply forked scissor tail is absent; the rear is a fan of straight dark streaks with no fork. The wings are not long crooked M-shapes, they are the chassis crescent smeared sideways and do not leave the body as separate airfoils. There is no hooked bill and no scarlet throat pouch of any kind.
rows.fix: Rebuild it airborne with no feet and no ground shadow: two very long angular M-kinked wings spanning the full canvas width and a hard deep V-fork in the tail, plus a scarlet inflated pouch under the chin.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x, at 5-10x nearest-neighbour crops of head/feet/tail, and on a gamma-lifted (0.33) full frame so the near-black shapes separate from the near-black background. The FAIL stands; the packet's three must-reads (deeply forked scissor tail / very long crooked M-shaped wings / hooked bill + inflated scarlet gular pouch) are all absent, and the packet's posture:flying is contradicted by the render.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A near-circular egg body (the shared family chassis) filling the mid-frame, dark charcoal with pale speckle/scale mottling and a thin light rim. A small round head sits high-left with NO neck at all — head sphere abuts the body sphere directly. Two yellow scaled feet with three splayed forward toes each are planted flat under the belly, and a soft elliptical CAST GROUND SHADOW sits beneath them, feet touching it. That is unambiguously a standing/perched ground pose, not flight — the packet asks for flying.

TAIL. The judge said 'just a fan of straight streaks'. Correct, but incomplete in a way a fixer needs: there ARE two separate things back there. (a) At the far right tip of the right wing, five straight, parallel, slightly-splayed dark streaks read as primaries, not tail. (b) Tucked UNDER the right wing plank and slightly below it there is one narrow dark triangular wedge tapering to a point at roughly 20 degrees below horizontal — this is almost certainly the intended tail, but it is a SINGLE unforked spike, it is dark-on-dark against both the wing above it and the background, and it reads as a shadow or a second wing rather than a tail. So the fix is not 'add a tail' — a tail primitive exists; it must be split into two long divergent scissor streamers with a deep V notch between them, and value-separated from the wing it currently hides under.

WINGS. The judge's 'no long crooked M-wings' is right on 'crooked' and 'M' but WRONG on 'long' — total span is roughly 2.2x body width, which is already respectably long. The defect is shape, not length: both wings are perfectly STRAIGHT flat planks held horizontally out from the body's mid-flank, right one long and tapering, left one shorter, with no wrist joint, no forward-swept hand, no elbow. A fixer who reacts to 'no long wings' by lengthening them will make it worse. What is missing is the wrist crook — the sharp angled bend that makes the frigatebird's M/W silhouette — plus the pointed swept-back hand beyond it. As drawn the planks also intersect a standing body, which is why the glider outline never registers.

BILL. Confirmed unhooked, and worse than the judge stated. At 10x it is a short, blunt yellow wedge about half a head-width long, with a straight top edge and a slightly concave lower edge, ending in a plain point that angles very slightly down but has NO hook, NO nail, NO downcurved tip. Frigatebird needs a bill roughly 1.5-2 head-widths long, slender, and terminating in a distinct downward hook. Current bill reads as a dove/pigeon bill.

GULAR POUCH. Fully absent — confirmed. The throat/breast region under the head is the same flat charcoal as the rest of the body; no scarlet, no red, no inflated balloon shape, no colour of any kind other than the yellow of bill and feet. This is the single most diagnostic frigatebird feature and there is zero trace of it.

GESTALT. The judge's 'dark pigeon or grouse' is fair; I read it as a dark pigeon/dove specifically (round no-neck head, short wedge bill, plump egg body, yellow perching feet on ground shadow). The straight wing planks with primary streaks add a faint pasted-on gull quality but the standing round body dominates completely. Nothing in the silhouette says frigatebird.

rows.readsAs: a generic white seabird or gull chick
rows.defect: The overall white body with a grey wing and a pointed pale bill is roughly in the right zone, but all three must-reads are missing: the head is pure white with no buff-yellow wash, there is no dark facial mask or dark bare skin around the eye and bill base, and the wingtip is mid-grey rather than jet black. The bill is also too short and too blunt to read as a plunge-diving dagger.
rows.fix: Wash the whole head and nape buff-yellow, ink a black mask around the eye and gape line, and hard-cut the outer third of the wing to true black.

rows.readsAs: a grey-white gull or duckling standing on a shadow
rows.defect: The enormous bill and slung throat pouch — the entire identity — are absent; the bill is the family's short yellow cone, shorter than the head. The bird is standing on two long visible legs over a ground shadow rather than swimming, and the legs are the family's thin sticks, not the very short heavy set called for. The neck is not long and is not kinked back onto the shoulders; the head sits directly on the egg body. Body is the same chassis as Booby and Gannet in a slightly dirtier grey.
