rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440; body bbox x83-354, y130-299, so 271w x 169h). A rotund egg-shaped body in dirty grey-white with a scaled/feather-stipple texture, a dark grey crescent arc across the flank for the folded wing, a grey wedge tail spearing out to the right, a small pale sphere head at upper left carrying a big glossy black bead eye with a white catchlight, a straight yellow bill pointing left, two short yellow legs, and a hard-edged elliptical cast shadow under the feet.

CORRECTION 1 - THE BILL IS NOT 'THE FAMILY'S SHORT YELLOW CONE, SHORTER THAN THE HEAD'. Measured yellow-pixel bbox for the bill: x84-148, y142-166, i.e. 65px long and 25px deep at the base. The head sphere is about 48px across (x141-186, y129-177). So the bill is roughly 1.35x the head's diameter - LONGER than the head, not shorter. And it is NOT the family's cone: the same measurement on Booby gives 58 long x 11 deep and on Gannet 55 long x 11 deep. The Pelican's bill is 2.3x deeper than its family-mates'. It is a broad solid wedge, not a needle. Anyone fixing this against the judge's wording would 'lengthen the bill' and miss the real defect.

THE REAL BILL DEFECT (the identity, and it does fail). There is no pouch, at all. The depth profile climbs monotonically and smoothly from 1px at the tip to 24-25px at the base (84:1 90:9 96:14 102:17 108:20 114:22 120:23 126:24 132:24 138:24 144:24) - a clean isoceles triangle with a straight lower edge. There is no second mandible line, no sagging or bulging curve under the lower edge, no gular skin in a contrasting flesh/orange tone, no distension. At 4x magnification the pixels immediately below the bill's lower edge are plain dark background all the way from tip to gape. So it reads as a thickened heron/tern dagger. It is also not 'enormous' in pelican terms: 65px against a 271px body is 24% of body length, where a real pelican's bill is 40-50% of body length and visually rivals the entire head+neck. mustRead 1 ('enormous bill with a stretchy throat pouch slung beneath') is unmet - the pouch, which is the single most identifying structure on the animal, is entirely absent.

CORRECTION 2 - THE LEGS ARE NOT LONG. At 6x the legs run from the belly edge at about y=275 to the toes at about y=298: roughly 23px against a 169px body height, about 13-14% - genuinely short and mostly tucked under the mass. mustRead 2 ('heavy body on very short legs') is the ONE must-read that is actually satisfied, and the judge scored it as a defect. Do not lengthen or shorten the legs. The legitimate complaints about the lower half are (a) the feet are three thin splayed unwebbed toes, where a pelican is totipalmate with all four toes joined by full webbing, and (b) the posture: the reference calls for 'swimming' and this bird is standing on land on a hard-edged shadow ellipse, so it is not floating on a waterline at all. Both of those the judge got right.

CORRECTION 3 - THE NECK. The judge is correct here. The head sits on a short straight vertical grey column dropping directly onto the shoulder mass - about a head's-depth of neck, no curve in it. There is no long neck and no S-kink folding it back onto the shoulders. mustRead 3 unmet.

SHARED-CHASSIS CLAIM CONFIRMED. Read against Booby.png and Gannet.png side by side, the three are one drawing. Identical egg body outline, identical dark crescent folded-wing arc in the same place at the same angle, identical grey wedge tail exiting right at the same pitch, identical head sphere seated at the same spot, identical yellow legs with the same three splayed toes, identical shadow ellipse. Body bboxes: Pelican 271x169, Booby 248x145, Gannet 256x149 - the same shape scaled. What varies is a slightly dirtier grey wash, a slightly larger head, and the thicker bill wedge. The chassis reads as a generic plump gull/tern standing on a beach.

SECONDARY: headFrac measures about 0.18 (48px head / 271px body) against the required 0.3, and 'eyes: small' is not honoured - the eye is a prominent 14px bead with a specular highlight on a 48px head, matching Booby's 'prominent' eye setting rather than the Pelican row's 'small'.

BAND. Two of three must-reads absent, including the one that IS the organism, plus the wrong posture and a body that is demonstrably a family-mate's chassis. It reads as a stocky gull with a thick yellow beak, not a pelican. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic green cartoon fish / vaguely a bass-shaped decal
rows.defect: The large hinged bucket mouth - the single feature that IS a bass - is not weak, it is entirely absent: the head tapers to a bare geometric point with no mouth, lip or jaw line drawn anywhere. The dorsal is one crown of four flat triangles, so there is no spiny-front-joined-to-soft-rear structure either; only the moderately deep compressed body reads. No lateral black stripe, no head/operculum break.
rows.fix: Draw the jaw: cut a wide gape line from the snout back past the eye with a heavy hinged lower jaw and a blunt upper lip, and split the dorsal crown into a spiny triangle set joined by a low membrane to a rounded soft rear lobe.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated cause. I read the 440x440 PNG at full size and then re-cropped/upscaled three regions with nearest-neighbour (head 240,150 120x100 at 8x; dorsal 160,110 180x80 at 7x; whole body 100,150 240x120 at 7x) and measured the alpha bbox. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: the animal is a symmetric pointed lens/almond in flat olive-green, pointed at BOTH ends. Alpha bbox x116-325, y141-241 (210x101 incl. dorsal spikes and tail). Body proper runs ~x130-325 with max depth ~62-66px measured at x=210-240 (the 76px column reading there includes the ventral fin lobe), giving aspect ~3.0-3.1 against the spec 2.8. MUST-READ 2 (large hinged bucket mouth) IS GENUINELY ABSENT and this is the fatal defect: at 8x the snout narrows to a bare geometric vertex at x=325 with zero mouth geometry - no gape, no upper/lower lip, no maxilla line, no jaw hinge, not even a short scratch of a mouth slit. On a largemouth bass the jaw hinge extends BEHIND the eye and is the entire read of the species; here the eye (a small white ring with a dark pupil, sitting high and very far forward at ~x=305) is the only forward feature, so the head is not a head, it is the pointed end of a leaf. MUST-READ 1 (spiny front dorsal joined to a soft rear one) IS ALSO ABSENT AS STRUCTURE: the dorsal is one continuous flat dark-olive sawtooth crown of exactly four identical triangular spikes on a single unbroken base, spanning roughly x=200-270, drawn BEHIND the body silhouette with no ray lines, no membrane shading and no notch. There is no differentiated soft-rayed rear lobe of any kind - the rear two spikes are simply shorter copies of the front two, so nothing reads as 'spiny front joined to soft rear'; it reads as a stegosaur/crown decoration bolted to a fish. CORRECTION 1 TO THE CLAIM: the head is NOT wholly bare. There is a distinct curved dark operculum/gill-cover arc behind the eye (roughly x=288 curving from the topline down to the ventral edge), faint vertical hatch striations on the cheek in front of it, and a pale horizontal lateral line running the body length. So the fixable gap is specifically the MOUTH, not 'no head detail at all' - an artist reading the claim literally might add gill/cheek detail that is already present and still ship a mouthless fish. CORRECTION 2 TO THE CLAIM: 'only the moderately deep body reads' overstates must-read 3. At aspect ~3.0-3.1 the body is slimmer than the 2.8 spec and, worse, it is a top/bottom SYMMETRIC lens - it has none of a bass's deep-shouldered dorsal mass over a flatter belly line, so 'deep laterally compressed body' reads only weakly, at best partially. The claim also omits three things a fix pass should know: (a) the caudal is a flat dark triangular wedge that visually detaches from the sharp caudal peduncle vertex at x~130, leaving a pinched gap; (b) a pectoral fan and a single small ventral triangle (one lump doing duty for pelvic+anal) are present but flat and rayless; (c) there is no dark lateral blotch band, the other classic largemouth cue - not in the must-read list, but its absence plus the missing mouth is why this reads as generic green cartoon fish rather than as Bass. VERDICT: two of three must-reads absent outright and the third only weakly present. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a yellow bluegill or a generic yellow pancake panfish - it is the Sunfish render in another colour

rows.readsAs: a pale green bluegill / panfish - broadly the right thing

rows.readsAs: a generic gold baitfish or minnow with a spiky crown

rows.readsAs: a grey farm pig, or a capybara

rows.readsAs: a pig

A stray pink flap hangs below the snout that reads as a lolling tongue rather than a jaw.

rows.readsAs: a plain grey-brown pig
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent or inverted. There are no upward-curving tusks — the only white shape is a flat crescent band laid across the top of the muzzle that reads as a bandage or a paint smear, not a tusk, and it curves the wrong way. There are no fleshy facial warts anywhere on the cheek or jaw. There is no erect bristly mane: the topline is the same smooth dead-level back as the Pig. The tufted tail is present but hangs DOWN in a droopy arc, the exact opposite of the antenna-straight-up carriage that is the warthog's signature, and it sprouts high on the back rather than at the rump. Body is the short-legged barrel of a farm pig, not the leggy flat-fronted wedge described.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy brown pig with one tusk
rows.defect: The high shoulder hump is absent — the topline is flat and level from shoulder to rump, identical to the domestic Pig's, so the front-heavy wedge silhouette that IS a boar never appears; if anything the rump reads as high as the shoulder. The bristly spinal mane is not there either: the hair strokes that do exist fringe the BELLY, not the spine. The single pale wedge near the snout is the only tusk cue and it sits above the muzzle line pointing back rather than emerging up from the lower jaw, so it half-reads as a horn.

rows.readsAs: a generic green mackerel-shaped fish with a row of white spikes stuck along its belly; nobody names a pike
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply absent and the third is wrong. (1) NO duck-bill snout: the head is an undifferentiated point identical to the tail point, with no jaw line, no mouth, no elongated flattened bill, and no separation between skull and snout. (2) NO dorsal fin anywhere — the topline is one unbroken clean arc from nose to caudal peduncle; brightening the file 3x reveals only five near-invisible hairline vertical strokes over the MIDDLE of the back, which are not readable at normal exposure and are in the wrong place regardless (a pike's dorsal sits far back, over the anal fin, just ahead of the tail). (3) The body is not an elongate torpedo but a symmetric almond lens, deepest at mid-length, and it carries a hexagonal scale net instead of the pale bean markings — no bean blotches are present at all. The teeth that are drawn read as a floating comb of seven white hooks hanging OUTSIDE the ventral outline and running rearward past the gill arc, i.e. under the throat rather than in a jaw. Anal fin also missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head instead of decorating it: extend the front third into a long flat-topped duck-bill with a straight upper profile and a hinged lower jaw line that opens the mouth back to under the eye, seat the tooth row INSIDE that jaw on both upper and lower edges, then move the deepest point of the body rearward and add a clearly visible dorsal fin (mirrored by an anal fin) directly over the caudal peduncle.

rows.readsAs: a clump of soap bubbles / a bunch of peeled white grapes / a cauliflower — not a mushroom with hanging teeth
rows.defect: The identity must-read — a pom-pom of LONG icicle spines cascading downward over the whole mass — is essentially absent. The silhouette is ~85% large smooth glossy spheres with hard specular highlights; the spines are a short, sparse band roughly one-fifth of the body height, confined to a narrow horizontal strip across the middle, and they are drawn BEHIND a further layer of spheres that occludes their lower halves. So the teeth do not hang off the underside of the mass at all — they appear to grow out of its equator and then get swallowed. Nothing about the surface is shaggy; Hericium reads as a fuzzy white waterfall and this reads as bubble wrap. The remaining must-reads pass (no cap, no stem, no gills; creamy-white colour; single unbranched mass), and the render itself is clean — centred, uncropped, with a ground shadow — but the one must-read that IS the organism is missing.
rows.fix: Invert the mass-to-spine ratio: shrink the interior spheres so they only suggest the lumpy core, then draw the spines as the outer silhouette — long tapered icicles (40–60% of body height) emitted from the BOTTOM and lower-front of the mass, dense enough that the blob's lower edge is entirely a fringe of hanging teeth, and drawn in front of everything so nothing occludes them.

rows.readsAs: A generic pond minnow or small green chub — a plain sage-green leaf-shaped fish with no species cues at all
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent or invisible. (1) No red at all: the body is one flat sage green from nose to tail with zero red-edged rear scales — the single feature that names this fish (pirarucu = red fish) simply is not drawn. (2) The dorsal and anal fins are not set far back framing the tail; they are dull near-black smears at roughly 45-70% of body length, tucked BEHIND the body silhouette so they read as shadow blobs, and a long bare gap separates them from the caudal paddle, which therefore reads as a detached square flap rather than the third blade of a paddle cluster. (3) There is no bony flattened head and no small upward mouth — the head end is just the body outline sharpened to a needle point, with no jaw line, no opercular plate, and no mouth aperture whatsoever. The body is a symmetric almond pointed at BOTH ends, where an arapaima is blunt-headed and deepest toward the rear. The eye is a bright white ring pasted near the top of the snout, far too high-contrast and too far forward for the reference small eye.
rows.fix: Rebuild the rear third: push the dorsal and anal fins back so their bases run from ~70% to the caudal peduncle and let them visually merge with the caudal into one continuous paddle, then flood the scales over that same rear third with the crimson trailing-edge rim (a red arc on each scale, not a wash) so the red-tailed identity reads at thumbnail size.

rows.readsAs: A wooden ruler, a stick of butter, or a burlap-wrapped knife handle — the blunt-ended tan slab does not read as a living fish
rows.defect: The silhouette is a flat-sided slab squared off at BOTH ends: the head end terminates in a blunt vertical face and the tail end in another, so the animal reads as a cut length of dowel rather than a fish. Two of the three must-reads are entirely missing. (1) No barbels — the chin is a bare blunt corner; nothing projects from it. (2) No steeply upturned drawbridge mouth — the jaw is a single straight horizontal dark slot scribed low on the snout face, almost parallel to the lateral line, which is the exact opposite of the near-vertical oblique gape that IS the arowana. (3) The long ribbon dorsal and anal fins are only half-present: they exist as a flat grey rim hugging the top and bottom edges, indistinguishable from an outline stroke, with no rays, no depth, and no flare. The caudal is a tiny dark wedge with three or four stray hair-rays hanging off the left end, so small and so disconnected from the blunt body face that it reads as damage. The all-over square knurl texture reads as woven basketwork or canvas, not as the arowana's big metallic mosaic scales, and the flat khaki colour carries no sheen. The eye disc sits at the extreme upper-front corner of the block rather than on a modelled head.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: cut the snout back into an oblique wedge and swing the lower jaw up to a near-vertical hinged plate that meets the upper jaw at the very top of the head, then hang two long forward-curving barbels off its tip — and give the dorsal/anal ribbons real width with visible rays so they read as fins instead of an outline.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan plush monkey, indistinguishable from the Capuchin and Macaque in the same batch
rows.defect: The long dog-like muzzle that IS the baboon is absent — the face is the family's flat button snout with no jaw projection at all. The tail is the shared smooth C-curve, not the sharply kinked-then-hanging profile the note calls out, and there is no shoulder cape.
rows.fix: Build a real projecting snout: extend the skull forward into a long deep dog muzzle with close-set eyes pushed to the top of it, and rebuild the tail as two straight segments — a steep upward stub at the base then a sharp break into a hanging drop.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then re-read it at 6x on the head, 4x on the tail, 5x on the feet and 3x on the whole body. The FAIL stands, and it stands for a harder reason than the original judge gave: this asset is the Capuchin chassis recoloured. Rendering Capuchin.png side by side, the two are the same drawing — same round frontal skull with a dark cap band across the brow, same two round side-set ears, same close-set white eyes, same egg-shaped torso, same two stubby forelimbs framing a pale belly, same squat hind legs with paddle feet, same tail springing from the same point on the animal's right. Baboon is that figure scaled up, tinted tan and given darker blotches. There is nothing baboon-specific anywhere on it; it reads as a generic macaque/capuchin monkey posed face-on and upright, not a quadruped dog-faced baboon.

MUST-READ 1 (long dog-like muzzle with close-set eyes) — HALF PRESENT, and correct the judge here. The eyes ARE close-set: two small white orbs sitting near the midline of the face with only a narrow bridge between them. Do not touch those. The muzzle is the failure. At 6x the lower face is a rounded ball with a small darker patch bearing two nostril dots and a short curved mouth line — so calling it a 'flat button snout' is fair in effect but slightly wrong in detail (there is a nose and a mouth, they are simply painted flat onto a sphere). There is zero forward projection: no snout mass, no jaw depth, no length from the eyeline to the mouth, no muzzle silhouette breaking the head's circular outline. Because the head is drawn dead face-on, a baboon muzzle can only read here as a long forward-thrust cylinder foreshortened toward the viewer, or the head must be turned to three-quarter/profile. Neither was attempted. The single feature that IS the baboon is absent.

MUST-READ 2 (tail kinked sharply upward at the base then hanging down) — ABSENT, and it fails in two ways, not the one the judge named. Correct: it is a smooth continuous C-curve with no kink or break anywhere along it, exactly the shared family tail. Additional defect the judge missed: the tail ROOT is in the wrong place. It attaches high on the animal's right flank at roughly mid-torso/shoulder height, well forward of and above the rump, so it appears to sprout from the ribcage rather than the hips. And the distal end does not hang — it curls up and inward, ending with the tip raised, so the second half of the note ('then hanging down') is unmet independently of the missing kink. A fix must move the root down to the rump, put a hard angular break just past the base, and drop the remainder vertically.

MUST-READ 3 (cape of long hair over the shoulders in males) — ABSENT, judge correct. At 3x the shoulders are the plain smooth torso outline in the same flat fur as the belly. There is no mane, no fringe, no shaggy break in the silhouette edge, no tonal separation between a shoulder mantle and the back. The only tonal variation on the torso is soft round blotches scattered over the whole trunk, which read as generic mottling, not a cape. The head cap band is a hairline marking, not a shoulder cape, and it is shared with the Capuchin so it cannot carry the identity.

Other observations: feet at 5x are undifferentiated rounded paddles with no toes and no hand/foot distinction, which is wrong for a primate of any kind. Posture is specified 'quadruped' but the figure is drawn upright and frontal with the forelimbs hanging free, so the posture spec is not met either. Aspect reads far squarer than the specified 1.7. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent and the third is half-present; the asset does not read as the named organism.

rows.readsAs: a small brown monkey — roughly right, but only because the capuchin is close to the family's generic default

The tail is the shared stiff C, not a long curling prehensile tail, and the body is the family's heavy barrel rather than a small slender frame.

rows.readsAs: a dark ape — the ears do carry it, but it is nearly invisible against the background
rows.defect: The two protruding round ears are present and are the one genuine variation in the batch, but the pale muzzle and heavy brow are absent — the face is a flat dark disc with the family's white dot eyes. The arms are the shared noodles, so 'reaching past the knees' does not read. The whole figure is near-black on a near-black field with almost no value separation.

rows.readsAs: a squatting tan ape — a gorilla or an orangutan, never a gibbon
rows.defect: The identity must-read is inverted: the arms are SHORTER here than on any other asset in the batch, tucked as stubs against the torso, so the arm span that defines a gibbon is not merely weak, it is the least of the family. The posture is specified upright and rendered as the same squat as the thirteen quadrupeds, and there are no hook-shaped hands.

rows.verifyWhy:
VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440; silhouette occupies x148-288, y128-300, so ~140w x 172h). A face-on, hunched, pot-bellied ape blob: round ball head sitting directly on the shoulders with no neck, a dark elliptical cap/brow band across the forehead, two small rounded ears on the sides (left one smaller and partly behind the skull, right one a fuller rounded lobe), pale tan muzzle with two nostril dots and an upturned smile line, normal white-ringed round eyes. Torso is a wide trapezoid with a light rim-light stroke down both flanks and around the belly. Below the belly sit two large dark rounded thigh/knee ellipses that stop ~24px ABOVE the ground line. Outboard of those, two dark limb columns run down the OUTSIDE of the torso and do reach the ground, ending in flat splayed plinth-shaped foot pads. A dark navy cast-shadow ellipse with its own rim highlight sits between the feet and reads almost like a bowl the animal is standing in.

CLAIM 1 -- 'the arms are SHORTER here than on any other asset in the batch, tucked as stubs against the torso'. WRONG on both counts. (a) The arms are not stubs and are not tucked: they are full-height columns descending from the shoulder region all the way to the ground with flat foot pads. (b) They are not the shortest in the batch. Marmoset and Capuchin use the identical flush-limb treatment (measured: same all-blob silhouette, two ground pads, zero arm/torso separation), so the Gibbon is tied with them, not the minimum.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THE ARMS -- and this is the real defect. The arm columns are drawn FLUSH with the torso silhouette edge: from y164 (shoulder) to y240 the outer contour is a single unbroken line, so the arm has no readable outline of its own and only separates from the body value-wise in the bottom ~35% (y240-300). Compare directly against the other three apes in the same batch, where the arm is a DETACHED column with clear background gaps between it and the torso: Orangutan arms run x124-148 and x296-320, y232-316, giving a ~200px span on a 208px-tall body; Gorilla and Chimpanzee both show the same detached outer columns down to y336. So the batch's arm-span ranking is exactly inverted: Orangutan, Gorilla and Chimpanzee -- whose rows do NOT make arm span the headline -- all show a bigger, clearly readable arm span than the Gibbon, whose note says 'the arm span is the dominant proportion'. The must-read 'arms far longer than the legs, reaching the ground' fails on the 'far longer than the legs' half; the shoulders do not sit higher than the hips and nothing about the proportion reads as brachiator.

CLAIM 2 -- 'no hook hands'. CORRECT AND CONFIRMED at 9x magnification. The two ground contacts are flat, splayed, symmetric pad/plinth shapes, pixel-for-pixel the same foot form used across the family. There is no hook, no elongated curved hand, no finger mass anywhere on the asset.

CLAIM 3 -- 'posture specified upright and rendered as the same squat as the thirteen quadrupeds'. CORRECT. The chassis is verifiably shared with Chimpanzee and Orangutan: same face-on ball head, same dark brow-band ellipse, same eye/nostril/smile stamp, same rim-lit trapezoid torso, same inner thigh ellipses, same plinth feet. Only hue, scale and arm separation change. Row asks for posture: upright; what is drawn is the family crouch.

MUST-READ TALLY. (1) arms far longer than legs, reaching the ground -- FAIL (they reach the ground but read as no span at all). (2) long hook-shaped hands -- ABSENT. (3) no tail at all -- PRESENT and correct; the silhouette is genuinely tailless, and this is a real differentiator since Capuchin and the other monkeys in the batch do carry visible tails. One of three identity must-reads present, and the one the note calls dominant is the one that reads least. The asset reads as a small generic brown ape-blob interchangeable with the Chimpanzee, not as a gibbon.

FIX DIRECTION: detach the arm columns from the torso outline with real background gap (at least the Orangutan's separation), start them at the shoulder not the hip, extend them so the hand pads land at or below the foot line while the thigh ellipses stay clearly shorter, and replace the flat plinth pad with a curved elongated hook hand. Do not shorten or lengthen a 'stub' -- there is no stub to work from.

STRONGER THAN CLAIMED: 'reads as a juvenile chimpanzee' is literally true - I rendered Chimpanzee.png and Gibbon.png from the same family and they are the SAME CHASSIS. Identical dome skull with the same dark cap band, identical round side ears, identical white-sclera eye pair, identical barrel torso with the same pale ventral blob texture, identical thigh ovals, identical mitts and the same squat. The Spider Monkey differs from the Chimpanzee only in overall tone/scale plus a C-tail glued to the left hip. The primate family is one body in several colours, exactly the canid/felid pony-chassis failure.

ONE DEFECT NEITHER OF US LISTED: the row asks for posture 'quadruped' at aspect 1.5 (long-bodied). The render is an upright frontal squat with a body 105 wide x 154 tall - aspect 0.68 excluding the tail. There is no quadruped stance and no horizontal topline at all. Also the dark brow cap is wrong for the species: a spider monkey's face read is a bare dark face with pale eye rings, not a headband.

FIX ORDER: (1) break the arms out of the torso outline and re-proportion them to ~1.5x torso length at ~half the current width, with a visible elbow and a hook hand; (2) give the tail a real fifth-limb read - longer than head-to-rump, tapering, with a curled gripping tip; (3) narrow the chest and shoulders so the low belly actually contrasts, and shrink the skull to ~0.22; (4) stop sharing the ape chassis.

rows.readsAs: a golden lion tamarin, or at least a small orange monkey with a mane

rows.readsAs: a generic blue-grey blotched fish

There are no fleshy lobed fins on muscular stalks anywhere — the only fins are two faint flat dark triangles painted onto the back and flank with no stalk and no separation from the body. rows.verifyWhy:
I decoded the 440x440 PNG, gamma-boosted it (the art is very dark on a near-black field) and re-read it at 4x, then at 9-11x on the tail, mid-body and belly. Verdict UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are described wrongly and would send the fix to the wrong place.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Fish faces RIGHT (white-ringed eye at the right tip). Body is the family's symmetric almond/lens chassis, pointed at BOTH ends, with a single straight pale lateral line running nose-to-tail, a hexagonal scale stipple fill, and a faint arc near the eye standing in for the operculum. No head mass at all - headFrac 0.28 is not expressed; the front third is just the taper of the almond.

CLAIM 1 (lobed fins) - CONCLUSION RIGHT, GEOMETRY WRONG. There are NOT 'two flat dark triangles painted onto the flank'. The fin shapes are FIVE rounded humps drawn BEHIND the body and clearly separated from the silhouette: two on top breaking above the dorsal topline (one around x~205-235, one around x~265-290 in source px), and two/three shallow bumps breaking below the belly line (the largest, at x~200-230 y~215-222, is only ~5px tall). They are rounded flaps, not triangles, and they DO poke outside the outline. Separately, painted INSIDE the flank at x~245-270 y~185-200 there is one faint translucent fan of radiating rays in almost exactly the body tone - the pectoral fin - which is invisible at 1x and only appears under gamma boost. So the must-read still fails, but for a different reason than stated: nothing anywhere carries a fleshy muscular STALK. The coelacanth's identity is paired pectoral and pelvic fins mounted on thick limb-like fleshy peduncles that project away from the body and can be seen as two segments (stalk + paddle). Here the dorsal/anal shapes are stubby rounded flaps flush to the outline, and the one paired fin that exists is a flat, near-transparent fan with zero contrast against the flank. Fix target: build a two-segment stalked fin (visible dark peduncle + terminal paddle) for the pectoral AND pelvic pair, in a tone that separates from the body - not 'redraw the triangles'.

CLAIM 2 (tail) - FULLY CONFIRMED, including the sibling comparison. At 11x the tail is a squarish blob with rounded corners and faint radiating rays, butted onto the caudal point. I rendered Bowfin and Gar side by side: all three carry the identical rounded-square paddle with the same ray fan and the same two stray diagonal hairline strokes floating outside it. No upper lobe, no lower lobe, no notch, and no central epicaudal spike - the single most diagnostic silhouette feature of this animal is entirely absent. It is one shared component, not a per-species tail.

CLAIM 3 (colour) - lands, with a caveat. The body is a pale steel blue-grey and does carry small light dots. But those dots are the SAME hexagonal scale stipple used on Bowfin (rendered olive) and Gar (rendered khaki) - it is the chassis texture recoloured, not a coelacanth white-fleck pass. The diffuse darker mottled blotches on the flank do read as coelacanth-ish camouflage patches, which is the one genuinely species-specific mark on the asset.

FAMILY NOTE. Bowfin, Gar and Coelacanth are demonstrably one chassis: same almond outline, same nose-to-tail lateral line, same scale stipple, same eye, same faint flank fan, same tail paddle. Only hue, aspect ratio and the count/placement of the rounded dorsal humps change. Two of three identity must-reads for Coelacanth are absent and both are the silhouette-defining ones, so it reads as a generic primitive fish in blue. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or pike
rows.defect: There is no beak. The olive spindle simply tapers to a point at the head end; no narrow rostrum ever separates from the skull, so the single feature that makes a gar a gar is missing. The row of white teeth is a short fringe on the last sixth of the underside, sitting on a taper rather than lining a beak. No diamond armour scale pattern — the flank carries the same generic crosshatch as its neighbours — and there are no dorsal or anal fins set far back near the tail; the tail is the same blunt trapezoid paddle.
rows.fix: Give it a genuine beak: a parallel-sided rostrum a third of body length, clearly narrower than the head, with tooth rows along both jaws, then move the dorsal and anal fins to sit opposite each other right at the tail base.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-cropped the head, flank and tail at 6-16x with a gamma boost and again as a background-difference silhouette map, and ran a per-column top/bottom scan of the silhouette. Measured body: x-span 91..348 (258 px long), max depth 40 px sustained from x=207..264, aspect 6.45 (spec 6.5 - proportion is fine). Head is at the RIGHT.

UPHELD, and the core of the claim is correct: THERE IS NO BEAK. The column scan shows the front end tapering smoothly and gradually from 40 px deep at x=264 to 32 px at x=300, 28 px at x=320, 25 px at x=330, 20 px at x=340, ending at x=349. Critically the snout does NOT terminate in a point (correct this part of the claim) - the diff-silhouette shows a BLUNT, ROUNDED, bullet-shaped nose still ~20-22 px deep (half the max body depth) right up to the last 3 px. It is a fat cone, not a rostrum. The eye - a small white ring with a dark pupil - sits at x~327, y~182, so the pre-orbital snout is only ~21 px = 8% of body length and about 0.75x the local body depth. A gar needs the pre-orbital rostrum at roughly 25-30% of total length and near parallel-sided at ~0.2x body depth, visibly narrower than and separated from the skull. Nothing like that is present. The taper at the head is essentially a mirror of the taper at the tail.

Teeth: ~7 small white spikes hang below the ventral edge from x~300 to x~347 (a 47 px run), pointing down/outward, lower jaw only, no upper row. The claim's 'short fringe on a taper' is accurate - they are stuck to a blunt cheek, so they read as an underbite on a blunt-headed fish, not as a toothed beak.

CORRECTION 1 - 'no far-back dorsal/anal fins' is wrong as stated. Two fins ARE drawn far back: at 9x diff-render I can see a thin dark hairline stroke above and a matching one below the caudal peduncle, each roughly 9 px long and 1-2 px thick, angled back, sitting essentially ON the base of the caudal fin rather than on the body ahead of it. They have no area and no silhouette contribution, so at 1x they read as two stray scratches, not fins. The fix is not 'add fins', it is 'give the existing far-back dorsal and anal real filled area (soft triangular/rounded lobes breaking the topline and ventral line) and shift them forward off the tail base so a gap of body shows between fin and caudal'.

CORRECTION 2 - 'generic crosshatch flank' is wrong. There is NO crosshatch anywhere. At 16x the flank is flat olive/khaki carrying (a) one pale horizontal lateral-line stripe through the mid-flank and (b) a sparse single row of very faint darker square-ish dots along the lower flank, barely above noise and invisible at 1x. So the finding is right that the diamond ganoid armour is missing, but the cause is 'flank is essentially plain with a lateral line and a faint dot row', not 'wrong pattern applied'. Needs an actual interlocking rhombic plate lattice with visible edge highlights.

CORRECTION 3 - the read. It does not read as a barracuda or a pike; both of those have a distinctly longer, wedge-pointed jaw than this. With a blunt rounded bullet nose, a forward-set eye, a plain olive body and a lower-jaw tooth fringe, it reads as a generic blunt-headed cigar fish - closest to a wolffish/blenny or a nondescript baitfish.

Other observed detail (not defects, for the record): one small dark triangular pectoral fin at x~265-285 pointing down-back, correctly placed behind the head; caudal is a rounded fan ~41x20 px with visible rays and a short peduncle - acceptable for a gar's short rounded tail; a soft drop shadow ellipse sits below the body.

Band FAIL stands: the single identity-defining must-read (long narrow toothed beak snout) is absent, a second must-read (diamond armour) is absent, and the third (far-back dorsal/anal) is present only as unreadable hairlines. Three of three must-reads fail to read.

rows.readsAs: a lamprey
rows.defect: The identity reads — the round jawless disc with concentric rings of rasping teeth is convincing, seven dark gill pores sit in a row behind the eye, and the body carries no paired fins. What is wrong is geometry: a flat opaque grey wedge lies along the whole topline from mid-body to the head, reading as a separate flat sheet floating above the eel rather than as part of its volume, and the tail end flattens into a bare strap with no caudal fin. The gill pore row also sits too far back, nearer mid-body than the head.
rows.fix: Delete or reshade the grey topline sheet so the body reads as one round tube, and finish the tail with a low continuous fin fold.

rows.readsAs: a small brown loach or minnow with a smudge for a tail
rows.defect: Nothing about this is eel-like — it is the short stubby version of the family almond, roughly 3.5:1 not the 6:1 asked for, deepest at mid-length with a blunt snub at both ends. There is no pointed continuous tail fin: the tail is a tiny black bristle brush stuck on the left end, reading as a stranded scribble rather than a fin. The thread-like filamentous limb fins are entirely absent — no filaments leave the silhouette anywhere. The brown core also sits inside an offset grey membrane halo that reads as a ghost outline rather than a body.
rows.fix: Stretch the body into a long eel and run one continuous low fin from mid-back around a pointed tail tip to the vent, then hang four long thread filaments where the paired fins belong.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but three of the four stated causes are wrong and the fix would miss if made against them. Measured from the pixels (440x440 canvas, bg 5,6,12, column scan at delta>28): the painted silhouette runs x118-339, y157-213 = 222 x 57 px, aspect 3.9:1 against a spec of 6 -- not 3.5:1. More important, that 3.9 is the OUTER shape. The warm scaled core inside it is x133-339, y170-200 = 206 x 31 = 6.6:1, i.e. the actual fish body is already at (slightly past) the spec aspect. It reads stubby only because a second, featureless blue-grey almond ~1.8x the core's height is painted around it. So 'stubby chassis' is the wrong diagnosis; 'correct-aspect body drowned in an oversized fringe shape' is the right one.

GREY HALO -- the judge calls it 'offset'. It is NOT offset. Grey vertical centre = (157+213)/2 = 185.0; warm-core centre = (170+200)/2 = 185.0. They are exactly concentric over the whole length. The real defect is different and worth naming precisely: (a) the grey almond is completely featureless -- no rays, no membrane texture, no value break -- so it reads as a ghost/drop-shadow rather than as the continuous median fin fringe it presumably wants to be; (b) the brown core carries its own heavy bright-white keyline all the way round, so you get two closed outlines nested inside each other, which is what produces the 'double exposure' look; (c) at the head end the grey almond does not taper -- it stops in a hard vertical square cut at x~315 (clearly visible top and bottom in the head crop) about 24px short of the snout, leaving two stranded grey stubs beside the head.

TAIL -- 'tiny black bristle brush / stranded scribble' is wrong. At 18x the tail is a single smooth solid grey-brown wedge, x117-140 (~22px, ~10% of body length), ~11px tall at its base, tapering to a BLUNT squared-off tip, not a point and not strands. There are no bristles anywhere in it. The 'brush' the judge saw at 1x is the scene's pale diagonal water-streak backdrop, which happens to converge just left of the tail and blends into the wedge when downsampled. The verdict on the tail still stands for a different reason: the body ends in a fully blunt white-keylined capsule end at x~133 and the wedge is stuck on OUTSIDE that closed outline, and the grey median almond does not continue into it. So there is no 'pointed continuous tail fin' -- there is a closed pill with a low-contrast stub glued to its back end. Fix must merge the caudal into the body taper, not redraw a brush.

LIMB FINS -- 'entirely absent' is FALSE and this is the biggest error in the original claim. There is a clearly drawn pectoral fin behind the head at roughly x250-292, y172-205: a broad pale rounded lobe with a dark curved leading edge, plus a fan of about six dark radiating rays sweeping rear-and-down. It is real geometry, not a marking. What is wrong is (i) it is a generic webbed ray-fan, the opposite of the required thread-like filamentous limb, (ii) it is drawn entirely INSIDE the body silhouette so nothing protrudes past the ventral edge and at 1x it reads as a scribble on the flank, and (iii) there is only one pair -- the entire rear 60% of the fish (x150-245) is completely bare: no pelvic pair, no dorsal, no anal, nothing but checker scale texture and one lateral line. So the fix is 'replace the webbed fan with two pairs of protruding threads', not 'add missing fins'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE AND CORRECT: fine checker scale texture across the whole flank plus a lateral line (satisfies 'smooth scaled skin'); a blunt, undifferentiated head. Against that, the eye is a bold high-contrast white annulus with a black pupil, far too loud for the row's 'eyes: small', and it is the single most salient feature in the whole asset.

BAND: FAIL stands, not POLISH. Two of the three must-reads are unreadable as specified (no pointed continuous tail fin; no filamentous limb fins), the silhouette reads 35% too short because of an artifact shape, and the ghost double-outline is a rendering defect rather than a styling choice. At 1x the asset reads as an anonymous pill-shaped fish, not as a lungfish.

rows.readsAs: a swordfish or billfish
rows.defect: The rostrum is long enough but it is the wrong shape — a narrow tapering spike that comes to a point, not a broad flat spatula, so with the forked tail behind it the whole animal reads as a billfish. The cavernous gaping toothless mouth is missing entirely; the mouth is a single thin line under the eye. The flank carries the same crosshatch stipple as the scaled species in this batch, which contradicts the smooth scaleless skin.
rows.fix: Widen the rostrum into a parallel-sided flat paddle with a blunt rounded tip, and open the jaw into a wide gaping cavern behind it.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan minnow with a dark blob stuck on its nose
rows.defect: A dark grey lozenge floats at the front of the snout, barely touching it — it reads as a detached fragment or a smudge, not as a snout, a mouth or barbels. There are no barbels at all under it. The rows of bony scutes that are the whole identity of a sturgeon are absent: the back and flanks carry only the same flat crosshatch stipple used on Bowfin, Gar and Lungfish, with one generic triangular dorsal bump. The tail is a small symmetric fork, not the shark-like upturned asymmetric tail.
rows.fix: Attach a long tapered snout with four hanging barbels beneath it, then run three ridges of raised pointed scutes along the back and both flanks and make the upper tail lobe clearly longer than the lower.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at native size and again at 7-9x nearest-neighbour zoom on head/dorsal/tail, plus a background-subtracted 6x gain pass to hunt for faint thin geometry. The FAIL stands, but ONE OF THE THREE stated causes is factually wrong and must not be 'fixed'.

MUST-READ 1 - rows of bony scutes ridging back and flanks: ABSENT. CONFIRMED. The entire flank carries one uniform checkerboard/stipple grid of tiny same-sized square scales, edge to edge, plus a single pale continuous lateral-line stripe. There is no row of large discrete plates, no size hierarchy, no highlight-per-plate, and critically the dorsal SILHOUETTE (zoomed at 9x, x=130-260, y=158-188) is a perfectly smooth unbroken arc with a clean rim highlight - not one scute bump breaks the outline. The judge's 'same flat crosshatch stipple as its neighbours' is substantiated: I opened Paddlefish.png alongside and it is the SAME CHASSIS - identical fusiform outline, identical checkerboard stipple, identical triangular pectoral fan in the same spot, identical low-contrast dark dorsal hump, identical gill arc; only the hue differs (Sturgeon olive-tan, Paddlefish pale cyan). Note Paddlefish's own mustRead says SCALELESS smooth skin, so that stipple is a generic default painted on every member of the family, not a sturgeon decision. THIS IS THE HEADLINE DEFECT - the scute rows are the whole identity and nothing stands in for them.

MUST-READ 2 - four barbels under a long pointed snout: BARBELS ABSENT, CONFIRMED at 6x gain against a subtracted background (any 1px hair-thin barbel would have blown out to bright yellow; nothing appeared anywhere under the snout). The 'long pointed snout' half is arguably PRESENT - the head does taper to a genuine sharp point over roughly 55px, about 0.25 of body length, matching headFrac. The floating lozenge claim is CORRECT and I can give it coordinates: a flat dark-grey ellipse roughly 41x16px centred at approx (356,207), long axis horizontal, lying almost entirely FORWARD of the snout tip at approx (336,204) and overlapping it by only ~2-4px. It is ~1/3 the luminance of the body, so it does not read as continuous with the head at all - it reads as a detached dark blob parked in front of the face. Best guess at its intent: a rostrum/mouth primitive placed with a forward offset and not colour-matched or hull-merged into the head.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE ORIGINAL JUDGE MISSED: the eye is drawn OUTSIDE the head silhouette. The white ring with dark pupil is centred at approx (321,194); the upper edge of the snout at that x sits at y~198, so the ring floats on the dark background ABOVE the snout and is merely tangent to the outline at its bottom. Two detached elements on one head (eye ring + snout lozenge) - this looks like a shared placement bug in how head furniture is anchored when the head is a narrow taper, worth checking across the whole family rather than nudging one species.

MUST-READ 3 - shark-like upturned asymmetric tail: THE JUDGE IS WRONG. This one is PRESENT AND CORRECT. Zoomed at 8x with gain, the caudal is plainly heterocercal: fork joint at approx (118,203), upper lobe tip at approx (64,164), lower lobe tip at approx (89,225). Upper lobe length ~67px, lower lobe ~36px - a ratio of about 1.8:1, with the long lobe swept distinctly UP and back. It is neither symmetric nor especially small (it spans ~80px against a ~218px body). The only legitimate criticism of the tail is TONE, not shape: it is painted very dark, close to the background value, so at native size it reads as a faint smudge and its asymmetry is easy to miss - which is likely exactly how the judge lost it. Do not restyle this tail's geometry; lift its value/contrast so the existing correct shape is legible.

BAND: FAIL upheld. Two of three must-reads fail (scutes absent outright, barbels absent), the body is a verbatim shared chassis with its family neighbour, and two head elements are detached from the silhouette. It currently reads as generic-fish, not sturgeon. FIX ORDER: (1) real scute rows - a dorsal ridge plus one lateral row of large discrete plates that BREAK the dorsal outline, at a clearly coarser scale than the flank stipple; (2) four barbels as a ventral fringe under the snout; (3) merge the snout lozenge into the head hull and colour-match it, and re-anchor the eye inside the silhouette; (4) raise the caudal's value. Do NOT touch the tail's shape.

rows.readsAs: a generic yellow reef fish, closest to a yellow tang or a small sunfish
rows.defect: The identity must-read - a rigid armoured BOX-shaped carapace - is entirely absent. The body is a soft rounded ovoid with a continuous curved outline: no flat facets, no hard dorsal or ventral keels, no square-cut cross section, no hexagonal plate tessellation. The texture over it is ordinary curved fish scaling, not armour. The second must-read fails too: the caudal fan is large and broad rather than a tiny fin poking out of a rigid box, so nothing reads as appendages escaping a shell. The third fails as well - there are no pursed lips or any mouth whatsoever, just blank yellow where the face should end, and the eye is a small flat dot rather than a big prominent one. It is the pufferfish drawing stretched wider and recoloured yellow.
rows.fix: Redraw the body as a hard-edged box: a trapezoidal/triangular cross-section with a straight flat ventral floor, straight angled dorsal slope, visible corner ridges running nose-to-tail, and hexagonal plate tessellation over the whole carapace - then shrink the caudal and pectoral to small fins poking out of holes in that shell, and put a big eye and pursed protruding lips on a blunt squared-off face.

rows.readsAs: a round-bodied khaki fish - plausibly a puffer, but equally a discus or a small drab tang
rows.defect: The round body is roughly there, so the organism is not wrong, but two of the three must-reads are not visibly present. There are no big protruding eyes - just one small flat white dot with a pupil, sitting flush on the flank with no bulge or socket. There is no small beaked mouth: the front of the fish is completely blank, no beak, no lip line, no dental plate. The fins also work against the read - the caudal is a broad rounded fan larger than anything on a puffer, rather than tiny fluttering fins. The body is only mildly rounded (about 1.25:1) so it neither commits to the taut inflated balloon nor to the stated uninflated ovoid, and the drab khaki fill with no prickles or spot pattern gives the eye nothing else to lock onto.
rows.fix: Push the body to a near-circular taut balloon and add the two signature features at the face - a pair of bulging domed eyes standing proud of the outline and a small hard beak with a visible central seam - then shrink the caudal to a small fluttering fan.

rows.readsAs: an ordinary pet rabbit, in brown
rows.defect: The whole identity of a hare is absent. The body is a pudgy round egg, not lean or angular, and the hind legs are two short dark pegs with no hock, no elongated foot and no rangy thigh — the animal is shorter-legged than the Rabbit asset it is supposed to out-run. The ears are dark brown over their full length with no distinct black tip, so the one marking called out is not readable either. Side by side with Rabbit.png this is the same silhouette in a warmer hue.
rows.fix: Rebuild the hind limb as a long visible hock: raise the rump, drop a real thigh mass outside the belly line, add a long flat hind foot planted on the ground, and stretch the body ~25% longer so the topline reads lean rather than egg-shaped — then paint the outer third of each ear black.

rows.readsAs: a pale cream pet rabbit
rows.defect: Same chassis as Hare and Rabbit with the fill lightened. The ears are only marginally longer than the head, not enormous. The 'very long powerful hind legs' are two thin dark stubs poking from under the belly with no thigh, no hock and no foot. The eye is a small round dot sitting mid-skull just behind the muzzle, not large and not set high or far back. Two of three must-reads are simply not on the canvas.
rows.fix: Give it the sprinter's rear: a deep muscled thigh breaking the silhouette, a long angled hock, and a long hind foot on the ground — and enlarge the eye and slide it up and back toward the ear base so the skull reads jackrabbit.

rows.readsAs: a small brown rabbit
rows.defect: This is the rabbit chassis shrunk. The ears are tall pointed upright ovals — rabbit ears — when the packet note says explicitly they must be short and round, not long like a rabbit's. The rear carries the same dark comma swirl plus a protruding stub, so a tail reads where there must be none. The body is not an egg pressed to the rock: it stands on the same two pegs with clear daylight under the belly. The defining pika silhouette is entirely absent.
rows.fix: Replace the ears with two low round pale-rimmed discs set on the sides of the skull, delete the rear stub and swirl so the rump ends in a clean tailless curve, and drop the belly onto the ground so no leg gap shows.

rows.readsAs: a rabbit
rows.defect: The species a stranger would actually name — but it is carrying the family's whole silhouette on its own. The long upright ears read. The short round powder-puff tail does not exist: the rear shows the same dark brown comma swirl the other three have, with no pale round puff anywhere. The hind legs are not heavy or crouched; the haunch is a smooth undifferentiated body curve and the only leg is a thin dark peg with no foot. The white rectangle on the muzzle reads as a stuck-on paper tag rather than incisors.
rows.fix: Add a distinct pale round puff tail clear of the body outline, and separate the hind leg into a heavy folded thigh plus a planted hind foot instead of a peg.

rows.readsAs: a tan lamb or young ram with a lemur's tail stuck on
rows.defect: Every must-read is absent or inverted. The tail is banded but hangs DOWN in a limp droop off the croup — the identity trait is that it is carried straight UP like a flagpole, and the picture shows the exact opposite. The snout is a short blunt DOWN-turned ram muzzle with a forehead bump; the long, thin, UPTURNED flexible probe that names a coati is nowhere. The body is a deep barrel-chested ungulate torso on four straight vertical column legs ending in small dark cloven wedges, not a long low body on plantigrade five-toed feet. The single curled hook ear reads as a horn.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette: drop the barrel to a long low tube, put the head DOWN at shoulder height on a slender neck, replace the muzzle with a narrow snout that extends well past the jaw and kinks UPWARD at the tip, rotate the banded tail to a rigid vertical flagpole, and replace the hoof wedges with flat plantigrade feet showing toes.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 8-9x zooms of head (245,115,110x90), tail (95,175,100x100) and feet (150,215,175x85). The FAIL stands: all three must-reads fail on their defining property, and the animal reads as a tan lamb/hogget with a ringed tail hooked on. Corrections to the original claim follow.

TAIL (the identity item). The judge said it 'hangs DOWN in a limp droop'. What is actually drawn: the tail leaves the rump roughly HORIZONTALLY at hip height, rises a few pixels over the first two rings, then arcs down and FORWARD in a hook, the solid dark tip finishing at mid-thigh height, level with the belly line — a question-mark/curl, not a straight droop. That distinction matters for the fix: the whole tail has to be re-rooted and rotated to vertical from the BASE (flagpole, tip above the topline), not merely straightened at the tip. Also correcting the judge by omission: the banding itself is present and is the single most legible coati cue in the picture — 6-7 hard-edged dark-brown rings on cream, high contrast. The packet asks for a FAINTLY banded tail; this is over-contrasted, closer to a ring-tailed lemur/raccoon tail than a coati's soft bands. So the tail is not missing, it is mis-carried and over-marked.

SNOUT. The judge called it a 'short blunt down-turned ram muzzle'. Down-turned and blunt are right; 'short' is wrong and would misdirect the fix. Measured on the zoom, back-of-skull x~273, eye centre x~299, nose tip x~324 — the muzzle from the eye is ~49% of total head length, i.e. already moderately long. The defects are shape and direction, not length: it is a THICK wedge that blends into a heavy jaw with a drooping mouth-line beneath it, and the terminal tip curves DOWN with the nostril dot set on the upper-front. A coati needs that same length thinned to a narrow mobile probe with the last third turned UP past the lip. Length is the one dimension that is already near-correct.

BODY/FEET. Confirmed. Deep barrel chest, level topline barely higher at the withers, very high belly clearance, short upright neck carrying the head well above the shoulder — the low, long, hunched, nose-down foraging line of a coati is entirely absent, and the coat is painted as a woolly fleece stipple which is what pushes the read to lamb. I read the PNG at full size, then decoded it and re-rendered two nearest-neighbour crops (7x on the whole animal, 18x on the head) plus a pixel row-profile, so every number below is measured, not guessed. VERDICT UPHELD — but three of the four factual claims in the original finding are WRONG and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Fish + fins occupy x 123-316, y 175-214 in a 440x440 frame. Facing RIGHT (eye at right, caudal fan at left).

CORRECTION 1 - the head does NOT taper to a sharp point and the eye is NOT on the tip. The snout end is a BLUNT, essentially squared-off rounded cap: the silhouette holds full body depth (right edge x=316) across rows 197-204 and only rounds off in the last 2-3 rows. There is no taper at all. The eye is a small white-ringed disc centred near x=300, y=193, i.e. ~16 px BEHIND the snout tip and set high in the upper half of the head. So 'high-set eye near a blunt front end' is literally present. What is missing is head MASS: the head is exactly the same depth as the trunk, with no steep forehead, no jowl, no thick lip, and NO MOUTH DRAWN ANYWHERE. Only a single thin curved opercular arc at x~272 hints that a head region exists. The mustRead asks for a blunt BULLDOG head; the drawing gives a blunt tube end. Half-met, and the missing half is the reason the head has no character.

CORRECTION 2 - the dorsal is NOT four detached sawtooth triangles. It is ONE CONTINUOUS FIN with a solid base: at rows 182-190 the fin scans as a single unbroken run from x=202 to x=284 (83 px, no gaps); the notches only appear in the top ~6 rows (176-181), where the profile resolves into FIVE peaks, not four (row 176 runs: 202-205, 220-225, 240-245, 261-265, 282-284). So 'continuous' is satisfied; 'sawtooth crest instead of a fin' and the count are the accurate complaints. The real failure is EXTENT: the fin spans x 202-284, which is only 43% of the 191 px body length, sitting from ~17% to ~60% of the way back from the snout. It stops 32 px short of the head and 77 px short of the tail. A blenny's dorsal must start just behind the skull and run almost to the caudal peduncle. As drawn it reads as a mid-back spiky crest, not a full-length dorsal.

CORRECTION 3 - it is NOT rendered at a fifth of frame width. The animal spans 194 of 440 px = 44% of frame WIDTH. What is true is that it is only 40 px tall = 9% of frame HEIGHT, so the painted area is small and the composition looks empty; that is a framing/height observation, not a width one.

CONFIRMED, AND IT IS THE DECISIVE ONE - THERE ARE NO CIRRI. I swept every pixel in x 284-340, y 168-190 (directly above and forward of the eye) against the per-row background: every delta sits at 13-15, identical to the background vignette noise elsewhere on those rows. Nothing is drawn there. The feathery supraorbital tufts, the single most diagnostic blenny feature, are entirely absent.

WHY IT STILL READS AS THE WRONG ORGANISM. The body TUBE alone measures 191 x ~18 px = roughly 10.6:1. The packet asks for aspect 4.5. The overall silhouette only reaches 4.85 because the dorsal crest adds height; strip the crest and the animal is more than twice as slender as spec, a uniform-diameter rod with no depth change from snout to caudal peduncle. That rod, plus a mid-back spiky crest and no cirri, is what produces the needlefish/pike read. headFrac 0.25 is effectively unreadable — nothing demarcates a head.

SHADOW. There is a detached elliptical cast shadow roughly x 175-295, y 235-265. It is real and it is detached, but 'far below' overstates it: the gap from the belly (y~212) to the shadow's top edge is ~23 px, about 1.2 body depths. Still wrong (a swimming pose should either ground the shadow or omit it), but it is a secondary defect, not the reason for the band.

FIX BRIEF: deepen the body to ~4.5:1 and give the anterior third visible head bulk with a steep blunt brow and a wide terminal mouth; extend the dorsal to run from just behind the skull to the caudal peduncle as a low continuous membrane (drop the 5-tooth sawtooth); add two feathery branched cirri tufts rising above the eye; reattach or remove the cast shadow.

BANDS - ABSENT, CONFIRMED NUMERICALLY. Body bbox is x159-307, y159-265. Of 12,884 opaque body pixels: 11,041 orange, 1,413 dark ink (outline/hatch/shadow), and only 60 white (0.47%). Every one of those 60 white pixels sits in columns x=281-290 - i.e. they are the sclera ring of the eye. There is no white pixel anywhere else on the fish. A per-column mean-luminance profile across the whole body shows no periodic light/dark structure at all: values wander 78-120 with the hatch texture and fall off only at the two silhouette ends. So there is not even a faint, low-contrast, or wrong-coloured attempt at banding - not white, not dark, not vertical, in any place. The colour histogram of the body is 100% orange/brown ramps (168,72,24 / 240,96,24 / 192,72,24 ...).

WHAT COULD BE MISTAKEN FOR MARKINGS (and is not): there ARE three ink lines on the flank - a dark arc curving down behind the eye (operculum/gill line), a second dark line lower and further back near the pectoral root, and a pale hairline running lengthwise from snout to tail base (the lateral line). None of these is a band: two are head-local gill strokes and the third is horizontal, running along the fish rather than across it. All three appear identically on the Parrotfish, so they are chassis furniture, not Clownfish markings.

FINS - THE CLAIM IS PARTLY WRONG. The judge said the fins are 'the shared sawtooth crest, not rounded paddles'. The DORSAL is indeed a crown of ~5 free-standing sharp triangular spikes in dark brown standing clear above the topline - wrong for an anemonefish, which has one continuous, only slightly notched, soft-edged dorsal. The PECTORAL is a small angular wedge, also not a paddle. But the CAUDAL is in fact a rounded-cornered fan with radiating ray spokes - that one IS a rounded paddle, and it is the correct shape for a clownfish. So must-read 2 fails on the dorsal and pectoral, not on all fins; a fix must reshape the dorsal into a low continuous fin and round the pectoral, and should leave the tail alone.

SNOUT - ABSENT, an additional failure the original claim did not name. The head end is a smooth, unbroken taper to a fairly pointed oval tip. There is NO mouth drawn anywhere - no lip, no jaw line, no mouth slot. Must-read 3 ('blunt stubby snout') therefore has nothing to read at all.

PROPORTION - a further defect not named. Measured body bbox is 149 x 107 px = aspect 1.39, against the packet's requested 2.0. The fish is a deep near-disc plate, which is exactly why it lands in parrotfish/butterflyfish territory.

CHASSIS - the 'identical to the Parrotfish' claim is very nearly right but overstated. Side by side, Clownfish and Parrotfish share: the same almond/lens deep-disc body, the same scale-hatch texture and its row spacing, the same pale lateral hairline, the same gill arc, the same white-ring black-pupil eye at the same relative position, the same small triangular pectoral wedge, the same rounded ray-spoked fan tail sitting slightly detached behind the caudal peduncle, and the same small anal bump under the belly. The ONE difference is the dorsal: Clownfish gets the sawtooth crown, Parrotfish gets a low smooth dorsal slab. So it is one chassis recoloured orange with a different dorsal decal - not literally the same drawing.

BAND: FAIL. Two of three must-reads (the bands, which ARE the organism, and the snout) are wholly absent, the third is only one-third present, and the silhouette is off-spec aspect. This reads as a generic orange reef disc, not as Amphiprion.

rows.readsAs: a sea urchin, or a tick
rows.defect: This is not a fish silhouette at all. It is a red-brown ellipse with straight white and red quills radiating in every direction — forward, backward, up and down — with no tail fin, no caudal peduncle, no head separated from the body and only a single dot for an eye. rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x and again at 3x/5x/6x crops of the head, rear and full body. The FAIL stands, and the core of the claim is accurate, but several specifics need correcting before anyone works a fix against it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS. A single smooth brick-red ellipse, roughly 1.55:1 wide, centred in frame with a soft rim-light along its upper-left and a shadow under its lower-right. Across it run SIX dark-brown vertical bands, drawn as lens/almond shapes (pointed top and bottom, fat in the middle) rather than as bands wrapping a body. From the ellipse edge radiate roughly eighteen rigid, perfectly straight rods arranged as a full 360-degree halo, evenly spaced like the spokes of a sun or the spines of an urchin. Each rod is the SAME primitive: a slightly tapered spindle, rounded at the tip, with a hard two-tone split down its long axis (a pale grey-white face and a dark grey underface), and about half of them carry a red-brown wash on the upper half instead of white. A black bead eye with a small white specular dot sits at the extreme front-upper edge of the ellipse. That is the entire asset.

MUST-READS (aspect 1.5 / headFrac 0.3 / eyes normal / posture swimming):
1. 'Fan of long venomous dorsal spines' — NOT MET, and this is the load-bearing failure. Spines exist in quantity but they are not a fan and not dorsal. They radiate from every point of the perimeter: I confirmed at 6x that one rod exits horizontally FORWARD from the snout position, directly where the mouth should be, and at 5x that three more exit rearward from the tail position; several point straight down from the belly. A lionfish's spines fan upward and backward from a dorsal ridge, which is what makes the silhouette read; a radial halo reads as echinoderm or arthropod. The rods are also stiff, hard-edged and uniform-width — real spines are filamentous, unequal in length, and carry membrane between them.
2. 'Feathery separated pectoral fin rays spread like wings' — ABSENT, exactly as claimed. There is no membrane, no webbing, no plume, no fan of finer rays, and no appendage at the pectoral position that differs in any way from the other seventeen. Every appendage is the same rigid spindle. This is the second identity-defining must-read and nothing on the canvas gestures at it.
3. 'Red-brown and white zebra banding' — HALF MET, and the other judge under-described this by calling it merely 'a banded ellipse'. Banding is genuinely present and is the one thing working: six clean vertical dark bands on a red-brown ground. But there is NO WHITE in the banding at all — it is dark brown on brick red, so the high-contrast zebra read that carries a lionfish at thumbnail size is missing. The only white in the piece is on the spine rods. The bands are also lens-shaped rather than parallel-sided, so they read as segment plates on a shell rather than as pigment stripes on a flank.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM. (a) 'One dot for an eye' is slightly wrong: the eye is a black bead with a white specular highlight, so it is a two-tone glossy bead, not a bare dot. It still fails, but for a different reason — it has no orbit, ring or lid, and it is parked on the bare curve of the ellipse with no head for it to belong to. (b) 'No tail fin, no caudal peduncle' — CONFIRMED at 5x; the rear terminus is an unbroken elliptical arc with nothing but spine rods coming off it. (c) 'No head' — CONFIRMED at 6x and stronger than stated: there is no snout, no mouth line, no jaw, no opercle/gill line, and no taper or notch anywhere separating a head mass from the body. The specified headFrac of 0.3 is not expressed by a single pixel. (d) 'Not a fish silhouette at all' — CONFIRMED; strip the colour and the outline is an ellipse with radial spikes, which is the sea-urchin/tick silhouette the judge named.

VERDICT. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent, the third is present only in structure and not in colour, and the underlying body has none of the fish scaffolding (peduncle, caudal fin, head mass, mouth) that the spines are supposed to decorate. Nothing here is 'present but small' or 'drawn where the judge did not look' — I went looking specifically for a hidden pectoral plume and a hidden tail and neither exists. FAIL is correct and this needs a rebuild from the silhouette up, not a polish: build a proper fusiform fish body with a distinct head third and a fanned caudal fin, restrict the spines to a dorsal ridge fan with membrane between them, add webbed feathery pectorals as the largest single feature, and repaint the bands as alternating red-brown and WHITE.

rows.readsAs: a cyan sunfish; the Clownfish drawing in a different colour

There is no beak — no fused tooth plate, no mouth of any kind, just the shared scribed jaw wedge; the forehead is not blunt or bulging but the same gently tapering almond nose every disc fish in this batch has; and there are no large paddle pectorals for rowing, only the single shared belly lobe. rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4x, 9x and 16x crops plus a contrast-boosted snout crop, and side-by-side against Clownfish.png at identical crop/scale. FAIL upheld: two of the three must-reads are absent, and the third is present but unreadable.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A cyan almond/disc body, nose-right, spanning roughly x157-315, y151-266 in the 440px canvas -- body length ~158px, body depth ~115px, so the rendered aspect is ~1.37:1 against the packet's specified 2.6. That alone is the wrong body plan: a parrotfish is an elongated oval, this is a plate. Features present: a small round white-ringed eye with a Pac-Man-notch pupil high and far forward; one long scribed opercular arc curving from the topline down behind the eye to the belly; dense stamped scale rows; a low rounded dorsal lobe over the mid-back with three or four thin ray filaments trailing up and back; a small anal-fin nub under the belly; a detached palm-frond fan tail at far left; and -- contra the judge -- a pectoral fin.

CORRECTION 1 (the judge is wrong on the pectorals being absent). A pectoral IS drawn. At source x~222-275, y~207-238 there is a triangular fan with about eight radiating ray strokes, apex pinned at the gill arc and spreading back and down across the flank. The defect is not absence, it is prominence and shape: it is rendered as a translucent inset the same cyan as the body with only faint dark ray lines, roughly 40x30px on a 158px body, and it is a narrow swept triangle, not a broad rounded rowing paddle. It reads as a body marking, not as a limb. Any fix must ENLARGE and RE-TONE the existing fan (broad rounded blade, own value separation from the flank, tips clear of the ventral line), not add a fin that isn't there.

CORRECTION 2 (the judge is wrong that it is a pure Clownfish recolour). Everything below the topline is identical to Clownfish.png -- same almond outline, same eye size and placement, same single gill scribe, same faint triangular pectoral in the same pixel neighbourhood, same detached fan tail, same anal nub, same scale stamps. The one silhouette difference is the dorsal: Clownfish carries a three-point sawtooth crest, Parrotfish a low smooth lobe with thin trailing filaments. So it is the same chassis with a swapped dorsal and a hue change, not a straight recolour. That distinction matters because the chassis, not the paint, is the thing to fix.

CONFIRMED FAILURES. (a) 'fused beak-like teeth plates' -- absent, and absent at every contrast level I could pull. At 16x with a 2.2x contrast lift the snout tip (x~305-315) is bare: no beak, no lip, no tooth plate, no terminal line of any kind. The only mouth-adjacent mark is a faint dark horizontal scribe at y~225-230 running x~250-290, i.e. the shared family jaw wedge, and it dies ~25px short of the snout tip so it does not even close as a mouth. (b) 'blunt bulging forehead' -- absent. The dorsal-to-snout profile is a single smooth convex arc that tapers to a point, the same almond taper carried by Clownfish, Butterflyfish and the rest of the disc set; there is no steep brow, no forehead bulge, no break in the curve above the eye.

Net: the asset reads as a generic cyan reef disc. The two features that make a parrotfish a parrotfish -- the fused beak and the bulging blunt head -- are not on the canvas, and the third is drawn too small and too flat to register.

rows.readsAs: a pale blue disc fish; the Tang drawing in a lighter blue

At 10x the body ellipse's rear edge meets the caudal fin directly - the fan's ray convergence point sits ON the body outline with zero narrowing, no wrist, no keel. The silhouette there is a clean unbroken arc. Inside it there is only the generic scale-row texture plus one faint pale horizontal streak (a lateral-line highlight artifact, not a blade); no dark slash, no notch, no protruding spine, no scalpel-yellow accent. So the fix is not 'add a mark' - it needs a narrowed peduncle built first and the blade hung on it, otherwise there is nowhere anatomically for the spine to live.

MUST-READ 2 (oval compressed body + steep forehead) - HALF PRESENT, and the judge undersold the half that works. The body IS a deep, laterally-compressed disc and that part reads fine. But it is drawn nearly circular - body-only width:height is roughly 1.15, against the packet's 1.7 - so the front profile is just the same circular arc as everything else. There is no separately modelled steep forehead: the head crop shows one smooth even curve running from under the crest down to a blunt taper, with a single cyan mouth line and a curved gill-cover line as the only head detail. No small pointed grazing snout either. It reads as a generic round reef disc (butterflyfish/tang territory), not a surgeonfish head.

The entire rear half of the back, from mid-body to the tail, is completely bare. It is also flat-shaded vector-style with hard polygon edges, against a painterly stippled/scaled body - a render-style mismatch on top of the anatomy miss.

OTHER: caudal is a broad triangular ray-fan, not the family's lunate/crescent tail; anal fin is a small unshaped nub under the belly; pectoral is a faint translucent triangle low on the flank. The judge's 'this is the Tang drawing in a lighter blue' is fair and I confirmed it by opening Tang.png - same disc body, same five-spike crest, same fan tail, same eye, only a deeper blue and slightly smaller. Neither carries its family's tail-base spine, so the two are currently indistinguishable except by hue.

VERDICT: one of three must-reads half-present, the name-giving feature absent, and the asset is chassis-identical to its sibling species. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a blue tang, or just a blue fish

rows.readsAs: a teal sunfish
rows.defect: Every must-read fails. The eyes are not set far back and high away from the mouth — the single eye sits right at the snout tip, as close to the mouth as it can get; there is no erectile trigger spine on the forehead at all, just two soft rounded humps well behind the head; and the body is a plump symmetric oval, not a leathery diamond, with no rowing second dorsal and anal fins (the second dorsal is a small blob and the anal is the shared belly lobe). It is the Clownfish/Parrotfish silhouette in teal.
