rows.verifyWhy:
Measured the PNG at 440x440 and re-cropped the head, back, belly and tail at 6-14x. Silhouette bbox x126-313, y139-262. The tail fan occupies x126-178; the body proper runs x~180-313 (133px long) with a max depth of ~120px (excluding fins) -> body aspect ~1.1, near-circular; overall aspect with tail ~1.5 against the packet's 1.8. Column profile (top/bottom of the green mask): x=200 157/254, x=220 140/260, x=260 146/249, x=291 180/232, x=310 200/214. That is a smooth convex almond/lens, fore-aft near-symmetric, pointed at both ends, with no angular corners anywhere -- not a leathery rhombus with straight converging dorsal/ventral edges and a pinched peduncle.

MUST-READ 1 (eyes set far back and high, well away from the mouth) -- FAILS. The white sclera ring measures x286-296, y191-202, so the eye centre is (291, 196.5). The snout tip is x=313, i.e. the eye sits 22px behind the tip on a 133px body = 16.5% of body length, roughly 1.5 eye-diameters from the nose. At x=291 the body spans y180-232 (local mid 206), so the eye is only 9.5px above local centre out of 52px of depth -- it reads as a centred eye on a tapering snout, not an eye pushed up under the dorsal profile and set a third of the way back. So the judge is right that the eye is at the snout and not far back/high.

CORRECTION to the judge on the mouth: there is NO mouth drawn at all. At 14x on the snout (source x270-318, y180-228) the head is a clean smooth taper -- no lip line, no jaw notch, no dark mouth stroke, nothing. The only linework forward of the eye is a pale horizontal lateral-line stripe that passes just below the eye and dies out about two-thirds of the way to the tip, plus a faint dark curved gill arc behind and below the eye. So "right beside the mouth" is not verifiable and is the wrong phrasing: the defect is the eye's absolute forward/central placement PLUS a completely absent mouth (a triggerfish's small terminal chisel mouth at the end of a long snout is itself a missing read).

MUST-READ 2 (erectile trigger spine on the forehead) -- FAILS, absent. There are exactly two dorsal elements, both dark-teal rounded humps drawn BEHIND the body outline and rising only ~15px above the back: a rear one at x~215-240 and a forward one at x~253-272 (peak ~x262). The forward one sits 41-60px behind the snout tip, i.e. over the mid-back, not on the forehead, and its profile is a rounded bump, not an erect spike. The dorsal contour from x=272 to the snout at x=313 is an unbroken smooth curve with nothing on it. No spine, no trigger, no locking first-dorsal group of any kind.

MUST-READ 3 (rowing second dorsal and anal fins) -- CORRECTION, the judge overstated this. The fins are not absent: besides the two dorsal humps there is a small dark ventral nub peeking below the belly at x~203-225 (visible only as a ~10px bulge past the outline). The real failure is that these are vestigial rounded bumps, fore-aft OFFSET rather than mirrored (rear dorsal 215-240 vs anal 203-225), roughly half the anal's size difference, and painted behind/under the silhouette so they read as background lumps rather than the tall matched sculling pair that defines the balistid.

Other observations for the fix: the caudal is a large dark D-shaped fan with radiating ray lines butted flush against the rear point with no peduncle (it does touch the body, so it is not detached, but there is no narrow caudal wrist); a hatched fan-shaped pectoral is drawn INSIDE the silhouette at mid-body (x~250-285, y~200-230) where it reads as a dark smudge over the flank rather than a fin; the flank carries dense bright dash-rows reading as ordinary fish scales plus one bright full-length lateral stripe, so the surface reads scaly, not leathery/plated.

Verdict: the judge's band and their overall gist ("Clownfish/Parrotfish silhouette in teal") stand. Two of the three must-reads are genuinely absent or inverted and the third is present only as vestigial bumps. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or a small piranha
rows.defect: The cigar body is right, but the dentition is drawn as a row of about seven big white sawtooth fangs running the whole jaw line, which reads as a predatory barracuda rather than a pair of protruding buck teeth, and the large fan pectoral fins that are supposed to be doing the swimming are absent entirely — there is no pectoral fin on the flank at all. Body, hatch texture and tail are the shared elongate spindle it uses with Blenny and Goby.

rows.readsAs: a crouched brown cartoon rabbit
rows.defect: The must-read that IS the agouti — slender delicate legs with hoof-like claws under a high rump — is absent: the body is the shared ball and the legs are two stubby dark pegs poking out of the belly outline with no joint, no length and no foot. Erect pink-lined ears and a whiskered wedge face complete the rabbit read.
rows.fix: Redraw the legs as long thin two-segment columns that leave the silhouette at a visible shoulder and hip, ending in three small dark hoof-like nails, and raise the body clear of the ground so the leg length is the first thing seen.
rows.verifyWhy:
I read the PNG at full size, then at 4x, then at 8x with a 2.2x brightness boost over the lower body so dark-on-dark limbs separate, and I measured the silhouette column-by-column. The FAIL stands, but three parts of the stated cause are factually wrong and must not be fixed against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. Silhouette spans x=142..296, top of back y=157, ground contact y=262 (440x440 canvas). Head faces right. Body is one smooth convex ovoid.

LIMB COUNT IS WRONG: there are TWO limbs, not four. At y=255 exactly two dark masses exist -- x=177..213 and x=229..236 -- and nothing between them but the ground-shadow ellipse. There is no far-side pair at any opacity; I checked the boosted crop and the pixel map. Reporting 'four pegs' will send a fix at the wrong problem: the creature is standing on one hind leg and one foreleg.

'JOINTLESS PEGS' IS HALF WRONG. The foreleg (x=226..241, y=236..262, only ~26px long against a ~105px body) IS a jointless peg -- a rounded-top column that flares into a small blunt pad, no shoulder, no wrist, no digits. But the HIND limb is not a peg at all: it is a thick blunt BOOT. A wide column drops from the haunch, bends at roughly ankle height, and turns forward into a broad flat foot lying along the ground from x~177 to x~213. That is a plantigrade rabbit slipper, ~36px of sole. It is the single strongest reason the asset reads lagomorph, and it is the opposite of the defect described.

'POKE OUT OF THE BELLY' IS WRONG FOR THE HIND LIMB. There is a drawn haunch: a pale crescent arc runs from about (170,232) up over (200,205) and down to (232,240), enclosing a shaded thigh disc, and the hind limb emerges from the bottom of that disc. The attachment is anatomically placed. Only the foreleg drops straight off the unbroken belly line with no shoulder mass.

MUST-READ 2 IS GENUINELY ABSENT -- the judge is right on substance. 'Slender delicate legs with hoof-like claws': the two limbs present are thick, dark, undifferentiated and short. No hock, no cannon, no elongation, no digits, and above all no hoof-like nail tips -- both feet terminate in soft rounded pads. Nothing on this asset says cursorial.

MUST-READ 1 IS ALSO NOT MET, and the previous judge did not raise it. 'Arched hunched back rising to the rump': the topline reads 202,185,177,172,167,164,161,159,158,157 from the rear, holds 157 across x=196..214, then falls 159,161,162 to the neck. The peak sits at mid-back, ~38% forward of the rump, and the rump itself is a dome that falls away. Worse, the head is carried HIGH -- crown at y=152..166, level with or above the back peak -- where an agouti carries the head low under a hip-peaked arch. The result is a ball with a bump in the middle, not a rump-loaded arch.

MUST-READ 3 IS MET. 'Essentially no tail' -- the rear dome at 8x is completely clean, no tail, no stub, no tuft. Credit where due.

GESTALT CONFIRMS 'BROWN CARTOON RABBIT', and there is more evidence for it than was cited. Two narrow ERECT TRIANGULAR ears with pale inner surfaces stand well clear of the crown. The eye is a large white-ringed disc with a black pupil and a specular dot -- cartoon, not the small dark agouti eye. Below the blunt muzzle hangs a WHITE INCISOR BLOCK, a rectangle split by a vertical seam into two buck teeth, drawn outside the mouth line; agoutis show no such thing in profile. Add the ball body and the flat slipper hind foot and the read is unambiguous.

CHASSIS NOTE for the family pass: two pale seam arcs are visible -- one ringing the head where it meets the body, one ringing the haunch. Both look like generic chassis part-boundaries rather than agouti-specific fur breaks, worth checking against the other 20 rodents.

MEASUREMENTS vs SPEC: silhouette aspect 154/105 = 1.47 against aspect 1.7 (too tall/round, feeding the ball read). Head length ~50px = 0.32 of body length against headFrac 0.27 (slightly oversized). Posture quadruped and eyes prominent are nominally satisfied.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs four limbs, not four better pegs -- a long slender hind limb with a real hock and a narrow hoof-tipped foot standing OFF the ground plane, a matching slender foreleg with a visible elbow, and far-side partners at reduced value. Then drop the head below a topline that peaks over the hips, shrink the ears to small rounded flaps, and delete the external white incisor block.

rows.readsAs: a beaver, mostly — or an otter carrying a beaver's tail
rows.defect: The flat crosshatched paddle tail lands and this is the only asset off the family chassis, but the body is long, low and otter-like rather than stocky and humped, and the big orange chisel incisors are simply not drawn — the muzzle is closed and blank, so the single most recognisable rodent feature is missing.

rows.readsAs: the Agouti image again, a brown cartoon rabbit
rows.defect: Pixel-for-pixel this is the Agouti chassis with a marginally different flank shade. The blunt squared-off brick head that IS the capybara is absent — the head is a small round wedge with a tapered whiskered muzzle and erect pointed ears — and a stub tail is visible where the reference says none. The barrel body sits on peg stubs with no hint of a webbed foot, and the eyes/ears/nostrils are not set high on the skull.
rows.fix: Replace the head with a deep rectangular brick, muzzle squared off at the front, and push the eye, ear and nostril up onto the top plane of that brick; delete the tail stub.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but one of the three stated causes is factually wrong and must not be fixed.

WHAT I SAW (read at full size, then re-cropped and magnified 6-8x on head, rump and feet):

HEAD - the FAIL stands. The head is a small egg/teardrop in profile whose front third narrows continuously into a pointed muzzle; the nose ends in a tiny dark point with three whisker pairs radiating from it, and a pair of flat cream chisel incisors hangs off the underside of that point. There is no blunt vertical brick face, no flat square muzzle-front, no deep boxy jaw - the profile is a squirrel/agouti wedge. headFrac measures right (head is ~0.28 of body length) but the SHAPE is the wrong organism's. This alone is the defining must-read and it is absent.

EYES/EARS/NOSTRILS - the judge's claim is HALF wrong and needs restating so the fix aims correctly. The EARS are in fact set high: two tall upright triangular points sit on the crown of the skull. The defect is not their height, it is their FORM - they are tall pricked squirrel triangles where a capybara wants small, short, rounded ears set far back. The EYE is genuinely mis-sited: one large white-ringed round eye with a black pupil sits at mid-height on the side of the head, roughly level with the muzzle line, not up near the crown, and it is drawn as a big cartoon eye rather than the packet's 'eyes: small'. The NOSTRIL is a small dark point at the very tip of the tapered muzzle, i.e. on the front of a cone, not on a high flat rostrum. So: ears high but wrong shape; eyes and nostrils genuinely low.

TAIL - the judge is WRONG here; do not 'remove a tail'. There is no tail stub. The dark shape they read as one is the HIND LIMB: at 8x you can see a thigh column dropping from under the haunch swirl and a foot that turns and extends FORWARD (leftward past the body edge is only the heel), with a matching smaller foreleg stub further right. The rear silhouette behind the rump is a clean, unbroken curve. The 'no visible tail' must-read is actually SATISFIED.

BODY - a single smooth egg blob with a decorative haunch swirl outlined in a thin white arc. Legs are two short dark stubs; no webbing, no toe splay. Silhouette bbox is 215x128 = aspect 1.68 against the packet's 2, so it is also too short/round for a barrel-bodied animal. The topline peaks at x~194 (mid-body, rump side) versus ~150-155 over the shoulder, so 'rump higher than shoulders' is present only incidentally as the dome of a generic blob, not as a read.

SHARED-CHASSIS CLAIM - confirmed quantitatively. Cropped to their own bounding boxes and resampled to 128x128, Capybara vs Agouti silhouette IoU = 0.852 and Capybara vs Guinea_Pig = 0.827 (Capybara vs Beaver, a genuinely differentiated rodent, = 0.399). Agouti's aspect is 1.66 against Capybara's 1.68. Side by side the two are the same body blob, same haunch swirl, same two limb stubs, same head, same ear pair, same eye, same incisor plate - Capybara is only rendered slightly larger and a shade browner. 'Effectively the same image as Agouti' is accurate.

FIX TARGET: rebuild the head as a blunt rectangular brick with a flat vertical muzzle face and a squared jaw; drop the eye to small and raise it to the top edge of the skull; move the nostrils to the top-front of the flat muzzle; swap the tall triangles for small rounded ears; stretch the body toward aspect 2 with visible short splayed legs. Leave the tail alone - there isn't one.

rows.readsAs: a plain brown rabbit with a squirrel tail glued on
rows.defect: The bold dark-and-pale back and face stripes — the entire identity of a chipmunk — are completely absent; the coat is an unbroken flat brown gradient from nose to rump. There are no cheek pouches either. All that survives is a tail held up behind, on the same shared ball body as Agouti and Capybara.
rows.fix: Paint the stripe set on: five dark dorsal stripes separated by cream ones running shoulder to rump, plus the dark eye-stripe and pale brow stripe on the face.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated cause. I decoded the PNG and read it at 3x and 6x (head, back, feet crops), plus ran luminance scans across the torso and face, plus a 4-up against Ground Squirrel / Hamster / Gerbil.

MUST-READ 1 — 'bold dark and pale stripes along back and face': GENUINELY ABSENT, confirmed instrumentally, not just by eye. Vertical luminance columns through the torso (x=180/200/220/240/260, y=155..275) return a single smooth ramp — roughly L 100 to 145 — with no alternating bands anywhere. Horizontal rows along the topline (y=170/180/190) are equally monotonic. The only non-gradient values in the whole coat are isolated single-pixel spikes (L~154-162) that are the 1px pale outline strokes of the head circle and the haunch circle, and the eye's white sclera ring on the face column (L 229/239/217 at x=275) — that ring is an eye, not a face stripe. There is no dorsal banding, no eye-stripe, no pale supraorbital line. The face is a plain sphere.

CORRECTION A to the claim: 'the coat is unbroken flat brown' is imprecise and would mislead a fixer into merely adding shading. The coat is NOT flat — it carries a strong radial gradient, a thin pale rim-light along the entire topline, a pale stroke where the head sphere meets the torso, a pale stroke ringing the haunch, and a long pale lozenge highlight running down the middle of the tail. So pale marks DO exist on this asset; none of them is a stripe. The correct diagnosis is: zero longitudinal banding and zero tonal contrast beyond lighting — the tail lozenge is the one pale marking present and it is a specular highlight, not a chipmunk stripe.

MUST-READ 2 — 'tail held up behind': PRESENT and the judge correctly credited it. A thick tail arcs up off the rump and forward over the back. It is however a smooth lozenge, not a plume.

MUST-READ 3 — 'bulging cheek pouches': GENUINELY ABSENT. At 6x the head is an unmodified sphere with a small cone muzzle projecting forward; there is no cheek swelling, no jaw mass, nothing below or behind the whisker root. Confirmed.

CORRECTION B / the judge's 'shared rabbit body' — verified empirically and it is stronger than stated. Chipmunk, Ground Squirrel, Hamster and Gerbil are ONE chassis with only hue and tail swapped: identical ball torso, identical haunch-circle stroke in the same place, identical head sphere overlapping the shoulder, identical single eye with white ring, identical 4-whisker fan, identical white two-block incisor plate, identical pair of dark stub limbs, and identical TALL NARROW ears with pink inner lining. CORRECTION 2: so an arch does exist, but it arches BEHIND the rump, entirely clear of the spine, with the tip pointing back down instead of forward over the shoulders. 2) TAIL — claim CONFIRMED, and I ruled out the usual escape hatches. There is NO tail: not short, not stubby, not tucked, not drawn dark-on-dark, not hidden behind the far haunch. I scanned the leftmost lit pixel of every row from y153 to y252; the rear edge runs 241 -> 189 -> 166 -> 149 -> 143 -> 139 -> 137 (minimum at y209-213) -> 142 -> 153 -> 168, a perfectly smooth convex arc with zero protrusion at any row. The only dark shape near the rear is the hind foot/leg, which sits UNDER the belly at x~155-200, well inside the body outline, and is a foot not a tail. Must-read 'short furred tail about half the body length' is entirely missing — for a ~180px body that would be a ~90px appendage, i.e. the largest single missing feature on the asset.

3) MUZZLE — the judge did NOT mention this and should have. Must-read is 'blunt rounded muzzle with a chubby face'. The face does read chubby, but the muzzle tapers to a fairly narrow rounded point and the incisors are rendered as a detached white rectangle with two vertical dividers pasted on the OUTSIDE of the face contour, floating below the whisker root rather than emerging from under a lip. Also note the packet asks for eyes: small. The eye is drawn large, with a bold white sclera ring around a black pupil and a highlight — it reads prominent, not small, which further removes the small-eyed vole cue.

4) 'INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE VOLE ASSET EXCEPT FOR HUE' — substantially correct, with one factual correction. I rendered Vole.png at the same crop. FIX DIRECTION: this is not a polish-level correction. The head needs new ears — small, low, rounded, set well back and mostly sunk into the neck fur so only the top arc of each shows. The rump needs a tail added: a thick, furred, tapering tail ~half the body length (~90px at this scale), same fur colour as the body rather than a naked pink rat tail, trailing back and slightly down from the base of the haunch. The muzzle should be blunted and widened and the incisor block brought inside the face contour. The eye should shrink and lose the heavy white ring. rows.readsAs: a dark cartoon otter pup or spotted newt toy, nearly invisible against the background

UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and the worst defect is misscoped. WHAT I SAW (read at native, then re-read at 2x with gain 3.5 / gamma 0.55, plus 5-6x crops of head, limbs and tail, plus pixel sampling).

1) IDENTITY — CONFIRMED, this is the decisive failure. Component-labelled the warm pixels: NINE discrete ochre/cream spot blobs (76-203px each) sit on the shoulder, dorsum and flank at (319,185) (279,192) (215,193) (194,195) (292,202) (213,206) (279,210) (231,215), plus a tenth on the cheek just behind the jaw at (346,228). Salamandra atra's entire diagnosis is UNIFORM unbroken glossy black; a spot scatter is Salamandra salamandra, which is item #4 of this same batch (the packet's own note calls #4 'a fire/spotted salamander'). MustRead 1, 'glossy jet-black moist skin', is broken by the paint job. Within the batch, #1 and #4 are the same organism in two hues.

2) 'Generic Salamander with the paint darkened' — CONFIRMED AND QUANTIFIED. Silhouette masks of Alpine_Salamander.png vs Salamander.png give IoU 0.845. Shared verbatim: the same trunk topline, the same tail (same length, same upward hook at the tip), the same ovoid skull, the same white rim-stroke arc over the crown, the same eye glyph, the same four limb stations, the same ground-shadow ellipse. Only the base hue (slate-black vs tan) and the spot seed differ. This is one chassis, repainted.

3) 'The skin is flat matte with no wet sheen' — WRONG AS STATED. There IS a gloss treatment, and it is the brightest thing on the asset: a hard white specular stroke runs the full dorsal ridge from mid-back to the snout, a second white crescent arcs over the crown and brow of the skull, and a broad pale-grey highlight band lies along the top of the trunk. The real fault is different: the rim is a hard-edged OUTLINE stroke, not a blooming wet specular, and the interior of the flank is a single flat value with no form modelling, so the gloss reads as a cartoon keyline rather than a moist surface. Fix the note to 'gloss is an outline stroke; add interior specular falloff', not 'add sheen'.

4) 'Tail and hind legs vanish into the backdrop' — right direction, wrong scope, and understated. Sampled: body base is RGB(9,10,13); backdrop next to it is RGB(5,6,12)-(7,11,17). Mean luminance of the trunk interior is 11.92 against a backdrop mean of 13.65 — the BODY IS ACTUALLY DARKER THAN THE SKY, by ~2 levels of 255. The tail (8,9,12) and the legs (6,9,12 / 3,3,4) are no worse than the trunk; the trunk only looks legible because the white keyline outlines it. Lightening only the tail and hind legs would not fix this — the whole silhouette needs to be lifted off the field, or the backdrop dropped, or the keyline extended around the tail and limbs.

5) DEFECTS THE JUDGE DID NOT NAME. (a) POSTURE: the row specifies 'sprawling' and it is not drawn. The 5x crop of the limbs shows four columnar limbs dropping straight down beneath the trunk, ending in dark wedge/boot feet, with the belly held clear of the ground — mammal-erect carriage, no lateral elbow/knee splay, no splayed soft toes. This is the pony-chassis limb model, not an amphibian's. (b) EYES: the row says eyes 'prominent' and mustRead says 'bulging'. The 6x head crop shows a SMALL flat white ring with a dark pupil, sitting flush inside the head silhouette; it never domes out of the skull profile. It is legible (it is white on black) but it is not bulging, and it is the identical glyph on the generic.

6) WHAT IS ACTUALLY MET: 'blunt rounded head' — yes, a clean blunt ovoid skull with a curved mouth line, no snout point. 'Rounded tail' — yes, thick, smoothly tapering, upcurved at the tip, roughly body length. Those two must-reads pass; the failure is mustRead 1 plus the posture and eye specs.

BAND: FAIL. The single most identity-defining must-read (uniform jet black) is contradicted by the artwork, the asset is provably a repaint of the batch's generic, and the whole body sits below backdrop luminance.

rows.readsAs: a brown cartoon otter cub or river-mammal mascot

I tried to break this FAIL and could not. Verified at 1x, then cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled the head (6x and 10x), the flank (8x), the feet and the tail (7x), and pixel-measured features against the generic Salamander, Alpine and Blind assets. Packet row: aspect 5.5 / headFrac 0.24 / eyes small / posture sprawling / mustRead 'broad flattened shovel head - wrinkled fleshy skin folds along the flanks - tiny lidless dot eyes'. No note row.

MUST-READ 1 (broad flattened shovel head) - ABSENT, and the FAIL's description is accurate. At 10x the skull is a plain smooth egg: a domed crown falling to a rounded snout tip, no flattening of the cranial roof, no widened lateral jaw line, no squared shovel muzzle, no separation between cranium and snout. Measured in source pixels the head oval runs roughly x 307-387 by y 177-233, i.e. about 80 long x 56 tall = 1.4:1 in side view; a shovel-headed cryptobranchid at this scale should read as a low wedge nearer 2.5-3:1 with a blunt squared front. The mouth is a single thin upcurved arc that stops well short of the snout tip - a smile, exactly as claimed - where the defining giant-salamander feature is a huge near-straight gape running almost the full head length.

MUST-READ 2 (wrinkled fleshy skin folds along the flanks) - ABSENT. At 8x the flank is a clean unbroken ovoid: one soft lighter dorsal band along the topline and a scatter of soft gold-tan blob spots, and nothing else. Zero fold contours, zero costal grooves, zero lateral frill. Worse than merely absent - the gold spot scatter is the fire/spotted-salamander marking lifted straight off the generic Salamander asset, so the flank actively transmits the WRONG signal (a spotted fire salamander) rather than just failing to transmit the right one. Any fix must remove the gold spots as well as add the folds.

MUST-READ 3 (tiny lidless dot eyes) - ABSENT and inverted, exactly as claimed. The eye is a bright white annulus with a black pupil, measured bbox 13x13 px at x343-355 / y190-202, about 16% of head length. Hard cross-asset proof that this is a shared primitive and not a species choice: generic Salamander eye white measures 12x13 at y191-203, Alpine 11x11 at y192-202 - same size, same vertical seat, same white-sclera cartoon construction on all three, despite the packet asking Alpine for 'prominent' and Giant for 'small'. The eyes token is driving nothing.

WHERE THE FAIL IS IMPRECISE (correct these before quoting it as the fix spec): 'It is the generic Salamander asset in a lighter brown' is overstated. The two are not the same render. The Giant is genuinely longer-bodied (creature bbox 329x81 px vs the generic's much stubbier trunk; packet aspect 5.5 vs 3.5), its head is proportionally larger (headFrac 0.24 vs 0.17), its tail is a thicker blunt cylinder, and it carries an extra large dark elliptical mass sitting behind and under the tail base that the generic does not have - a soft unshaped smudge that may be intended as a compressed caudal fin but reads as a shading blob, not as anatomy. So the difference is more than colour: length, head fraction and tail mass all differ. What is genuinely shared is every identity-bearing primitive - egg skull, white-ring eye, smiling mouth arc, four short dark stub limbs, dorsal band, gold spot scatter, ground-shadow ellipse. The verdict stands on that: parameters were varied, the chassis was not, and all three must-reads are missing.

One small credit the FAIL did not give: posture and aspect are correct-ish - the animal is low, long and sprawling with four short splayed limbs, and the rim light on the topline is clean. The failure is entirely in the three identity features, not in the pose or the paint quality.

rows.readsAs: a generic orange-red fish; indistinguishable from this batch's Salmon and Trout except for hue

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two of the three stated causes corrected. WHAT I SAW at 4x-12x zoom (440x440 source; body bbox x=104..335, y=151..239).

MUST-READ 1 -- 'pale spots on a dark ground (not dark on pale)': INVERTED, exactly as claimed, and this alone is disqualifying. The flank ground is a light salmon-orange (sampled 140..212 R on the lower flank, e.g. 188,89,67 / 207,98,73 / 212,124,108 at x=230). Sitting on it are eight or nine large soft DARK grey-brown blotches (sampled ~79,46,34 and darker in the blotch cores), concentrated on the lower flank and belly with a couple more behind the gill. That is dark-on-pale, the precise polarity the row warns against. Worth recording for the fix: a pale-dot rendering path already EXISTS on this asset -- the hexagonal scale mesh carries a small bright specular highlight in every cell (a fine lattice of light-orange dots). It does not read as spots because the dots are lattice-aligned, uniform, and one-third the size they would need to be, and because the big dark blotch layer sits on top and wins. The fix is three moves, not one: (a) drop the ground to a dark olive/slate-brown, (b) DELETE the dark blotch layer entirely, (c) add a discrete, irregularly-scattered pale cream/pink/rose spot layer at roughly eye-diameter, positioned along the mid and lower flank.

MUST-READ 2 -- 'white leading edges on lower fins': ABSENT, claim correct, but the described defect understates it. The problem is not that existing lower fins lack white margins -- it is that there is essentially no lower fin structure to mark. Scanning below the ventral outline, the ONLY sub-belly geometry is a single smooth crescent lobe spanning x=195..228, dipping ~7px below the belly line at its deepest (bottom y=233 at x=210 vs body ventral y=226). At 12x it is a featureless dull-red flat shape (73,36,30) with no rays, no ray-tips, no anterior margin treatment. There is no separate pelvic fin and no separate anal fin -- one merged lobe stands in for both. So the white leading edge cannot simply be painted on; the pelvic and anal fins have to be drawn first. IMPORTANT TRAP FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS: there IS a bright pale-grey/white line along the belly, and it is easy to mistake for the Char mark. It is not. It is the body silhouette stroke -- it runs the full length of BOTH the dorsal and ventral edges, it passes over the TOP (base) of the ventral lobe rather than along its front margin, and Trout and Salmon in this same batch carry the identical stroke while having no such must-read. Do not count it.

MUST-READ 3 -- 'slender streamlined body': THE JUDGE IS WRONG HERE, and I am correcting it. They wrote 'the body is the family's deep lens, not slender.' Measured: snout tip x=335, caudal peduncle pinch x=140 -> body length 195px; maximum body depth (pale outline to pale outline, fins excluded) 52px at x=230. That is aspect 3.75 against the packet's requested 3.8 -- essentially on spec, and if anything the mid-body taper reads slightly slimmer than the number. The body is NOT deep. What is genuinely wrong with the silhouette is a different thing: it is a symmetric double-pointed almond with a needle-sharp snout and no head modelling at all (no blunt rounded Salvelinus snout, no jaw line, no operculum -- just a thin curved gill arc), and it is bit-for-bit the same outline as Trout, Salmon, Grayling and Whitefish. Filing that under 'not slender' sends the fix in the wrong direction; the note should read 'generic shared lens, no snout/head modelling'.

FAMILY / CHASSIS: the judge's 'same blotch field as this batch's Salmon and Trout, just redder' is correct and in fact stronger than stated. Side-by-side at identical crop, Char and Salmon share the same outline, the same dorsal fin, the same rayed pectoral fan at the same anchor, the same forked tail, the same eye and gill-arc placement, the same hex scale mesh, AND nearly the same hue (both salmon-orange-red; Char is marginally more saturated). They differ only in where the dark blotches happen to land. At thumbnail size Char is not distinguishable from Salmon. Trout is the identical chassis again in olive-gold.

VERDICT: the single defining field mark that separates a char from every other fish in this family is inverted, and the second must-read has no substrate to exist on. The asset reads as 'a second Salmon'. FAIL stands.

FAIL stands, but two of the first judge's stated causes are factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (440x440 native; measured by per-column top-of-ink vs top-of-pale-body scan, and read at 3x/6x/8x with contrast boost):

1. THE DORSAL FIN IS NOT MISSING, AND IT IS NOT THE FAMILY'S SHARED LOBE. A dorsal IS drawn, it IS attached, and it IS the largest in the batch. It spans x199-x311 of a x103-x337 bbox (~112px, 48% of total length) and rises to a maximum of 23px above the pale topline at x=247. Its lower boundary coincides with the body topline for the whole span -- it is rooted on the back, not floating behind it. The claim 'measurably the same shape as the Whitefish's, only a few pixels taller' is FALSE: the same scan gives Whitefish 13px peak over 59 columns and Trout 14px over 72; Grayling is 77% taller and 85% longer than the Whitefish's. The claim 'no attachment to the topline, so it reads as a shadow behind the back' is also FALSE -- at 8x with gain the fin is a solid mid-blue translucent membrane carrying ~10 evenly spaced vertical RAY LINES, seated flush on the topline.

2. THE DORSAL STILL FAILS, FOR THE RIGHT REASONS. Body depth under the fin's peak is 56px (topPale 180 -> belly 236), so the fin is only ~41% of body depth. A grayling's flag is roughly as tall as the body is deep and, critically, is RECTANGULAR: near-constant height along its length, its tallest point at the POSTERIOR end, and a squared-off (often trailing-lobed) rear edge. What is drawn is a symmetric low DOME -- rising and falling in a single smooth arc, tallest at mid-span, tapering to nothing at both ends. It reads as an enlarged generic fish dorsal, not a banner. And it carries NO SPOTS -- the mustRead's 'spotted' clause is fully unmet; the fin has ray lines only. Fix = re-shape to a tall square banner (>=90% of body depth, roughly constant height, squared trailing edge, rear lobe tallest) and add 3-4 horizontal rows of dark ocelli/spots between the rays.

3. NO MOUTH -- CONFIRMED. At 8x the snout is a bare pale wedge terminating in a point. There is no mouth line, no gape, no jaw seam, no lip. The only line on the head is a curved operculum/gill arc well behind the eye (that is a gill cover, not a mouth). 'Small mouth' cannot read because nothing reads.

4. NO ADIPOSE FIN -- CONFIRMED. At 6x the topline from the dorsal's posterior taper (x~199) to the caudal root (x~139) is a single unbroken smooth curve. No bump, no nub, no separate element.

5. WHAT DOES PASS: the forked tail is present and correct -- deeply forked, ray-lined, clearly bilobed. The eye is 'prominent' as spec'd (large white sclera ring, dark pupil), though it is pasted on top of the head silhouette and breaks the dorsal contour of the skull.

6. BODY SHAPE ALSO MISSES. mustRead asks for a 'trout-shaped body'; spec aspect is 3.8. Measured bbox is 235x87 = 2.70, the DEEPEST of the five (Trout 3.17, Whitefish 2.88). This reads as a deep-bodied bream/sunfish blank, not a slender salmonid.

7. CHASSIS FINDING (supports the FAIL). Rendered side by side at 3x, Grayling and Whitefish are one chassis: identical body outline, identical allover pale scale-grid texture, identical mouthless pointed snout, identical pasted-on ringed eye, identical single triangular pectoral, identical soft ventral shadow lobe, identical forked tail. Hue (blue-grey vs olive) and dorsal size are the only differences. The larger dorsal is the ONE thing distinguishing this asset from the family blank, and it is the wrong shape and unspotted -- so with no mouth, no adipose, and the wrong body depth, nothing on this asset says grayling.

Verified at 6-14x magnification on the head, feet, tail and both wing tips. FAIL stands, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and one is confirmed exactly.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Body: one large smooth egg/oval (approx x95-250, y165-280 on the 440 canvas) covered in a dappled overlapping-scale pattern that reads as golf-ball dimpling or fish scales rather than feather tracts. Head: a featureless light-grey SPHERE stuck on the front-upper-left of that egg with NO neck, no crown/nape shading, no facial break at all, carrying one large round black bead eye with a single square specular dot. Feet: TWO yellow legs each ending in three splayed unwebbed stick-toes, planted on a large dark elliptical CAST GROUND SHADOW that spans nearly the whole body width. Tail: present and the judge did not mention it - a short flat dark-grey triangular wedge projecting back-right from the rear of the body to a point at about x=290, correctly short against the bulky body, so mustRead #3 passes.

CORRECTION 1 - THE WINGS ARE THE ONE THING DONE RIGHT, NOT A DEFECT. Calling them 'two flat grey planks' is wrong as a criticism. Total span is roughly x=10 to x=425 (about 415px) against a 155px body, i.e. 2.7x body length, matching the 2.6 aspect. Both wings are narrow, stiff, plank-straight and taper to sharp points - which is precisely what the reference note demands ('narrow and plank-straight, not broad and fingered like a raptor's'). The near (right) wing is NOT flat and undetailed: it carries five drawn primary-separation lines at the outer third and a pale elliptical underwing panel at the root. mustRead #1, 'immensely long narrow stiff-held wings', is PRESENT and readable. The real wing defect is geometric, not shape: both wings exit the body at the SAME mid-flank height and read as a single rod skewered fore-and-aft through the belly, with no shoulder/scapular join, no carpal bend, and the far (left) wing is a plain untextured dark silhouette with no feather structure at all.

CORRECTION 2 - THE BILL, described slightly wrong but the substance holds. It is not a triangle; at 14x it is a downward-angled parallelogram wedge with a dark brown outline and a faint darker line hinting at a lower mandible, blunt/rounded at the tip, only about 0.6x the head diameter long. There is NO hook, NO terminal nail, NO gape line, and critically NO tube nostril anywhere on the side or top of it. mustRead #2, 'heavy hooked bill with tube nostrils on the sides' - the single feature that IS the albatross and the only thing separating it from the nine other birds in this family batch - is entirely ABSENT.

CONFIRMED - POSTURE. The claim that it stands rather than flies is exactly right. Reference posture is 'flying'; the asset has two weight-bearing legs with toes splayed on a cast ground ellipse. Feet are not tucked, there is no body pitch, no motion, and the ground shadow nails the bird to a surface. So it is a standing bird with two glider wings taped through its waist.

VERDICT. 2 of 4 identity criteria fail, including the defining tubenose bill and the required posture. The organism as drawn reads as a plump generic perching bird - the judge's 'fat pigeon' is fair, allowing that the surface texture is scale-like rather than pigeon plumage. FAIL upheld.

FIX LIST: (1) build a real heavy tubenose bill - long, deep at the base, distinct upper/lower mandible plates with a visible gape line, a strongly hooked terminal nail, and a raised tube nostril cylinder on the side of the upper mandible; pink-horn rather than saturated yellow. (2) Put it in the air: tuck/remove the legs, delete the ground shadow ellipse, pitch the body. (3) Keep the long narrow planks but re-root them - a shoulder mass and a carpal bend so they leave the back, not the belly, and give the far wing the same primary separations as the near one. (4) Give the head a neck join into the shoulders and drop the golf-ball dimple texture for directional feathering.

BILL (must-read 1: 'heavy hooked-tipped bill') - ABSENT, and the judge described it correctly. At 14x the bill is a symmetric isoceles triangle in flat ochre-yellow (approx #E0A62B) with a straight upper edge, a straight lower edge, a single dark gape line down the middle, and a sharp apex. Minor correction to the judge's wording: at low zoom the apex can look like it droops, and the shape is a pointed triangle rather than a duck's spatulate bill, so 'duckling' misnames the bill even though the overall chick read is right.

WINGTIPS / MANTLE (must-read 2: 'clean white body with a grey mantle and black wingtips') - the judge is exactly right and I can put numbers on it. The arc swoosh over the back samples RGB(101,102,104) at (228,190) and (236,190). The single grey point projecting past the rear samples RGB(101,102,104) at (268,235) through (298,235) - byte-identical to the swoosh. There is one grey in this asset and it is mid-grey, not black; true black wingtips would be near #1A1A1A. The only darker pixels are the 3-4px anti-aliased tip at x=304 (34,37,41) fading into the near-black background (8,13,19), which is edge falloff, not a black primary panel. Also, the grey is not a mantle: the crown, nape and upper back are all white; the grey is a crescent painted across the middle of the flank plus a second pale-grey teardrop 'folded wing' inside it, so the back-versus-underside two-tone that defines a gull is missing entirely. Body white itself is clean (250-255) - that part is fine.

WINGS BEYOND TAIL (must-read 3) - only nominally. A single undifferentiated grey dart does extend past the body to x=321, but wing and tail are the same shape and same colour, so there is no readable 'long wings crossing beyond the tail'. There is a set of very faint thin dark hatch strokes below and behind the dart (visible only when brightened) that appear to be intended as tail feathers; against the dark background they are effectively invisible and cannot be counted as a feature.

SILHOUETTE - the real killer, and something the judge did not mention. Ink bbox is 204x147 including the tail dart; the body alone is roughly 150 wide x 147 tall, i.e. aspect 1.0, a near-perfect circle, with a small round head sitting on top and no neck. The packet asks for aspect 2. Legs are thin ochre sticks with one forward and one rear toe each, unwebbed. The composite read is a round white chick/ball-bird, not a herring gull.

Fixes: give the bill real depth plus a downcurved nail and a gonys angle (and a red spot); repaint the grey as a true dorsal mantle over crown-to-back, not a mid-flank crescent; add a genuinely black (near #1A1A1A) primary block with white mirrors at the projecting tip so it separates from the grey mantle; and stretch the chassis from a 1.0 ball to the 2.0 horizontal body the packet specifies.

So the wing exists - it is folded at rest on a standing bird instead of extended and angled. The fix is repose-to-flight (open the wings, lift the bird off the shadow, drop the feet), NOT 'add wings'. What is actually wrong is (a) the arc is a gentle bow with NO terminal reversal - a chamois horn goes near-vertical and then snaps into a tight fishhook in the last fifth of its length, and neither horn here changes direction at all; and (b) the pair SPLAY OUTWARD IN A V/LYRE rather than rising parallel, so the near horn is an almost dead-vertical prong leaning slightly one way while the far horn leans the other. The silhouette therefore reads as generic caprid brow-prongs, not the chamois hook. Fix is a sharp direction reversal in the top ~20% of each horn plus parallel, not splayed, bases.

What is missing is antelope PROPORTION and ANGULATION: the limbs are short relative to the deep barrel, the hock/knee break is barely articulated, and the stance is the same square four-post stance as the Goat, so nothing about them says 'antelope'.

There is also no dark dorsal stripe and no dark leg/belly countershading, so the body has no tonal structure for a facial mask to sit against, and no tail is visible at the rump at all.

NET: with the mask absent outright, the horn hook absent, the coat texture borrowed from the sheep chassis and the silhouette provably identical to its Goat sibling, the asset reads as a tan-recoloured sheep wearing prong horns. It does not read as a chamois. FAIL upheld.

So the fix is 'reorganise the existing markings into dark chevron bars and warm the base coat toward rufous', not 'add texture to a flat field'.

Chassis claim: substantially right. Net: one must-read present but under-scaled, two must-reads flatly absent, and the asset is a hue-and-texture recolour of the Godwit stamp. It reads as a generic small brown wader, not a snipe. FAIL stands. Fix order: (1) drive the eye high and rearward on the skull, (2) paint 2-4 bold cream longitudinal braces down the mantle plus a striped crown, (3) roughly double the bill length and thin it. Do NOT 'add a missing bill'.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 PNG; zoomed the head at 8x/18x, the feet at 8x/10x, the mantle at 7x, and measured non-background bboxes for the whole family).

1) CREST — PRESENT, and at the BACK of the crown, not the front. The judge's 'spiky topknot added at the FRONT of the crown' is factually wrong. The head ball spans source x=150-183 (bill points LEFT, so larger x = rear); centre x~166. The crest stalk attaches at x~167-170 — dead centre to slightly rear of the crown — rises up-and-slightly-forward to a point at (162,148), and then throws THREE shorter tines that fan DOWN-AND-REARWARD, the lowest reaching x~186. The whole plume mass is centred rear of the head centre. So the must-read 'slight peaked crest at the back of the crown' is correctly POSITIONED. Its defect is scale and character, not location: it is a fully raised 4-tine splayed fan (cockatiel / crested-lark / hoopoe register), where the reference asked for a SLIGHT peak — a small pointed rise in the rear crown feathering continuous with the skull, not a separate stalked ornament standing ~10px clear of the head. FIX = shrink it to a low triangular peak merged into the crown silhouette; do NOT move it forward, and do NOT delete it.

2) THE QUAIL READ IS REAL, BUT IT COMES FROM THE BODY, NOT THE CREST. The silhouette is a fat rounded egg with the head ball perched high on the front-top shoulder and the belly bulging below the leg line — an upright, rotund gamebird carriage. The reference note explicitly demands the opposite: 'a horizontal, long-bodied songbird, not an upright perching finch.' Measured bbox is 159w x 130h = aspect 1.22 against a spec aspect of 1.6, and almost all of that width is the tail wedge, not the body: the body core alone is about as tall as it is long. There is no low-slung horizontal topline, no elongated rear body carried out over the legs.

3) 'IT IS THE SPARROW BLOB' — SUBSTANTIVELY RIGHT AT THE CHASSIS LEVEL, BUT NOT A COPY. Side-by-side with Sparrow.png the shared parts are unmistakable and should be named: identical head-ball placement on the front-top of the mass, identical big wing-oval decal with the same heavy dark outline sweeping from shoulder to rump, identical short pointed tail wedge, identical two yellow stick legs. But the measurements refute a literal 'same blob': Lark bbox 159x130 (1.22) vs Sparrow 120x132 (0.91) — the Lark tail wedge is genuinely longer and projects further rearward — and the Lark bill is a slim straight pointed cone, clearly slimmer than Sparrow's fat triangular seed-cracker. Two real differentiations exist; the chassis underneath them does not.

4) HIND CLAW — GENUINELY ABSENT. CONFIRMED. At 10x both feet show a tarsus dropping from the belly and then only FORWARD-raked toe strokes (down-and-left). Nothing whatsoever projects rearward from either ankle: the pixel field behind both ankles is bare background/shadow. The single most lark-specific must-read on the row — the long straight hind claw (elongated hallux) — is not drawn at all. One correction to the judge's wording: at this render each foot resolves to roughly TWO forward strokes plus the tarsus, not a clean 'three-forward-toe' set; the substance (all toes forward, no hallux) is right, the count is not.

5) PLUMAGE — 'streaky brown ground-bird' is NOT delivered. The bird is pale blond/cream sand, lighter than Sparrow, carrying a fine random mottled dapple of short flecks plus two heavy dark contour bands (the wing-oval outline and a back shade). There are no dark longitudinal STREAKS on the breast or mantle, and the ground tone is sandy cream rather than earth brown. The judge's 'sandy tan' description of the colour is accurate.

VERDICT: one of three must-reads (long straight hind claw) is entirely absent; a second (streaky brown plumage) is not delivered — mottled cream, no streaks; the third (rear crest) is present and correctly placed but drawn at ornamental scale; and the row's governing note (horizontal long-bodied ground bird) is contradicted by an upright rotund gamebird body on the shared songbird chassis. FAIL upheld.

Verdict upheld, but the headline cause in the original claim is FLATLY WRONG and must not be used to drive the fix. I cropped and rescaled the tail region (src x225-340, y185-270 at 7x) and then thresholded the whole bird to a pure silhouette (src x90-340, y145-275 at 3x). The tail is NOT 'a plain undivided pointed spike'. It is a genuine, deeply forked tail with two long thin outer streamers: the notch apex sits at src x~270, essentially flush with the rear edge of the body mass (x~268), and both streamer tips reach x~323 — so the fork depth is ~55px, i.e. effectively 100% of the tail's length. The streamers are ~4px thick at midpoint, pointed, and diverge in a clean wide V (upper one rising, lower one dropping). In the threshold silhouette this fork is by far the most legible feature on the whole asset. Must-read #1 ('deeply forked tail with long outer streamers') is PRESENT and reads correctly. Do not touch the tail.

What actually fails:

(1) WINGS — must-read #2 ('long narrow pointed swept-back wings') is absent, and the original description understates it. It is not merely 'the family's folded comma stroke': in the threshold silhouette there is NO wing in the outline at all. The body edge is one unbroken plump egg from breast to rump. The 'wing' exists only as a painted panel on top of the back — a broad, blunt, scallop-textured lobe with a dark covert bar, whose rear end is a rounded lump, not a swept point. There is nothing scimitar-shaped anywhere, and no wing is deployed away from the body.

(2) BILL — must-read #3 ('tiny flat bill with a wide gape') is absent and actively inverted. At 9x the bill is a big saturated yellow triangular spear ~26px long against a head diameter of ~32px, i.e. ~80% of head width, projecting well clear of the face with a hard point. That is a thrush/starling dagger, the opposite of a swallow's minuscule stub. There is no gape line, no wide flat base. ('Pointed wedge' in the claim is fair as far as it goes but undersells the scale — the problem is that it is LONG and high-chroma yellow, so it dominates the head.)

(3) POSE / BODY — posture spec is 'flying' and the render is grounded. Confirmed at 9x: two pale-yellow feet with three splayed forward toes plus a hind toe, planted flat, attached almost directly to the belly with no visible leg, sitting on a dark elliptical cast ground shadow. The claim's 'lying prone' is slightly overstated — it reads as a bird squatting/crouched on the ground, not lying on its side. The bigger unstated defect is BULK: the silhouette body is a barrel-shaped oval (~165x70px) with a short neck and a round head, closer to a duck or grebe than to a swallow's slim streamlined dart. Strip the tail off and nobody would name this bird a swallow.

Aspect (~2.1 measured across x103-323 by y155-265) does meet the 2.2 spec, but only because the streamers supply the length; the body itself is stubby.

Net: 1 of 3 must-reads present. The identity feature survives; everything carrying it does not. Fix list, in order: slim the body to a streamlined dart and lift it off the ground (drop the planted feet, splayed toes and ground shadow, or tuck the feet to a nub); replace the folded back-panel with two long narrow swept-back scimitar wings that BREAK the silhouette; shrink the bill to a tiny dark stub with a wide gape. Keep the forked streamer tail and the dark-blue-back/rufous-belly colouring exactly as they are — both are already correct barn-swallow reads.

The bill is a pointed yellow wedge, not a tiny bill with an enormous gape. What I saw (440x440, bird occupies x~85-345, y~155-265; inspected at 3x whole-body, 8x head, 8x feet, 7x tail, plus a 4.5x brightness-boosted silhouette pass to pull the far side out of the dark background).

CHASSIS — the judge's headline is CORRECT and literally verifiable. I rendered Swallow.png through the identical crop and the two images are the same chassis pixel-for-pixel in shape: same plump horizontal duck/tern body, same ball head, same bill, same two stacked folded wing leaves, same forked streamer tail, same yellow feet, same elliptical contact shadow. Only the palette differs — Swallow is steel-blue with an orange belly crescent; Swift is warm pale grey-taupe with cream speckle flecks, a white rim-light along the back and a glossy top highlight. This is a recolour of the Swallow asset, which is precisely the failure mode the packet note names ("Often drawn as a swallow").

WINGS — must-read "scythe-shaped crescent wings swept far back" is ABSENT. Correction to the judge: it is not "just the folded comma stroke" (singular). There are TWO overlapping folded wing leaves lying flat along the back — an upper long speckled leaf from the nape to x~285 and a second, paler leaf beneath it running to the rump. Both are closed-wing perched geometry, hugging the body outline; nothing projects away from the torso, and there is no crescent/sickle curvature anywhere in the silhouette. The boosted pass confirms no faint far-side wing hiding in the dark.

BILL — must-read "tiny bill with an enormous gape" is ABSENT. Judge is right that it is a pointed yellow wedge. Adding detail: it is a solid saturated-yellow triangular spike attached at mid-head height, roughly 0.6x the head diameter long and tapering to a sharp tip, with a thin darker culmen line and NO gape line, no gape corner behind it, no mouth opening. It reads as a tern/shorebird bill. Note it is also not "tiny" — it is conspicuously long, the opposite error from a swift's near-invisible stub.

LEGS — must-read "cigar body with almost no visible legs" is ABSENT/contradicted. Two bright saturated-yellow legs hang clear of the belly line at x~150-215, each with 3-4 long splayed toes, at the highest contrast anywhere in the image apart from the bill. Small correction: they are not "planted on" the ground shadow — they hang free, overlapping the dark elliptical contact shadow without touching down, so the bird reads as floating just above a surface rather than standing. That does not soften the defect; the legs are the single most eye-catching feature of the render. The body is also not a cigar — it is a deep-bellied oval about 2.0 tall-to-long, against the packet's aspect 3.

TAIL — the judge's description is WRONG here, and the truth is worse for the asset. It is NOT a "long undivided pointed tail." At 7x it is clearly DIVIDED: two long tapering streamers spring from a common base at x~275 and diverge into a shallow V with a distinct wedge notch between them, the upper one reaching x~345. That is a deeply forked tail with long outer streamers — the Swallow's must-read, and exactly what the Swift note forbids ("a much shorter notched tail, and no long streamers"). Beneath the tail base sits a fan of ~8 thin dark hairline strokes that read as stray hatching rather than feathers.

POSTURE — packet says flying; the render is a grounded/settled pose complete with a cast contact shadow.

Net: all three Swift must-reads are absent and the asset is a palette swap of the neighbouring Swallow. No reading of the pixels rescues this. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: this species needs its own chassis, not a tint. Open the wings into two long stiff sickle crescents swept far behind the body (anhedral bow, no folded-leaf overlay); shrink the bill to a near-invisible dark stub with a wide gape line running back under the eye; delete the legs and feet entirely (or leave a barely-visible dark tuck at the belly); replace the streamer tail with a short tail about one-quarter its current length carrying a shallow central notch; slim the torso to a true cigar at aspect ~3; and remove the ground shadow in favour of an airborne pose.
