rows.readsAs: a green fish wearing a bubble helmet with a green box inside it
rows.defect: The transparent dome does read (a clean circle over the front of the head), but what is inside it is a single flat mint-green RECTANGLE — one solid slab, not two upward-pointing tubular eyes; there is no barrel form, no pair, no upward gaze. Worse, the two dark spots that should be the nostrils on the FRONT of the face are sitting on top of that green slab inside the dome, so they read as a pair of pupils on a face — the render produces exactly the misreading the packet's note warns against. The rest is the family lens body with the shared scale mesh, cyan belly-dot chain and triangular tail wedge.
rows.fix: Replace the slab with two distinct vertical green cylinders side by side inside the dome, each capped with a bright lens facing straight UP, and move the two dark nostril pits down onto the snout at the front of the head, outside the dome and clearly below the barrels.

rows.readsAs: a pink puffer-ish fish with a big nose — close to blobfish but not obviously gelatinous
rows.defect: The pink colour, the slumped oval mass and the bulbous drooping snout lobe all read, and this is the closest the chassis gets to its target. But the whole body is covered in the family crosshatch SCALE mesh, which directly contradicts the must-read 'no scales' and makes it look armoured rather than gelatinous; the mouth is a faint straight hairline under the nose with no downturn at all, so the defining frown is absent; and the tail is the same stiff triangular wedge every other asset in the batch wears rather than a flimsy translucent fin.
rows.fix: Strip the scale hatch entirely and render the surface as smooth, slightly translucent jelly with soft sag folds, then cut a clearly downturned frowning mouth line under the drooping nose.

rows.readsAs: a bright red needlefish or a chilli-pepper-coloured cutlassfish
rows.defect: The long glowing chin barbel — the single feature that names this animal — is entirely absent; nothing hangs from the jaw, the underside of the head is a clean empty curve. The body is also saturated CRIMSON RED rather than the specified eel-like black, so it reads as a tropical surface fish, not an abyssal one. The fangs are four tiny white spikes at the very tip of the lower jaw, far too short and not transparent. Only the cyan photophore row along the belly is doing its job, and it is the same dot chain reused on Barreleye, Lanternfish and Viperfish.
rows.fix: Add a long barbel hanging from the chin — a slender filament at least a third of the body length with a glowing bulb at its end — and repaint the body near-black with only a dull red sheen.

rows.readsAs: a brown piranha with white spikes stuck on its face
rows.defect: The stocky dark-brown mass and the alternating up/down white fangs do roughly carry the idea, but the head has no mouth: the fangs float on bare cheek with no jaw line, no lip and no gape behind them, and one spike overlaps the eye. The 'huge blunt head' does not exist as a form — it is simply the front half of the same oval used for Blobfish, undifferentiated from the trunk. The deep pitted grooves and ridges on the skull, a stated must-read, are nowhere on the render; the only texture is the shared crosshatch mesh, and it is applied to the REAR half of the body while the head is left flat.
rows.fix: Build an actual blunt boxy head with a hinged gaping jaw so the fangs sit in a mouth, and carve the characteristic pits and bony ridges into the skull as visible sculpted grooves rather than leaving it a smooth oval.

rows.readsAs: a small silvery fish with glowing dots on its belly
rows.defect: The cyan photophore chain along the lower flank reads well and the silver-blue body is right in tone, but the eye — specified prominent and the animal's signature along with the lights — is rendered as the same tiny white ring used on the 'small eyes' assets in this batch, so the oversized-eye must-read is invisible. There is no adipose fin before the tail, and the tail is the shared flat triangular wedge with no fork cut into it. Body is also shorter and deeper than the 3.5 aspect asks for.
rows.fix: Enlarge the eye to occupy most of the short blunt snout, then cut a real V-fork into the caudal fin and add the small adipose nub ahead of it.

rows.readsAs: a piece of nigiri sushi, or a silver loaf wearing a red dome
rows.defect: Nothing about this is a ribbon. The body is a short fat silver sausage of roughly 4:1, not the 'many times longer than it is deep' ribbon the reference and the aspect 18 both demand. The crimson crest is rendered as one enormous SOLID pink dome slab that caps the entire length of the back and is taller than the fish is deep — it is a filled shape, not a crest of individual elongated dorsal rays, and it is not concentrated over the head where the oarfish crest actually rises. The long trailing oar-like pelvic streamers are missing entirely; there is one small grey fin mid-flank and a couple of stray wisps at the tail end. The overall silhouette reads as food, not an animal.
rows.fix: Redraw the body as a genuinely ribbon-thin silver band many times longer than deep, run the red dorsal fin as a fringe of separate fine rays the whole length, elongate only the first few rays into a crest plume over the head, and hang two long paddle-tipped pelvic streamers below.

rows.readsAs: a tripod fish — a fish standing on three long stilts on the seabed
rows.defect: The three stiff stilt rays are long, clearly weight-bearing and splay into small contact feet on the floor, and the two pectoral feelers sweep forward past the snout like antennae — the identity lands immediately and the silhouette is the only one in the batch that escapes the family oval. Minor: the eye is drawn as the same bright white ring-and-pupil used everywhere else rather than the tiny vestigial eye the reference calls for, and the three stilts are spaced evenly like insect legs instead of reading as a pelvic pair plus the lower caudal lobe.
rows.fix: Shrink the eye to a barely-there dark speck and re-space the stilts as two pelvic stilts under the chest plus one trailing from the lower tail lobe.

rows.readsAs: a grey blimp with teeth — indistinguishable from the Fangtooth in this same batch apart from colour
rows.defect: The first dorsal ray drawn out into a long lure whip over the head — a stated must-read and half of this animal's identity — is completely absent; there is no filament of any kind above the body. The body is a fat head-heavy teardrop of about 2.5:1 where the reference asks for a slim 6:1, so 'slim dark body' fails too. The fangs are the same floating white spike decal used on Fangtooth, stamped on a face that has no mouth line or jaw at all, so they do not read as fangs that close OUTSIDE the mouth past the eyes — they read as spikes glued to a cheek. The photophore row is four dots confined to the rear third of the belly instead of running the body.
rows.fix: Add the long dorsal lure whip arcing forward over the head with a light at its tip, and re-proportion the body to a slim elongated 6:1 with a hinged gaping jaw so the oversized fangs visibly close outside it past the eye.
rows.verifyWhy:
Read at 1x, at 5-6x nearest-neighbour crops of the head/dorsal/tail, and at a 4x contrast boost that reveals dark-on-dark geometry. Packet asks aspect 6, headFrac 0.2, prominent eyes, swimming, mustRead = (a) fangs so long they close outside the mouth, past the eyes, (b) first dorsal ray drawn out into a long lure whip over the head, (c) photophore rows on a slim dark body.

UPHELD, but the stated causes need three corrections.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Head faces RIGHT. Silhouette measured by luminance threshold: bbox 238 x 57 px (x 102-339, y 168-225), max depth 57 px at x=285. Body alone excluding the caudal fin is 205 x 57. Photophores ARE present and readable: five cyan discs in a single ventral row at x=155-205 on the rear tube, with a grey lateral bar above them. Caudal is a small dark forked fin at x=102-135. Eye is a white ring with a dark pupil at approx (318,186), prominent, correct.

CORRECTION 1 - the aspect number is wrong. It is 4.18:1 overall (238/57), 3.6:1 body-only, NOT 2.5:1. It is still well short of the 6 asked and it is genuinely head-heavy (deepest section sits only ~54 px behind the snout tip), so the verdict stands, but a fix brief written against 2.5:1 would overshoot. Target: stretch length to ~340 px at the same 57 px depth, and move the depth maximum rearward off the head.

CORRECTION 2 - there IS a mouth line. A thin dark dashed slit runs from x≈272 to x≈336 at y≈196, passing under the eye, and the fangs straddle it. The claim of 'a face with no mouth or jaw line' is factually wrong. What is true is that it is a hairline decal with no gape, no lower-jaw contour and no articulation, so the fangs still do not read as rooted in anything - they are six white bidirectional spindles (points UP and DOWN on each), which is the give-away that they are a stamped cluster rather than teeth. The two tallest (x≈300 and x≈327) do project below the ventral silhouette edge, so must-read (a) is PARTIALLY met - fangs do close outside the mouth - but they sit BELOW the eye rather than reaching PAST it, and they read as a sticker.

CORRECTION 3 - 'same organism as Fangtooth in a different colour' overstates it. I opened Fangtooth.png side by side: the fang cluster and ring eye ARE the identical shared decal, same relative placement, so that half of the claim is confirmed and is a real defect. But the silhouettes are not confusable - Fangtooth is a deep ~1.4:1 brown oval with a scaled flank patch and a big triangular caudal; Viperfish is an elongated blue-grey teardrop with a ventral photophore row. They share a FACE, not a body.

THE DEFECT THAT ACTUALLY CARRIES THE FAIL - must-read (b) is genuinely absent, as claimed. Under 4x boost the only dorsal element is a soft low grey hump at x≈195-270 carrying about five short bristle strokes ~8-9 px tall on its crest. No ray is elongated; nothing rises above the back line by more than ~9 px; there is nothing forward of the snout at all. The defining viperfish silhouette - a single dorsal ray drawn out into a long whip arcing forward over the head with a lure at its tip - does not exist in this image. Combined with the body being 4.2:1 instead of a slim 6:1, two of three must-reads fail and the third (fangs) is carried by a shared decal.

EXTRA DEFECT NOT IN THE ORIGINAL CLAIM. The body is two butt-joined primitives: a fat teardrop front and a thin rounded-rectangle rear tube, meeting at a visible seam/step at x≈250 where the ventral edge jumps. The photophore row and lateral bar live only on the tube. It reads as assembled parts, not one animal. Fix in the same pass as the elongation.

FIX ORDER: (1) grow the frontmost dorsal ray of the existing crest into a long forward-arcing whip clearing the snout, tipped with a photophore bulb - the crest is already there as an anchor; (2) merge the two body primitives into one continuous taper and stretch to ~6:1; (3) replace the shared spindle decal with fangs rooted in an articulated lower jaw so Viperfish and Fangtooth stop sharing a face.

rows.readsAs: A green leaf, or at best a generic needle-snouted minnow / young garfish — nobody names a killifish
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply absent and one of them IS the identity. (1) There is no flattened-topped head with an upturned mouth: the front of the fish is a bare symmetric spearpoint with zero head structure — no flat dorsal profile over the skull, no gill cover, no jaw line, no mouth aperture at all, and the topline over the 'head' slopes DOWN to the point instead of running flat. The small white eye ring is stuck onto the dorsal contour with roughly its upper half hanging over black background outside the silhouette. (2) The dorsal fin is not set far back near the tail: the faint dark hump above the topline spans about 38-70 percent of body length measured from the tail, centred near mid-body and biased toward the head — the exact opposite of the posteriorly-placed killifish dorsal — and it is rendered as an out-of-focus dark smudge painted behind the crisp body outline, with no rays, no defined edge and no visible attachment. (3) The caudal is the only must-read partly delivered: it is roughly rounded, but it is a dull dark near-rectangular slab, blurrier and much darker than the body, joined to the rear point by a single hairline pixel with no caudal peduncle, so it reads as a detached paddle rather than a tail fin.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front third: flatten the dorsal profile from the eye forward into a straight table-top, cut the snout short and blunt, and terminate it in a small upturned superior mouth whose lower jaw juts past the upper — then slide the dorsal fin back so its origin sits behind the anal-fin origin at roughly 70-80 percent of body length, give it a hard rayed edge in front of the body silhouette, and blend the caudal onto a short peduncle instead of a hairline join.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon lollipop tree with brown berries — nobody says oak
rows.defect: Every one of the four must-reads is missing. The crown is a narrow ball perched on a bare pole, taller than wide, instead of a broad spreading crown as wide as it is tall — and there is not one visible branch, so no spreading limb frame exists. The leaves are small spiky sawtooth fronds with pointed serrations, the opposite of the deeply lobed rounded oak outline. The acorns are four featureless brown spheres floating on the crown face with no nut taper and no scaly cup at all — they read as berries or cherries. The trunk is a flat, smooth, evenly-shaded brown stick with no fissures, no plates, no texture whatsoever.
rows.fix: Rebuild the oak on its own chassis: a short thick fissured trunk that forks low into 3-4 heavy sinuous limbs carrying a crown visibly wider than it is tall, with round-lobed leaf blades and acorns drawn as an oval nut sitting in a visibly cross-hatched scaly cup hanging at twig ends.

rows.readsAs: a palm, yucca or dracaena — a spiky tropical rosette tree, not a willow
rows.defect: The identity must-read is not merely weak, it points the wrong way: every leaf blade radiates UPWARD and OUTWARD from the crown in a stiff starburst, so there is not a single drooping, pendulous or whip-like twig anywhere in the image. The blades are long and lance-shaped, which is right, but they are all one flat mid-green with no silvery pale undersides, so the crown does not flicker two-tone. The trunk is the identical smooth brown pole from the Oak card — not grey, not fissured, not leaning. The catkins are pale beaded vertical strings glued to the crown face rather than soft grey buds on hanging twigs.
rows.fix: Invert the twig direction — hang long weeping strands from an arching high crown down past the trunk toward the ground, and put two-tone green/silver on the blades so the drooping curtain reads at thumbnail size.

rows.readsAs: a duckling or coot chick with a yellow beak — most strangers would say 'duck' or 'blackbird'
rows.defect: The casque — the single feature that IS a hornbill — is completely absent: the bill is a plain flat yellow wedge with nothing sitting on top of it, and it is barely downcurved (the upper edge is almost straight). The tail is a short pointed spike poking off the right flank, not a long broad fan. There is no bare coloured throat or eye skin and no lashes; the eye is a plain black bead with a grey ring. The body is a neckless squat egg with the belly nearly on the ground, so the whole thing reads as a waterfowl chick, and it is indistinguishable from the Toucan in the same batch apart from the bill's orange band.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: add a large hollow casque as a separate raised ridge riding the whole top of the upper mandible and rising above the crown, lengthen the bill to roughly half the body length with a real downward sweep, then lengthen the body and extend a long broad banded tail well past the rump so the silhouette stops being an egg.

rows.readsAs: a black bird with an oversized yellow bill — a stranger would probably guess toucan, but only from the bill colour, not the body
rows.defect: The bill is present and oversized (about 55-60% of body length) with one orange band, but it is drawn as a straight tapered dagger coming to a needle point — exactly the straight cone the reference warns against — instead of a deep, blunt-tipped, slightly downcurved banana. The vivid yellow-white bib is entirely missing: the breast and throat are the same flat near-black as the rest of the body, so the most recognisable colour block on the animal is gone. There is no blue bare skin ringing the eye; the eye ring is plain pale grey. And the body underneath is the identical squat neckless duckling egg used for the Hornbill, with the belly on the ground and a stub tail off the flank, rather than a slim long-tailed perching bird.
rows.fix: Give the bill real vertical depth with a blunt rounded tip and a downward curve, then paint a large cream-to-yellow bib covering the whole throat and upper breast with a hard black border under it.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon lollipop tree with five sunflowers stuck to it
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive. The crown is a bumpy cumulus blob that is round-to-slightly-wide, not a flat-topped umbrella — there is no flat table-top line and no horizontal layering, the fine sprigs radiate outward in a starburst including straight up. The bare trunk is a plain straight stick with no branch fork at the top to spread an umbrella from. The paired white thorns at the nodes are absent: the only white marks are short dashes painted on the TRUNK face, which read as bark scratches or claw marks, and there are no nodes to pair them at. The flowers are five large bright-yellow ray-petalled daisy heads with dark brown centres — those are sunflowers, not cream puffballs, and they are the loudest thing in the frame, so they drive the whole read. No seed pods anywhere.
rows.fix: Rebuild the crown as a flat-topped umbrella: fork the trunk into 2-3 upswept limbs near the top and hang two or three broad, thin HORIZONTAL foliage slabs off them with a hard flat top edge and sky visible under the lowest layer; then replace the yellow daisies with small pale-cream fuzzy pom-pom spheres and add paired white spines along the limbs.

rows.readsAs: a melon or gourd tree — a green bush on a stick with four striped fruits in it
rows.defect: The defining feature is simply not drawn. The trunk is the family's standard narrow brown stick, the same width as the Acacia's and the Tamarind's — there is no swollen barrel, no massive girth, no smooth grey bark, no taper. Nothing about the silhouette says baobab. The stubby root-like top branches are absent; the stick just disappears into the foliage. The crown is a dense, fully leafed green ball, which is the opposite of the recognisable state the reference calls for (sparse to bare). The pods are four round striped gourds sitting flat INSIDE the crown on tiny 6px stems, resting on the leaves like apples in a bush — they do not dangle, there is no long cord, and their round shape reads as melon rather than an elongated velvety pod.
rows.fix: Replace the stick with an enormous smooth grey barrel trunk occupying most of the frame width, wider at the base, tapering to a flat shoulder, and sprout a few short bare crooked root-like branches from the top; drop the leaf ball almost entirely and hang two or three elongated grey-brown pods below the branches on long visible cords.

rows.readsAs: a generic round leafy shade tree; nobody names the species
rows.defect: The billowing feathery dome half-works — the blob is round and the pinnate comb sprigs give a genuinely fine texture — but it is built as a spoke rim, every sprig radiating outward from the centre like a dandelion clock, with a soft empty green haze in the middle instead of layered foliage masses, so it reads as a starburst rather than a billow. The hanging pods fail outright: I can find only three or four dark olive-brown lozenges (upper centre, mid left, lower centre-right) buried among the leaves at low contrast, and they read as shadows or dead leaves. They are not cinnamon-brown, not knobbly, not crooked, and critically not HANGING — nothing dangles below the canopy line and there is no cluster. The trunk is again the identical featureless family stick.
rows.fix: Move the pods to the canopy's lower edge so they hang clear of the foliage in a cluster of 4-6, and repaint them in high-contrast cinnamon brown with a crooked, lumpy, constricted outline; then break the spoke rim by clumping the sprigs into 3-4 overlapping rounded foliage masses.

rows.readsAs: a small green ant
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads are present. The body is not a soft pear-shaped bulbous sac — it is the family's three-bead ant string (sphere head, smooth ovoid thorax, ribbed ovoid abdomen) with a hard waist pinch between beads, which is the exact opposite of an aphid's single undivided teardrop. There are no cornicles: the two thin rearward spikes at the abdomen tip are the same tapered leg strokes used everywhere else in the batch, at the same weight and colour, so they read as a hind leg pair and not as paired tubes rising off the back of the abdomen. There is no stem and no beak at all — nothing is being fed on, and the head bead has a big glossy ant eye and antennae where the rostrum should be.
rows.fix: Redraw the body as ONE undivided fat teardrop (widest at the rear, narrowing smoothly to a small tucked head, no waist), plant a needle rostrum from under the head into a green stem segment drawn behind the animal, and add two short thick pale TUBES standing up off the rear dorsal surface — noticeably shorter, blunter and lighter than the legs so they cannot be misread as limbs.

rows.readsAs: a grey housefly or mosquito
rows.defect: The head is the family's sphere bead with a single enormous central glossy eye — that is a FLY head, and it is what a stranger names first. The must-read blunt WIDE head with the eyes pushed out to the corners is absent, so the widest point of the animal is the thorax rather than the skull. The wings also violate the packet's explicit note: instead of one broad plate tented roof-like along the back in an inverted V, they are a splayed multi-lobed FAN of thin translucent straws radiating backward and outward past the abdomen, more like a feather duster or a sheaf of grass than membranous forewings, and the venation is straight parallel lines with no cross-veins or leading-edge thickening. Nothing in the silhouette says cicada.
rows.fix: Replace the sphere head with a short blunt trapezoidal skull that is WIDER than the thorax and push one hemispherical eye onto each front corner, then collapse the wing fan into a single long triangular forewing plate lying flat along the back from the thorax to well past the abdomen tip, angled down at the trailing edge so the tent shape reads in profile.

rows.readsAs: a gold beetle or cricket with a mantis arm
rows.defect: The raptorial foreleg lands — the folded triangular hooked grasping arm at the front is the one genuinely species-specific piece of drawing in this whole batch and it is legible. But the body fails its must-read: instead of a FLAT oval leaf-shaped brown plate it is a tall bulbous dome with a pronounced crest, taller than it is deep, with separate curved plates over the back that read as beetle elytra. In profile it has real volume where a water bug should read as a squashed leaf. The head is also barely there — headFrac 0.12 has collapsed the head into a tiny black dot at the junction where the arm meets the dome, with no distinct capsule, and the short piercing beak tucked under the head is completely absent.
rows.fix: Flatten the dorsal profile — drop the crest so the body becomes a low wide oval with a straight flat topline and a leaf-like pointed tail — and add a small distinct head capsule ahead of the shoulder with a short dark beak angled back under it.

rows.readsAs: a long-legged spider or harvestman on a black field
rows.defect: The long splayed legs are present and dominant — they sweep nearly the full frame width — so the primary cue survives, but everything around them is wrong or missing. The water surface is entirely absent: there is no water plane and no dimples denting it under the feet, so the animal is floating in a void above a detached oval shadow with no contact points at all, which strips the single behaviour that makes a strider a strider. The body is not a narrow slim boat — it is the same three-bead ant string as the aphid and cicada, with a bulbous rounded thorax bead and the same ribbed abdomen bead. The leg tips run out to roughly x=20 and x=425 in a 440px frame, effectively grazing both edges. The whole asset is also rendered near-black on a near-black background and is the least legible image in the batch.
rows.fix: Draw a horizontal water plane through the leg tips with four soft elliptical dimples pressed into it directly under the feet, then lift the body value several steps so the animal separates from the background, and slim the thorax and abdomen into one narrow tapered boat hull.

rows.readsAs: a turtle — a stranger names it correctly on sight
rows.defect: The exact failure the reference note warns about is present: the shell is a separate hat, not the body wall. A horizontal rim line cuts across mid-body and below it sits a plain rectangular trunk slab that the legs hang from, so the dome covers only the upper half of the trunk instead of the whole trunk. The dome is also rendered semi-transparent — the dark background gradient is clearly visible through its upper-left quadrant, which makes it read as a glass cloche set over the animal rather than as keratin plate. The concentric scute rings are drawn as thin uniform arcs with no plate edges, reinforcing the glassy look. Secondary issue: a yellow-green triangular wedge floats below and behind the head where the front limb should be, disconnected from the front leg column, so the forelimb reads as two unrelated pieces.
rows.fix: Make the shell the silhouette: drop the shell rim down to just above the leg tops so the domed carapace forms the entire trunk outline, delete the rectangular trunk slab, make the dome fully opaque, and have the neck and both legs emerge from under the rim.

rows.readsAs: a small brown cartoon tortoise
rows.defect: The high domed shell reads, but the trait the animal is NAMED for is completely absent: the plastron is a plain flat unmarked slab with no transverse hinge line and no closed-box state, and it sits so high that the underside is a wide open gap. The feet are not elephantine, scaly or clawed — each leg is a plain flat-bottomed rectangle with three scratched notches. The shell pattern is a concentric spiderweb fan, not a scute mosaic. Side by side it is the same drawing as the Tortoise asset in a slightly darker brown.
rows.fix: Draw the plastron as a deep vertical wall closing the belly with a clear horizontal hinge seam across its middle, and rebuild the legs as tapering scaly columns ending in a splayed round foot with visible claws.

rows.readsAs: a green tortoise — the Box Turtle image recoloured
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The shell is the same tall hemispherical dome as the Box Turtle and Tortoise, the exact thing the reference note forbids ("the shell is low and streamlined, not high-domed like a tortoise"). The feet show no webbing at all — they are the identical flat rectangular columns with toe notches. The head is not extended forward on a wrinkled neck; it sits on the same short smooth stub as every other asset. Nothing but hue distinguishes this file from Box_Turtle.png.
rows.fix: Flatten the carapace to roughly half its present height with a long low streamlined teardrop topline, break its surface into a mosaic of flat polygonal scutes, and widen the hind feet into webbed fans with the skin visible between splayed toes.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the full PNG, then at 6x-8x crops of the head, the feet and the front shoulder, and ran a hue-robust silhouette mask over all six turtles in the batch. The FAIL stands, but two of the judge's stated causes are inaccurate and one is understated.

MUST-READ 1 - 'low flattened domed shell with a scute mosaic': FAILS on 'low'. Measured from the mask, the carapace apex is at y=131 and the widest row at y=198, with a shell span of roughly x=102..282, giving a dome height/width of 0.372. The Tortoise in the same batch measures 0.309 and the Box Turtle 0.396. The Pond Turtle is therefore MORE domed relative to its shell width than the Tortoise it is explicitly told not to resemble. Overall silhouette aspect is 1.52 against a spec of 2.0 - the asset is far too tall and short for its own row. The shell markings are present but are the same concentric growth-ring arcs plus a few radial spokes used on Box Turtle and Tortoise; that reads as tortoise growth rings, not a freshwater slider's polygonal scute mosaic. Partial credit at best, and the defining word 'low' is simply not delivered.

MUST-READ 2 - 'webbed clawed feet': FAILS on webbing, and the judge is WRONG that the feet are bare rectangles. At 6x the two visible legs are dark rectangular columns that terminate in a slightly flared foot pad carrying three to four tiny pale claw ticks along the front edge. Claws ARE drawn (small but real). What is absent is any webbing: no interdigital membrane, no splayed toes, no paddle outline - the foot is the stumpy clubbed pad the packet assigns to the TORTOISE row ('stumpy and clubbed with no webbing, unlike a turtle's'). Fix target: the claws exist, add splayed toes joined by a membrane; do not re-add claws from scratch.

MUST-READ 3 - 'head extended forward on a wrinkled neck': FAILS, but not for the reason given. The judge says 'no forward extension'; in fact the head tip reaches x=345 while the shell front edge is near x=282, so the head does project about 60px clear of the carapace. What is missing is the NECK: the large ovoid skull is butted straight onto the shell front through a short, smooth, untextured shoulder mass with no cylindrical neck and no wrinkle/annulation banding at all. An 8x crop of the Pond Turtle head next to the same crop of Box_Turtle is shape-identical - same ovoid skull, same dark wedge beak with the same notch, same eye-ring at the same offset, same smooth join.

CHASSIS: confirmed shared, but the judge named the wrong sibling. Mask IoU against Pond Turtle is 0.86 for Tortoise and only 0.73 for Box Turtle (Box is drawn smaller, 207x147 vs 244x160). Pond Turtle is a recoloured TORTOISE, not a recoloured Box Turtle. Shared parts: domed carapace with concentric ring scutes, four straight rectangular column legs with clawed pad feet, the identical beaked ovoid head on a neckless shoulder, and an identical downward-pointing triangular flap at the front shoulder (present unchanged on Box and Tortoise, so it is a chassis element and must not be mistaken for a flipper or webbing).

Net: all three must-reads fail. The asset reads as a green tortoise.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise floating with two stumpy paddles stuck on
rows.defect: The shell is the same tall dome with the same concentric fan as the land assets — not the flattened streamlined teardrop the reference demands. The front flipper is a short rounded lobe no longer than a third of the shell and is the same size and shape as the rear one, so the wing-like forelimb that IS the sea turtle's identity is absent; there is no long tapering blade, no trailing edge, no swimming sweep. Only the blunt beaked head reads. The result is the family chassis with its leg columns replaced by two identical blobs.
rows.fix: Replace the dome with a low flattened teardrop carapace and redraw the forelimb as a long tapered wing-like flipper roughly as long as the shell, angled forward and clearly larger than the rear paddle.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but the stated cause is half wrong and the real defect is worse than described.

WHAT I MEASURED (440x440 render, head faces right).

SHELL — the judge is RIGHT and understated it. I profiled the carapace top edge of Sea_Turtle.png against Tortoise.png from the same batch. Sea: x=101..292 (w=191), apex at x=191 (apexFrac 0.471 of width), apexY=136, plastron baseline y=202 -> dome height 66. Tortoise: x=98..285 (w=187), apex at x=186 (apexFrac 0.471 — IDENTICAL), apexY=141, baseline y=202 -> dome height 61. Sampled top edge at 10% intervals the two curves are the same curve, Sea sitting a uniform 4-5px HIGHER at every station. So the sea turtle's shell is not merely 'the same tall dome' as the family tortoise — it is 8% TALLER-domed than the land tortoise standing next to it in the same packet. The arc is symmetric front-to-back (apex essentially dead centre, in fact 3% REARWARD of centre), so there is zero teardrop: no forward-set high point, no long taper to a pointed rear, no low streamlined profile. Overlaid on it is the same concentric-arc + radial-spoke scute fan used on Tortoise and Box Turtle, pixel-for-pixel the family motif. Must-read 1, 'flattened teardrop shell', is ABSENT. Since the carapace is 231px of a ~275px creature, this alone decides how the sprite reads.

FLIPPERS — the judge's DESCRIPTION IS WRONG, their conclusion survives. They are not 'short rounded lobes' and not 'blobs'. Row-scanning the limb band: the rear limb runs from (169,218) to (82,260) and the front limb from (240,218) to (327,260) — each is an elongated, cleanly tapered ovoid paddle about 96px along its axis, i.e. HALF the carapace length, with a blunt rounded tip and no claws, no toes, no ankle. They are genuine paddles, splayed down-and-out in a shallow V, and the chassis has correctly dropped the tortoise leg columns. Credit where due: whoever drew this did change the limb primitive. The actual defect is that the front paddle is a pixel-mirror of the rear one — identical axial length (96 vs 96), identical width taper, identical root width and root Y. There is therefore no fore/aft asymmetry at all, and nothing wing-like: no long slender blade, no distinct swept leading edge, no forelimb reaching forward past or below the head to a narrow tip, no rear limb reduced to the short broad rudder that makes the contrast legible. Must-read 2, 'long wing-like front flippers', is at best half-present — 'paddles yes, wings no'.

HEAD — the judge did not mention it and it is the one must-read that PASSES. At 8x the head is a full egg-shaped mass carried forward on a short thick neck, entirely outside the shell, with a dark wedge upper beak overhanging a visible lower jaw line, and a small white-ringed eye with black pupil set high and forward. 'Blunt beaked head that cannot retract' is satisfied as written. Caveat for the fixer: it is the identical head primitive used on Tortoise and Box Turtle, so it satisfies the letter of the must-read while contributing no sea-turtle specificity.

OTHER: no tail element anywhere — the rearmost pixel at x=82 is flipper, 19px behind the shell edge. The packet sets posture 'swimming', but the sprite sits on a ground-contact drop shadow with both paddles angled down toward it like splayed legs, which actively reinforces the land read.

NET: one of three must-reads present, one half-present, and the missing one is the silhouette. Standing beside Tortoise.png this is the same animal with paddles instead of columns. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION (in priority order): (1) rebuild the carapace as its own low teardrop — target dome height ~30-35px on a 191px width (ratio ~0.17, roughly half the current 0.35), apex pushed forward to ~0.35 of width from the rear, with a long straight-ish taper running back to a narrow, near-pointed rear margin, and drop the concentric-fan overlay for a forward-fanning row of large flat scutes; (2) make the front flipper roughly 1.7-2x the rear one's length, narrow it into a swept blade that reaches forward and down past the head's leading edge and finishes in a narrow tip, and shrink the rear limb to a short broad rudder; (3) if the packet's 'swimming' posture is meant to render, remove or soften the ground shadow and lift the flippers to a horizontal downstroke rather than pointing them at the floor.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by decoding the PNG and re-rendering brightened crops (subject occupies x85-369, y146-271 of the 440px canvas; animal faces RIGHT). The FAIL stands, and the central structural claim is CORRECT, but two sub-claims need correcting.

CONFIRMED - tail is on the wrong end. There is exactly one long tapering tail primitive in the render and it is welded to the FRONT of the animal. Its base is a parallelogram at src x~256, y~215 - the neck/throat junction directly below and slightly behind the rear of the skull, sitting on top of the front leg - and it rakes forward-and-down to a needle point at src x=369, which is the rightmost pixel of the entire subject, ~64px BEYOND the beak tip (~x305) and below the jawline. The judge said 'under the CHIN'; more precisely it is under the throat/neck at the shoulder, not the chin itself, but the consequence they describe is exactly right. The rear of the shell (verified by a 7x crop of x70-180) is a clean, smooth, unbroken dome edge with NO tail, no tail stub, and no serrated marginal scutes - only the two hind legs. So the required 'long saw-toothed crested tail' is doubly failed: wrong end AND the shape is a perfectly smooth flat wedge with zero saw-tooth crest or serration.

CORRECTION 1 - 'no massive hooked beak' is partly wrong. A beak IS drawn: a tan/olive wedge that starts at the eye, runs forward and terminates in a distinct DOWNWARD HOOK that overhangs past the face outline (clearly visible at 8x). The defect is scale and character, not absence - it is a small bird-of-prey beak pasted flat on the cheek, not the massive shearing snapper jaw, and it has no gape line, no wide mouth corner, no upturned lower jaw.

CORRECTION 2 - the head is undersized rather than merely 'a small rounded blob'. Measured, the skull is a smooth featureless ovoid ~52px wide (246-298) and with the beak reaches x305, so head+beak is ~59/285 = headFrac 0.21 against the packet's required 0.28. There is no cranial bulk, no cheek mass, no jaw muscle - it is the generic tortoise head primitive.

It is not literally featureless: it carries several pale arc scute lines across the dome, but those read as specular highlight arcs on a polished surface, not as the rough keeled ridges and serrated rear margin of a snapper.

Net: two of three must-reads are absent (rough undersized ridged shell; saw-toothed crested tail at the rear) and the third is present only in miniature. Verified by cropping the 440x440 PNG and re-rendering the head, forelimb tips, feet and tail at 7-16x with a 3-4.5x brightness gain (the asset is near-black on near-black, so nothing can be judged at native exposure). The FAIL stands: the asset reads as a face-on squatting macaque/capuchin, not an aye-aye. Detail, with two corrections to the original claim.

SILHOUETTE: face-on quadruped squat. Rounded skull ~45px wide inside a shaggy fur halo/mane that pushes the head outline to ~68px. Dark elliptical brow band across the forehead that reads as a cap or visor. Two large round white-sclera eyes with tiny dark pupils, pink naked muzzle with two nostril dots and a faint mouth line. Torso ~81px wide x ~142px tall, pale mottled cream belly blotches over grey-brown. Four smooth dark limbs. A bright white rim-light stroke traces the top of the skull and both flanks of the torso; at native exposure it is the most legible line in the image and reads as a headband/bald cap rather than as lighting.

MUST-READ 1, enormous naked bat-like ears: ABSENT. Confirmed at 16x. There is an ear per side, but it is a faint round furred button at eye level, ~6px across on a ~45-55px skull (roughly 10-12 percent of skull width), same brown as the head, sitting flush against the skull edge and half-swallowed by the fur halo. No pinna outline, no naked skin tone, no standing spoon shape, no bat silhouette. CORRECTION to the original claim: the nubs are not 'dark' -- the right one is very slightly LIGHTER than the surrounding fur, which is the only reason it is findable at all; and the head is not bare-sided but ringed by a shaggy mane that further buries them. The defect is size and shape, not tone.

MUST-READ 2, skeletal wire-thin elongated middle finger: ABSENT. Confirmed at 16x on the left forelimb tip and again across the whole foot line at 8x. Every one of the four limbs is a smooth featureless dark tube that terminates in a plain oval ground pad. There are zero digits anywhere in the asset -- no fingers, no toes, no claw, no splayed hand, nothing elongated. The original claim's 'undifferentiated paddles' is accurate.

MUST-READ 3, huge shaggy tail bigger than the body: ABSENT AS SPECIFIED. Confirmed at 6x and 7x, and re-rendered twice to be sure. The tail is a smooth, naked, uniform-width rope about 7-8px thick that leaves the left rump and arcs up and to the left, tapering only slightly at the tip. CORRECTION to the original claim: it is NOT 'about a third of the body' -- its unrolled arc length is roughly equal to the torso height (~125px vs ~142px), so length is closer to right than the claim allows. The real failure is mass and texture: at ~9 percent of torso width and with a perfectly clean silhouette edge, it carries under a tenth of the body's visual area where an aye-aye's tail should out-mass the whole animal, and it has no fur strands, no shag, no plume flare, no volume. It is a monkey rope tail. (An early crop at 4.5x gain appeared to show segmentation and tufts; re-rendering the identical region twice showed a clean smooth tube, so that first read was an artifact and should be disregarded.)

VERDICT: zero of three must-reads are readable. Nothing in this image would let a viewer name it an aye-aye; the head, the fur halo, the brow band and the pink muzzle actively push it toward Old World monkey. Fix order: (1) give it real digits at all four limb tips and make the third finger a long thin skeletal wire, since that is the single unmistakable cue; (2) replace the ear buttons with enormous naked dark spoon pinnae standing clear of the skull at roughly half to two-thirds skull height, and clear the fur halo away from the ear roots so they read against background; (3) rebuild the tail as a shaggy plume at least as wide as the torso with a broken, fur-strand silhouette edge. WHAT I SAW (440x440 PNG, read at 1x, then cropped and nearest-neighbour zoomed 5x/10x/14x, and again at 1.6x-2.2x brightness boost to pull detail out of the near-black plate).

SILHOUETTE / CHASSIS - the judge is RIGHT, and it is provable numerically, not just by eye. Measured opaque bbox: Deep-Sea_Fish 188x69 px; Cold-Water_Fish 201x82 px. Sampling column depth at 24 even stations head-to-tail gives Deep-Sea [55 41 27 13 12 22 29 35 41 45 51 58 58 59 58 54 48 39 34 28 22 21 10 2] and Cold-Water [68 52 34 16 13 23 34 42 49 55 63 71 72 72 70 66 59 47 39 33 26 24 11 2]. That is the SAME curve at a uniform 1.21x scale (68/55, 52/41, 71/58, 72/59, 66/54). Same dorsal-hump position, same caudal peduncle pinch, same fin anchor points. It is one chassis, recoloured plum, with a bead row added. Confirmed.

MOUTH - the judge's description is WRONG and the correction matters. They wrote 'the mouth is a hairline slit'. There is NO mouth at all. At 14x, with brightness pushed 2.2x, the snout is an unbroken smooth taper running to a single needle point; there is no slit, no jaw seam, no lip line, no gape, nothing. The only dark stroke anywhere on the head is the curved gill/opercle arch sitting well BEHIND the eye, plus the dark triangular pectoral fin below it. So the fix is not 'widen the slit' - it is 'a jaw has to be drawn from scratch'. The oversized jaw crowded with needle fangs (mustRead #1) is 100% absent.

EYE - the judge is right that it is undersized but wrong about what it is. It is not 'a tiny white dot'. It is a small pale-white ANNULUS (open ring) with a dark crescent pupil inside, ~8 px across on a 188 px body = ~4% of body length. It is also positioned oddly: it straddles the dorsal contour at the very top of the snout, half-overhanging the silhouette edge rather than being inset into the head mass. This is pixel-for-pixel the same eye treatment as Cold-Water_Fish. Packet asks eyes: prominent and mustRead #2 asks for large light-gathering eyes; neither is honoured. Absent.

PHOTOPHORES - the judge's description here is accurate and is the one must-read that partially lands. There are ~18 soft cyan discs, uniform diameter (~10 px each, i.e. ~15% of body depth), evenly spaced in a single unbroken line hugging the ventral contour from just ahead of the caudal peduncle forward to near the snout tip. They read as a string of pearls / bubbles rather than as specks, and they are far too large and too regular. There are NO scattered specks anywhere on the flank. WARNING for whoever fixes this: the forward end of that same bead row runs along the lower-jaw region and at thumbnail size can be misread as a tooth row - it is not, they are the identical ventral discs. A ventral photophore line is genuine bathypelagic morphology (lanternfish/hatchetfish), so this element is the only thing keeping the image from reading as a plain trout.

BODY - judge is right: mauve/plum flank carrying a clearly visible hexagonal scale mesh, a pale lateral-line stripe, a soft-rayed dorsal with individual ray strokes visible, a dark pectoral triangle and a forked caudal. All of it is Cold-Water Fish furniture. mustRead #3's 'black soft body' is not met.

DEFECTS THE FIRST JUDGE DID NOT CATCH: the packet asks aspect 2.2 (stubby) and the drawing measures 2.72; Cold-Water asks aspect 3.5 and measures 2.45. The two are drawn at nearly identical proportion, and what differentiation exists runs BACKWARDS - the species that should be stubbier is the longer one. The aspect parameter is not reaching the renderer for either. headFrac is specified 0.35; the head forward of the gill arch measures ~41/188 = 0.22.

VERDICT: two of three must-reads are entirely absent (jaw+fangs, large eyes), the third is present only as an over-scaled ventral bead row on the wrong body, and the silhouette is a measurable clone of another species in the same batch. It reads as a generic bony fish with glowing belly lights, not as a bathypelagic predator. FAIL stands.

rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, with corrections to the stated causes. What is actually on canvas: a deep-bodied, lime-green fish in left-facing profile, body (excluding caudal) spanning roughly x135-x350 by y145-y280 — an aspect of about 1.6:1, an OVAL, not the packet's 3.4 ribbon. The judge's 'near-circular deep disc on a narrow stalk' overstates it: it is not circular, it is a symmetrical rounded ellipse whose rear end is BLUNTLY ROUNDED (it does not taper hard to the rear as the mustRead demands) and which necks down over a short, moderately slim caudal peduncle — not a thin stalk. The overall read is discus / deep-bodied surgeonfish, which is the correct diagnosis even if the geometry was described loosely.

MustRead 1 — blunt vertical male forehead: ABSENT, confirmed. The dorsal profile of the head descends in one smooth convex arc from the high point of the back to a POINTED snout at the far right; there is no vertical wall, no step, no brow mass. The eye (white sclera, black pupil, small white catchlight) sits high and unusually far forward, close to the snout tip, which further reads as tang/discus rather than dolphinfish.

MustRead 2 — single dorsal running from just behind the eye to the tail: ABSENT as specified, but the judge under-described what IS there. It is not merely 'a short triangular fin mid-back'. There is a dark-green triangular dorsal lobe at roughly x215-x280 / y145-y175, AND behind/above it a set of thin hair-like filament rays (about six or seven fine strokes) rising off the dorsal ridge from ~x230 to ~x300. So an attempt at a dorsal ray line exists — it is just sparse, thread-thin, sits only over the middle third of the back, starts far behind the eye, and never reaches the caudal peduncle, so it cannot read as the continuous full-length sail that defines the species. Any fix should extend and web that filament line forward to just behind the eye and back to the tail, not add a new fin.

MustRead 3 — deeply forked tail: PRESENT and the strongest element. Large dark-green caudal with two long swept lobes and a deep V notch, attached around x130-x140. Correct in form, though oversized relative to the stubby body.

Also present and unmentioned by the judge: a small dark pectoral fin (downward triangle around x260-x280 / y215-y245) and a small anal fin near x290-x310 / y225-y245 — so the claim that 'only the forked tail is correct' is slightly unfair; the paired-fin placement is plausible. Surface is a uniform saturated lime green with a hexagonal scale-cell lattice and a lighter belly gradient; there is no trace of the blue-green flank with gold ventral wash or the iridescent speckling.

Verdict: two of three identity must-reads are missing and the silhouette aspect is off by more than 2x (1.6 vs 3.4). This does not read as a mahi-mahi. FAIL stands.

WHAT I SAW. Read at 1x, then re-read a 3x crop of the crown, a 6x crop of the crest, a 2x crop of the tentacle field, and a contrast-boosted (gain 5) pass over the body to hunt for faint structure. Ink bounding box measured by pixel scan (bg = rgb(4,5,11), threshold 60): x 152-287, y 84-354, i.e. 136 px wide x 271 px tall.

BODY: an oblate ellipse, distinctly WIDER than tall (~136 x ~100 px, spanning y 84 to ~185), medium blue-violet, flat-filled. The contrast-boosted pass shows the interior is completely featureless - no pleats, no ridge, no sail, no crimping, no fore/aft asymmetry. Tucked just inside the LOWER rim there is a ring of ~20 short vertical tick-marks - the classic jellyfish marginal-tentacle fringe. Long tentacles emerge from the full width of that rim and hang as an even skirt. This is a jellyfish bell in the most literal sense, and the packet note is explicit: 'not a jellyfish and has no bell'.

CREST: at 6x the 'crest' is a single ~2 px hairline arc following the crown. It is not even on the silhouette - it bows slightly ABOVE the dome, leaving a visible sliver of dark background trapped between the arc and the body at the apex, and it fades out symmetrically toward both shoulders. It has no thickness, no serration, no scallops, no pleating - nothing that could read as the crimped sail. The judge's 'reads as a specular highlight' is exactly right; it reads as a rim-light on a smooth balloon, and the apex gap makes it read as a detached wire hoop. The crimped sail crest, which is THE identity feature, is absent as geometry.

CORRECTION 1 - 'renders near-square' is WRONG. The asset is clearly portrait: 136 x 271 px, aspect 0.50. It misses the declared 0.3, but by ~1.7x, not by collapsing to square. Do not fix this by 'making it taller' in the abstract - the cause is that the float is drawn 136 px WIDE (a bell's proportion) instead of a narrow fore-aft float, so the width is what is wrong as much as the height.

CORRECTION 2 - 'tentacles are short and even' is half wrong. They are not short: they run y~185 to y~354, about 170 px, i.e. ~1.7x the float's height, and the tips are staggered (per-column lowest ink ranges y=270 to y=354), so there IS length variation. The real defects are (a) they hang from the ENTIRE bell rim as a symmetric skirt rather than clustering beneath a float, (b) all ~24 strands are the same weight and same order of length, and (c) there is no single dominant fishing tentacle running many body-lengths down - which is what 'extremely long trailing curtain' means for this animal.

CORRECTION 3 - the judge understated it. Besides the long strands from the rim, there is also the short marginal-tentacle fringe inside the lower bell edge, which is a second, independent jellyfish cue.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRESENT: the blue-violet colour is correct, and a gas-filled float-like sac and stinging tentacles both exist. That is not enough. Must-read 1 (crimped sail crest on a float) fails outright; must-read 2 (extremely long trailing curtain) is only partially met; and the note's explicit prohibition on a bell is violated. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: replace the oblate bell with a narrow, elongated fore-aft float (long axis roughly horizontal-diagonal, width ~0.35 of current), give it a real raised crest along the top with 5-8 visible crimp folds and pointed ends, delete the marginal fringe entirely, hang the tentacles from a compact cluster under ONE end of the float, and add one dominant strand running to the bottom of the frame so total height reaches the declared 0.3 aspect.

rows.readsAs: a generic small yellow daisy or miniature sunflower on a fern-like leafy stalk

rows.readsAs: four white canoe hulls or feathers nailed to a brown fence post

At 3x each blade carries two to three pale hairline arcs nested concentrically around its trunk-end, plus a faint outer arc near the tip. They exist in the render. But they sit at roughly 2-3% contrast against a 246,243,236 body and are completely invisible at 1x, and they are drawn as thin scribed lines on a flat plate rather than as ridged zonation with tonal steps. CORRECTION 2 - the judge did not mention the colour error, which is as bad as the shape error. The reference calls for a grey-brown zoned upper crust with a pale cream pore surface beneath. CONFIRMED PARTS OF THE CLAIM: (a) sharp-tipped lens blades instead of one thick woody hoof - correct, and worse than stated, because the concentric arcs prove these are meant to be top-down half-discs, yet a top-down half-disc must terminate in a smooth semicircular outer margin, not a knife point; (b) no pore surface - correct, no underside is visible on any of the four; the only thing under each blade's outer half is a thin dark shadow arc, which reads as drop shadow, not pale cream pores; (c) flat rectangular trunk - correct, no bark, no taper, no cylindrical shading beyond the one hard stripe; (d) the many-thin-tiers form reserved for Shelf Fungus - correct, four evenly spaced equal-size thin tiers is exactly the shelf silhouette the note forbids for this species.

ONE MORE DEFECT NEITHER SIDE NAMED: each blade has a detached thin dark hairline stroke floating in empty background above and right of its top edge, not touching the body. Four stray strokes, one per blade. They read as rendering debris.

FIX DIRECTION: one (or at most two, strongly unequal) thick half-disc(s) with a rounded outer margin and visible depth at the margin; grey-brown zoned top with high-contrast concentric bands; a tilt or a cutaway so the pale cream pore face shows; a rounded, barked, tapering trunk; delete the four stray hairlines.

Band: FAIL, upheld.

rows.readsAs: three generic yellow toadstools with burnt-black cap tops

Zoomed 10x at the junction, the cap underside curves down and inward into a small flared collar that runs smoothly into the stem, with no ring - that is mustRead #3 ('cap tapering smoothly into a solid stem, no ring') and it IS satisfied. 'Paler posts' is fair though: the stem samples (240,201,121) lit / (185,155,93) shaded - a desaturated cream-buff, visibly not the same colour as the yolk cap, so the colour line 'cap and stem the same colour' is violated a second time. So mustRead #2 fails on character, not on absence - a fix must fatten and fork them and carry them onto the stem, not simply add lines. CORRECTION 3: the wavy lobed margin. There IS a wave, but it is on the boundary between the black crown and the golden cap top, not where it counts. The actual outer margin of every cap is a smooth unbroken ellipse in profile with no lobes, undulations or splits. WHAT IS DECISIVELY MISSING: no funnel and no vase. The cap never hollows upward into a trumpet; the profile is a convex-topped toadstool with a downturned edge, and the silhouette is generic cap-and-stem. rows.readsAs: pale blue-white ice shards or feathers on a brown post
rows.defect: This is the Bracket Fungus image re-tinted - identical brown rectangular post, identical four tapered lens blades at identical heights and offsets - with the fill changed from cream to a cold blue-white. The species' entire identity is colour, and the brilliant sulphur-yellow to salmon-orange top and bright yellow pore underside are completely absent; the render is the coldest thing in the batch. No suede wavy lobed edge, no fleshy thickness, no pore surface.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the defect is worse and wider than the claim states. WHAT I SAW: a dark brown vertical post (columns x=87-148, 343 rows tall, hue ~20) with four elongated pointed lens/lance blades jutting right from its right edge, at y78-115, y145-173, y215-249, y276-308. Every blade body pixel I sampled is hue 202-207 at saturation 0.42-0.48 and lightness 0.77-0.96 -- e.g. rgb(241,246,250), rgb(220,234,242), rgb(191,216,231). That is pale ice-blue/cyan, the exact complement of the required sulphur-yellow/salmon-orange. Whole-image hue histogram: 17,001 px in the 200-210 bucket (the organism) and 21,027 px in the 20 bucket (which is ONLY the brown post -- Bracket 21,190, Shelf 21,135, Turkey Tail 21,590 all carry the same ~21k post, so it is chassis, not organism colour). Yellow-band search (hue 40-75, s>0.15) inside the blade region returns 50 pixels, all anti-alias fringe at lightness 0.05, i.e. invisible. There is no orange, no salmon and no yellow anywhere on the fungus. The species' single most diagnostic trait is its colour, and it is not merely missing, it is inverted.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM: (1) 'identical four blades in identical positions' is close but not accurate -- this is a re-tint PLUS a shrink, not a pure re-tint. The post is pixel-identical to Bracket Fungus (same columns, same height, same brown). The four blades sit in the same four slots but are consistently thinner and shorter: blade1 h38/tip x352 vs Bracket h51/tip x352; blade2 h29/tip x294 vs h39/tip x329; blade3 h35/tip x327 vs h44/tip x333; blade4 h33/tip x304 vs h42/tip x332. Blade-region coverage 19,223 px vs Bracket's 24,206 px (-21%). Mask IoU between the two renders is 0.848 -- same chassis, slimmer shelves. A fix that only re-hues will not be enough. (2) 'coldest image in the batch' is confirmed: Chicken is the only earth-fungi render with ANY cool pixels -- 14,800 blue px in its blade region against exactly 0 for Bracket, Shelf, Turkey Tail and Maitake.

TWO FURTHER MUST-READS FAIL INDEPENDENTLY OF COLOUR, which the judge did not name and which a re-hue alone would leave broken: (a) 'a bright yellow pore surface underneath' -- there is no underside stratum drawn at all. Each blade is one continuous top-lit gradient; sampling the bottom edge of every blade (y=113, 171, 247, 306) returns the same hue 202-206 s~0.45 as the top. The only differentiated mark is a thin dark hairline along the TOP of each blade (a spine/shadow), not a pore band beneath. (b) 'a suede-soft wavy lobed edge' -- the outlines are smooth analytic lens curves terminating in a sharp lance point; there is zero lobing or waviness on any margin. (c) 'thick fleshy overlapping shelves' also misses: the blades are thin slivers separated by clear background gaps and do not overlap one another, where the organism is defined by fat crowded overlapping fans.

ROOT CAUSE: Bracket Fungus, Shelf Fungus and Chicken-of-the-Woods are all one shared 'post + lens blades' chassis differing only by blade count and fill tint (Shelf = 5 red blades, Bracket = 4 cream, Chicken = 4 ice-blue). The packet's own Bracket note asks that a bracket read as one thick woody hoof and a shelf as many thin tiers; neither is achieved, so the family needs a real geometry split, not a palette pass. No reading of this image identifies the organism: it reads as frost-coated blades on a stake.

rows.readsAs: three bare winter saplings or a dead shrub at night
rows.defect: It reads as leafless trees, not a fungus. There are three separate stems rising from three separate points instead of one dense cluster from one thick base, and the branching is fine, wiry and repeatedly bifurcating to sharp hairline points - the opposite of the required blunt or forked fleshy tips. The mass is open and airy rather than dense, and the outline is a tree crown, not an antler clump.
rows.fix: Fuse the stems into one thick fleshy base, thicken every branch so the taper is gradual and the branch stays plump to its end, and cap each tip with a rounded blunt or two-pronged fork.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld — the asset reads as a small grove of three bare winter saplings, not a Ramaria clump. Verified at 1x and at 5x crops of the base (x130-320,y230-340) and both crown halves.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Three pale cream poles rise from three SEPARATE ground contacts at roughly x=170, x=210, x=265 (image is 440x440), with 15-20px of black gap and clean rounded stroke-ends between them; no shared fleshy foot, no common stipe, only a single soft elliptical ground shadow underneath all three. Each pole is smooth and slightly tapering and runs BARE for its lower ~120px (y=325 up to y=230) before any branching begins — a trunk-and-crown tree schema. The left two poles lean toward each other and CROSS in an X at y~235; the right pole splits in a clean Y at the same height. Above that the mass explodes into 4-6 orders of branching and ends up spanning x=50 to x=390 (~77% of the frame width) while the three feet occupy only ~25% — the crown is far wider than tall and far wider than its own base, i.e. an umbrella/tree-crown envelope. Interior ink coverage inside that envelope is very low; it is mostly black.

MUST-READ SCORING. (1) 'dense upward-branching antler cluster from one thick base' — fails on all three terms: not dense (airy, see-through), not upward (the outer crown branches run horizontally and several on the left at y~200-230 angle DOWNWARD-outward), and not one base (three separate bases). (2) 'branches dividing repeatedly into blunt or forked tips' — fails. (3) 'no caps and no gills anywhere' — PASSES; there are none, and the cream/pale-ochre colour with slightly paler branch highlights is on-palette.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM. (a) The tips are NOT 'sharp hairline points'. Zoomed 5x, every terminal twig is a CONSTANT-WIDTH hairline of about 2px that ends in a flat/square stroke cap — there is no taper to a spike at all. The real defect is that the branches never change calibre: the trunk is ~10px and every branch above the first fork is the same 2px wire, so there is no fleshy 3-5px blunt finger anywhere. Fixing 'sharpness' would fix nothing; the fix is calibre falloff by order plus visibly rounded, thick terminal knobs. (b) 'bifurcating' is too generous. The dominant branching mode is MONOPODIAL/alternate, not dichotomous: the right crown clearly shows one long axis continuing outward for ~90px with four short side twigs sprouting off its upper edge at ~30-40 degrees. That alternate-twig-off-a-continuing-axis pattern is precisely what makes the eye call 'tree'. Coral fungus needs equal-armed Y forks at narrow (20-30 degree) angles with both arms continuing upward. (c) The judge's 'three separate stems from three separate points' is CORRECT and confirmed at pixel level.

FIX DIRECTION: one thick common base occupying most of the footprint width; branching starting within ~15% of ground height (kill the bare trunk region); dichotomous Y forks, max 3-4 orders; all arms biased strongly upward so the silhouette is taller than wide and columnar/antler-shaped; branch width stepping down 10->7->5->4px with rounded blunt caps; crowd the branches so the clump reads solid.

rows.readsAs: orange-tipped matchsticks or corn dogs stuck in a brown bread roll
rows.defect: The host is an anonymous smooth brown ellipse lying on the ground with a few short tick marks along one edge - no head, no thorax, no legs, no segmentation, nothing that reads as an insect. The packet's note says exactly this case fails: without a legible host it is just a club fungus. The stalks are hairline sticks of uniform width and the fertile heads are smooth speckled capsules with no roughened swelling, so they read as matches rather than stromata.
rows.fix: Model the host as a recognisable insect - segmented abdomen, curled legs, a head with visible eyes - lying on its side, and have the clubs erupt from between its segments with visibly swollen, pitted fertile heads.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD on the host, but the first judge's description of the clubs is materially wrong and must not be used to drive the fix.

WHAT I DID: read the 440x440 PNG at full size twice, then decoded it and re-rendered three nearest-neighbour crops of the base at 6x/8x with brightness multipliers of 1.0, 2.6 and 5.5 to rule out dark-on-dark anatomy hidden against the near-black backdrop. Nothing is hidden. Crops: scratchpad host.png / host2.png / host3.png (region x140-310, y270-360).

THE HOST (the defining must-read) - FAILS, claim confirmed. The host is a single flat brown horizontal ellipse, roughly x=163..300, y=298..340 (about 137 x 42 px), colour a flat mid-brown (~#5A4433) with a slightly darker soft drop-shadow ellipse offset behind and below it. Its outline is a mathematically clean ellipse: at 5.5x brightness the left and right ends are smooth unbroken arcs with NO head bulge, NO abdomen taper, NO thoracic constriction, NO waist, NO leg stubs, NO antennae, NO eye, NO mandible, NO wing-case seam, NO ventral segment plates. The only internal detail is SEVEN (not "a few" vaguely - seven, evenly spaced) short straight dark-brown vertical hairline strokes across the upper half of the ellipse, all the same length, all stopping well short of the lower edge - so they never reach or notch the silhouette, and the outline stays a smooth uninterrupted oval. They read as hatching on a bread roll or a rake-mark in soil, not as arthropod tergites. Because the shape is horizontal, flat, and the same brown as the shadow it casts, the most natural reading is a mound of dirt or a log, not a carcass. This is exactly the packet's own stated failure case ("The insect must stay legible - without a visible host it is just a club fungus") and it is worse than that: the host does not even read as an object with an axis, so must-read #2 ("the insect host still clearly recognisable beneath") is absent, and must-read #1 ("erupting directly out of a dead insect's body") is only half-satisfied - the clubs do rise from the mound, but the mound is not an insect.

CORRECTION 1 - THE CLUB TIPS ARE NOT SMOOTH CAPSULES. The judge is wrong here. Each of the six tips is a distinctly swollen ovoid head about 22 x 32 px, i.e. roughly 5x the stalk width, with a warm orange-to-vermilion vertical gradient, a darker maroon rim along the shaded side, and - critically - a scatter of six to ten small pale cream speckles and short dashes stippled across the lit face of every head. Those speckles read convincingly as perithecial ostioles. Must-read #3 ("a swollen roughened fertile head at the club tip") is therefore PRESENT and is the strongest thing in this asset. The heads' outer SILHOUETTE is smooth (no bumpy/granular edge), which is a legitimate but much smaller polish note; the surface is not smooth. Do not "fix" the heads.

CORRECTION 2 - THE STALK CRITICISM IS RIGHT, and it is a polish item, not the failure. All six stalks are dead-uniform 3px pale tan (~#D8C48E) lines with zero taper from base to head, zero tonal variation along their length, and no darkening where they meet the host. Two of them cross in an X near the base. Uniform pale stick + swollen orange head does give a matchstick impression, which the flat unshaded stalk colour amplifies. Real Ophiocordyceps stipes are darker ochre/brown, thicker at the base, and taper into the fertile head rather than butting into it.

MINOR: content bounding box is about 170w x 250h (aspect ~0.68) against the packet's stated aspect 0.5, so the piece also sits wider than spec.

BAND: FAIL stands, on one cause only - the host insect is an anonymous smooth brown ellipse with seven surface tick strokes and no arthropod anatomy of any kind. Fix priority: give the base an insect silhouette (distinct head with an eye, thorax, tapering segmented abdomen, at least two or three curled dead legs breaking the outline, antennae), orient it along an axis rather than as a flat horizontal mound, and let the segmentation notch the silhouette instead of floating inside it. Keep the speckled fertile heads as-is; taper and darken the stalks as a secondary pass.

rows.readsAs: a small green-shaded table lamp
rows.defect: Cap colour, the white ring and the white stem all read. Two failures: the sac-like volva - the packet's stated identifying feature - is only a slightly wider rounded solid pedestal at the stem foot, with no cup lip, no ragged sac wall and no separation from the stem, so it reads as a lamp base. And the cap is scored with dozens of hard evenly spaced radial ribs running to the rim, which reads as an umbrella frame or lampshade panelling rather than 'faint radiating fibrils' on a smooth cap.

rows.readsAs: a white art-deco desk lamp

rows.readsAs: a naval mine / a spiked sea urchin ball
rows.defect: The rays are thin needle spikes stabbing outward from the equator of a grey sphere. The must-read is a THICK outer skin split into pointed rays peeled BACK and downward so the sac sits in the bowl of a star - here nothing is peeled back, there is no star lying under the sac, and the rays have no thickness or inner/outer surface. The single raised pore is present as a dark dot, but it is the only correct element. The whole render is also so dark it is barely legible against the background.

rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but several of the stated causes need correcting before anyone fixes against them. I decoded the PNG and re-rendered it at 3-6x with gamma lift, plus separate lifts of the apex and base regions, so nothing is hidden in the darkness.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a near-perfect pale sphere (subject bbox 134,163 to 303,251 = 169w x 88h; the sphere alone is ~90px across, i.e. the ball IS the whole organism and the entire extra width comes from spikes). Radiating from behind the sphere are 7-8 thin isoceles slivers, ~4-6px wide where they meet the sac edge and tapering to needle points. A single dark disc with a soft light rim sits on the front face. Below is only a soft elliptical ground shadow.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM:
(1) 'from the equator' is not accurate. Lifting the top and bottom crops shows the rays are radial all the way around, urchin-fashion: a short blunt point at ~11 o'clock, a longer one at ~1:30, two long laterals left, two long laterals right, one at ~4:30, and a small stub at ~7:30. The two longest happen to be horizontal, which is why it scans as equatorial, but the fix is not 'move the spikes down' — the whole radial fan is wrong.
(2) 'a grey sphere' understates the colour miss. Sampled RGB at the lit sac centre is (58,60,79) — blue-dominant, cool lavender-grey, not neutral and nowhere near the spec 'leathery tan to grey-brown'. Worse, and the original judge did not mention this: the rays are the SAME colour and value as the sac. There is zero hue or value separation between skin and spore sac, so even if the rays were the right shape they would not read as a separate leathery layer.
(3) 'the raised pore dot is the only correct element' is too generous. The dot is present and does read as raised, but the apex of the sac is BARE — the dot sits on the front face at roughly 40% across and 35% down, not at the top of the sac as mustRead requires. Face-on, off-centre, on a spiked ball, it reads as a single cyclops eye, and it is actively one of the things driving the wrong-organism read rather than the one salvageable element.
(4) 'nothing is peeled back, no thick outer skin, no star lying under the sac' — fully confirmed. The extreme-lift base crop shows the sphere's bottom silhouette is smooth and unbroken and meets the ground shadow directly. There is no star platform, no folded flaps, no thickness to any ray, and the sac is not seated in anything; the rays are occluded by the sphere so their bases are invisible, which is the opposite of an earthstar where the rays are broad triangular flaps folded down and outward beneath the ball.
(5) 'so dark it is barely legible' — confirmed numerically. Peak subject luminance is ~31% of full at the brightest highlight, the sac body sits around 24%, and the background is near-black. At native size it is a dim blob.

SCORE AGAINST MUST-READS: ray 1 (thick outer skin split into pointed rays peeled back like a star) ABSENT. Ray 2 (round papery spore sac sitting in the CENTRE of the star) half-present — there is a round sac, but it sits in nothing. Ray 3 (single raised pore at the TOP of the sac) present but misplaced to the front face. Aspect is also off: 169/88 = 1.92 vs spec 1.5, and it is wide for the wrong reason (two long needles, not a broad low star).

rows.readsAs: a sweet potato or a lump of amber putty
rows.defect: The convoluted brain-like folding that IS this organism is absent - the form is two smooth rounded blobs merged into a potato silhouette, with three or four thin scratched lines drawn on the surface as a substitute for folds. It is fully opaque with a solid amber fill, so no light passes through any lobe. There is no bark and no substrate; it sits on a bare shadow ellipse.
rows.fix: Rebuild the mass out of many overlapping wavy lobes so the outline is frilled and the interior self-shadows, drop the opacity so back lobes show through front ones, and clamp it onto a visible bark surface.
rows.verifyWhy:
VERDICT UPHELD, but three of the four stated causes are inaccurate and should not be fixed against as written. What is actually on canvas (measured, body bbox 160,160 -> 269,271 = 110x112 px inside a 440x440 frame, i.e. the subject occupies only ~25% of frame width): a cluster of soft airbrushed amber-orange ellipsoids sitting on a plain brown ground-shadow ellipse in empty dark space.

CORRECTION 1 — not 'two smooth merged blobs'. At 5x zoom I count roughly FIVE to SIX overlapping ellipsoid lobes: a large round upper-left lobe, an upper-centre lobe, a right-hand lobe running out to the right margin, a smaller lobe tucked behind it, and a big pendant egg-shaped lower-centre lobe (the largest single mass, hanging down to the shadow). The defect is not lobe COUNT — the count is fine — it is that every lobe is a smooth Gaussian-feathered sphere with a single soft light-to-dark gradient. No lobe has an edge, a lip, a crease, or a wavy frill. So the fix is not 'add more lobes'; it is 'give each lobe a folded, rolled, convoluted margin'.

CORRECTION 2 — not 'three or four scratched lines'. There are roughly 10-14 thin dark-brown strokes, densely clustered in the upper-middle third of the mass in a tangled scribble, plus 2-3 separate crescent strokes low and right of centre. The judge undercounted by ~3x. The real problem is their CHARACTER: every stroke is the same hairline weight, uniformly dark, with no paired highlight on the opposite side and no local shading break in the underlying gradient. They therefore read as surface scratches or skin blemishes on a tuber, not as gyri/sulci relief. Adding more of the same strokes will make it worse. Convoluted brain-like folding — the single defining must-read for this organism — is genuinely ABSENT, and that is what upholds the FAIL.

UNCITED FEATURE the judge missed: there is one prominent hard-edged near-WHITE arc sweeping across the top-left lobe (roughly from 10 o'clock to 1 o'clock on that lobe). It is the only wet/gelatinous cue in the piece, and it currently reads as a stray white pen stroke floating on top of the form rather than a specular on a gel surface — it has hard ends, sits at constant width, and does not follow any modelled curvature.

CORRECTION 3 — 'the fill is fully opaque so no light passes through any lobe' is WRONG AS STATED. The lobes ARE alpha-composited against each other: the elliptical boundaries of the rear lobes are plainly visible reading THROUGH the front lobes (most obvious where the right lobe passes behind the lower pendant lobe), and the mass carries a brighter internal core with cooler, darker margins. Internal translucency between lobes is present. What is missing is transmission at the SILHOUETTE: the outer edges fade to dark against the background instead of glowing, there is no backlight or rim transmission anywhere on the contour, no background is visible through any thin margin, and thin sections do not gain saturation or brightness the way real amber jelly does. The accurate defect is 'no light passes OUT through the margins / no backlit read', not 'no translucency at all'. PNG alpha is uniformly 255 across all 193,600 pixels with the dark background baked in, so translucency has to be painted as a lighting effect and currently only the inter-lobe blend attempts it.

CORRECTION 4 — 'No bark substrate' is CONFIRMED and is the second failing must-read. Beneath the mass there is only a flat, untextured brown gradient ellipse acting as a contact shadow. There is no log, no branch, no wood grain, no bark ridging, no substrate of any kind; the fungus floats in undifferentiated dark space. The 'no stem' half of that must-read IS satisfied — the mass sits directly on the ground plane with no stalk.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT neither judge cited: ASPECT. The packet calls for aspect 1.3 (sprawling wider than tall). The rendered body measures 110w x 112h = 0.98 w/h — essentially square, and slightly tall if anything. Including the shadow it is 144x120 = 1.20, but the shadow is not the organism. The mass needs to spread laterally along its substrate, not stack vertically.

On the judge's headline read: 'sweet potato' is a fair characterisation of the full-size impression — a single lumpy orange tuber with dark blemish scratches — though the zoomed form is closer to a cluster of merged dough balls or a bunch of peaches than to one elongated tuber. Either way it is the wrong organism. Two of three must-reads (convoluted brain-like folds; sitting on bark) are absent and the third (translucency) reads only internally, so FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a brown broccoli head or a bare-trunk tree crown hovering over a small white cone
rows.defect: The mass is a cloud of smooth chocolate-brown lobes with no ruffled spoon-shaped fronds, no overlapping rosette tiering, and no white branched stalk base — the single white cone below is disconnected from the mass by a visible gap of empty background, so the fronds do not spring from anything. Colour is a flat dark brown with no fawn/grey range and no white undersides anywhere.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled the crown (x60-380, y90-340 at 3x) and the base (x150-300, y230-340 at 6x), then pixel-probed columns and rows to settle what is fill vs. background. The FAIL stands, and the stated cause is substantially correct, but three parts of it need correcting or sharpening.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A single opaque blob occupying roughly x=90-350, y=110-250, built from ~12 bulbous circular puff lobes bumping along the outer contour. Probing proves the blob is ONE FLAT FILL: every interior sample from y=115 to y=250 and x=116 to x=320 returns exactly rgb(67,51,31).
