The only interior marks are ~12-14 hairline cream arcs (sampled 92,78,60 and 78,64,45, 2-3px wide) laid over the UPPER face of individual lobes - the standard foliage/cloud highlight-rim convention. Read as drawn it is a tree crown or a head of broccoli.

CORRECTION 1 - 'no white undersides' is right in effect but imprecise as stated: pale strokes DO exist, there are a dozen of them, but they are top-of-lobe highlight arcs, not gill/underside surfaces, and no lobe has a pale lower margin anywhere. A fix that just recolours those existing arcs will not produce the must-read.

CORRECTION 2 - the judge did not mention the central cleft. There is a narrow dark wedge down the middle of the crown (at y=200 it spans only x=202-236) that splits the mass into a left and a right half. Probing shows it is pure background (20,16,8) with no fill in it, i.e. negative space, not a stalk. Far from helping, it reads as the fork/trunk gap of a tree crown and reinforces the wrong organism.

CORRECTION 3 - the gap is larger than 'a visible gap' suggests, and the cone is smaller. The cream cone is a single smooth unbranched dome, roughly x=195-245, y=278-308 (about 50x30px, ~11% of canvas width), flat-cut along its base and sitting on an elliptical ground shadow. A full horizontal sweep at y=260 from x=140 to x=295 returns only background (17,14,9) - absolutely nothing bridges crown to cone. The vertical clearance is 73px at the nearest lobe bottom and 110px straight down the centre notch, i.e. a quarter of the canvas height of empty space. MUST-READS. (1) 'dense ruffled rosette of overlapping grey-brown spoon-shaped fronds' - ABSENT. (2) 'fronds all springing from a single branched white stalk base' - ABSENT. The only white element is one isolated unbranched cone with no branches, no contact and no lobes attached to it. (3) 'the mass sitting like a hen at the foot of a tree' - ABSENT; it hovers. Zero of three defining must-reads are readable, so the organism reads as the wrong thing entirely. FAIL upheld.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS: shade the mass into distinct value tiers so lobes overlap; replace circular puffs with wavy-edged spoon/tongue fronds whose free margins ruffle; give each frond a pale cream lower edge; and drop the crown down to meet a white stalk that BRANCHES two or three times, with every frond visibly springing off a branch tip - no air between stalk and mass.

rows.readsAs: a speckled brown rock, a potato, or a lump of ore with gold flecks

Two things in their wording are imprecise: the sparkles are not confined to the body -- roughly half of them form a halo OUTSIDE the silhouette, which is a large part of why it reads as a glowing mineral rather than an organism; and the fill is not uniformly 'ochre-brown' but has soft internal highlight blooms that read as sub-surface glow, reinforcing the gemstone/ore impression rather than a powder film. What a fix has to build: a substrate plane first (a leaf blade with a midrib, or a taut fabric field), then a thin semi-transparent chalky-white to pale-grey film laid over PART of it in irregular disconnected blotches with feathered, fraying edges, letting the substrate colour and its veins/weave read through the film at 40-70% opacity. Delete the sparkle field and halo entirely -- they are the single loudest wrong signal in the image. Zero of the three must-reads survive; FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a mossy green rock or an asteroid with glowing specks
rows.defect: Identical blob silhouette to Mildew and Yeast with only the hue changed to green and the speckles to pale mint. None of the three must-reads is drawn: no tangled white hyphal fuzz, no upright stalks, and above all no dark round spore capsules on stalk tips — the dots are flat scattered specks inside the blob, not sporangia standing above a mat. No circular colony patches either.

rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated cause. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS: one closed, hard-edged, low-poly lump filling the frame (measured silhouette bbox 264x183 px in a 440x440 canvas, aspect 1.44). The fill is a flat desaturated grey-green (mean body RGB 34,47,34) carrying a very low-contrast cloudy mottle, plus roughly 60-70 discrete pale round dots scattered across it and a matching halo of the same dots sprayed loosely outside the outline in the vignette. That is the entire asset. Zoomed 3x-4x with a 2.0-2.4 gamma lift over the top edge (x 130-340, y 105-205) and the bottom edge (y 230-335): the outline is a clean straight-faceted polygon in both places, with no thread, filament, spike, stalk or fuzz crossing it anywhere. A column-scan of the top edge (every 4 px from x=94 to x=354) returns a smooth, almost monotone curve rising 241 -> 129 -> 241 with no excursion greater than about 12 px, i.e. mathematically no upright protrusions. MUST-READS: (1) 'a low fuzz of tangled white hyphal threads' - ABSENT. There is not one thread anywhere; the edge is a hard polygon and the interior mottle is a soft cloud, not filaments. (2) 'upright stalks each topped by a dark round spore capsule' - ABSENT, and this is the fatal one. The dots are not on stalks (nothing connects any dot to the body edge) and they are the WRONG POLARITY: they are BRIGHTER than the mat, not darker. (3) 'colonies spreading in circular patches' - only weakly, and only by accident: the outer speck halo is an ellipse of loose dots, but it is the same generic halo Mildew and Yeast carry, so it carries no species information. CORRECTION 1 to the original claim: 'identical blob silhouette' is overstated as literal geometry. I aligned the three masks by centroid and computed IoU - Mold vs Mildew 0.90, Mold vs Yeast 0.87, Mildew vs Yeast 0.89. The vertex jitter and the aspect differ slightly (Mold 1.44, Mildew 1.50, Yeast 1.37). They are not the same pixels; they are three seeds of ONE lump generator. The substance of the claim stands and is arguably worse than stated: the shared chassis is not just the outline but the whole pipeline - same closed convex-ish polygon, same cloud-mottle fill, same speck field, same speck halo, same framing. Only hue and a jitter seed change (Mold 34,47,34 green-grey; Mildew 70,49,21 ochre; Yeast 77,74,63 warm grey). CORRECTION 2: 'hue-shifted green' implies green is the defect. Green-grey is defensible for a mold spore head; the defect is that the MAT is green rather than white and the SPORE HEADS are pale rather than dark - the colour assignment is inverted relative to the reference row's 'white fuzzy mat with blue-green, black or grey spore heads'. FAMILY CONSEQUENCE: because Mold and Mildew are the same drawing, the packet's own Mildew note ('drawing Mildew as deep three-dimensional fluff makes it read as mold instead') cannot even be tested - neither one reads as fluff or as film; both read as a speckled stone. WHAT THIS ASSET READS AS TODAY: a mossy boulder or a lichen-flecked rock, not a fungal colony. FIX DIRECTION: kill the closed polygon body. Mold needs (a) a low, wide, soft-edged white/pale mat whose OUTER boundary is fuzzy and thread-broken, not faceted, ideally with a hint of the substrate visible under its thinner margin; (b) a forest of thin upright stalks standing clear ABOVE that mat's topline so the silhouette is spiky, each terminating in (c) a round capsule DARKER than everything else in the image (blue-green/near-black), sized ~2-3x the current speck; (d) the circular-patch read from one or two concentric tone rings in the mat rather than from the ambient halo. Remove the free-floating specks outside the body - they currently supply the only 'spore' cue and they supply it wrongly.

rows.readsAs: a morel mushroom
rows.defect: The conical head, the pale cream stalk and the head-fused-at-the-base attachment are all correct and it is the only purpose-built body in the batch. But the pit texture is a flat repeating diamond lattice printed onto the dome — a wallpaper pattern with uniform cell size and no depth. The ridges are thin dark lines rather than pale raised walls, and the cells are not recessed, so the honeycomb reads as a decorative motif rather than a pitted surface.
rows.fix: Invert the value structure of the lattice: make each ridge a pale raised bevel with a highlight along its lit edge and each pit a dark recessed chamber with a cast shadow, and vary the pit size and row alignment so the network deforms with the cone's curvature.

rows.readsAs: orange flame licks or corn kernels jammed into a dark fence post
rows.defect: This is the shared shelf chassis: four sharply-pointed amber lozenges alternating off a dark post, the same shape used for Shelf Fungus and Turkey Tail. Nothing about it is an oyster mushroom — no fan or shell outline (the caps taper to a spike instead of widening to a fan), no gills of any kind let alone white gills running down to a stem, no stubby off-centre stem, and no inrolled wavy margin. The saturated marigold-orange also contradicts the pale grey-to-fawn colour called for.
rows.fix: Replace the pointed lozenges with wide fan/shell caps, broad at the free edge and narrowing to a short lateral stem at the wood, and rake white gill lines across the visible underside of the lower caps so the gills are the read.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at full size and again at 3-4x on three crops (top shelf, bottom shelf, the post column). The FAIL stands, but two parts of the stated cause need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a flat dark-brown vertical bar occupying x~78-140 of a 440px canvas, running nearly the full height (y~45-395). It is a plain two-tone rectangle - a slightly darker strip down its right third, no bark texture, no rounding, no end-grain, no taper. Four saturated marigold/amber lozenges project rightward from it. Each lozenge is squared off flat on its LEFT edge, abutting the post (they DO touch the post - they are not floating, so 'on wood' is at least gestured at), swells to maximum depth about a third of the way out, then tapers to a single sharp spear point at the right. Two thin dark grey hairline strokes trail past each tip along the upper edge, extending beyond the orange body into the black - stray line primitives with no anatomical referent.

CORRECTION 1 TO THE CLAIM - 'no gills at all' is too absolute. Each lozenge carries two or three pale cream arc lines on its surface. But they are CONCENTRIC arcs that follow the lozenge outline (growth-zone banding, the way a Ganoderma or Trametes bracket is marked), drawn on the UPPER surface, and they run parallel to the margin. Gills on Pleurotus are RADIAL, WHITE, on the UNDERSIDE, and converge on the attachment point. So the marking is present but is the wrong topology, wrong surface and wrong colour - it reads as zone lines, not gills. The judge is right that the gill must-read is not delivered; they are wrong that nothing at all is drawn there, which matters for the fix (the arc primitive exists and needs re-aiming radially onto a visible underside, not adding from scratch).

CORRECTION 2 - the shape failure is worse than 'no fan or shell outline' conveys, and it is specifically INVERTED. An oyster shell or fan is NARROW at the point of attachment and BROAD at the free margin. These lozenges are the exact opposite: broad, straight and blunt where they meet the post, tapering to a needle point at the free end. That is a leaf/canoe/blade silhouette. Fixing it is not adding a fan on top of the current shape, it is flipping the width profile end for end.

CORRECTION 3 - 'overlapping tiers' also fails, which the claim did not mention. The four shelves are separated by clean black gaps of 30-50px; nothing overlaps or shingles. Pleurotus grows in imbricate clusters where each cap partly covers the one below.

CONFIRMED AS STATED: no stem of any kind, off-centre stubby or otherwise - the caps meet the post directly with a hard vertical cut. No inrolled or wavy margin - every edge is a crisp hard-edged curve ending in a point; there is no undulation and no thickened rolled lip anywhere. Colour is confirmed wrong: a strong golden-orange gradient (roughly #E8A93C to #F5C86A) against a spec of 'pale grey to fawn-brown cap, white gills and flesh'. That saturation pushes it toward Laetiporus / chicken-of-the-woods rather than Pleurotus.

NET: one of three must-reads is partially served (something wood-like exists and the shelves attach to it, in tiers). The cap-shape half of that must-read fails, and the other two must-reads - white gills decurrent to an off-centre stubby stem, and a smooth inrolled wavy margin - are wholly absent. With the colour also outside the stated range, the asset does not read as an oyster mushroom; it reads as generic orange bracket fungus, or at low confidence as blades stuck in a fence post. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a generic small brown toadstool, rendered as a doll in the middle of a mostly empty frame
rows.defect: The identity must-read — a fat barrel/bulbous stem far thicker than the cap is tall — is absent: the drawn stem is a narrow straight cylinder roughly a quarter the cap's width, taller than it is wide, which is the profile of a fragile agaric, not a bolete. The white net is drawn but as a small hard-edged rectangular wireframe grid floating on the stem rather than a fine raised reticulation following the stem's curve. The underside is a thin stippled band that could equally be gills. The whole organism occupies about a sixth of the canvas.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x, 6x and 18x zoom plus a pixel-column silhouette scan of the 440x440 PNG. FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes are measurably mis-described and one real defect was missed.

MEASUREMENTS (background sampled at 5,6,12; threshold d>40): subject bbox is x176..268, y166..258 = 93x93 px inside a 440x440 frame. Cap max width 93 px at y=190. Cap top y=166, widest y=190, underside band ends y~202, so total cap depth ~36 px and the dome above the widest point is only 24 px (dome/width = 0.26 -- a low, flattish plate rather than a fat bun). Stem row widths from y=205 to y=256, sampled every 3 px: 39,39,40,40,41,39,40,40,40,40,40,40,40,40,40,40,39,38,37.

CLAIM 1 (stem) -- RIGHT CONCLUSION, WRONG NUMBER. The stem is NOT 'about a quarter the cap's width': it is 40 px against a 93 px cap = 43%, nearly half. Do not fix this by widening to ~50% -- it will still fail. What actually fails is the PROFILE: the width series is dead flat (39-41 px over 45 px of length, +/-2 px = 5% variation) and then TAPERS to 37 px at the very base. That is a straight tube that narrows downward, i.e. the exact inverse of a bolete's swollen, ventricose foot. Second, the mustRead demands the stem be 'far thicker than the cap is tall': stem 40 px vs cap depth 36 px is 1.1x, not 'far'. The fix is a barrel/club silhouette that bulges through the mid-to-lower stem, is widest near the ground, and reads roughly 65-75% of cap width -- not just a wider cylinder. The judge's shorthand 'agaric profile' is fair.

CLAIM 2 (net) -- CORRECT, confirmed at 18x. The white reticulation is present and correctly PLACED (a band on the upper stem, y~203-218, i.e. the top third), so it is not absent -- but it is rendered as 4 perfectly straight horizontal lines crossed by 3 perfectly straight vertical lines forming rectangles. There is zero curvature, zero perspective compression of the mesh toward the stem's left and right edges, and no highlight/shadow pairing on the strands. It reads as a rectangle of window screen laid flat over the stem, exactly as claimed. Real reticulation needs the horizontals to arc downward with the cylinder, the verticals to crowd together at the silhouette edges, mesh cells to be irregular polygons rather than uniform rectangles, and each strand to carry a lit top edge and a dark underside so it sits proud.

CLAIM 3 (framing) -- DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT, number slightly off. The subject is 93 px in a 440 px frame = 21% linear (about a fifth, not a sixth) and only ~4.5% of frame area. Either way it is drastically undersized and floats in a sea of empty vignette; it should fill the frame.

WHAT THE JUDGE GOT WRONG BY OMISSION -- the pore surface is actually the least broken must-read and should NOT be touched blindly. There are no gills anywhere; the underside is a flat cream shelf (RGB ~239,230,205) carrying scattered olive-grey blobs clustered along the cap margin and thinning toward the stem. It does not read as gills, so 'boletes drawn with gills' is not the failure here. It is still weak -- the specks are sparse irregular blotches over large areas of plain flat cream rather than a dense sponge of fine pores, and the shelf has no thickness or downward bulge -- so it wants densification, not replacement.

DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED: the stem shading is broken. A razor-hard vertical seam runs down the stem at roughly x=222 (mid-stem), with flat untextured cream to its left and an abruptly dark desaturated grey to its right, and at the top of the stem that grey is a hard-cornered RECTANGULAR block that terminates mid-stem rather than fading. The stem therefore reads as two flat panels butted together, not a cylinder, and the dark side is near-neutral grey rather than the specified 'pale buff'. Fix this at the same time as the barrel silhouette or the widened stem will just be a wider two-tone slab.

BAND: FAIL. The single defining silhouette read of a bolete -- the fat bulbous barrel stem -- is genuinely absent, and the net, while present, is a flat grid decal. The asset currently reads as a generic brown-capped agaric with a screen-door sticker on its stalk.

rows.readsAs: a grove of pale bare trees, a banyan, or a mushroom cloud

CONFIRMED: there is genuinely no cushion and no mat. Between and below the trunks is bare dark background - the only marks there are the shadow ellipse and a scatter of small soft-focus pale motes (spore dust) floating at mid-trunk height. Nothing reads as a spongy low cushion or a springy ground mat, so mustRead 1 (spongy cushion of hollow tubular stalks) and mustRead 3 (springy mat texture) are both unmet at the form level. Branching in threes and fours IS present, but only up in the crown, which is the wrong place for it - on Cladonia the podetia fork from near the base upward, and here the lower half is deliberately kept bare.

MISSED DEFECT A: the crown interior is an OPAQUE filled pale mass with dark punched holes, not an open airy lattice. At 4x the outer 15% is beautiful fine dichotomous twigging, but inside that the fill goes solid, so the crown reads as foam/cloud/foliage rather than a thicket of hollow tubes.

MISSED DEFECT B: mustRead 2 ('branch tips fine, drooping and all nodding one way') is only half met. The tips are correctly fine and drooping, but they nod RADIALLY - down-and-left on the left rim, down-and-right on the right rim, a mirrored fountain. There is no single shared nod direction anywhere in the figure.

ON SPEC: colour is correct - pale ash grey-green bleaching to near-white - and there are no leaves and no flat lobes.

FIX DIRECTION: delete the bare trunk zone entirely and the ground shadow with it; start the forking at the base so the silhouette is a low mounded cushion wider than it is tall; keep the existing fine tip work but open up the solid crown interior into visible tubes with dark gaps; bias every tip's nod to one side.

rows.readsAs: red pepper pods, canoe hulls or flame licks stuck to a dark post
rows.defect: The exact chassis used for Oyster Mushroom and Turkey Tail, recoloured crimson with one extra blade. Each 'shelf' is a pointed lozenge, so there is no semicircular outline, no flat top, no flat underside and no staircase step-out — the blades all project the same distance and taper to a spike. The colour is a saturated tomato red rather than banded ochre and umber, and no pale buff pore surface is visible anywhere. It also fails the packet's own separation test against Bracket Fungus, since it reads as neither.
rows.fix: Swap the lozenge for a true half-disc bracket seen from slightly above — flat top with concentric growth bands, flat pale buff underside — and stagger the stack so each tier projects further than the one above it.
rows.verifyWhy:
I tried to break this FAIL and could not. What is on the 440x440 canvas: a dark umber vertical post (x roughly 79-141, running y 48-390) on the left, and five separate blades springing rightward from its right face. At 3x zoom each blade is a lens/leaf: a straight-ish horizontal LOWER edge, a convex swelling upper edge, and a sharp point at the outer right end. Sampled body colour is rgb(222,65,77) at five points down the stack - a flat tomato/crimson red with a light-to-dark left-to-right gradient. Verdict upheld: this reads as red leaves, feathers or chilli pods pinned to a post, not as a fungus.

Where the original claim is RIGHT: no semicircular outline (every blade tapers to a point); no flat TOP (the upper edge is a convex swell); no staircase step-out - I measured the red span per row and all five blades begin at exactly x=141, the same trunk face, with right extents 304 / 303 / 309 / 279 / 270, i.e. non-monotonic and slightly SHRINKING downward, so there is no stepping outward in either direction; no pale buff pore surface anywhere - the undersides are the same red as the tops; and the banded ochre-and-umber colour is entirely absent.

Where the original claim is WRONG or imprecise, and the fix should be written against these corrections:
(1) 'no flat underside' is incorrect. The UNDERSIDE of each blade IS essentially flat and horizontal from the trunk outward. It is the top surface and the pointed tip that destroy the bracket read. Do not spend the fix flattening the underside; it is already flat.
(2) 'one extra blade' is only true relative to Oyster Mushroom. Blade counts are Oyster 4, Shelf Fungus 5, Turkey Tail 6 - so Shelf has one FEWER than Turkey Tail, not one more.
(3) The claim implies the blades are featureless recolours. They are not quite: each blade carries two faint pale-pink concentric arcs inside it, a gesture at growth zoning. They fail because they are a single pale tint on red rather than contrasting ochre/umber bands, and because they sit in the middle of the plate instead of forming a rim.
(4) Unmentioned and worth fixing: every blade has a thin dark hairline stroke that is DETACHED from the body, floating in the black just above and beyond the tip (clearly visible at 3x on all five). It reads as a stray path, not as a margin.
(5) Unmentioned: the tiers do not overlap. Each blade is separated from the next by a band of clean background, so even the 'overlapping tiers' half of must-read 1 is not met - only 'stacked up a trunk' survives.
(6) Unmentioned: ink bounding box is 281 wide x 343 tall = aspect 0.82, against the packet's specified aspect 1.5. The composition is taller than wide when it should be half again wider than tall.

The chassis charge is CONFIRMED and is the root cause. I opened Oyster_Mushroom.png and Turkey_Tail.png alongside. All three shelf-family assets are the same drawing: identical dark trunk bar at the same x and width, identical pointed-lens blades emanating rightward, identical internal double-arc marking, identical detached hairline above each tip. Only hue (tomato red / gold-amber / tan-brown) and blade count differ. This is exactly the 'one pony in twelve colours' failure the batch header warns about, and it means the packet's distinguishing note is unserved twice over: Shelf Fungus is not distinguishable from Bracket Fungus, and it is not distinguishable from its own two family siblings either.

Must-read scoring: 'several thin brackets stacked in overlapping tiers up a trunk' - PARTIAL (stacked up a trunk yes, overlapping no, brackets no). 'each shelf semicircular with a flat top and flat underside' - ABSENT (pointed lozenge). 'the stack stepping outward like a staircase' - ABSENT (measured, all flush at x=141). Specified colour - ABSENT. Two of three defining must-reads plus the whole colour spec are missing, so FAIL is the correct band and POLISH would be too generous.

Fix direction: replace the lens/blade primitive with a true half-disc - flat straight rear edge against the trunk, flat top plane, flat underside, semicircular outer margin, no point; make each successive plate down the trunk project further from the trunk so the stack steps outward; recolour to banded ochre/umber concentric zones on the top face with a distinctly paler buff underside visible on the lower plates; and remove the detached hairline strokes. Crucially, do this by giving the shelf family three genuinely different plate primitives (Shelf = thick-ish half-disc staircase, Oyster = fan with visible gills and a lateral stub stem, Turkey Tail = thin many-banded wavy fan rosettes), not by recolouring one shape three ways again.

rows.readsAs: two tiny generic tan toadstools
rows.defect: The identity must-read, the cracked cap surface showing white flesh through the fissures, is completely absent — the caps are smooth domes with faint radial streaks. The margin is not inrolled and carries a row of hard dots instead of a fringe of white veil remnants; the gills are implied only by that dot row, never shown; and the stem is a thin, smooth, straight white pin set centrally, not a tough fibrous off-centre stalk. Both subjects are rendered at about a seventh of the frame height, leaving most of the canvas empty.
rows.fix: Scale the pair up to fill the frame and cut a network of pale fissures across each cap so white flesh shows through the umber skin, then roll the cap margin under and hang a ragged white veil fringe from it.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4x and 12x zoom on the 440x440 PNG. VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

CORRECTION 1 - the white cap cracking is NOT 'completely absent'. Both caps carry white flesh marks. The right specimen has a clear starburst of ~8 thin cream slashes radiating from the cap apex down toward the margin; the left specimen has 4 sparser ones (one long stroke running down-left, a short vertical pair at the apex, one comma at the right shoulder). So the feature was attempted and is drawn. The real defect is its FORM: they are thin, tapered, brush-stroke RADIAL STREAKS - a sunburst / scratch pattern - not the shiitake's crazed tortoiseshell fissuring. Shiitake cracking is a network of irregular closed polygons (mud-crack / turtle-shell cells) with brown islands floating in white fissure lines, densest at the centre and fading to the margin, and the fissures are WIDE (white area comparable to brown area). Here the strokes never join, never enclose a cell, and cover under 10% of the cap. Fix = replace the radial stroke set with a crack NETWORK; do not add 'cracks' as if from nothing.

CORRECTION 2 - the margin band is not a 'dot row'. It is a straight horizontal cream slab across the whole cap underside with a row of ~14 evenly spaced DARK RECTANGULAR NOTCHES cut into its top edge - a machined dentil/castellation, identically pitched on both specimens. It is ambiguous by construction: it reads equally as gill teeth and as veil fringe, and therefore delivers neither. The judge's substantive point stands: the cap bottom is a hard straight line, there is zero inroll (no downward curl of the margin, no shadowed cavity under the rim), and the fringe is geometric rather than torn cottony veil scraps.

CORRECTION 3 - the scale claim is overstated. Measured subject bbox is x131-308, y173-251 = 178 x 79 px, i.e. 18.0% of frame height and 40.5% of width, roughly a FIFTH not a seventh. It is still a hard scale fail: the packet aspect is 1 (square) yet the drawn subject is 2.25:1 and floats in the upper-middle of the frame over ~82% empty background, so at card size the cap markings are sub-pixel and the thing reads as a generic brown toadstool.

WHAT IS GENUINELY MISSING (the fail case):
- Crowded white gills: absent entirely. The cap underside is a flat cream slab with one faint grey smudge where the stem meets it. No radiating gill lines, no gill depth, no shadow gradient from rim to stem.
- Tough fibrous off-centre stem: absent. Both stems are smooth flat cream columns, straight-sided with a single soft shading edge on the right, no vertical fibril striation, no shaggy/scurfy surface, no ring zone. Judge's 'thin white pins' is a mischaracterisation of thickness - the stems are ~20% of cap width and proportionate, not pins - but 'smooth' and 'central' are correct: left stem sits ~4px right of its cap centre, right stem ~5px left of its cap centre, i.e. jitter, not a deliberate off-centre stalk.
- Colour is acceptable (tea-brown cap, cream stem) and the cap dome shape is fine; the failure is all texture and structure.

NET: 1 of 4 must-reads partially present but drawn in the wrong idiom, 3 of 4 absent, plus a disqualifying scale/aspect miss. Reads as an anonymous cap-and-stem mushroom, not a shiitake.

rows.readsAs: a stinkhorn, or at a glance a pair of white candles with green tips
rows.defect: The tall pale pitted phallic stalks and the dark olive thimble heads do land the core read. But the stalk rises from a flat splayed disc foot, not from a white egg sac — the volva, which is half the described identity, is not drawn. The head is a flat matte olive shape with no glisten, no highlights and no drips, so it does not read as slime, and there are no flies on it at all. The stalk pitting is a few soft grey smudges rather than a spongy chambered texture.
rows.fix: Sit each stalk in a split white egg sac at the base, then repaint the head as wet olive-black slime with specular highlights and a drip or two at its rim, and add two or three small dark flies on and around it.

rows.readsAs: tan canoe hulls or dried leaves pinned to a dark post
rows.defect: Third use of the identical shelf chassis, this time in flat tan with six blades. The species IS its banding, and there is none: each blade is a single uniform tan gradient with one faint pale swoosh, so the many contrasting concentric rings of rust, ochre, blue-grey, cream and black are entirely absent, as is the pale cream wavy outer rim and any velvety surface. The blades are also large, few and pointed rather than dozens of small overlapping rosetted fans.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, with two corrections to the stated cause.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440): a flat dark-brown rectangle log running vertically down the left third (x~88-148, full height, no bark texture, no taper, no highlight), with SIX long lance/leaf-shaped blades attached along its right edge and projecting horizontally right. Each blade is ~190px long, ~55px tall, blunt at the log end and drawn to a sharp point at the free end, with a thin near-black hairline stroke along its lower/outer edge. The blades stack vertically and overlap slightly; the whole fruiting mass reads taller than wide (bbox roughly 190w x 305h). This is the same chassis as Shelf_Fungus.png in the same batch, which I opened side by side: identical log rectangle, identical pointed-blade geometry, identical interior arc marks, only the count (5 vs 6) and the hue (crimson vs tan) differ. So the "shared shelf chassis, recolored" part of the claim is confirmed by direct comparison.

CORRECTION 1 - the blades are NOT "one uniform gradient." I cropped x140-340, y190-320 and upscaled 4x nearest-neighbour, and sampled RGB scanlines at y=230/250/270. There ARE interior marks: two to three pale hairline arcs nested inside each blade, curving from the log end toward the tip. But they are hairlines, not bands - one to two pixels wide, and the scanline shows their amplitude is about +8 to +14 in R (e.g. ad8154 -> b28b62, then straight back to a87e51; 9a744c -> 9b7751). Hue is constant tan across every one of them. They read as gloss/contour scratches, not as rings. At full size they are effectively invisible. So the judge's verdict is right for a slightly different reason than stated: the banding is not ABSENT, it is present as three low-contrast single-hue hairlines where the must-read demands "many contrasting concentric rings" that "vary in hue as well as tone." The note's own failure condition ("a single-colour ringed bracket reads as a different species") is not merely met, it is undershot - this is a single-colour UNringed bracket.

CORRECTION 2 - the outer rim is not just missing the cream, it is the inverse. The scanline running outward along a blade decays monotonically from b98a59 at the log to 604a32 / 2d2419 at the tip, and the silhouette edge carries a near-black stroke. The pale cream wavy outer rim - the single most diagnostic band on a real Trametes versicolor - is replaced by the DARKEST value in the image. Fixing this needs a light-value rim, not just an added ring.

STILL ABSENT AND CORRECTLY CALLED: no velvety/tomentose surface (the fill is a clean linear gradient with zero grain or fibre); no white pore underside anywhere; no rosette - six large blades in a single vertical column instead of dozens of small overlapping fans; and the blade OUTLINE is pointed/lanceolate rather than the semicircular-to-kidney fan with a wavy lobed margin that the species requires. Colour hits none of the called palette: rust, blue-grey, cream and near-black are all missing, leaving only ochre.

Verdict: with no rings, no hue variation, no cream rim, no fan margin and no rosette, every element of the mustRead is failed. Nothing here distinguishes this asset from the crimson Shelf Fungus except its hue, which is exactly the substitutability the note warns about. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a grey speckled rock or a dust-covered stone
rows.defect: The same blob chassis as Mildew and Mold, recoloured beige with white specks. Yeast is defined by its cells and none are drawn: there are no rounded oval single cells, no smaller bud swelling off one side of any cell, no bud scars, and no loose cluster of a few cells. A single opaque lump reads as bulk paste at best, and the halo of specks reads as dust, not as cells.
rows.fix: Drop the blob and draw five or six translucent oval cells at large scale, each with a smaller round bud budding off one shoulder and a few ring-shaped bud scars pocking the wall, arranged as a loose unattached cluster.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, but several parts of the stated cause are wrong and the fix should be made against what is actually on the canvas. WHAT I SAW: one single connected opaque mass filling roughly x=102-334, y=117-308 (233x192 px, aspect 1.21 - already wider than the packet's aspect 1.0). I read the PNG at native size, then re-cropped and upscaled the body 3x and 6x, and re-read it at 2.6x brightness gain to hunt for faint linework. CORRECTION 1 - it is not a smooth 'blob'. The silhouette is a faceted convex POLYGON with visible straight chords: a long straight bevel across the upper left (approx. 150,150 to 200,130), a straight diagonal down the upper right, and a straight chord across the lower right. Plus a stray thin dark spur, about 3-4 px wide, poking off the right edge at approx. (334,205) - a loose polygon vertex, not a bud. The read is a pebble/asteroid, not a rounded cell. CORRECTION 2 - the speck layer is UNCLIPPED, which the claim does not mention and which is a separate, mechanical defect. I counted 149 bright pixels sitting on pure black background OUTSIDE the mass (e.g. a ~4px dot centred (216,117) at luminance 135 against a ring-average background of 16; another at (167,132)). The dots form a snow/dust halo floating around the silhouette. Whatever draws the specks is not masked to the body path. CORRECTION 3 - the colour is not 'beige'. Sampled fill measures RGB (93,90,76) to (103,100,84) across y=180/220/260 - a dark, desaturated olive-grey-buff. The packet asks for 'translucent pale cream to buff cells'; this is roughly half the intended value, fully opaque, with no translucency, no rim light and no subsurface glow. CONFIRMING THE ABSENCES (the claim is right on all three must-reads): (a) rounded oval single cells - none. There is not one cell outline, membrane edge or interior boundary anywhere on the mass, even with brightness pushed 2.6x; the interior is soft airbrushed cream blotches only. (b) a smaller bud swelling off one side - none. The vertical-extent-per-column profile is a single smooth hump (peak 157 px near x=198, tapering monotonically to 0 in both directions), so there is no second lobe, no neck, no waist anywhere on the outline. (c) bud scars pocking the cell wall - none. The white dots are CONVEX, hard-edged, uniform-brightness specks lying ON TOP of the surface; a bud scar must read as a concave ring/crater on a cell wall, and they are also scattered at random rather than gathered near one pole. (d) loose clusters of a few cells - none; one single connected mass, zero separate bodies. FIX DIRECTION: this needs to be rebuilt as 3-5 discrete translucent pale-cream ovals (each ~aspect 1.3, overlapping loosely, not fused into one outline), at least one carrying a smaller daughter oval budding off its flank with a visible constricted neck, and two or three concave darker-rimmed ring scars on the parent walls. The current asset shares no geometry with that.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of red-orange medicine capsules on black
rows.defect: Nothing of the acid-mine habitat is drawn: the field is dark navy-black, not rust-red iron-stained water; there is no orange iron precipitate flocking the cells and no corroded mineral or pyrite grains anywhere. The colour is also inverted from the reference — the cells are painted red-orange while the reference calls them colourless in red water. The rods are chunky, not 'very small slender'. Strip the hue and this is byte-for-byte the Cryophile/Halophile/Methanogen rod field.
rows.fix: Flood the field with turbid rust-red acid water and hang orange ferric floc and angular pyrite grains through it, then draw the rods small, slender and near-colourless so the water carries the colour, not the cells.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, and the pixel data proves it harder than the original claim did. WHAT I SAW: 11 identical capsule rods (measured blobs ~60-100px long x ~24px wide on a 440px field, aspect ~3) scattered at random rotations, each with the same soft top-left specular sheen and the same faint mid-rod septum tick, floating on an empty gradient. Nothing else is in the frame. MUST-READ AUDIT (packet row: aspect 2.2, 'colourless small rods in orange-red iron-stained acid water'): (1) 'very small slender rods scattered in a rust-red fluid' — HALF present: the rods are there and are slender, but they are drawn large, not 'very small', and the fluid is not rust-red; (2) 'orange iron precipitate flocking around the cells' — ABSENT, zero floc; (3) 'corroded mineral grains and pyrite fragments nearby' — ABSENT, zero non-rod blobs anywhere above 40px. Two of three must-reads are entirely missing and they are the two that carry the acid-mine-drainage identity. PROOF THE HABITAT IS ABSENT, NOT MERELY FAINT: I re-decoded the PNG and gamma-boosted it 1/3.2 to lift the shadows, then looked again. The lifted field is a perfectly clean blue-grey radial vignette with the 11 rods on it — no particulate, no grain, no wash, no texture of any kind. Background corner samples are RGB 5/6/12 rising to ~9/15/21 at centre, and those samples are BIT-IDENTICAL to Cryophile, Halophile, Methanogen and Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria. This is the shared microbe backdrop with nothing painted over it. CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (all of these matter for scoping the fix): (a) 'dark navy' is generous — it is near-black desaturated blue-black, not a navy anyone would read as water; (b) the colour-inversion charge is CORRECT and is the sharpest single defect: the reference wants colourless cells suspended in orange-red water, and the asset delivers strongly saturated vermilion cells (peak rod bucket ~RGB 208/64/32) in colourless water. The hue is on exactly the wrong object; (c) 'strip the hue and it is the same rod field' is right about the CHASSIS but wrong about the FIELD. The rod scatter is re-rolled per species — Acidophile has 11 rods in its own arrangement, Cryophile 7 clusters, Halophile 5, Nitrogen-Fixing 11, all in different positions. What is shared is the drawing vocabulary (identical capsule primitive, identical sheen, identical septum, identical background), not a copy-pasted layout. Do not fix this by re-randomising positions; that is already random and it changes nothing. FAMILY CONTEXT THAT ARGUES AGAINST LENIENCY: Iron-Oxidizing Bacteria in the same batch shows the engine can do more — ribbed stalk sheaths with holdfast beads, 7017 distinct RGB values versus Acidophile's 1951 (second-lowest in the family after Methanogen's 1555). Acidophile is among the least-rendered assets in its own batch, so the missing habitat is not a platform limitation. VERDICT: with the packet in hand this asset is indistinguishable from Halophile or Nitrogen-Fixing except by hue, and the hue it does carry is applied to the wrong element. It does not read as an acidophile; it reads as generic rod bacteria. FIX DIRECTION: desaturate the rods toward colourless/pale translucent, move the orange-red into the surrounding fluid as a rust wash, add ochre iron floc haloing the cells, and drop a few angular dark mineral grains with metallic pyrite glints into the field.

rows.readsAs: a smooth grey egg or a teardrop-shaped stone
rows.defect: It has no pseudopods at all — the outline is a clean convex egg with one small pointed nub on the right, no blunt finger-like lobes anywhere, which is the single feature that makes an amoeba an amoeba. The interior is a smooth airbrushed gradient with no granular texture, and no clear ectoplasmic rim reads against it. One dark nucleus and two faint pale circles are present but sit in an otherwise featureless blob.
rows.fix: Break the outline with three or four fat blunt lobopodia of unequal length pushing out asymmetrically in one direction of flow, and give the endoplasm visible grain inside a clear hyaline rim.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated cause. I decoded the PNG and scanned the silhouette row by row as well as looking at 4x and 8x crops.

SILHOUETTE (the fatal defect, confirmed): the body is one closed blob, bbox 110,107 to 329,323 (220x217 px, aspect 1.01 vs the spec's 1.2). Row extents widen strictly monotonically from y=107 (span 17) to y=221 (span 219) and then narrow strictly monotonically to y=317. There is not one re-entrant bay anywhere on the left, top or bottom edge. So the first must-read - 'a shapeless blob throwing out blunt finger-like pseudopods' - is genuinely absent. There are ZERO lobopods.

CORRECTION 1 to the claim: the single protrusion is NOT 'one small nub'. It is a large, hard-edged TRIANGULAR WEDGE on the right side - two straight edges running from roughly (300,180) and (293,281) to a sharp vertex at (329,221), about 30 px of overhang and about 100 px of base. It is a pointed beak/teardrop tail with a hard corner, the opposite shape family from a lobopod (which is a rounded, blunt, cylinder-ended finger). This matters for the fix: the correction is not 'add more nubs', it is 'delete the wedge and rebuild the outline from 3-5 rounded blunt lobes of unequal length, one leading and asymmetric, mid-flow'. The packet note warns against a neat symmetric star of arms; this asset errs the opposite direction - no arms at all.

CORRECTION 2: the claim says there is no hyaline rim, which is right in substance, but it omits that there IS a 1-2 px bright hairline stroke tracing the ENTIRE perimeter (edge pixels reach grey ~167 against a body of ~74-137). That hairline is an outline stroke, not a hyaline rim, and it actively hurts: it makes the cell read as a hard-shelled cartoon decal rather than a soft translucent one. The fix is a wide (roughly 8-15 px) lighter clear ectoplasmic band set INSIDE the edge, with the hairline removed or dropped to near the body value.

INTERIOR (confirmed, and measured): the fill is a single smooth radial airbrush, highlight centred around (175,190), grey range 23-167. Over a 70x120 interior patch the Laplacian median is 1 (p99 = 7, max 19) and the adjacent-pixel difference median is 1 (p99 = 3). That is zero high-frequency content - no granules, no endoplasm/ectoplasm split, no crystals, no food vacuoles. The second must-read ('a clear outer rim around a granular grainy interior') is absent on BOTH halves.

IN THE ASSET'S FAVOUR (the judge did not mention this, and it is real): the THIRD must-read is substantially met. There is a clean round nucleus - a solid dark disc, grey ~43, about 55 px across, centred near (243,215) - and three pale translucent circles that can be read as vacuoles: a large one at ~(215,180) overlapping the nucleus, a small one at ~(222,250), and a large one at ~(268,265). I checked the last one for a clipping bug because it visually appears to cross the lower-right edge; it does not - every pixel outside the outline on rows y=246..300 measures background (8,12,18) identical to the control rows, so the organelles are correctly clipped. No spill defect exists.

GESTALT: a smooth grey ovoid + one solid near-black round 'eye' + a pointed beak on the right reads as a cartoon fish or bird head, or a comma/teardrop - not an amoeba. Two of the three must-reads are missing, and the missing one is the identity feature. FAIL stands.

FIX ORDER: (1) rebuild the outline as 3-5 unequal rounded lobopods with one leading pseudopod and a trailing uroid, no straight edges and no hard vertices; (2) add a granular endoplasm - many small overlapping specks/vesicles of varied size and value - inside a clear hyaline band; (3) keep the nucleus but lift it off near-black so it stops reading as an eye, and keep exactly one crisply-outlined circular contractile vacuole rather than three ambiguous pale discs.

rows.readsAs: four Euglena — teardrop cells with long whipping flagella and red eyespots
rows.defect: This is the wrong organism: pointed teardrop cells each trailing one long sinuous whip-flagellum and carrying a bright red eyespot is the textbook Euglena read, not a buoyant balloon cell with a stout trailing tentacle from a cleft. The required large near-spherical buoyant cells are absent, the cleft and stout tentacle are absent, and the emitted colour is mint green-teal — the note explicitly forbids green and demands cold blue-cyan. There is no sparking/flash quality; the cells simply glow flat.
rows.fix: Redraw as fat translucent near-spherical balloons with a single short stout tentacle emerging from a cleft, and swap the emission to a cold cyan-blue flash that blooms off the cells into the surrounding water.
rows.verifyWhy:
I looked hard for the balloon/cleft/tentacle in case they were small or placed oddly, and cropped the bottom-right cell to 4x to check the silhouette edge. They are not there. The canvas (440x440, near-black navy field) holds FOUR cells, all identical in construction, scattered on a loose diagonal. Each cell is a smooth lens/spindle roughly 55x105px (~1:2 elongation), NOT near-spherical and not balloon-like: it is pointed at BOTH ends - a narrow apex where the filament emerges and a tapering blunt posterior point. (Minor correction to the FAIL claim: 'pointed teardrop' undersells it; a teardrop is round at one end, these are leaf/spindle shapes pointed at both, which is even further from the required sphere.) From that apex runs a HAIRLINE filament, ~2px wide and about 1.5x the cell length, drawn as a sinuous S/W wave - unmistakably a whip flagellum, not the required 'single stout trailing tentacle'. The 4x crop shows the apex as a clean continuous curve: there is NO cleft, notch, girdle, groove or sulcus anywhere on the outline; the filament simply sprouts from an unbroken tip. So mustRead #1 (large near-spherical translucent buoyant balloon cells) and mustRead #2 (stout trailing tentacle from a cleft) are both wholly absent, not merely small.

COLOUR, measured not eyeballed. Sampled cell-body pixels: (228,165) R144 G253 B245; (133,255) R145 G253 B245; (262,350) R146 G254 B247; midtones (175,175) R120 G214 B203 and (140,270) R95 G175 B159; brightest pixel on the canvas (124,254) R177 G250 B241. Green exceeds blue in EVERY sample; computed hue runs ~168-176 degrees, i.e. mint/aquamarine on the GREEN side of cyan (180). Cold electric blue would sit ~200-230. The judge's 'mint green-teal' is accurate and the note ('The glow is blue-cyan, never green') is violated outright. Two further colour/light misses the FAIL did not name: (a) the spec's translucent PINK-GREY cell body is nowhere - the bodies are flat saturated mint with a faint grey nuclear smudge and a lighter rim highlight, no pink, no grey cast; (b) mustRead #3 fails on BEHAVIOUR as well as hue - there is no sparking at all. No halo, no scattered flash points, no bloom into the surrounding water; the cells are evenly self-lit fills with only a thin edge glow, reading as continuous shine, which the note explicitly contrasts against 'flashes on agitation'.

EACH cell also carries one solid red-orange oval (~14px) set in the anterior-middle third - a textbook Euglena stigma/eyespot, which nothing in the packet asks for and which actively pushes the read toward the wrong organism. The judge's 'red eyespot' call is correct and correctly located.

Secondary miss not in the original claim: scale is specified 'field of many' and only four widely-spaced cells are drawn, so even the population density under-reads.

Net: the target is Noctiluca scintillans - a big translucent buoyant sphere with a ventral cleft and one thick tentacle, flashing cold blue. What is drawn is a Euglena/spermatozoid chassis: elongated mint-green spindle, hairline sinuous flagellum, red stigma, continuous green glow. Every one of the three must-reads is absent and the note's one explicit prohibition is broken. FAIL upheld; the claim was substantially correct on every point I could test.

FIX DIRECTION: replace the spindle+flagellum chassis with large near-spherical translucent cells (aspect ~1, soft rim-lit membrane so they read buoyant), cut a visible V-cleft into the lower edge of each and hang ONE thick tapering tentacle (many times the flagellum's width, short and stout, not a whip) from inside that cleft; delete the red eyespot entirely; re-hue the emission to cold electric blue (B channel must clearly lead G, ~205-225 deg) over pink-grey translucent bodies; and give the light a sparking read - a few bright flash points and blue scatter in the surrounding water rather than an even fill. Also raise the count so it reads as a field.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of pale blue medicine capsules on black
rows.defect: The ice is entirely missing — no faceted ice-crystal boundaries frame the field and no thin liquid brine veins hold the cells, so the one cue that distinguishes a cryophile from any other rod is absent. The only surviving must-read is the blue-white cast, which is delivered purely by tinting the identical rod chassis shared with Acidophile, Halophile, Methanogen and Nitrogen-Fixing.

What is actually on the canvas: 13 pale blue-white capsule rods, aspect ~2, opaque with a soft top-left specular highlight, scattered freely across a 440x440 frame on a near-black radial vignette. Two rods (the long one upper-right, one bottom-centre) carry a faint transverse septum line; three pairs meet at V/T junctions. That is the entire image.

The rods are not trapped or confined by anything; they float in wide open black gaps, which is the opposite of the required reading (cells squeezed into narrow interstitial brine channels).

MUST-READ 2 - 'faceted ice crystal boundaries framing the cells': ABSENT, confirmed instrumentally. The background is a pure smooth radial gradient - corner pixels sample (5,6,12), centre-top (7,10,16) - and a Sobel map amplified 20x shows only concentric 8-bit quantisation rings from that gradient. Zero straight lines, zero polygonal junctions, zero triple points. The only edges in the whole image are the 13 rod outlines. So the judge's phrasing is exactly right: the ice is not faint or subtle, it was never drawn.

MUST-READ 3 - 'a cold blue-white cast over the whole field': PARTIAL, and this is the one place the judge's wording needs correcting. The cast is not entirely gone - the cells themselves are genuinely pale blue-white. And crucially the tint does not do identity work, because Methanogen in this same packet (family rod, colour 'pale grey-lilac') is rendered in an almost indistinguishable pale grey-blue on the identical chassis. Secondary: the colour line asks for 'translucent, near colourless'; these rods are opaque solids with a plastic-capsule shading model, no light passing through and no substrate visible behind them.

Two of three must-reads - the two that carry the cryophile identity, the brine veins and the faceted ice - are wholly absent, so the FAIL stands. The fix is environmental, not cellular: build the ice matrix first (faceted polygonal crystal plates meeting at triple junctions, with a network of narrow brighter brine channels along the boundaries) and then seat the rods inside those channels so they read as confined; the rod chassis itself is fine and does not need re-derivation.

rows.readsAs: a schematic line drawing of a pennate diatom, or a lined leaf

The 'interlocking polygonal plates' are wheel sectors, not the irregular tessellated thecal plates of a dinoflagellate, and the render is thin gold linework with no armour substance.

The interior fill is a smooth radial glow gradient (bright yellow core fading to dark brown at the rim) with no plate faces, no bevel, no suture relief, no thickness. Measured silhouette bbox is x 87-352, y 87-352 = 266 x 266 px, aspect w/h = 1.000.

One nuance the judge did not mention and a fixer needs to know: two of the 16 spokes lie exactly on the horizontal midline (one left, one right of centre), and at thumbnail size those two collinear strokes can be misread as a girdle. They are not - they are ordinary radial spokes of the same family, they run inward to the hub rather than around the cell, and they are drawn in the identical hairline as the other 14. Do not 'fix' this by thickening them; the groove has to be a belt with two edges and a shaded channel that visibly cinches the silhouette.

But they are annular sectors tiled uniformly around a single centre - the pattern of a centric test, not an armour of interlocking plates with distinct apical / precingular / postcingular series and asymmetric suture lines. So mustRead 1 is half-drawn and reads as the wrong structure. Colour is roughly on brief (amber/olive-brown) but the linework carries no armour substance, which the judge got right.

ONE PART OF THE CLAIM TO CORRECT: 'reads as a centric diatom' collides with nothing in this batch - Diatom.png here is drawn as a pennate boat with a raphe and transverse striae, a completely different and quite good asset. The wrong-organism collision is specifically with Radiolarian, not with the diatom.

Egg/top silhouette at ~0.8 w/h; a deep transverse girdle belting the equator, drawn as two edges with a shaded recess that pinches the outline; a shorter sulcus groove running down the hypotheca from the girdle; the theca tessellated into irregular interlocking polygons with raised sutures (apical series above the girdle, postcingular below), not a radial hub-and-spoke; a transverse flagellum shown as a ribbon curled inside the girdle and a longitudinal flagellum trailing from the sulcus past the silhouette edge.

Every one of those is a ciliate organelle and is pixel-for-pixel in the same place in Paramecium.png. Deleting the cilia alone would still leave a ciliate. (b) 'literally this batch's Paramecium recoloured green' is not exact — the cilia are individually jittered differently, so it is the same generator/chassis with a different seed, not a copied file. (c) the cilia are drawn as a dense, fairly long fringe (~10-18px spikes) around 100%% of the rim, which additionally makes the surface read as ciliated rather than as Euglena's smooth striated pellicle — worth saying because Euglena should have NO surface fringe at all, not a shorter one. rows.readsAs: a foraminiferan shell, though the halo reads as a sun-animalcule's spines

The shell walls show no pores, and the colour is a pale mint-green rather than chalky white or honey calcite.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of hot-pink medicine capsules on black
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The cells are not densely crowded — there are about nine sparse rods with large empty gaps, so the field is not stained pink by their density; the brine around them is flat near-black navy. There are no angular salt crystals anywhere. No cells are flattened into squares or plates; every one is the same rounded capsule used by Acidophile, Cryophile, Methanogen and Nitrogen-Fixing. It is that identical rod chassis with the hue dialled to magenta, and it is barely separable from Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria, which is the same pink at lower saturation.
rows.fix: Pack the frame edge-to-edge with cells so the brine itself glows hot pink from their sheer density, scatter angular halite crystals through the liquid, and flatten a proportion of the cells into irregular square plates.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld. I tried hard to refute it — decoded the PNG, ran a connected-component analysis on the pink mask, and gamma-lifted the whole field to 0.30 to hunt for low-contrast crystals hidden in the shadows. Nothing survives for the defence.

WHAT IS THERE: roughly 11 rods (not 'about nine' — the judge undercounted slightly), every one the identical capsule primitive: straight shaft, hemispherical cap at each end, same diagonal specular highlight stripe. They sit in only 4 connected clumps — a 5-rod tangle upper-left (bbox 72,54-204,201), a 4-rod tangle lower-centre (110,289-258,385), and two lone rods (227,94 and 303,319). Pink ink covers 7.14% of the 440x440 canvas. An 8x8 occupancy grid has the entire top row, entire bottom row, the whole middle band (row 5), and both outer columns completely empty. So the 'big gaps' characterisation is correct and if anything understated: the centre and the entire right half are void.

MUST-READ 1 — 'densely crowded rods staining the whole field hot pink': FAIL. 7% coverage is a scatter, not a crowd, and the density-tinting the packet note specifically calls for ('the brine should be tinted by their density, not dyed') cannot happen at that spacing.

CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE ON THE BRINE: they said 'flat black'. It is worse than flat black — it is flat BLUE-black. Mean background RGB over all non-cell pixels is (7.2, 10.0, 16.1): the BLUE channel is the highest of the three. The field is tinted the opposite hue from the one the identity requires. Under an extreme gamma lift it resolves as a smooth cool blue-grey vignette with a faint noise dither and nothing else. Critically, this exact value (7.2, 10.1, 16.1) is also the mean background of Nitrogen-Fixing_Bacteria.png — it is a shared, entirely unmodified backdrop, not a brine that was drawn and then under-tinted.

MUST-READ 2 — 'angular salt crystals scattered through the brine': ABSENT. Confirmed by measurement, not eyeballing: the pink-mask component list returns exactly 4 components and ZERO components under 40px, i.e. there are no small scattered objects of any kind. At gamma 0.30 (a lift that would expose anything above ~2/255) the empty field shows no straight edges, no facets, no cubes, no rhombs. The judge is right.

MUST-READ 3 — 'some cells flattened into irregular squares or plates': ABSENT. Component bounding boxes are all elongated capsule forms (e.g. 65x25, 57x75 for a crossed pair); nothing is square, nothing is a plate. At 3x magnification every element is unmistakably the same rounded-cap rod. FAIL.

ONE FEATURE THE JUDGE MISSED (does not rescue it): at 3x, several rods carry a thin transverse septum line across the shaft — clearly visible on the right-hand vertical rod in the upper cluster and on two rods in the lower cluster. That is a real drawn detail, a binary-fission division line. But it is a generic bacterial cue, not a halophile cue, and it does not stand in for crystals or plates.

CONFUSOR CLAIM — CONFIRMED AND STRONGER THAN STATED. Halophile and Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria share family 'rod', share aspect 2.2, share the identical capsule chassis, and share a pixel-identical backdrop. The ONLY separator is hue: Halophile's rods are saturated magenta, NFB's are desaturated salmon. Worse, NFB is the DENSER and better-distributed of the two — 11 separate components spread across most of its occupancy grid versus Halophile's 4 clumps — so Halophile loses its own defining 'densely crowded' must-read to the very species it is supposed to be distinguished from.

FIX DIRECTION: the rod chassis itself is fine and does not need re-deriving. What is missing is (a) 4-6x more rods, packed and overlapping so they fill the frame edge to edge with no void quadrants; (b) a warm magenta wash on the brine itself, driven by cell density — brightest where rods pile up, so the black field becomes stained pink rather than staying blue-black; (c) a scatter of small angular hard-edged salt crystals (cubes/rhombs with straight facets and specular corners, deliberately NOT capsules) through the gaps; (d) a handful of cells swapped from rods to flattened irregular square plates. Items (b), (c) and (d) are the three things that would make this stop reading as Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria with the saturation turned up.

rows.readsAs: orange segmented worms or noodles — a recoloured copy of this batch's Cyanobacteria
rows.defect: The defining structure is absent: there is no bean-shaped cell trailing a long twisted ribbon stalk. What is drawn is four evenly stacked horizontal filaments each with a sphere at its midpoint and ladder hatching along it — the identical construction used for Cyanobacteria, orange instead of teal. Nothing mats into ochre sludge; the background is the same empty navy. And the note's specific warning is violated head-on: the rust colour is painted onto the whole cell body rather than onto a secreted stalk.
rows.fix: Draw a small pale near-colourless bean cell at the tip of each element with a long rust-crusted twisted ribbon stalk streaming behind it, and let the stalks tangle into a matted ochre sludge instead of floating in a void.

Each tube is one continuous smooth cylinder with a rounded cap at both ends. Each carries a single sphere sitting ON the tube at roughly its MIDPOINT (not at an end) - spheres at approx (185,100), (305,175), (195,268), (243,325). Each tube is split into two halves by that sphere: the half on one side is bright saturated orange with a specular top highlight and is crossed by ~10-12 straight transverse hatch ticks perpendicular to the tube axis (classic septa / cell-division rungs); the half on the other side is a plain darker brown tube with a pale highlight line and NO hatching. Nothing else is in the frame - no substrate, no mat, no particulate, no haze. The bottom 100px band is uniform dark navy.

MUST-READ 1 - 'a bean-shaped cell trailing a long twisted ribbon stalk behind it': ABSENT. I looked hard for a small bean at the strand ends; every end is a plain rounded cylinder cap, and at 4x the top-left cap is just the tube's own hemispherical terminus. The only candidate cell-like body is the midpoint sphere, and it fails on three counts: it is a perfect sphere, not a bean/kidney; it sits mid-filament with tube on BOTH sides, so nothing 'trails behind' it; and it is the same rust orange as the tube. The stalk is equally absent: the tubes have zero helical twist - the hatch marks are straight perpendicular rungs, not the diagonal/chevron banding a twisted ribbon would produce, and the tube silhouette has no ribbon edge, no flatness, no torsion.

MUST-READ 2 - 'the stalk crusted in rust-coloured iron oxide': not readable, because there is no stalk/cell distinction to hang the crust on. The rust is a smooth glossy gradient on a clean-edged tube; nothing reads as encrustation or accreted mineral.

MUST-READ 3 - 'stalks matting into an orange ochre sludge': ABSENT, as claimed. The four strands are evenly spaced, parallel, non-touching, and non-crossing, and the background is flat dark navy with no ochre wash whatsoever.

NOTE VIOLATION ('the rust colour belongs to the secreted stalk, not to the cell body'): confirmed violated, but state it precisely - it is not that a correct cell got mis-tinted; there is only ONE body in the drawing and the entire thing, sphere included, is painted rust orange to brown. The spec's 'cells themselves near-colourless' has no representative on canvas at all.

CORRECTION 1 to the claim: it is not literally the Cyanobacteria file recoloured. Side-by-side with earth-microbe/Cyanobacteria.png, that image has FIVE tubes including a crossing X pair in the middle band, with four spheres; this one has FOUR tubes, no crossings, four spheres, and a different curvature set. So it is the same shared filament-chassis primitive re-run with a different seed and an orange ramp, not the identical drawing. The judge's structural point stands - the construction, the mid-filament sphere, and the ladder hatch are the same chassis - but the file is not a straight recolour.

CORRECTION 2 to the claim: 'ladder hatch' should be recorded as running over only about half of each tube (the segment on one side of the sphere), not the full length. This matters for the fix, because that half-hatched tube plus a mid-filament sphere is precisely the Cyanobacteria must-read ('beaded chains of identical cells strung end to end · occasional larger paler cells set into the chain'), so the current drawing actively asserts the WRONG species identity rather than merely omitting features.

BAND: FAIL. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent and the third is unrepresentable; the asset reads as an orange cyanobacterial filament, not as a stalked iron-oxidizer. The fix is a redraw of the primitive, not a tint: kill the septa hatching and the mid-filament bead, put a small pale bean-shaped cell at ONE END of each strand, make the trailing element a helically twisted flat ribbon (visible torsion/edge flips along its length) rendered in crusty rust, and let several ribbons tangle and merge into an ochre sludge mat behind them.
