Both the bubble stream and the anoxic sediment substrate have to be authored from nothing, and the body colour has to be pulled off Cryophile's blue toward grey-lilac, before this reads as a methanogen at all.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of salmon-pink capsules on black — the Halophile image at lower saturation
rows.defect: The root nodule is missing entirely: there is no host tissue, no enclosing nodule wall and no leghaemoglobin pink flush around the cells — the surround is the same empty navy as every other asset, so the pink appears on the rods instead of in the tissue, which inverts the reference. The cells are loosely scattered rather than densely packed inside anything. The swollen irregular Y-shaped bacteroids are absent; the couple of Y shapes visible are just two plain rods crossing at a corner, same rounded capsule as everywhere else.
rows.fix: Enclose the whole field in salmon-pink nodule tissue with the rods packed tight inside it, and mix in genuinely swollen, branched, club-headed Y bacteroids among the plain rods.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 master at 1x, at 3x nearest-neighbour, at 7x bicubic on the two rod junctions, and at 6x brightness gain to hunt for faint background structure. What is actually on the canvas: 13 salmon-pink capsules, all struck from one identical primitive (uniform width end to end, hemispherical caps, one white specular sweep down the long axis, a soft dark contact shadow), scattered loosely across the frame at roughly 12 percent coverage with large empty gaps. Nothing else is drawn. All three must-reads fail.

MUST-READ 1 'short rods packed densely inside a plant root nodule' - ABSENT on all three counts. There is no nodule: no host tissue, no enclosing wall, no cortical boundary, no vascular strand, not even a soft containing envelope. The rods are also not dense (13 cells with wide black gulfs between them, not a packed interior) and not short - I measured the bottom-left horizontal rod at about 65 x 17 px, an aspect near 3.8:1, against the packet's stated aspect 2.2 and the word 'short'. So even the plain-rod baseline is off-spec before the nodule is considered.

MUST-READ 2 'swollen irregular Y-shaped bacteroid forms among the plain rods' - ABSENT. I confirm the judge on the substance and sharpen the count: there are TWO junctions, not one. Upper-left (approx x30-160, y120-230) two separate whole capsules overlap at their lower ends into a V. Centre (approx x180-320, y155-285) three-to-four capsules cross into a loose X/K. At 7x both resolve as plain capsules merely laid over one another - each keeps its own rounded cap and its own constant girth right through the overlap; there is no swelling, no club or pear taper, no branch emerging from a single cell body. Zero of the 13 cells differs in width or silhouette from the other 12, so there is no 'among the plain rods' contrast at all. One thing the judge did not mention that a fixer must know: several rods carry a thin dark transverse line at midpoint. That is a fission septum, and at thumbnail size it can be mistaken for a feature that is doing the bacteroid work. It is not - it reads as binary division and should not be counted as credit.

MUST-READ 3 'the surrounding nodule flushed pink' - INVERTED, and worse than a simple omission. The judge said the pink lands on the rods instead of the tissue, which is correct, but the backdrop is not neutral. At 6x gain the background resolves as a blue-grey radial vignette: corner pixels RGB 5,6,12; brightest background region 9,14,20 - blue dominant, B > G > R everywhere in the field. So the canvas actively pushes cool blue exactly where leghaemoglobin should be flushing warm. The colour spec is doubly inverted: it calls for pale CREAM rods inside SALMON-PINK tissue, and the render gives salmon-pink rods (edge sample 49,30,39, core reading as a mid salmon) on cold blue nothing. Cream appears nowhere in the image.

I also verified the Halophile comparison directly rather than taking it on trust, and it is accurate and in fact understated. Halophile.png is not merely similar - it is the same generator: the same scatter of plain uniform capsules with the same specular sweep and the same dark radial vignette, differing only in hue (hot magenta vs salmon) and in count. This is not 'reads like a desaturation', it is a demonstrable hue swap on a shared rod-family chassis. Halophile's own must-reads (salt crystals, whole-field staining, flattened square plates) are likewise missing from it, which is consistent with one untailored rod primitive serving the whole microbe rod family.

Verdict: the asset carries none of the three identity cues. Stripped of the filename it reads as generic pink bacilli, indistinguishable from the neighbouring Halophile. FAIL upheld. Fix order: (1) draw the nodule first - a warm salmon-pink host-tissue field with a defined wall filling most of the frame, the pink belonging to the tissue not the cells; (2) restate the rods as pale cream, shortened to aspect ~2.2, packed densely inside that field; (3) add three or four genuinely swollen, irregular, branching Y and club bacteroids among them so the contrast against the plain rods is visible at thumbnail size; (4) kill the blue vignette, which fights the leghaemoglobin cue.

rows.readsAs: a ciliate — probably a paramecium, from the all-over cilia fringe
rows.defect: The cilia fringe is present and well drawn and the ciliate read lands, but the outline is a plain symmetric ellipse: there is no asymmetric slipper or shoe profile, no blunt anterior against a narrower tapered posterior, so the shape that names this species is missing. The oral groove is reduced to a short straight tick beside the centre and does not read as a diagonal groove cutting into the cell side. The khaki-olive tint is duller than the pale grey-green called for, and the body is the same ellipse used for this batch's Euglena.
rows.fix: Reshape the outline into a true asymmetric slipper — broad rounded front, narrowing tapered rear, one flank straighter than the other — and cut a clear diagonal oral groove running back from the front into the side with denser cilia lining it.

rows.readsAs: a long branching chain of lemon-yellow beads - a streptococcus chain or a bent bead necklace
rows.defect: The signature is a flat packet of EXACTLY FOUR spheres and the packet note says a chain reads as something else entirely - what is drawn is roughly 25 spheres in a Y-shaped, three-armed chain. Colour is wrong too: bright lemon-yellow, not salmon pink to red-orange. And there is no heavy layered envelope rim on any cell; each sphere is a plain glossy ball with a soft dark edge, the same bead used inside the Sulfur-Oxidizing filaments.
rows.fix: Draw four spheres only, in a 2x2 flat packet with the cells pressed flat against each other, recoloured salmon-to-red-orange, each ringed by a thick double-line envelope so the wall is visibly several times heavier than the cell outlines elsewhere in the family.
rows.verifyWhy: I looked hard for a way to refute this and could not. VERIFIED COUNT (not eyeballed): I thresholded the specular highlights and ran a connected-component pass — 26 discrete highlight blobs, one per sphere, areas 60-209px, no other blobs. So the drawing is 26 cocci, not four. The judge's 'roughly 25' is accurate; call it 26. LAYOUT: they are strung as a branched filament, not a packet. Reading the 2x upscale: a five-sphere near-horizontal run across the upper left (x~65-215, y~125); a junction at its left end from which a six-sphere chain descends to the lower left; a second junction near (120,225) feeding a six/seven-sphere chain that runs left-to-right along the bottom left and terminates in a short two-sphere spur pointing down-right; and from the RIGHT end of the top run, a long unbroken ten-to-twelve-sphere diagonal sweeping down to the lower right corner (ending ~(370,315)). Two clear branch points, three to four arms — the judge's 'three-armed branching chain' is a fair description of the silhouette. There is nowhere in the frame a readable sub-group of exactly four in a flat 2x2 square; every cluster is either a linear run of five-plus or a junction of three arms. This is precisely the failure the packet note warns against verbatim: 'a lone sphere or a long chain reads as something else entirely.' What it actually reads as is a streptococcus/staphylococcus chain, or — worse inside this batch — as the yellow sulfur granules of #5 Sulfur-Oxidizing Bacteria, whose reference row literally specifies 'bright lemon-yellow sulfur globules'. COLOUR: sampled, not guessed. The dominant bright-pixel buckets are 224,192,64 / 192,160,32 / 160,128,32 / 128,96,32 / 224,160,64 — hue ~42-48 degrees, i.e. goldenrod-amber with brown-gold shadow. There is not one pixel in the salmon-to-red-orange band (hue ~5-15) anywhere in the frame. The judge's 'bright yellow' is right in substance; I'd refine it to saturated goldenrod/amber rather than lemon, but it is nowhere near pink-red. ENVELOPE RIM — the one place worth correcting the judge's phrasing: at 9x zoom on a single cell each sphere is NOT bare. It carries a soft radial gradient plus a thin pale arc (about 1-2px at native scale) along its upper-left limb. But that arc is a light-source rim highlight, present only on the lit side and absent on the shadowed lower-right limb — it is not a wall. There is no closed band of differing value ringing the cell, no concentric layering, and nothing that reads as an unusually thick envelope; the cells look like plain glossy plastic beads. So the must-read 'an unusually thick layered cell envelope drawn as a heavy rim' is genuinely absent, and the judge is right, but a fixer should know the render already has a rim-light channel to work with — the fix is to add a closed, full-circumference multi-value envelope band, not to add lighting from scratch. NET: of three must-reads, the tetrad is absent (fatal on its own per the note), the heavy layered envelope is absent, and the glossy sheen is the only one present — and it is present in the wrong hue. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a radar sweep screen, or a red dartboard/wheel - a flat UI graphic, not an organism
rows.defect: It is a flat 2-D wireframe: one circle outline, three concentric rings and twelve straight spokes, filled with a red radial glow. Not one spine crosses the outer circle, so the defining halo of long fine radiating needles is entirely absent - the silhouette is a plain unbroken disc. The shell reads as red-on-black rather than clear glassy silica, there is no nested inner shell, and the 'dark central capsule' is a soft glow rather than a body. Nothing about it is three-dimensional or glassy.
rows.fix: Push a few dozen long straight needles out well past the shell so the silhouette is a spiked star, and rebuild the sphere as a lattice of hexagonal holes shaded to read as glass, with a small opaque dark capsule visible through it at the centre.
rows.verifyWhy:
I tried to refute this and could not; the FAIL stands, and the judge's geometry is accurate down to the counts. What is on the 440x440 canvas: a hard-edged crimson disc centred at (220,220). Pixel-measured structure -- FOUR concentric circles at r=32, r=65, r=98 and the outer rim at r=132-134, plus EXACTLY 12 straight spokes on a perfect 30-degree pitch (measured crossings at 0/29.5/59.75/90/119.75/149.75/180/209.75/239.75/269.5/299.25/329.25 deg, identical set at r=60 and r=120). That is a polar/radar grid, not an organism. The judge said 'three concentric rings and twelve spokes over one circle' -- correct on every number.

SPINES: absent, and I verified this the hard way rather than by eye. A 180-angle radial sweep returns an outer ink radius of 132-135 px at EVERY angle (variance under 3 px, i.e. antialias jitter only). A whole-image scan for any pixel with R>=10 gives a maximum radius of 134 with a hard cliff (counts per radius ring: 132->848 px, 133->546, 134->110, 135->0). Dropping the threshold to R>=8 only picks up the background dither (8,11,17 vs bg 5,6,12) scattered uniformly to the corners, not directional needles. So the defining halo of long fine straight radiating spines is 100% missing; every spoke terminates ON the outer circle instead of piercing it, which is what turns the silhouette into an unbroken disc. This alone is a must-read failure.

COLOUR: the judge is right that it is red, and it is worse than 'red' -- there is no glass reading whatsoever. Lattice lines run 216,76,91 at the rim down to 118,43,54 on the inner rings; the fill is a red radial gradient from 131,48,59 at centre falling smoothly to 20,15,20 at r=126 before the bright rim stroke (161,59,72). Hue is pinned around 350-355 deg everywhere -- zero cool/cyan/white highlights, zero iridescence, no specular hits that would say silica.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the judge's wording, neither of which saves the asset:
(1) 'no nested inner shell' is the weakest part of the charge and should not be cited as the fix target -- that must-read is qualified 'sometimes', so it is optional, and the r=32 and r=65 rings are arguably a nested-ring attempt. Do not let a fixer spend effort there.
(2) The judge missed a defect that IS load-bearing: the colour row also calls for a DARK CENTRAL CAPSULE, and the centre is the BRIGHTEST point of the image (131,48,59 falling monotonically outward), i.e. the capsule is inverted into a glow. The judge also under-charged must-read #1: 'a hollow SPHERE of glass built as an open geometric lattice'. A lattice of sorts exists, but nothing reads as a sphere -- the latitude rings are perfect circles with no foreshortening into ellipses, there is no volumetric shading, no terminator, no near-side/far-side lattice differentiation. It is a flat 2-D wheel seen face-on.

Net: of three must-reads, the spine halo is entirely absent, the 'hollow sphere' half fails (lattice yes, sphere no), and the palette is inverted from clear-glass-with-dark-capsule to opaque-red-with-bright-core. It reads as a radar sweep screen / dartboard, not a radiolarian. FAIL upheld. Fix priority: (a) push 20-40 fine straight spines well past the shell edge so the silhouette becomes spiky -- this is the single change that recovers the identity; (b) repaint shell to pale cool silica with iridescent rim and a dark inner capsule blob; (c) foreshorten the horizontal lattice rings into ellipses so it reads as a sphere.

rows.readsAs: a single spherical colony ball tiled with pale overlapping scales - a scaly seed pod, a pinecone, or a Volvox coloured red
rows.defect: Scale is 'field of many' and the identity is a bloom, but this is one compact sphere floating in black. The water is not discoloured at all - the background is the same near-black void as every other asset in the batch - and there are no surface streaks or swirls. The cells are pale pinkish-white lens shapes with concentric contour rings, reading as scales or onion slices; none carries a girdle groove, and the red only survives as narrow gaps of ground colour showing between them, so the ball reads pale, not brick-red.
rows.fix: Replace the ball with a rust-red field: flood the whole frame with brick-red stained water, run two or three lighter swirl streaks through it, and scatter the plated cells at high density across that field with a clear horizontal girdle groove cut across each cell.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at full size and at 4x/10x zoom on the 440x440 PNG. What is actually drawn: ONE compact globe centred in the frame, roughly 175px across, tiled with ~40 pale salmon overlapping ellipses (lens/scale shapes) each carrying a bright white cell-wall rim, sitting on a solid red base sphere with a charcoal shading crescent at upper-left and lower-right. It reads as a single colonial sphere -- a Volvox / morula / scaly seed pod -- not as a bloom. Packet requires aspect 0.9, scale 'field of many', family 'plated', colour 'brick red to rust brown, STAINING THE SURROUNDING WATER', and three mustReads.

MUSTREAD 1 (armoured plated cells with a girdle groove, packed at huge density): HALF present. Density is genuinely there -- the cells are packed edge-to-edge with heavy overlap, and the white rims do give a plated/armoured cell-wall impression. The GIRDLE GROOVE is genuinely absent, and I am correcting the judge's phrasing here: the cells are NOT featureless. Every cell carries a fine dark thin CONCENTRIC INNER ELLIPSE, roughly centred inside the cell outline. That mark reads as a nucleus, a pore, or a lens ring -- it is a closed centred ring, not a transverse equatorial furrow. A girdle groove must run all the way across the cell's width, sit off-centre (dividing epitheca from hypotheca), and notch the cell silhouette where it meets the edge. None of the ~40 cells does any of that. So the defect is real but the fix is not 'add a missing line' -- it is 'move and reshape the line that is already drawn': take the existing centred inner ellipse and convert it to an off-centre full-width transverse groove with an edge notch, plus a second short longitudinal sulcus.

MUSTREAD 2 (the water itself discoloured rust-red by the bloom): ABSENT, judge is exactly right. I sampled background pixels at ten points -- (10,10),(430,10),(10,430),(430,430),(220,20),(220,420),(20,220),(400,220),(100,100),(340,340) -- and got RGB 5,6,12 in the corners rising only to 6,9,15 near the mid-edges. That is the standard blue-black void with a faint BLUE-grey vignette, i.e. the only tint in the water is cool, the opposite of rust. There is zero red anywhere outside the globe's own silhouette. This is the single biggest miss: the species is defined by staining its medium and the medium here is empty black.

MUSTREAD 3 (streaks and swirls of concentrated cells at the surface): ABSENT, judge is right. No streaks, no swirls, no surface line or horizon, no windrows, no density gradient of any kind. The cells are distributed evenly over a sphere with no directional flow.

SCALE: also wrong and worth stating explicitly -- packet says 'field of many' but the art commits to a single bounded object with a lit rim and cast shading, which is what makes the Volvox misread inevitable regardless of the cell detail.

CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE'S COLOUR CLAIM: 'the red survives only as thin gaps between pale scales' is inaccurate. The red gaps are not thin -- there are broad red-orange wedges across the upper third and down the mid-right, and I sampled 181,60,48 inside one at (220,150), which is a genuine brick red and on-spec. The base sphere under the tiling is fully red. The real cause of the pale read is the SCALE FILL itself: the lens shapes sample at 208,138,133 / 198,136,132 / 183,112,107 -- a washed salmon-pink -- and they are too opaque and too whitened, and they cover roughly 75-80% of the disc. So the judge's conclusion (the thing reads pale, not brick-red-to-rust-brown) stands, but the fix is to darken and desaturate the plate fill toward rust and drop its opacity so the red base bleeds through, NOT to widen the gaps.

VERDICT: FAIL upheld. Two of three mustReads are wholly absent, the third is half-present with the defining girdle mislocated as a centred ring, the scale is a single organism instead of a field, and the colour spec's 'staining the surrounding water' clause is contradicted by a measured 5,6,12 background.

rows.readsAs: a speckled egg or a smooth grey river stone freckled with rust
rows.defect: The pale ground with scattered red-orange specks does get the watermelon-pink idea across, but it is painted as a shaded 3-D ellipse lit from the upper left and vignetted into black, so it reads as one solid object rather than a snowfield. There is no granular snow-crystal texture anywhere - the ground is a smooth airbrushed gradient. The cysts are flat soft dots with no thick wall and no rim, and not a single one shows the green chloroplast core the reference calls for, so the 'still green-cored' must-read is missing outright.

rows.readsAs: five long segmented filaments - readable as bacteria, but the beads make them look like snakes that each swallowed an egg
rows.defect: The filaments are stacked as five neat near-parallel horizontal bands with even gaps, a diagram layout rather than a tangled mat, and nothing overlaps or crosses. Each filament carries exactly ONE large sphere instead of being stuffed along its whole length with refractile granules, and that sphere is the same lozenge primitive that builds the coccus chain and the Thermophile rod. Worst of all the filament and the granule are the same pale yellow, so the lemon-yellow-globules-in-a-chalk-white-tube contrast that is the whole point does not exist. There is no dark sediment or vent surface under the mat - just void.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of generic orange rod bacteria on a slide - could be any bacillus
rows.defect: The rods themselves are fine, but they are sparse and randomly angled with big empty gaps and a stray pair drifting alone at the bottom of the frame - the opposite of the dense streaming bands the reference asks for. There is no banded mat and no sense of flow direction. The pale sinter mineral crust and the steam are both completely absent; the background is the same flat near-black void used everywhere in this batch, so nothing says hot spring. The rods also carry no visible thick wall - they are the plain glossy lozenge primitive stretched to aspect 2.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise
rows.defect: Reads as a tortoise, but the carapace is a semi-transparent glassy dome with a thin concentric wireframe laid over it — it reads as a glass cloche or a covered-wagon canopy sitting on the animal rather than as keratin scutes, and you can see the body silhouette THROUGH it. Only two legs exist in the whole render (one fore, one hind); the far pair is entirely absent, so the animal reads flat and two-legged. The legs themselves are straight-sided featureless rectangles with three nick marks at the bottom for toes. Geometrically identical to s1 and s17 — pure hue swap.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise
rows.defect: Same identical tortoise geometry as s0 and s17 with only the hue changed to pale blue-grey, which is the family defect in its purest form. The pale palette makes the already-translucent shell dome read almost as an empty glass bubble — the wireframe grid and the body behind it show straight through, and shell and sky are nearly the same value at the top edge. Again only two legs are drawn; the far pair is missing. Legs are flat untapered rectangles.
rows.fix: Opaque, value-separated carapace with a dark rim and raised scutes, plus the missing far-side leg pair — and vary the shell profile/limb length from s0/s17 so the three are not one mesh in three colours.

rows.readsAs: a stubby long-bodied furry dog or weasel
rows.defect: Coherent and namable as a short-legged furry quadruped, but it is the batch chassis with fur texture on top: the same generic snout-blob head with one big round eye and a dot nostril, the same horizontal forward-right neck carriage, the same constant-diameter tube legs dropping out of the bottom of a uniform barrel with no shoulder or hip. The forelimb region is a separate pale lozenge pasted over the torso with a visible seam, and the two hind legs fuse into one slab so the animal reads as having three legs. Bottlebrush tail is a flat brush stroke stuck on at the barrel's end rather than emerging from a croup.

rows.readsAs: a jellyfish, or a mushroom cap on roots
rows.defect: The dome-plus-hanging-strands silhouette does read as a jellyfish or a stalked fungus, but there is a stray unfilled parallelogram outline sitting on the upper-left of the cap that is plainly a render artifact, not anatomy. The three pink dots read as eyes but are scattered without symmetry and one is half-buried under the cap rim so it is clipped. All ten tentacles are the same uniform-width noodle, all terminate at exactly the same ground line with a blunt flat cut, and none taper — they read as spaghetti props rather than as tentacles or roots.
rows.fix: Kill the stray quad outline, taper the tentacles and vary their lengths and terminations, and either place the sensory dots symmetrically or drop them.

rows.readsAs: a red glowing pony-shaped beast with a horn
rows.defect: Straight chassis reissue: same arched topline into a short right-facing neck, same deep untapered barrel, same tube legs exiting the bottom edge of the barrel, same lumpy toe-pad feet, same meerkat snout head with one round eye, same bottlebrush tail. The white glow orbs float unattached in front of and over the body with no emitter on the skin, so they read as lens flare pasted on rather than as bioluminescent organs. The horn is a plain white cone glued to the muzzle with no boss or base. Dark speckle markings clump into a blotch over the shoulder instead of following the form.

rows.readsAs: a six-legged orange plated beast
rows.defect: Adding a third leg pair does not make a new animal — it is the same chassis with the same dowel repeated: three identical constant-diameter tube legs per side, all dropping vertically out of the flat bottom of the same barrel, all ending in the same lumpy toe pad, all the same length and all evenly spaced like table legs. Same right-facing snout-blob head with one eye, same horizontal neck, same bottlebrush tail. The dorsal plates are five identical teardrop shapes sitting ON the topline rather than growing out of it, and they float clear of the back at the tail end. Glow orbs again unattached.

rows.readsAs: a dark eight-legged plated beast
rows.defect: The torso is so dark it reads as a hole in the image rather than as mass, and a lighter translucent grey sheet is draped over it that you can see the barrel through, so the body has no solid read at all. The four pale ribbed leg pairs are crammed together with almost no spacing, all identical in length and diameter, all dropping vertically from the flat underside — they read as a row of fluted columns, not limbs. Head is the same snout-blob, nearly lost against the dark torso. Dorsal plates again sit on top of the line rather than growing from it.

rows.readsAs: nothing — a stray torpedo shape in the corner of an empty frame
rows.defect: Broken render. The entire organism is a small pale-teal torpedo shoved into the lower-right quadrant, leaving the top ~60% and the whole left half of the canvas empty. It has no legs, no readable head-to-body relationship — just a fin/spike at the left end, a tube, and two blunt knobs at the right — and it hovers above the ground shadow rather than standing on it. Worst of all, three vertical tick marks are stranded at the far LEFT edge of the frame at mid-height, completely detached from the body: a fragment orphaned off to one side. rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but several of the stated causes are wrong and one much worse defect was missed. Packet reference row is NONE (procedural — judge coherence and against batch siblings), so I rendered s13/s14/s16/s17 alongside: every one of them faces RIGHT, tail LEFT, head with a visible eye and muzzle, four legs with feet, subject centered and filling the frame. That is the batch convention s15 is measured against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured on the 440x440 PNG; body bbox lum>45 is x172..381, y272..364, i.e. 209x92 px; only 2.56% of frame pixels are lit; bbox area is 9.9% of the frame):
- LEFT END: a genuinely well-drawn two-lobed FORKED CAUDAL FIN — upper and lower triangular lobes meeting at a clean peduncle, painterly warm-cream rim light on both leading edges. This is the strongest part of the asset and is correctly placed at the tail end per batch convention.
- MIDDLE: a competent fusiform torpedo trunk, desaturated sage/teal-grey with a continuous cream dorsal highlight ridge. Rendering craft here is fine.
- RIGHT END (= the HEAD end by batch convention): THE HEAD IS ENTIRELY ABSENT. The trunk terminates in a hard, perfectly vertical FLAT-CUT WALL (a straight geometric seam, not anatomy) at approx x=352. Out of that truncation emerge two thin tapering stick appendages: an upper one arcing up-right to a rounded club tip at (381,291), and a lower one angling down-right to a hoof/club at (378,340). There is NO cranium mass, NO eye, NO jaw, NO muzzle, NO ear anywhere in the frame — I brightness-boosted 2.6x and zoomed 10x on x300-390/y280-360 to confirm. The other judge said 'no readable head-to-body relationship', which implies a head exists but is illegible; the truth is harder — there is no head object at all, and the flat vertical truncation where it should attach is itself a render artifact.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM:
1. 'legless' — OVERSTATED. There IS one prominent stick limb ending in a hoof at lower-right (the lower of the two front appendages), plus TWO tiny vestigial dark triangular nubs on the ventral line at approx x=305 and x=340 — the leg system fired but generated near-zero-length limbs. The trunk carries no walking legs, so the read is legless, but the fix target is 'limbs generated at ~0 length' not 'limbs missing'.
2. 'entire left half of the frame empty' — WRONG. The upper caudal lobe reaches x=172, which is 48 px LEFT of the frame midline (x=220). The empty band is the left 39% (x<172), not the left half.
3. 'top 60% ... empty' — CONFIRMED and precise: topmost body pixel is y=272 = 61.8% down the frame.
4. 'shoved into the lower-right quadrant' — CONFIRMED. Body centroid approx (276,318) vs frame center (220,220): +56 px right, +98 px down.
5. 'hovering above its ground shadow' — PARTIALLY RIGHT. The trunk belly (approx y=338) does float roughly 7-10 px above the shadow ellipse (shadow occupies y approx 345..385, centered x approx 255), but the LOWER CAUDAL LOBE dips to y=364 and does cross into the shadow. So it is the torso/limb that hovers, not the whole organism.

rows.verifyWhy:
Packet row: batch-002 entry 11, reference row NONE (procedural) -- so the only test is internal coherence, judged against the batch. I read the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 4x-9x on head, dorsal line, mid-torso, legs, feet and tail, plus scanline alpha runs to measure widths. VERDICT UPHELD, but MOST OF THE STATED CAUSES ARE WRONG -- do not fix against their list.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN (the real reason this fails):
1. TORSO. Confirmed and it is the whole defect. The dorsal line is a scalloped chain of ~6 circular lobes running rump-to-shoulder, and the notch between each pair cuts down about a third of a lobe radius, so the rim light climbs over each lobe and dives all the way into the valley between them. The profile is cumulus cloud / bunch of grapes, not a spine. This is the largest single mass in the drawing and it reads as inorganic. Correction to their wording: these are NOT hard-edged seams. At 9x the interior boundaries between lobes are SOFT tonal overlaps (one sphere's radial shading darkening over its neighbour) and the lower half is unified by a single smooth belly slab, so 'every seam showing' is false -- the failure lives entirely in the SILHOUETTE notches along the top, not in interior linework. The fix is to shallow or fully merge the dorsal notches into one back curve (and drop the arbitrary straight horizontal tonal step that runs across the belly), not to repaint interior seams.
2. LEGS. Eight legs, and they are genuinely hard to parse as four pairs -- they are near-black, the lowest-contrast element on the model, and they sit against a dark ground shadow. Their bottoms are square-cut on the ground line with only a small toe nub on about half of them, so 'no foot' is fair. But 'hairline two-pixel dark sticks with no hip' is factually wrong: scanline measurement gives each leg 12-13 px wide at the upper shank and 9-10 px at the ground (measured at y=320 -> eight runs of 12-13 px; y=372 -> eight runs of 9-10 px), each carries a bright rim-light stripe on its leading edge, several show a knee angle change at mid-shank, and each one meets the belly through a visible broad haunch cone. The fix is contrast/value on the shanks and a real foot termination, not thickness or hips.

WHAT THE FAILING JUDGE GOT WRONG -- these are all fine and must not be 'fixed':
- HEAD IS NOT A PINHEAD ON A WIRE NECK. At 5x the head is fully modelled: a brow ridge, a tapered muzzle with a nostril mark, a proper eye with dark iris and a white specular highlight, TWO upright pointed ears (the near one crisply drawn, a second point behind it), and five whiskers fanning off the right side of the muzzle. Measured: head ~44 px across (49 px including whiskers) on a neck ~30 px wide against a torso ~167 px long. The neck is a thick tapered column that blends continuously into both the skull and the shoulder mass -- no join visible, no wire.
- TAIL IS NOT DETACHED. The barbed arrowhead is fused to the shaft: same fill, one continuous rim light running from shaft into barb. The tail tapers correctly out of the hip. The only real criticism at the tail is that it roots on a discrete rump BALL that reads as a stuck-on sphere.
- SAIL IS NOT A FLAT PASTED CRESCENT. It is a translucent membrane with two internal curved ribs/fold lines and a bright leading-edge highlight, arcing forward over the shoulders. Its weakness is different: the base is not rooted -- the dorsal lobes show straight through it and its lower spur simply overlaps the lobes with no muscle or attachment flare.
- The back also carries small dark bristle/hair marks the judge did not mention.

BAND REASONING: this is a near-POLISH that I still call FAIL on coherence, not on identity. Head, neck, tail and sail are all drawn at a high, deliberate fidelity; the torso and legs are at primitive-assembly fidelity, and the mismatch sits on the biggest mass in the frame, so the animal reads as a good alien head and sail bolted onto a heap of bubbles on bars. Merging the dorsal lobes into one back curve and raising the leg value alone would lift this to PASS -- everything else is already there.

Body and limbs are the batch chassis with six legs.

rows.readsAs: a millipede
rows.defect: Reads instantly and correctly — overlapping tergite segments, a dense fringe of short legs on both sides, and a pair of antennae. Only weakness is that the head end is barely differentiated from the tail end apart from the antennae.

rows.readsAs: a broken render — a dark six-legged dinosaur outline with a rod skewered through its body
rows.defect: A dead-straight pale grey bar runs the full length of the torso from the rear haunch to the shoulder and breaks OUT past the silhouette on the left, with four translucent pink and blue discs threaded onto it like beads. It sits on top of the body, ignores the body's form entirely, and reads as a rendering artifact impaling the animal. Compounding it, the body fill is almost pure black against a near-black field, so only the green rim-light is visible and the creature reads as an empty outline. It also has SIX legs where every other quadruped in the batch has four, and a bulbous lobe on the rear-left that reads as a second head.

rows.verifyWhy:
Packet row is 'reference row: NONE (procedural or unlisted - judge coherence)', so there are no must-reads to defend; the test is whether the thing reads as one coherent animal. It does not, and the FAIL stands - but three of the four stated causes are described wrong, so fix against this instead.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A six-legged long-necked grazer in left-facing side view on a 440x440 canvas: rounded cranium on a thick upward-sweeping neck at x~330-380 with a broad soft snout lobe and two tiny dark dots stacked VERTICALLY (they read as eye-over-nostril, not a pair of eyes; no mouth line, no ear); a run of seven-plus large triangular dorsal spikes from x~95 to x~250; a barrel torso; a big featureless sphere at the rear; six thin stick legs ending in ball feet; a soft elliptical ground shadow. As an alien megafauna silhouette that is coherent - it is not the wrong organism.

THE DECIDING DEFECT (judge is right that it exists). A dead-straight, unshaded, near-white rod runs horizontally across the torso at y=232-241, from x~86 to x~278 - roughly 190px, about 65% of the body length. It is the BRIGHTEST THING IN THE IMAGE: peak luminance 208.6 at (95,229), against a torso-core mean of 33 and a background mean of 12-19. It has no taper into or out of the body, no form shading, no attachment to any anatomy, and a small cross/fletch tick at its left tip (visible at src x~96-101) that makes it read as a lance with a crossguard. It is a stray primitive sitting on top of the creature. That alone is a FAIL: at thumbnail size the animal reads as having a stick through it.

CORRECTION 1 - IT DOES NOT BREAK THE SILHOUETTE. I scanned rows y=226..241 pixel by pixel. At y=238, luminance is flat background (14-15) from x=60 all the way to x=82, then jumps at x=84 (22) -> 86 (102) -> 90 (186). x~84-88 IS the body's rim edge in the notch between the dorsal spike run and the rump lobe, so the bar's bright tip coincides with the rim and never enters empty field. Same at the other end: at y=238 the bar reads 118 at x=265 falling to 100 at x=277, drops to 55 at x=279 (plain torso fill), and the neck rim does not start until x~287. BOTH ENDS TERMINATE INSIDE THE SILHOUETTE. 'Breaks out past the silhouette on the left' is false - the correct description is that it stops flush against the rim in the rear notch, which is why it looks like it exits.

CORRECTION 2 - THE DISCS AND THE BAND ARE TWO SEPARATE FEATURES. Under the bar there is a salmon/dusty-pink horizontal flank BAND (roughly a rounded-end rectangle, src x~135-250, y~240-255). Sitting on that band are FOUR hard-edged translucent circles: three pale grey-blue (centres src x~150, ~192, ~233) and one salmon-pink (centre src x~170). The count of four is right, but the pink is not disc-colour variation - one disc is pink and there is also a pink band beneath all four. Their centres sit BELOW the bar line; the bar crosses their upper third, so 'threaded like beads' is directionally right but geometrically the rod grazes their tops. The discs are their own defect independent of the bar: perfectly circular, uniformly translucent, hard-edged, with zero conformance to the barrel of the torso, so they read as bubbles or a UI overlay rather than as skin markings.

CORRECTION 3 - THE FILL IS NOT NEAR-BLACK, BUT THE CONTRAST IS GENUINELY BAD. Measured means: background left of body 11.8, background above the back 18.8, torso core 33.1, rump lobe 53.1, head 60.8, torso upper band 87.6. So the body fill is a dark OLIVE (sample RGB 30,35,18), roughly 2-3x the field, and the interior mass plus its dorsal-to-belly gradient do read once you look - the upper torso is clearly lighter than the field. But sRGB contrast ratio between torso core and field is only about 1.2:1, so the read is carried overwhelmingly by the yellow-green rim light. 'Only the rim-light reads' overstates it; the accurate statement is that fill-to-field contrast is ~1.2:1 and needs the body value lifted or the field darkened, not that the fill is absent.

CORRECTION 4 - THE REAR LOBE IS NOT A SECOND HEAD. At src x~45-95, y~245-292 there is a featureless sphere about 45px across (the real head is about 42px, so yes, head-sized) with a small nub at its lower-left. It has no eyes, no snout, no neck, and it sits low and flush against the rump. It reads as an oversized rump sac / tail-base lobe, not as a head - the actual head is unambiguous because it is on a long neck with a snout and facial dots. The judge's underlying worry is still legitimate: a head-sized featureless ball at the opposite end does create front/back ambiguity at thumbnail scale, and it should be reshaped or shrunk. But 'reads as a second head' is not what I see.

CONFIRMED AS STATED - SIX LEGS. I counted six distinct shafts with ball feet at approx src x = 95, 123, 172, 235, 280, 300. Six legs is legitimate for procedural alien fauna and is not by itself a defect. What IS weak: all six are identical thin sticks with identical ball feet and no fore/hind differentiation, and the spacing is irregular (28px, then 63px, then 20px), so they read as a picket fence rather than as three limb pairs.

BAND. FAIL upheld, on the bar alone. Fix order: (1) remove or re-anchor the white lance primitive - it is a foreign object, not a polish item; (2) make the four discs conform to the torso form or drop them; (3) lift the body fill value so fill-to-field clears ~2:1 instead of 1.2:1; (4) reshape the rear lobe so it cannot be mistaken for a front end.

rows.readsAs: a headless fish with a two-pronged fork where its head should be
rows.defect: The scaled hull ends in a big forked caudal fin at the left, and at the right the body simply stops and two thin knobbed stalks stick out into empty space with a visible gap between them and the body. There is no head, no eye, no mouth, no gill — the entire head end is absent, and the two floating prongs read as stranded fragments. Verified at 1x, then re-read with 2.4x brightness lift and 5x/8x nearest-neighbour crops of both ends (left end 45,180 160x200; right end 290,230 110x110). The FAIL verdict stands, but two of the stated causes are wrong and the fix should not be made against them.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A single fusiform, fish-like hull runs horizontally across the frame (roughly x=95 to x=327, y=235 to y=310), lit by a hard warm rim along its entire dorsal contour, with a soft ground-shadow ellipse painted below it. LEFT END: confirmed a large lunate/forked caudal fin -- two swept triangular lobes meeting at a narrow peduncle around x=95,y=280, with a small bright highlight bead at the peduncle joint. This is unambiguously a tail, so the RIGHT end is the head end, and the judge is right about which end carries the identity.

RIGHT END, CORRECTED. The judge says the hull 'simply stops' and that 'two thin knobbed stalks float in empty space with a gap to the body.' Both halves of that are wrong in ways that matter.
(a) The hull does not taper out or fade -- it is cut by a HARD, PERFECTLY VERTICAL STRAIGHT EDGE, a ~35px chord at x=327 spanning roughly y=265 to y=300. This is a clipped/unclosed hull cap: a straight machined wall where a snout should be. That straight vertical chord is the single most diagnostic geometric defect and it is not mentioned in the claim.
(b) NEITHER STALK IS DETACHED. At 8x the upper stalk is continuous with the body -- the dorsal rim highlight runs unbroken out of the back contour, up over the stalk and around its terminal knob, with no seam and no gap; it is a limb growing off the dorsal-caudal corner of the truncation. The lower stalk attaches flush to the BOTTOM corner of the same vertical wall (its proximal end sits at x=327, y=298, exactly on the hull edge) and angles down-right to a rounded pad/hoof terminal at ~x=365,y=320. The dark rectangular wedge between them is a NOTCH BETWEEN TWO ATTACHED LIMBS, not a gap between the body and floating parts. Anyone fixing this against 'reattach the floating stalks' will move geometry that is already attached and the asset will still fail.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. There is a rounded secondary lobe in the silhouette immediately before the truncation (roughly x=275-327) that occupies the position a head would take, but it carries ZERO features: no eye, no eye socket, no pupil dot, no mouth line, no jaw, no nostril, no gill slit or operculum, no cheek plane, no snout taper, no ear or barbel. I checked the terminal knobs of both stalks specifically for eyestalks -- neither knob contains a pupil, iris or any darker inset; they are plain shaded clubs, one club-tipped and one hoof/pad-tipped, so they read as limbs or flippers, not as eye-stalks that could stand in for a head. The result reads as a fish hull with its head sliced off at a vertical plane, with two legs bolted to the cut face. Wrong-organism-level failure: the head end that is the identity is absent, exactly as claimed.

SECOND DEFECT NOT IN THE CLAIM. On the lower flank at roughly x=155-200, y=288-312 there is a small rhomboid drawn as a THIN 2D OUTLINE ONLY -- a four-line diamond with no fill, no shading, no rim light, no shadow, sitting flat on the painted hull. Presumably an intended pelvic/anal fin, it currently reads as a wireframe/debug overlay pasted onto a painterly body and violates the painterly-canvas law on its own. Fix it in the same pass as the head.

FIX DIRECTION: close the hull with an actual cranium forward of x=327 -- snout taper, jaw/mouth line, and a readable eye placed on the rounded lobe -- rather than touching the two limbs, which are correctly attached; and re-render the flank rhomboid as a shaded fin volume.

Packet row is **NONE** (procedural), so this is judged on coherence alone -- and it is not coherent as a plant. VERDICT UPHELD, with corrections to the stated causes.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (440x440 canvas): (1) A flat teal slab spanning x~72-368, y~365-385, ~20 px tall. Measured fill is rgb(33,116,108) at x=120, x=220 and x=330 and falls only to rgb(31,108,102) at its bottom -- i.e. an essentially unmodulated solid fill, no gradient, no texture, no interior modelling. Its top edge resolves in ONE pixel (y=365 rgb(27,90,87) -> y=366 rgb(33,113,106)) while every plant element carries a 6-10 px blur radius, so the judge's 'only crisp thing in the image' is literally measurable, not rhetoric. Profile is a dead-straight top with tapered rounded ends and a soft dark elliptical drop-shadow beneath it -- an edge-on plate/lens. (2) Eight stems: straight, uniform-width (~4-5 px) vertical bars, slightly splayed, no taper, no curve, no node, no sheath, with flat hard-cut tops AND bottoms. Their colour is rgb(22,18,35) to rgb(37,30,54) against a rgb(10,10,21) background -- only 8-25 levels of separation, which is why they are nearly invisible at normal exposure. (3) Seven heads: soft blue-white lumps, rgb(188,214,230) core, built from one or two overlapping blurred circles. At 10x the top-left head is a featureless octagonal smudge: no petals, no radial symmetry, no calyx, no bract, no shading gradient. (4) At 6x gain over the entire frame there is NO leaf, NO frond, NO basal rosette, NO soil, NO root, and nothing hiding in shadow. The organism occupies only x~130-315, y~210-340 -- about 42% of frame width and 30% of height, floating in the upper-middle with the whole top half empty.

TWO DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL CLAIM MISSED, and they are the worst ones: (a) EVERY stem terminates in a soft flat cut roughly 25 px ABOVE the slab. Sampled down column x=147: y=340 is stem tail rgb(25,21,39), y=350/355/360 are pure background rgb(11,10,21), then y=364 is slab. The plant is not standing on the ground plane, it is suspended over it. (b) The LEFTMOST individual's head is detached from its own stem -- the blob bottom ends near y=250 and its stem does not begin until y~262, with clean background between. Conversely the stem at x~215 has a hard flat top and no head at all. So the render contains a headless stem and a stemless head in the same frame.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM: 'no stem structure' is wrong as written -- stems are present and countable (8 of them). The accurate defect is that they are structureless and disconnected: untapered rectangles at near-background contrast, floating free at the bottom and, in one case, at the top too. 'Green plastic tray' is the wrong colour and the wrong object: the slab is teal/cyan rgb(33,116,108), and its silhouette (flat top, tapered ends, cast shadow) reads as a dish/plate/petri seen edge-on or a UI progress bar, not a walled tray. WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW. 440x440. A magenta-pink foliage mass occupying roughly x=140-325, y=25-250 (about 185px wide x 215px tall), sitting on a thin dark-brown vertical stem that runs from behind the mass at y~250 down to a flat cut at y~385, over a separate soft elliptical drop shadow. CORRECTION 1 - it is NOT 'one amorphous blob'. Under contrast stretch the canopy resolves into roughly 18-20 DISCRETE overlapping soft spheres, each carrying its own radial centre highlight, unioned into a metaball mass, plus a global top-left key gradient (upper-left lobes bright, lower-right lobes dim). So the puff/mass layer is present and functioning correctly. This matters: the missing thing is not 'the canopy'; it is the LEAF-SPRITE layer that should be scattered on top of the mass. Same-batch sibling flora-h0-s11 proves the generator can do it - that asset draws individual pinnate leaf sprites with visible midribs, radiating outward from visible branch stubs at the crown, over the same kind of soft haze mass. flora-h0-s10 has ZERO leaf sprites and zero branch stubs. This is a dropped/zero-count layer, not a style variant, and it is exactly why the asset reads as cotton candy rather than a plant.

CONFIRMED: no internal branching anywhere. The stem vanishes behind the mass at y~250 with no fork, no crown stubs, no branch strokes inside the mass, and no darker interior separating foliage clusters. Silhouette edge is smooth circular arcs with a soft gaussian falloff - no serration, no scallop, no leaf points anywhere on the outline. The concave notch the other judge called 'a bite out of its side' is real: a large re-entrant gap on the right between the upper-right and lower-right lobe groups, which with the overall S/C-shaped outline is what makes it read as an amoeba.

CORRECTION 2 - 'perfectly straight uniform-width rod with no taper' is directionally right but factually off. Measured stem widths (background-relative threshold): 12px at y=260, 12 at y=280, 12 at y=300, 12 at y=320, 11 at y=340, 11 at y=365, 10 at y=378, 10 at y=382. So it DOES taper about 17% - but the WRONG WAY: it is thinnest at the ground and thickest at the crown, the inverse of a real trunk. Centre-x measured 220.5 at every sampled row, so it is dead vertical with zero curve, lean or sway.

CONFIRMED: no root flare. The stem terminates in a flat horizontal cut at y~385 with no widening, no flare, no ground-contact detail; the only ground cue is the detached ellipse shadow, and the stem tip does not even meet the shadow's visual centre convincingly.

SCALE DEFECT the other judge did not quantify: an ~11px stem carrying a ~185px-wide canopy is a ~17:1 canopy-to-stem ratio. That alone destroys the plant read regardless of the foliage fix - the stem needs to be several times thicker with a flared base before the mass looks supported.

EXTRA DEFECT they missed: an isolated near-black single-pixel speck inside the canopy at approximately (185,161), with no surrounding form or shading. Reads as noise/dirt, not as a berry or a gap.

DEPTH: the canopy's total luminance spread is only 59.5-168.5, and most of the mass sits in a narrow mid band, so beyond the shallow top-left gradient the mass has no lit-versus-shadow separation and no sense of volume behind the front lobes.

BAND. The must-read that constitutes the identity of a canopy plant - readable foliage (leaves and/or branch armature) - is genuinely absent, not merely small or drawn where the judge did not look; I looked at 3x-5x and under contrast stretch and there is nothing there. Against the batch, flora-h0-s11 sets the bar with real leaf sprites and this asset is far below it. FAIL stands.

FIX ORDER: (1) restore the leaf-sprite scatter layer over the existing puff mass - the mass layer is fine, keep it as the soft backing haze; (2) draw branch stubs from the stem into the mass so the foliage has something to hang on; (3) thicken the stem ~3x and reverse the taper so it is widest at the ground, with a root flare meeting the shadow; (4) break the smooth arc silhouette with leaf points; (5) remove the stray dark pixel at (185,161).

I read the 440x440 PNG at native size, at 6-8x crops on the bottom disc and the top two discs, and at gamma 2.4 to pull anything hiding in the dark. I also decoded the PNG and measured it numerically. The FAIL STANDS, but two parts of the stated cause need correcting and the real geometric defect is sharper than described.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Five pink ellipses threaded on a brown vertical rod, over a green radial vignette, with a soft ground-contact shadow ellipse at the base (the shadow and vignette are only visible under gamma boost -- the judge did not mention them, but they exist). Measured discs, top to bottom: major axis 70 / 108 / 144 / 180 / 218 px. Because the widths widen monotonically downward and the stem meets a ground shadow, the SILHOUETTE does legibly read as a conifer / pagoda-plant. This is not the wrong organism. It fails on execution, not identity.

CONFIRMED PARTS OF THE CLAIM.
- 'Five perfectly flat ellipses': confirmed, exactly 5 connected pink regions.
- 'Pure uniform fill': confirmed in effect. The entire disc body measures RGB 189,82,164 (outer four) with no gradient of any kind -- a vertical scan through the bottom disc at x=160 reads 189,82,164 flat from y=268 to y=282, and the only non-uniform pixels in the whole asset are 1-2px of rim antialiasing (the 621 'distinct colors' are all edge interpolation). Correction of detail: the fill is not literally single-valued -- there is a ~10px band of 194,84,165 directly over the stem column. That is a 5/255 delta, imperceptible, and it is LIGHTER not darker, so it is not shading.
- 'Unbroken smooth rims, no leaf tips': confirmed and verified numerically, not just by eye. I traced the bottom disc's top and bottom boundary at 4px intervals across its full 212px width. Top edge runs 272-271-270-269-268...263...268-269-270-271-273 and the bottom edge mirrors it -- both are perfectly monotone arcs. Zero notches, zero lobes, zero serrations, no leaf tips, no radial veins, no midrib.
- 'No self-shadowing where they meet the stem': confirmed, and it is worse than stated. The stem is drawn BEHIND the discs and the pixels where they cross are 194,84,165, i.e. slightly LIGHTER than the surrounding 189,82,164 -- the exact inverse of a contact shadow. There is also no inter-disc occlusion: the pink on disc 5 that sits directly under disc 4's footprint is the identical 189,82,164 as disc 5's outer rim.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG -- 'no perspective'. Perspective is not absent; it is present and geometrically IMPOSSIBLE, which is the actionable defect. Every one of the five discs has an identical minor axis of 24px (measured heights 24/25/24/24/24) while the major axes run 70/108/144/180/218. So the axis ratio climbs 2.92 -> 4.32 -> 6.00 -> 7.50 -> 9.08. A stack of horizontal circles seen from one camera must share a CONSTANT major:minor ratio; here each tier implies a different viewing tilt. The top disc reads as a near-3:1 saucer seen from well above, the bottom as a 9:1 razor slice seen edge-on. The generator is clearly stamping a fixed 24px height and only varying width. That single constant is what makes the stack read as plates rather than foliage, and it is the thing to fix. Secondary: no disc shows any thickness or edge wall, and no disc distinguishes underside from topside (tiers above eye level should show their undersides, none do).

ADDITIONAL CAUSES THE JUDGE DID NOT NAME, which drive the 'tiered cake' read as much as the flatness. Tier spacing is machine-uniform: gaps of 29/29/30/29px. Every disc is centered on exactly cx=219.5 -- zero horizontal jitter, zero asymmetry, perfect bilateral mirror. The stem is a constant-width 10px rod from y=38 to y=383 with no taper whatsoever (8px at the extreme tips is antialiasing only), no root flare at the ground, and no branch junctions where the tiers attach -- a real leader shoot would thin toward the apex and show whorl nodes.

VERDICT. Hard-edged flat-fill vector primitives with a single solid color and no self-shadowing are a direct violation of the CF HD painterly-canvas engine law. Nothing is present-but-small that the judge missed; I looked specifically for rim detail, leaf tips and hidden shading and there is none at any zoom or gamma. FAIL upheld, with the perspective diagnosis corrected from 'no perspective' to 'inconsistent perspective caused by a fixed 24px minor axis across all five discs'.

Verdict upheld, but roughly half the stated geometry is wrong and the fixes must not be made against it. Measured on the 440x440 PNG (pixel-scanned plus 5x/6x nearest-neighbour crops).

WHAT THE JUDGE GOT WRONG:
(1) 'spans the full frame width' - FALSE. The purple element runs x=73..366, i.e. 293px = 67% of frame width, with a clean ~73px margin on BOTH sides. It is centred and inset, not edge-to-edge.
(2) 'jammed against the bottom edge' - FALSE. Its bottom lip is at y=387; there are 52px (12% of the canvas) of empty background below it, and a soft elliptical cast shadow is painted in that gap. It is floated above the bottom edge, not jammed into it.
(3) 'bar' - it is not a rectangle. At 5x it is a shallow lens/dish: flat top slab, tapered rounded ends, a thin darker under-rim and a soft drop shadow. It reads unambiguously as an intentional soil bed / planter dish, colour RGB(107,76,179). The judge is right that it is hard-edged and flat-filled, and that is a real defect (see below), but 'stray purple bar' mis-describes it.
(4) 'five stalks' - there are SIX stalks: five in the left clump (x~112, ~140, ~148, ~178, ~205) and one on the right (x~335). Of the five left stalks, only FOUR carry heads - the second from the left is a bare headless stalk that just stops in mid-air, which is its own defect and the judge missed it.
(5) 'no plant body, stem or foliage' - wrong on stems. Six stems are clearly drawn, ~4-6px wide, in a desaturated violet-grey, with visible taper. The right-hand stalk is thicker and additionally carries TWO pale lateral lobes flanking the stem just below its terminal cluster - the only leaf-like forms in the whole image. So 'no stem' is false; 'no foliage' is essentially true.
(6) 'pins stuck in a shelf' - it is worse than that. Nothing is stuck in anything. Every stem terminates and fades to transparency at y~345-349, while the top of the dish is at y=362. There is a 13-16px void between the feet of all six stalks and the ground plane. The plant hovers above its own soil.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS (fix against this list):
A. SEVERED CONTACT - the single worst defect. All six stems end ~14px short of the dish and fade out rather than meeting or entering it. No root flare, no contact shadow, no occlusion. Fix: extend stems to y>=364 and overlap the dish top, or lower the dish to y=348.
B. NO FOLIAGE - not one leaf, blade, frond, sheath or bract on any of the six stems except the two vague lobes on the right stalk. For a flora asset this is the identity must-read and it is absent.
C. STRUCTURELESS HEADS - the four left heads are featureless white discs (RGB>235) with zero interior modelling: no petals, no cap gills, no filament texture, no rim darkening, no hue variation. The right head is a lumpy fused two-lobe blob. They read as cotton buds / map pins, not as blooms or capsules.
D. FOCUS MISMATCH - the entire organism is heavily gaussian-blurred (head edges ramp over 8-10px) while the dish is razor-sharp with a 1px edge. Two render passes disagreeing in the same frame. Sibling flora-h1-s4 in this same batch is knife-sharp throughout, so the blur is this asset's fault, not the batch's.
E. COMPOSITION - the organism occupies only y=223..348, the bottom 28% of the canvas; everything above y=223 (the top half, not the top two-thirds as claimed) is empty background. s4 by contrast runs y=35..395. This asset is undersized and bottom-loaded.
F. TWO SPECIMENS, NOT ONE - a ~118px void separates the left clump (ends x~212) from the lone right stalk (starts x~330). It reads as two unrelated plants sharing a tray rather than one specimen.
G. GROUND-PLANE CONVENTION BREAK - siblings sit on a soft dark elliptical shadow; this one gets an opaque saturated violet slab that is the highest-chroma object in the frame and pulls the eye away from the organism.

The asset does not read as the WRONG organism - 'white-headed cotton-grass stalks' is a legible alien-flora idea. It fails because the defining flora must-read (foliage) is absent, the organism is physically disconnected from its ground plane, and the render is out of focus against a sharp prop. FAIL stands.

The genuine silhouette defect the judge did not name is a large C-shaped bite cut out of the lower-right around x250-275 / y150-205, which severs a right-hand lobe and makes the mass read as two colliding blobs rather than one crown.

CONFIRMED AND DECISIVE - 'no branch armature or attachment' is exactly right, and it is the reason this fails. There is not a single secondary branch, fork, or twig anywhere in the image. That is a rectangle, not a painted trunk, and it violates the HD painterly-engine law (no flat primitives). WHAT I SAW (440x440, bg #06070D, measured pixel-by-pixel, not eyeballed). Five solid teal horizontal ellipses stacked on one dead-straight vertical bar, all sharing centre x=219.5. Measured bands (y-range / max width): 68-89 / 66px, 119-140 / 100px, 169-190 / 136px, 220-241 / 170px, 271-292 / 204px. Every band is exactly 22px tall regardless of its width, and the widths step by a constant +34px. A vertical cross-section through tier 3 at x=240 reads 50,177,174 on EVERY row from y=169 to y=190 -- twenty-two consecutive rows of byte-identical RGB. That is a fill(), not a painted bough: no underside shadow, no rim light, no needle/frond texture, no clump union, no overlap depth, no value break between the lit top and the shaded belly. The trunk is a constant-width flat stroke of #2C2440 (I sampled 44,36,64 verbatim in every inter-tier gap at y=200/250/300) with no bark, no taper, no root flare; it fades into the bottom vignette and meets a plain dark ellipse ground shadow centred ~y=385. There is no apex leader, no branch, no bud, no organ anywhere on the asset.

CLAIM CLAUSE 1 -- "same five flat zero-thickness ellipses on the same straight pole as flora-h2-s4" -- CORRECT, and stronger than they put it. It is not a resemblance, it is literally the same nine lines of code. Both s4 and s8 fall through proceduraloverrides.planFor() to the verbatim engine and land in hdart.verbatim.js:2468, the conifer cform==='layered' branch: `for(let ti=0;ti<5;ti++){ const ty=S*(0.30+ti*0.115), w=S*(0.075+ti*0.04); g2.ellipse(bx,ty,w,S*0.026) }`. The constant S*0.026 semi-minor is the source of the identical 22px band height at every tier; the 0.075/0.115/0.155/0.195/0.235 progression is the +34px step. s4 measures 68/106/142/180/216px against s8's 66/100/136/170/204 -- a ~5% scale delta from _fitPlant normalisation, nothing more. Note for the fixer: the sibling cases in the SAME switch (cf==='bushy', 'dense', 'round') all route through _canopyMass and come out painterly; 'layered' and 'spire' are the two that still emit raw primitives. That is the localised cause and the localised fix.

CLAIM CLAUSE 2 -- "recoloured teal" -- WRONG as stated, and the error matters. s8 is not a colour swap of s4; it is the LUMIN variant of the same rig. g.lumin is true here, which is why the trunk is #2C2440 (the lumin trunk) where s4's is #31241A (the wood trunk), and why the backdrop radial is the purple #150F20 instead of s4's green-black #0F1A10. Three coordinated palette channels, all gene-driven. A fix that just re-tints the discs will reproduce the defect.

CLAIM CLAUSE 3 -- "unexplained magenta bloom BEHIND the stem ... reads as a render artifact" -- the perception is fair, the diagnosis is wrong on both counts. It is not behind the stem and it is not unexplained. It is hdart.verbatim.js's `glow(bx, S*0.35, S*0.16)` -- the bioluminescence gradient the lumin gene has always specified -- drawn LAST, with globalCompositeOperation='lighter' at alpha 0.5, so it composites ON TOP of the trunk and the disc faces, not behind them. Proof: the trunk pixel at x=220,y=101 reads 141,77,147 against the 44,36,64 it reads everywhere else, and the tier-1 face at x=220,y=80 reads 103,200,222 against the 52,179,178 of undisturbed teal. It is a clean radial centred exactly on the trunk axis at y~101, which is dead centre of the bare gap between tier 1 (ends y=89) and tier 2 (starts y=119), falling off smoothly to background by r~90px. So the real defect is not that it is an artifact -- it is that the engine paints a light source with NO EMITTER: there is no bulb, node, cone, catkin or organ drawn at S*0.35, just a glow hanging over blank trunk. Give the lumin flag a body to come from and the same gradient becomes a feature.

WHY FAIL AND NOT POLISH. With no reference row this is judged on coherence and against its batch, and the batch makes the gap unarguable: flora-h2-s7 and flora-h2-s9 in the same set carry gradient-shaded lobes, midribs, tendril curls, stem-over-leaf overlap and real form shading. Next to them s8 is an assembly of flat primitives -- a straight-line violation of the HD engine law (everything visual goes through the painterly canvas engine, no flat primitives). It does still read as 'a layered conifer-ish plant', so it is not the wrong organism; but the remedy is not a touch-up, it is replacing the 'layered' branch's raw ellipse fills with the _canopyMass path its siblings already use and anchoring the lumin glow to a drawn organ. That is rig work, which puts it below POLISH.

That proves the generator already owns a fungal vocabulary — substrate, clustering, lobed fruiting bodies, sheen — and that fungi-h0-s4 exercises none of it. This is not a case of a small feature drawn somewhere the first judge did not look; the feature set was simply never invoked for this seed.

I considered and rejected the strongest refutation available: that a giant puffball (Calvatia/Lycoperdon) genuinely is a near-featureless sphere, which would make this a legitimate fungus. It does not hold. A puffball reads as fungal through cream-to-buff colour, a flattened partially-buried base, a visible sterile base or cord, and raised warts with their own micro-shadows. This asset has none of those four: it is saturated orange, perfectly circular at the base, unattached, and its markings are flat. Strip the shadow ellipse and this image is indistinguishable from the desert-planet sphere primitive.

Band FAIL. Fix direction: this seed needs the whole fungal skeleton added — substrate, stipe, a cap distinct from the stipe, and an underside treatment — not a texture tweak. rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, but two of the stated causes are wrong and the real one is missing. Below each, a curtain of ~46 thin threads falling to y~280-300px. A rounded arcing bough crosses behind them, and a soft ground ellipse sits at the bottom. CORRECT in the claim: it reads as two jellyfish, not fungus. CORRECT: neither dome has any stipe, boss, or contact with the bough -- the caps hover roughly a full cap-height clear of the wood with nothing but the threads spanning the gap, so nothing anchors the fruit body. WRONG #1: 'the teeth drift past the substrate rather than growing from it' inverts the anatomy. The teeth are the one part correctly attached -- they are drawn from y = cy + h*0.2, i.e. BEHIND and ABOVE the cap's own bottom edge at cy + h*0.28, and in the render they visibly emerge from under the flat cap rim. They were never supposed to grow from the substrate. WRONG #2: 'brown substrate bar ... filaments dangle well below it into empty space' overstates and mislabels. It is not a bar: it is a rounded quadratic bough with a darker bark under-shadow stroke and 12 pale horizontal bark hatch strokes, and it reads acceptably as a bough. Pixel scan: brown bough pixels run y=186 to y=280 and stop; red thread pixels persist to y=301 but only 1-17 px per row, i.e. roughly three to five tip-ends clearing the bough silhouette by ~20px (4.8% of frame). That overhang is real and should be fixed, but it is a minor blemish, not the reason this fails. THE ACTUAL CAUSE OF THE JELLYFISH READ, which the claim does not name: the teeth are wrong in every dimension. (a) LENGTH -- drop = h*(1.5 + cos(u*1.5)*1.15)*(0.7 + r()*0.55) with h = S*0.10 yields up to 0.33S, measured ~140px of thread under a ~60px-tall cap, i.e. 2.3x the cap height. Hydnoid spines are a short dense pelt, never longer than the cap is tall. (b) PROFILE -- each spine is a constant-width stroke (tw fixed per spine) with lineCap 'round', so it never tapers; it ends in a blunt rounded tip. A tooth is a cone. (c) VALUE -- the per-spine gradient runs p.dark at the top to p.lit at the bottom, so the tips are the BRIGHTEST pixels in the whole asset. A pelt of teeth is shadowed at its tips; lit glowing tips are precisely the cnidarian tentacle cue. (d) JITTER -- +/-25% random length per spine plus +/-4.5px lateral jitter at both the mid control point and the tip makes them cross and splay into separated tendrils instead of a solid combed underside; the 3.4px pitch is dense at the rim but opens into see-through gaps lower down. Also correcting 'featureless dome': each cap does carry one arc, the c.strokeStyle 'rgba(232,240,255,0.30)' specular at line 108, but at 30% alpha over the salmon lump gradient it renders as a DARK blue-grey hairline following just inside the rim, not a highlight -- so the one mark on the bell reads as a jellyfish bell margin and makes the misread worse rather than better. FIXES, in order of payoff: shorten the teeth to <= 0.6x cap height, taper them to points (per-spine tapering polygon, not a round-capped stroke), invert the gradient so tips are dark, cut the length and lateral jitter to a fraction of current, seat each cap ON the bough with a visible sessile attachment or short lateral stipe, repair the specular so it reads white, and clip the teeth so no tip crosses the bough's lower silhouette. Family note: the batch is not one chassis -- fungi-h0-s2 (a coral/branching white form) and fungi-h0-s6 (stalked knobs) are structurally distinct, so this is a per-family defect, not a shared-body defect.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x and again at 3x/6x crops of the tip band and the base band. The asset is nine upright purple spikes on a dark ground with a soft elliptical drop shadow; no cap, no stipe/pileus distinction, no gills/pores, no substrate, no mycelial pad, no branching. Packet row is NONE (procedural), so the bar is coherence + reads-as-its-kingdom, and it does not read as fungus at any zoom. My first read was 'purple grass / sansevieria clump' and it held at 6x.

WHAT THE FAILING JUDGE GOT RIGHT (confirmed on the pixels):
- Points: ALL nine apices are acute triangular spikes with straight-sided taper. At thumbnail size three of them (fingers 3, 5 and 6 from the left) LOOK domed, and I initially wrote them down as rounded club tips; at 6x every one of them resolves to a needle point. No blunt or lobed apex exists anywhere in the asset.
- Curling tip: correct, the far-right finger is a sickle that arcs right and hooks over — reads as a wilting leaf blade, the single most grass-like element in the frame.
- Midrib: correct as described. Each finger carries one thin, hard-edged, near-constant-width pale line running most of its length, roughly central (drifting slightly left near the tips, slightly right near the base). It does not behave like a specular band on a cylinder — it does not widen, fade at the ends, or shift with the finger's lean; it is a drawn line, and it reads as a leaf midrib/keel.
- Flat section: broadly correct. The lower half of every finger is near-uniform mid-purple wall to wall with hard edges and no terminator darkening on the shade side, so the cross-section reads as a ribbon, not a rod. There IS a faint lateral gradient in the upper thirds of the two leftmost fingers, so 'flattened blades' is slightly overstated for those two, but not for the other seven.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG OR INCOMPLETE — fix against this, not against the original wording:
1. 'Club/coral fungi ... have a fused fleshy base' is not a safe rule and should not drive the fix. Clavaria / Clavulinopsis / Alloclavaria purpurea are caespitose: many separate unbranched purple spindles from separate bases in a dense tuft, and Clavaria acuta is literally named for its pointed apex. A tuft of separate pointed purple spindles is therefore a legitimate fungal form, so 'separate bases + points' alone does not condemn this asset. It fails for other reasons.
2. The real base defect is worse and different from 'no fused base'. At 6x, every finger terminates in a HARD, FLAT, HORIZONTAL CROP — a straight chopped rectangle end with a crisp edge — and those crops sit ABOVE the shadow ellipse with a gap. The stalks are clipped, floating rods that touch nothing. There is no foot, no ground contact, no taper-out, no attachment geometry of any kind. This is a rendering/composition defect independent of taxon and it must be fixed regardless of what organism this becomes.
3. Profile is wrong for a club in a way the claim never names: each finger is a long parallel-sided shaft that tapers monotonically to a point from roughly its lower third upward. Club and fairy-club fungi SWELL toward the apex and pinch to a hair-thin, often downy base. This one is thick at the bottom and thin at the top — the exact opposite distribution, and exactly a grass blade's profile.
4. Surface quality is not mentioned and is a major part of the wrong read: the fill is glossy, plastic-smooth and perfectly even, with zero waxy/matte fungal flesh, no longitudinal grooving or contortion, no translucency at the tips, no colour break between apex and base. Every finger is the same clean geometric extrusion, which is what makes the clump read procedurally generated rather than grown.

FIX DIRECTION: kill the hard central line and replace it with a soft off-axis cylinder gradient plus a terminator; round every apex to a blunt or slightly flattened lobe; delete the sickle-curl finger or reduce it to a gentle lean; invert the taper so each spindle is fattest in its upper third and pinches to a thin whitish base; fuse or at least seat the bases into a shared fleshy pad on the ground plane so nothing floats; break the geometric uniformity with slight contortion and grooving. As drawn it is a clump of purple grass, and it should not ship in a fungi family.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated cause. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (440x440, viewed at 1x, then at 3x and 8x with gamma boost so nothing hides in the near-black background): a single geometrically perfect circle, ~150px across, centred, filled with a soft radial gradient in desaturated periwinkle grey-blue (highlight centred around the 10 o'clock upper-left quadrant, falling off to a cool shade at the lower-right limb). Scattered across the surface, clustered heavily in the lower-centre and lower-left third and thinning to nothing above the equator, are roughly 35 small flat discs a few shades darker than the body, radii ~1.5-5px. Under the substrate is one hard-edged black ellipse ~185x40px. That is the entire drawing. There is no second form of any kind.

CORRECTION 1 to the claim — the drop shadow is NOT detached. At 8x on the base, the sphere's lower arc is drawn ON TOP of the shadow ellipse and descends to roughly the ellipse's vertical mid-line, so the contact point itself reads fine. The real substrate defect is different and worth stating precisely for the fix: there is no substrate BODY at all — no duff pad, no soil ellipse, no log, no mycelial fringe, no basal rooting — which is exactly what sibling s12 (blue puffball pair on a brown soil pad) and s17 (toothed caps on a log) supply and what makes them read as fungi. Do not 'fix the shadow'; add a substrate and a base.

CORRECTION 2 — the dark speckles are not craters and not warts. Each is a flat uniform-value filled circle with no rim, no cast shadow and no top-lit highlight; they carry zero relief in either direction. They read as pits only because a smooth sphere gives the eye nothing else to interpret them as. A wart pass needs a light-top/dark-bottom pair per bump plus a bumpy silhouette; a pore pass needs a rim. Currently it is neither.

NEW DEFECT the first judge did not name: the white crescent is not merely a rim light, it is MIS-REGISTERED. Zoomed 14x at the 3-4 o'clock position, the white stroke sits clearly OUTSIDE the body silhouette with a dark background gap of 1-2px between stroke and body, then terminates in a blunt flat cut end while the body edge continues on down-left. The arc runs from ~11 o'clock over the apex to ~4 o'clock and is an independent stroked path offset right of the body circle, not a highlight on it. It also fights the shading: the broad diffuse highlight is upper-LEFT, the specular limb is upper-RIGHT. Two light directions in one 150px object.

FUNGAL MUST-READS, checked one at a time: apical pore/ostiole — ABSENT; at 8x the apex is one unbroken smooth arc with no dimple, dot, star-split or peridium tear. Stipe/base/volva — ABSENT. Cap/hymenium separation — ABSENT (no gills, teeth, pores, tubes, margin or cap-edge anywhere). Warts/scurf/spines — ABSENT (see correction 2). Substrate contact — ABSENT (see correction 1). Irregular lumpy peridium outline — ABSENT; the silhouette is a machine-perfect circle, which is itself the single loudest wrong signal, since real puffballs are never circular.

BATCH CONTEXT, which makes this worse rather than excusable. This is NOT a shared-chassis failure — batch 011's fungi are genuinely diverse: s12 puffball pair on soil, s13 pink coral-fungus spike cluster, s14 classic reticulate cap on a white stipe, s16 fringed cup pair, s17 Hericium-like toothed caps on a log, s18 pink spiny spore-ball with a dark central pore, s19 particulate spore cloud. Every one of those is legible as a fungus in under a second. s15 is the one asset in the group that received the bare sphere primitive with no ornament pass at all. Critically, the puffball archetype it is presumably reaching for is already solved TWO CELLS AWAY in s12, which has the lumpy non-circular outline, the surface mottling, the reticulate cracking on the smaller ball and the soil pad. s15 has none of it. Its palette is also the coldest and least organic in the batch (blue-grey against the batch's ochres, creams and pinks), which pushes the read further toward rock.

VERDICT: the object reads as a moon or asteroid, or at best an inanimate marble. Not one feature on it is diagnostic of a fungus, or of a living thing. The first judge's headline read is correct; only the shadow-detachment and crater wording were wrong. FAIL stands. FIX ORDER: (1) break the circle — irregular lumpy peridium outline; (2) apical pore or peridium split at the apex; (3) real warts with per-bump light/shade instead of flat discs; (4) substrate pad plus basal rooting; (5) delete or re-register the offset white arc so the specular agrees with the upper-left key light.
